title: feat(crypto): construct fixed-key FHE under explicit circular security
body:
Next bounded milestone under #322, following #478 / #472. Construct and certify the fixed-key scheme whose public evaluation key encrypts its own secret key. The key generator takes only the security parameter; there is no depth budget. Keep #322 open until the complete recovery criteria are audited, and retain the separate concrete-LWE obligation.

Acceptance criteria:

- Define the actual sampler: one supported base key pair (pk, sk), bitwise encryption of sk under pk, serialized public artifact (pk, encrypted-sk), and sk as the private artifact. No secret plaintext is exposed publicly. Reuse this single encrypted-key sample across every refresh.
- Reuse the existing ordinary-circuit compiler and refresh evaluator to evaluate every finite shared Boolean circuit. All circuits are permitted. Prove correctness for arbitrary pointwise decrypting, well-sized inputs, including outputs of previous evaluations, with the same key and ciphertext width. Do not replace correlated self-link reuse by independently sampled links.
- Prove perfect correctness of the actual Scheme, exact secret/ciphertext widths independent of circuit size/depth, and polynomial compactness/decryption cost from the native decryption-circuit generator. Key generation has no supplied circuit or depth bound.
- Give native uniform certificates for key generation, encryption, decryption and evaluation on their complete encoded inputs, including malformed public artifacts and references. Reuse semantic/circuit/list automation; do not add theorem-specific TM implementations.
- Define a precise one-key, bitwise circular/KDM assumption comparing (pk, Enc_pk(sk)) and (pk, Enc_pk(0^|sk|)) against uniform native PPT tests. Keep ordinary base IND-CPA separate. The assumption must not simply assert IND-CPA of the output scheme, and no circular security is claimed from ordinary IND-CPA.
- Prove actual output-scheme adaptive two-stage IND-CPA through the public-artifact hybrids and an explicit base adversary for the zero-link world. Charge saved state and complete public encoding. A supported independent key sample can supply the zero-word length under fixed supported secret width; do not assume an efficiently computable width merely for security.
- Instantiate construction/correctness/runtime premises in concrete finite regressions, explicitly label insecure examples, test repeated evaluation with the same public artifact, and include a leaking example rejected by the security notions. Do not claim a concrete secure LWE instantiation from these tests.
- Assemble the fixed-key all-circuit correctness, native efficiency, compactness and conditional security results for the same algorithms. Add axiom guards, update ROADMAP, assess the curated abstract catalogue, pass all six gates and independent exact-revision API/correctness review.

Planned reusable files: Encryption/Circular.lean for the explicit self-encryption experiment; Homomorphic/FixedKey/{Encoding,Basic,Correctness,PolyTime,Security,Bootstrapping}.lean for the construction. Adjust placement if concrete reuse or review warrants it. Existing encryptedWires_evaluateLayers already permits pointwise valid repeated keys/links and old evaluated ciphertexts.

Source: Craig Gentry, [Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/hits09/gentry-homomorphic-encryption.pdf), Section 2, especially the self-loop paragraph following Theorem 5. The proof plan and precise experiment above require implementation and independent review; they are not completed results.

Owner/session: worker-codex-gentry-fixedkey-20261023. Planned branch: feat/gentry-fixedkey-20261023 in an independent checkout initially stacked on #478. Root authors the circular experiment, security reduction, assembly and regressions; /root/maintenance_audit will author construction/correctness/native certificates in a separate checkout. /root/refactor_plan_review provides read-only source/model reconnaissance; /root/library_map remains independent of authoring.

title: feat(logspace): define SL via USTCON reductions, prove SL = L, and share unary-header injectivity
body:
## Scope

Complete two items from the Reingold milestone in `ROADMAP.md`:

1. **Shared unary-header injectivity**:
   - Export `List.replicate_append_cons_inj` in `Complexity/Foundations/Data/List/Basic.lean` (and add `Christian Reitwiessner` to `Authors:` for the shared lemma).
   - Deduplicate `Cslib.TreeEval.Tree.replicate_true_append_inj` in `Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/Encoding.lean` and `Cslib.Complexity.USTCONInstance.replicate_append_false_inj` in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Problems/USTCON.lean` to reuse the shared lemma.

2. **Symmetric logarithmic space `SL` and `SL = L` (Reingold 2008, Theorem 4.2)**:
   - In `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/LogSpace/USTCON.lean`, define `SL enc := {A | LogSpaceReducible enc encUSTCON A USTCON}` via the logspace-reduction characterization of symmetric logarithmic space [Lewis–Papadimitriou 1982; Reingold 2008, Section 1 and Theorem 4.2].
   - Construct two-vertex connected and disconnected `USTCONInstance` witnesses and prove `USTCON_logSpaceHard_L : LogSpaceHard L encUSTCON USTCON` and `USTCON_logSpaceComplete_L : LogSpaceComplete L encUSTCON USTCON`.

title: feat(crypto): complete leveled bootstrapping for polynomial depth families
body:
Completion-audit follow-up under #322 after #478 and #480. The existing leveled construction accepts an efficiently computable unary budget. The roadmap target quantifies over every polynomially bounded depth family, which need not itself be computable. Recover that exact public quantifier using an executable polynomial majorant; preserve the existing algorithms and theorems.

Acceptance:
- Given any depth : Nat → Nat with PolynomiallyBounded depth, choose constants c,d and budget n = c*(n+1)^d dominating depth at every n, including the finite prefix. The output scheme must compute budget, never depth.
- Expose a single leveled endpoint for the actual constructed algorithms: correctness for every circuit of depth at most depth n, exact budget-independent secret/ciphertext widths with polynomial bounds, native certificates for all four algorithms, and ordinary-base-IND-CPA transfer without circular security.
- Make compact decryption explicit: the decryption algorithm and its resource bound must be independent of the selected depth budget; derive any needed parameter-only consequence from the native certificate and polynomial fixed widths. Reuse the semantic/native and circuit-transfer APIs instead of writing a new TM implementation.
- Keep the existing efficient-budget theorem and public names unchanged. Do not broaden Scheme.Correct into unsupported reuse of acyclic wrapper ciphertexts.
- Regressions must cover an arbitrary bounded predicate-dependent depth family without a computability premise and a large finite-prefix depth spike; instantiate construction/runtime hypotheses with the existing explicitly insecure tagged fixture, and keep conditional security honest. Add headline axiom guards.
- Run all six gates, obtain independent exact-revision API/correctness review, update ROADMAP, and assess selected abstracts.

Scope is the missing endpoint/corollary and explicit compactness evidence, not a concrete LWE cryptosystem. Read-only audit by /root/library_map is checking remaining statement obligations. Root worker-codex-gentry-endpoint-20261023 will own implementation in isolated branch feat/gentry-endpoint-20261023, initially based on #480. The separate concrete LWE construction and security reduction are tracked in #486; #322 retains the generic conditional bootstrapping theorem. Source: Gentry2009 Section 2; upstream polynomiallyBounded_iff_le supplies the all-input polynomial majorant.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
**M0 design and claim**: `worker-claude-fhe-c4b0c164` (Claude), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. State: **active**. Branch `feat/gsw-bootstrappable-486`, worktree `/home/samuel/Code/complexitylib-wt/486-1`.

### Where `main` stands

Everything on the pre-pause branches is already on `main`: `feat/balanced-code-543`, `feat/gsw-shallow-decryption-528` and the `feat/gsw-*-20261023` branches are either patch-equivalent to `main` or were superseded by later sweeps. There is nothing to recover.

- **Milestone 1 is done (#607).** `GSW.DecryptionCircuit.circuit` agrees with `decryptSerialized` on every well-sized raw input (`DecryptionCircuit.correct`). Its depth is at most `28 + 18⌈log₂(w+1)⌉ + 12⌈log₂ n⌉` (`depth_circuit_le`). Its NAND augmentation compiles to at most `DepthParameters.depthBudget` layers (`layers_augment_le_depthBudget`). Both circuits have native generators (`computableInPolyTime_circuit`, `computableInPolyTime_layeredAugment`).
- **The parameter family of milestone 2 is on `main` (#552).** `GSW.DepthParameters` has `noise_margin : 4·m·η·(N+1)^L < 2^w` with `L = depthBudget`, and `DepthParameters.indCPA` under decision LWE for exactly this family. The modulus `2^(16384·(1+⌈log₂(λ+2)⌉)²)` is quasi-polynomial.
- **The missing piece links the two.** GSW has no homomorphic evaluator for circuits, so nothing proves that the scheme *evaluates* its own augmented decryption. There is also no `Homomorphic.Scheme` value for GSW, so #481's `DecryptionCircuits` and `Bootstrappable` cannot be instantiated yet.

My first PR therefore completes milestone 2, and milestone 3 follows it.

### PR 1 (milestone 2): GSW evaluates its own augmented decryption

**New `GSW/CircuitEvaluation.lean` (namespace `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW`):**

```lean
/-- Noiseless public constant `Flatten(μ · I_N)`. -/
def constSerialized (n w : ℕ) (μ : Bool) : List Bool
/-- Compile with `Layered.compile`, run the layers (const ↦ `constSerialized`, copy ↦ the wire
cut to `N²` bits, NAND ↦ `nandSerialized`) and return designated output 0. Deterministic and
independent of the public key. -/
def evaluateCircuit (n w : ℕ) (C : Σ k, Circuit signature k 1) (inputs : List (List Bool)) :
    List Bool
/-- GSW's "B-bounded error", on a complete serialized word. -/
def BoundedError (n w : ℕ) (secret : List Bool) (bound : ℕ) (μ : Bool) (c : List Bool) : Prop :=
  c.length = ((n + 1) * w) ^ 2 ∧ ∃ e, HasError (decodeSecret n w secret)
    (decodeCiphertext n w c) μ e ∧ ∀ i, (e i).natAbs ≤ bound

theorem boundedError_evaluateCircuit (C : Σ k, Circuit signature k 1) (bits : List Bool)
    (hbits : bits.length = C.1) (hinputs : List.Forall₂ (BoundedError n w secret bound) bits inputs) :
    BoundedError n w secret (((n + 1) * w + 1) ^ (2 * C.2.depth) * bound)
      (C.2.eval interpretation (BitString.ofList C.1 bits) 0) (evaluateCircuit n w C inputs)

theorem evaluateCircuit_correct (hw : 0 < w)
    (hkeys : keys ∈ (ProbComp.eval (keyGenSerialized n m w η)).support)
    (hmargin : 4 * (m * η) * ((n + 1) * w + 1) ^ (2 * C.2.depth) < 2 ^ w)
    (hbits : bits.length = C.1)
    (hinputs : List.Forall₂ (fun μ c => c ∈ (ProbComp.eval (encryptSerialized n m w keys.1 μ)).support)
      bits inputs) :
    (evaluateCircuit n w C inputs).length = ((n + 1) * w) ^ 2 ∧
      decryptSerialized n w keys.2 (evaluateCircuit n w C inputs) =
        C.2.eval interpretation (BitString.ofList C.1 bits) 0
```

A companion `CircuitEvaluation/PolyTime.lean` certifies the evaluator natively on arbitrary raw inputs, with a `foldl` and bounded growth, reusing `computableInPolyTime_nandSerialized` and `Layered.computableInPolyTime_compile`.

**New `GSW/DepthParameters/Scheme.lean`:**

```lean
noncomputable def DepthParameters.scheme : Homomorphic.Scheme where
  keyGen k := keyGenSerialized (dimension k) (samples k) (width k) (noise k)
  encrypt k := encryptSerialized (dimension k) (samples k) (width k)
  decrypt k := decryptSerialized (dimension k) (width k)
  evaluate k _ C inputs := pure (evaluateCircuit (dimension k) (width k) C inputs)
  permitted k C := 2 * C.2.depth ≤ depthBudget k
-- secretWidth k := dimension k * width k, ciphertextWidth k := rows k * rows k
theorem DepthParameters.correct : scheme.Correct
theorem DepthParameters.fixedWidth : scheme.FixedWidth secretWidth ciphertextWidth
def DepthParameters.decryptionCircuits : DecryptionCircuits scheme secretWidth ciphertextWidth
theorem DepthParameters.bootstrappable : Scheme.Bootstrappable decryptionCircuits
```

`DecryptionCircuit/Parameters.lean` gains the matching budget fit for the bare decryptor, as well as the augmentation. No public statement on `main` changes. Estimated size is 800–1,100 lines with tests. The tests run the evaluator at small concrete dimensions on noisy and noiseless words.

**Source mapping.** Gentry–Sahai–Waters, ePrint 2013/340 full version dated June 8, 2013 (fetched and checked):
- §3.3, NAND (p. 11): "NAND(C1, C2) · v = (I_N − C1 · C2) · v = (1 − µ1 · µ2) · v − µ2 · e1 − C1 · e2 … the error is increased by a factor of at most N + 1".
- §3.3, "Circuits" (p. 11): "the final ciphertext's error will be bounded by (N + 1)^L · B, where L is the NAND-depth of the circuit, and B is the original bound on the error of a fresh encryption of {0, 1}".
- §3.4 (pp. 11–12): "As long as q/B > 8(N+1)^L, we can evaluate a depth-L circuit of NANDs over B-bounded ciphertexts to obtain a q/8-bounded ciphertext, which Dec will decrypt correctly".

In Lean, the paper's `L` becomes `2·depth` layers of `Layered.compile`: two NAND microlevels per De Morgan level, and copy layers add no error. `B = m·η`, and `q = 2^w`. The margin `4·B·(N+1)^L < q` comes from the library's existing middle-half decoder (`decrypt_eq_of_hasError`), not from GSW's `Dec`, so it does not reproduce GSW's constant 8.

Gentry, STOC 2009, p. 171: Definition 4 (g-augmented decryption circuits) and Definition 5, "We say that E is bootstrappable with respect to Γ if D_E(Γ) ⊆ C_E". `Scheme.Bootstrappable` is the case Γ = {identity, NAND}.

**Library choices, stated as such.** Constants are the noiseless `Flatten(μ·I_N)`. GSW uses `I_N` in NAND and `Flatten(α·I_N)` in MultConst (§3.3, pp. 10–11). Evaluation is deterministic and ignores `pk`, which matches the abstract (p. 1): "The evaluator can do homomorphic operations without knowing the user's public key at all, except for some basic parameters." The paper's dimension and modulus reduction before bootstrapping (§3.4, citing [BV11b]) is not used, so no Brakerski–Vaikuntanathan locator is needed.

### PR 2 (milestone 3): concrete FHE from GSW

PR 2 instantiates `Leveled.exists_scheme_of_polynomiallyBounded` and `FixedKey.fullyHomomorphic` with `DepthParameters.scheme`. The premises are `DecisionLWE dimension samples width (fun k => noiseLaw (width k) (noise k))` and, for the fixed-key endpoint only, the explicit hypothesis `Encryption.CircularSecure scheme.keyGen scheme.encrypt`; circular security is not derived from LWE. Public statements will be plain, with tidy computability only inside proofs. The same PR adds the formal abstract and catalogue entry, and the ROADMAP update.

Nothing in this comment is a completion claim.

- **The missing piece links the two.** GSW has no homomorphic evaluator for circuits, so nothing proves that the scheme *evaluates* its own augmented decryption. There is also no `Homomorphic.Scheme` value for GSW, so #481's `DecryptionCircuits` and `Bootstrappable` cannot be instantiated yet.

body:
**Design: formal abstract for the GSW FHE endpoints (droppable headline proposal)**: `worker-claude-fhe-c4b0c164`

This would be a separate proposal PR after #1025. It adds `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/GSWFHEAbstract.lean`, a bridge `GSWFHEBridge.lean`, and a catalogue entry `gsw-fhe` marked as Samuel's editorial call, which can be dropped as with #968. Nothing below changes a library statement.

**What the abstract states.** The abstract is self-contained, using only upstream Cslib and Mathlib plus the shared `ComplexityAbstracts.Encoding` and `Computation` modules.

- **Boolean circuits.** Upstream `Cslib.Circuits.Circuit` over `Boolean.signature`, with its `eval` and depth. The circuit's input encoding is restated as about 40 lines of framing.
- **The base GSW scheme in full.** The depth family's parameters, from #552:
  - `t = 1 + ⌈log₂(λ+2)⌉`
  - `w = 16384·t²`
  - `n = λ + 1`
  - `m = (n+1)·w + 2λ`
  - `η = λ + 1`

  It also restates the key-generation and encryption laws, in the same style as `GSWSecurityAbstract`.
- **Both assumptions, exactly.** `DecisionLWE` for this family. `CircularSecure` is the one-key real-versus-zero self-encryption experiment for that base scheme.
- **Generic predicates on a four-algorithm bit-encryption scheme `S`.**
  - `HomomorphicFor S allowed`: fresh encryptions decrypt correctly, and every allowed circuit evaluates correctly on supported fresh encryptions.
  - `Compact S bound`: every supported fresh or evaluated ciphertext has length at most `bound λ`.
  - `Efficient S`: key generation, encryption and evaluation are uniform strict PPT, with circuits given by their encoding, and decryption is polynomial time.
  - `ChosenMessageSecure S`: single-challenge IND-CPA.
- **Headlines.**

```lean
theorem leveled (hLWE : DecisionLWE) :
    ∃ (bound : ℕ → ℕ) (decrypt : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → Bool),
      Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded bound ∧
      ∀ depth : ℕ → ℕ, Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded depth →
        ∃ S : Scheme, S.decrypt = decrypt ∧
          HomomorphicFor S (fun k C => C.2.depth ≤ depth k) ∧ Compact S bound ∧
          Efficient S ∧ ChosenMessageSecure S

theorem fullyHomomorphic (hLWE : DecisionLWE) (hcirc : CircularSecure) :
    ∃ (S : Scheme) (bound : ℕ → ℕ), Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded bound ∧
      HomomorphicFor S (fun _ _ => True) ∧ Compact S bound ∧ Efficient S ∧
      ChosenMessageSecure S
```

The quantifier order puts one compactness bound and one decryption algorithm before the depth family, which is Gentry's Definition 3, p. 170: "they all use the same decryption circuit". The bound does not depend on the depth.

**The trade-off to decide.** #486 asks the abstract to state "the actual construction". In this design the GSW base scheme and both assumptions are explicit, but the bootstrapped wrapper is existential: the key chain, refresh, and #607's decryption circuit of `131(n+1)(w+1)²` gates. The bridge instantiates it with `Leveled.scheme decryptionCircuits budget` and `FixedKey.scheme decryptionCircuits`, and the docstring names them.

Spelling out the wrapper inside the abstract would mean either restating the shallow decryption circuit, which is thousands of library lines, or allowlisting the Homomorphic, Circuit and GSW modules. Their closure includes the tidy-machine modules, which the abstract guidance says to avoid. I recommend the existential form, labelled as such. If Samuel wants the wrapper explicit, it can be done as a separate allowlisted appendix.

**Size and reuse.** Roughly 350 lines for the abstract and 500–700 for the bridge. The bridge reuses `GSWSecurityBridge`'s strict PPT and IND-CPA transfers, generalized from the base scheme's algorithms to any scheme with the same encodings.

No Lean has been written for this yet. I will start once #1022 and #1025 have their review verdicts, unless the coordinator or Samuel prefers otherwise.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
**Design and claim: formal abstract for the GSW FHE endpoints**: `worker-claude-fhe-abstract-c4b0c164` (Claude), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. State: **active**. Branch `feat/fhe-abstract-486`, worktree `/home/samuel/Code/complexitylib-wt/486-3`.

This replaces the existential design above. Following Samuel's decision of 2026-10-25, the abstract **names the construction**: GSW at the depth family, `Leveled.scheme decryptionCircuits budget` and `FixedKey.scheme decryptionCircuits`. Correctness, compactness, native runtime, IND-CPA, decision LWE and circular security are restated in elementary terms, and the bridge proves them equivalent to the library's notions. One PR, no library statement changes.

### Files

- New shared foundation `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/Randomized.lean`. It holds `uniformBits`, `StrictPPT`, `Negligible`, `probability` and `Indistinguishable`, moved verbatim from `CryptographyAbstract`. Abstracts cannot import other abstracts, so reusing these notions requires the move. `CryptographyAbstract` imports the foundation, with unchanged meaning, and `CryptographyBridge` drops its private copies of these notions.
- `GSWFHEAbstract.lean`, `GSWFHEBridge.lean`, a catalogue entry `gsw-fhe` (foundations `Encoding`, `Computation`, `Randomized`), the README table, and ROADMAP landmark 3. ROADMAP keeps open uniform compactness, multi-hop evaluation and the exact concrete loss.

### Abstract statements (`security` is λ)

**Parameters**, all elementary:
- `logSize s = 1 + Nat.clog 2 (s + 2)`, `width s = 16384 * logSize s ^ 2`, so the modulus is `2 ^ width s`.
- `dimension s = s + 1`: the secret dimension, and also the centered-binomial width.
- `rows s = (dimension s + 1) * width s`, `samples s = rows s + 2 * s`.
- `secretWidth s = dimension s * width s`, `ciphertextWidth s = rows s * rows s`.

**Base GSW laws.** `keyGeneration`, `encryption` and `uniformPublic` are PMFs with the same text as `GSWSecurityAbstract`, instantiated at this family.

**Assumptions:**
```lean
def DecisionLWE : Prop :=
  Randomized.Indistinguishable (fun s => (keyGeneration s).map Prod.fst) uniformPublic
noncomputable def selfEncryption (real : Bool) (s : ℕ) : PMF (List Bool) := do
  let keys ← keyGeneration s
  let encrypted ← (if real then keys.2 else List.replicate keys.2.length false).mapM
    (encryption s keys.1)
  return Encoding.encPair Encoding.encBits (Encoding.encList Encoding.encBits) (keys.1, encrypted)
def CircularSecure : Prop := Randomized.Indistinguishable (selfEncryption true) (selfEncryption false)
```

**Named construction:**
```lean
noncomputable def baseScheme : Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme :=
  Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.scheme
noncomputable def leveledScheme (budget : ℕ → ℕ) : Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme :=
  Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.scheme
    Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.decryptionCircuits budget
noncomputable def fixedKeyScheme : Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme :=
  Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.FixedKey.scheme
    Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.decryptionCircuits
def decryptionCircuit (s : ℕ) : Cslib.Circuits.Circuit Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.signature
    (secretWidth s + ciphertextWidth s) 1 :=
  Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.decryptionCircuits.circuit s
```

**Properties of a scheme `S`.** Each is elementary, over `ProbComp.eval` supports, and none mentions the library's `permitted` field:
- `Homomorphic S allowed`: fresh ciphertexts decrypt correctly, and every allowed circuit evaluates correctly on pointwise supported fresh encryptions. This is Gentry's "correct for C_E".
- `FixedWidths S allowed sw cw`: supported secret keys, fresh ciphertexts and evaluated ciphertexts have widths `sw s` and `cw s`.
- `DecryptsWith S sw cw circuit`: on every well-sized key and ciphertext, `circuit s` computes `S.decrypt`, with secret bits first.
- `Native S`: key generation, encryption and evaluation are `Randomized.StrictPPT`, and decryption is `Computation.PolyTime`. Circuits are given by `Boolean.encCircuit 1`.
- `ChosenMessageSecure S`: single-challenge IND-CPA, `GSWSecurityAbstract`'s game generalized to any `S`.

**Theorems:**
```lean
theorem base_scheme (s : ℕ) :
    Cslib.ProbComp.eval (baseScheme.keyGen s) = keyGeneration s ∧
      ∀ pk μ, Cslib.ProbComp.eval (baseScheme.encrypt s pk μ) = encryption s pk μ

theorem leveled (hLWE : DecisionLWE) :
    ∃ circuit : ∀ s, Cslib.Circuits.Circuit Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.signature
        ((3 * secretWidth s + 1) + (ciphertextWidth s + 1)) 1,
      Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded (fun s => (circuit s).size) ∧
      Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded (fun s => 3 * secretWidth s + 1) ∧
      Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded (fun s => ciphertextWidth s + 1) ∧
      ∀ budget : ℕ → ℕ, Computation.PolyTime budget Encoding.encUnary Encoding.encUnary →
        DecryptsWith (leveledScheme budget) (fun s => 3 * secretWidth s + 1)
          (fun s => ciphertextWidth s + 1) circuit ∧
        Homomorphic (leveledScheme budget) (fun s C => C.2.depth ≤ budget s) ∧
        FixedWidths (leveledScheme budget) (fun s C => C.2.depth ≤ budget s)
          (fun s => 3 * secretWidth s + 1) (fun s => ciphertextWidth s + 1) ∧
        Native (leveledScheme budget) ∧ ChosenMessageSecure (leveledScheme budget)

theorem fullyHomomorphic (hLWE : DecisionLWE) (hcircular : CircularSecure) :
    DecryptsWith fixedKeyScheme secretWidth ciphertextWidth decryptionCircuit ∧
      Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded (fun s => (decryptionCircuit s).size) ∧
      Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded secretWidth ∧ Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded ciphertextWidth ∧
      Homomorphic fixedKeyScheme (fun _ _ => True) ∧
      FixedWidths fixedKeyScheme (fun _ _ => True) secretWidth ciphertextWidth ∧
      Native fixedKeyScheme ∧ ChosenMessageSecure fixedKeyScheme
```

### Quantifier order

- **Leveled.** The only existential is the wrapper's decryption-circuit family, which is genuinely existential in Lean (`Leveled.exists_decrypt_circuits`). It is chosen first, before any budget.
- **The budget is universal, not existential.** Every component lemma that `Leveled.exists_scheme_of_polynomiallyBounded` assembles (`correct`, `fixedWidth`, the `isPPTOn_scheme_*` lemmas, `computableTidilyInPolyTime_scheme_decrypt`, `indCPA_scheme`) holds for every budget computable in unary polynomial time. So the abstract names `leveledScheme budget` for every such budget. That is stronger than the library's `∃ budget`, and the bridge proves it from exactly those lemmas.
- **Polynomially bounded depth.** A polynomially bounded depth family `d` is covered by the budget `c * (s + 1) ^ e` taken from its bound. The docstring says so.
- **Fixed key.** Nothing is existential.

### The cost: a large allowlist

The construction lives in the library, so naming it means `#check_abstract … allowing [...]` over the closure of `DepthParameters.scheme`, `decryptionCircuits`, `Leveled.scheme` and `FixedKey.scheme`. I computed that closure with the audit's own traversal: **58 modules**. They cover:
- GSW algorithms and parameters;
- the shallow decryption circuit (`CarryLookahead`, `CarrySave`, `Modular.*`, `BalancedFold`);
- the generic wrappers (`KeyChain`, `Refresh`, `Evaluation`, `Layered`, the encodings);
- `Layered.Compile`, `Boolean.Encoding` and the machine encoding/decoder modules;
- `ProbComp`.

No tidy-machine module is in the closure. The largest existing allowlist has 10 modules, so this departs from "narrowly identified foundational models". The docstring will list the groups and say plainly that **the construction is inspected in the library, while every claim and both assumptions are stated here**. `base_scheme` makes the assumptions readable without the allowlist. Restating the wrappers, `Layered.compile`, the decoders and the decryption circuit abstract-side instead would mean thousands of lines of parallel definitions. The earlier existential form avoids the allowlist but does not name the construction.

### Existing notions considered

- **`CryptographyAbstract`**: `StrictPPT`, `Negligible`, `probability`, `Indistinguishable`, `uniformBits`. Reused by moving them into the `Randomized` foundation.
- **Shared foundations**: `Encoding.encPair`/`encList`/`encUnary`/`encBits`/`encBool` and `Computation.PolyTime`. Reused.
- **`GSWSecurityAbstract`** (uncatalogued, cannot be imported): its GSW laws are for the narrower `Parameters` family, so the laws are restated here for the depth family, and its `ChosenMessageSecure` is generalized from the fixed GSW algorithms to any scheme.
- **Library**:
  - `Homomorphic.Scheme` is the type of the named construction.
  - `Scheme.Correct` and `FixedWidth` become `Homomorphic` and `FixedWidths`, with an explicit circuit class instead of `permitted`.
  - `DecryptionCircuits` becomes `DecryptsWith`.
  - `IsPPTOn` and `ComputableInPolyTime` become `StrictPPT` and `PolyTime`.
  - `Encryption.INDCPA`, `Crypto.DecisionLWE` and `Encryption.CircularSecure` become `ChosenMessageSecure`, `DecisionLWE` and `CircularSecure`.

### Source mapping (checked in the fetched PDFs)

Gentry, *Fully homomorphic encryption using ideal lattices*, STOC 2009:
- Section 1.1, p. 169: correctness. "E is correct for circuits in C_E if, for any key-pair (sk, pk) output by KeyGen_E(λ), any circuit C ∈ C_E, any plaintexts π1, …, πt, and any ciphertexts Ψ = ⟨ψ1, …, ψt⟩ with ψi ← Encrypt_E(pk, πi), it is the case that: ψ ← Evaluate_E(pk, C, Ψ) ⇒ C(π1, …, πt) = Decrypt_E(sk, ψ)".
- p. 170: Definitions 1–3. Definition 3: "they all use the same decryption circuit, E^(d) is homomorphic for all circuits of depth at most d (that use some specified set of gates Γ), and the computational complexity of E^(d)'s algorithms is polynomial in λ, d, and (in the case of Evaluate_E(d)) the size of C."
- Section 2, p. 171: Definitions 4–5 and Theorems 3–4. Theorem 4's loss `ε/ℓ(d+1)` is **not** formalized; the abstract states asymptotic IND-CPA.
- p. 172: the self-loop paragraph, "if E is KDM-secure, we can shorten the public key to include pk and and an encryption of sk under pk, a "self-loop" rather than an acyclic chain of encrypted secret keys." `CircularSecure` is a one-key, bitwise specialization of that KDM premise.

Gentry–Sahai–Waters: ePrint 2013/340 full version, Sections 3.1–3.4.

Estimated size: about 450 lines of abstract, 450 of bridge and 120 for the foundation move. I am starting the implementation now. Nothing here is a completion claim.

body:
**Completed** (`coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`). The concrete instantiation of Gentry's bootstrapping with GSW is on `main`:
- **#1022:** GSW evaluates its own augmented decryption circuit (bootstrappable).
- **#1025:** `exists_leveled_of_decisionLWE` gives leveled FHE from decision LWE alone, for GSW's logarithmic-depth parameter family. `fullyHomomorphic_of_decisionLWE_of_circularSecure` gives the fixed-key self-loop FHE under the same LWE assumption plus an explicitly stated one-key circular-security assumption.
- **#1077:** the checked formal abstract `gsw-fhe`. It pins GSW key generation, encryption and decryption and Gentry's self-loop key explicitly. title: feat(crypto): instantiate bootstrapping with a concrete LWE-based scheme
body:
## Scope

Recover the concrete LWE-based homomorphic encryption goal as a separate development from the generic conditional Gentry bootstrapping theorem in #322. The generic endpoint was completed in #481; it does not exhibit a secure and correct concrete cryptosystem.

The deterministic GSW algebra with exact noise and correctness proofs is merged (#488 / PR #496). Finite sampling and supported correctness are tracked in #495; statistical hiding with a shared public matrix is in #494 / PR #498. The next independently reviewable milestones are #500 (complete native key generation and encryption) and #501 (the exact decision-LWE reduction and actual scheme IND-CPA theorem). Ownership and active status are recorded in the comments. Decryption/evaluation runtime, shallow augmented decryption, admissible bootstrapping parameters and the concrete FHE instantiation remain part of this parent objective.

## Required result

- Define the actual key generation, encryption, decryption, evaluation, and finite sampling algorithms for a concrete LWE-based construction, with explicit parameter and noise families.
- State the decision-LWE assumption as a precise computational distinguishing experiment matching those algorithms and the library's uniform probabilistic polynomial-time adversaries. Prove the encryption security reduction to that assumption.
- Prove correctness, noise growth, output widths, and native polynomial-time certificates for the actual algorithms. Construct the decryption circuits and establish the augmented-decryption bootstrappability hypotheses rather than assuming the desired output properties in a structure.
- Give an explicit nonvacuous admissible parameter family and connect the construction to the leveled endpoint for every polynomially bounded requested depth family. Separate requested depth, executable budget, ciphertext size, and decryption cost.
- Address the library's perfect-support correctness contract explicitly. Unbounded noise tails cannot be silently discarded: any bounded or truncated sampler needs an appropriate correctness argument and a security comparison supporting the exact stated assumption.
- If a fixed-key, arbitrary-depth endpoint is provided, expose its separate one-key circular-security assumption unless it is proved from a clearly stated stronger assumption. Do not infer circular security from ordinary IND-CPA or ordinary decision-LWE without a proof.

## Completion and review

The final theorem must identify all cryptographic and parameter assumptions and the actual constructed scheme. A Regev-style public-key encryption result, a functional toy scheme, or a security-only fixture is a milestone, not completion of this issue. Require meaningful client examples, all repository checks (the global axiom audit covers the standard axioms; named guards only for results meant to use fewer axioms, per #996), and independent API/correctness review of the final statements against the primary sources. Keep ROADMAP.md accurate throughout. Once the full endpoint is proved, provide a checked Lean formal abstract and generated PDF stating the actual construction, correctness and parameter conditions, computational security assumptions, native resource guarantees and compactness. State any circular-security assumption separately. Independently review the abstract against the final Lean definitions and statements; supporting algebra alone does not complete this headline.

The withdrawn worst-case quantum lattice-to-LWE reduction (#330, roadmap target 10) is a separate theorem goal; using a precise decision-LWE assumption does not claim that reduction has been recovered.

## Primary sources and dependencies

- Gentry, *Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices* (STOC 2009): https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/hits09/gentry-homomorphic-encryption.pdf
- Gentry, Sahai, and Waters, *Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors: Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based* (CRYPTO 2013), a candidate construction to assess during the design milestone: https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/340
- Generic conditional bootstrapping: #322 and #481.

AI-assisted task decomposition by worker-codex-gentry-endpoint-20261023. This issue records an open target, not a completed construction or security proof.

title: feat(crypto): construct the GSW algebra with exact noise correctness
body:
First construction milestone under #486: implement the actual deterministic Gentry–Sahai–Waters encryption and NAND formulas and prove their noise/decryption behavior. This is not yet a sampled secure cryptosystem, a native-runtime certificate, or a bootstrappable scheme.

Use the documented power-of-two specialization q=2^ell and N=(n+1)*ell. GSW uses floor(log2 q)+1 digits; at a power of two our minimal ell-bit representation omits its redundant top digit. Represent ciphertext entries as bits so the 0/1 invariant is structural; use Mathlib ZMod and Matrix for modular semantics, with explicit integer noise witnesses.

Acceptance:
- Define actual bit decomposition, recomposition, powers-of-two expansion and flattening; prove reconstruction/product preservation for all inputs, including nonbinary inputs to flattening. No assumed gadget laws.
- Construct s=(1,-t) and the public matrix A=[B*t+e | B] from actual t,B,e; prove A*s=e modulo q.
- Define public encryptWithCoins(A,mu,R)=Flatten(mu*I+BitDecomp(R*A)), taking only the public matrix, message and binary coins. Prove its exact recomposition and approximate-eigenvector equations, with integer error R*e bounded by sum |e_j| and hence m*beta.
- Define actual NAND(C1,C2)=Flatten(I-C1*C2). Prove exact integer noise -mu2*e1-lift(C1)*e2 and bound B1+N*B2, preserving multiplication order and Boolean message semantics.
- Define actual wraparound-aware Boolean decryption using the coordinate (0,ell-1), with explicit ell>0, deterministic boundary behavior and correctness under 4*|error|<q. A half-open middle-half test is permitted and will support a later top-two-bit circuit implementation.
- Concrete positive-noise tests must cover both messages, all NAND input pairs, negative-error wraparound and boundary/malformed algebra cases. Suggested fixture: q=64, n=m=1, t=5, B=[3], e=[1], all-one coins; this has no security interpretation. Add headline axiom guards, run all six gates and obtain independent exact-revision API/correctness/source review.
- Update ROADMAP and assess the curated abstracts; keep #486 open. Add primary source credit in a focused bibliography/documentation commit.

Explicit later obligations under #486: actual finite noise and matrix samplers; efficient binary serialization and uniform native algorithms on all inputs; a precise computational decision-LWE experiment and reduction plus leftover-hash argument; admissible parameter families; and an actual shallow decryption circuit/augmented-decryption bootstrappability proof. The current ripple-carry circuit depth alone cannot discharge that last obligation. Perfect support correctness must not be inferred from GSW's negligible-tail definition of bounded noise.

Source: Gentry, Sahai and Waters, *Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors: Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based*, Sections 2.3 and 3.1–3.4: https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.857/2021/files/Gentry-Sahai-Waters13.pdf .

Design reviewed independently by /root/library_map; root worker-codex-lwe-design-20261023 owns implementation and will record delegated file ownership before edits. AI-assisted development.

title: feat(wordram): complete NativePrimitives for Basis.standard, Basis.additive, Basis.arithmetic, and Basis.exact
body:
Complete the scalar `GenericRAM.Model.NativePrimitives` bundles and polynomial-bound proofs (`NativePrimitives.IsPolynomial`) for `Cslib.WordRAM` over `Basis.standard`, `Basis.additive`, `Basis.arithmetic`, and `Basis.exact` under the `(encNat, encNat, encUnary)` encoding (binary values and addresses, unary runtime word width).

### Scope and completion criteria
1. **Binary natural bitwise and shift operations (`PolyTime/Nat/Binary.lean`):**
   - Certify `Nat.bitwise` (for `op false false = false`), bitwise `&&&`, `|||`, `^^^`, and right shift `>>>` in `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` over `encNat`, with `@[fun_prop, program_certificate]` registration.
2. **WordRAM scalar primitives and basis bundles (`WordRAM/Native.lean`):**
   - Define `Basis.encoding (B : Basis) : B.genericModel.Encoding := ⟨encNat, encNat, encUnary⟩`.
   - Certify `checkedConstant`, `evalTest` (`eq` and `lt`), `address`, `validMove`, and `validPC` for arbitrary `B : Basis`.
   - Certify `checkedOp` for all operations of `Basis.standard` (`add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `mod`, `and`, `or`, `xor`, `shiftLeft`, `shiftRight`, and `width`) and `Basis.exact` (retaining exact faults on `y > x` for `.sub` and `y = 0` for `.div`/`.mod`), rejecting `.shiftLeft` overflow without materializing unchecked `x <<< y` when `y > w`.
   - Provide `Basis.nativePrimitives` / `Basis.nativePrimitives_isPolynomial`, sub-basis restriction transfer (`Basis.restrict`), and concrete bundles for `Basis.standard`, `Basis.additive`, `Basis.arithmetic`, and `Basis.exact`.
3. **Tests, nonvacuity, and documentation:**
   - Exercise all operations, exact vs. standard fault boundaries, zero-width and overflow boundaries, and end-to-end `WordRAM.transport_inO` / `WordRAM.transport_polyTime` on concrete `WordRAM` programs in `ComplexityTests/GenericRAMNative.lean` and `ComplexityTests/GenericRAMSimulation.lean`, with `#print axioms` guards.
   - Update `ROADMAP.md` and pass all six validation gates (`scripts/check.sh`).

### Dependencies and limitations
- Builds on #303 (`GenericRAM.Native`) and #311 (`WordRAM.transport_inO`, `WordRAM.transport_polyTime`).
- Width remains a unary-encoded runtime input; uniform arbitrary-program dispatch and general width-selection/input-fit reductions remain separate obligations.

title: feat(counting): define MAJSAT and prove PP-completeness
body:
## Scope

Extend `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Problems/CountingSAT.lean` with `MAJSAT` and its `PP`-completeness [Gill 1977; Simon 1975; Arora–Barak 2009, Chapter 17]:

1. **Definition of `MAJSAT`**:
   - Define `MAJSAT : Set (CNF ℕ) := {φ | 2 ^ φ.vars.toFinset.card < 2 * SharpSAT φ}` (CNF formulas satisfied by strictly more than half of the truth assignments to their occurring variables).

2. **Membership `MAJSAT_mem_PP : MAJSAT ∈ PP encCNF`**:
   - Certify that the occurring-variable count `φ ↦ φ.vars.toFinset.card` is polynomial-time computable in unary (`encCNF → encUnary`) via `SharpSAT.isFirst`, so `φ ↦ 2 ^ φ.vars.toFinset.card` is in `SharpP encCNF` via `binary_two_pow` and `SharpP.of_polyTime`.
   - Combine with `SharpSAT_mem_SharpP`, `SharpP.mul`, and `mem_PP_of_lt` to obtain `MAJSAT ∈ PP encCNF`.

3. **Hardness and completeness `MAJSAT_ppHard : PolyTimeHard PP encCNF MAJSAT` and `MAJSAT_ppComplete : PolyTimeComplete PP encCNF MAJSAT`**:
   - Construct a polynomial-time many-one reduction from `SharpSATAtLeast` to `MAJSAT` (using a fresh selector variable combining `φ` with a threshold CNF on `φ`'s occurring variables that has a prescribed number of satisfying assignments) and compose with `SharpSATAtLeast_ppHard`.

## Completion Criteria
- Zero `sorry`, zero custom `axiom`, zero `native_decide`.
- Nonvacuous test coverage and named `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/CountingSAT.lean`.
- All 6 validation checks in `scripts/check.sh` pass.
- Update `ROADMAP.md` and `paper/sections/randomness.tex` + `paper/main.pdf`.
- Independent cslib-style API review, mathematical correctness review, and theorem-index review.

The finite random-input samplers have native certificates, but the modular matrix algorithms that turn those samples into public keys and ciphertexts do not. This task closes that specific efficiency gap and supplies the executable encryption needed by the decision-LWE reduction.

Scope and acceptance:

- Define total serialized public-key, secret-key and ciphertext algorithms with explicit dimension and binary operand encodings. Prove exact bridges to `GSW.publicMatrix` and `GSW.encryptWithCoins`, including bit order, padding/normalization and output framing. Malformed input words must have specified total behavior.
- Certify signed modular reduction for errors and subtraction. Reuse existing binary arithmetic, remainder, bit extraction, range/map and list-index APIs; avoid enumeration of the modulus and fixed-size finite-type certificates as evidence of uniform efficiency.
- Certify the actual public-matrix and encryption computations uniformly over growing unary dimensions and the complete binary inputs. Compose with #495's samplers and exact distribution bridges to certify full probabilistic key generation and encryption.
- Account for complete output lengths, including `N^2` ciphertext bits, where `N=(n+1)*w`. Every input and saved value used in a computation must be charged.
- Exercise negative wraparound, ragged/malformed inputs, zero dimensions, width zero and little-endian bit order. Supply growing-parameter clients and headline axiom guards.
- Pass the six repository checks, obtain independent exact-revision API/correctness review, and assess the formal abstract catalogue. Update the roadmap without claiming decryption, NAND runtime, security or bootstrappability complete.

Source inspection by `/root/maintenance_audit` found existing native arithmetic/list routines sufficient in principle; this is a design assessment, not a completed certificate. Decryption and NAND certification are a following independently reviewable extension using the same routines.

State: available. No implementation owner is claimed by this issue creation. AI-assisted scope recorded by `worker-codex-lwe-design-20261023`.

title: feat(crypto): reduce sampled GSW IND-CPA security to decision LWE
body:
Part of #486. Depends on the shared-public-matrix hiding theorem (#494 / #498), exact supported sampling (#495), and the complete native encryption certificates in #500.

The endpoint is IND-CPA security of the actual sampled GSW encryption against uniform native PPT adversaries, under a precisely stated decision-LWE assumption. The assumption must be the exact sampled distribution, not an assumed encryption-security field.

Scope and acceptance:

- Define the real public ensemble by independent uniform `t,B` and independent centered-binomial errors `e`, with `A=[B*t+e | B]` over `ZMod(2^w)`. Compare it with a uniformly sampled public matrix. All rows share the same secret. The challenge exposes only the encoded public matrix, never the secret or complete key-generation inputs.
- State computational indistinguishability for this exact error distribution and uniform adversary model. Preserve source credit to Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013); do not infer Gaussian equivalence, a worst-case lattice reduction or hardness of arbitrary bounded noise.
- Build one actual uniform reduction: given the public matrix, run message selection, sample a hidden fair bit, perform actual encryption, preserve the adversary's saved state, run guessing and return the guess XOR the hidden bit. Prove the fixed-bit game identities and the signed mixture identity. No parameter-dependent choice of the more successful bit is allowed.
- Derive `Adv_GSW <= 2*Adv_LWE(reduction) + N*sqrt(2^(w*(n+1))/2^m)`, then the `Encryption.INDCPA` corollary under negligible LWE advantage and an explicit negligible statistical term. Use the public-key marginal law rather than claiming public and secret keys independent.
- Instantiate the reduction's full native runtime certificate from #500, with total behavior on arbitrary challenge words and all saved-state/input lengths charged. Uniformly computable dimensions are required; polynomial bounds alone do not supply an algorithm.
- Prove a usable entropy condition such as `m >= w*(n+1)+2*lambda`, with polynomial `N`, and give a growing positive-noise parameter client satisfying both that condition and the existing strict fresh/one-NAND correctness margins. Numerical feasibility does not prove the LWE assumption.
- Tests and independent review must cover correlated adversarial state, secret non-exposure, malformed inputs, nonvacuous parameter/runtime premises and headline axioms. Run all six checks and assess/update the formal abstract catalogue appropriately.

This establishes base encryption security. Shallow augmented decryption, complete homomorphic evaluation, bootstrappability and fixed-key circular security remain separate obligations in #486. In particular, ordinary decision LWE does not provide the library's separate joint self-encryption security premise.

Read-only reduction design by `/root/refactor_plan_review`; scope recorded by `worker-codex-lwe-design-20261023`. State: available; no implementation ownership is claimed.

title: feat(counting): prove uniform indexed product closure
body:
Prove actual uniform polynomially indexed product closure for jointly uniform #P and GapP functions. For `f : α × ℕ → ℕ` (respectively ℤ) in #P (GapP) under `encPair enc encUnary`, and `r : α → ℕ` computed in polynomial time with unary output, prove that `a ↦ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (r a), f (a,i)` belongs to the same class.

This goes beyond homogeneous powers and PR44's special products of FP targets minus one fixed GapP value. Do not assume product closure. No overlap with #49's two-sided WPP/LWPP specialization; use a new SharpP/Products module and leave shared Aggregation and WPP files unchanged.

Construction: for #P, pad the index-i certificate of length `p(2|a|+1+i)` with false bits to common width `p(2|a|+1+r(a))`, check all indexed rows, and use exact cardinality factorization. Total certificate length before final padding is row count times common width. For GapP, expand the product of positive/negative differences over Boolean choices, use the proved uniform #P products on the selected joint family, and sum with a certified polynomial-time parity sign. Verify the actual encoding-length formula, including zero index, in source.

Completion criteria: both full closure theorems, efficient verifier and count identity, nonvacuous tests for varying index-dependent factors/certificate lengths, empty product, zero and signed factors and cancellation, named axiom guards, all six gates, source credit, exact declaration links and index/PDF assessment, independent correctness/API/index review. This is a useful class-algebra prerequisite for future AWPP PP-lowness, not a claim that lowness has been proved.

Source credit: Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes* (1994); explicit verifier/padding and Boolean-expansion implementation follows the existing uniform counting algebra. Parent coordinator #30 approved this API/resource plan. Worker session `indexed-products-20261020`, branch `codex/counting-indexed-products`, isolated worktree `/tmp/complexitylib-fusion-quadratic` after PR46 handoff.

title: feat(circuit): construct uniform logarithmic-depth binary addition
body:
Part of the concrete bootstrapping recovery in #486. The existing `Boolean.finishCircuit w w` has a proved depth bound `7*w`; the ordinary word adder also propagates carries sequentially. Shallow GSW decryption needs a logarithmic-depth finisher. Increasing the modulus does not repair a decryption-depth bound linear in the modulus bit width.

Construct an actual Boolean carry-lookahead/prefix adder, reusing the current circuit composition and balanced-tree APIs after checking upstream for overlap. Acceptance:

- Prove exact addition of two unsigned `w`-bit words and a carry-in, including the output carry, for every input and width. Derive the modular `2^w` result needed by carry-save clients; cover zero width and overflow explicitly.
- Prove an explicit bound `depth ≤ C*(Nat.clog 2 (w+1)+1)` for an absolute constant and a polynomial size bound. Polynomial size is sufficient for this milestone; linear-size optimization is not required.
- Construct and certify one native polynomial-time generator of the serialized circuit from unary width. An existential circuit family or a polynomial size bound alone does not establish uniform construction.
- Provide a checked client replacing the sequential carry-save finishing stage while preserving its value modulo `2^w`. Keep the existing public adder interfaces compatible.
- Credit the actual prefix/carry-lookahead construction used; add meaningful carry-chain/overflow clients and axiom guards, run all six repository checks, and obtain independent API/correctness review.

Existing consumers: `Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/CarrySave.lean` (`finishCircuit`, `val_fstBits_eval_finishCircuit_mod`), `Boolean/Word.lean`, and the planned GSW shallow-decryption circuit. Place the reusable result in the Boolean circuit library, without crypto dependencies.

This issue proves an arithmetic circuit primitive, not GSW bootstrappability. AI-assisted task decomposition from the read-only #486 feasibility review. State: available; no implementation claim.

title: feat(crypto): certify native serialized GSW decryption and NAND
body:
Part of #486, continuing the actual algorithms from merged #500 / #519. Key generation and encryption now have native certificates; this milestone supplies the deterministic decryption and homomorphic NAND operations needed for evaluation.

Acceptance:

- Define total serialized decryption and NAND programs using the existing secret/ciphertext codecs and the deterministic `GSW.decrypt` / `GSW.nand` semantics. Reuse the checked modular word and matrix routines; do not infer efficiency from fixed-dimensional finite types.
- Prove agreement with the existing typed operations for all input words, including the chosen padding/truncation behavior on malformed words. Preserve exact output widths and handle zero/small widths explicitly.
- Prove uniform native polynomial-time certificates charging unary dimensions, all supplied bitstrings, intermediate values and complete output. Parameter-dependent code or merely polynomially bounded noncomputable parameter functions are insufficient.
- Transport the existing fresh and NAND noise/correctness results to these actual serialized algorithms without strengthening their hypotheses silently.
- Add meaningful clients for well-sized and malformed inputs, native-certificate composition and boundary widths; add headline axiom guards. Run all six checks and obtain independent API/correctness review.

The implementation should use the semantic composition/transfer APIs wherever possible. Record concrete API friction and improve a reusable helper when the client benefit is demonstrated.

This bounded milestone does not claim a full evaluator, shallow decryption circuits, bootstrappability or security of public evaluation keys. The generated-key IND-CPA reduction is separately in #501 / #524; ordinary LWE does not supply circular security. Keep the broader #486 objective open.

Mathematical source: Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), with current construction conventions recorded in `GSW.Basic`, `GSW.Noise` and `GSW.Serialized`. AI-assisted task decomposition. State: available; no implementation claim.

title: fix(abstracts): keep explanations with declarations and reserve footer space
body:
Follow-up to the completed PDF pipeline work in #421 and #432. Rendering the supporting GSW security abstract in #524 exposed layout defects despite passing the current text-margin checks: explanatory paragraphs could be orphaned from their declarations, a native-efficiency explanation split awkwardly across pages, and a code-box border touched the multi-line provenance footer.

The reviewed standalone PDF was repaired using local TeX layout changes only. The repository renderer remains unchanged, so this issue tracks a reusable fix rather than treating the one-off artifact as a renderer repair.

Acceptance:

- Keep a complete explanatory paragraph with a short following declaration when it fits on a page. Preserve deliberate paragraph boundaries; avoid regexes that capture only the final line or split the code environment.
- Allow genuinely long declarations to break safely; do not solve short-block pagination by making every possible block unbreakable.
- Reserve sufficient vertical space for the full provenance/footer, including non-text code-box borders. Current text bounding boxes alone did not catch the contact.
- Use the checked [GSW security abstract](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/blob/a406f81f19d5cb9c7383cacc1ca37e3d82e60eae/ComplexityTests/Abstracts/GSWSecurityAbstract.lean) as a regression fixture, along with representative selected abstracts and a long-block case. Keep source text, declaration links, exact-revision provenance and source credit intact.
- Run the renderer tests and inspect every page of the representative generated PDFs. Record exact source and artifact revisions and independent visual review. Do not commit generated PDFs.

Likely scope: `scripts/build_abstracts.py`, `scripts/abstract_to_tex.py` and focused tests. No Lean theorem changes or catalogue promotion are required. AI-assisted finding from independent review by `/root/refactor_plan_review`. State: available; no implementation claim.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
blocked (`worker-claude-536-c4b0c164`): the change is committed locally (`0e840a89` on `ci/abstracts-deps-536`), but I can't push it. GitHub rejects workflow-file updates from the available OAuth token because it lacks the `workflow` scope. Next step: push once a credential with that scope is available (for example, after the maintainer runs `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow`). Then I'll open the PR and compare its CI artifact with the `formal-abstracts` release.

Findings:

- **What the renderer reads.** I mapped the recorded `pdflatex` inputs (`.fls`) of the full build and of the renderer test to packages with `dpkg -S`. They come only from `texlive-fonts-extra`, `texlive-latex-extra`, `texlive-plain-generic` (`binhex.tex`), `lmodern` (the renderer test only) and their dependencies. From `texlive-fonts-extra` it reads 82 files (about 3 MB): Libertine, newtxmath, Inconsolata/zi4 and mweights. The noble Contents index lists no other package that ships `libertine.sty`, `newtxmath.sty`, `zi4.sty` or `mweights.sty`, so the 629 MB package stays. `fonts-linuxlibertine` and `fonts-inconsolata` contain only OpenType, which would require a different engine.
- **Packages dropped.** Nothing uses `texlive-science`. Dropping it also removes `texlive-lang-greek`, `texlive-fonts-recommended` and the GFS fonts, which brings the runner download from 846 MB to about 758 MB. That alone can't avoid the timeouts: the slow runs fetched at 30–50 kB/s.
- **How often the install is slow.** In the last day, 5 of 54 build attempts used the full 30 minutes in the install step, and 4 more spent over 1000 s there before they were cancelled. The median install takes 111 s.
- **Fix.** Install the reduced set and cache the downloaded `.deb` archives with `actions/cache/restore` and `actions/cache/save`, pinned to v6.1.0's commit SHA. The cache key is a digest of the exact archive list from `apt-get --print-uris`, and an older cache is restored as a fallback. Only main (and manual dispatches) save; PRs read main's cache. apt still verifies every archive, and cache maintenance can't fail the build. The cost is about 760 MB in an Actions cache that the 2.5 GB Lean caches already keep above 10 GB.
- **Verification so far.** In a clean `ubuntu:24.04` container I ran the workflow's own step scripts as a sudo user, then the build. All 40 renderer tests passed with none skipped. Compared with the release built from `fe7bc578` at 150 dpi, all 69 pages are identical except for the 12-character source-SHA text on the 24 pages that show it. Extracted text, embedded fonts and all 232 link targets and rectangles also match once the SHA is normalised. The cache-restored install showed "Need to get 0 B/779 MB". It isn't faster than a fast mirror (about 90 s either way); what it removes is the dependence on the mirror's speed.

<details><summary>Patch (workflow and README)</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/abstracts.yml b/.github/workflows/abstracts.yml
index 1da65b62..3db11744 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/abstracts.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/abstracts.yml
@@ -29,18 +29,65 @@ jobs:
     timeout-minutes: 30
     outputs:
       artifact-id: ${{ steps.artifact.outputs.artifact-id }}
+    env:
+      # What pdflatex reads: Libertine, newtxmath, Inconsolata (zi4) and mweights from
+      # texlive-fonts-extra; tcolorbox, enumitem, xurl and titlesec from texlive-latex-extra;
+      # binhex.tex from texlive-plain-generic; and Latin Modern for the renderer test. Poppler's
+      # pdftotext checks margins.
+      TEX_PACKAGES: >-
+        latexmk lmodern texlive-latex-extra texlive-fonts-extra texlive-plain-generic poppler-utils
+      # The downloaded archives (about 760 MB) are cached so that runs do not depend on the speed
+      # of the Ubuntu mirror; apt still resolves them from its index and verifies their digests.
+      TEX_DEBS: /var/cache/tex-debs
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           persist-credentials: false
       - name: Validate the curated selection
         run: python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check
-      - name: Install PDF tooling and fonts
+      - name: Resolve PDF tooling packages
+        id: tex-debs
         run: |
           sudo apt-get update
+          sudo install -d -o "$USER" "$TEX_DEBS"
+          # The cache key names the exact archives (file, size, digest) that apt would download.
+          apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y -qq --print-uris \
+            -o Dir::Cache::Archives="$TEX_DEBS" $TEX_PACKAGES \
+            | awk '{print $2, $3, $4}' | sort > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tex-debs.txt"
+          test -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/tex-debs.txt"
+          echo "prefix=tex-debs-$ImageOS-" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "key=tex-debs-$ImageOS-$(sha256sum < "$RUNNER_TEMP/tex-debs.txt" | cut -c1-16)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+      - name: Restore cached TeX packages
+        id: tex-debs-cache
+        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
+        with:
+          path: /var/cache/tex-debs

- **What the renderer reads.** I mapped the recorded `pdflatex` inputs (`.fls`) of the full build and of the renderer test to packages with `dpkg -S`. They come only from `texlive-fonts-extra`, `texlive-latex-extra`, `texlive-plain-generic` (`binhex.tex`), `lmodern` (the renderer test only) and their dependencies. From `texlive-fonts-extra` it reads 82 files (about 3 MB): Libertine, newtxmath, Inconsolata/zi4 and mweights. The noble Contents index lists no other package that ships `libertine.sty`, `newtxmath.sty`, `zi4.sty` or `mweights.sty`, so the 629 MB package stays. `fonts-linuxlibertine` and `fonts-inconsolata` contain only OpenType, which would require a different engine.
- **Packages dropped.** Nothing uses `texlive-science`. Dropping it also removes `texlive-lang-greek`, `texlive-fonts-recommended` and the GFS fonts, which brings the runner download from 846 MB to about 758 MB. That alone can't avoid the timeouts: the slow runs fetched at 30–50 kB/s.
- **How often the install is slow.** In the last day, 5 of 54 build attempts used the full 30 minutes in the install step, and 4 more spent over 1000 s there before they were cancelled. The median install takes 111 s.
- **Fix.** Install the reduced set and cache the downloaded `.deb` archives with `actions/cache/restore` and `actions/cache/save`, pinned to v6.1.0's commit SHA. The cache key is a digest of the exact archive list from `apt-get --print-uris`, and an older cache is restored as a fallback. Only main (and manual dispatches) save; PRs read main's cache. apt still verifies every archive, and cache maintenance can't fail the build. The cost is about 760 MB in an Actions cache that the 2.5 GB Lean caches already keep above 10 GB.
- **Verification so far.** In a clean `ubuntu:24.04` container I ran the workflow's own step scripts as a sudo user, then the build. All 40 renderer tests passed with none skipped. Compared with the release built from `fe7bc578` at 150 dpi, all 69 pages are identical except for the 12-character source-SHA text on the 24 pages that show it. Extracted text, embedded fonts and all 232 link targets and rectangles also match once the SHA is normalised. The cache-restored install showed "Need to get 0 B/779 MB". title: feat(circuit): certify native generation of balanced circuit trees
body:
Part of shallow GSW decryption (#528) and the FHE recovery (#486). The existing `Circuit.balanced` preserves a precise half-split tree. Its semantic/depth results do not yet supply a uniform native generator of the complete serialized circuit. Reuse the circuit-code primitives in #531 / PR #534 and the full-code size bound from #526 / PR #542; the carry-save generators in #540 are the intended client.

Scope and completion criteria:

- Generate exactly `(Circuit.balanced op unit cs).code`, including the existing half-split topology. For five leaves this is `(ab)(c(de))`; an adjacent-pair round algorithm has a different tree, which matters for carry-save pairs.
- Require uniform native generation of op/unit and the complete leaf-code list (or a jointly native input/index generator with an efficient count). Input/output arities and list lengths may vary. No per-parameter finite-type shortcut or assumed construction-runtime bound.
- A private dynamic program over contiguous sublists in increasing length is an accepted implementation direction: prove agreement with the existing balanced fold, then the typed circuit. Keep the public interface small; do not introduce an unused generic recursion framework.
- Bound the complete encoded intermediate state, including all interval rows, framing, indices, current accumulator and captured codes. Derive bounds from the input generators and existing full-code size bounds. Circuit gate counts admit the bound `unit.size + sum leaf.size + k*op.size`.
- Exercise empty/nontrivial-unit, singleton/unused expensive op, three/five leaves, unequal/repeated leaf blocks, varying arities and zero-output circuits with dead gates. Include an unbounded-width native client, exact raw-code equality and axiom guards.
- Run all six repository checks and obtain independent API/correctness review of the final revision. Assess the formal abstract catalogue; record the remaining full #528 circuit work accurately.

A read-only independent design review found the private interval-table approach viable; it is not an implementation proof. No duplicate native balanced-fold task was found. AI-assisted task decomposition (OpenAI Codex).

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
`worker-claude-545-c4b0c164`: the predicate and bridges compile and are pushed. M2 batches can start from branch `refactor/plain-polytime-545` at `1780c5e5`. These names are final.

- `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut` in the new candidate module `Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.PolyTime` (imports only upstream cslib), with `ComputableInPolyTime.of_eq`, `.of_finite`, `.id'`, `.const`.
- In `…/Complexity/PolyTime/Plain.lean`:
  - `computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut ↔ ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut`
  - `ComputableInPolyTime.tidy` (plain → tidy), `ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy` and `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime` (tidy → plain)
  - `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInPolyTime`: a polynomial time bound alone suffices (plain analogue of `.computableTidilyInPolyTime`)
  - closure: `ComputableInPolyTime.polyBounded_length`, `.comp`, `.comp'`, `.pair`, `.prod`, `.fst`, `.snd`, `.ite'`

`ComputableInPolyTime` is `@[fun_prop]`-registered, and `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime` is a `fun_prop` transition rule, so `fun_prop` proves plain goals from plain hypotheses and from any tidy certificate. Typical migrations are `⟨f, .of_tidy h, …⟩` or `by fun_prop` for plain goals, and `hf.tidy` to feed a plain hypothesis to tidy-only rules. Next: `polytime` support, the convention note, tests.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Finding from #546 (`worker-claude-546-c4b0c164`): `fun_prop` on a plain goal can fail where the tidy goal succeeds, when a composition needs an intermediate encoding. Example, on `d57db0ef`:

```lean
example : ComputableInPolyTime (fun w : List Bool => w.tail.headD false) encBits encBool := by
  fun_prop  -- fails: picks `encList encBool` for `w.tail` via the generic `headD` rule
```

The tidy goal is proved by `fun_prop`, and the plain goal by `polytime` or `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`. A similar case is `TQBFCNF_mem_PSPACE` (`QBF.rounds` after unfolding encodings). In #546 I used `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)` at these sites (two tests, one library proof). Not blocking for #546.

title: refactor(api): add plain polynomial-time computability with tidy bridges
body:
Milestone M1 of #456: a plain polynomial-time predicate that definitions and public statements can use, with tidy bridges so proofs keep the existing automation.

**Scope**
- Define `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut := ∃ t s : ℕ → ℕ, Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded t ∧ Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded s ∧ ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength f encIn encOut t s`. This is the form both abstract bridges already use. It depends only on upstream cslib declarations, so put it in a new `-- upstream: candidate` module that could be submitted without `crei/tidy-universal`. The vendored `PolyTime.lean` must not grow.
- In the local companion `PolyTime/Plain.lean`, add bridges both ways: an iff with `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, plus one-step `.tidy` / `.of_tidy`-style shortcuts. Also record "polynomial time alone suffices" for a plain machine as a lemma. Names follow Mathlib conventions; propose them in the PR.
- Transport the basic closure API (identity, composition, pairing/`ite` as used by class proofs) and decide whether to `@[fun_prop]`-register the plain predicate. The design commitment is that computability predicates stay automatable. Show a before/after client: a public `ComputableInPolyTime` goal discharged directly, or through one bridge rewrite.
- Document the convention (M5): tidy notions are proof devices; definitions and public results use plain computability.

**Out of scope:** changing any class or reduction definition (M2 batches); plain space/`O` counterparts (M1b); switching the abstract bridges (waits for #497 to avoid conflicting with #497/#541).

**Done when:** the six gates pass, `ComplexityTests` covers the bridges and a nonvacuous client, and the M2 batches can start from this branch.

title: feat(api): register plain resource notions with fun_prop
body:
Follow-up to #551 / #555 (M1b of #456). The design commitments say computability predicates are `@[fun_prop]`-registered. #554 does this for `ComputableInPolyTime`. The plain resource notions added in #555 are not registered yet, so a plain goal has to go through `.tidy`/`.of_tidy` by hand.

**Scope**
- In `Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolySpace/Plain.lean`, mirroring #554's `PolyTime/Plain.lean`:
  - `attribute [fun_prop] ComputableInPolySpace`.
  - `@[fun_prop]` on `ComputableTidilyInPolySpace.computableInPolySpace` as the tidy-to-plain transition rule.
  - Plain closure rules proved through `.tidy`, matching the tidy set at `PolySpace.lean:143` (`of_polyTime`, `id'`, `prod`, `ite`, `comp'`).
  - `of_polyTime` takes #554's `ComputableInPolyTime`.
- Optional, same pattern: `ComputableInFPTTime` in `Parameterized.lean`, with `ite` and composition along a parameter bound. `ComputableInO`/`ComputableInSpace` carry explicit bounds, so they are less natural `fun_prop` targets; register them only if a consumer needs it.

**Consumers.** These are the M3 restatements of polynomial-space results that build deciders compositionally today with tidy `fun_prop`/combinators:
- `setOf_exists_mem_PSPACE`, `mem_PSPACE_iff_computableTidilyInPolySpace` and `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PSPACE` (`Classes/Inclusions.lean`)
- `Classes/Counting/Space.lean`, `Classes/SharpP/Space.lean`
- `Classes/IP/PSPACE.lean`, `Classes/IP/Simulation.lean`
- `Classes/Space/TM2.lean`

**Done when:** a plain `ComputableInPolySpace` goal built from plain and tidy parts closes by `fun_prop`, with a test client, and the six gates pass.

Depends on #555 and #554.

title: perf(polytime): make fun_prop fail fast and cover common plain/tidy mixes
body:
Follow-up from #456 (found while migrating classes in #557): automation around the plain `ComputableInPolyTime` (#554) has three rough edges that make migrated proofs worse than they should be.

1. **Slow failure.** `by fun_prop` on a *tidy* goal, given only *plain* hypotheses, runs to the heartbeat limit instead of failing quickly. This happened in `Classes/WPP/Robustness.lean` and `Classes/WPP/TwoSided.lean`. Plain→tidy can't be a `fun_prop` transition rule without creating a cycle, so the search should fail fast rather than explore.
2. **Tidy-only rules don't accept plain hypotheses.** Verifier combinators such as `selectVerifier`, `andVerifier` and `orVerifier` need `hV.tidy` or `mem_X_iff_tidy.mp` first.
3. **Plain goals `fun_prop` can't decompose.** Two arithmetic or test shapes still need `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`: the threshold `3 * (k a * 2 ^ q n)` in `inter_mem_SBP_of_mem_BPP`, and the `sharpTest` verifier in `Classes/Toda.lean`.

**Done when:** (1) has a minimal reproducer and either fails fast, for example with a `fun_prop` discharger or config, or is documented with the recommended pattern; (2) and (3) are either covered by a small set of plain rules or documented in `PolyTime/Plain.lean`, each with a test. Before/after examples should come from the files above.

title: refactor(toda): clarify the parity sign convention and move a word-counting lemma to WordCount
body:
Two small clarity fixes from a source-only quality review (at `fe7bc578`), checked against current `main`. Neither changes a theorem statement.

1. **Toda's sign convention.** The introduction of `Classes/Toda/Counting.lean` describes Toda's amplifier as giving `-1` modulo `2^K` on odd counts, then presents the identity the module actually implements, `[c odd] = ∑ i < c, (-2)^i * choose c (i + 1)`, which gives `+1`. The proofs and regression example consistently use `+1`. Say explicitly that this module uses the `+1` convention, and how it relates to Toda's `-1` amplifier.
2. **Placement of `card_filter_take_drop`.** This general lemma counts words satisfying independent prefix and suffix conditions, yet it lives in `Classes/ValiantVazirani/Reduction.lean:551`. `Toda/Counting.lean` (via `ValiantVazirani.card_filter_take_drop`) and `Toda/Isolation.lean` import the Valiant–Vazirani development partly for it. Move it to `Complexity/Foundations/Data/BitString/WordCount.lean`, in the `Cslib.BitString` namespace per AGENTS.md rule 6, and leave a deprecated alias at the old name. Also check whether `ZPP.lean`'s private `card_filter_take_drop` (line ~153; a different but related statement) can be derived from the moved lemma.

**Done when:** the docstring distinguishes the conventions; the lemma has a foundational home with a deprecated alias; the Toda modules import `WordCount` directly where that is now enough; the six gates pass. This makes no build-speed claim.

Available. Found by a peer quality review relayed to `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

title: perf(build): reduce cache invalidation from growing hub modules
body:
Build caches, both Lake's local artifact cache and CI, are invalidated mostly by growth of a few widely imported general-purpose modules. Under the module system, proof-only edits don't rebuild dependents, but adding *any* declaration to a module changes its public interface, and every module downstream rebuilds even when none of them uses the new declaration.

Measured on `main` (`ba134c18`), counting 1,850 library modules: downstream modules (transitive importers) × edits in the last four days.

| Module | Downstream | Edits |
|---|---|---|
| `Foundations/Data/List/Basic` | 550 | 14 |
| `Foundations/Data/BitString/List` | 462 | 9 |
| `Probability/PMF` | 455 | 8 |
| `Foundations/Data/BitString/Basic` | 689 | 3 |
| `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Plain` | 387 | 4 |

Each `List/Basic` addition invalidates about 30% of the library.

**Plan (separate PRs):**
1. **Guidance.** Amend AGENTS.md "Placement and reuse": place new general lemmas in the lowest suitable *narrow* module (a small topic file imported by its consumers), not by appending to a widely imported hub. Mention the `@[expose]` cost as well: exposed definition bodies are part of the interface.
2. **Split `Foundations/Data/List/Basic`** into topic modules. Keep `List/Basic` as a thin re-export for compatibility, and repoint the heavy consumers to the narrow modules. Record the before/after downstream counts in the PR.
3. Then do the same for `BitString/List` and `Probability/PMF`, if (2) shows a real reduction.

**Done when:** the guidance has landed, and each split PR shows reduced downstream fan-out for typical additions, with declaration names preserved (re-export or deprecated aliases) and the six gates passing. This is infrastructure, not mathematics; it makes no claim about build speed beyond the measured fan-out.

Available. Analysis by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` at Samuel's request.

body:
The four-module split is supported by recent interface churn, not just hypothetical fan-out. I inspected `git log -p` at exact base `ba134c185f6b76f68bd31c3a6b89abe8afd0f3c6` over the four days ending at #569 creation: **2026-10-19 22:03:28 UTC through 2026-10-23 22:03:28 UTC**. There are 14 non-merge commits touching `List/Basic`, plus three merge resolutions.

| Commit | Proposed destination | Change within `List/Basic` |
|---|---|---|
| `ca7a33d1` | Lookup | Add `map_range_eq_ofFn`; proof-only OfFn import accompanies it |
| `4c1fcab8` | Append | Add `zip_tail_append_cons` |
| `946f5a4b` | Lookup | Add `getD_map_range` |
| `0e84efe6` | Counting | Move `countP_and_not_add_countP_and` into the module |
| `98c81881` | Lookup | Add shared `getD_idxOf` |
| `b198618a` | Fold | Extract `foldl_take_invariant` |
| `c9072f50` | Append | Add both unary-delimiter injectivity lemmas; preserve source credit |
| `dcbc89d8` | Lookup | Add shared `getD_mem_or` |
| `ca2f92a5` | Lookup | Rename `forall_mem_set` to `forall_mem_set_of_forall_mem` |
| `ad887c0f` | Lookup | Add four shared register-file lemmas |
| `f6d09f5d` | Counting | Move/generalize `decide_mem_eq_any` into the module |
| `51944df4` | Counting / existing OfFn home | Remove `countP_range_eq_card_filter` from Basic and move it to `List/OfFn`; narrow public imports |
| `4ac8dd31` | Counting | Add shared `length_flatMap_le` |
| `e078395c` | Counting / later OfFn home | Initially place `countP_range_eq_card_filter` here |

Classification: **Lookup 6, Counting 5, Append 2, Fold 1**. Twelve commits add or relocate public theorem declarations into this module; one renames a public declaration and one removes/relocates one. None of these fourteen is merely a proof-body edit or an exposed-definition-body change. They are interface-affecting source categories, not fourteen separately measured rebuilds. `countP_range_eq_card_filter` was temporary here and is already in `OfFn` at the base; the split will not move it back.

The three merges are not counted again as independent additions: `bfb7529a` unions the Counting additions; `efefbe75` resolves Counting's relocation against Lookup's new register lemmas; `b70ae996` unions Counting's membership lemma with Lookup's register lemmas. `git show --remerge-diff` confirms these combine existing branch work; the latter two span groups. No non-merge edit in this window spans the proposed groups.

Only one of fourteen non-merge interface edits is Fold, so Fold's remaining **530/563** downstream reach is a real limitation but does not dominate this observed window. The spread supports four coherent modules while avoiding the original nine-file navigation cost. Current-graph reach and this history are separate evidence; neither establishes historical wall-time savings or actual cache invalidations.

Reproduce the history with:

```sh
git log ba134c185f6b76f68bd31c3a6b89abe8afd0f3c6 --no-merges \
  --since='2026-10-19T22:03:28Z' --until='2026-10-23T22:03:28Z' -p \
  -- Complexity/Foundations/Data/List/Basic.lean
```

No source edits have been made; the integration-order gate remains in effect.
