author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Worker audit_prerequisites completed the bounded READ-ONLY preparation on exact public source dfe3ca3c62edae28a2cc28db31e664eb403853d3. No builds, cache/worktree/source edits or PR were made; this does not re-review #810 mathematics.

The exact six public contracts, all in Cslib.GenericRAM.BoundedNat (Native/Nat.lean:77–129), differ from the desired plain statements only in the predicate:

| Name | Uniform input/output encoding and function |
| --- | --- |
| constant_polyTime (c : ℕ) | model.checkedConstant c : ℕ → Option ℕ; encNat → encOption encNat |
| operation_polyTime (op : model.operations.Op) | model.checkedOp op; encPair encNat (encPi encNat) → encOption encNat |
| test_polyTime (t : model.tests.Op) | fun p => model.evalTest p.1 t p.2; encPair encNat (encPi encNat) → encOption encBool |
| address_polyTime | fun p => model.address p.1 p.2; encPair encNat encNat → encOption encNat |
| validMove_polyTime | fun p => model.validMove p.1 p.2; encPair encNat encNat → encBool |
| validPC_polyTime | fun p => model.validPC p.1 p.2; encPair encNat encNat → encBool |

The model remains the exact exclusive runtime bound, fixed Unit symbols with Fin 2 argument vectors, binary values/addresses/configuration, distinct none versus some false, and rejection at bound zero. Only constant_polyTime and operation_polyTime currently have program_certificate; preserve those exact registrations and every binder/name.

**Callers and duplication.** Exact-name search finds no direct source call to these six outside Native/Nat. Each is used once in nativePrimitives and once in nativePrimitives_isPolynomial: those are the twelve repeated unpack/rebound/erase terms at 133–183. Downstream bundle consumers include GenericRAMNative's six polynomiality checks, its addressAccepted composition/time-rfl check at 61–66, and GenericRAMSimulation's inflated constant certificate time/space additions at 163–165. GenericRAMNative also has the named raw checkedOp/checkedConstant `polytime` controls at 73–76; retain their original tactics/budgets and test the intended explicit-raw path when implementation is authorized. They are implicit registration consumers, not direct theorem-name references.

**Lowest existing rules and the genuine direct gap.** Plain core comp/prod/fst/snd/const/of_eq/ite_decide already suffice for the structural proof. Direct pi_apply (Internal/PolyTimePiPrimitives:96) handles fixed Fin 2 arguments, including its existing empty-domain semantics; optionSome is direct in Internal/PolyTimeOptionPrimitives:35. However, at this pin binary_add and binary_lt in PolyTime/Nat/Binary:293/351 are still high-level ComputableTidilyInPolyTime rules. I found no direct plain polynomial-time counterpart for either. The bare existing word-add/bit-position comparison algorithms can supply a later direct shared slice without changing algorithms, but that is a separate primitive implementation, not a fact established here. Internal/BinaryComparison.natLt is not a polynomial-time substitute: its time is `(p.1+1)*(encodedPairLength+1)^2`; numeric p.1 may be exponential in its binary encoding. Likewise the older LinearSpaceArith.natAdd has a numeric-operand time factor and is itself raw. Do not silently use those bounds to assert binary PT.

**Smallest honest implementation plan.** After actual #810 squash: change the six public predicates to plain, reuse the existing direct structural rules, and replace the twelve repackagings by the six `ofPolyTime (…_polyTime …)` fields plus matching `ofPolyTime_isPolynomial` calls. To make their derivations genuinely S4-direct, first provide/reuse the exact plain binary_add and polynomial binary_lt certificates from the existing word algorithms in the shared canonical arithmetic source. A transitional `.of_tidy` view of the two existing complete raw scalar certificates would remove the public tidy surface/duplication, but would *not* close that direct-primitive S4 gap; it must be labelled as such, not presented as the direct solution. No new Native abstraction or public converter is needed.

**Data-preservation obligation, stronger than proposition equivalence.** Keep NativeCertificate.ofPolyTime, exists_polynomial and ofTimeAndSpace unchanged. Each old manual term already has exactly `ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut`, as does its replacement. body:
Worker `review_559`, independent READ-ONLY source diagnosis of2edfe545/28dbad2b/d4010419; no builds, edits, new rule or mathematical/API approval. Reused [controlled evidence6405980546](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6405980546).

**Goal modes matter.** LiuPass256 is the LIBRARY `OneWay/LiuPass.lean` preparation proof (not the unrelated test file's line256): `hprep : ComputableInPolyTime … encBits := by …; fun_prop`, with unary input arithmetic. CookLevinPolyTime57 is likewise a bare `fun_prop` proof of an explicit PlainPT constructor with arbitrary encoded input and CNF output. Consequently a fix confined to `polytimeRawFromPlain`'s explicit-raw eligibility cannot resolve the entire blocker: neither of these entry scripts calls `polytime` or starts as RawPT. PseudoentropyLearning109 starts as IsPPTOn; its existing `isPPTOn_extractLabels_list` named route asks for PLAIN hhash/hsamples with the full captured pair encoding. Source alone does not establish which alternate branch actually exhausts that goal, so I do not label its timeout “raw mirror work” without the pending trace.

**What the installed FunProp actually supports.** `Mathlib/Tactic/FunProp/Theorems.lean` recognizes uncurried and compositional function rules. The28db captured `binary_add'` is a legitimate compositional form and avoids the bare rule's uncurrying/decomposition on LiuPass, as the measured result confirms. But `Core.getDeclTheorems` sorts FUNCTION entries by applied-argument distance, then number of main arguments; it does NOT use the stored FunctionTheorem.priority. `tryTheorems` tries compositional rules directly and uncurried rules through decomposition/comp. Attribute.add does not parse a custom priority, and erasure is explicitly unimplemented. Thus a speculative low-priority attribute or reordering folklore is not a supported fix. Tactic config/dischargers/unfold lists do not provide an unchanged-script rule-selection switch either.

**Bounded recommendation.** Do not ship28db as green: it fixes LiuPass but the two original failures remain. The ONLY currently executed all-three-green integration is d401: retain direct binary_add as a named/unregistered primitive, with direct composition/product available, and retain binary_lt's existing registration. That is an honest *named primitive* scope, not fulfillment of the proposed automatic-addition contract. If delivery requires automatic binary addition, keep that obligation open and retain the original automatic fixtures/budgets; do not silently rewrite them to named proofs. Audit is already running the one authorized exact-branch trace, without production changes. Use its first deciding branch to choose any bounded encoding/selection correction; a supported compositional shape alone has already been disproved as sufficient by28db.

The distinction is important: named-only is the smallest causally established non-regressing configuration, while an automatic-all-clients fix has NOT been established. A raw-goal fallback change, global raw transition, encoding preference/blacklist, new specialized family, priority trick or budget increase is not justified by the present evidence. No claim of non-PPT/noncomputability follows from a search timeout. Direct addition/comparison mathematics, original statements/algorithms/encodings and all tests remain untouched by this diagnosis.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Bounded diagnostic completed by worker audit_prerequisites; production remains **28dbad2b**. No engine, theorem, test, budget or registration change was made in this phase. Worker 559 received the exact paths and first divergence points; all jobs are terminal.

**Inputs and method.** I compared captured registration 28dbad2b with named-only d4010419 on separate diagnostic branches/private outputs. CookLevinPolyTime and PseudoentropyLearning have identical Git blobs across these heads (`f2cee4ee…` and `12ab97d5…`). All four full-source trace copies match those exact original files after removing ONLY command-local FunProp/Aesop trace and diagnostics options. Imports, statements, scripts and original 200000 heartbeats are unchanged; no producer fixture was added. Named-only import outputs were refreshed from the exact eight original direct imports before tracing. An initial unsupported `trace.aesop.steps` setup was corrected to the registered `trace.aesop`; conclusions below use only clean final logs.

**CookLevin: a genuine PLAIN search branch, not an explicit raw-goal mirror.** The original line57 begins as bare `fun_prop` on PlainPT of relabel(initClauses(parameters…)). The trace decomposes relabel/initClauses and speculates that the parameter has **encNat** through the pre-existing binary_mul' rule. At captured trace lines125/130, HAdd candidates are unary_succ, new binary_add', unary_add; named-only has unary_succ/unary_add. The new captured rule extends that binary arithmetic branch inside a size expression needed by the unary constructor interface. Ordinary FunProp later tries its legacy Raw→Plain transition on some unsuccessful plain atoms; that is not #810's explicit-raw-entry mirror. Thus gating only raw-goal mirror work cannot remove the first deciding plain branch.

Tracing itself is material here: BOTH traced CookLevin copies hit the unchanged200k cap. Therefore these traces establish mode/candidate selection, **not** a traced named-only success or a cost ranking. The earlier untraced controlled A/B remains the actual acceptance evidence: captured fails, named-only passes at original200k. No budget was raised to get a more convenient trace.

**Learning: the deciding branch is entirely PLAIN/PPT encoding inference.** The target is IsPPTOn; extractLabels_list asks for plain callback and sample certificates. Its shared label encoding starts as `?label`. Captured Aesop trace G11 (line1194) asks for PlainPT `word.length+1` with that encoding unresolved; the sample branch later has G18 fixed to **encNat** (1667). Safe polytimeFunPropFast (1728) closes it using new binary_add' (1761). The sibling callback is then fixed at input `encList encNat` but must return **encUnary**: its headD branch fails (1986). There are **zero RawPT or rawFromPlain occurrences anywhere in either clean Learning trace**. This is not evidence for an explicit raw mirror failure.

In named-only Learning, the binary +1 branch cannot close; search eventually chooses **encUnary** for the shared label encoding (2630). The same callback headD then closes (2788), and the traced run exits0 at the unchanged budget. The problem is a prematurely committed encoding choice across sample/callback premises, not a missing mathematical equality. In particular, a uniform callback converting arbitrary binary-encoded Nat labels to unary would not have the same polynomial resource contract; that is not a valid substitute for choosing the correct label encoding.

**Decision boundary.** No production fix is proposed as already validated. The existing direct mathematics remains focused-pass, and named-only publication could be an explicitly limited milestone, but pair/captured automation and the two original controls remain promised acceptance work. I made no priority/order patch, new helper family, test rewrite, raw fallback or full-gate rerun. matching_paragraphs: **Inputs and method.** I compared captured registration 28dbad2b with named-only d4010419 on separate diagnostic branches/private outputs. Named-only import outputs were refreshed from the exact eight original direct imports before tracing. An initial unsupported `trace.aesop.steps` setup was corrected to the registered `trace.aesop`; conclusions below use only clean final logs.

**CookLevin: a genuine PLAIN search branch, not an explicit raw-goal mirror.** The original line57 begins as bare `fun_prop` on PlainPT of relabel(initClauses(parameters…)). The trace decomposes relabel/initClauses and speculates that the parameter has **encNat** through the pre-existing binary_mul' rule. At captured trace lines125/130, HAdd candidates are unary_succ, new binary_add', unary_add; named-only has unary_succ/unary_add. The new captured rule extends that binary arithmetic branch inside a size expression needed by the unary constructor interface. Ordinary FunProp later tries its legacy Raw→Plain transition on some unsuccessful plain atoms; that is not #810's explicit-raw-entry mirror. Thus gating only raw-goal mirror work cannot remove the first deciding plain branch.

**Learning: the deciding branch is entirely PLAIN/PPT encoding inference.** The target is IsPPTOn; extractLabels_list asks for plain callback and sample certificates. Its shared label encoding starts as `?label`. Captured Aesop trace G11 (line1194) asks for PlainPT `word.length+1` with that encoding unresolved; the sample branch later has G18 fixed to **encNat** (1667). Safe polytimeFunPropFast (1728) closes it using new binary_add' (1761). The sibling callback is then fixed at input `encList encNat` but must return **encUnary**: its headD branch fails (1986). There are **zero RawPT or rawFromPlain occurrences anywhere in either clean Learning trace**. This is not evidence for an explicit raw mirror failure.

In named-only Learning, the binary +1 branch cannot close; search eventually chooses **encUnary** for the shared label encoding (2630). The same callback headD then closes (2788), and the traced run exits0 at the unchanged budget. The problem is a prematurely committed encoding choice across sample/callback premises, not a missing mathematical equality. In particular, a uniform callback converting arbitrary binary-encoded Nat labels to unary would not have the same polynomial resource contract; that is not a valid substitute for choosing the correct label encoding.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Read-only S4 codec plan, worker review_560, pinned actual main **43d1e5729dc0f66ae087275c9aa77b76a6c73701**. No source/package edits or builds. Claim: https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6407160515 . Open PRs inspected: #1145 touches only Native/Nat + baseline; #1113 touches legacy PolyTime/List and callers, so coordinate its List facade hunk when integrating. No competing codec-field task found. This is planning, not field-change approval or S4 completion.

**Exact remaining contract.** `MultiTape/Combinators/Encoding.lean:179–234` owns all three **Prop** classes. PairEncoding has `pair`, `fst`, `snd`; OptionEncoding has `none_eq`, `some`, `getD d`; ListEncoding has `headD d`, `tail`, `isEmpty`. The seven linear operation capabilities (two Pair, two Option, three List) use `ComputableTidilyInLinearTimeAndSpace`. Pair `pair` instead accepts TWO exact tidy `(t,s)` witnesses and returns ∃c with time `c*(t+1)` and space `c*(s+encodedPairLength+1)`; `pair_mono` retains independent summed time/workspace formulas. `none_eq` is an encoder equality and must stay unchanged. Sources and concrete instances in Encodings/{Basic,Pair,List,Option} are locally vendored Christian Reitwiessner crei/tidy-universal @7f7c0696 (encOfEquiv @9cce4cc7); retain that credit/upstream correspondence. Current cslib package is pinned 6ff325e8; this is local vendored code, not a request to edit that package.

**Data distinction.** These capability classes contain propositions, not selected constants/machines/clock functions. Linear c and machine/state/k live under existential propositions. Replacing a capability proof can choose another c/machine without changing encPair/encList/encBits/encOption or any transducer program. It does NOT prove equal selected witnesses or `Classical.choose` data. Any consumer exposing selected time/space data needs its own definitional/observational check, as Native/Nat did; predicate equivalence alone is insufficient. Preserve the pair formulas above literally, not an exact same-machine/same-c assertion.

**Existing lower support.** `ResourceBounds:123` already defines plain Linear with exactly ∃c, exact plain TS at common `c*(inputLength+1)` bounds. `Internal/NormalForm.linear` returns a bare tidy machine at another existential common linear constant. `NormalForm.bigO` supports INDEPENDENT T/S without an output premise: its proof caps workspace by `min(s,k*t+k)` before cleanup. Thus there is no missing independent-bound normalization theorem. `Internal/LinearPrimitives` already has direct transducer/frame/unframe/dropFrame/of_eq/const/of_finite/comp; LinearPairPrimitives directly proves STANDARD framed fst/snd. Generic field consumers must not silently specialize to that standard encoding.

**Actual consumers.** Internal/{DegreePrimitives,DegreeOptionPrimitives,DecoderPrimitives,BinaryPrimitives,PolyTimeListLookup,PolyTimeListPrimitives,PolyTimeNatFrontends,PolyTimePiPrimitives} currently unpack codec witnesses and erase bare tidiness; PolyTimePrimitives.pair normalizes its plain callbacks then calls the tidy `PairEncoding.pair_mono`. Loops/map/lookup import these transitively. Legacy consumers also exist in Degree/Lists/InSpace/Streaming/PreparePair/Universal and the List/Option facades. Merely changing concrete instance proofs leaves `Combinators.Encoding`'s public Append/Ite/raw-linear imports in the closure, so proof-only instance replacement does NOT accomplish S4.

**Smallest coherent implementation proposal (not implemented).** Separate the existing encBool definition + SAME named classes from the high-level tidy closure module into a lower canonical codec capability home, preserving universe/instance scopes; no parallel classes/alias. Change seven linear capability propositions to plain Linear, and pairing/pair_mono to plain exact TS premises/conclusion with the SAME displayed ∃c formulas. Build instances from the unchanged frame/head/isEmpty machines. For pairing, normalize the supplied independent plain TS witnesses through existing bare NormalForm.bigO, run the EXISTING frame/append kernel, then erase tidiness; constants may grow inside ∃c but T/S remain independent and output charge stays exactly where stated. The direct Linear wrappers for headT/isEmptyT and subtype-restricted empty/default choice, plus direct linear append/ite/restrict support, are currently absent from LinearPrimitives: expose only those actually required, from existing bare machines/combinators. This is a missing convenient plain leaf/composition interface, not a missing machine algorithm. Keep raw closure compatibility internal or retire callers during the same join, rather than reimporting it into the new codec home. Coordinate the extraction carefully: LinearPrimitives already imports low NormalForm/ResourceBounds, so the new class home must not import a provider that imports its instances.

**Acceptance before delivery.** Compare pure encoder/transducer definitions byte-for-byte and exposed formulas/telescopes structurally; enumerate all instances and generic callers. Cover arbitrary/nonfinite element types, arbitrary PairEncoding/ListEncoding, captured inputs, independent T/S, empty/default cases, malformed frame all-word laws, missing capabilities/callback negatives and instance synthesis. Recheck original Decoder/Native/Step/list lookup clients; inspect any choice-selected resource data with actual identity tests rather than proof equivalence. Add import-closure checks rejecting high tidy Linear/TS calculus in the direct codec/provider closure while allowing bare Internal kernel normalization. Use a fresh native inventory/ratchet with decreases only after coherent source compiles; do not infer counts from this read-only scan. Reuse #810 field72/semantic73 and #1119 frame-machine reviews; new public capability types still require bounded outside review. No new normalizer/converter/model or package mutation is indicated.

**Exact remaining contract.** `MultiTape/Combinators/Encoding.lean:179–234` owns all three **Prop** classes. PairEncoding has `pair`, `fst`, `snd`; OptionEncoding has `none_eq`, `some`, `getD d`; ListEncoding has `headD d`, `tail`, `isEmpty`. The seven linear operation capabilities (two Pair, two Option, three List) use `ComputableTidilyInLinearTimeAndSpace`. Pair `pair` instead accepts TWO exact tidy `(t,s)` witnesses and returns ∃c with time `c*(t+1)` and space `c*(s+encodedPairLength+1)`; `pair_mono` retains independent summed time/workspace formulas. `none_eq` is an encoder equality and must stay unchanged. Sources and concrete instances in Encodings/{Basic,Pair,List,Option} are locally vendored Christian Reitwiessner crei/tidy-universal @7f7c0696 (encOfEquiv @9cce4cc7); retain that credit/upstream correspondence. Current cslib package is pinned 6ff325e8; this is local vendored code, not a request to edit that package.

**Existing lower support.** `ResourceBounds:123` already defines plain Linear with exactly ∃c, exact plain TS at common `c*(inputLength+1)` bounds. `Internal/NormalForm.linear` returns a bare tidy machine at another existential common linear constant. `NormalForm.bigO` supports INDEPENDENT T/S without an output premise: its proof caps workspace by `min(s,k*t+k)` before cleanup. Thus there is no missing independent-bound normalization theorem. `Internal/LinearPrimitives` already has direct transducer/frame/unframe/dropFrame/of_eq/const/of_finite/comp; LinearPairPrimitives directly proves STANDARD framed fst/snd. Generic field consumers must not silently specialize to that standard encoding.

**Actual consumers.** Internal/{DegreePrimitives,DegreeOptionPrimitives,DecoderPrimitives,BinaryPrimitives,PolyTimeListLookup,PolyTimeListPrimitives,PolyTimeNatFrontends,PolyTimePiPrimitives} currently unpack codec witnesses and erase bare tidiness; PolyTimePrimitives.pair normalizes its plain callbacks then calls the tidy `PairEncoding.pair_mono`. Loops/map/lookup import these transitively. Legacy consumers also exist in Degree/Lists/InSpace/Streaming/PreparePair/Universal and the List/Option facades. Merely changing concrete instance proofs leaves `Combinators.Encoding`'s public Append/Ite/raw-linear imports in the closure, so proof-only instance replacement does NOT accomplish S4.

**Acceptance before delivery.** Compare pure encoder/transducer definitions byte-for-byte and exposed formulas/telescopes structurally; enumerate all instances and generic callers. Cover arbitrary/nonfinite element types, arbitrary PairEncoding/ListEncoding, captured inputs, independent T/S, empty/default cases, malformed frame all-word laws, missing capabilities/callback negatives and instance synthesis. Recheck original Decoder/Native/Step/list lookup clients; inspect any choice-selected resource data with actual identity tests rather than proof equivalence. Add import-closure checks rejecting high tidy Linear/TS calculus in the direct codec/provider closure while allowing bare Internal kernel normalization. Use a fresh native inventory/ratchet with decreases only after coherent source compiles; do not infer counts from this read-only scan. body:
Read-only result at codec **6df5e5e7a25de8668b9e001fde94632a07c5c682**: the smallest coherent next cut is a **fixed-machine fold compiler**, not another existential tidy closure layer. No source/build/cache changes or math re-audit were performed.

The remaining route is `Internal/PolyTimePrimitives.foldl:173–220 → Combinators/Foldl → {Comp, Encoding, IterateWhile}`. `Internal/OLoops.foldl:52–115` independently uses the same raw-TS fold. Thus moving only the PT import, or renaming `Foldl.BigO`, would not remove the dependency.

1. **Lower the existing loop machine, preserving its data.** Extract `IterateWhile` tape embeddings/state words, `iterateWhileRound`, public `MultiTapeTM.iterateWhile`, tape-transform proofs and `computesTidily_iterateWhile` (through line286) into an Internal kernel module; retain their qualified names, visibility, program bodies and formulas through the original facade. Keep the two existential `ComputableTidily…iterateWhile` theorems in the legacy facade. `CopyWord` contains only machine/data/run facts but imports the higher `TidyZeroSpace` facade: redirect that dependency to existing `Internal/KernelZeroSpace` (which already owns `tidyCopy`). Preserve `loadWord/copyWord/emitWord` and their tape-transform laws; no new counter or loop algorithm. Existing `RepeatUntilBlank`, `OnWords`, `KernelComp`, `KernelIte` and `Internal.conditional` provide the bare operations.

2. **Reassemble the existing fold at witness level under Internal.** Keep the pure `Foldl.arg/next/foldStep/rounds/roundCost` equations and reachable-prefix proof, with their current private scope (they are not exposed public APIs). Replace the private higher `Foldl.BigO` mini-calculus and `bigO_foldStep` applications with direct supplied-machine assembly: normalize the plain codec projection/head/tail/empty/some/getD witnesses once, use the plain pair capability plus normal form for the *same complete encoded pair*, fixed-machine comp and conditional, then the extracted iterate-while run theorem. Return a finite machine witness and its fixed-machine run law, not a new `ComputableTidily…` interface or public conversion. Do not move the higher `BigO` helper unchanged into Internal and call that deletion.

The required compiler contract is exactly the existing fold contract: common-input list/init time `t`, workspace `s`; callback time `tStep` and independent workspace `sStep`; `htMax/hsMax` only at `i < list.length`; complete encoded remaining-list/accumulator state bound at every `i ≤ list.length`. Return one uniform machine with time `c*(t+(length+1)*(tMax+lMax+1))` and space `c*(s+sMax+lMax+1)`, plus complete output equality. Preserve empty input/element cases without adding inhabitance. Final output fits the retained final-state bound; do not infer output≤workspace for an arbitrary uncharged machine or replace independent space by time.

3. **Switch only the direct callers first.** `Internal/PolyTimePrimitives.foldl` already normalizes its three plain inputs; consume those bare witnesses directly. Keep its arbitrary encodings and same-universe Type-u telescope, polynomial `L`, and separate list-length, callback-argument and complete-state bounds. `Internal/PolyTimeLoops` then retains `foldl'`, `foldlWith`, spec/growth and iterate families unchanged: the captured callback is `(reader × accumulator) × element`, reader is computed uniformly, and prefix/member bounds are not all-state bounds. `Internal/OLoops.foldl/foldlWith` must preserve the current exact exposed charged-O formulas: time `Tl+Ti+(length+1)*(R+B+encodedListLength)` and space `Sl+Si+Q+B+encodedListLength`, with the existing full-output charge. This is not a numeric-time/unary materialization shortcut.

Do not import these legacy facades back into the new direct closure. Original `Combinators/Foldl` remains a legacy facade until callers collapse, not a second shipped plain API.

**Data and namespace obligations.** Public `iterateWhile` and lower word-movement machine definitions are data: move bodies literally, preserving qualified names, tape/state layouts and all fixed-machine resource formulas; proposition equivalence is insufficient. Existing PT/O fold conclusions are propositions with existential witnesses, not exposed chosen Native data, so no old/new chosen-machine equality is claimed. Any downstream chosen data depending on a moved public definition needs kernel `rfl` checks. Pair capability is plain TS with the real pair-space allowance; preserve the bound at that exact use rather than assuming tidy normalization selects the same existential machine. No new helper family/alias/codec redesign is needed by source inspection. Compiler sufficiency remains unbuilt, so a proof-level kernel gap may still emerge.

The fully paginated open-PR inventory found #1146 is the live same-file predecessor (`Foldl`, `PolyTimePrimitives`, `Comp`); #869 is the preserved diagnostic spike, and #1113 edits the higher List facade, not this kernel. Reconcile whichever lands first; do not widen #1146. body:
Read-only next-step result at **6257412acd703456677ff9b5087954987820b940**: `Internal/OCountedIteration.lean` can be lowered **in place**, using existing bare APIs. No missing mathematical/kernel contract was found in source; this is not a compiled follow-up verdict. #1160 is unchanged; no build/cache/source mutation occurred.

The actual higher-calculus uses are confined to `iterate`: two `change ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace …` repackagings (82,101), `hf.iterateWhile` (96), `hit.comp_linear h₀` (103), existential `h.computableInTimeAndSpace` (155), and existential `h₀.length_le` (163). Their imports are the legacy `Combinators.IterateWhile` facade and explicit `Combinators.Comp`; the latter also supplies legacy erasure/length conveniences. `countStep_inO` itself is already direct plain O and should remain unchanged. `open ComputableTidilyInO (length_encNat_mono)` refers only to the credited PURE lemma in `Internal/BinarySizeFacts`; it does not import/define that predicate. Its lexical namespace cleanup is separate, not a reason to rename APIs here.

Smallest implementation theme:
- Unpack the two existing `NormalForm.inO` results directly into their fixed machines, pointwise run proofs and the retained initial output charge `l₀`; remove the two existential casts.
- Replace the high iterate-while wrapper by **existing `computesTidily_iterateWhile` from `Internal/KernelIterateWhile`**, using the same `countStep`, stopping proof `hr`, trajectory words and `Finset.Iic` time/space/length suprema. Keep its existing machine `tm.iterateWhile true`; the old wrapper already only unpacks a machine and calls this run law.
- Compose with the normalized start machine using **`ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace.comp` from `Internal/KernelComp`**. Its exact overheads are `4*intermediateLength+9` time and `5*intermediateLength+6*max(kStart,kLoop)+20` space. The old common coefficient can still be `6*max(kStart,kLoop)+29`; absorb that overhead in the same existing estimates without inventing a new generic helper. Erase the resulting fixed-machine run pointwise into the existing plain `of_bounds`; replace `h₀.length_le x` by the start machine's `length_output_le`. Preserve `l₀ x` for SPACE: do not replace the charged output bound by a time bound there.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Read-only binary multiplication map at frozen source `8246414bdf8fdd33ccb2217125ccdccbc4e8bf27` (actual-main parent `731c6e9c`); no source/build/cache mutation. #1053/#1172 remain frozen and worker560 retains the only builder.

Exact current route: `ComputableInPolyTime.binary_mul'` in `Complexity/PolyTime/Nat/Binary.lean:615` erases the raw captured `binary_mul'` (line366), which composes raw `binary_mul` (line265), which uses `computableTidilyInDegree_mul` in `Complexity/Arith.lean:120` and its higher Degree fold/composition/ite/product calculus. The public plain captured theorem has arbitrary `α : Type`, arbitrary `input : α ↪ List Bool`, independently supplied plain binary `left`/`right` certificates and unchanged binary output. **There is no existing public `ComputableInPolyTime.binary_mul` pair theorem at this pin**; the pair-named theorem is in the raw namespace. A new public plain pair name would therefore need explicit API scope, not be described as a proof-only replacement.

Existing algorithm and proof data are sufficient for the qualitative plain replacement. Arith's `NatMul.mulStep (acc, sh) bit = (if bit then acc + sh else acc, sh + sh)` is folded over `m.bits`, initialized with `(0,n)`, then projected. `foldl_mulStep` proves the result, while `foldl_mulStep_le` and `size_le_of_le` bound **every prefix including final**. For encoded input length `N`, the original state bound is exactly `3*N+1`; the iteration count is `m.bits.length ≤ N`, never numeric `m`. The exponential `2^prefixLength*n` occurs only in the pure value invariant and is converted to a linear binary-size bound; it is not a runtime loop or allocated unary operand.

Smallest proposed follow-up: move those four credited pure NatMul declarations unchanged into the existing low `Encodings/Nat/Arithmetic` home (one copy; Arith imports/reexports them). Keep their qualified names and explicitly check visibility/public-data correspondence rather than `import all` or private helper copies. In existing `Internal/PolyTimeBinaryPrimitives`, prove a private pair multiplication certificate via the already-direct `ComputableInPolyTime.foldl'`: raw-bit list `m.bits` from the encoding identity, direct `(0,n)` initializer, callback formed from the direct **named** `binary_add` twice plus plain conditional/product/projections, and the unchanged full-prefix bound above. Project the final accumulator using `foldl_mulStep`. Replace only the existing public plain captured `binary_mul'` proof with direct composition of that private pair certificate and `hleft.prod hright`, preserving its entire telescope/registration. This needs no new algorithm, normalizer, higher raw transport, missing bare-machine contract or numeric-value repetition. Reuse the existing direct fold/kernel rather than reconstructing a multiplier machine.

Resource boundary: this public plain theorem promises existential polynomial time/workspace, not fixed degrees. Its direct fold proof retains separately certified clocks/workspace and full encoded-state/output charges; it must not use output≤workspace or workspace→time. The old raw theorem's **explicit degree contract is `3/1`** (time/workspace degree3, independent output degree1); it should remain unchanged in this narrow proof-only replacement. A qualitative PT certificate does **not** establish that exact 3/1 resource interface. Directly replacing that additional quantitative theorem would require an explicit quantitative addition certificate (the existing new direct addition exports PT, not Degree2/1) and corresponding direct O/Degree fold estimates; no missing bare compiler law was found, but that extra quantitative proof is a separate scope and cannot be claimed from this PT change. Likewise the existing public raw pair/captured rules and old Arith import remain transitional until their own deletion/caller phase.

No live open binary-multiplication provider task was found in the PR title/claim/source inspection. No change to global registration/search ordering is proposed. Future validation should preserve the original captured binary encoding/missing-premise clients and #1103 product/word clients, plus long binary operands/zero and a no-high-calculus import guard for the direct supplier; original guide/named/privacy/PPT scripts and budgets remain untouched. Existing arithmetic mathematics/credit is reused; no fresh mathematical audit, build or new theorem was performed in this planning task.

Worker audit_prerequisites for coordinator-codex-01a16ab8, not Samuel. Stopping after this bounded note; implementation is not started.

The smallest concrete family is **raw-word length / binary bit-length**, replacing just two existing proof bodies, with no new public theorem:

```lean
@[fun_prop]
theorem ComputableInPolyTime.length_bits :
  ComputableInPolyTime (fun l : List Bool => l.length) encBits encUnary

@[fun_prop, program_certificate]
theorem ComputableInPolyTime.binary_size :
  ComputableInPolyTime Nat.size encNat encUnary
```

Keep each name, complete type and attribute event at its current facade location (`PolyTime/List.lean:941`, `PolyTime/Nat/Binary.lean:571`); do not move registrations into a lower import. Current length_bits erases raw length_bits; current binary_size uses raw list length composed with raw natBits and then erases it.

An existing DIRECT leaf already provides the answer: `Internal.DecoderWords.unary_degree : ComputableInDegree List.length encBits encUnary 1 1` in `Internal/DecoderPrimitives.lean`. It unpacks the existing unaryLengthT machine, with actual clock `2*word.length+3`, **zero workspace**, and independent linear encoded output. Its `.computableInPolyTime` method in Degree/Bounds directly unpacks plain independent time/workspace witnesses; it is not a raw bridge or new normalizer. Use that for length_bits. For binary_size, compose it with the already-supported plain encoding-identity certificate for `Nat.bits : ℕ → List Bool` from encNat to encBits, then rewrite only `Nat.size_eq_bits_len`. No loop, new machine/helper, output≤workspace assumption, inhabitance premise or new API is needed. The output is unary bit-length (including zero), not the numeric operand in unary.

The existing captured theorem `length_bits_comp {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {word : α → List Bool} (hword : ComputableInPolyTime word input encBits) : ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (word a).length) input encUnary` already uses plain `length_bits.comp hword` and needs no edit. Arbitrary captured binary-size clients similarly use existing `binary_size.comp hnat`; no new captured wrapper should be added. This removes the two proof routes only: the old raw declarations and other imports remain staged. It does not manufacture a fixed quantitative degree theorem from PT; the independent count-machine bounds are the pre-existing leaf's, and the public replacement contracts remain qualitative PT.

A later change should coordinate/rebase this adjacent hunk and preserve all three additions/credit; no reservation or competing copy is needed. For an even smaller first checkpoint, binary_size alone is directly provable from the decoder leaf without touching List or waiting for #1113. Actual main's decoder leaf/List source is unchanged from the inspected predecessor.

Fixed unary_pow really exists, but its current ordinary unary_mul/unary_add dependencies are still raw-backed; I am not presenting it as a transitively direct ready family. No power/bitwise/division inventory or theory is proposed here. The length pair is the easiest concrete next step. Future checks should cover empty/false/long raw words, zero/exponential binary operands, arbitrary captured input/missing-premise and current facade automation at unchanged budgets, plus the zero-workspace/nonempty-output distinction. Those checks were not run in this read-only task.

title: S4 (#456): delete the tidy computability calculus; keep only a machine-level kernel
body:
**Decision (Samuel, 2026-10-24):** tidy computability is confined to an internal library. Outside it, tidy does not appear at all: not in statements, which S2/S3 already enforce, and **not in proofs either**. This completes #456's direction: plain is the only calculus users, contributors and other areas see.

## Why
S2 sweeps make statements plain, but proofs underneath keep tidy originals and convert back and forth. Measured outside `Complexity/Computability/Machines/**`, with approximate grep counts:

| | main @ 2026-10-24 19:00 | after the Classes sweep #854 |
|---|---:|---:|
| public tidy statements (Classes area) | 590 | 5 |
| private tidy declarations | 119 | 214 |
| local `fun_prop` tidy views | 44 | 191 |
| `.tidy`/`.of_tidy` round trips | 1,062 | 2,262 |
| files mentioning tidy | 402 | 373 |

Every bridge is a missing plain rule. Contributors outside Machines still need to know both calculi and the bridge idioms. The boundary is also where today's hardest bugs sit: #810's raw-evidence bypass, #813's timeouts, and the local workarounds in #847.

## End state (revised 2026-10-24: Samuel adopted deletion, after the spike #869)
**The tidy *calculus* is deleted.** There is one computability calculus: the plain predicates (`ComputableInPolyTime`, `ComputableInO`, `ComputableInBigO`, `ComputableInDegree`, space, …), their closure rules and plain-only `fun_prop`. Each primitive closure rule is proved directly: normal-form the plain machines inside the proof, compose them with the machine combinators, conclude plain. The spike #869 did this, sorry-free, for PolyTime composition, pairing, `if`, fold and projections, for O composition and `if`, and for Degree composition, with bounds matching today's (report 6388790221). Plain-only `fun_prop` also removes the documented plain↔tidy search cycle.
- **What remains is a small machine-level kernel**, about 130 declarations: cslib's `ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace`/`TransformsTapes`, the tidy normal form, the machine combinators, the raw constructions, and exact-bound streaming lemmas, which get plain corollaries. author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

### Claim & M0 Design — KEM–DEM Hybrid Public-Key Encryption (#881, Step 1 of #1000)

* **Agent / session:** `worker-antigravity-20261024` (role: worker)
* **Branch / worktree:** `feat/hybrid-encryption-881` (`/home/samuel/Code/complexitylib-wt/agy-881-hybrid`)
* **Files:** `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/Hybrid.lean`, `Complexity.lean`, `ComplexityTests/Crypto/HybridEncryption.lean`, `ROADMAP.md` (PR #1015)

---

### 1. Source Pins (`[BonehShoup2023]`)

All definitions and theorems follow [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*, Version 0.6 (2023)][BonehShoup2023], Exercise 11.9 (*Modular hybrid construction*, printed pp. 460–461, PDF pp. 476–477) and Section 2.2 (printed p. 16, PDF p. 32):
* **Exercise 11.9(a) (Key encapsulation mechanism and hybrid construction, printed pp. 460–461):** Key generation `keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)`, encapsulation `encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)` returning `(k, ctKem)`, deterministic decapsulation `decaps : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool` returning the encapsulated key `k`, and the generic KEM–DEM combination `hybridEncrypt` / `hybridDecrypt`.
* **Exercise 11.9(b) (Semantic security of a KEM and of the hybrid construction, printed p. 461):** Real experiment `kemRealGame` passes `(pk, (k, ctKem))` from `(pk, sk) ← keyGen n` and `(k, ctKem) ← encaps n pk` (encoded via `encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)`) to a uniform `Distinguisher`; ideal experiment `kemIdealGame` replaces `k` with an independent uniform `n`-bit key `k' ← BitString.sampleList n` while keeping `ctKem`. Combining a semantically secure KEM (`KEMINDCPA`) with a one-time semantically secure DEM (`DEMOneTimeINDCPA`) yields an IND-CPA public-key encryption scheme (`Encryption.INDCPA keyGen (hybridEncrypt encaps encryptSym)`), with quantitative advantage bounds via both two per-bit KEM distinguishers (`Adv_hyb ≤ Adv_KEM(D_0) + Adv_KEM(D_1) + Adv_DEM(B_s)`) and a single hidden-bit KEM distinguisher (`Adv_hyb ≤ 2 * Adv_KEM(B_kem) + Adv_DEM(B_s)`).
* **Section 2.2, Attack Game 2.1 & Definition 2.2 (One-time symmetric semantic security, printed p. 16):** `demGame` samples `k ← BitString.sampleList n`, invokes `adversary.choose n []`, encrypts the selected challenge bit under `encryptSym n k`, and passes `(choice.2, ciphertext)` to `adversary.guess n`.
* **Specializations relative to Boneh–Shoup Exercise 11.9:**
  - Single-bit messages (`Bool`), matching `Encryption.game` and `Encryption.INDCPA`.
  - Uniform $n$-bit ideal keys (`BitString.sampleList n` in `kemIdealGame` and `demGame`). Because `KEMINDCPA` is asymptotic, finitely many or negligibly probable real key-length deviations remain compatible with `KEMINDCPA`, whereas non-negligible deviations from length $n$ are detectable by a PPT distinguisher comparing `(unframe (dropFrame challenge)).length` with $n$.
  - Total deterministic decapsulation (`decaps : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, no `Option` / $\bot$); correctness quantifies over supported outputs of `encaps` and `encryptSym`.
  - Explicit public-key framing in the single-argument KEM `Distinguisher` challenge via `encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits) (pk, (k, ctKem))`.

---

### 2. Exact Lean Declarations (`namespace Cslib.Crypto.Encryption`)

All public statements are plain-first (`ComputableInPolyTime`, `IsPPT`, `IsPPTOn`; no `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` on the public surface, per #456):

1. **KEM IND-CPA (`kemRealGame`, `kemIdealGame`, `KEMINDCPA`):**
   ```lean
   def kemRealGame (keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
       (encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
       (distinguisher : Distinguisher) (n : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool

   noncomputable def kemIdealGame (keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
       (encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
       (distinguisher : Distinguisher) (n : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool

   def KEMINDCPA (keyGen : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
       (encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool)) : Prop :=
     Game.Indistinguishable
       (fun D n => ProbComp.eval (kemRealGame keyGen encaps D n))
       (fun D n => ProbComp.eval (kemIdealGame keyGen encaps D n))
       (IsPPT encBool)

   theorem isPPTOn_kemRealGame ... :
       IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => kemRealGame keyGen encaps distinguisher (n a))
   theorem isPPTOn_kemIdealGame ... :
       IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => kemIdealGame keyGen encaps distinguisher (n a))
   ```

2. **One-Time Symmetric Bit Encryption (`demGame`, `DEMOneTimeINDCPA`):**
   ```lean
   noncomputable def demGame (encryptSym : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
       (adversary : Adversary) (bit : Bool) (n : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool

   def DEMOneTimeINDCPA (encryptSym : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)) : Prop :=
     Game.Indistinguishable
       (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (demGame encryptSym adversary false n))
       (fun adversary n => ProbComp.eval (demGame encryptSym adversary true n))
       Adversary.IsPPT

   theorem isPPTOn_demGame ... :
       IsPPTOn input encBool (fun a => demGame encryptSym adversary (bit a) (n a))
   ```

3. **Hybrid Encryption Construction & Correctness (`hybridEncrypt`, `hybridDecrypt`):**
   * Ciphertexts `(ctKem, ctDem)` are encoded with `encPair encBits encBits` and decoded with `unframe` / `dropFrame`.
   ```lean
   def hybridEncrypt (encaps : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool))
       (encryptSym : ℕ → List Bool → Bool → ProbComp (List Bool))
       (n : ℕ) (pk : List Bool) (bit : Bool) : ProbComp (List Bool)

   def hybridDecrypt (decaps : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool)
       (decryptSym : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → Bool)
       (n : ℕ) (sk ct : List Bool) : Bool :=
     decryptSym n (decaps n sk (unframe ct)) (dropFrame ct)

   theorem isPPTOn_hybridEncrypt ... :
       IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits encBool)) encBits
         (fun p => hybridEncrypt encaps encryptSym p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)

   theorem computableInPolyTime_hybridDecrypt ... :
       ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × List Bool × List Bool => hybridDecrypt decaps decryptSym p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
         (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool

   theorem hybridDecrypt_encPair ...
   theorem hybridDecrypt_hybridEncrypt ...
   ```

4. **Boneh–Shoup Exercise 11.9(b) Reductions & Asymptotic Security:**
   * Intermediate game `hybridIdealGame` replacing the encapsulated key with `BitString.sampleList n`.
   * Reductions `hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, and `hybridToDEMAdversary`, with strict PPT certificates `isPPT_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `isPPT_hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, and `isPPT_hybridToDEMAdversary`.
   * Exact distributional bridges `eval_kemRealGame_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `eval_kemIdealGame_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `eval_demGame_hybridToDEMAdversary`, and `abs_prob_kemRealGame_sub_kemIdealGame_hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`.
   * Quantitative bounds `advantage_hybridEncrypt_le` and `advantage_hybridEncrypt_le_two_mul_kem_add_dem`.
   * Asymptotic composition: `indcpa_hybridEncrypt`.

5. **Non-vacuous One-Time Pad DEM (`otpEncrypt`, `otpDecrypt`):**
   * `otpEncrypt n k bit := pure [k.headD false ^^ bit]` and `otpDecrypt n k ct := k.headD false ^^ ct.headD false`.
   * `otpDecrypt_otpEncrypt`, `isPPTOn_otpEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_otpDecrypt`, `eval_demGame_otpEncrypt_eq` (`1 ≤ n`), `demOneTimeINDCPA_otpEncrypt`, and `indcpa_hybridEncrypt_otpEncrypt`.

---

### 3. Reuse Plan

* Reuses `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.Adversary`, `Adversary.IsPPT`, `Encryption.game`, and `Encryption.INDCPA` from `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/PublicKey.lean`.
* Reuses `Cslib.Crypto.Distinguisher`, `IsPPT`, and `Game.Indistinguishable` from `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Foundation.lean` and `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Game.lean`.
* Reuses `BitString.sampleList`, `BitString.uniformList`, `BitString.eval_sampleList`, and `BitString.uniformList_succ` from `Complexity/Languages/Probabilistic/BitString.lean` and `Complexity/Foundations/BitString/Uniform.lean`.
* Reuses `encPair`, `unframe`, `dropFrame`, `unframe_frame_append`, and `dropFrame_frame_append` from `Complexity/Turing/Encoding.lean` and `Complexity/Turing/Post.lean`.

title: feat(Crypto): formalize KEM-DEM hybrid public-key encryption (Boneh-Shoup Exercise 11.9)
body:
Parent: #640 (Track C, Item 3: Hybrid encryption) and #1000 (Step 1).

## Scope

Formalize Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEMs), one-time symmetric Data Encapsulation Mechanisms (DEMs), and the KEM–DEM hybrid public-key encryption paradigm following [Boneh and Shoup, Version 0.6, Section 2.2 (Attack Game 2.1, Definition 2.2) and Exercise 11.9][BonehShoup2023] in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/Hybrid.lean`:

1. **Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (`kemRealGame`, `kemIdealGame`, `KEMINDCPA`)**:
   - Real and ideal KEM IND-CPA experiments (`kemRealGame`, `kemIdealGame`, Exercise 11.9) where `kemIdealGame` replaces the encapsulated key with an independent uniform `n`-bit key `BitString.sampleList n`.
   - Strict PPT certificates (`isPPTOn_kemRealGame`, `isPPTOn_kemIdealGame`) and asymptotic security predicate `KEMINDCPA`.
2. **One-Time Symmetric Bit Encryption (`demGame`, `DEMOneTimeINDCPA`)**:
   - One-time symmetric chosen-plaintext experiment (`demGame`, Section 2.2, Attack Game 2.1 and Definition 2.2) keyed by `BitString.sampleList n` against uniform two-stage `Encryption.Adversary` distinguishers.
   - Strict PPT certificate (`isPPTOn_demGame`) and asymptotic security predicate `DEMOneTimeINDCPA`.
3. **Hybrid Encryption Construction and Correctness (`hybridEncrypt`, `hybridDecrypt`)**:
   - `hybridEncrypt encaps encryptSym` and deterministic `hybridDecrypt decaps decryptSym` encoding `(ctKem, ctDem)` via `encPair encBits encBits` (Exercise 11.9(a)).
   - Polynomial-time certificates (`isPPTOn_hybridEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_hybridDecrypt`) and exact decryption correctness (`hybridDecrypt_encPair`, `hybridDecrypt_hybridEncrypt`).
4. **Boneh–Shoup Exercise 11.9(b) Reductions and Asymptotic Security**:
   - Direct per-bit KEM distinguisher `hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, single hidden-bit KEM distinguisher `hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, and two-stage DEM adversary `hybridToDEMAdversary`, with strict PPT certificates (`isPPT_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `isPPT_hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, `isPPT_hybridToDEMAdversary`).
   - Exact distributional bridges (`eval_kemRealGame_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `eval_kemIdealGame_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `eval_demGame_hybridToDEMAdversary`) via the intermediate game `hybridIdealGame`.
   - Quantitative per-`n` advantage bounds `advantage_hybridGame_le_two_mul` (Exercise 11.9(b) single hidden-bit distinguisher bound `2 * Adv_KEM + Adv_DEM`) and `advantage_hybridGame_le` (two-distinguisher triangle-inequality variant).
   - Asymptotic Boneh–Shoup Exercise 11.9(b) (`KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa`): `KEMINDCPA` and `DEMOneTimeINDCPA` imply `Encryption.INDCPA` for `hybridEncrypt`.
5. **Non-vacuous One-Time Pad DEM (`otpEncrypt`, `otpDecrypt`)**:
   - Exact correctness (`otpDecrypt_otpEncrypt`), polynomial-time certificates (`isPPTOn_otpEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_otpDecrypt`), exact zero advantage for `n ≥ 1` (`eval_demGame_otpEncrypt_false_eq_true`, `advantage_demGame_otpEncrypt_eq_zero`), unconditional security (`demOneTimeINDCPA_otpEncrypt`), and the KEM-to-PKE corollary (`KEMINDCPA.hybrid_otpEncrypt_indcpa`).
6. **Tests & Validation (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/HybridEncryption.lean`)**:
   - Non-vacuous runtime/distributional checks (`not_kemINDCPA_leaking`, `kemINDCPA_idealEncaps`, `indcpa_hybridEncrypt_idealEncaps_otpEncrypt`).

### Claim: Item 5 — Unified Gap Convention for `GapMCSP` and `GapMINKT` (#884 F13)

• **Agent/Session**: `worker-jetski-b5844be2` (session `b5844be2-557b-4d63-859e-d7561a4d7c65`)
• **Scope**: Item 5 (Gap convention under F13):
  - Establish a unified gap convention across all lengths for both `GapMCSP` and `GapMINKT`:
    - Move `truthTableLanguage` to `Complexity/Computability/MCSP/Basic.lean` and define `GapMCSP (s₁ s₂ : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ∀ n, s₁ n ≤ s₂ n) : PromiseProblem (List Bool)`, matching OPS19 Def. 2.4 and `PromisePPoly` / `PromiseBPP`.

body:
### Claim: F7, one family of error predicates (M0 design)

`worker-claude-unify-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Branch `refactor/unify-error-predicates-884`, worktree `/home/samuel/Code/complexitylib-wt/884-f7`. One PR.

**Overlap.** Item 4 (claimed 13:52 by `worker-jetski-9fbb7ac4`) splits `Promise/Reduction.lean`, and F7 edits the same section. Nothing is locked: whichever PR lands first, the other rebases. F7 *moves* `SolvesWith*`, `Promise{BPP,RP,CoRP}`, their membership and `ofSet` lemmas, `compl_mem_PromiseBPP`, `SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP` and `PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP` into `BPP.lean`/`RP.lean`. It also rewrites the proofs of `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP` and `RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`. If Item 4 moves these declarations without editing them, the rebase stays mechanical.

#### Direction: general on promise problems, decision version by `ofSet`
A language `A` is the promise problem `ofSet A = ⟨A, Aᶜ, _⟩`, and a promise problem is not in general a language. So the promise form is the general one. The reverse direction is not available: defining `PromiseBPP` from `BPP` through `promiseClass` would give the lift, and `promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP` is only an inclusion. Goldreich's semantic `PromiseBPP` asks for bounded error on the promise only, not for a `BPP` separator.

Each predicate is defined once, on `PromiseProblem`, in the **pointwise shape** that the four decision predicates already use:
```lean
-- BPP.lean
def PromiseProblem.SolvesWithBoundedError (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
    (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (Q : PromiseProblem α) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, (a ∈ Q.yes → 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
      3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
        V (a, List.ofFn r) = true).card) ∧
    (a ∈ Q.no → 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
      3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
        V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card)
def DecidesWithBoundedError (enc) (p) (V) (A : Set α) : Prop :=
  (PromiseProblem.ofSet A).SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V
```
The other three follow the same pattern: `SolvesWithOneSidedError` (`RP.lean`), `SolvesWithErrorExponent` (`BPP/Amplification.lean`) and `SolvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent` (`RP.lean`). Each has its `DecidesWith… := (ofSet A).SolvesWith…`.

**Meaning.**
- Each `DecidesWith*` unfolds definitionally to its current body, since `a ∈ (ofSet A).no` is `a ∉ A` by `rfl`. `BPP`, `RP` and `coRP` keep their current definitions. `ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP` and `ofSet_mem_PromiseRP` become `Iff.rfl`.
- One change is not definitional. `SolvesWithBoundedError` and `SolvesWithOneSidedError` currently read `(∀ a ∈ Q.yes, …) ∧ ∀ a ∈ Q.no, …` and become pointwise. The two forms are equivalent by `forall_and` but not `rfl`.
  - Their only uses are in `Promise/Reduction.lean`; no tests or abstracts use them.
  - The PR will flag this, so it needs `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023`.
  - The alternative, keeping Goldreich's conjunction shape, would break `rfl` for all four `DecidesWith*` and their roughly 15 client files instead.

#### Lemmas: once on the general form
- **Bounded error.** `SolvesWithBoundedError.compl` gives `compl_mem_PromiseBPP`, and `compl_mem_BPP := ofSet_compl ▸ compl_mem_PromiseBPP hA`.
- **Amplification.**
  - The general lemmas are `SolvesWithBoundedError.repeatMajority`, `SolvesWithErrorExponent.solvesWithBoundedError`, `SolvesWithOneSidedError.repeatAny`, `SolvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent.solvesWithOneSidedError` and `SolvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent.solvesWithErrorExponent`. Their statements are the current ones with `A` replaced by `Q`.
  - New class-level general forms: `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_forall_solvesWithErrorExponent` and `mem_PromiseRP_iff_forall_solvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`. `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent` and `mem_RP_iff_forall_decidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent` keep their statements and become these at `Q := ofSet A`.
- **Certificate.** `SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate` (statement unchanged) gives `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`. `DecidesWithOneSidedError.isVerifier` (statement unchanged) is derived from it, and `RP_subset_NP` from `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`.
- **Inclusions.** `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP` becomes three lines through amplification, replacing about 35 hand-written lines. `RP_subset_BPP` is its `ofSet` instance, and `coRP_subset_BPP` and `PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP` follow the same way.
- **PPT characterizations.** `mem_Promise{BPP,RP,CoRP}_iff_exists_isPPTOn` are already general and stay as they are. No decision-class copies exist, and none are added.
- **`RPReducible` closure.**
  - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`: amplify `Y`'s decider through the general iff to one-sided error `1/4`, then compose. The result rejects a no-instance with probability at least `(2/3)(3/4) = 1/2`, so no `and2` is needed.
  - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`: amplify to error `1/8`, then compose. A single run is not enough, since it rejects a no-instance with probability below `2/3`. So the private `and2` stays, but `maj3`, `probability_maj3` and the chained constants 20/27, 9/11, 7/27, 2/11, 17/33 and 289/1089 are deleted.

**Deleted public declarations.** Each one's statement is, definitionally, an instance of its general replacement:
- `DecidesWithBoundedError.repeatMajority`, `DecidesWithErrorExponent.decidesWithBoundedError`, `DecidesWithOneSidedError.repeatAny`, `DecidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent.decidesWithOneSidedError` and `DecidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent.decidesWithErrorExponent`. Callers using dot notation still resolve, because Lean unfolds the head; callers that use the names are updated.
- `solvesWithBoundedError_ofSet_iff` and `solvesWithOneSidedError_ofSet_iff`, which become `Iff.rfl`.
- `DecidesWithBoundedError.compl`, which equals `ofSet_compl ▸ h.compl` and has no other caller.

No aliases and no deprecations.

#### Existing notions considered
- **`PromiseProblem`, `ofSet` and `ofSet_compl`** (`Promise/Basic`): the general carrier. `BPP.lean` will import `Promise.Basic`, which only adds `NP` and has no cycle.
- **`promiseClass`**: rejected as the definition of `PromiseBPP` and `PromiseRP` (see above).
- **`IsVerifier`, `mem_PromiseNP_iff`**: reused. The certificate lemma is stated once, in `mem_PromiseNP_iff`'s shape.
- **`DecidesWithErrorExponent`, `DecidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`**: the same family (a seeded verifier, counted over random strings), so they are folded in.
- **`MultiTapePTM.DecidesWithBoundedErrorInTime`** (`Time.lean:105`): a *different* family. It works at machine level: fair-coin PTM runs with a clock, a halting condition and a `ProbComp` law. It has no promise twin, and folding it in would need a promise `BPTIME`. Not folded; `mem_BPP_iff_exists_mem_BPTIME` is its bridge.
- **`DecidesWithZeroError` (ZPP), `DecidesByMajority`/`DecidesByNonstrictMajority` (PP), `BP·C` (`Operators`) and the Valiant–Vazirani sets**: the same seeded shape, but no promise twins. They are unchanged and keep consuming or producing the `DecidesWith*` specializations, which stay definitionally equal to their current bodies.
- **`acceptCount`, `andVerifier`, `orVerifier`, `repeatAny`, `repeatMajority`** and `uniformList_acceptCount_toReal`: reused.
- **`OracleComp.replicate` / `IsPPTOn.replicate_bool`**: considered as a replacement for `and2`. A two-run conjunction through `replicate` needs product-law lemmas that cost more than `and2`'s 20 lines, so `and2` stays private.

#### Sources
No new citations. Moved docstrings keep their current Goldreich and Arora–Barak pins verbatim; I have not re-checked them.

#### Also
- **F8 and F5.** My coordinator suggested them as follow-ups, but they sit inside `worker-jetski-9fbb7ac4`'s Items 4 and 6, so I am not taking them.
- **Duplicate-definition survey.** After the F7 PR, I will run the survey (`scripts/audit_queries.py`, extended to definitions) and post it on #949.

  - The general lemmas are `SolvesWithBoundedError.repeatMajority`, `SolvesWithErrorExponent.solvesWithBoundedError`, `SolvesWithOneSidedError.repeatAny`, `SolvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent.solvesWithOneSidedError` and `SolvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent.solvesWithErrorExponent`. Their statements are the current ones with `A` replaced by `Q`.
  - New class-level general forms: `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_forall_solvesWithErrorExponent` and `mem_PromiseRP_iff_forall_solvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`. `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent` and `mem_RP_iff_forall_decidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent` keep their statements and become these at `Q := ofSet A`.
- **Certificate.** `SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate` (statement unchanged) gives `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`. `DecidesWithOneSidedError.isVerifier` (statement unchanged) is derived from it, and `RP_subset_NP` from `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`.
- **Inclusions.** `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP` becomes three lines through amplification, replacing about 35 hand-written lines. `RP_subset_BPP` is its `ofSet` instance, and `coRP_subset_BPP` and `PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP` follow the same way.
- **PPT characterizations.** `mem_Promise{BPP,RP,CoRP}_iff_exists_isPPTOn` are already general and stay as they are. No decision-class copies exist, and none are added.
- **`RPReducible` closure.**
  - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`: amplify `Y`'s decider through the general iff to one-sided error `1/4`, then compose. The result rejects a no-instance with probability at least `(2/3)(3/4) = 1/2`, so no `and2` is needed.
  - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`: amplify to error `1/8`, then compose. A single run is not enough, since it rejects a no-instance with probability below `2/3`. So the private `and2` stays, but `maj3`, `probability_maj3` and the chained constants 20/27, 9/11, 7/27, 2/11, 17/33 and 289/1089 are deleted.
