title: feat(Crypto): indexed signatures and Merkle signatures from one-time signatures
body:
Milestone M1 of #1001: Merkle's tree signature from any one-time signature scheme and a collision-resistant hash family. It comes with an explicit-loss security reduction whose two reductions are certified efficient. The design is in [the M0 comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1001#issuecomment-6398003266).

**Stacked on #1024** (Kilian's Merkle verifier and binding game), which is in turn stacked on #1023 (Merkle trees). The signature verifier checks the tree opening with #1024's `merkleVerify`. The collision case uses #1024's `isCollision_of_merkleVerify`.

## What is proved

**`IndexedSignature.lean`.** This module adds indexed signature schemes (Boneh–Shoup Definition 14.6). The signer takes an index `u < q(n)` as an explicit input, and the security game refuses to sign twice under one index. This is how the stateful use of Merkle's scheme is modelled: the state is the leaf counter, and the signer's obligation never to repeat it is what the game enforces. It differs from the source in four ways, each labelled in the module doc:

- **Signing** may be randomized.
- **Messages** are arbitrary bit strings.
- **Refusal instead of restriction.** The oracle refuses a repeated or out-of-range index, so every oracle adversary is admissible.
- **Forgeries** may name any index; the scheme's verifier must reject indices outside its capacity.

**`MerkleSignature.lean`.** `MerkleSignature.scheme S H depth hH hlen hcap` is an indexed scheme of capacity `2 ^ depth n`.

- **Keys.** The public key is a uniform `n`-bit hash key and the Merkle root of `2 ^ depth n` one-time verification keys.
- **Signature.** A signature at leaf `u` consists of the one-time key, the one-time signature on the digest `H k msg`, and the authentication path.
- **Verification.** It uses `merkleVerify` (path length `depth n`, `u < 2 ^ depth n`, root) and then the one-time check.
- **Lemmas.** Completeness is `verify_sign`; the strict PPT and polynomial-time certificates are `isPPTOn_keyGen`, `isPPTOn_sign` and `computableInPolyTime_verify`.

**`MerkleSignature/Security.lean`.**

- **The bound**, `succProbability_indexedEufCmaGame_le`. For every forger `A` and every `n`:

  `Pr[A forges] ≤ 2 ^ depth n · Pr[oneTimeForger A wins the one-time game of S] + Pr[collisionFinder A finds a collision of H]`.

  - `collisionFinder` generates all keys and answers honestly. If the forged verification key differs from the one at the named leaf, it extracts a tree collision. Otherwise it returns the forged message together with a signed message at that leaf with the same digest.
  - `oneTimeForger` plants its challenge at a uniform leaf (`leafIndex`, exactly uniform on `2 ^ depth n` values). It answers that leaf through its one-time oracle, truncating to a polynomial bound. Its simulation is proved exact (`eval_run_plantedHandler`), so the loss is exactly `2 ^ depth n`.
- **Efficiency:** `isPPT_collisionFinder` and `isOraclePPT_oneTimeForger`.
- **Security:** `SignatureScheme.OneTimeEUFCMA.indexedEUFCMA_merkle`, and `OneWay.exists_indexedEUFCMA`. The latter combines it with Lamport (`OneWay.exists_oneTimeSignature`): a one-way function and a `HashFamily` give indexed EUF-CMA signatures of every polynomial capacity.

## Sources and notation

- **Merkle**, *A Certified Digital Signature*, CRYPTO '89, LNCS 435, pp. 218–238, §6 "Tree Authentication". I checked it against the author's posted 1979 manuscript of the same text:
  > The use of tree authentication to create tree signatures is now fairly clear, A transmits Yi to B, A then transmits the authentication path for Yi, B knows R, the root of the authentication tree, by prior arrangement.
- **Boneh–Shoup** `[BonehShoup2023]`, v0.6. I checked §14.6.1, p. 597:
  > Definition 14.6. A q-indexed signature system is a signature system S = (G, S, V) where the message space is M0 = {1, . . . , q} × M and the signing algorithm S is deterministic. We say that S is a secure q-indexed signature if for all efficient q-query signature adversaries A, the quantity iSIGadv[A, S] is negligible.

  > Security of this construction follows immediately from the security of the underlying one-time signature. The proof of security uses the same "plug-and-pray" argument as in Exercise 13.2.

  > Place the q one-time public keys at the leaves of a Merkle tree and compute the corresponding hash at the root. This single hash value at the root is the public key for the q-indexed scheme. […] A signature on a message (u, m) contains the Merkle proof needed to authenticate the one-time public key pk_u, along with the one-time signature on m using sk_u.

  And §13.2, p. 533, Theorem 13.1, with `SIGadv[A, S'] ≤ SIGadv[B_S, S] + CRadv[B_H, H]`.

How the sources' notation maps to the Lean:

| Source | Lean |
|---|---|
| `q` | `capacity n = 2 ^ depth n` |
| `(u, m)` | index `u : ℕ`, message `msg : List Bool` |
| `pk_u`, `sk_u` | `(keys.getD u ([], [])).1`, `.2` |
| Merkle proof | `merklePath` (#1023) |
| `iSIGadv` | `Game.succProbability` of `indexedEufCmaGame` |
| one-time security | the existing `SignatureScheme.eufOneTimeGame` / `OneTimeEUFCMA` |
| `CRadv` | `collisionGame H (fun _ _ => true)` |

The explicit bound composes the sourced pieces: plug-and-pray, the Merkle-tree collision extraction behind Boneh–Shoup Theorem 8.8, and hash-and-sign (Theorem 13.1). The composition is original to this library, and the docstrings say so.

## Not in this PR

- **Counter layer.** The design proposed a counter-stateful layer, `CounterEUFCMA`, derived from `IndexedEUFCMA`. It is not included and stays open on #1001.
- **Later milestones.** M2 (stateless, via GGM and Boneh–Shoup Theorem 14.6) through M4 (Rompel) are untouched.

## Other changes

- **List lemmas.** `List.getD_append_cons_length` and `List.getD_append_cons_of_ne` are now in `Foundations/Data/List/Lookup.lean`. `OneWayToSignature` had a private copy of the second; that copy is replaced.
- **`fun_prop` locality.** In `OneWayToSignature`, three `@[fun_prop] private` rules become `attribute [local fun_prop]`. As CONTRIBUTING warns, the private rules were exported and broke `polytime` in importers (found here). Statements are unchanged.

## Validation

- Hosted CI: [Lean Action CI run 40202104986](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40202104986) on `13778adc`.
- **Local runs:**
  - `scripts/check.sh` (all six gates)
  - `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
  - `python3 scripts/check_changed_files.py --base pr/1024`
  - `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py` (no new tidy statements)
  - `lake exe mk_all --check`
- **No Lean MCP server** was available in this session, so I iterated with `lake env lean`.
- **Tests** (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/MerkleSignature.lean`) run concrete instances: Lamport on the identity, a toy truncating hash, two leaves at `n = 4`.
  - Honest signatures at both leaves verify, and the signer produces exactly the checked signature.
  - A message with another digest is rejected, while a toy-hash collision is accepted: that is the case the collision reduction handles.
  - The signature of leaf 0 is rejected at leaf 1. At index `0 + 2` the opening recomputes the root, and only the range check rejects it.
  - The capacity hypothesis holds for constant depth and for depth `Nat.clog 2 (n + 1)`.

**Size.** The PR is about 1.8k lines, above the usual 1.5k target. Most of it is the security file (about 1.1k lines). Each oracle-PPT certificate of the one-time forger needs a manual reply-size bound (`plantedHandler_bound`).

**Abstracts:** no impact; no catalogue or abstract changes. A headline for signatures belongs with M2 or M4 and is Samuel's call.

**Framework friction (#733):**

reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-52 — PRE-CHECK (non-approving; author delegated by coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023, so the verdict belongs to coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023) at 140d48bb34d8b02328aff427a735c9869ef58fe6

Agent review, not human approval.

I found no correctness problems. Every claimed `rfl` and equivalence checks (see Verified). Two items should be fixed before approval. Both are documentation only.

### Should fix
1. **Arora–Barak locators are attached to the new promise-level statements.** These docstrings now cite AB for statements about promise problems:
   - `BPP/Amplification.lean:90`: `SolvesWithBoundedError.repeatMajority`
   - `BPP/Amplification.lean:154`: `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_forall_solvesWithErrorExponent`
   - `RP.lean:211`: `SolvesWithOneSidedError.repeatAny`
   - `RP.lean:287`: `mem_PromiseRP_iff_forall_solvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`
   - `RP.lean:307`: `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP`. Its docstring on main had no citation.

   AB state these results only for languages (`BPP`, `RP`). The promise forms are new statements, so the PR text's "No new citations" is not accurate. The generalization is mathematically immediate, since the argument works instance by instance. Suggested fix: keep the AB pins on the decision-level instances (`mem_BPP_iff_…`, `mem_RP_iff_…`, `RP_subset_BPP`). On the promise forms, say that the argument is AB's applied on the promise, e.g. "the per-instance argument of [Arora and Barak, Section 7.4.1], for promise problems", or label them as library generalizations. Then update the PR text.
2. **Stale pointer.** `Promise/Reduction.lean:41-43` still says `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP` and `PromiseCoRP` "live in `…Classes.Promise.Probabilistic`". They are now defined in `Classes.BPP` and `Classes.RP`. `Promise.Probabilistic` keeps their PPT characterizations and closure lemmas.

### Nits (nonblocking)
3. `Promise/Probabilistic.lean:16`: `import …Classes.SharpP.Combinators` looks unused now that the `orVerifier` proof has moved. A copy of the file without that line compiles cleanly at this head.
4. `RP.lean:191` and `RP.lean:320` pass `(a := ofSet A)`, which names the bound variable of `Set`'s `⊆` and so depends on Mathlib's binder name. Both of these alternatives compile at this head: `ofSet_mem_PromiseNP.1 (PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP (ofSet_mem_PromiseRP.2 hA))` and `ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP.1 (PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP (ofSet_mem_PromiseRP.2 hA))`.
5. Ergonomics, for awareness only. Deleting the decision-level amplification lemmas means `h.solvesWithOneSidedError …` on a `DecidesWith…` hypothesis returns `(ofSet A).SolvesWithOneSidedError …`, so `.isVerifier` no longer chains. `RP/Closure.lean:145-146` now spells out `DecidesWithOneSidedError.isVerifier (…)`. This was the only such case I found. I am not asking for a change.
6. `mem_PromiseBPP_iff` and `mem_PromiseRP_iff` were listed under `## Main results` in main's `Promise/Probabilistic.lean`, and now no module lists them. Optional, since `mem_BPP` is not listed either.
7. Tests reach the new general lemmas only at `ofSet` instances, through dot notation on `DecidesWith…` in `ResourceClasses3`. No example uses a promise problem whose yes- and no-instances do not cover everything. Optional: add one concrete example where the verifier is arbitrary outside the promise, then apply `.repeatMajority`.
8. The private `probability_sampleList_verifier` (`Promise/Randomized.lean:435`) repeats the step that `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn` and `mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn` do inline. Optional: make it public next to `uniformList_acceptCount_toReal` and reuse it.

### Verified
- **Meaning preservation.** I wrote a scratch file at this head with main's bodies (a17902df) copied verbatim under `Old*` names. It compiles with no errors.
  - `rfl` holds for `@DecidesWithBoundedError α = @OldDecidesWithBoundedError α`, and likewise for `DecidesWithOneSidedError`, `DecidesWithErrorExponent`, `DecidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`, `BPP`, `RP` and `coRP`.
  - `Iff.rfl` holds for `ofSet A ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔ A ∈ BPP enc` and for `ofSet A ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔ A ∈ RP enc`.
  - `Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V ↔ OldSolvesWithBoundedError enc p V Q` holds by `simp only [SolvesWithBoundedError, OldSolvesWithBoundedError, forall_and]`, and the same proof works for `SolvesWithOneSidedError`. A `#guard_msgs` check confirms that `rfl` fails for the bounded-error equation.
  - `PromiseBPP enc = OldPromiseBPP enc`, `PromiseRP enc = OldPromiseRP enc` and `PromiseCoRP enc = OldPromiseCoRP enc` all hold.
- **Deleted declarations.** Each of the seven deleted declarations, stated as on main, is closed by the general lemma: by dot notation on a `DecidesWith…` hypothesis (`h.repeatMajority q`, `h.solvesWithBoundedError hq`, `h.repeatAny q`, `h.solvesWithOneSidedError hq`, `h.solvesWithErrorExponent`), or by `Iff.rfl` for the two `…_ofSet_iff`. `repeatMajority` and `repeatAny` also close the verbatim old bodies at `Q := ofSet A`.
- **Declaration sets.** Comparing the declarations in the five core files between main and head shows exactly the 7 public deletions, the 9 new public declarations, `maj3`/`isPPTOn_maj3`/`probability_maj3` deleted and 1 new private helper. Nothing became private.
- **Leftover names.** No reference to any deleted name remains in `.lean`, `.md`, `.json`, `.txt`, `.py` or `.toml` files. No parallel promise-level or decision-level copy remains. `DecidesWithZeroError` and `DecidesWithBoundedErrorInTime` have no promise twin and are out of scope, as the PR says.
- **Imports.** Adding `Promise.Basic` to `BPP.lean` brings in only two modules, `Classes.NP` and `Promise.Basic` itself. I found no cycle. Every `Cslib.…` name under `## Main results`/`## Main definitions` in `BPP.lean`, `BPP/Amplification.lean`, `RP.lean` and `Promise/Probabilistic.lean` is declared in that file.
- **Goldreich pins.** After normalizing whitespace, the docstrings of `SolvesWithBoundedError`, `SolvesWithOneSidedError`, `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP`, `PromiseCoRP`, `mem_PromiseBPP_iff` and `mem_PromiseRP_iff` match main's text exactly; only the line wrapping changed. I did not check them against the book.
- **`RPReducible` constants.**
  - For `PromiseCoRP`: `Yᶜ`'s solver is reduced to error 1/4, and composing gives 2/3 · 3/4 = 1/2 on `X.no`, with no acceptance on `X.yes`.
  - For `PromiseBPP`: with error 1/8, two runs give (7/8)² = 49/64 ≥ 2/3 on yes-instances and (1/3 + 1/8)² = 121/576 ≤ 1/3 on no-instances.
- **Tests.** The `PromiseRP` example in `ComplexityTests/PromiseProbabilistic.lean` keeps its statement; only the shape of the proof term changed. The concrete `ResourceClasses3` instances (`Set.univ`, `encBits`) now go through the general lemmas.
- **CI.** Lean Action CI run 40211983159 and the title check both passed at `140d48bb`. The head merges cleanly with current main (`99cdcf05`, which adds two unrelated Crypto tests).

title: refactor(Classes): one family of bounded- and one-sided-error predicates (#884 F7)
body:
Refs #884 (finding F7). This PR follows the [M0 design](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/884#issuecomment-6398661122) and is restacked on #1030's file layout. It is a refactor of definitions and proofs with no new mathematics, and it removes 41 lines in total (+436/−477).

The bounded-error, one-sided-error and error-exponent conditions are now each defined once, on `PromiseProblem`. The decision-problem predicate is the instance at `PromiseProblem.ofSet A = ⟨A, Aᶜ, _⟩`:

```lean
def DecidesWithBoundedError enc p V (A : Set α) : Prop := (ofSet A).SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V
```
`DecidesWithOneSidedError`, `DecidesWithErrorExponent` and `DecidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent` are defined the same way. The promise form is the general one, because a language is a promise problem but not conversely. The opposite direction, `promiseClass BPP`, would only give the lift, which is contained in Goldreich's semantic `PromiseBPP` but is not equal to it.

### What changes
- **Placement.** The decision predicates are defined from the promise ones, so the promise definitions must sit below `BPP.lean` and `RP.lean`.
  - `SolvesWithBoundedError` and `SolvesWithOneSidedError` move from `Promise/Probabilistic.lean` into `BPP.lean` and `RP.lean`, with `compl` and `exists_certificate`.
  - So do `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP` and `PromiseCoRP`, with `mem_PromiseBPP_iff`/`mem_PromiseRP_iff`, `ofSet_mem_Promise{BPP,RP,CoRP}`, `compl_mem_PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP` and `PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP`.
  - `BPP.lean` now also imports `Promise.Basic`. That adds only `NP` and creates no cycle.
  - `Promise/Probabilistic.lean` keeps the PPT characterizations, `mem_PromiseCoRP_iff`, the `promiseClass` inclusions, `PromiseP_subset_*` and the deterministic closure.
- **Error reduction is stated once, for promise problems.** This covers `repeatMajority`, `repeatAny` and the conversions between error conditions, plus the new class-level `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_forall_solvesWithErrorExponent` and `mem_PromiseRP_iff_forall_solvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`.
- **The decision statements are their `ofSet` instances**, each by `Iff.rfl` or an argument instantiation: `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent`, `mem_RP_iff_forall_decidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`, `RP_subset_BPP`, `coRP_subset_BPP`, `RP_subset_NP` and `compl_mem_BPP`.
- **`PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP`** is now three lines through error reduction. It replaces a 35-line two-run bound written by hand.
- **The certificate lemma is proved once.** `DecidesWithOneSidedError.isVerifier` is derived from `SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate` rather than proved a second time.
- **`RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP` and `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`** (`Promise/Randomized.lean`) now use the shared error reduction. The private `maj3`/`probability_maj3` and the chained constants (20/27, 9/11, 7/27, 2/11, 17/33, 289/1089) are deleted.
  - For `PromiseCoRP`: `Y`'s solver is reduced to error 1/4, and composing it with the reduction gives `2/3 · 3/4 = 1/2`.
  - For `PromiseBPP`: the solver is reduced to error 1/8. Two runs of the composition are still needed, since one run rejects a no-instance with probability below `2/3`, so the private `and2` stays. The only constants left are `7/8 = 1 − 2⁻³` and `11/24 = 1/3 + 2⁻³`.
- **Time-bounded predicates.** `MultiTapePTM.DecidesWithBoundedErrorInTime` is not folded in. It is a machine-level condition (fair-coin runs, a clock, halting, a `ProbComp` law) with no promise twin; `mem_BPP_iff_exists_mem_BPTIME` stays its bridge.

### Public statements and definitions (needs review outside the fleet)
1. **Definitions whose meaning is unchanged.** `DecidesWithBoundedError`, `DecidesWithOneSidedError`, `DecidesWithErrorExponent` and `DecidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent` unfold definitionally to their previous bodies, since `a ∈ (ofSet A).no` is `a ∉ A` by `rfl`. So do `BPP`, `RP`, `coRP`, `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP` and `PromiseCoRP`.
   - `ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP` and `ofSet_mem_PromiseRP` are now `Iff.rfl`.
   - `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent` and `mem_RP_iff_forall_decidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent` keep their statements and are proved as `mem_Promise…_iff_forall_… (Q := ofSet A)`.
   - No existing statement that mentions these definitions changes.
2. **One definition change that is not `rfl`.** `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithBoundedError` and `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithOneSidedError` change shape:
   - before: `(∀ a ∈ Q.yes, …) ∧ ∀ a ∈ Q.no, …`
   - after: the pointwise `∀ a, (a ∈ Q.yes → …) ∧ (a ∈ Q.no → …)` that all four decision predicates already use.

   The two shapes are equivalent by `forall_and`, but not definitionally equal, so `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP` and `PromiseCoRP` keep their meaning. The alternative was to keep Goldreich's shape and break `rfl` for the four `DecidesWith*` predicates and their roughly 15 client files instead. The only clients were in `Promise/` and in one test.
3. **New public statements.** They are the general forms whose `ofSet` instances are existing statements:
   - `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithErrorExponent` and `SolvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`;
   - `SolvesWithBoundedError.repeatMajority`, `SolvesWithErrorExponent.solvesWithBoundedError`, `SolvesWithOneSidedError.repeatAny`, `SolvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent.solvesWithOneSidedError` and `.solvesWithErrorExponent`;
   - `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_forall_solvesWithErrorExponent` and `mem_PromiseRP_iff_forall_solvesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-38 — findings pre-check at 7e76c4e0a4791bf14e65beab18ea3807598c4ee4 (not an approval; the approving reviewer is coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023)

I found no blocking issues. The four requested checks follow, then four optional nits.

**1. Statement.** I compared `#check` output for both rules after importing `PolyTime/List.lean` with the payload. The binders match exactly, and only the predicate differs: `{α γ : Type} {encA} {encIn} {encL} [ListEncoding encA encL] [SizedListEncoding encA encL] {l} {i} (d : α)`, `hl : … encIn encL`, `hi : … encIn encNat`, and the conclusion `(fun x => (l x).getD (i x) d) encIn encA`. Neither rule is `@[fun_prop]`. The cost depends on the encoded index length. `hcap` folds over `(encNat (i x)).reverse`, which has `Nat.size (i x)` bits. Every accumulator is capped by `(l x).length`, which is the `B` bound and is polynomial through `hlen.polyBounded_length`, so no index is expanded to unary. I also checked a client whose index comes straight from the input, `encPair (encList encNat) encNat`. There the index can be exponential in the input length. The rule applies, and `fun_prop` still fails with the full `PolyTime/List` rule set in scope.

**2. No tidy calculus.** I computed the import closure of the new module from source at this head; it has 80 local modules. None of the modules that define `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, `ComputableTidilyInDegree` or `ComputableTidilyInO` (`Complexity/PolyTime.lean`, `Complexity/Degree.lean`, `Complexity/BigO.lean`) is in it. The closure does mention tidy in two ways:
- the machine-level `ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace`/`ComputesTidily…` kernel, in `Combinators/`, `Plumbing/` and `Internal/`;
- docstrings in `ResourceBounds.lean` and `Complexity/BigOLe.lean`.

Both are the accepted boundary. `#print axioms` gives `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`. The step identity holds for all naturals, not only when `v ≤ cap`. With truncated subtraction, `cap - v - v - b = cap ∸ (2v+b)`, and `cap ∸ (cap ∸ s) = min cap s`. The cases `s = cap`, `s > cap`, `cap = 0` and `b ∈ {0,1}` all hold, and `omega` closes it in the file.

**3. Scope and baseline.** Exactly the four stated files changed. The head merges cleanly into the integration head `3dc4e97f`, which differs from `0ea0f469` only in `GMW/Simulator.lean`, a module already named as failing. I did not reproduce the full 25-module comparison. As a spot check, I re-elaborated these files against the worker's with-payload build outputs, with no errors:
- the committed module;
- the test;
- three clients that use the raw rule unqualified under `open … ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`: `Circuit/Boolean/CodeSubstitution`, `Problems/TSP` and `Circuit/Boolean/DepthTime/PolyTime`.

I checked that the files really were elaborated: an injected error was reported. None of the 9 client files opens `ComputableInPolyTime`, so the new public import cannot change how unqualified `listGetD_binary` resolves. Hosted `ci-checks` was still pending when I posted this.

**4. Tests.** They are meaningful. The generic client repeats the complete telescope. The raw-bit, framed and computed-pointer clients cover the instances that matter. The controls are valid: the unary `listGetD` rule and `fun_prop` reject a binary certificate, the new rule rejects a unary one, and dropping `SizedListEncoding` blocks it.

**Nonblocking**
- (a) *Reuse.* The capped-binary fold now exists three times:
  - the raw `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.listGetD_binary` (`PolyTime/List.lean:745`);
  - the private raw `binary_min_unary` (`PolyTime/Nat/Binary.lean:508`), whose public plain `ComputableInPolyTime.binary_min_unary` (`:614`) is only an `.of_tidy` wrapper;
  - this proof.

  `hcap` already computes `min (l x).length (i x)`, with the length in unary and the index in binary, which is plain `binary_min_unary'`. For the integration in #862, the direct argument could become the proof of `binary_min_unary`, moved into an Internal module. `listGetD_binary` would then be `(listGetD d).comp (hl.prod (binary_min_unary' hlen hi))`, leaving one copy and one fewer `.of_tidy` wrapper. This is outside this slice.
- (b) The `decide` facts at `ListBinaryLookup.lean:70-72` test only core `List.getD`, not the new rule or the capping. They add no evidence for this PR. Either drop them or replace them with a fact about the capping equation.
- (c) `fail_if_success` (lines 28-29, 38, 47) does not pin the reason for failure, so the `SizedListEncoding` control would also pass on an unrelated elaboration error. A `#guard_msgs` on the expected synthesis failure would pin it. There is also no matching control that drops `ListEncoding`. That class is independent of `SizedListEncoding` (`Encodings/List/Size.lean:22` does not extend it).
- (d) The module doc (`PolyTimeListBinaryLookup.lean:23-24`) points to the raw rule's file as the source of the fold. That pointer goes stale once #862 deletes the raw rule. Naming `Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue` alone would be enough.

No inhabitance, equality, output-growth or scalar bound premise was added. The conclusion and default/out-of-range semantics match. The new rule is neither fun_prop nor program_certificate, just like the old rule; the facade adds no alias or automation policy.

The arithmetic identity `cap - (cap - v - v - b) = min cap (2*v+b)` is valid without assuming v≤cap, including cap = 0 and saturation. hcap folds over the **reversed binary encoding**, with every prefix state bounded by list length. Thus cost is polynomial in the complete encoded input through hl/hi and the bounded accumulator; the numeric binary index is never expanded to unary. The proof uses the direct primitives and accepted machine-witness normalization boundary, not a high-level raw transport. title: feat(polytime): prove plain binary-index list lookup directly
body:
Supplier PR for #862 (slice assigned in [this comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6398569171), gap reported from #1022 [here](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6398299015)). It is based exactly on frozen `0ea0f469`. It targets `integration/plain-threesource-reviewed-api-608-codex` only to give a reviewable diff and hosted CI. `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8` decides whether to merge or cherry-pick it; the author will not merge it.

**What changed.** A plain lookup rule for a binary index, proved directly. The capped-binary fold is the same one the raw-calculus rule `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.listGetD_binary` uses. Before this change that raw rule had no plain counterpart.

```lean
theorem Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.listGetD_binary
    {α γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
    {encL : List α ↪ List Bool} [ListEncoding encA encL] [SizedListEncoding encA encL]
    {l : γ → List α} {i : γ → ℕ} (d : α)
    (hl : ComputableInPolyTime l encIn encL)
    (hi : ComputableInPolyTime i encIn encNat) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (l x).getD (i x) d) encIn encA
```

**Statement mapping.** The telescope is the raw rule's, unchanged:
- arbitrary element and input encodings;
- any list encoding with `ListEncoding` and `SizedListEncoding`;
- a fixed default `d`;
- a computed list `l`, and a computed index `i` certified in binary (`encNat`).

The conclusion is plain `ComputableInPolyTime`, with independent polynomial time and space bounds. Like the raw rule, it is not `@[fun_prop]`. There is no external source: this restates an existing library rule in the plain calculus, and its proof is the library's own capped-binary argument.

**Proof.** The new module `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Internal/PolyTimeListBinaryLookup.lean` does not import the tidy calculus. The test checks that `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, `ComputableTidilyInDegree` and `ComputableTidilyInO` are absent from its environment. The proof uses only the direct plain prerequisites at `0ea0f469`:
- **Unary list length.** The direct `foldl'` with `unary_succ` over the list itself, bounded by `SizedListEncoding.length_le`.
- **Capped index.** The direct `foldlWith` over `(encNat (i x)).reverse`, with the length as parameter and step `min cap (2 * v + b.toNat)`. Every state is at most the length (`boundedBinaryValue_le`). The fold reads the encoded index once, bit by bit, so the cost is polynomial in the encoded index length. An unbounded binary index is never expanded to unary.
- **The step.** There is no direct plain unary `min` or `add` at the base, and the plain `unary_add` is a raw-calculus wrapper. The unchanged step is certified through `min cap (2v + b) = cap - (cap - v - v - b)`, which needs only the direct `unary_sub` and `of_finite`.
- **Lookup.** The direct `listGetD` at the capped unary index, with the raw rule's equation (`boundedBinaryValue_eq`, `binaryValue_reverse_bits`).

`PolyTime/List.lean` gains one `public import`, so every existing client of the list rules sees the plain rule. The aggregator gains the module's line.

**Not changed.** The raw rule and its library clients are untouched. Migrating them, and deleting the raw rule, belongs to the integration (#862). The generic FHE endpoints are also untouched; they are already plain at the base. The PR adds no wrapper, alias or second lookup API.

**Tests** (`ComplexityTests/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Internal/ListBinaryLookup.lean`):
- **Generic client.** The complete telescope.
- **Raw-bit client.** `encBits`/`encBool` over `encPair encBits encNat`.
- **Framed client.** `encList encNat`.
- **Computed binary index.** A pointer stored in the list's first entry.
- **Controls.**
  - The unary `listGetD` rule and `fun_prop` both reject a binary index certificate, so the gap was real.
  - The new rule rejects a unary index certificate.
  - The new rule does not apply without `SizedListEncoding`.

```lean
theorem Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.listGetD_binary
    {α γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool}
    {encL : List α ↪ List Bool} [ListEncoding encA encL] [SizedListEncoding encA encL]
    {l : γ → List α} {i : γ → ℕ} (d : α)

    (hi : ComputableInPolyTime i encIn encNat) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (l x).getD (i x) d) encIn encA
```

The conclusion is plain `ComputableInPolyTime`, with independent polynomial time and space bounds. Like the raw rule, it is not `@[fun_prop]`. There is no external source: this restates an existing library rule in the plain calculus, and its proof is the library's own capped-binary argument.

title: feat(counting): construct a parsimonious binary-guess scanner
body:
## Change

Closes #100.

Construct one fixed shared-core `MultiTapeCTM 0 Bool Unit` that guesses one bit per input symbol and then takes a singleton halt. For every input of length `n`, every branch halts without getting stuck, every terminal trace has exactly `n + 1` instructions, and `w.map Bool.toNat ++ [0]` is a bijection from length-`n` Boolean words to terminal occurrence traces. The output is exactly `w`. There are `2^n` branches, including one when `n = 0`, and every Boolean output-predicate count equals its witness count.

`Counting/Program.lean` supplies the finite-index choice handler for the existing shared FreeM `runConfigFrom`: a query at `n` has responses `Fin n`, and List interpretation preserves repeated occurrences and singleton instructions. It introduces no second branch model. The scanner's interpreted program generates each length-`n` word with multiplicity one. The proof uses a permutation of the existing word enumeration, preserving exact multiplicities without assuming its order matches chronological scanner choices.

This is the guessing prerequisite for the reverse counting-machine direction. Witness-length preparation, singleton deterministic verifier composition, and the reverse #P/GapP characterizations remain open. #92 retains ownership of the efficient forward checker. No efficiency of an arbitrary output predicate or external List interpreter is assumed.

Sources: standard witness guessing in counting complexity [Valiant 1979]; the scanner invariant adapts `MultiTape.Probabilistic.Sampling` and its credited cslib `crypto` source `5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`. Existing common machine/program infrastructure and the VCVio oracle interface retain their source and author credit.

reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-40 — APPROVED at 122eb275f8d4d9b137c1fd1000379f955ca0fa13 (delegated-review exception, AGENTS.md; classification: documentation- and test-only)

Agent review, not human approval.

- **Classification.** Every changed line in `LiuPass.lean` sits inside a `/-! … -/` or `/-- … -/` block. The rename from "polynomial-overhead" to "polynomial-threshold" is doc-only, and no occurrence of the old label remains anywhere in the repo. `GKRProtocol.lean` changes only its module doc. The new declarations are test fixtures and test theorems in `ComplexityTests.Crypto.HybridEncryption`. No library statement, definition or abstract changes.
- **LiuPass attribution, checked against the proof.** The proof of `CondEPPRG.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` gets `p₀` from `exists_timeBounded_of_computableInPolyTime (computableInPolyTime_truncGen hG_poly)`. In that proof, `p₀ = (c_tm+1)(X+1)^(d_tm+1)` comes from `polynomiallyBounded_iff_le` applied to the certificate's time bound. The proof then sets `pG = p₀.comp (X + C (2γ+3))`, and `hlen_enc` bounds the encoded `(count, seed)` length by `m + (2γ+3)`. `truncGen` takes the count in unary and drops that many trailing bits. `exists_etimeBoundedComplexity_universalTM_le_ofMultiTapeTM` uses the same `t` on both sides, with an additive constant only (a zero-time-overhead `Simulation`). The new note matches all of this.
- **Source wording, checked against the arXiv:2009.11514v1 PDF.** §1.2 p. 7: "a cond EP-PRG that can be computed in time n + O(n^α), where α < 1 — we refer to this as a rate-1 efficient PRG". §5.1 p. 11 defines rate-1 efficiency as running time n + O(n^ε) for some ε < 1. Theorem 5.2 (§5.2, p. 11) assumes a rate-1 efficient µ-condEP-PRG. Theorem 5.6 (§5.3, p. 17) builds one from OWFs by padding. The source's `U` has polynomial overhead, but `U(Π, 1^t)` runs `M(w)` for `t` steps (§2.2, p. 8), so the near-linear range does rest on the generator's running time. Every locator is correct.
- **ROADMAP.** The converse landed in #1005, so removing it closes that direction. The replacement is a single direction with no status notes, and it describes the remaining gap accurately.
- **Tests.** `kemRealGame` and `kemIdealGame` match `Encryption/Hybrid.lean`: the real challenge is `(pk, (pk, pk))` and the ideal one is `(pk, (kIdeal, pk))`. So the real game accepts with probability 1 and the ideal game accepts with probability `2⁻ⁿ`, and the advantage is exactly `1 − 2⁻ⁿ`. Truncated subtraction is exact here because `2⁻ⁿ ≤ 1`, and the advantage is 0 at `n = 0`, as it should be. The values `1/2` and `3/4` at `n = 1, 2` are correct. `not_kemINDCPA_sameLengthLeaking` adds the negligible `2⁻ⁿ` to get the constant 1, which is a sound and nonvacuous rejection.
- **GKR.** By `protocol_sound`, the error is `(width depth + Σ 5·width i)/|F|`. With `width 0 = 1` and `width 1 = 0`, that is two degree-2 sumcheck rounds at `2/101` each, one line step at `1/101`, and `0` for the output step. The new text gives this breakdown.
- **CI and merge.** Hosted `ci-checks` (run 40202414571) and `check-title` are green at the exact head. `mergeStateStatus` is CLEAN, and `git merge-tree` against current `origin/main` reports no conflicts.

Nonblocking nits:
1. `LiuPass.lean` module doc: "gives the generator's multi-tape machine enough steps to print each output from its seed" would be more exact as "the truncated generator's machine … from the encoded (count, seed) input". The preceding sentence already names the truncated generator, so this is optional.
2. `uniformList_bind_decide_eq_apply_true` is a general point-probability fact about `BitString.uniformList`, and the library has no equivalent yet. It could move to `Probability/BitString.lean` later. Keeping it test-local is fine.

title: doc(LiuPass,ROADMAP,tests): correct the Liu–Pass time-bound note; add a same-length leaking KEM test
body:
Fixes four issues found by an external agent review shared by Samuel. The PR changes documentation and tests only: no library statement or definition changes.

1. **`LiuPass.lean` time-bound note.** The note credited the polynomial threshold `∃ p, ∀ t ≥ p` to "polynomial-overhead universal simulation" (`DescriptionMethod.exists_etimeBoundedComplexity_universalTM_le_ofMultiTapeTM`). That theorem is clock-preserving: it uses the same `t` on both sides and adds only a description-length constant. The rewritten note says where the threshold actually comes from. `exists_timeBounded_of_computableInPolyTime` takes the generator's own `ComputableInPolyTime` running-time certificate, gets constants `c', d'`, and sets `p₀(n) = (c'+1)(n+1)^(d'+1)`. Theorem 5.2 then shifts this to `p_G(m) = p₀(m + 2γ + 3)` to cover the encoded truncation count. The note keeps the explicit statement that only the polynomial-threshold form is proved, and keeps the convention that `K^t` counts steps of the described machine. The module's label "M2a polynomial-overhead form" carried the same misattribution, so every remaining occurrence now reads "M2a polynomial-threshold form".
2. **`ROADMAP.md`.** The Liu–Pass converse (`exists_oneWay_of_mildlyHardOnAverage_timeBoundedNat` and the equivalences) landed in #1005, so this PR drops it from the open directions. In its place, the roadmap now lists the near-linear regime of Theorem 3.1 (c).
3. **`ComplexityTests/Crypto/HybridEncryption.lean`.** The existing `leakingEncaps` fixture stays as the length-boundary case: its leaked key has `n + 1` bits, so a length mismatch alone detects it. The new fixture `sameLengthLeakingEncaps n pk := pure (pk, pk)` leaks a uniform `n`-bit key under `toyKeyGen`. The tests prove:
   - the real game accepts with probability 1 (`eval_kemRealGame_sameLengthLeaking`);
   - the ideal game accepts with probability `2⁻ⁿ` (`eval_kemIdealGame_sameLengthLeaking_true`);
   - the advantage is exactly `1 - 2⁻ⁿ` for every `n` (`advantage_kem_sameLengthLeaking`), with instances at `n = 1` (`1/2`) and `n = 2` (`3/4`);
   - the fixture is not IND-CPA secure (`not_kemINDCPA_sameLengthLeaking`);
   - the fixture has a PPT certificate (`sameLengthLeakingEncaps_ppt`).
4. **`ComplexityTests/GKRProtocol.lean`.** The module doc now gives the correct breakdown of `5/101`: two sumcheck challenges of at most `2/101` each and one line challenge of at most `1/101`. The output step adds nothing, because the output layer has width 0.

**Source check (arXiv:2009.11514v1, checked against the PDF).** Theorem 3.1 (c), §3, p. 9: "For all constants d > 0, ε > 0, and every polynomial t(n) ≥ (1 + ε)n, K^t is mildly hard-on-average to (d log n)-approximate." §5.1, p. 11: "We say that G has rate-1 efficiency if its running time on inputs of length n is bounded by n + O(n^ε) for some constant ε < 1." Theorem 5.2 (§5.2, p. 11) assumes a rate-1 efficient condEP-PRG, and Theorem 5.6 (§5.3, p. 17) builds one from OWFs by padding. The near-linear range therefore rests on the generator's rate-1 running time, not on rate-1 universal simulation. The old note's phrase "rate-1 universal simulation" was corrected to match, and the ROADMAP direction uses the same wording.

**Review classification.** Documentation- and test-only. The new declarations are test fixtures and test theorems in `ComplexityTests`; no library statement, definition, abstract or security claim changes.

**Abstracts.** No impact: no abstract or catalogue entry refers to the changed text.

**Validation.** Local: all six `scripts/check.sh` gates, `check_hygiene.py`, `check_changed_files.py --base origin/main` and `lake exe mk_all --check` pass. The touched modules were rebuilt after rebasing onto #1027. CI: [ci-checks run 40202414571](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40202414571).

body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-43 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 3fa6426d9d21f9dcb6f996e2338ac8f964e3e958

Agent review, not human approval. I checked the statements against the local Boneh–Shoup v0.6 text (printed page numbers below). I could not obtain Pedersen's CRYPTO '91 paper, so its locators are unverified.

**What holds.**
- **The mathematics is right.**
  - Hiding is perfect for every fixed key `h ≠ 0`. Over a uniform key exponent, the advantage of an unbounded adversary is at most `1 / m`, coming only from `α = 0`.
  - Binding is an exact, zero-loss reduction to the existing `discreteLogGame`. The extractor `(r₁ - r₀)⁻¹ (m₀ - m₁)` is computed through Fermat's little theorem.
  - `isPPTOn_pedersenToDLAdversary` certifies that the reduction is strict PPT (#733), and `DiscreteLog.pedersenBinding` uses the existing `F.DiscreteLog setup` unchanged.
  - Messages and openings are words read modulo `q`, and distinctness is taken in `ZMod q`, which is the right notion for message space `Z_q`.
- **The games have the right shape.** They match Boneh–Shoup's definitions (Section 8.12, p. 344): hiding as Experiment `b` (the adversary sends `m₀, m₁`, receives `C(m_b)` and guesses), and binding as two accepting openings of one commitment to distinct messages. They also match the uniform system parameter `h` of Exercise 20.5 (p. 844).
- **Validation.** Hosted `ci-checks` passed at this head ([run 40203197117](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40203197117)). The branch merges cleanly with current `main`.

**Blocking**

1. **A parallel commitment notion.**
   - `PedersenHidingAdversary` (`PedersenCommitment.lean:243`) is a second two-stage choose/guess adversary with a state word, beside `CommitmentReceiver` (`Crypto/Computational/Commitment.lean:215`).
   - `pedersenHidingForKey`/`pedersenHidingGame` (`:251`, `:284`) and `pedersenBindingGame` (`:409`) are Pedersen-specific copies of Boneh–Shoup's general hiding and binding experiments.
   - The PR body justifies this by contrast with `Complexity/Crypto/Commitments/Basic.lean`, which does not exist. The existing API is `Crypto/Computational/Commitment.lean`.
   - Fix:
     - Define the Section 8.12 experiments once, for a commitment scheme with public parameters: the hiding experiment with a two-stage adversary over message words, and the binding experiment. Make Pedersen an instance.
     - Then either express Naor's `CommitmentReceiver`/`commitmentHidingGame`, where the receiver chooses `r`, through the same definitions, or say in the PR why that game needs its own shape and open a follow-up.
2. **Source locators and quotes** (AGENTS.md, new-statement standard).
   - Boneh–Shoup v0.6 has no section on Pedersen commitments. The module doc cites "Chapter 19" (`:27`, `:104`), which is Sigma protocols (Chaum–Pedersen, not Pedersen commitments). The PR body cites "Section 20.6.1", which v0.6 does not have; 20.6 is SNARKs, p. 842.
   - The v0.6 sources for what this PR proves are:
     - Section 8.12, p. 344: the commitment definition, `BINDadv` and the hiding experiment (Definition 8.8).
     - Section 10.6.1, pp. 414–415: Fact 10.3 ("Dlog_g h = (α − α′)/(β′ − β)") and Theorem 10.4 ("The hash function H_dl is collision resistant under the DL assumption … CRadv[A, H_dl] = DLadv[B, G]"), with `H_dl(α, β) := g^α h^β`. This is exactly your binding reduction.
     - Exercise 20.5, pp. 843–844: commitments `g^{β_i} h^{b_i}` under a uniform system parameter `h`.
   - Please cite these. In the PR body, quote verbatim the statements each theorem formalizes, including whatever "[Pedersen1991], Section 3" and "Theorem 3.1" (`:552`) say, which I could not verify.

**Nonblocking**

3. `instDecidableEqCarrier` (`:393`) is a general instance on `PrimeOrderGroupFamily` defined in a scheme module. Move it beside the structure in `DiscreteLog.lean`, or let `checkPedersenCollision` compare `F.encode d` images instead.

reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-48 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 7f7786fffaaf46f73fe0c791897d6f736b73f88b

Agent review, not human approval. This reviews the delta `3fa6426d..7f7786ff` after reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-43's review ([comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1043#issuecomment-6399470432)).

**Resolved.**
- **Item 2 (citations).** The docstrings and the PR body now cite Boneh–Shoup v0.6:
  - Section 8.12 (Definition 8.8, p. 344);
  - Section 10.6.1, Fact 10.3 and Theorem 10.4 (pp. 414–415);
  - Exercise 20.5 (pp. 843–844).

  I checked each against the v0.6 text. The "Chapter 19" and "20.6.1" locators are gone. The quote from [Pedersen1991] is still unverified; I could not obtain the paper either.
- **Item 3.** `instDecidableEqCarrier` is gone, and `checkPedersenCollision` compares `F.encode d` images instead.
- **The Pedersen-specific mathematics is unchanged** from the earlier review: perfect hiding for `h ≠ 0`, the `1 / m` bound over a uniform `α`, and the exact zero-loss reduction to `discreteLogGame`. Those conclusions still hold.
- **Validation.** Hosted `ci-checks` passed at this head ([run 40207516586](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40207516586)). The branch merges cleanly with current `main`.

**Blocking**

1. **`CommitmentScheme.Binding` is not Boneh–Shoup's binding.**
   - In Section 8.12 (p. 344), a commitment scheme is a pair `(C, V)`. `C(m)` outputs a commitment string `c` and an opening `o`, and `V(m, c, o)` accepts or rejects. `BINDadv` is the probability that the adversary outputs `(c, m₁, o₁, m₂, o₂)` with `m₁ ≠ m₂` and both openings accepted by `V`.
   - `CommitmentScheme` (`Commitment.lean:1295`) has no opening and no verifier. `bindingGame` and `Binding` (`:1375`, `:1385`) test the free field `checkCollision`, and nothing ties that field to `commitDist`.
   - So setting `checkCollision := fun _ _ => false` makes any scheme `Binding`. That includes the one-time-pad commitment that Remark 8.1 gives as non-binding. The general definition cites Definition 8.8 but does not express binding.
   - Fix:
     - Let `commitDist` return `(c, o)`, add `verify : Key → List Bool → List Bool → List Bool → Bool` (message, commitment, opening), and require correctness on the support.
     - Define the binding experiment on the adversary's output `(c, (m₀, o₀), (m₁, o₁))`. It accepts iff `m₀ ≠ m₁` and both openings verify.
     - For Pedersen, `verify` recomputes `encode (m • g + o • h)` and compares it with `c`. It must also accept only canonical message words, for example `ofBits m < q` and `(ofBits m).bits = m`. Otherwise two distinct words with the same residue break binding trivially. Alternatively, give the scheme a message type.
     - The discrete-log reduction should go through with only the extraction step adapted.

2. **`CommitmentHidingAdversary` is a third copy of the two-stage choose/guess adversary.**
   - `Encryption.Adversary` (`Encryption/Basic.lean:54`) has `choose : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp ((Bool × Bool) × List Bool)` and `guess : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → ProbComp Bool`.
   - `CommitmentReceiver` (`Commitment.lean:227`) has the same shape, with challenge `(r, b₀, b₁)`.
   - The new `CommitmentHidingAdversary` (`:1273`) differs from `Encryption.Adversary` only in its carrier types: the public input is `Param` instead of `List Bool`, and the challenge messages are `List Bool` instead of `Bool`.
   - `CommitmentScheme.hidingGame` is likewise `Encryption.game` with the commitment algorithm in place of `encrypt`. Section 8.12 calls its hiding definition "a semantic security definition" for exactly this reason.
   - Fix: define the two-stage adversary once, generic in the public-input and challenge types, and use it for commitment hiding. You could generalize `Encryption.Adversary` and its `IsPPT` over those types, or add a small generic structure in `Crypto/Game.lean`.
   - Then either migrate `Encryption.Adversary` and `CommitmentReceiver` to it in this PR, or record that migration on #949 item 9 with the declaration names. The "Framework friction" note explains why Naor's game has its own shape, but the follow-up that the earlier review asked for has not been opened.

**Nonblocking**

3. `PedersenHidingAdversary` (`PedersenCommitment.lean:280`) is now an `abbrev` for `CommitmentHidingAdversary (F.Desc × List Bool)`. `pedersenHidingForKey`, `pedersenHidingGame` and `pedersenBindingGame` (`:285`, `:313`, `:433`) are one-line wrappers around the general experiments. Stating the theorems directly about `F.pedersenScheme.hidingGame (F.pedersenKeyDist setup)` and `F.pedersenScheme.bindingGame` would remove four names.
4. `commitDist` is a `PMF`. CONTRIBUTING ("Algorithms are programs") asks for commit algorithms to be `ProbComp` programs. Here the `PMF` matches `DiscreteLog`'s `PMF` setup and its exactly uniform `ZMod q`, which `ProbComp` cannot sample: `sampleMod` is only nearly uniform. That is a reasonable exception, but please say so in the `CommitmentScheme` docstring.
5. `negligible_inv_two_pow` (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/PedersenCommitment.lean:57`) is the third copy of this lemma in the tests, after `DiffieHellman.lean:56` and `SchnorrDiscreteLog.lean:55`. Consider moving it to `Crypto/Negligible/Basic.lean`.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-57 — CHANGES REQUESTED at c68398d36a8dbc3e6cc52098d7f09a82d973cc74

Agent review, not human approval. This reviews the delta `7f7786ff..c68398d3`, a single commit, after reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-48's review ([comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1043#issuecomment-6400237328)). I checked the quotes against the Boneh–Shoup v0.6 text, using its printed page numbers. I also obtained Pedersen's paper (the LNCS 576 scan), so this time the Pedersen quote is checked.

**Resolved from the previous review**
1. **Binding now tests the verifier.**
   - `CommitmentScheme` has `verify`, `ValidMessage`, and correctness on the support of `commitDist`.
   - `isBindingCollision` requires `m₀ ≠ m₁` and that both openings verify.
   - Pedersen accepts only canonical message words. Distinct valid words give distinct residues (`hm_nat`, `ZMod.val_natCast_of_lt`), so the extraction still recovers `α`.
   - I checked locally that `Binding` now rejects a non-binding scheme (item 3).
2. **One adversary type.** `CommitmentHidingAdversary` is gone and `Encryption.WordAdversary` is reused. `Encryption.Adversary` and `Encryption.INDCPA` became abbreviations, and their clients compile. The `CommitmentReceiver` follow-up is recorded on #949 ([comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/949#issuecomment-6400371456)).
3. **The Pedersen wrapper names are removed.**
4. **The `PMF` choice is documented** in the `CommitmentScheme` docstring.
5. **The duplicate `negligible_inv_two_pow` is removed.**

**Earlier evidence that still holds.** The Pedersen mathematics is unchanged, except that extraction now goes through `verify`:
- perfect hiding for `h ≠ 0`;
- the `1 / m` bound over a uniform `α`;
- the exact reduction to `discreteLogGame`, certified strict PPT by `isPPTOn_pedersenToDLAdversary` (#733).

Hosted `ci-checks` passed at this head ([run 40213610034](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40213610034)), and the branch merges cleanly with current `main`.

**Blocking**

1. **The quotes in the PR body's "Primary-Source Audit" are not in the cited sources.**
   - Before this round, the body paraphrased Section 8.12 and Fact 10.3 without quotation marks, and it had an accurate Theorem 10.4 quote. That quote is now gone, and these blocks are presented as quotations:
   - **(a) The commitment-scheme definition.** "A commitment scheme consists of two algorithms: a commitment algorithm C and a verification algorithm V. …" does not occur in v0.6. Section 8.12, p. 344 says: "a commitment scheme for a finite message space M, is a pair of efficient algorithms C = (C, V) where: • Algorithm C is invoked as (c, o) ←R C(m), where m ∈ M is the message to be committed, c is the commitment string, and o is an opening string. • Algorithm V is a deterministic algorithm invoked as V(m, c, o) and outputs accept or reject. • Correctness property: for all m ∈ M, if we compute (c, o) ←R C(m), then V(m, c, o) = accept with probability 1."
   - **(b) Definition 8.8.** "Definition 8.8 (Binding and hiding). Let C = (C, V) be a commitment scheme... We say that C is binding if no efficient adversary can win … hiding if it is semantically secure when we view c as an encryption of m …" does not occur. Definition 8.8 (p. 344) reads in full: "A commitment scheme C = (C, V) is secure if it is both hiding and binding." The two notions are the bullets just before it:
     - "Binding: … for every efficient adversary A that outputs a 5-tuple (c, m1, o1, m2, o2) the advantage BINDadv[A, C] := Pr[m1 ≠ m2 and V(m1, c, o1) = V(m2, c, o2) = accept] is negligible."
     - "Hiding: … in Experiment b adversary A begins by sending m0, m1 ∈ M to the challenger, who computes (c, o) ←R C(mb) and sends c to A; finally, A outputs a guess b̂ ∈ {0, 1}. … HIDadv[A, C] := |Pr[W0] − Pr[W1]| is negligible."
   - **(c) Fact 10.3.** The quoted statement (cyclic group of prime order `q`, `h = g^α`, `β₁ ≠ β₂`, "Then γ₁ ≠ γ₂ …") is not in the book. Fact 10.3 is on p. 415: "Fact 10.3 (Computing DL from two representations). Suppose we are given (α, β) and (α′, β′), which are two different representations (relative to g and h) of the same group element. Then we can efficiently compute Dlog_g h as follows: Dlog_g h = (α − α′)/(β′ − β)."
   - **(d) Pedersen.** The [Pedersen1991] block is a paraphrase formatted as a quote. Section 3 (p. 131) defines `E(s, t) = g^s h^t`, and Theorem 3.1 reads: "For any s ∈ Z_q and for randomly uniformly chosen t ∈ Z_q, E(s,t) is uniformly distributed in G_q. If s, s′ ∈ Z_q satisfies s ≠ s′ and E(s,t) = E(s′,t′), then t ≠ t′ mod q and log_g h = (s − s′)/(t′ − t) mod q."
     - This matches `pedersenCommitLaw_eq_uniform_of_ne_zero`, which makes Pedersen's implicit `h ≠ 1` explicit, and `pedersenExtractNat_eq_of_isBindingCollision`.
   - Fix:
     - Replace the four blocks with the source text above, or present them as paraphrases without quotation formatting.
     - Restore the Theorem 10.4 quote.
   - Nonblocking wording: the Lean docstrings cite "Definition 8.8" for the binding and hiding experiments. Those experiments are the p. 344 bullets of Section 8.12; Definition 8.8 itself only defines "secure".

2. **`CommitmentScheme.hidingForKey` lets the adversary challenge with invalid messages** (`Commitment.lean:1305-1311`).
   - Section 8.12 has the adversary send "m0, m1 ∈ M". Here `choice.1` can be any words, including words outside `S.ValidMessage k`.
   - With the new `ValidMessage` field, this makes `StatisticalHiding` and `ComputationalHiding` strictly stronger than Boneh–Shoup's hiding. Take a scheme with message space `{[]}` whose commitment string is the message word. It is perfectly hiding in Boneh–Shoup's sense, since there is only one message. Yet it fails `StatisticalHiding` here: I checked locally that `¬ singletonScheme.StatisticalHiding` (code below).
   - Pedersen is unaffected, because its `commitDist` depends only on `ofBits msg` mod `q`. The general definition, however, is what later results will assume.
   - Fix: commit to `m_b` only when both words are valid, so invalid choices make the two worlds identical, for example:
     ```lean
     let msg := open Classical in
       if bit ∧ S.ValidMessage k choice.1.1 ∧ S.ValidMessage k choice.1.2 then choice.1.2
       else choice.1.1
     ```
     I tried this locally. The Pedersen module and its tests build unchanged, and the counterexample no longer goes through.
   - Alternatively, keep the stronger game, and state the strengthening in the `hidingForKey` docstring and in the PR's "Differences from textbook statements".

3. **Add a regression witness that the repaired `Binding` is nonvacuous.**
   - In the previous revision, `Binding` held for every scheme. A test that a non-binding scheme fails it pins the fix.
   - The `openScheme` below has an empty commitment string and opening equal to the message. A constant adversary breaks it with probability 1, and the adversary's PPT certificate is plain.
   - The proof checks at this head.

<details><summary>Witnesses (checked at c68398d3)</summary>

```lean
import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.PedersenCommitment
import Complexity.Crypto.Negligible.Basic
import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.PPT

open Cslib Cslib.Probability Cslib.Crypto Turing.MultiTapeTM
open scoped NNReal

/-- Commitment string empty, opening = message: perfectly hiding, not binding. -/
noncomputable def openScheme : CommitmentScheme Unit where
  encodeKey _ := []
  ValidMessage _ _ := True
  commitDist _ m := PMF.pure ([], m)
  verify _ m c o := decide (c = [] ∧ o = m)
  validMessage_of_verify _ _ _ _ _ := trivial
  verify_of_mem_support _ m co _ hco := by
    rw [PMF.support_pure, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hco
    subst hco
    simp

def cheat : ℕ → List Bool →
    ProbComp (List Bool × (List Bool × List Bool) × (List Bool × List Bool)) :=
  fun _ _ => pure ([], ([], []), ([true], [true]))

example : ¬ openScheme.Binding (fun _ => PMF.pure ()) := by
  intro h
  have hA : IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encBits)
      (encPair encBits (encPair (encPair encBits encBits) (encPair encBits encBits)))
      (fun input => cheat input.1 input.2) :=
    ComputableInPolyTime.isPPTOn (ComputableInPolyTime.const _)
  have hs : ∀ n, Game.succProbability
      (openScheme.bindingGame (fun _ => PMF.pure ()) cheat n) = 1 := by
    intro n
    simp [Game.succProbability, CommitmentScheme.bindingGame, CommitmentScheme.isBindingCollision,
      openScheme, cheat]
  exact not_negligible_const (c := 1) one_ne_zero (by simpa [hs] using h cheat hA)

/-- Message space `{[]}`, commitment string = message word: hiding in the sense of Section 8.12,
but the adversary here may challenge with the invalid word `[true]`. -/
noncomputable def singletonScheme : CommitmentScheme Unit where
  encodeKey _ := []
  ValidMessage _ m := m = []
  commitDist _ m := PMF.pure (m, [])
  verify _ m c _ := decide (m = [] ∧ c = [])
  validMessage_of_verify _ _ _ _ h := by simp at h; exact h.1
  verify_of_mem_support _ m co hm hco := by
    rw [PMF.support_pure, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hco
    subst hco
    simp [hm]

def distinguisher : Encryption.WordAdversary where
  choose _ _ := pure (([], [true]), [])
  guess _ _ c := pure (decide (c = [true]))

example : ¬ singletonScheme.StatisticalHiding (fun _ => PMF.pure ()) := by
  intro h
  have hadv : ∀ n, Game.advantage
      (singletonScheme.hidingGame (fun _ => PMF.pure ()) distinguisher false n)
      (singletonScheme.hidingGame (fun _ => PMF.pure ()) distinguisher true n) = 1 := by
    intro n
    simp [CommitmentScheme.hidingGame, CommitmentScheme.hidingForKey, singletonScheme,
      distinguisher]
    rw [Game.advantage_comm, Game.advantage_pure_false]
    simp [Game.succProbability]
  exact not_negligible_const (c := 1) one_ne_zero (by simpa [hadv] using h distinguisher trivial)
```
</details>

**Nonblocking**

4. **A tidy certificate in the tests.** `ComplexityTests/Crypto/PedersenCommitment.lean:93` certifies the constant adversary with `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.isPPTOn (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.const _)`. The plain `ComputableInPolyTime.isPPTOn (ComputableInPolyTime.const _)` works, as in the witness above, and adds no new tidy use (#862).
5. **Duplicate generalization in #1053.** #1053 adds `Encryption.AdversaryOf`, `INDCPAOf` and `WordINDCPA` in the same form, and `WordINDCPA` has no client in this PR. Whichever PR lands second should drop the duplicate hunk.
6. **Efficiency is undocumented for `verify`.** Boneh–Shoup's `(C, V)` is "a pair of efficient algorithms", but `CommitmentScheme` requires efficiency of neither. The docstring explains this for `commitDist` but not for `verify`, and `pedersenVerify` is not certified polynomial-time. One sentence would cover it.

reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-60 — APPROVED at 60b9c616017e8158a5344b7205702c01a92438bd

Agent review, not human approval. This is a delta review of `c68398d3..60b9c616` (one commit), after reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-57's review ([comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1043#issuecomment-6401105628)). The base is unchanged at `0b838c43`, and `git range-diff` shows commits 1–5 identical. I checked the quotes word for word against two sources: the Boneh–Shoup v0.6 text, using its printed page footers, and the scan of Pedersen's paper (LNCS 576, p. 131).

**Reviewer-57's blocking findings: all resolved**
1. **Quotes.** Every quoted block in "Primary-Source Audit" is now source text.
   - The §8.12 commitment definition (p. 344) and Definition 8.8 (p. 344) are verbatim.
   - The Binding and Hiding bullets are verbatim excerpts, with the omissions marked by ellipses.
   - Fact 10.3 (p. 415) is verbatim, and the Theorem 10.4 excerpt is restored.
   - Pedersen's Theorem 3.1 matches the scan.
   - Exercise 20.5 is a paraphrase without quote formatting, which is fine.
   - The Lean docstrings now cite "Section 8.12, p. 344, and Definition 8.8", and give p. 415 for Fact 10.3.
2. **Hiding.**
   - **The change.** `CommitmentScheme.hidingForKey` (`Commitment.lean:1311`) now commits to `m₁` only when `bit` holds and both words satisfy `S.ValidMessage k`. Otherwise it commits to `m₀`.
   - **Why it matches the source.** Valid challenge pairs reproduce Experiment b of Boneh–Shoup exactly, and invalid pairs make the two worlds identical. So `StatisticalHiding` and `ComputationalHiding` now match §8.12's "m0, m1 ∈ M", and the docstring says so.
   - **The counterexample is pinned.** Reviewer-57's counterexample no longer goes through, and the test file now proves the opposite: `singletonScheme.StatisticalHiding (fun _ => PMF.pure ())`.
   - **Pedersen is unaffected.** `hidingForKey_eq_of_map_fst_commitDist_eq` and the Pedersen hiding theorems apply unchanged, because their hypothesis is message independence for all words.
3. **Regression test.** `example : ¬ openScheme.Binding (fun _ => PMF.pure ())` pins the verifier-based binding. It uses the constant `cheat` adversary with a plain `ComputableInPolyTime` certificate.

**Reviewer-57's nonblocking items**
- **4 (tidy certificate):** fixed; the test now uses `ComputableInPolyTime.isPPTOn (ComputableInPolyTime.const _)`.
- **6 (efficiency of `verify`):** documented in the `CommitmentScheme` docstring.
- **5 (overlap with #1053):** see below.

**Earlier evidence that still holds.** The delta changes only `hidingForKey`'s choice of message, docstrings and tests. The Pedersen mathematics is unchanged:
- perfect hiding for `h ≠ 0`;
- the `1/m` bound over a uniform key exponent;
- verifier-based extraction;
- the exact strict-PPT reduction to `discreteLogGame`.

Reviewer-57's conclusions on these, and on the earlier rounds' fixes, stand.

**Validation**
- **Hosted CI.** `ci-checks` passed at this head ([run 40219615746](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40219615746)), including build, test, lint and the tidy ratchet.
- **Mergeability.** The branch merges cleanly with `main` at `a512b10b`. That run predates #1049 (`EncryptThenMAC`), which touches none of the files changed here. The merge queue will confirm.

**Overlap with #1053 (nonblocking)**
- **Identical hunks.** Both PRs carry byte-identical `Encryption/Basic.lean` and `Encryption/PolyTime.lean`, which add `AdversaryOf`, `INDCPAOf`, `WordAdversary` and `WordINDCPA`. Whichever PR lands second loses those hunks on rebase, without a conflict.
- **ROADMAP conflict.** Both PRs edit the same `ROADMAP.md` line ("Diffie–Hellman and ElGamal"), so the second one to land will conflict there.

**Nit (nonblocking)**
- **Page locator.** `PedersenCommitment.lean:540` and `:551` cite Theorem 10.4 at "pp. 414–415", but the theorem and its proof are on p. 415 only. The PR body has the same locator.

body: Follow-up note (`coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`): this PR introduces `Encryption.WordINDCPA` (`Msg = List Bool`), which does not yet require the two challenge messages to have the same length, as the textbook games do. It is therefore strictly stronger than the textbook notion; see pre-check 6401713216 on #1096 and 6401720487 on #1053. This PR has no client of `WordINDCPA`, so I am letting it land, and the fix goes in one shared place: an admissibility relation on the challenge pair. #1053, which carries the same hunk, and #1096's 1CCA game will adopt it.

body:
Closes #1040.

### Summary (Mathematical & Infrastructure Progress)
- **Shared two-stage adversary interface (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/Basic.lean`)**:
  - Generalizes `Encryption.AdversaryOf (Msg : Type)` with `Encryption.WordAdversary := AdversaryOf (List Bool)`, reused by both encryption IND-CPA and commitment chosen-message hiding.
- **Public-parameter commitment scheme interface (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Commitment.lean`)**:

  3. In `pedersenKeyDist`, $\alpha$ is drawn uniformly from all of `ZMod (F.order d)` (matching `discreteLogGame` and [BonehShoup2023], Exercise 20.5), so the degenerate key $\alpha = 0$ ($h = 0$) occurs with probability $1 / \text{order}(d)$, giving exact hiding for every fixed $h \ne 0$ (`pedersenHidingForKey_eq_of_ne_zero`, matching Pedersen's Theorem 3.1 with $h \neq 1$ made explicit) and hiding advantage $\le 1/m$ over `pedersenKeyDist` when supported groups have order $\ge m$ (`advantage_pedersenHidingGame_le`).

reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-43 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 45f21b5582098e76fd779185cb4da959c7d430ad

Agent review, not human approval. I checked the statements against the authors' STOC 2019 PDF ([people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf](https://people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf)).

**What holds.**
- The main bound is sound and matches the #798 design: "MMW19 Theorem 1.4 (third bullet), specialized to plain De Morgan circuits, decision MCSP and no depth bound".
  - Under `NP encBits ⊆ PPolyOn encBits`, `∃ c > 0, ∀ s n, complexity (single ((MCSPAt s).slice (2 ^ n))) ≤ 2 ^ n * c * (n + s n + 1) ^ c`. That is `N · poly(n + s(n))` fan-in-2 De Morgan gates, with one constant for all `s`.
  - The conditional is stated as a conditional, with no hidden hypothesis.
  - Because `c` is uniform in `s`, the contrapositive may choose `s` depending on `c`, which is slightly stronger than the source. Dropping `s(n) ≥ n` is harmless because the bound is in `n + s(n)`.
- Circuit size is the library's `complexity interpretation (single _)`, and certificates come from `readCertificate`/`certLength`. Soundness and completeness go through `exists_circuit_of_checkCertificate`/`exists_checkCertificate_append`. No public statement mentions tidy.
- The `CircuitMinMergeLanguage` yes-instance in the tests is a real check.
- Hosted `ci-checks` passed at this head ([run 40205028121](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40205028121)). The branch merges cleanly with current `main`.

**Blocking**

1. **Second name for the MCSP language.** `MCSPAt` (`Magnification.lean:86`) is an `abbrev` for `GapMCSP.yesSet`, and `ofFn_mem_MCSPAt_iff` (`:90`) restates `GapMCSP.ofFn_mem_yesSet_iff`, with that lemma as its proof.
   - Fix: state everything with `GapMCSP.yesSet s`, and move `slice_MCSPAt_eq_true_iff` to `MCSP/Basic.lean` as `GapMCSP.slice_yesSet_eq_true_iff`.
   - If `MCSP[s]` deserves a better name, rename it at the source and update clients, rather than adding a second name.
2. **A partial second certificate verifier** (#884 F2 removed the last one).
   - `validCert` (`:145`) repeats `checkCertificate`'s well-formedness conjunct, `codeCheck m c.1 && decide (c.2 < m + c.1.length)`, from `MCSP/NP.lean:108`. `evalCert` (`:151`) repeats its evaluation, `evalOutput y c.1 c.2` on `readCertificate`.
   - `computableInPolyTime_validCert`/`_evalCert` (`:189`, `:218`) re-prove polynomial time for those pieces.
   - The all-inputs conjunct cannot be reused, because `n` is unary here, so quantifying over inputs (`AgreesWithChildren`) is right.
   - Fix: name the two pieces once in `MCSP/NP.lean`, define `checkCertificate` from them, and use them here.
3. **A second copy of Karp–Lipton quantifier elimination.**
   - The private `PPolyOn_exists_of_computableInPolyTime_length`/`PPolyOn_forall_…` (`:379–425`) redo the existential step that the successor case of `SigmaP_subset_PPolyOn_of_NP_subset_PPoly` (`KarpLipton.lean:314`) already performs through `mem_PPoly_of_exists_frame_append`.
   - `PPolyOn_inter`/`PPolyOn_union` (`:358`, `:364`) are closure properties of the public `PPolyOn`. Per #926 they belong beside `PPolyOn.compl` in `PPoly.lean`, as public lemmas.
   - Fix, either way leaving one copy:
     - (a) show `CircuitMinMergeLanguage ∈ SigmaP 3 encMerge` (MMW: "any bit of the output … can be computed by a Σ₃^A machine") and finish with `SigmaP_subset_PPolyOn_of_NP_subset_PPoly`; or
     - (b) make the bounded-∃ closure lemma public in `KarpLipton.lean` and derive the successor case of `SigmaP_subset_PPolyOn_of_NP_subset_PPoly` from it.
4. **Attribution and the new-statement standard.**
   - (a) `exists_complexity_MCSPAt_le_of_NP_subset_PPoly` and `_pow_` are labeled "MMW19 Lemma 3.1", but that lemma is unconditional: "There is a uniform AC circuit family for MCSP^A[s(n)] of Õ(2^n · s(n)/ℓ(n)) size and O(n/log ℓ(n)) depth with Circuit-Min-Merge^A[s(n)] oracle gates, where each oracle gate takes only ℓ(n) bits of input." The Lean statement is the `C = P/poly` case of the *proof of Theorem 1.4* (Section 5): Lemma 3.1's merge tree with the oracle gates replaced by polynomial-size circuits. It also uses a binary tree over subcubes, not the `d`-ary tree with `ℓ = s³`. Relabel the docstrings, the module doc and the PR body.
   - (b) The Theorem 1.4 docstrings (`:1114–1156`) should state the specialization:
     - decision `MCSP[s]` instead of search-MCSP^A[s];
     - no oracle;
     - fan-in-2 De Morgan circuits;
     - a size-only bound, where the source has size `N·poly(s)` and depth `poly(s)`.

     Each makes the Lean hypothesis stronger than the source's, so the Lean theorems are special cases. A decision lower bound implies a search lower bound, since a search circuit plus an `N·poly(s)` check decides. A size-only lower bound implies a size-and-depth one. Please say this. The same applies to `CircuitMinMergeLanguage`: it takes the least valid size-`≤ s` certificate under `wordLt`, not "the lexicographically first minimum-size circuit", over two half-subcubes rather than `t` intervals. Call it "adapted from" MMW's Circuit-Min-Merge.
   - (c) The PR body needs the verbatim source statement with its locator (AGENTS.md, new-statement standard). For example, Theorem 1.4: "Let s(n) ≥ n, and let A ∈ PH. … If search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on inputs of length N = 2^n does not have circuits of N · poly(s(n)) size and poly(s(n)) depth, then NP ⊄ P/poly."
   - (d) The body also says the proof uses `PH.subset_PPoly` and a Σ₂ certificate "`CircuitMinMergeLanguage = Projection (CoProjection MergeBaseLanguage)`". None of these exist in the code, and the language is Σ₃. Describe the proof the code gives.

**Nonblocking**

5. `inSubcube p x := x.take p.length == p` (`:232`) is core's `p.isPrefixOf x`.
6. In `ComplexityTests/Magnification.lean`, the eight `example … := theorem` lines only restate signatures (CONTRIBUTING, quality standard 8). Keep the concrete checks; a no-instance of `CircuitMinMergeLanguage` would be a good addition.

Agent review, not human approval. This is a delta review against 45f21b55 and reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-43's comment 6399442094. I checked the source text against the authors' STOC 2019 PDF.

**Resolved since 45f21b55**
- **Item 1.** `MCSPAt` and `ofFn_mem_MCSPAt_iff` are gone, every statement uses `GapMCSP.yesSet s`, and `GapMCSP.slice_yesSet_eq_true_iff` now lives in `MCSP/Basic.lean`.
- **Item 3, option (b).** `PPolyOn.exists_of_computableInPolyTime_length` is public in `KarpLipton.lean`, and the successor case of `SigmaP_subset_PPolyOn_of_NP_subset_PPoly` is now derived from it. `PPolyOn.sup`/`inf` sit beside `PPolyOn.compl`. The private copies are deleted, so one copy remains.
- **Item 4(a), (b), (d).**
  - The upper-bound docstrings now cite the `C = P/poly` case of the proof of Theorem 1.4 and mention the binary subcube tree.
  - The four specializations are stated in the module doc and in each Theorem 1.4 docstring.
  - The body no longer mentions `PH.subset_PPoly` or Σ₂.
- **Items 5 and 6** are done.
- **Core bound.** Apart from replacing `MCSPAt` with its definitional unfolding, the statement is unchanged:
  - `NP encBits ⊆ PPolyOn encBits → ∃ c > 0, ∀ s n, complexity (single ((GapMCSP.yesSet s).slice (2 ^ n))) ≤ 2 ^ n * c * (n + s n + 1) ^ c`.
  - `c` is fixed from the P/poly constant before `s` and `n` are chosen, and there is no other hypothesis.
  - The tree-composition proof is unchanged. The only changes to the proof are renames and the new public ∃/∀ lemmas.
  - The diff has no `sorry`, `axiom` or `native_decide`.

**Blocking**

1. **The branch does not merge with `main`, and hosted CI has not run at this head.**
   - GitHub reports `CONFLICTING`. `Complexity/Computability/MCSP/NP.lean` conflicts with #1034, which added `checkCertificateOn`.
   - The last `Lean Action CI` run is at 45f21b55 ([run 40205028121](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40205028121)). No workflow has run for 888c1db8.
   - Fix: rebase onto `main`.
2. **Item 2 reopens after the rebase: one certificate verifier.**
   - On `main`, `checkCertificateOn` (`NP.lean:121`) inlines the well-formedness conjunct `codeCheck m c.1 && decide (c.2 < m + c.1.length)` and the evaluation `evalOutput (input t) c.1 c.2`. `computableInPolyTime_checkCertificateOn` re-proves polynomial time for both.
   - This PR names those pieces `validCertificate` and `evalCertificate` (`NP.lean:111`, `:116`). Leave one copy, either way:
     - (a) define `checkCertificateOn` from `validCertificate`/`evalCertificate`, and derive `computableInPolyTime_checkCertificateOn` from `computableInPolyTime_validCertificate`/`_evalCertificate`; or
     - (b) drop the new pieces and use `checkCertificateOn` in `Magnification.lean`, for example with the tests `[x]` for the point check.
   - `exists_circuit_of_validCertificate` and `exists_validCertificate_of_circuit` (`Magnification.lean:140`, `:152`) are soundness and completeness for public `NP.lean` definitions. Per #926 they should be public beside those definitions. Alternatively, replace them with `exists_circuit_of_checkCertificateOn`/`exists_checkCertificateOn_append`.
3. **Item 4(c): source quotes and locators.**
   - **The Theorem 1.4 quote in the PR body is not in the paper.** The paper has no "for all c > 0", no "N · s^c and depth s^c", and no "NP^A ⊄ P/poly (and P^A ≠ NP^A)". Replace it with the source text: "Theorem 1.4 (Section 5). Let s(n) ≥ n, and let A ∈ PH. … • If search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on inputs of length N = 2^n does not have circuits of N · poly(s(n)) size and poly(s(n)) depth, then NP ⊄ P/poly."
