title: feat(threshold): realize ordered scalar classes by real comparison trees
body:
Refs #1138. Stacked on #1134: review this diff against `feat/scalar-capacity-1132-chatgpt`; retarget to main after that dependency lands.

Adds `WeightedThreshold.exists_scalarComparisonTree_iff` in ScalarActivity. A supplied class index `index x < L`, strictly ordered by the real score `weightedSum w x`, is computed by a real-threshold tree with exactly `L` structural leaves, depth ≤ `q`, and true-answer energy ≤ `e` iff `0 < L ∧ L ≤ BitString.ballSize q e`. The construction relabels #1134's integer queries with `DecisionTree.mapQueries`, preserving shape and resources. Each integer cut uses the least score in its upper class, or a threshold above all scores when the upper class is empty. Equality takes the true branch. Negative/fractional weights and tied scores within a class are allowed.

A class can contain several distinct scores, and several inputs can share one score. The ordering premise rules out different class indices at the same score. If every index below L occurs, every counted leaf is reached; otherwise L is an exact structural leaf count and unused leaves are permitted. No minimality of the supplied partition is claimed.

## Source and scope

Source: proof of Theorem 4.1 of *Threshold Circuits as Decision Trees and Finite-State Programs*, [manuscript commit 451c4f88, line 541](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/threshold-circuits/blob/451c4f88151e5843ab4e7f1da93077a225c506a9/threshold_circuit_representations.tex#L541):
> Query a threshold between the groups and recurse

Source score is `weightedSum w x`, ordered runs are supplied by `index`, and `q/e/L` are depth/true-answer/leaf budgets. The separator lemma is private proof plumbing. All previous public statements and circuit lower bounds are unchanged. No parallel model or capacity definition is introduced.

**Remaining:** automatic extraction of maximal monochromatic runs, Boolean output relabelling as needed, and compilation into q native input-reading circuit stages. This is not the full scalar-circuit iff or the O(qe+N) normalization compiler. The explicit extractor port also remains open.

## Tests and validation

Hosted [Lean Action CI run 40255975290](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40255975290) succeeded at head `a1dea0240ba85922c6337e476fc434ec7adbac0e`, including the full build, tests, lint and import/style checks. No local Lean/Lake run is claimed. Independent exact-head mathematical/API review is still required before integration.

The first run compiled the theorem but found two test-only issues: a file-wide Classical scope and a real-division definition lacking `noncomputable`. The current head fixes both without changing the theorem.

ScalarComparisonCapacity tests Hamming-weight ties with a concrete depth-two/energy-one tree, equality at thresholds, signed fractional scores realizing all four classes, impossibility above capacity, the zero direction, zero-dimensional inputs, and impossibility of distinguishing equal scores with any tree. Tests use the existing Lake glob; no library aggregate change is needed.

An exact-rational Python mirror additionally checked 21,166 relabelled trees and 277,052 scalar evaluations across 588 score partitions, including merged classes and empty upper cuts. These finite checks supplement, not replace, the Lean verification.

No curated abstract: this is a supporting realization theorem, not the completed circuit endpoint.

AI-authored by ChatGPT session `worker-chatgpt-scalar-realization-20261026`. Author self-review only; no independent or human approval is claimed. Coordinator review requested.

body:
Closes #1130.

The median laws and coordinatewise Hamming-distance proofs in `Complexity/Foundations/Data/BitString/Hamming.lean` repeated expanded Boolean expressions in eleven local truth-table lemmas. This replaces those copies with small case splits, keeping the extensionality and coordinate-sum arguments visible. The affected proof bodies shrink from 65 lines to 33 (18 additions, 50 deletions overall).

All public declarations, statements, definition bodies, imports, attributes and docstrings are unchanged. The curated abstract catalogue is unaffected. Existing `ComplexityTests.CircuitHamming.Gates` coverage includes concrete distances, median identities, empty-index cases, and the guards that `median_assoc` and `median_median_distrib` use only `Quot.sound`.

All six required validation gates pass in [Lean Action CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40255552459) for commit `25fe517137c8f9a413d891fb78811653993f33f3`: strict library build, import-aggregate check, full tests, lint, style, and Init imports. Local strict build, full tests (including the global axiom audit), targeted Hamming tests, source hygiene, abstract catalogue, changed-file lints, and PR-description name checks also pass.

Internal source review by non-authoring agent hamming_review found no issues in blob `ac28bc6d6be9a828221c23c551259e0e6481b5e4`. Ready for coordinator review; this internal review is not maintainer approval.

diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,300 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Renfei Zhou. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Renfei Zhou
+-/
+
+-- upstream: local-only (formal abstract library)
+
+import ComplexityAbstracts.Check
+import ComplexityAbstracts.RandomizedWordRAMBridge
+import Cslib.Probability.PMF
+import Mathlib.Data.List.Sort
+import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log
+
+/-! # The randomized word RAM and in-place quicksort: a formal abstract
+
+This file states the randomized word-RAM model, its worst-case and expected running time, and the
+correctness and cost bounds of randomized in-place three-way quicksort.
+
+At word size `w`, a *word* is a natural number below `2 ^ w`. A machine has `r` registers
+`R[0], …, R[r - 1]` and memory `M[a]` for `a : ℕ`. Its ten deterministic instructions, `init`, and
+`InputFits` match `WordRAMAbstract` (restated because an abstract cannot import another abstract,
+and in-place algorithms inspect final memory at `halt`). Alongside them, `rand d i` reads
+`n = R[i]`, faults when `n ≥ 2 ^ w`, and otherwise draws a uniform integer in `{0, …, n}` into
+`R[d]` in one step and one random call (`n = 0` returns `0` and still counts as one call).
+
+Simplifications relative to `Cslib.WordRAM` and `Cslib.Algorithms.WordRAM.Quicksort`:
+
+* `AluOp` fixes `Basis.exact` (as in `WordRAMAbstract`) instead of a general `Basis`. The bridge
+  lifts `Quicksort` from `Basis.standard` because it uses no division or remainder and no reached
+  subtraction underflows.
+* `Instr` lists the eleven flat instructions directly instead of `Op`, `Cond`, and `Code`.
+* `Comp` specializes `ProbComp` to finite-depth uniform trees over `Fin (n + 1)` with direct
+  `CallsAtMost` and `Comp.eval` (`RandBitsBounded` stays in the library).
+* `State` and `Cfg.halted` carry `reg` and `mem` directly without `Data`, keeping final registers
+  and memory at `halt` for in-place postconditions.
+* Array slices and unchanged memory use `slice` and address bounds instead of `Block.Realizes` and
+  `Modifies`, and `logWidth 3 n` is written inline as `3 * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`.
+
+Lean checks the proofs via `RandomizedWordRAMBridge` under `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and
+`Quot.sound`; `#check_abstract` verifies zero allowlisted project modules.
+
+## References
+
+* [T. H. Cormen, C. E. Leiserson, R. L. Rivest and C. Stein, *Introduction to
+  Algorithms*][CLRS2009]
+* [M. L. Fredman and D. E. Willard, *Surpassing the information theoretic bound with fusion
+  trees*][FredmanWillard1993]
+* [M. Mitzenmacher and E. Upfal, *Probability and Computing*][MitzenmacherUpfal2017]
+-/
+
+namespace ComplexityAbstracts.RandomizedWordRAMAbstract
+
+/-! ## Words, operations, and instructions
+
+Each arithmetic, bitwise, or shift operation in `AluOp` computes its exact value on natural
+numbers, returning `none` where undefined (`x - y` when `y > x`, and `x / 0` and `x % 0`). In
+`AluOp.eval`, a bare natural number stands for `some n`. The instruction `rand d i` draws a
+uniform integer in `{0, …, R[i]}`.
+-/
+
+/-- The ten exact binary operations on natural numbers. -/
+inductive AluOp
+  | add | sub | mul | div | mod | and | or | xor | shl | shr
+
+/-- Exact value of a binary operation before word-range checking, or `none` when undefined. -/
+def AluOp.eval : AluOp → ℕ → ℕ → Option ℕ
+  | .add, x, y => x + y
+  | .sub, x, y => if y ≤ x then x - y else none
+  | .mul, x, y => x * y
+  | .div, x, y => if y = 0 then none else x / y
+  | .mod, x, y => if y = 0 then none else x % y
+  | .and, x, y => x &&& y
+  | .or, x, y => x ||| y
+  | .xor, x, y => x ^^^ y
+  | .shl, x, y => some (x * 2 ^ y)
+  | .shr, x, y => some (x / 2 ^ y)
+
+/-- Instructions over `r` registers: ten deterministic instructions and bounded random sampling
+`rand`. -/
+inductive Instr (r : ℕ)
+  | const (d : Fin r) (x : ℕ)         -- R[d] := x
+  | copy (d i : Fin r)                -- R[d] := R[i]
+  | alu (f : AluOp) (d i j : Fin r)   -- R[d] := f(R[i], R[j])
+  | width (d : Fin r)                 -- R[d] := w, the word size
+  | load (d a : Fin r)                -- R[d] := M[R[a]]
+  | store (a i : Fin r)               -- M[R[a]] := R[i]
+  | jump (t : ℕ)                      -- go to instruction t
+  | branchEq (i j : Fin r) (t : ℕ)    -- go to t if R[i] = R[j], else next
+  | branchLt (i j : Fin r) (t : ℕ)    -- go to t if R[i] < R[j], else next
+  | halt (i : Fin r)                  -- stop with output R[i]
+  | rand (d i : Fin r)                -- R[d] ← uniform on {0, …, R[i]}
+
+/-- A program over `r` registers is a list of instructions indexed from `0`. -/
+abbrev Program (r : ℕ) := List (Instr r)
+
+/-! ## Finite-depth uniform sampling trees
+
+A clocked execution builds a finite-depth tree `Comp α` of uniform draws `sample n next` over
+`Fin (n + 1)` (`{0, …, n}`). Keeping the tree separates output distributions from pathwise call
+counts, including `rand` on `0` whose output distribution is a point mass. `Comp.eval` maps a tree
+to a discrete probability distribution (`PMF α`), and `Comp.CallsAtMost m R` states that every
+branch makes at most `R` draws.
+-/
+
+/-- A finite-depth computation tree whose random choices draw uniformly from `Fin (n + 1)`. -/
+inductive Comp (α : Type) : Type
+  | pure (a : α)
+  | sample (n : ℕ) (next : Fin (n + 1) → Comp α)
+
+/-- Sequential composition of sampling trees. -/
+def Comp.bind {α β : Type} : Comp α → (α → Comp β) → Comp β
+  | .pure a, f => f a
+  | .sample n next, f => .sample n fun k => (next k).bind f
+
+/-- Probability distribution induced by answering every `sample n` uniformly on `Fin (n + 1)`. -/
+noncomputable def Comp.eval {α : Type} : Comp α → PMF α
+  | .pure a => PMF.pure a
+  | .sample n next =>
+    (Cslib.Probability.PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (n + 1))).bind fun k =>
+      (next k).eval
+
+/-- Every branch of `m` performs at most `R` random draws. -/
+def Comp.CallsAtMost {α : Type} : Comp α → ℕ → Prop
+  | .pure _, _ => True
+  | .sample _ _, 0 => False
+  | .sample _ next, R + 1 => ∀ k, (next k).CallsAtMost R
+
+/-! ## Configurations, clocked runs, and cost measures
+
+A configuration is `running` at a `State`, `halted` with scalar output `v` alongside final registers
+`reg` and memory `mem`, or `faulted`. Both `halted` and `faulted` are absorbing: further clock ticks
+leave them unchanged and make zero `rand` calls.
+
+At an active state `s`, `rand d i` faults when `s.reg i ≥ 2 ^ w`. When `s.reg i < 2 ^ w`, it draws
+`k` uniformly from `Fin (s.reg i + 1)` (`{0, …, s.reg i}`), writes `k` to `R[d]`, and advances `pc`
+to `pc + 1` in one step and one `sample` node.
+
+Expected running time `expectedTime w p s` takes values in the extended nonnegative reals `ENNReal`
+(`[0, ∞]`). It sums over `t : ℕ` the probability that the configuration after `t` steps is
+`running`. Because `halted` and `faulted` are absorbing, a branch that halts after `n` steps is
+`running` at horizons `0, 1, …, n - 1` and contributes `n`, while non-terminating mass contributes
+`∞`.
+-/
+
+/-- Machine state: instruction index `pc`, registers `reg`, and memory `mem`. -/
+structure State (r : ℕ) where
+  /-- Index of the next instruction. -/
+  pc : ℕ
+  /-- Register file `R[0], …, R[r - 1]`. -/
+  reg : Fin r → ℕ
+  /-- Unbounded natural-addressed memory `M[a]`. -/
+  mem : ℕ → ℕ
+
+/-- Configuration of a clocked randomized run: active, halted with final data, or faulted. -/
+inductive Cfg (r : ℕ)
+  | running (s : State r)
+  | halted (v : ℕ) (reg : Fin r → ℕ) (mem : ℕ → ℕ)
+  | faulted
+
+/-- One step of program `p` at word size `w`. Halted and faulted configurations are absorbing. -/
+def stepRand {r : ℕ} (w : ℕ) (p : Program r) : Cfg r → Comp (Cfg r)
+  | .halted v reg mem => .pure (.halted v reg mem)
+  | .faulted => .pure .faulted
+  | .running s =>
+    let next (d : Fin r) (x : ℕ) : Comp (Cfg r) :=
+      .pure (.running
+        { s with pc := s.pc + 1, reg := Function.update s.reg d x })
+    let nextWord (d : Fin r) (x : ℕ) : Comp (Cfg r) :=
+      if x < 2 ^ w then next d x else .pure .faulted
+    match p[s.pc]? with
+    | none => .pure .faulted
+    | some (.const d x) => nextWord d x
+    | some (.copy d i) => next d (s.reg i)
+    | some (.alu f d i j) =>
+      match f.eval (s.reg i) (s.reg j) with
+      | some x => nextWord d x
+      | none => .pure .faulted
+    | some (.width d) => next d w
+    | some (.load d a) => next d (s.mem (s.reg a))
+    | some (.store a i) =>
+      .pure (.running { s with
+        pc := s.pc + 1
+        mem := Function.update s.mem (s.reg a) (s.reg i) })
+    | some (.jump t) => .pure (.running { s with pc := t })
+    | some (.branchEq i j t) =>
+      .pure (.running
+        { s with pc := if s.reg i = s.reg j then t else s.pc + 1 })
+    | some (.branchLt i j t) =>
+      .pure (.running
+        { s with pc := if s.reg i < s.reg j then t else s.pc + 1 })
+    | some (.halt i) => .pure (.halted (s.reg i) s.reg s.mem)
+    | some (.rand d i) =>
+      if s.reg i < 2 ^ w then
+        .sample (s.reg i) fun k => next d k.val
+      else .pure .faulted
+
+/-- Clocked `T`-step sampling tree from configuration `cfg`. -/
+def runRand {r : ℕ} (w : ℕ) (p : Program r) : ℕ → Cfg r → Comp (Cfg r)
+  | 0, cfg => .pure cfg
+  | T + 1, cfg => (stepRand w p cfg).bind (runRand w p T)
+
+/-- Distribution over configurations after `T` steps starting from state `s`. -/
+noncomputable def evalRand {r : ℕ} (w : ℕ) (p : Program r) (T : ℕ)
+    (s : State r) : PMF (Cfg r) :=
+  (runRand w p T (.running s)).eval
+
+/-- Every positive-probability outcome after `T` steps from `s` has halted cleanly. -/
+def HaltsWithin {r : ℕ} (w : ℕ) (p : Program r) (s : State r) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∀ cfg ∈ (evalRand w p T s).support, ∃ v reg mem, cfg = .halted v reg mem
+
+/-- Every execution branch over `T` steps from `s` makes at most `R` `rand` calls. -/
+def RandCallsBounded {r : ℕ} (w : ℕ) (p : Program r) (s : State r)
+    (T R : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  (runRand w p T (.running s)).CallsAtMost R
+
+/-- Expected running time in `ENNReal`, as the sum over `t` of the probability of still running. -/
+noncomputable def expectedTime {r : ℕ} (w : ℕ) (p : Program r)
+    (s : State r) : ENNReal :=
+  ∑' t : ℕ,
+    (evalRand w p t s).toOuterMeasure {cfg | ∃ u, cfg = .running u}
+
+/-! ## Input convention, memory slices, and randomized quicksort
+
+An input `x₁, …, xₖ` starts at `init` with `M[0] = k`, `M[1] = x₁, …, M[k] = xₖ`, and `0`
+elsewhere; `slice a b mem` reads `[M[a], …, M[b - 1]]`. One fixed 16-register program sorts in
+place by iterative three-way randomized quicksort (splitting around a random pivot into `<`, `=`,
+and `>`), using `M[n + 1 .. 3 n + 1)` as a `2 n`-word stack. At word size
+`w ≥ 3 * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)` (`Nat.log 2 0 = 0`, so `w ≥ 3` addresses `3 n + 3` for all `n`) on any
+word-fitting input, every branch halts within `20 n² + 8 n + 32` steps and `n - 1` `rand` calls,
+leaving a sorted (`Pairwise (· ≤ ·)`) permutation of `input` in `M[1 .. n + 1)` and preserving
+memory outside `1, …, 3 n`. Across all inputs, including duplicates, its expected running time is at
+most `120 n (Nat.log 2 n + 1) + 32`.
+-/
+
+/-- Start state on `input = [x₁, …, xₖ]`: `pc = 0`, registers `0`, `M[0] = k`, `M[1..k] = input`. -/
+def init {r : ℕ} (input : List ℕ) : State r :=
+  ⟨0, fun _ => 0, fun a => (input.length :: input).getD a 0⟩
+
+/-- An input fits word size `w` when its length and every element are words below `2 ^ w`. -/
+def InputFits (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ) : Prop :=
+  input.length < 2 ^ w ∧ ∀ x ∈ input, x < 2 ^ w
+
+/-- The memory slice `[mem a, mem (a + 1), …, mem (b - 1)]` of length `b - a`. -/
+def slice (a b : ℕ) (mem : ℕ → ℕ) : List ℕ :=
+  (List.range (b - a)).map fun i => mem (a + i)
+
+/-- **In-place randomized quicksort.** One fixed 16-register program sorts every word-fitting input
+of length `n` in place at word size `w ≥ 3 * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`. Every branch halts within
+`20 n² + 8 n + 32` steps and `n - 1` `rand` calls with a sorted permutation of `input` in
+`M[1 .. n + 1)` and memory outside `1, …, 3 n` unchanged. Expected running time is at most
+`120 n (Nat.log 2 n + 1) + 32`. -/
+theorem quicksort :
+    ∃ p : Program 16,
+      ∀ (w : ℕ) (input : List ℕ),
+        3 * (Nat.log 2 input.length + 1) ≤ w →
+        InputFits w input →
+        let n := input.length
+        let T := 20 * n ^ 2 + 8 * n + 32
+        HaltsWithin w p (init input) T ∧
+        RandCallsBounded w p (init input) T (n - 1) ∧
+        (∀ cfg ∈ (evalRand w p T (init input)).support,
+          ∃ reg mem, cfg = .halted 0 reg mem ∧
+            (∀ i, reg i < 2 ^ w) ∧
+            (∀ a, mem a < 2 ^ w) ∧
+            (slice 1 (n + 1) mem).Perm input ∧
+            (slice 1 (n + 1) mem).Pairwise (· ≤ ·) ∧
+            (∀ a, a < 1 ∨ 3 * n + 1 ≤ a →
+              mem a = (init (r := 16) input).mem a)) ∧
+        expectedTime w p (init input) ≤
+          ((120 * n * (Nat.log 2 n + 1) + 32 : ℕ) : ENNReal) :=
+  RandomizedWordRAMBridge.quicksort
+    ⟨AluOp, .add, .sub, .mul, .div, .mod, .and, .or, .xor, .shl, .shr,
+      @AluOp.rec, AluOp.eval,
+      Instr, .const, .copy, .alu, .width, .load, .store, .jump,
+      .branchEq, .branchLt, .halt, .rand, @Instr.rec,
+      Comp, @Comp.pure, @Comp.sample, @Comp.bind, @Comp.eval,
+      @Comp.CallsAtMost,
+      State, .mk, Cfg, .running, .halted, .faulted, @stepRand, @runRand⟩
+    (by refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_,
+        ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_,
+        ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;>
+      simp_all [AluOp.eval, Comp.bind, Comp.eval, Comp.CallsAtMost,
+        stepRand, runRand])
+
+/--
+info: 'ComplexityAbstracts.RandomizedWordRAMAbstract.quicksort' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms quicksort

title: feat(probability): generalize rewinding to state-dependent challenges
body:
The shared rewinding lemma previously required uniform challenges. This generalizes its existing experiment laws to a finite challenge distribution that can depend on the saved first-stage state, and proves δ ≥ ε² − κ ε and ε ≤ κ + √δ when each supported state's challenge atoms have mass at most κ. First-stage and answer types remain arbitrary, and the two challenge and answer samples are independent conditional on the saved state.

The new bounds are `Cslib.Probability.Rewinding.sq_sub_mul_le_twice` and `Cslib.Probability.Rewinding.le_add_sqrt_twice`; their statements require only `[Finite T]`.

`Rewinding.once` and `Rewinding.twice` now take the conditional challenge law explicitly. The uniform corollaries retain their names and caller-facing parameters. Forking and Sigma identification now supply their original uniform challenge laws explicitly. Concrete tests cover biased challenges, sharpness at the heavy atom, fresh response randomness, unreachable states, and a uniform marginal whose conditional challenges are deterministic. No sampler-efficiency or new computational-security claim is made. Closes #1131.

This is an original extension of the existing formalization, with no literature-novelty claim. The preserved uniform corollary specializes to Boneh–Shoup v0.6, §19.1, Lemma 19.2, printed p. 758 ([source](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf#page=772)); its displayed conclusion is “Pr[f(X,Y)=1 ∧ f(X,Y′)=1 ∧ Y≠Y′] ≥ ε²−ε/N.” The source assumes finite nonempty state and challenge sets and mutually independent X, Y, Y′, with uniform Y and Y′. Here X is the first-stage outcome, Y and Y′ are the challenges, f is the deterministic-answer special case of the acceptance test, ε is one-run success, and N is the challenge-type cardinality. The existing formalization already allowed an arbitrary first-stage type and randomized answers. The biased extension replaces 1/N by a bound on each conditional challenge atom, not on the marginal distribution.

**Framework friction:** the shared lemma could not directly express a biased conditional challenge law. The existing definitions and proof are generalized in place; no parallel game or adversary interface is introduced.

**Validation:** Passed on the exact tree of `7dcfac10ad2105fb46ee515721f7e9046e6116a4`: `scripts/check.sh` (all six strict project gates), `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, and `python3 -B scripts/check_changed_files.py --base b9804168c880068b36c707a09f63ddd6ffde4e10`. The affected Forking/Sigma clients and new regression module also passed targeted compilation. The published tree exactly matches the reviewed source. Hosted [Lean Action CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40257949779) is running. The exact published description also passes `python3 -B scripts/check_pr_names.py --file /tmp/rewinding-pr-1143.md --base b9804168c880068b36c707a09f63ddd6ffde4e10 --strict`.

**Abstract assessment:** no impact on the selected abstracts, their definitions, statements, models, or scope; no PDF changes.

AI assistance: ChatGPT (GPT-6 Astra Pro) authored the implementation and regression tests. The separate non-authoring agent `/root/rewinding_review` reviewed the mathematics, API, source mapping, and abstract impact. This is agent review; independent coordinator review is requested.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-85 — APPROVED at 5b65c48394bf529138806b0cfe2d571b797998e8

Agent review, not human approval.

Scope: statements, definitions, faithfulness and API of the +509/−13 diff against `main`. Hosted `ci-checks` passes at this exact head ([run 40318829563](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40318829563)), and so does `check-title`. `git merge-tree` against current `main` (`95cf6d73`) is clean. The 13 commits to `main` since the base do not touch CNF, SAT, `#P` or list files. No local build.

What I checked:
- **Count preservation is an exact equality and unconditional.** `CNF.modelCount_toThreeOccurrence` states `φ.toThreeOccurrence.modelCount = φ.modelCount` for every `φ : CNF V`, with no width hypothesis. `modelCount_toThreeSATThree` adds only the width ≤ 3 guard of the existing compiler, and `CNF.modelCount_compact` holds for empty or infinite `V`. All three go through the existing `CNF.modelCount_eq_card_filter`. That lemma is a `Finset.card_bij`, whose injectivity comes from its `↔` hypothesis, so it gives a bijection of solution sets, not a surjection or a `≤`. `ParsimoniousReducible` then gives `∀ φ, SharpThreeSAT φ = SharpThreeSATThree (toThreeSATThree φ)`. The new `eval_toThreeOccurrence_iff` is a correct `↔`: a split assignment is a model exactly when its occurring copies agree with some source model.
- **Not vacuous.** The tests give counts of 0, 1, 2 and 3. They show that `SharpThreeSAT` accepts a width-3 formula on which `SharpThreeSATThree` rejects (count 1 vs. 0), and that the compiler repairs it. The rejected-syntax branch `[[]]` is covered by `decide` and agrees with the 0 returned by `SharpThreeSAT`.
- **The existing construction is reused, not copied.** The reduction is the existing `toThreeSATThree`, with the existing `computableInPolyTime_toThreeSATThree`, `numberCopy_injective` and `CNF.modelCount_relabel`. `satisfiable_toThreeOccurrence` is now derived from the new `iff`, so there is no parallel splitter.
- **No parallel counting notion.** Both counting functions are guarded uses of the existing `CNF.modelCount`, the body of `SharpSAT`. Their guards match `ThreeSAT` (width ≤ 3) and `ThreeSATThree.syntaxCheck`. Both are used later in the stack (`PlanarThreeSATThree.lean` at #1180's head). The statements are plain and use no tidy machinery.
- **Hygiene.** The diff has no `native_decide`, `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `set_option`, and no heartbeat raises.
- **Sources.** Neither the PR text nor the diff quotes anything. Hunt–Marathe–Radhakrishnan–Stearns is not cited in this layer. I checked arXiv cs/9809017v1 anyway. Its parsimony results are about crossover boxes and planar reductions (Theorem 3.2 and onward). I found no bounded-occurrence (3SAT-3) parsimony result there, so it is correctly not cited here.

Nonblocking findings:
1. **Label the new counting results as original.** `Counting.lean:34-36` credits only the construction ("documented in `ThreeSATThree`"). `ThreeOccurrence.lean` cites Papadimitriou Prop. 9.3 only for the construction and the NP-hardness. Neither file credits `modelCount_toThreeOccurrence`, `modelCount_toThreeSATThree` or the parsimonious reduction, or labels them as original. By contrast, `Compact/ModelCount.lean` already says "elementary counting property". Suggested sentence for `Counting.lean`'s references: "Count preservation is original here: an elementary consequence of `CNF.copies_agree`." This can go in any later layer.
2. **The new list lemmas duplicate private copies until later in the stack.** `Data/List/{Filter,Last,Range}.lean` have no clients in this layer, while `main` keeps private copies:
   - `idxOf_range_of_lt` (`SAT/Planar/Occurrence.lean:242`)
   - `lastD_eq_getElem` (`SAT/Planar/Semantics.lean:121`)
   - `two_paths_of_filter_length` (`SAT/Planar/Paths/Occupancy.lean:40`)
   - `other_path_index` (`SAT/Planar/Correctness.lean:57`)

   I confirmed that #1180's head `d7effb7e` deletes all four and calls the public lemmas. If the stack stalls, switching those four clients is a small follow-up.
3. **Optional reuse and simplification:**
   - Writing the two counting functions as `if … then SharpSAT φ else 0` (definitionally the same) would tie them to the `#SAT` notion.
   - A bridge like `SharpSAT.mem_SAT_iff`, for example `φ ∈ ThreeSAT ↔ 0 < SharpThreeSAT φ`, would connect them to the decision languages.
   - The proof of `modelCount_compact` repeats the shape of `modelCount_relabel`. A `Set.InjOn` version of `modelCount_relabel` would give both.
   - `List.getLastD_eq_getElem` follows from core's `getLastD_eq_getLast?` and `getLast_eq_getElem`.
   - `exists_pair_indices_of_two_le_filter_contains` and `two_le_filter_contains_of_indices` are converses and could be one `iff`.

title: feat(CNF): preserve model counts under occurrence splitting
body:
## Change

Layer 1/8 of #1144, based on main. The complete stack and review handoff are recorded on #1147.

First milestone of the split parsimonious planar-SAT development in #1144. Prove that occurrence splitting and its injective numbering preserve the number of satisfying assignments. Add a parsimonious reduction from width-at-most-three model counting to occurrence-at-most-three model counting, using the existing binary CNF encodings and polynomial-time compiler. Counts range over occurring variables; total guards return zero outside their syntax. Compaction also preserves counts, including empty support and infinite ambient variable types. Extract three small list APIs needed by later layers and retain the requested ASP follow-up in ROADMAP.md.

This PR does not switch the planar compiler; the full objective remains open in #1144 and is completed by the dependent stack.

Public entry point: `parsimoniousReducible_SharpThreeSAT_SharpThreeSATThree`.

Existing notions considered: Reuses CNF modelCount, existing syntax checks, implication cycles, copy numbering and ParsimoniousReducible. The two new guarded counting functions specialize those existing notions; they introduce no alternate assignment semantics. The list lemmas generalize proofs already used by canonical-path occupancy.

## Validation and review

All six local `scripts/check.sh` gates pass at `5b65c48394bf529138806b0cfe2d571b797998e8` with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4`: strict build, aggregate check, full tests including the axiom audit, lint, style and Init imports. Hygiene checks pass. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40318829563) is linked separately from these local results.

[Internal technical review and source-identity record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1147#issuecomment-6415439402). Outside-fleet coordinator approval remains required.

## Headline abstracts

No selected abstract statement, definition, scope, catalogue entry or rendering changes. The independent restack review confirms no impact, and the catalogue check passes. No new PDF review is needed.

## AI assistance

Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) implemented the original development and this split, with separate non-authoring internal review contexts. No human or outside-fleet approval is claimed.

title: feat(threshold): emit native prefix-selected scalar stages
body:
Refs #1149. **Native-stage milestone, not the full tree compiler.** This PR targets main and is independent of #1134/#1139. The full objective in #1149 remains open.

Adds `WeightedThreshold.ScalarStage.append`, a native Program extension with m prefix-indicator gates and one scalar query. The theorems give exact evaluation, preservation of earlier values and aggregated input coefficients, unique-pattern threshold selection, false padding, and exactly one extra input reader iff w is nonzero. The Program index charges m+1 gates. `eval_append_readout` reuses the constructor with zero direct vector, zero selected thresholds and baseline one to recognize any accepting pattern, including empty or repeated pattern banks.

The regression file composes two adaptive stages and a native readout into a five-gate OR circuit, and uses the accepting-pattern construction in a seven-gate program. It covers ties, signed/fractional coefficients, zero direct vector, empty histories/banks, contradictory repeated reads, and duplicate-pattern blending. Distinctness is required by the threshold selector, not by the unconditional evaluation equation or accepting-pattern OR.

## Source and scope

Source: *Threshold Circuits as Decision Trees and Finite-State Programs*, proof of Theorem 4.1, [stage paragraph at 451c4f88](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/threshold-circuits/blob/451c4f88151e5843ab4e7f1da93077a225c506a9/threshold_circuit_representations.tex#L543). Exact excerpt: “the selected threshold is a function of the previous”. Source h/z become the supplied pattern and selected earlier gate values. The indicator uses ±1 coefficients and threshold equal to pattern weight. The query uses w and flag coefficient baseline−threshold. Sparse banks and the shared accepting-pattern readout are implementation refinements here.

Existing Line/Program/Circuit types, inputWeight, inputGates and wire extensions are reused. Binary minterm circuits do not supply the single weighted-threshold gate per prefix required by this charge. No parallel model, free Boolean postprocessing or assumed compiler is introduced. Existing public statements are unchanged.

**Remaining in #1149:** deriving the stage schedule from an arbitrary tree, distinctness of padded leaf paths, the whole-program trace invariant, and global size/activity theorems. Automatic maximal-run extraction and the O(qe+N) enumerative normalization are separate. No curated abstract is proposed for this supporting milestone.

## Validation and review

Hosted [Lean Action CI run 40281428256](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40281428256) succeeded for head `08cd1ebe12b912d47bb7d6591d93bb2e74e74511`, testing its main-integration merge `14aed2dc90c4eb3bde6e0747137bb10d2f7c5a99`. The full build, regression tests, Lean lint, import aggregate, style and init-import checks succeeded. CI checks were not changed. The temporary frozen-base validation target used during proof repair has been removed; the PR targets main.

No local Lean/Lake run is claimed; local Lean and Lean MCP were unavailable. Supplementary exact-rational checks passed for 1,500 stage instances / 9,299 evaluations and 600 whole-tree prototypes / 3,865 evaluations with padded accepting readout. These finite checks do not prove the whole-tree Lean endpoint.

AI-authored by ChatGPT session `worker-chatgpt-native-scalar-20261026`; author self-review only. **Independent exact-head mathematical/API review is requested before integration.** Do not close #1149 when this bounded stage milestone lands.

The callback machine is fixed and certified at pointwise independent `tStep`/`sStep`; their maxima are required only on actual prefixes `i < length`. The complete encoded state, including the remaining list and accumulator, is bounded through `i ≤ length`. The proof treats the terminal empty-list round separately, without demanding a callback bound there, and charges its scan/retained accumulator. It returns one finite machine and one constant before quantifying over all inputs, with exactly the advertised clock `c*(t+(length+1)*(tMax+lMax+1))` and workspace `c*(s+sMax+lMax+1)`.

Round assembly uses the plain codec capabilities and supplied machines. Intermediate encoded-state lengths are charged explicitly; workspace remains a maximum/peak bound rather than accumulating over rounds, and no input-dependent workspace term enters the time formula. Empty input and element types are handled without adding an inhabitance premise. The original captured-reader/size package and all canonical plain PT/O/OnWords/conditional theorem headers are unchanged. The legacy fold header is exact and delegates to this compiler; its private BigO mini-calculus is removed.

I reused the [kernel move/classification review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6408748132) and [three-path disposition](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6408754101). Normal-import guards are strengthened, the exposed OnWords data equation is checked, and existing programs/assertions/limits are retained. Agent review, not human approval.

1. **Content.** `cost_dualRail` proves that the AND cost of the dual-rail translation equals `Boolean.binaryCost` of the original circuit. A negation becomes `or [r, r]`. An AND or OR gate yields one AND and one OR gate. Constants yield constants. This is correct, and it is what the fusion step needs, because `pairCoverComplexity_le_ecomplexityFrom_bool` charges only AND gates. The resulting chain `ρ(f) ≤ binaryCost(c) ≤ size(c)` and `ρ(f) ≤ C(f)` strictly implies the removed `ρ ≤ 2·size` and `ρ ≤ 2·C`. `pairCoverComplexity_complexity_bounds` tightens from `t ≤ 2C` to `t ≤ C`. The arbitrary `admissible` semifilter class is kept.
2. **Public definition change.** `dualGates`, and the mirrored `dualOp` and `dualGateDM`, change only in the `.not` case, and the PR discloses this. `eval_dualRail` on `railBits` inputs and `size_dualRail = 2·size` are unchanged. The logspace writer is updated in lockstep (`map_dualGates` is still `rfl`). The new `dualGateDM` argument list for `.not` stays inside the existing space budget.
3. **API.** There are no new definitions. The PR reuses `Boolean.binaryCost` and `Program.cost_binaryCost_le`. The renamed endpoints carry no aliases, which follows the AGENTS no-alias rule. A repository grep finds no remaining clients of the old names.
4. **Tests.** NAND and NOR, each with an internal negation, have translated AND cost exactly 1. They give `ρ ≤ 1`, down from 4, and `ecomplexityFrom ≤ 1`, down from 16. The ordinary-size form is also instantiated.
5. **Originality and CI.** The refinement is labeled as original accounting of the existing construction, and nothing is quoted. Hosted CI passed at this head (run 40293537705). The head merges cleanly into current `main` (`731c6e9c`). AI disclosure and the handoff (#1162) are present.

Nonblocking nit:
- No translated gate reads the leading constant-`true` input (wire `0`) any more. Its only role now is to keep the uniform `2w + 1`/`2w + 2` wire layout. The `DualRail` module doc could say so in one line. Dropping the rail would change the MCV instance layout, so that belongs in a follow-up, not here.

The existing semantics on railBitString inputs is preserved; the public translation changes behavior on off-contract inputs whose leading rail is false. This is a mathematical strengthening and public-definition change, requiring independent coordinator review.

The cost refinement is original to this change's accounting of the existing construction. It does not construct a new explicit fusion obstruction or strengthen the reverse quadratic bound. The selected abstract catalogue is unaffected.

+/-!
+# Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup Encryption Scheme and Adaptive Projective-Hash Rejection
+
+This module formalizes the **Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup public-key encryption scheme**
+($\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$, [Boneh and Shoup, Section 12.5.3 and Exercise 12.27, printed
+pp. 488–493, 521–522][BonehShoup2023], specialized to associated data
+$\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$) over a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, proves its algebraic and word-level
+decryption correctness and polynomial-time computability certificates, and establishes the
+**adaptive Lemma 12.8 projective-hash rejection bound** and **Lemma 12.6 one-time group-mask
+challenge blindness** (Games 3 $\to$ 3.5 $\to$ 4 $\to$ 5 of Theorem 12.9, printed pp. 492–493)
+against an adaptive `CCA2AdversaryOf Msg`. Groups are written additively as
+`ZMod (F.order d)`-modules (matching `DiscreteLog`, `DiffieHellman`, `ElGamal`, and
+`ProjectiveHash`).
+
+## Source Statements ([BonehShoup2023], Sections 12.5.2–12.5.3 & Exercise 12.27)
+
+Verbatim from [BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.2 (printed pp. 486, 488):
+> **Lemma 12.6.** In Attack Game 12.4, $\Pr[W_0] = \Pr[W_1]$ for all adversaries $\mathcal{A}$.
+> …
+> **Lemma 12.8.** In Attack Game 12.5, for any adversary $\mathcal{A}$ that outputs at most $Q$
+> tuples, the probability that it wins is at most $Q/q$.
+
+Verbatim from [BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3 (printed pp. 488–493):
+> - the key generation algorithm runs as follows:
+>   $$\begin{aligned}
+>   G() :=\quad & \alpha \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; u \leftarrow g^\alpha,\;
+>     \sigma, \tau \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; h \leftarrow g^\sigma u^\tau \\
+>   & \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2 \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\;
+>     h_1 \leftarrow g^{\sigma_1} u^{\tau_1},\; h_2 \leftarrow g^{\sigma_2} u^{\tau_2} \\
+>   & pk \leftarrow (u, h, h_1, h_2),\;
+>     sk \leftarrow (\sigma, \tau, \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2),\;
+>     \text{output } (pk, sk);
+>   \end{aligned}$$
+> …
+> **Game 5.** We again widen the rejection rule at line (5), replacing it with:
+> $$(5) \qquad \text{if } \hat{v}^\alpha \ne \hat{w} \text{ or }
+>   \mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v}) \text{ or } z' \ne f'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{\rho})$$
+> So this rule will reject the ciphertext if $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \notin L_u$.
+> Let $Z_5$ be the event that in Game 5, some decryption query, which would not have triggered the
+> rejection rule of Game 4, does trigger the wider rejection rule in Game 5. Clearly, Games 4 and 5
+> proceed identically unless event $Z_5$ occurs. By the Difference Lemma, we have
+> $$|\Pr[W_4] - \Pr[W_5]| \le \Pr[Z_5]. \quad (12.26)$$
+> We will argue that $\Pr[Z_5] \le Q_d / q$. $(12.27)$
+> …
+> **Game 6.** Everything we did so far was leading to this point, which is the crux of the proof. We
+> replace line (2) in Fig. 12.3 with $z \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{G}$. We claim that
+> $\Pr[W_6] = \Pr[W_5]$. $(12.28)$ This follows from Lemma 12.6, and the fact that in processing
+> decryption queries in Game 5, we only need to evaluate $f(\hat{v}, \hat{w})$ at points
+> $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \in L_u$.
+> …
+> **Remark 12.3 (Group membership verification).** For reasons similar to that discussed in
+> Remark 12.1, it is essential that given a ciphertext $(v, w, z', c)$, the decryption algorithm for
+> $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$ verifies that $v$ and $w$ are in $\mathbb{G}$. It is not necessary to
+> explicitly check that $z'$ is in $\mathbb{G}$, since the check that
+> $v^{\sigma_1 + \rho \sigma_2} w^{\tau_1 + \rho \tau_2} = z'$ implies that $z'$ is in $\mathbb{G}$.
+
+Verbatim from [BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27 (printed pp. 521–522):
+> **12.27 (Multiplicative Cramer-Shoup encryption).** Consider the following multiplicative version
+> of the Cramer-Shoup encryption scheme (presented in Section 12.5) that supports associated data
+> (see Section 12.7) coming from a set $\mathcal{D}$. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a cyclic group of prime
+> order $q$ with generator $g \in \mathbb{G}$. Let
+> $H' : \mathbb{G}^3 \times \mathcal{D} \to \mathbb{Z}_q$ be a hash function. The encryption scheme
+> $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}} = (G, E, D)$ is defined over $(\mathbb{G}, \mathcal{D}, \mathbb{G}^4)$
+> as follows. Key generation is exactly as in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$. For a given public key
+> $pk = (u, h, h_1, h_2) \in \mathbb{G}^4$ message $m \in \mathbb{G}$, and associated data
+> $d \in \mathcal{D}$, the encryption algorithm runs as follows:
+> $$E(pk, m, d) := \beta \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; v \leftarrow g^\beta,\;
+>   w \leftarrow u^\beta,\; e \leftarrow h^\beta \cdot m,\;
+>   \rho \leftarrow H'(v, w, e, d),\; z' \leftarrow (h_1 h_2^\rho)^\beta,\;
+>   \text{output } (v, w, e, z').$$
+> For a given secret key
+> $sk = (\sigma, \tau, \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2) \in \mathbb{Z}_q^6$ and a ciphertext
+> $(v, w, e, z') \in \mathbb{G}^4$, and associated data $d \in \mathcal{D}$, the decryption
+> algorithm runs as follows:
+> $$D(sk, (v, w, e, z', d)) := \rho \leftarrow H'(v, w, e, d);\;
+>   \text{if } v^{\sigma_1 + \rho \sigma_2} w^{\tau_1 + \rho \tau_2} = z'
+>   \text{ then output } e / (v^\sigma w^\tau) \text{ else output reject}.$$
+> Show that $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$ is CCA secure, provided $H'$ is collision resistant and the
+> DDH assumption holds for $\mathbb{G}$.
+
+## Existing Notions Considered
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily` (`DiffieHellman.lean`) and `ElGamal` (`ElGamal.lean`):
+  reused for group descriptions, carriers, generators, encodings, and word-level group operations.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.ProjectiveHash` (`CramerShoup/ProjectiveHash.lean`): reused for `projHash`,
+  `projHashAux`, `projHash2`, `projHash2Aux`, fiber identities, `projHashFiberEquiv`,

+* `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.CCA2AdversaryOf` (`Encryption/CCA.lean`) and
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollisionFor` (`CollisionResistant.lean`): reused for adaptive 1CCA adversaries
+  and Phase 2 hash collisions in `ZMod (F.order d)`.
+
+## Main definitions and results
+
+* `cramerShoupHashMod`, `cramerShoupPublicKey`, `cramerShoupEncrypt`, `cramerShoupDecrypt`,
+  `encodeCramerShoupPublicKey`, `encodeCramerShoupEncrypt`, `encodeCramerShoupChallenge`,
+  `decodeCramerShoup`: algebraic and word-level Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup operations.
+* `cramerShoupDecrypt_cramerShoupEncrypt`, `decodeCramerShoup_encode`,
+  `decodeCramerShoup_cramerShoupEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey`,
+  `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupEncrypt`,
+  `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupChallenge`, `computableInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup`:
+  decryption correctness and polynomial-time computability certificates.
+* `cramerShoupGame3`, `cramerShoupGame3Half`, `cramerShoupGame4`, `cramerShoupGame5`,
+  `advantage_cramerShoupGame3_game3Half_le`, `advantage_cramerShoupGame3Half_game4_le`,
+  `advantage_cramerShoupGame3_game4_le`, `cramerShoupGame5_false_eq_true`,
+  `advantage_cramerShoupGame4_game5_le`: the adaptive Lemma 12.8 projective-hash rejection bounds
+  (`Q₁ / m`, `Q₂ / m`, `(Q₁ + Q₂) / m`) and Lemma 12.6 one-time group-mask bound (`1 / m`).
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily
+
+open Probability Turing.MultiTapeTM ProjectiveHash Encryption
+open scoped ENNReal NNReal
+
+variable (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily)
+/-! ### Framing for 3-tuples and 4-tuples of bit strings -/
+
+/-- Canonical framing of a 3-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def encBits3 : (List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) ↪ List Bool :=
+  encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)
+
+/-- Unpack a canonically framed 3-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def decodeBits3 (w : List Bool) : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool :=
+  let r1 := dropFrame w
+  (unframe w, unframe r1, dropFrame r1)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem decodeBits3_encBits3 (p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) :
+    decodeBits3 (encBits3 p) = p := by
+  rcases p with ⟨a, b, c⟩
+  simp [encBits3, decodeBits3, encPair_apply, unframe_frame_append, dropFrame_frame_append]
+
+/-- Canonical framing of a 4-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def encBits4 : (List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) ↪ List Bool :=
+  encPair encBits (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))
+
+/-- Unpack a canonically framed 4-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def decodeBits4 (w : List Bool) : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool :=
+  let r1 := dropFrame w
+  let r2 := dropFrame r1
+  (unframe w, unframe r1, unframe r2, dropFrame r2)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem decodeBits4_encBits4 (p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) :
+    decodeBits4 (encBits4 p) = p := by
+  rcases p with ⟨a, b, c, d⟩
+  simp [encBits4, decodeBits4, encPair_apply, unframe_frame_append, dropFrame_frame_append]
+
+/-- Extract the framed `(v, w, e)` triple from an encoded 4-tuple ciphertext `ct`. -/
+def extractCramerShoupTriple (ct : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  let parts := decodeBits4 ct
+  encBits3 (parts.1, parts.2.1, parts.2.2.1)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem extractCramerShoupTriple_encBits4 (v w e z' : List Bool) :
+    extractCramerShoupTriple (encBits4 (v, w, e, z')) = encBits3 (v, w, e) := by
+  simp [extractCramerShoupTriple]
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4 :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime decodeBits4 encBits
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))) := by
+  unfold decodeBits4; fun_prop
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_extractCramerShoupTriple :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime extractCramerShoupTriple encBits encBits := by
+  have h := computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4
+  exact (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits3).comp
+    (h.fst'.prod (h.snd'.fst'.prod h.snd'.snd'.fst'))
+
+/-- `decodeBits4` is computable in polynomial time. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_decodeBits4 :
+    ComputableInPolyTime decodeBits4 encBits
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))) :=
+  .of_tidy computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4
+
+/-- `extractCramerShoupTriple` is computable in polynomial time. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_extractCramerShoupTriple :
+    ComputableInPolyTime extractCramerShoupTriple encBits encBits :=
+  .of_tidy computableTidilyInPolyTime_extractCramerShoupTriple
+
+/-! ### Algebraic Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3 & Exercise 12.27) -/
+
+/-- The $\mathbb{Z}_q$-valued hash family $H'_d(x) = (\mathrm{ofBits}(H(d, x)) : \mathbb{Z}_q)$
+induced by a word-level hash function `H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool`
+([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27, printed p. 521). -/
+def cramerShoupHashMod (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc) (x : List Bool) :
+    ZMod (F.order d) :=
+  (ofBits (H (d, x)) : ZMod (F.order d))
+
+/-- Encode a triple of group elements `(v, w, e) : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d` as a
+framed bit string. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupTriple (d : F.Desc) (v w e : F.Carrier d) : List Bool :=
+  encBits3 (F.encode d v, F.encode d w, F.encode d e)
+
+/-- Algebraic Cramer–Shoup public key `pk = (u, h, h₁, h₂) ∈ G⁴` generated from secret exponents
+`(α, σ, τ, σ₁, τ₁, σ₂, τ₂)` ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, printed p. 489). -/
+def cramerShoupPublicKey (d : F.Desc) (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+    F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d :=
+  let u := α • F.generator d; let h := projHashAux F d σ τ u
+  let h₁₂ := projHash2Aux F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ u
+  (u, h, h₁₂.1, h₁₂.2)
+
+/-- Algebraic Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup encryption $E(pk, m; \beta) = (v, w, e, z')$
+([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27, printed p. 521, with $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$). -/
+def cramerShoupEncrypt (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d)
+    (m : F.Carrier d) (β : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+    F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d :=
+  let v := β • F.generator d; let w := β • pk.1; let e := β • pk.2.1 + m
+  let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d v w e)
+  (v, w, e, β • (pk.2.2.1 + ρ • pk.2.2.2))
+
+/-- Under a genuine public key `cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂`, the components of
+`cramerShoupEncrypt` coincide with projective hash evaluation (`Game 0 = Game 1`,
+[BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, equation (12.21), printed p. 490). -/
+theorem cramerShoupEncrypt_cramerShoupPublicKey (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ β : ZMod (F.order d)) (m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂) m β =
+      let v := β • F.generator d
+      let w := (α * β) • F.generator d
+      let e := projHash F d σ τ v w + m
+      let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d v w e)
+      let z' := projHash2 F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ ρ v w
+      (v, w, e, z') := by
+  dsimp only [cramerShoupEncrypt, cramerShoupPublicKey]
+  have hw : β • (α • F.generator d) = (α * β) • F.generator d := by rw [smul_smul, mul_comm]
+  have he : projHash F d σ τ (β • F.generator d) ((α * β) • F.generator d) =
+      β • projHashAux F d σ τ (α • F.generator d) := by rw [← hw, projHash_smul_generator]
+  have hz' (ρ : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+      projHash2 F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ ρ (β • F.generator d) ((α * β) • F.generator d) =
+        β • ((projHash2Aux F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ (α • F.generator d)).1 +
+          ρ • (projHash2Aux F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ (α • F.generator d)).2) := by
+    rw [← hw, projHash2_smul_generator]
+  rw [hw, ← he, ← hz']
+
+/-- Algebraic Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup decryption $D(sk, (v, w, e, z'))$
+([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27, printed p. 522): check
+$f'_{\sigma_1,\tau_1,\sigma_2,\tau_2}(v, w, \rho) = z'$ where $\rho = H'(v, w, e)$, and if so
+output `some (e - f_{σ,τ}(v, w))`. -/
+def cramerShoupDecrypt [∀ d, DecidableEq (F.Carrier d)]
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ZMod (F.order d) × ZMod (F.order d)) ×
+      ((ZMod (F.order d) × ZMod (F.order d)) × (ZMod (F.order d) × ZMod (F.order d))))
+    (ct : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) : Option (F.Carrier d) :=
+  let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d ct.1 ct.2.1 ct.2.2.1)
+  if projHash2 F d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 ρ ct.1 ct.2.1 = ct.2.2.2 then
+    some (ct.2.2.1 - projHash F d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 ct.1 ct.2.1)
+  else
+    none
+
+/-- **Algebraic Cramer–Shoup decryption correctness** ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3 &
+Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 489, 521–522): decrypting an honest encryption under
+`cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂` with `((σ, τ), ((σ₁, τ₁), (σ₂, τ₂)))` recovers
+`some m`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem cramerShoupDecrypt_cramerShoupEncrypt [∀ d, DecidableEq (F.Carrier d)]
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ β : ZMod (F.order d)) (m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.cramerShoupDecrypt H d ((σ, τ), ((σ₁, τ₁), (σ₂, τ₂)))
+      (F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂) m β) = some m := by
+  rw [F.cramerShoupEncrypt_cramerShoupPublicKey]; simp [cramerShoupDecrypt]
+
+/-! ### Word-level polynomial-time Cramer–Shoup operations -/
+
+/-- Encoding of a 6-tuple secret key `((s, t), ((s₁, t₁), (s₂, t₂)))` of natural-number
+exponents. -/
+abbrev encCramerShoupSK : ((ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) ↪ List Bool :=
+  encPair (encPair encNat encNat) (encPair (encPair encNat encNat) (encPair encNat encNat))
+
+/-- Encoded group negation `-x = (q - 1) • x` computed via `F.smul (d, F.order d - 1, z)`. -/
+def encodeGroupNeg (d : F.Desc) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.smul (d, F.order d - 1, z)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeGroupNeg_encode (d : F.Desc) (x : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeGroupNeg d (F.encode d x) = F.encode d (-x) := by
+  have hneg : ((F.order d - 1 : ℕ) : ZMod (F.order d)) = -1 := by
+    rw [Nat.cast_sub (F.prime_order d).pos, ZMod.natCast_self, Nat.cast_one, zero_sub]
+  simp only [encodeGroupNeg, F.smul_encode, hneg, neg_one_smul]
+
+/-- Word-level universal projective hash `f_{s,t}(v, w) = s • v + t • w`. -/
+def encodeProjHash (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (v w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.add (d, F.smul (d, s, v), F.smul (d, t, w))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeProjHash_encode (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (v w : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeProjHash d s t (F.encode d v) (F.encode d w) =
+      F.encode d (projHash F d (s : ZMod (F.order d)) (t : ZMod (F.order d)) v w) := by
+  simp only [encodeProjHash, F.smul_encode, F.add_encode, projHash]
+
+/-- Word-level public projection `h = f_{s,t}(g, u) = s • g + t • u`. -/
+def encodeProjHashAux (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (u : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.encodeProjHash d s t (F.encode d (F.generator d)) u
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeProjHashAux_encode (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (u : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeProjHashAux d s t (F.encode d u) =
+      F.encode d (projHashAux F d (s : ZMod (F.order d)) (t : ZMod (F.order d)) u) := by
+  simp only [encodeProjHashAux, encodeProjHash_encode, projHashAux]
+
+/-- Word-level $\text{universal}_2$ projective hash
+`f'_{s₁,t₁,s₂,t₂}(v, w, r) = f_{s₁,t₁}(v, w) + r • f_{s₂,t₂}(v, w)`. -/
+def encodeProjHash2 (d : F.Desc) (s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r : ℕ) (v w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.add (d, F.encodeProjHash d s₁ t₁ v w, F.smul (d, r, F.encodeProjHash d s₂ t₂ v w))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeProjHash2_encode (d : F.Desc) (s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r : ℕ) (v w : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeProjHash2 d s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r (F.encode d v) (F.encode d w) =
+      F.encode d (projHash2 F d (s₁ : ZMod (F.order d)) (t₁ : ZMod (F.order d))
+        (s₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) (t₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) (r : ZMod (F.order d)) v w) := by
+  simp only [encodeProjHash2, encodeProjHash_encode, F.smul_encode, F.add_encode,
+    projHash2_eq_projHash_add]
+
+/-- Encode a 4-tuple of group elements `(u, h, h₁, h₂)` together with `d : F.Desc` as the public
+key word presented to a 1CCA adversary. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupPublicKeyValues (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) : List Bool :=
+  encPair F.encDesc encBits4
+    (d, (F.encode d pk.1, F.encode d pk.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.2))
+
+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup public key generation from `d : F.Desc`, an encoded
+`u = encode (α • g)`, and natural-number secret exponents
+`sk = ((s, t), ((s₁, t₁), (s₂, t₂)))`. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupPublicKey (d : F.Desc) (u : List Bool)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) : List Bool :=
+  encPair F.encDesc encBits4 (d, (u, F.encodeProjHashAux d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 u,
+    F.encodeProjHashAux d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 u, F.encodeProjHashAux d sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 u))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_encode (d : F.Desc) (α : ZMod (F.order d))
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) :
+    F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d (F.encode d (α • F.generator d)) sk =
+      F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKeyValues d
+        (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2) := by
+  simp only [encodeCramerShoupPublicKey, encodeCramerShoupPublicKeyValues,
+    encodeProjHashAux_encode, cramerShoupPublicKey, projHash2Aux]
+
+/-- Encode a 4-tuple ciphertext `(v, w, e, z') : (F.Carrier d)⁴` as a canonically framed bit
+string. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupCiphertext (d : F.Desc)
+    (ct : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) : List Bool :=
+  encBits4 (F.encode d ct.1, F.encode d ct.2.1, F.encode d ct.2.2.1, F.encode d ct.2.2.2)
+
+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup encryption from the public key `(u, h, h₁, h₂)`, encoded message `m`,
+and randomness `b : ℕ`. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupEncrypt (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) (m : List Bool) (b : ℕ) : List Bool :=
+  let v := F.smul (d, b, F.encode d (F.generator d)); let w := F.smul (d, b, pk.1)
+  let e := F.add (d, F.smul (d, b, pk.2.1), m)
+  let r := ofBits (H (d, encBits3 (v, w, e)))
+  encBits4 (v, w, e, F.smul (d, b, F.add (d, pk.2.2.1, F.smul (d, r, pk.2.2.2))))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeCramerShoupEncrypt_encode (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) (m : F.Carrier d) (b : ℕ) :
+    F.encodeCramerShoupEncrypt H d
+      (F.encode d pk.1, F.encode d pk.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.2)
+      (F.encode d m) b =
+      F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d
+        (F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d pk m (b : ZMod (F.order d))) := by
+  simp only [encodeCramerShoupEncrypt, encodeCramerShoupCiphertext, cramerShoupEncrypt,
+    encodeCramerShoupTriple, cramerShoupHashMod, F.smul_encode, F.add_encode]
+
+/-- Word-level Game 1 challenge encryption from `(v, w)` (encoded group elements), secret key
+`sk`, and encoded message `m` ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, Game 1, printed p. 490). -/
+def encodeCramerShoupChallenge (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (v w m : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  let e := F.add (d, F.encodeProjHash d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 v w, m)
+  let r := ofBits (H (d, encBits3 (v, w, e)))
+  encBits4 (v, w, e, F.encodeProjHash2 d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 r v w)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeCramerShoupChallenge_encode (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (v w m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H d sk (F.encode d v) (F.encode d w) (F.encode d m) =
+      let e := projHash F d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 v w + m
+      let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d v w e)
+      let z' := projHash2 F d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 ρ v w
+      F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d (v, w, e, z') := by
+  simp only [encodeCramerShoupChallenge, encodeProjHash_encode, F.add_encode,
+    encodeProjHash2_encode, encodeCramerShoupTriple, cramerShoupHashMod,
+    encodeCramerShoupCiphertext]
+
+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, Remark 12.3, and
+Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 489, 493, 522): given `(d, sk, ct)`, unpack `(v, w, e, z') :=
+decodeBits4 ct`, check canonical framing `encBits4 (v, w, e, z') == ct`, check group membership
+`isElem (d, v) && isElem (d, w) && isElem (d, e)`, and check
+`encodeProjHash2 d s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r v w == z'`; if all pass, return
+`some (encode (e - f_{s,t}(v, w)))`, else `none`. -/
+def decodeCramerShoup (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool)
+    (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (ct : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) :=
+  let parts := decodeBits4 ct
+  let v := parts.1; let w := parts.2.1; let e := parts.2.2.1; let z' := parts.2.2.2
+  let r := ofBits (H (d, encBits3 (v, w, e)))
+  if (encBits4 parts == ct) && isElem (d, v) && isElem (d, w) && isElem (d, e) &&
+      (F.encodeProjHash2 d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 r v w == z') then
+    some (F.add (d, e, F.encodeGroupNeg d (F.encodeProjHash d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 v w)))
+  else
+    none
+
+/-- **Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption matches algebraic `cramerShoupDecrypt` on encoded
+ciphertexts**. -/
+theorem decodeCramerShoup_encode [∀ d, DecidableEq (F.Carrier d)]
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (hmem : ∀ d x, isElem (d, x) = true ↔ x ∈ Set.range (F.encode d))
+    (d : F.Desc) (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ)))
+    (ct : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) :
+    F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem d sk (F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d ct) =
+      (F.cramerShoupDecrypt H d
+        (((sk.1.1 : ZMod (F.order d)), (sk.1.2 : ZMod (F.order d))),
+          (((sk.2.1.1 : ZMod (F.order d)), (sk.2.1.2 : ZMod (F.order d))),
+            ((sk.2.2.1 : ZMod (F.order d)), (sk.2.2.2 : ZMod (F.order d))))) ct).map
+        (F.encode d) := by
+  rcases ct with ⟨v, w, e, z'⟩
+  have hv : isElem (d, F.encode d v) = true := (hmem d _).mpr ⟨v, rfl⟩
+  have hw : isElem (d, F.encode d w) = true := (hmem d _).mpr ⟨w, rfl⟩
+  have he : isElem (d, F.encode d e) = true := (hmem d _).mpr ⟨e, rfl⟩
+  have hinj : ∀ a b : F.Carrier d, (F.encode d a == F.encode d b) = decide (a = b) := fun a b => by
+    rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff, beq_iff_eq, decide_eq_true_eq]; exact (F.encode_injective d).eq_iff
+  simp only [decodeCramerShoup, encodeCramerShoupCiphertext, decodeBits4_encBits4, beq_self_eq_true,
+    hv, hw, he, Bool.true_and, encodeProjHash2_encode, hinj, encodeProjHash_encode,
+    encodeGroupNeg_encode, F.add_encode, cramerShoupDecrypt, encodeCramerShoupTriple,
+    cramerShoupHashMod, sub_eq_add_neg, decide_eq_true_eq]
+  split_ifs <;> rfl
+
+/-- **Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption of an honest encryption recovers
+`some (F.encode d m)`**. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem decodeCramerShoup_cramerShoupEncrypt
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (hmem : ∀ d x, isElem (d, x) = true ↔ x ∈ Set.range (F.encode d))
+    (d : F.Desc) (α β : ZMod (F.order d))
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem d sk
+      (F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d
+        (F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d
+          (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2)
+          m β)) = some (F.encode d m) := by
+  classical
+  rw [F.decodeCramerShoup_encode H isElem hmem, F.cramerShoupDecrypt_cramerShoupEncrypt]; rfl
+

+    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop))

+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool} {isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits)
+    (hisElem : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime isElem (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBool)
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc}
+    {sk : γ → (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))} {ct : γ → List Bool}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hsk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime sk encIn encCramerShoupSK)
+    (hct : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime ct encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem (d a) (sk a) (ct a))
+      encIn (encOption encBits) := by
+  have hparts := computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4.comp hct
+  have hv := hparts.fst'; have hw := hparts.snd'.fst'
+  have he := hparts.snd'.snd'.fst'; have hz' := hparts.snd'.snd'.snd'
+  have hr := ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsToNat.comp (hH.comp (hd.prod
+    ((ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits3).comp (hv.prod (hw.prod he)))))
+  have hbeq : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => p.1 == p.2) (encPair encBits encBits) encBool := by polytime
+  have hand : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun p : Bool × Bool => p.1 && p.2) (encPair encBool encBool) encBool := by polytime
+  have hframe := hbeq.comp (((ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits4).comp hparts).prod hct)
+  have htagEq := hbeq.comp ((F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash2 hd
+    hsk.snd'.fst'.fst' hsk.snd'.fst'.snd' hsk.snd'.snd'.fst' hsk.snd'.snd'.snd' hr hv hw).prod hz')
+  have hcond := hand.comp ((hand.comp ((hand.comp ((hand.comp
+    (hframe.prod (hisElem.comp (hd.prod hv)))).prod (hisElem.comp (hd.prod hw)))).prod
+    (hisElem.comp (hd.prod he)))).prod htagEq)
+  have hmsg := F.computableInPolyTime_add.tidy.comp (hd.prod (he.prod
+    (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeGroupNeg hd
+      (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash hd hsk.fst'.fst' hsk.fst'.snd' hv hw))))
+  have hsome : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun x : List Bool => (some x : Option (List Bool))) encBits (encOption encBits) := by
+    polytime
+  exact .cond hcond (hsome.comp hmsg) (.const none)
+
+/-- **Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption is computable in polynomial time** whenever `H` and
+`isElem` are computable in polynomial time. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool} {isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits)
+    (hisElem : ComputableInPolyTime isElem (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime
+      (fun p : F.Desc × ((ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) × List Bool =>
+        F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encCramerShoupSK encBits)) (encOption encBits) :=
+  .of_tidy (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup hH.tidy hisElem.tidy
+    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop))
+
+/-! ### Stateless oracle simulation lemmas -/
+
+/-- Run a `WordOracleComp Unit α` against a stateless deterministic oracle
+`o : List Bool → List Bool` and feed its output to `next : α → Game`. -/
+noncomputable def runStatelessOracle {α : Type} (o : List Bool → List Bool)
