+/-!
+# Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup Encryption Scheme and Adaptive Projective-Hash Rejection
+
+This module formalizes the **Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup public-key encryption scheme**
+($\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$, [Boneh and Shoup, Section 12.5.3 and Exercise 12.27, printed
+pp. 488–493, 521–522][BonehShoup2023], specialized to associated data
+$\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$) over a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, proves its algebraic and word-level
+decryption correctness and polynomial-time computability certificates, and establishes the
+**adaptive Lemma 12.8 projective-hash rejection bound** and **Lemma 12.6 one-time group-mask
+challenge blindness** (Games 3 $\to$ 3.5 $\to$ 4 $\to$ 5 of Theorem 12.9, printed pp. 492–493)
+against an adaptive `CCA2AdversaryOf Msg`. Groups are written additively as
+`ZMod (F.order d)`-modules (matching `DiscreteLog`, `DiffieHellman`, `ElGamal`, and
+`ProjectiveHash`).
+
+## Source Statements ([BonehShoup2023], Sections 12.5.2–12.5.3 & Exercise 12.27)
+
+Verbatim from [BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.2 (printed pp. 486, 488):
+> **Lemma 12.6.** In Attack Game 12.4, $\Pr[W_0] = \Pr[W_1]$ for all adversaries $\mathcal{A}$.
+> …
+> **Lemma 12.8.** In Attack Game 12.5, for any adversary $\mathcal{A}$ that outputs at most $Q$
+> tuples, the probability that it wins is at most $Q/q$.
+
+Verbatim from [BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3 (printed pp. 488–493):
+> - the key generation algorithm runs as follows:
+>   $$\begin{aligned}
+>   G() :=\quad & \alpha \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; u \leftarrow g^\alpha,\;
+>     \sigma, \tau \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; h \leftarrow g^\sigma u^\tau \\
+>   & \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2 \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\;
+>     h_1 \leftarrow g^{\sigma_1} u^{\tau_1},\; h_2 \leftarrow g^{\sigma_2} u^{\tau_2} \\
+>   & pk \leftarrow (u, h, h_1, h_2),\;
+>     sk \leftarrow (\sigma, \tau, \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2),\;
+>     \text{output } (pk, sk);
+>   \end{aligned}$$
+> …
+> **Game 5.** We again widen the rejection rule at line (5), replacing it with:
+> $$(5) \qquad \text{if } \hat{v}^\alpha \ne \hat{w} \text{ or }
+>   \mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v}) \text{ or } z' \ne f'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{\rho})$$
+> So this rule will reject the ciphertext if $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \notin L_u$.
+> Let $Z_5$ be the event that in Game 5, some decryption query, which would not have triggered the
+> rejection rule of Game 4, does trigger the wider rejection rule in Game 5. Clearly, Games 4 and 5
+> proceed identically unless event $Z_5$ occurs. By the Difference Lemma, we have
+> $$|\Pr[W_4] - \Pr[W_5]| \le \Pr[Z_5]. \quad (12.26)$$
+> We will argue that $\Pr[Z_5] \le Q_d / q$. $(12.27)$
+> …
+> **Game 6.** Everything we did so far was leading to this point, which is the crux of the proof. We
+> replace line (2) in Fig. 12.3 with $z \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{G}$. We claim that
+> $\Pr[W_6] = \Pr[W_5]$. $(12.28)$ This follows from Lemma 12.6, and the fact that in processing
+> decryption queries in Game 5, we only need to evaluate $f(\hat{v}, \hat{w})$ at points
+> $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \in L_u$.
+> …
+> **Remark 12.3 (Group membership verification).** For reasons similar to that discussed in
+> Remark 12.1, it is essential that given a ciphertext $(v, w, z', c)$, the decryption algorithm for
+> $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$ verifies that $v$ and $w$ are in $\mathbb{G}$. It is not necessary to
+> explicitly check that $z'$ is in $\mathbb{G}$, since the check that
+> $v^{\sigma_1 + \rho \sigma_2} w^{\tau_1 + \rho \tau_2} = z'$ implies that $z'$ is in $\mathbb{G}$.
+
+Verbatim from [BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27 (printed pp. 521–522):
+> **12.27 (Multiplicative Cramer-Shoup encryption).** Consider the following multiplicative version
+> of the Cramer-Shoup encryption scheme (presented in Section 12.5) that supports associated data
+> (see Section 12.7) coming from a set $\mathcal{D}$. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a cyclic group of prime
+> order $q$ with generator $g \in \mathbb{G}$. Let
+> $H' : \mathbb{G}^3 \times \mathcal{D} \to \mathbb{Z}_q$ be a hash function. The encryption scheme
+> $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}} = (G, E, D)$ is defined over $(\mathbb{G}, \mathcal{D}, \mathbb{G}^4)$
+> as follows. Key generation is exactly as in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$. For a given public key
+> $pk = (u, h, h_1, h_2) \in \mathbb{G}^4$ message $m \in \mathbb{G}$, and associated data
+> $d \in \mathcal{D}$, the encryption algorithm runs as follows:
+> $$E(pk, m, d) := \beta \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; v \leftarrow g^\beta,\;
+>   w \leftarrow u^\beta,\; e \leftarrow h^\beta \cdot m,\;
+>   \rho \leftarrow H'(v, w, e, d),\; z' \leftarrow (h_1 h_2^\rho)^\beta,\;
+>   \text{output } (v, w, e, z').$$
+> For a given secret key
+> $sk = (\sigma, \tau, \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2) \in \mathbb{Z}_q^6$ and a ciphertext
+> $(v, w, e, z') \in \mathbb{G}^4$, and associated data $d \in \mathcal{D}$, the decryption
+> algorithm runs as follows:
+> $$D(sk, (v, w, e, z', d)) := \rho \leftarrow H'(v, w, e, d);\;
+>   \text{if } v^{\sigma_1 + \rho \sigma_2} w^{\tau_1 + \rho \tau_2} = z'
+>   \text{ then output } e / (v^\sigma w^\tau) \text{ else output reject}.$$
+> Show that $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$ is CCA secure, provided $H'$ is collision resistant and the
+> DDH assumption holds for $\mathbb{G}$.
+
+## Existing Notions Considered
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily` (`DiffieHellman.lean`) and `ElGamal` (`ElGamal.lean`):
+  reused for group descriptions, carriers, generators, encodings, and word-level group operations.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.ProjectiveHash` (`CramerShoup/ProjectiveHash.lean`): reused for `projHash`,
+  `projHashAux`, `projHash2`, `projHash2Aux`, fiber identities, `projHashFiberEquiv`,
+  `projHash2QueryFiberEquiv`, and `uniform_projHash_fiber_add`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.CCA2AdversaryOf` (`Encryption/CCA.lean`) and
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollisionFor` (`CollisionResistant.lean`): reused for adaptive 1CCA adversaries
+  and Phase 2 hash collisions in `ZMod (F.order d)`.
+
+## Main definitions and results
+
+* `cramerShoupHashMod`, `cramerShoupPublicKey`, `cramerShoupEncrypt`, `cramerShoupDecrypt`,
+  `encodeCramerShoupPublicKey`, `encodeCramerShoupEncrypt`, `encodeCramerShoupChallenge`,
+  `decodeCramerShoup`: algebraic and word-level Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup operations.
+* `cramerShoupDecrypt_cramerShoupEncrypt`, `decodeCramerShoup_encode`,
+  `decodeCramerShoup_cramerShoupEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey`,
+  `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupEncrypt`,
+  `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupChallenge`, `computableInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup`:
+  decryption correctness and polynomial-time computability certificates.
+* `cramerShoupGame3`, `cramerShoupGame3Half`, `cramerShoupGame4`, `cramerShoupGame5`,
+  `advantage_cramerShoupGame3_game3Half_le`, `advantage_cramerShoupGame3Half_game4_le`,
+  `advantage_cramerShoupGame3_game4_le`, `cramerShoupGame5_false_eq_true`,
+  `advantage_cramerShoupGame4_game5_le`: the adaptive Lemma 12.8 projective-hash rejection bounds
+  (`Q₁ / m`, `Q₂ / m`, `(Q₁ + Q₂) / m`) and Lemma 12.6 one-time group-mask bound (`1 / m`).
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily
+
+open Probability Turing.MultiTapeTM ProjectiveHash Encryption
+open scoped ENNReal NNReal
+
+variable (F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily)
+/-! ### Framing for 3-tuples and 4-tuples of bit strings -/
+
+/-- Canonical framing of a 3-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def encBits3 : (List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) ↪ List Bool :=
+  encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)
+
+/-- Unpack a canonically framed 3-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def decodeBits3 (w : List Bool) : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool :=
+  let r1 := dropFrame w
+  (unframe w, unframe r1, dropFrame r1)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem decodeBits3_encBits3 (p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) :
+    decodeBits3 (encBits3 p) = p := by
+  rcases p with ⟨a, b, c⟩
+  simp [encBits3, decodeBits3, encPair_apply, unframe_frame_append, dropFrame_frame_append]
+
+/-- Canonical framing of a 4-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def encBits4 : (List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) ↪ List Bool :=
+  encPair encBits (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))
+
+/-- Unpack a canonically framed 4-tuple of bit strings. -/
+def decodeBits4 (w : List Bool) : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool :=
+  let r1 := dropFrame w
+  let r2 := dropFrame r1
+  (unframe w, unframe r1, unframe r2, dropFrame r2)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem decodeBits4_encBits4 (p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) :
+    decodeBits4 (encBits4 p) = p := by
+  rcases p with ⟨a, b, c, d⟩
+  simp [encBits4, decodeBits4, encPair_apply, unframe_frame_append, dropFrame_frame_append]
+
+/-- Extract the framed `(v, w, e)` triple from an encoded 4-tuple ciphertext `ct`. -/
+def extractCramerShoupTriple (ct : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  let parts := decodeBits4 ct
+  encBits3 (parts.1, parts.2.1, parts.2.2.1)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem extractCramerShoupTriple_encBits4 (v w e z' : List Bool) :
+    extractCramerShoupTriple (encBits4 (v, w, e, z')) = encBits3 (v, w, e) := by
+  simp [extractCramerShoupTriple]
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4 :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime decodeBits4 encBits
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))) := by
+  unfold decodeBits4; fun_prop
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_extractCramerShoupTriple :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime extractCramerShoupTriple encBits encBits := by
+  have h := computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4
+  exact (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits3).comp
+    (h.fst'.prod (h.snd'.fst'.prod h.snd'.snd'.fst'))
+
+/-- `decodeBits4` is computable in polynomial time. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_decodeBits4 :
+    ComputableInPolyTime decodeBits4 encBits
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))) :=
+  .of_tidy computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4
+
+/-- `extractCramerShoupTriple` is computable in polynomial time. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_extractCramerShoupTriple :
+    ComputableInPolyTime extractCramerShoupTriple encBits encBits :=
+  .of_tidy computableTidilyInPolyTime_extractCramerShoupTriple
+
+/-! ### Algebraic Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3 & Exercise 12.27) -/
+
+/-- The $\mathbb{Z}_q$-valued hash family $H'_d(x) = (\mathrm{ofBits}(H(d, x)) : \mathbb{Z}_q)$
+induced by a word-level hash function `H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool`
+([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27, printed p. 521). -/
+def cramerShoupHashMod (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc) (x : List Bool) :
+    ZMod (F.order d) :=
+  (ofBits (H (d, x)) : ZMod (F.order d))
+
+/-- Encode a triple of group elements `(v, w, e) : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d` as a
+framed bit string. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupTriple (d : F.Desc) (v w e : F.Carrier d) : List Bool :=
+  encBits3 (F.encode d v, F.encode d w, F.encode d e)
+
+/-- Algebraic Cramer–Shoup public key `pk = (u, h, h₁, h₂) ∈ G⁴` generated from secret exponents
+`(α, σ, τ, σ₁, τ₁, σ₂, τ₂)` ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, printed p. 489). -/
+def cramerShoupPublicKey (d : F.Desc) (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+    F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d :=
+  let u := α • F.generator d; let h := projHashAux F d σ τ u
+  let h₁₂ := projHash2Aux F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ u
+  (u, h, h₁₂.1, h₁₂.2)
+
+/-- Algebraic Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup encryption $E(pk, m; \beta) = (v, w, e, z')$
+([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27, printed p. 521, with $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$). -/
+def cramerShoupEncrypt (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d)
+    (m : F.Carrier d) (β : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+    F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d :=
+  let v := β • F.generator d; let w := β • pk.1; let e := β • pk.2.1 + m
+  let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d v w e)
+  (v, w, e, β • (pk.2.2.1 + ρ • pk.2.2.2))
+
+/-- Under a genuine public key `cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂`, the components of
+`cramerShoupEncrypt` coincide with projective hash evaluation (`Game 0 = Game 1`,
+[BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, equation (12.21), printed p. 490). -/
+theorem cramerShoupEncrypt_cramerShoupPublicKey (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ β : ZMod (F.order d)) (m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂) m β =
+      let v := β • F.generator d
+      let w := (α * β) • F.generator d
+      let e := projHash F d σ τ v w + m
+      let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d v w e)
+      let z' := projHash2 F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ ρ v w
+      (v, w, e, z') := by
+  dsimp only [cramerShoupEncrypt, cramerShoupPublicKey]
+  have hw : β • (α • F.generator d) = (α * β) • F.generator d := by rw [smul_smul, mul_comm]
+  have he : projHash F d σ τ (β • F.generator d) ((α * β) • F.generator d) =
+      β • projHashAux F d σ τ (α • F.generator d) := by rw [← hw, projHash_smul_generator]
+  have hz' (ρ : ZMod (F.order d)) :
+      projHash2 F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ ρ (β • F.generator d) ((α * β) • F.generator d) =
+        β • ((projHash2Aux F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ (α • F.generator d)).1 +
+          ρ • (projHash2Aux F d σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ (α • F.generator d)).2) := by
+    rw [← hw, projHash2_smul_generator]
+  rw [hw, ← he, ← hz']
+
+/-- Algebraic Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup decryption $D(sk, (v, w, e, z'))$
+([BonehShoup2023], Exercise 12.27, printed p. 522): check
+$f'_{\sigma_1,\tau_1,\sigma_2,\tau_2}(v, w, \rho) = z'$ where $\rho = H'(v, w, e)$, and if so
+output `some (e - f_{σ,τ}(v, w))`. -/
+def cramerShoupDecrypt [∀ d, DecidableEq (F.Carrier d)]
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ZMod (F.order d) × ZMod (F.order d)) ×
+      ((ZMod (F.order d) × ZMod (F.order d)) × (ZMod (F.order d) × ZMod (F.order d))))
+    (ct : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) : Option (F.Carrier d) :=
+  let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d ct.1 ct.2.1 ct.2.2.1)
+  if projHash2 F d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 ρ ct.1 ct.2.1 = ct.2.2.2 then
+    some (ct.2.2.1 - projHash F d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 ct.1 ct.2.1)
+  else
+    none
+
+/-- **Algebraic Cramer–Shoup decryption correctness** ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3 &
+Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 489, 521–522): decrypting an honest encryption under
+`cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂` with `((σ, τ), ((σ₁, τ₁), (σ₂, τ₂)))` recovers
+`some m`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem cramerShoupDecrypt_cramerShoupEncrypt [∀ d, DecidableEq (F.Carrier d)]
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ β : ZMod (F.order d)) (m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.cramerShoupDecrypt H d ((σ, τ), ((σ₁, τ₁), (σ₂, τ₂)))
+      (F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂) m β) = some m := by
+  rw [F.cramerShoupEncrypt_cramerShoupPublicKey]; simp [cramerShoupDecrypt]
+
+/-! ### Word-level polynomial-time Cramer–Shoup operations -/
+
+/-- Encoding of a 6-tuple secret key `((s, t), ((s₁, t₁), (s₂, t₂)))` of natural-number
+exponents. -/
+abbrev encCramerShoupSK : ((ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) ↪ List Bool :=
+  encPair (encPair encNat encNat) (encPair (encPair encNat encNat) (encPair encNat encNat))
+
+/-- Encoded group negation `-x = (q - 1) • x` computed via `F.smul (d, F.order d - 1, z)`. -/
+def encodeGroupNeg (d : F.Desc) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.smul (d, F.order d - 1, z)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeGroupNeg_encode (d : F.Desc) (x : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeGroupNeg d (F.encode d x) = F.encode d (-x) := by
+  have hneg : ((F.order d - 1 : ℕ) : ZMod (F.order d)) = -1 := by
+    rw [Nat.cast_sub (F.prime_order d).pos, ZMod.natCast_self, Nat.cast_one, zero_sub]
+  simp only [encodeGroupNeg, F.smul_encode, hneg, neg_one_smul]
+
+/-- Word-level universal projective hash `f_{s,t}(v, w) = s • v + t • w`. -/
+def encodeProjHash (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (v w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.add (d, F.smul (d, s, v), F.smul (d, t, w))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeProjHash_encode (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (v w : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeProjHash d s t (F.encode d v) (F.encode d w) =
+      F.encode d (projHash F d (s : ZMod (F.order d)) (t : ZMod (F.order d)) v w) := by
+  simp only [encodeProjHash, F.smul_encode, F.add_encode, projHash]
+
+/-- Word-level public projection `h = f_{s,t}(g, u) = s • g + t • u`. -/
+def encodeProjHashAux (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (u : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.encodeProjHash d s t (F.encode d (F.generator d)) u
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeProjHashAux_encode (d : F.Desc) (s t : ℕ) (u : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeProjHashAux d s t (F.encode d u) =
+      F.encode d (projHashAux F d (s : ZMod (F.order d)) (t : ZMod (F.order d)) u) := by
+  simp only [encodeProjHashAux, encodeProjHash_encode, projHashAux]
+
+/-- Word-level $\text{universal}_2$ projective hash
+`f'_{s₁,t₁,s₂,t₂}(v, w, r) = f_{s₁,t₁}(v, w) + r • f_{s₂,t₂}(v, w)`. -/
+def encodeProjHash2 (d : F.Desc) (s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r : ℕ) (v w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  F.add (d, F.encodeProjHash d s₁ t₁ v w, F.smul (d, r, F.encodeProjHash d s₂ t₂ v w))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeProjHash2_encode (d : F.Desc) (s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r : ℕ) (v w : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeProjHash2 d s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r (F.encode d v) (F.encode d w) =
+      F.encode d (projHash2 F d (s₁ : ZMod (F.order d)) (t₁ : ZMod (F.order d))
+        (s₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) (t₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) (r : ZMod (F.order d)) v w) := by
+  simp only [encodeProjHash2, encodeProjHash_encode, F.smul_encode, F.add_encode,
+    projHash2_eq_projHash_add]
+
+/-- Encode a 4-tuple of group elements `(u, h, h₁, h₂)` together with `d : F.Desc` as the public
+key word presented to a 1CCA adversary. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupPublicKeyValues (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) : List Bool :=
+  encPair F.encDesc encBits4
+    (d, (F.encode d pk.1, F.encode d pk.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.2))
+
+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup public key generation from `d : F.Desc`, an encoded
+`u = encode (α • g)`, and natural-number secret exponents
+`sk = ((s, t), ((s₁, t₁), (s₂, t₂)))`. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupPublicKey (d : F.Desc) (u : List Bool)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) : List Bool :=
+  encPair F.encDesc encBits4 (d, (u, F.encodeProjHashAux d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 u,
+    F.encodeProjHashAux d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 u, F.encodeProjHashAux d sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 u))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_encode (d : F.Desc) (α : ZMod (F.order d))
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) :
+    F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d (F.encode d (α • F.generator d)) sk =
+      F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKeyValues d
+        (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2) := by
+  simp only [encodeCramerShoupPublicKey, encodeCramerShoupPublicKeyValues,
+    encodeProjHashAux_encode, cramerShoupPublicKey, projHash2Aux]
+
+/-- Encode a 4-tuple ciphertext `(v, w, e, z') : (F.Carrier d)⁴` as a canonically framed bit
+string. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupCiphertext (d : F.Desc)
+    (ct : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) : List Bool :=
+  encBits4 (F.encode d ct.1, F.encode d ct.2.1, F.encode d ct.2.2.1, F.encode d ct.2.2.2)
+
+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup encryption from the public key `(u, h, h₁, h₂)`, encoded message `m`,
+and randomness `b : ℕ`. -/
+def encodeCramerShoupEncrypt (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) (m : List Bool) (b : ℕ) : List Bool :=
+  let v := F.smul (d, b, F.encode d (F.generator d)); let w := F.smul (d, b, pk.1)
+  let e := F.add (d, F.smul (d, b, pk.2.1), m)
+  let r := ofBits (H (d, encBits3 (v, w, e)))
+  encBits4 (v, w, e, F.smul (d, b, F.add (d, pk.2.2.1, F.smul (d, r, pk.2.2.2))))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeCramerShoupEncrypt_encode (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (pk : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) (m : F.Carrier d) (b : ℕ) :
+    F.encodeCramerShoupEncrypt H d
+      (F.encode d pk.1, F.encode d pk.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.1, F.encode d pk.2.2.2)
+      (F.encode d m) b =
+      F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d
+        (F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d pk m (b : ZMod (F.order d))) := by
+  simp only [encodeCramerShoupEncrypt, encodeCramerShoupCiphertext, cramerShoupEncrypt,
+    encodeCramerShoupTriple, cramerShoupHashMod, F.smul_encode, F.add_encode]
+
+/-- Word-level Game 1 challenge encryption from `(v, w)` (encoded group elements), secret key
+`sk`, and encoded message `m` ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, Game 1, printed p. 490). -/
+def encodeCramerShoupChallenge (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (v w m : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  let e := F.add (d, F.encodeProjHash d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 v w, m)
+  let r := ofBits (H (d, encBits3 (v, w, e)))
+  encBits4 (v, w, e, F.encodeProjHash2 d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 r v w)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem encodeCramerShoupChallenge_encode (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (v w m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H d sk (F.encode d v) (F.encode d w) (F.encode d m) =
+      let e := projHash F d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 v w + m
+      let ρ := F.cramerShoupHashMod H d (F.encodeCramerShoupTriple d v w e)
+      let z' := projHash2 F d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 ρ v w
+      F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d (v, w, e, z') := by
+  simp only [encodeCramerShoupChallenge, encodeProjHash_encode, F.add_encode,
+    encodeProjHash2_encode, encodeCramerShoupTriple, cramerShoupHashMod,
+    encodeCramerShoupCiphertext]
+
+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption ([BonehShoup2023], Section 12.5.3, Remark 12.3, and
+Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 489, 493, 522): given `(d, sk, ct)`, unpack `(v, w, e, z') :=
+decodeBits4 ct`, check canonical framing `encBits4 (v, w, e, z') == ct`, check group membership
+`isElem (d, v) && isElem (d, w) && isElem (d, e)`, and check
+`encodeProjHash2 d s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r v w == z'`; if all pass, return
+`some (encode (e - f_{s,t}(v, w)))`, else `none`. -/
+def decodeCramerShoup (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool)
+    (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool) (d : F.Desc)
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (ct : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) :=
+  let parts := decodeBits4 ct
+  let v := parts.1; let w := parts.2.1; let e := parts.2.2.1; let z' := parts.2.2.2
+  let r := ofBits (H (d, encBits3 (v, w, e)))
+  if (encBits4 parts == ct) && isElem (d, v) && isElem (d, w) && isElem (d, e) &&
+      (F.encodeProjHash2 d sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2 r v w == z') then
+    some (F.add (d, e, F.encodeGroupNeg d (F.encodeProjHash d sk.1.1 sk.1.2 v w)))
+  else
+    none
+
+/-- **Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption matches algebraic `cramerShoupDecrypt` on encoded
+ciphertexts**. -/
+theorem decodeCramerShoup_encode [∀ d, DecidableEq (F.Carrier d)]
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (hmem : ∀ d x, isElem (d, x) = true ↔ x ∈ Set.range (F.encode d))
+    (d : F.Desc) (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ)))
+    (ct : F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d × F.Carrier d) :
+    F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem d sk (F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d ct) =
+      (F.cramerShoupDecrypt H d
+        (((sk.1.1 : ZMod (F.order d)), (sk.1.2 : ZMod (F.order d))),
+          (((sk.2.1.1 : ZMod (F.order d)), (sk.2.1.2 : ZMod (F.order d))),
+            ((sk.2.2.1 : ZMod (F.order d)), (sk.2.2.2 : ZMod (F.order d))))) ct).map
+        (F.encode d) := by
+  rcases ct with ⟨v, w, e, z'⟩
+  have hv : isElem (d, F.encode d v) = true := (hmem d _).mpr ⟨v, rfl⟩
+  have hw : isElem (d, F.encode d w) = true := (hmem d _).mpr ⟨w, rfl⟩
+  have he : isElem (d, F.encode d e) = true := (hmem d _).mpr ⟨e, rfl⟩
+  have hinj : ∀ a b : F.Carrier d, (F.encode d a == F.encode d b) = decide (a = b) := fun a b => by
+    rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff, beq_iff_eq, decide_eq_true_eq]; exact (F.encode_injective d).eq_iff
+  simp only [decodeCramerShoup, encodeCramerShoupCiphertext, decodeBits4_encBits4, beq_self_eq_true,
+    hv, hw, he, Bool.true_and, encodeProjHash2_encode, hinj, encodeProjHash_encode,
+    encodeGroupNeg_encode, F.add_encode, cramerShoupDecrypt, encodeCramerShoupTriple,
+    cramerShoupHashMod, sub_eq_add_neg, decide_eq_true_eq]
+  split_ifs <;> rfl
+
+/-- **Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption of an honest encryption recovers
+`some (F.encode d m)`**. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem decodeCramerShoup_cramerShoupEncrypt
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (hmem : ∀ d x, isElem (d, x) = true ↔ x ∈ Set.range (F.encode d))
+    (d : F.Desc) (α β : ZMod (F.order d))
+    (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) (m : F.Carrier d) :
+    F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem d sk
+      (F.encodeCramerShoupCiphertext d
+        (F.cramerShoupEncrypt H d
+          (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2)
+          m β)) = some (F.encode d m) := by
+  classical
+  rw [F.decodeCramerShoup_encode H isElem hmem, F.cramerShoupDecrypt_cramerShoupEncrypt]; rfl
+

+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeGroupNeg
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc} {z : γ → List Bool}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hz : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime z encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => F.encodeGroupNeg (d a) (z a)) encIn encBits :=
+  F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp
+    (hd.prod ((ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_sub'
+      (F.computableInPolyTime_order.tidy.comp hd) (.const 1)).prod hz))
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc} {s t : γ → ℕ} {v w : γ → List Bool}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hs : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime s encIn encNat)
+    (ht : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime t encIn encNat)
+    (hv : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime v encIn encBits)
+    (hw : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime w encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => F.encodeProjHash (d a) (s a) (t a) (v a) (w a)) encIn encBits :=
+  F.computableInPolyTime_add.tidy.comp (hd.prod
+    ((F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp (hd.prod (hs.prod hv))).prod
+      (F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp (hd.prod (ht.prod hw)))))
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHashAux
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc} {s t : γ → ℕ} {u : γ → List Bool}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hs : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime s encIn encNat)
+    (ht : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime t encIn encNat)
+    (hu : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime u encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => F.encodeProjHashAux (d a) (s a) (t a) (u a)) encIn encBits :=
+  F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash hd hs ht
+    (F.computableInPolyTime_generator.tidy.comp hd) hu
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash2
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc}
+    {s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ r : γ → ℕ} {v w : γ → List Bool}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hs₁ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime s₁ encIn encNat)
+    (ht₁ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime t₁ encIn encNat)
+    (hs₂ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime s₂ encIn encNat)
+    (ht₂ : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime t₂ encIn encNat)
+    (hr : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime r encIn encNat)
+    (hv : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime v encIn encBits)
+    (hw : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime w encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => F.encodeProjHash2 (d a) (s₁ a) (t₁ a) (s₂ a) (t₂ a) (r a) (v a) (w a))

+    ((F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash hd hs₁ ht₁ hv hw).prod

+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc} {u : γ → List Bool}
+    {sk : γ → (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))}

+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup public key generation is computable in polynomial time. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey :
+    ComputableInPolyTime
+      (fun p : F.Desc × List Bool × ((ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) =>
+        F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)

+  .of_tidy (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey

+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupChallenge
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits)
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc}
+    {sk : γ → (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))} {v w m : γ → List Bool}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hsk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime sk encIn encCramerShoupSK)
+    (hv : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime v encIn encBits)
+    (hw : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime w encIn encBits)
+    (hm : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime m encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H (d a) (sk a) (v a) (w a) (m a))

+  have he := F.computableInPolyTime_add.tidy.comp (hd.prod

+    (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash2 hd
+      hsk.snd'.fst'.fst' hsk.snd'.fst'.snd' hsk.snd'.snd'.fst' hsk.snd'.snd'.snd' hr hv hw))))

+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup secret-key challenge encryption `encodeCramerShoupChallenge` is
+computable in polynomial time whenever `H` is. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupChallenge
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime
+      (fun p : F.Desc × ((ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool =>
+        F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2.1 p.2.2.2.1 p.2.2.2.2)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encCramerShoupSK (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))))
+      encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupChallenge hH.tidy
+    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop))
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupEncrypt
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits)
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc}
+    {pk : γ → List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool} {m : γ → List Bool} {b : γ → ℕ}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hpk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime pk encIn
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits))))
+    (hm : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime m encIn encBits)
+    (hb : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime b encIn encNat) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => F.encodeCramerShoupEncrypt H (d a) (pk a) (m a) (b a)) encIn encBits := by
+  have hv := F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp
+    (hd.prod (hb.prod (F.computableInPolyTime_generator.tidy.comp hd)))
+  have hw := F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp (hd.prod (hb.prod hpk.fst'))
+  have he := F.computableInPolyTime_add.tidy.comp
+    (hd.prod ((F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp (hd.prod (hb.prod hpk.snd'.fst'))).prod hm))
+  have hr := ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsToNat.comp (hH.comp (hd.prod
+    ((ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits3).comp (hv.prod (hw.prod he)))))
+  have hz' := F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp (hd.prod (hb.prod
+    (F.computableInPolyTime_add.tidy.comp (hd.prod (hpk.snd'.snd'.fst'.prod
+      (F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.comp (hd.prod (hr.prod hpk.snd'.snd'.snd'))))))))
+  exact (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits4).comp (hv.prod (hw.prod (he.prod hz')))
+
+/-- Word-level Cramer–Shoup encryption is computable in polynomial time whenever `H` is. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupEncrypt
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime
+      (fun p : F.Desc × (List Bool × List Bool × List Bool × List Bool) × List Bool × ℕ =>
+        F.encodeCramerShoupEncrypt H p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2.1 p.2.2.2)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encBits4 (encPair encBits encNat))) encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupEncrypt hH.tidy
+    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop))
+
+@[local fun_prop]
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool} {isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits)
+    (hisElem : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime isElem (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBool)
+    {γ : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {d : γ → F.Desc}
+    {sk : γ → (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))} {ct : γ → List Bool}
+    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn F.encDesc)
+    (hsk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime sk encIn encCramerShoupSK)
+    (hct : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime ct encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem (d a) (sk a) (ct a))
+      encIn (encOption encBits) := by
+  have hparts := computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeBits4.comp hct
+  have hv := hparts.fst'; have hw := hparts.snd'.fst'
+  have he := hparts.snd'.snd'.fst'; have hz' := hparts.snd'.snd'.snd'
+  have hr := ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsToNat.comp (hH.comp (hd.prod
+    ((ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits3).comp (hv.prod (hw.prod he)))))
+  have hbeq : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => p.1 == p.2) (encPair encBits encBits) encBool := by polytime
+  have hand : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun p : Bool × Bool => p.1 && p.2) (encPair encBool encBool) encBool := by polytime
+  have hframe := hbeq.comp (((ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encode encBits4).comp hparts).prod hct)
+  have htagEq := hbeq.comp ((F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash2 hd
+    hsk.snd'.fst'.fst' hsk.snd'.fst'.snd' hsk.snd'.snd'.fst' hsk.snd'.snd'.snd' hr hv hw).prod hz')
+  have hcond := hand.comp ((hand.comp ((hand.comp ((hand.comp
+    (hframe.prod (hisElem.comp (hd.prod hv)))).prod (hisElem.comp (hd.prod hw)))).prod
+    (hisElem.comp (hd.prod he)))).prod htagEq)
+  have hmsg := F.computableInPolyTime_add.tidy.comp (hd.prod (he.prod
+    (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeGroupNeg hd
+      (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_encodeProjHash hd hsk.fst'.fst' hsk.fst'.snd' hv hw))))
+  have hsome : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun x : List Bool => (some x : Option (List Bool))) encBits (encOption encBits) := by
+    polytime
+  exact .cond hcond (hsome.comp hmsg) (.const none)
+
+/-- **Word-level Cramer–Shoup decryption is computable in polynomial time** whenever `H` and
+`isElem` are computable in polynomial time. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool} {isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits)
+    (hisElem : ComputableInPolyTime isElem (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime
+      (fun p : F.Desc × ((ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) × List Bool =>
+        F.decodeCramerShoup H isElem p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encCramerShoupSK encBits)) (encOption encBits) :=
+  .of_tidy (F.computableTidilyInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup hH.tidy hisElem.tidy
+    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop))
+
+/-! ### Stateless oracle simulation lemmas -/
+
+/-- Run a `WordOracleComp Unit α` against a stateless deterministic oracle
+`o : List Bool → List Bool` and feed its output to `next : α → Game`. -/
+noncomputable def runStatelessOracle {α : Type} (o : List Bool → List Bool)

title: feat(crypto): Multiplicative Cramer-Shoup scheme and adaptive Lemma 12.8 consumer (#1000)
body:
## Summary

Part of #1000 (Step 3: Cramer–Shoup CCA2-secure public-key encryption from DDH in the standard model, PR 2 following #1096).

This PR adds `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CramerShoup/Scheme.lean` and `ComplexityTests/Crypto/CramerShoup.lean`, formalizing:

1. **Algebraic and word-level Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup public-key encryption ($\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$)** ([Boneh and Shoup, _A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography_, Version 0.6](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf), Section 12.5.3 and Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 488–493, 521–522, specialized to associated data $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$):
   - Algebraic operations over `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`: `cramerShoupHashMod`, `encodeCramerShoupTriple`, `cramerShoupPublicKey`, `cramerShoupEncrypt`, `cramerShoupEncrypt_cramerShoupPublicKey`, `cramerShoupDecrypt`, and `cramerShoupDecrypt_cramerShoupEncrypt`.
   - Word-level operations and framing: `encBits3`, `decodeBits3`, `decodeBits3_encBits3`, `encBits4`, `decodeBits4`, `decodeBits4_encBits4`, `extractCramerShoupTriple`, `extractCramerShoupTriple_encBits4`, `encCramerShoupSK`, `encodeGroupNeg`, `encodeGroupNeg_encode`, `encodeProjHash`, `encodeProjHash_encode`, `encodeProjHashAux`, `encodeProjHashAux_encode`, `encodeProjHash2`, `encodeProjHash2_encode`, `encodeCramerShoupPublicKeyValues`, `encodeCramerShoupPublicKey`, `encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_encode`, `encodeCramerShoupCiphertext`, `encodeCramerShoupEncrypt`, `encodeCramerShoupEncrypt_encode`, `encodeCramerShoupChallenge`, `encodeCramerShoupChallenge_encode`, `decodeCramerShoup`, `decodeCramerShoup_encode`, and `decodeCramerShoup_cramerShoupEncrypt`.
2. **Polynomial-time computability certificates** (plain-first surface per #456):
   - `computableInPolyTime_decodeBits4`, `computableInPolyTime_extractCramerShoupTriple`, `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey`, `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupChallenge`, `computableInPolyTime_encodeCramerShoupEncrypt`, and `computableInPolyTime_decodeCramerShoup`.
3. **Adaptive Lemma 12.8 / Lemma 12.6 consumer (Games 3 $\to$ 3.5 $\to$ 4 $\to$ 5)** (reusing the stateless oracle interpreter `runStatelessOracle` and `Game` mixture/support bounds extracted in supplier #1193):
   - Group-order bound helper: `div_order_le_div_of_le`.
   - Phase 1/2 decryption replies, collision predicate, and non-DH bad-event predicate: `isCramerShoupCollision`, `isCramerShoupCollision_eq_isCollisionFor`, `cramerShoupPhase1Reply`, `cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Reply`, `skNatOfZMod`, `decodeCramerShoupDH`, `cramerShoupDHPhase1Reply`, `cramerShoupDHPhase2Reply`, `isCramerShoupBadDH`, `HonestPhase1QueryBound`, and `HonestPhase2QueryBound`.
   - Adaptive Lemma 12.8 projective-hash rejection and Lemma 12.6 one-time group-mask hybrid games and bounds: `cramerShoupGame3`, `cramerShoupGame3Half`, `advantage_cramerShoupGame3_game3Half_le` ($\le Q_1 / m$), `cramerShoupGame4`, `advantage_cramerShoupGame3Half_game4_le` ($\le Q_2 / m$), `advantage_cramerShoupGame3_game4_le` ($\le (Q_1 + Q_2) / m$), `cramerShoupGame5`, `cramerShoupGame5_false_eq_true`, and `advantage_cramerShoupGame4_game5_le` ($\le 1 / m$).

The follow-up PR 3 stacks directly on this module to add the approximate exponent sampler, the certified strict-PPT DDH distinguisher and CRHF collision-finder reductions, Games 0 $\to$ 1 $\to$ 2 $\to$ 3, and the end-to-end concrete and asymptotic `cca2GameOn` / `INDCCA2On` theorems.

## Source Statements ([Boneh and Shoup, v0.6](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf), Sections 12.5.1–12.5.3 & Exercise 12.27)

Verbatim from Boneh–Shoup v0.6, Sections 12.5.1–12.5.2 (Lemma 12.6 in §12.5.1, printed p. 486; Lemma 12.8 in §12.5.2, printed p. 488):
> **Lemma 12.6.** In Attack Game 12.4, $\Pr[W_0] = \Pr[W_1]$ for all adversaries $\mathcal{A}$.
> …
> **Lemma 12.8.** In Attack Game 12.5, for any adversary $\mathcal{A}$ that outputs at most $Q$ tuples, the probability that it wins is at most $Q/q$.

Verbatim from Boneh–Shoup v0.6, Section 12.5.3 (printed pp. 488–493):
> - the key generation algorithm runs as follows:
>   $$\begin{aligned}
>   G() :=\quad & \alpha \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; u \leftarrow g^\alpha,\;
>     \sigma, \tau \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; h \leftarrow g^\sigma u^\tau \\
>   & \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2 \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\;
>     h_1 \leftarrow g^{\sigma_1} u^{\tau_1},\; h_2 \leftarrow g^{\sigma_2} u^{\tau_2} \\
>   & pk \leftarrow (u, h, h_1, h_2),\;
>     sk \leftarrow (\sigma, \tau, \sigma_1, \tau_1, \sigma_2, \tau_2),\;
>     \text{output } (pk, sk);
>   \end{aligned}$$
> …
> **Game 5.** We again widen the rejection rule at line (5), replacing it with:
> $$(5) \qquad \text{if } \hat{v}^\alpha \ne \hat{w} \text{ or } \mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v}) \text{ or } z' \ne f'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{\rho})$$
> So this rule will reject the ciphertext if $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \notin L_u$.
> Let $Z_5$ be the event that in Game 5, some decryption query, which would not have triggered the rejection rule of Game 4, does trigger the wider rejection rule in Game 5. Clearly, Games 4 and 5 proceed identically unless event $Z_5$ occurs. By the Difference Lemma, we have
> $$|\Pr[W_4] - \Pr[W_5]| \le \Pr[Z_5]. \quad (12.26)$$
> We will argue that $\Pr[Z_5] \le Q_d / q$. $(12.27)$
> …
> **Game 6.** Everything we did so far was leading to this point, which is the crux of the proof. We replace line (2) in Fig. 12.3 with $z \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{G}$. We claim that $\Pr[W_6] = \Pr[W_5]$. $(12.28)$ This follows from Lemma 12.6, and the fact that in processing decryption queries in Game 5, we only need to evaluate $f(\hat{v}, \hat{w})$ at points $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \in L_u$.
> …

> **12.27 (Multiplicative Cramer-Shoup encryption).** Consider the following multiplicative version of the Cramer-Shoup encryption scheme (presented in Section 12.5) that supports associated data (see Section 12.7) coming from a set $\mathcal{D}$. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a cyclic group of prime order $q$ with generator $g \in \mathbb{G}$. Let $H' : \mathbb{G}^3 \times \mathcal{D} \to \mathbb{Z}_q$ be a hash function. The encryption scheme $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}} = (G, E, D)$ is defined over $(\mathbb{G}, \mathcal{D}, \mathbb{G}^4)$ as follows. Key generation is exactly as in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$. For a given public key $pk = (u, h, h_1, h_2) \in \mathbb{G}^4$ message $m \in \mathbb{G}$, and associated data $d \in \mathcal{D}$, the encryption algorithm runs as follows:
> $$E(pk, m, d) := \beta \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; v \leftarrow g^\beta,\; w \leftarrow u^\beta,\; e \leftarrow h^\beta \cdot m,\; \rho \leftarrow H'(v, w, e, d),\; z' \leftarrow (h_1 h_2^\rho)^\beta,\; \text{output } (v, w, e, z').$$

> $$D(sk, (v, w, e, z', d)) := \rho \leftarrow H'(v, w, e, d);\; \text{if } v^{\sigma_1 + \rho \sigma_2} w^{\tau_1 + \rho \tau_2} = z' \text{ then output } e / (v^\sigma w^\tau) \text{ else output reject}.$$

- `advantage_cramerShoupGame4_game5_le` proves the $1 / m$ one-time group-mask bound by applying `uniform_projHash_fiber_add` (Lemma 12.6) on every non-DDH tuple $\gamma \ne \alpha \beta$, with failure event $\gamma = \alpha \beta$ of probability $1 / |\mathbb{G}| \le 1 / m$.

Adds normal-CI automation regressions for the original unfolded AddTrivial construction and both #1063 nested unary-arithmetic proofs. The tests retain the original expressions, encodings, arbitrary parameters, locally derived arithmetic certificate, default tactic settings and 200,000-heartbeat limit. AddTrivial is unfolded before search; captured companions require both supplied graph/list certificates.

A **new** depth-four Boolean representative and missing-deep-branch control run under minimal direct-core and full-PPT imports. This does not claim to recover the lost historical reviewer probe. All four files are test-only; no library, tactic, proof API, program or budget changes. Existing Extraction12k, Cloud and #1168 coverage is reused.

This is a bounded milestone for [#1155](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1155), not completion: **LiuPass's original automatic threshold proof still fails at its original 200,000 limit**, and the full timing/coverage survey remains open. Its explicit production proof is unchanged. [Exact replay/evidence](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1155#issuecomment-6413678761); [source checkpoint/coverage limits](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1155#issuecomment-6413799662).

Validation: [exact hosted CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40307886044/job/121521441066). [Local source/log packet](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/tree/47d62411/evidence/1155/test-milestone-784105bf) includes the fresh unchanged896/132 ratchet and focused checks. [Nonauthor source/test assessment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1171#issuecomment-6413855250) is clean. The arithmetic fixtures use compact required local contexts; full historical-theorem replays remain separate evidence.

AI-assisted implementation by worker review_560; separate-context assessment by review_559, adopted by coordinator-codex-01a16ab8 under the AGENTS test-only delegated-review exception. No author selfapproval.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-84 — APPROVED at 82860094aa1363005e1674471d2a342dc429dbca

Agent review, not human approval.

Scope: statements, definitions, faithfulness and API of the +1342/−0 diff against #1147's head `5b65c483`. Hosted `ci-checks` and `check-title` pass at this exact head ([run 40318413562](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40318413562)). The base is #1147's branch, so this merges after #1147 lands. `git merge-tree` of this head with current `main` is clean. No local build.

What I checked:
- Uniqueness is proved in both directions as `∃!` statements. `Crossover.existsUnique_holds`, `Crossover.existsUnique_split_holds` and `PairedCrossover.existsUnique_holds` each give a kernel-checked satisfying `canonicalExtension a b` for every input pair. Each also proves that every satisfying assignment equals that extension at all variables, internal copies included. `OrdinaryRing.eval_formula_iff` and `PairedCrossover.eval_formula_iff` are exact `↔` characterizations. `PairedWire.eval_links_iff` is an iff under the explicit `Cell.Agree` hypothesis, and `Cell.Agree` is documented as an obligation for later local constraints. The tests show that the hypothesis is satisfiable and that the links alone do not force agreement. None of these statements is vacuous.
- `PairedCrossover` reduces correctly to the existing split crossover. `mapLiteral` separates each terminal's two incidences by polarity. Each `chain s` is a cycle `copy → port → port → copy`, closed by the ring equality. `terminal_occurrences = 2` per port is checked by `decide +kernel`. The counts are 57 variables and 78 = 74 + 4 clauses, which matches 8 ports, `center` and 8 × 6 copies.
- Reuse: `OrdinaryRing.formula` is `implicationCycle cyclicOrder`. The paired crossover builds on `Crossover.splitFormula`, `eval_splitFormula_iff`, `eval_ring_iff` and `boundary_eq_of_holds` (merged #1111/#1122 infrastructure), and wires use `Clause.imp`/`consecutivePairs`. The new `PairedWire` is not a parallel notion of `DirectedWire`: it is a two-lane equality wire, where `DirectedWire` is a one-lane wire that propagates truth in one direction. The side numbering 2 = bottom ↔ `.bTop` is documented and agrees with the existing layout, where `.bTop` sits at `(120, 20)`.
- Certificates: no `native_decide`, `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `set_option` (heartbeats or otherwise) in the diff. Finite facts use `decide +kernel`.
- Sources: the PR description quotes “3Sat is parsimoniously reducible to Pl-3SAT”. That text is verbatim from Theorem 3.2, §3, of arXiv cs/9809017v1. The paraphrases of Definition 3.1 (opposite terminal equality and unique extension) and Claim 3.3 are accurate. The new `references.bib` entry matches Crossref (SIAM J. Comput. 27(4):1142–1167, doi 10.1137/S0097539793304601). The Lichtenstein and Tromino credits are reused. The paired wire, ring, ports and spokes are labeled original. The statements are plain-first, with no tidy machinery.
- Size: +1342, within the reviewable range.

Nonblocking findings:
1. Source credit, `Complexity/Logics/Propositional/CNF/Planar/CrossoverCounting.lean:29-31`. `existsUnique_holds` is the parsimony property of Definition 3.1 in [HuntMaratheRadhakrishnanStearns1998], stated for the adapted Lichtenstein crossover. That paper's §3 Theorem 3.2 is exactly the result “the crossover box in [15] is parsimonious”, where [15] is Lichtenstein. The module currently credits only the construction, and it neither cites that result nor labels the uniqueness as original. The bib entry added here is first cited in #1180's endpoint. Suggested line: “Unique extension is the parsimony of Lichtenstein's crossover box, [HuntMaratheRadhakrishnanStearns1998, Theorem 3.2]; the adapted 13-variable table is checked here by kernel evaluation.” This file is unchanged through #1180, so this can land in a later layer or a follow-up without restacking.
2. Duplicated instance. This PR adds three more copies of `private instance (r : Route) : Decidable (IsOrthogonal r)`, at `OrdinaryRing.lean:117`, `PairedPorts.lean:97` and `PairedSpokes.lean:53`, besides the existing one in `CrossoverLayoutChecks.lean:97`. The stack tip has six. One public `instance : DecidablePred IsOrthogonal` beside `IsOrthogonal` in `Complexity/Foundations/Geometry/Orthogonal.lean` would replace all of them. A follow-up is fine.
3. Doc nit, `PairedCrossover.lean:27-30`. "Main results" omits the two headline statements, `existsUnique_holds` and `eval_formula_iff`.

For reviewers of later layers (not findings on this PR): at the #1180 tip, `DirectedWire` has no clients besides its own test. `PairedGeometry.lean` re-declares `boundary_eq_cases` as a thin wrapper of `PairedPorts.boundary_eq_cases`.

title: feat(planar-SAT): certify paired wires and unique gadget extensions
body:
## Change

Layer 2/8 of #1144, based on #1147. The complete stack and review handoff are recorded on #1147.

Add paired implication wires, eight-port equality rings and a 57-variable/78-clause crossover with unique extensions. Prove canonical assignments and uniqueness for the existing original and split crossovers as well. Each boundary port has two internal occurrences, reserving one external occurrence for the later compiler. Generic geometric interfaces certify lane-preserving accesses and clause spokes; this layer does not assemble a global drawing.

Source: [Hunt–Marathe–Radhakrishnan–Stearns, arXiv v1, §3, Theorem 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/9809017v1): “3Sat is parsimoniously reducible to Pl-3SAT”. Definition 3.1 and Claim 3.3 specify opposite terminal equality and a unique extension of the two input bits. Our uniqueness statements use that boundary relation for the repository's already credited crossover templates. The paired degree-three assembly and geometric interfaces are original; this is not a claim to formalize the paper's #P-completeness conclusion.

Public entry point: `Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF.PairedWire.eval_links_iff`.

Existing notions considered: Reuses existing CNF clauses, implication cycles, original crossover and split-variable types, Orthogonal routes and real-support geometry. New finite side/lane tags distinguish ports of the paired construction; generic wire agreement expresses the required four-port equality rather than defining another satisfiability relation.

## Validation and review

All six local `scripts/check.sh` gates pass at `82860094aa1363005e1674471d2a342dc429dbca` with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4`: strict build, aggregate check, full tests including the axiom audit, lint, style and Init imports. Hygiene checks pass. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40318413562) is linked separately from these local results.

[Internal technical review and source-identity record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1147#issuecomment-6415439402). Outside-fleet coordinator approval remains required.

## Headline abstracts

No selected abstract statement, definition, scope, catalogue entry or rendering changes. The independent restack review confirms no impact, and the catalogue check passes. No new PDF review is needed.

## AI assistance

Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) implemented the original development and this split, with separate non-authoring internal review contexts. No human or outside-fleet approval is claimed.

Independent source assessment at **de6e8d7ff633f23dc9695d63d97cbed049666cf6**, own payload above **8d9988a9719c15bef2177a8f3be75e0a8a5c3e94**: no blocking model/count/API finding. I checked the actual emitted formula, opposite link lanes, projection and extension proofs. Clauses preserve original literal order/signs; ordinary rings are emitted only for retained occupied noncrossing cells. `sourceVariable_mem_rawFormula` ensures each used source representative really occurs. `ordinary_occurrence_exists` prevents orphan rings, and `crossing_axes_exist` derives both occupied axes from the selected actual paths and source width/occurrence-three hypotheses. Thus crossover internal uniqueness is applied with both inputs determined, not a free unused input or supplied compatibility hypothesis. The four-way `raw_assignments_agree` case split covers original clauses, rings, crossovers and links. Existence is separately proved for every satisfying source assignment; projection gives an actual source model. The finite-image counting theorem consequently has both its fiber-agreement and image-surjectivity obligations discharged. Both counts are over occurring variables, and existing compaction preserves that convention; unrestricted values outside support are not counted.

The original compiler/decision endpoint remains operational. The migrated tests retain contradictory/empty/crossing assertions with the new compiler's actual sizes/ports; new count clients cover empty support/clause, repeated literals, tautology, contradiction, sparse labels and a nonempty selected crossing. There is no polynomial-time solution-map, native compilation or global embedding theorem claimed by this layer, no new counting notion, and no selected-abstract impact. Assignment construction uses the existing logical choice argument, with no computational interpretation attached.

Reused [exact-head successful hosted CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40318443901) and [prior technical evidence](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1147#issuecomment-6415439402); no Lean/build/cache/source edits or independent execution. **STACK HOLD:** actual parent squash, payload-only refresh preserving this source and exact new-head CI/delta confirmation remain required; root retains final coordinator adoption. title: feat(iteration): sharpen affine-controller power bounds by coefficient synthesis
body:
The existing affine-controller bound evaluates a separate affine circuit for each of the $2^q$ controller states. This PR computes the final matrix and offset coefficients as Boolean functions of the initial controller, then evaluates one affine map. For $F(u,v)=(g(u),A_u v+b_u)$, every fixed iterate has gate bound

```
(q + p*(p+1))*L + p*(5*(p+1)+1).
```

Here `L` bounds scalar synthesis on `q` inputs. The finite endpoint uses `L = 27*2^q/q` (natural division after multiplication) for `q ≥ 16`. The asymptotic endpoint uses `(1+ε)*2^q/q`, with a threshold uniform in `p`, `g`, the affine maps and the exponent. For `p=q`, the old $O(q^2 2^q)$ budget becomes $O(q2^q)$. An `m`-bit input exponent costs `m*(newBudget + 4*(q+p))` through the existing binary-powering theorem.

This is a derived application of classical scalar Shannon/Lupanov synthesis, not an established improvement over the published research state of the art. It retains the existing native De Morgan model, arbitrary autonomous controllers and arbitrary affine payloads, including singular maps. NOT, AND, OR and constant gates are charged; wiring and fanout are free. These are nonuniform existence bounds: construction time for the iterated coefficient tables is not bounded. The old all-width theorem remains available.

The proof reuses `controlledBits`, `controlledPayload_mem`, `affineMapSeed`, `affineHash_affineMapSeed`, `Synthesis`, and the scalar synthesis theorems. The only new definition is the explicit gate-budget expression; no new circuit or iteration model is introduced. See the [previous bound](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/blob/a563632336b598c88e5231437c4cbef68a0644a7/Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Iteration/AffineController.lean) and [scalar Lupanov theorem](https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/blob/6ff325e870ed89f86be10515f0e7297fa5a32845/Cslib/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Lupanov.lean). This PR derives its endpoint from those existing results rather than porting a quoted external theorem.

Validation and review:
- The three affected library modules and the regression module pass isolated Lean 4.36.0-rc1 checks without warnings, using the pinned dependencies and separate mutable outputs.
- Regressions use a controller-dependent nonsymmetric affine shear and offset, a nontrivial fourth iterate, arbitrary-time translations, zero payload width, and little-endian input time. Exact budget tests show more than 3× improvement at `q=p=16` and more than 6× at `q=p=32`.
- The four public endpoints use only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Proof hygiene, whitespace and aggregate-source checks pass. [Full repository CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40320339638/job/121563368340) passes on `a36ebb956389166c8172ac36671f449446b09e32`, including strict build, tests, lint, aggregate generation, style and initialization-import checks. Local full gates were attempted but blocked at dependency fetching; hosted CI completed all six gates.
- Internal mathematical/API review found no correctness issue; its documentation findings are resolved. This is agent review, not independent coordinator approval.
- Selected abstracts and their scope are unaffected; no catalogue/PDF change is needed.

title: feat(threshold): improve lower bounds for bounded direct input support
body:
The existing two-sided rectangle-free transfer gives $q \ge n/2-k$ input-reading gates. This PR improves its leading coefficient when each gate has bounded direct support on the original inputs. For fixed $d>0$, it proves $q>(1/[2(1-2^{-d})]-\varepsilon)n$ eventually when the rectangle threshold has sublinear binary logarithm. At $d=3$, the coefficient is **4/7**, compared with **1/2** in the general transfer. Internal predecessor fan-in, depth, fan-out, and real weights remain unrestricted; support uses the existing aggregated coefficients.

### What is proved

For both Boolean fibers $K$-rectangle-free across every coordinate partition, $K\le 2^k$, and every natural cutoff $T$,

$$
n \le \left(2(1-2^{-d})+\frac{d}{T+1}\right)q+2k+(T+1)\sqrt{2n}.
$$

The proof fixes high-incidence inputs, uses the exact probability $1-2^{-d}$ that a random cut meets a support of size $d$, and controls the cut deficit with Boolean Poincaré and complement symmetry. The implementation includes a reusable finite hypergraph-cut lemma, native program and circuit bounds, and the asymptotic consequence. The program theorem permits any fixed Boolean readout of all gate values.

A separate bridge from the existing probabilistic bias witness proves that, for every $n$, functions with both fibers $16(n+1)$-rectangle-free exist. The quantitative regression uses $n=2{,}000{,}000$, $K=32{,}000{,}016$, $k=25$, $d=3$, and $T=39$: the new bound requires **1,052,028** input-reading gates, while the old inequality requires **999,975**. Native-circuit tests also cover cutoff zero and fixing every input.

### Scope and review

This is a stronger conditional transfer under a direct-support restriction, with a nonconstructive witness. It does **not** supply an explicit polynomial-time hard family. The existing support-at-most-two theorem has a stronger coefficient in that regime. Follow-up research in #1203 found a stronger 3/5 consequence of the classical Chvátal–McDiarmid/Tuza transversal bound combined with the support-two transfer. Thus the support-three 4/7 corollary improves the prior library endpoint but is not the strongest available mathematical consequence. This PR does not claim an established beyond-the-literature result; #1203 is pursuing a stronger 2/3 endpoint. The explicit-family objective remains open in ROADMAP.

title: perf(sipser-lautemann): guide nested verifier proof search
body:
The Sipser–Lautemann verifier certificate leaves intermediate encodings open across nested list operations. Apply the existing search/count and unary-comparison closure rules explicitly, fixing the natural-number encodings before fun_prop solves the remaining smaller goals.

Only the proof of `Cslib.Complexity.SipserLautemann.verifier_polyTime` changes: 13 added lines and two removed. Every source byte outside that proof is unchanged, including the verifier, theorem statement, automation registration and curated abstract scope.

A controlled, unprofiled comparison of source baseline `74621a48` and submitted head `26bd75c1` gave:

| Target declaration interval (seconds) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First sample | 317.302 | 2.462 |
| Second sample | 313.084 | 6.410 |
| Mean | 315.193 | 4.436 |

The measured mean reduction is **98.59%**, with both adjacent paired comparisons favoring the patch. One temporary module checks the exact original source prefix once, then four exact renamed, untagged declarations in after/before/before/after order. It neither imports the original target module nor makes preceding copies available to automation. The copies omit the fun_prop registration, which Mathlib applies after compilation; their proof-search environment is preserved.

Lean v4.36.0-rc1 runs with one thread, synchronous elaboration, warnings as errors, standard linters and no profiling. Flushed monotonic timestamps immediately bracket each declaration; the intervals include common endpoint-marker and command overhead, including synchronous elaboration and kernel checking. Imports and the shared prefix precede the timed intervals. Fixed cached inputs come from checkout `7dcfac10`: all 23,924 recorded artifact metadata entries and the seven module artifact hashes, setup hash and runtime hash remained unchanged. All four proofs passed with exactly eight markers and zero diagnostics. Five unsuccessful or interrupted discovery/profiling attempts are excluded.

These are two samples per variant on a shared host, with variation in the after samples. The percentage applies to these declaration intervals; whole-module and end-to-end build savings are unmeasured.

[Full hosted Lean CI passed](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40332512309) for the submitted source against current dependencies, including all six required gates and the existing Sipser–Lautemann tests, abstract and abstract clients. The actual changed module built in 3.6 seconds; that is separate build evidence, not the basis of the percentage. The complete edited module also passed an uninstrumented local compiler check with zero diagnostics. Source hygiene, outside-proof byte comparison, catalogue validation and PR-description name checks pass.

A separate non-authoring ChatGPT agent reviewed the exact final source, benchmark harness, raw timestamps and input snapshots, independently reproduced the calculation, and found no blockers. This is internal agent review; maintainer/coordinator review is requested.

This bounded contribution to #622 is independent of #1173 and #1186.

AI assistance: ChatGPT implemented and benchmarked the change, with source and benchmark review by a separate ChatGPT agent.

title: feat(fo): define BIT on arbitrary-base full tuples
body:
Closes #112.

Defines `tupleBit L k`, an actual native first-order formula over canonical order and BIT, and proves exact BIT semantics for the lexicographic ranks of full base-n tuples on every `Fin n`, `n >= 2`. Both the represented value and index can exceed the source universe. High indices are rejected; dimension zero is explicitly false.

The construction uses checked radix-word affine arithmetic, multiplication, conversion, and a cardinality word obtained from `max + 1`. Its witnessed binary radix satisfies `B^3 < n`; seven digits encode the cardinality and `7k` digits encode each rank. Full-word index matching uses base-one conversion, so no out-of-domain scalar index is assumed. A fixed finite disjunction covers source sizes 2 through 8. No formula-size efficiency, restricted-domain BIT, or completed numeric-preserving composition is claimed.

Source: Neil Immerman, *Descriptive Complexity*, [Remark 1.32 and Exercise 1.33(3), printed p.25 / PDF p.37](https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/book/ch0_1_2.pdf#page=37). This is an explicit implementation of the full-domain exercise, not a claimed transcription of its arithmetic hint. Existing PLUS/TIMES source credit is preserved.

Validation at source `92915665afb129fbdbe0051fcb4a56c4b994be96`: all six repository gates passed; fresh focused Lean MCP diagnostics and the headline axiom guard are clean. Clients cover n = 2, 8, 9, 64; a true index 9 over Fin 9; MSB orientation; the seventh cardinality digit; high rejection; zero dimension; relabeling; inclusive carries; and exact overflow. Current main `68b94b2817a812b43069aff9558393af622ec71b` integrated cleanly at final head `c90ddbe0fdcfa21af2e239656ec73039e5c5ef3b`; all six combined gates also passed. Exact-head remote Lean CI and title/PDF checks passed.

Theorem-index assessment: one new curated entry plus corrected completion boundaries in preceding entries; three declaration links pin the exact source above. The combined PDF contains 142 entries. The local document builds cleanly and affected pages 9–12 were inspected. The [successful CI artifact](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/actions/runs/39510318731/artifacts/12305701403) matches that document; its clean synthetic merge source `ccb75cd7de3638aae9c78410585612140fc6a23f`, head/base provenance, PDF digest and all new links were verified. Independent semantic index review and final coordinator source/artifact/integration review are approved. Generated PDFs remain untracked.

Independent review: [radix design](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/issues/112#issuecomment-6302912869), [affine design delta](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/issues/112#issuecomment-6303036188), and [arithmetic-checkpoint approval](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/issues/112#issuecomment-6303284514). title: perf(time-hierarchy): reduce arithmetic proof search
body:
The private clocked-diagonal resource proof used general ring normalization for simple product/power identities and searched its whole accumulated context at the final arithmetic steps. Use the existing multiplication/power identities directly, prove one bound by transitivity, and retain only the four relevant bounds for each final omega search.

Only the proof of `Cslib.Complexity.Diagonal.clockedBounds_aux` changes: 13 added lines and eight removed. Every byte outside the proof, and its chosen witness, is unchanged. The public time-hierarchy statements, mathematical resource bounds, definitions, imports and curated abstract scope are preserved. This is a bounded compile-time contribution to #622.

Controlled, unprofiled comparison of source baseline `d042a032` and submitted head `7a51643e`:

| Target declaration interval (seconds) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First sample | 143.254 | 54.473 |
| Second sample | 218.422 | 52.028 |
| Mean | 180.838 | 53.250 |

The measured mean reduction is **70.55%**, with both adjacent paired comparisons favoring the patch. One compiler process checks the exact original prefix, then four exact renamed private declarations in after/before/before/after order. It neither imports the original target module nor reuses preceding copies. An untimed public sentinel after all eight markers satisfies the private-module linter.

Lean v4.36.0-rc1 runs with one thread, synchronous elaboration, warnings as errors, standard linters and no profiler. Flushed monotonic timestamps bracket each declaration, including synchronous elaboration, kernel checking and common marker/command overhead; imports and the shared prefix precede the intervals. All 23,924 recorded artifact metadata entries and seven module hashes, plus setup/compiler/harness/runner hashes, stayed unchanged. All four proofs passed with zero diagnostics. body:
## Change

Samuel asked for the roadmap to be improved and expanded tastefully. The file keeps its "directions only" convention: status lives on issues and PRs.

- **Landmarks.**
  - **Gentry's bootstrapping, instantiated, is complete.** #486 is closed and the checked abstract `gsw-fhe` is on `main`, so it leaves the priority list. Its open follow-ups (#1104) move into the "Modern fully homomorphic encryption" intro: uniform compactness, multi-hop evaluation, and Gentry's exact loss together with Theorem 4's `poly(ℓ, d)` running-time clause. The joint `(λ, d)` runtime landed in #1123, so it is not listed.
  - **New landmark 10: the Immerman–Vardi theorem** (FO(LFP) = P on ordered structures). Descriptive-complexity workers are being staffed now (#587). The order of the existing landmarks is unchanged.
- **Descriptive complexity.** The vague "further logical characterizations" bullet becomes concrete: Immerman–Vardi; FO(TC) = NL and FO(DTC) = L; SO-Horn = P (Grädel); and DLOGTIME-uniform AC⁰ = FO(≤, BIT) (Barrington–Immerman–Straubing).
- **Algebraic complexity.** Adds partial-derivative measures (the Nisan–Wigderson depth-3 bounds and shifted partials) and the depth-reduction chasms at depth four (Agrawal–Vinay) and depth three (Gupta–Kamath–Kayal–Saptharishi). #1188 is a first contribution in this direction.
- **Programs table.** Adds planar SAT and geometric hardness (#1079), the randomized Word RAM (#1124), and proof automation (#1155). The FHE row now points at its follow-ups (#1104).
- **Machines.** The certificate-automation direction links #1155 and states its goals: regression budgets, diagnostic failures and syntax-directed composition. The randomized Word RAM direction links #1124, with quicksort and selection as first clients.

All new citations name standard results without quoting them. Exact locators get pinned in each direction's M0 design, per the source-verification practice.

Documentation only. Prose lines are wrapped at 100 columns, and the only lines over 100 are tables and long URLs that were already there. Every anchor and link reference resolves. Hosted CI is pending. Review requested from `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023`, since the author is a coordinator.

title: fix: repair halted output, private automation, and tooling
body:
Refs #1198. This is the combined bug-fix PR requested by the user. It is a draft for coordinator-managed full validation and independent review.

## What was broken

- **Query-machine output changed after halting.** The transition freezes a halted state, but output still called its raw emission function on every padded clock tick. An initially halted machine with a nonempty emission produced extra output at clock 3. Output now ignores halted ticks, with stability lemmas for one step and arbitrary padding. The counter-program clients retain their first-halt hypotheses and simulation statements. The contract concerns clocks at or beyond halting; this does not introduce partial-output semantics for insufficient clocks.
- **Imported automation could crash on unavailable private constants.** Make 36 private `fun_prop` registrations local across five modules, including ten implicitly private degree lemmas in the universal-machine module. Their statements and proofs are unchanged. A new module-system regression checks project-owned private rules in all four imported theorem registries, including pending discrimination-tree entries, and exercises composed public polynomial-time certificates.
- **Upstream export missed real imports and changed literal data.** Parse the import header with the existing comment/string lexer, covering trailing comments, interleaved comments/newlines, modifiers, and multiple directives. Rewrite documentation references only inside actual comments. Marker-looking text in strings or block comments no longer removes source lines or masquerades as dependency status. Reject bare/malformed local module paths instead of crashing or aliasing another file.
- **Upstream status reports could use the wrong pin or status.** Read the cslib requirement through TOML rather than a regex spanning comments or other dependencies. Classify the leading marker status rather than explanatory prose. Report unequal hashes as DIFFERS, since equality alone cannot establish ancestry; missing pins are UNTRACKED.
- **Quick checks omitted executable clients.** Include explicit executable targets when local library changes can affect them, including non-default executables and roots importing local helper modules. Normalize source paths and support hyphenated target names. Dependency-only validation executables do not trigger unnecessary native builds.

The new output fixtures cover initially halted machines, exact first halt, padded clocks, out-of-range reads, and arbitrary padding. Tooling regressions cover the parsing/reporting failures and executable planning; a native Lean fixture changes a library value from Nat to Bool and confirms that quick validation builds—and rejects—the broken non-default executable client.

## Validation

Final refreshed source is `9f3327edf901eb8d03058a9cb04222a217430a55`, normally merged onto actual main `a8185833`. Actual #1113's GNI helper deletion wins; the obsolete locality hunk is absent. All16 remaining old payload files are byte-identical to independently reviewed1f0595cc. [Separate-context refresh confirmation](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1205#issuecomment-6423271787) reuses the prior query/non-query source assessments.

Current-head local validation:

- Full Python discovery:418 tests PASS, eight skips (410 passes).
- Explicit quick-check suite:35 tests PASS, ZERO skips, including all native cases, the real broken non-default executable and both final planner edges.
- Focused QueryMachineOutput/PrivateFunProp strict build PASS8152.
- ONE default-six sequence with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2`: all six gates PASS (strict library12633 jobs; whole original tests14020 jobs). No restart, memory-pressure abort, budget or assertion change.
- Freshness-aware native tidy ratchet PASS896 statements/132 modules, unchanged baseline; changed-file lint (8 library modules/2 test files), hygiene and diff checks PASS.

[Exact refreshed-head hosted CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40372160559) is running; hosted-green/merge readiness is not yet claimed. The successful old1f hosted run40363664727 is historical evidence, not substituted for the new head. All local jobs are terminal and source is frozen.

Reused unchanged-source evidence: the export lexer matched Lean's parser on2243 headers/7317 local import occurrences; baseline registry reproduction identified37 unavailable project-private rules before integration. The refresh correctly leaves36 locality changes after GNI removal. The two public composition fixtures are baseline API positives, not baseline failures. Earlier author overlays/interrupted full validation are historical only and are superseded by the complete current-head local sequence above. No claim that a broad audit establishes a bug-free library.

## Review and integration

Please arrange independent correctness/API review and manage CI, sequencing, and the merge queue through the coordinators in #587. Actual #1113 landed as8b36777f; its GraphNonIsomorphism helper deletion is preserved in the refresh, so no locality rule for that deleted helper remains.

The baseline registry additionally found two unavailable private rules in the pinned Mathlib module `Mathlib.Geometry.Convex.ConvexSpace.Topology`: `continuous_map_weights_apply` and `continuous_weights_apply`. They are dependency-owned findings for upstream follow-up; the project-scoped regression excludes them without an individual-name allowlist.

No selected abstract statement, resource hypothesis, or security claim changes. These are semantics, automation-visibility, and tooling repairs; the added output stability lemmas are direct consequences of the corrected definition. The broad audit found these reproducible defects and does not establish that the whole library is bug-free.

AI assistance: ChatGPT with delegated agents for machines, mathematical automation, and crypto/tooling audits, plus internal cross-review. The internal review found and resolved non-default executable, hyphenated target, and normalized-path omissions. It is not independent coordinator or human approval.
