+/-- Exact-exponent collision game matching the collision event between `cramerShoupGame2` and
+`cramerShoupGame3`. -/
+private noncomputable def cramerShoupExactCollisionGame
+    {Msg : Type} (encodeMsg : F.Desc × Msg → List Bool) (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc)
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (adversary : CCA2AdversaryOf Msg) (bit : Bool) (n : ℕ) : Game := do
+  let d ← setup n
+  let α ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let β ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let γ ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let σ ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let τ ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let σ₁ ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let τ₁ ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let σ₂ ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let τ₂ ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))
+  let sk := F.skNatOfZMod d σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂
+  let u := F.encode d (α • F.generator d)
+  let v := F.encode d (β • F.generator d)
+  let w := F.encode d (γ • F.generator d)
+  let pk := F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d u sk
+  let choiceOut ← ProbComp.eval ((OracleComp.interpret
+    (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun m => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin m))
+      (F.cramerShoupPhase1Oracle H isElem d sk))
+    (adversary.choose n pk)).run ())
+  let choice := choiceOut.1
+  let m₀ := encodeMsg (d, choice.1.1)
+  let m₁ := encodeMsg (d, choice.1.2)
+  if isElem (d, m₀) && isElem (d, m₁) then
+    let m := if bit then m₁ else m₀
+    let ct := F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H d sk v w m
+    runFinderOracle (F.cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Reply H isElem d sk ct)
+      (fun req => F.isCramerShoupCollision H d req ct) extractCramerShoupTriple
+      (adversary.guess n choice.2 ct) none
+      (fun cand => isCollisionFor (F.cramerShoupHashMod H) (fun _ _ _ => true) n d
+        cand (extractCramerShoupTriple ct))
+  else
+    return false
+
+private theorem advantage_cramerShoupGame2_game3_le_exactCollision
+    {Msg : Type} (encodeMsg : F.Desc × Msg → List Bool) (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc)
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (adversary : CCA2AdversaryOf Msg) (bit : Bool) (n : ℕ) :
+    Game.advantage
+      (F.cramerShoupGame2 encodeMsg setup H isElem adversary bit n)
+      (F.cramerShoupGame3 encodeMsg setup H isElem adversary bit n) ≤
+      Game.succProbability
+        (F.cramerShoupExactCollisionGame encodeMsg setup H isElem adversary bit n) := by
+  unfold cramerShoupGame2 cramerShoupGame3 cramerShoupExactCollisionGame
+  simp only [PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind, PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure]
+  refine advantage_bind_le_succProbability_bind (setup n) _ _ _ fun d => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun α => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun β => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun γ => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun σ => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun τ => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun σ₁ => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun τ₁ => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun σ₂ => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun τ₂ => ?_
+  refine bind_apply_le_add_bind_apply _ _ _ _ true fun choiceOut => ?_
+  by_cases h : (isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choiceOut.1.1.1)) &&
+      isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choiceOut.1.1.2))) = true
+  · simp only [h, ↓reduceIte]
+    let sk := F.skNatOfZMod d σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂
+    let v := F.encode d (β • F.generator d)
+    let w := F.encode d (γ • F.generator d)
+    let m := if bit then encodeMsg (d, choiceOut.1.1.2) else encodeMsg (d, choiceOut.1.1.1)
+    let ct := F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H d sk v w m
+    have hrun :
+        (ProbComp.eval ((OracleComp.interpret
+          (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun m => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin m))
+            (F.cramerShoupPhase2Oracle H isElem d sk ct))
+          (adversary.guess n choiceOut.1.2 ct)).run ())).bind
+            (fun guessOut => PMF.pure guessOut.1) =
+        runStatelessOracle (F.cramerShoupPhase2Reply H isElem d sk ct)
+          (adversary.guess n choiceOut.1.2 ct) PMF.pure := rfl
+    rw [hrun]
+    refine runStatelessOracle_le_runFinderOracle
+      (F.cramerShoupPhase2Reply H isElem d sk ct)
+      (F.cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Reply H isElem d sk ct)
+      (fun req => F.isCramerShoupCollision H d req ct) extractCramerShoupTriple
+      (fun cand => isCollisionFor (F.cramerShoupHashMod H) (fun _ _ _ => true) n d
+        cand (extractCramerShoupTriple ct))
+      (fun req hbad => by simp [cramerShoupPhase2Reply, cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Reply, hbad])
+      (fun req hbad => by
+        rw [← F.isCramerShoupCollision_eq_isCollisionFor H n d req ct]; exact hbad)
+      (adversary.guess n choiceOut.1.2 ct) PMF.pure true
+  · simp only [h, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
+    exact ⟨le_self_add, le_self_add⟩

+private theorem succProbability_cramerShoupExactCollisionGame_le
+    {Msg : Type} (encodeMsg : F.Desc × Msg → List Bool) (setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc)
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool) (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (hmem : ∀ d x, isElem (d, x) = true ↔ x ∈ Set.range (F.encode d))
+    (adversary : CCA2AdversaryOf Msg) (bit : Bool) (n : ℕ) :
+    Game.succProbability
+      (F.cramerShoupExactCollisionGame encodeMsg setup H isElem adversary bit n) ≤

+      9 / 2 ^ n := by

+      Game.advantage
+        (collisionGameFor setup (F.cramerShoupHashMod H) (fun _ _ _ => true) C n)
+        (F.cramerShoupExactCollisionGame encodeMsg setup H isElem adversary bit n) ≤
+      9 / 2 ^ n := by
+    unfold collisionGameFor cramerShoupExactCollisionGame C cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder
+    simp only [ProbComp.eval_bind, PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind, PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.bind_bind,
+      F.smul_encode]
+    refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal (setup n) _ _ fun d => ?_

+      let sk := F.skNatOfZMod d σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂
+      let u := F.encode d (α • F.generator d)

+        (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun m => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin m))
+          (F.cramerShoupPhase1Oracle H isElem d sk))
+        (adversary.choose n pk)).run ())).bind fun choiceOut =>
+        let choice := choiceOut.1
+        if isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choice.1.1)) && isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choice.1.2)) then
+          let m := if bit then encodeMsg (d, choice.1.2) else encodeMsg (d, choice.1.1)
+          let ct := F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H d sk v w m
+          runFinderOracle (F.cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Reply H isElem d sk ct)
+            (fun req => F.isCramerShoupCollision H d req ct) extractCramerShoupTriple
+            (adversary.guess n choice.2 ct) none
+            (fun cand => isCollisionFor (F.cramerShoupHashMod H) (fun _ _ _ => true) n d
+              cand (extractCramerShoupTriple ct))

+    let kTriple (α β γ : ZMod (F.order d)) : Game :=
+      (ProbComp.eval (F.sampleCramerShoupSK n d)).bind fun sk =>
+        let u := F.encode d (α • F.generator d)
+        let v := F.encode d (β • F.generator d)
+        let w := F.encode d (γ • F.generator d)
+        let pk := F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d u sk
+        (ProbComp.eval ((OracleComp.interpret
+          (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun m => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin m))
+            (F.cramerShoupPhase1Oracle H isElem d sk))
+          (adversary.choose n pk)).run ())).bind fun choiceOut =>
+          let choice := choiceOut.1
+          (ProbComp.eval
+            (if isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choice.1.1)) && isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choice.1.2)) then
+              let m := if bit then encodeMsg (d, choice.1.2) else encodeMsg (d, choice.1.1)
+              let ct := F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge H d sk v w m

+                (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun m => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin m))
+                  (F.cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Oracle H isElem d sk ct))
+                (adversary.guess n choice.2 ct)).run none) >>= fun out =>

+            else pure ([], []))).bind fun pair =>
+            PMF.pure (isCollisionFor (F.cramerShoupHashMod H) (fun _ _ _ => true) n d pair.1 pair.2)
+    have hstep1 := F.advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupTripleExponents_le n d kTriple
+    have hstep2 :

+            (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun β =>
+              (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun γ => kTriple α β γ)

+            (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun β =>
+              (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun γ =>
+                (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun σ =>
+                  (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun τ =>
+                    (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun σ₁ =>
+                      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun τ₁ =>
+                        (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun σ₂ =>
+                          (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun τ₂ =>
+                            kZMod α β γ σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂) ≤
+          6 / 2 ^ n := by
+      refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))) _ _ fun α => ?_
+      refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))) _ _ fun β => ?_
+      refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))) _ _ fun γ => ?_
+      refine F.advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupSK_le n d _ (kZMod α β γ)

+      by_cases h : (isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choiceOut.1.1.1)) &&
+          isElem (d, encodeMsg (d, choiceOut.1.1.2))) = true
+      · simp only [h, ↓reduceIte, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.bind_bind,
+          PMF.pure_bind]
+        rw [F.encodeCramerShoupChallenge_eq_skNatOfZMod H d ((s, t), ((s₁, t₁), (s₂, t₂))),

+        refine congrArg _ (funext fun out => ?_)

+          (F.cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher encodeMsg H isElem adversary bit) n) +

+private theorem length_encNat_mono {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) :
+    (encNat m).length ≤ (encNat n).length := by
+  simpa only [encNat_apply, ← Nat.size_eq_bits_len] using Nat.size_le_size h
+
+/-- Every encoded group element `F.encode d x` has bit-length polynomially bounded in
+`(F.encDesc d).length`. -/
+theorem exists_length_encode_le :
+    ∃ c k : ℕ, ∀ d : F.Desc, ∀ x : F.Carrier d,
+      (F.encode d x).length ≤ c * ((F.encDesc d).length + 1) ^ k := by
+  obtain ⟨co, ko, hord⟩ := F.computableInPolyTime_order.tidy.polyBounded_length.exists_le
+  obtain ⟨cg, kg, hgen⟩ := F.computableInPolyTime_generator.tidy.polyBounded_length.exists_le
+  obtain ⟨cs, ks, hsmul⟩ := F.computableInPolyTime_smul.tidy.polyBounded_length.exists_le
+  have hpoly : PolynomiallyBounded
+      (fun L => cs * (2 * L + 4 * (co * (L + 1) ^ ko) + 4 * (cg * (L + 1) ^ kg) + 7) ^ ks) := by
+    fun_prop
+  obtain ⟨c, k, hck⟩ := polynomiallyBounded_iff_le.mp hpoly
+  refine ⟨c, k, fun d x => ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨α, rfl⟩ := F.smul_generator_surjective d x
+  have hsmul_eq : F.encode d (α • F.generator d) =
+      F.smul (d, α.val, F.encode d (F.generator d)) := by
+    rw [F.smul_encode, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
+  rw [hsmul_eq]
+  have h1 := hsmul (d, α.val, F.encode d (F.generator d))
+  simp only [encBits_apply] at h1 hgen
+  have hα : (encNat α.val).length ≤ co * ((F.encDesc d).length + 1) ^ ko :=
+    (length_encNat_mono (Nat.le_of_lt (ZMod.val_lt α))).trans (hord d)
+  have hg := hgen d
+  have hlen :
+      (encPair F.encDesc (encPair encNat encBits)
+        (d, α.val, F.encode d (F.generator d))).length + 1 ≤
+      2 * (F.encDesc d).length + 4 * (co * ((F.encDesc d).length + 1) ^ ko) +
+        4 * (cg * ((F.encDesc d).length + 1) ^ kg) + 7 := by
+    simp only [length_encPair, encBits_apply]
+    lia
+  calc (F.smul (d, α.val, F.encode d (F.generator d))).length
+      ≤ cs * ((encPair F.encDesc (encPair encNat encBits)
+          (d, α.val, F.encode d (F.generator d))).length + 1) ^ ks := h1
+    _ ≤ cs * (2 * (F.encDesc d).length + 4 * (co * ((F.encDesc d).length + 1) ^ ko) +
+          4 * (cg * ((F.encDesc d).length + 1) ^ kg) + 7) ^ ks := by
+        gcongr
+    _ ≤ c * ((F.encDesc d).length + 1) ^ k := hck (F.encDesc d).length
+
+private theorem length_encBits4_encode_le {d : F.Desc} {B : ℕ}
+    (hB : ∀ x : F.Carrier d, (F.encode d x).length ≤ B)
+    (x₁ x₂ x₃ x₄ : F.Carrier d) :
+    (encBits4 (F.encode d x₁, F.encode d x₂, F.encode d x₃, F.encode d x₄)).length ≤
+      22 * B + 14 := by
+  have h1 := hB x₁; have h2 := hB x₂; have h3 := hB x₃; have h4 := hB x₄
+  simp only [encBits4, length_encPair, encBits_apply]
+  lia

+private theorem length_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_le {d : F.Desc} {B : ℕ}
+    (hB : ∀ x : F.Carrier d, (F.encode d x).length ≤ B)
+    (α : ZMod (F.order d)) (sk : (ℕ × ℕ) × ((ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ))) :
+    (F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d (F.encode d (α • F.generator d)) sk).length ≤

+  rw [F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_encode]

+    (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2).1
+    (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2).2.1
+    (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2).2.2.1
+    (F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α sk.1.1 sk.1.2 sk.2.1.1 sk.2.1.2 sk.2.2.1 sk.2.2.2).2.2.2

+private theorem negligible_const_div_two_pow (c : ℕ) :
+    Negligible (fun n => (c : ℝ≥0) / 2 ^ n) := by
+  have h : (fun n => (c : ℝ≥0) / 2 ^ n) =
+      fun n => (c : ℝ≥0) * (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0) ^ n := by
+    funext n
+    rw [div_eq_mul_inv, one_div, inv_pow]
+  rw [h]
+  exact (negligible_geometric (ratio := (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0)) (by norm_num)).polynomiallyBounded_mul
+    (by fun_prop)

+/-- **Asymptotic 1CCA security of Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup for a general message encoding**
+([BonehShoup2023], Theorem 12.9 & Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 488–493, 521–522): if DDH holds for
+`setup`, `cramerShoupHashMod H` is collision-resistant for `setup`, every supported group at
+parameter `n` has order at least `m n > 0` with `1 / m n` negligible, and supported group
+descriptions have polynomially bounded bit-length, then `cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game` is
+indistinguishable between `bit = false` and `bit = true` against all strict oracle PPT
+adversaries. -/
+theorem DDH.cramerShoupMsgINDCCA2
+    {F : PrimeOrderGroupFamily}
+    {Msg : Type} {encMsg : Msg ↪ List Bool}
+    {encodeMsg : F.Desc × Msg → List Bool}
+    (hencMsg : ComputableInPolyTime encodeMsg (encPair F.encDesc encMsg) encBits)
+    {setup : ℕ → PMF F.Desc}
+    {H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool}
+    {isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hH : ComputableInPolyTime H (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBits)
+    (hisElem : ComputableInPolyTime isElem (encPair F.encDesc encBits) encBool)
+    (hmem : ∀ d x, isElem (d, x) = true ↔ x ∈ Set.range (F.encode d))
+    (hDDH : F.DDH setup)
+    (hCR : CollisionResistantFor F.encDesc setup (F.cramerShoupHashMod H))
+    {m : ℕ → ℕ} (hm0 : ∀ n, 0 < m n)
+    (hm : ∀ n, ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support, m n ≤ F.order d)
+    (hinv : Negligible fun n => (1 / m n : ℝ≥0))
+    (hdesc : ∃ c k : ℕ, ∀ n, ∀ d ∈ (setup n).support,
+      (F.encDesc d).length ≤ c * (n + 1) ^ k) :
+    Game.Indistinguishable
+      (fun adversary n => F.cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game encodeMsg setup H isElem adversary false n)
+      (fun adversary n => F.cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game encodeMsg setup H isElem adversary true n)
+      (CCA2AdversaryOf.IsPPT encMsg) := by
+  intro adversary hA
+  obtain ⟨cd, kd, hdesc_le⟩ := hdesc
+  obtain ⟨ce, ke, henc_le⟩ := F.exists_length_encode_le
+  obtain ⟨c₁, d₁, c₂, d₂, cs, ds, hQ₁_raw, hQ₂_raw, hstate⟩ := hA.query_bounds
+  let Ld (n : ℕ) : ℕ := cd * (n + 1) ^ kd
+  let B (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ce * (Ld n + 1) ^ ke
+  let Lpk (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 * Ld n + 44 * B n + 30
+  let Lct (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 22 * B n + 14
+  let Lst (n : ℕ) : ℕ := cs * (n + Lpk n + 2) ^ ds
+  let Q₁ (n : ℕ) : ℕ := c₁ * (n + Lpk n + 2) ^ d₁
+  let Q₂ (n : ℕ) : ℕ := c₂ * (n + Lst n + Lct n + 2) ^ d₂
+  have hddh0 : Negligible fun n =>
+      Game.advantage
+        (F.ddhRealGame setup
+          (F.cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher encodeMsg H isElem adversary false) n)
+        (F.ddhIdealGame setup
+          (F.cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher encodeMsg H isElem adversary false) n) :=
+    hDDH _ (F.isPPTOn_cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher hencMsg hH hisElem hA false)
+  have hddh1 : Negligible fun n =>
+      Game.advantage
+        (F.ddhRealGame setup
+          (F.cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher encodeMsg H isElem adversary true) n)
+        (F.ddhIdealGame setup
+          (F.cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher encodeMsg H isElem adversary true) n) :=
+    hDDH _ (F.isPPTOn_cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher hencMsg hH hisElem hA true)
+  have hcr0 : Negligible fun n =>
+      Game.succProbability
+        (collisionGameFor setup (F.cramerShoupHashMod H) (fun _ _ _ => true)
+          (F.cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder encodeMsg H isElem adversary false) n) :=
+    hCR.negligible _ (F.isPPTOn_cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder hencMsg hH hisElem hA false)
+  have hcr1 : Negligible fun n =>
+      Game.succProbability
+        (collisionGameFor setup (F.cramerShoupHashMod H) (fun _ _ _ => true)
+          (F.cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder encodeMsg H isElem adversary true) n) :=
+    hCR.negligible _ (F.isPPTOn_cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder hencMsg hH hisElem hA true)
+  have hpoly_Q : PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => 2 * Q₁ n + 2 * Q₂ n + 2) := by
+    dsimp only [Q₁, Q₂, Lst, Lct, Lpk, B, Ld]
+    fun_prop
+  have hq_neg : Negligible fun n =>
+      ((2 * Q₁ n + 2 * Q₂ n + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ≥0) / (m n : ℝ≥0) := by
+    have heq : (fun n => ((2 * Q₁ n + 2 * Q₂ n + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ≥0) / (m n : ℝ≥0)) =
+        fun n => ((2 * Q₁ n + 2 * Q₂ n + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ≥0) * (1 / m n : ℝ≥0) := by
+      funext n
+      rw [div_eq_mul_inv, one_div]
+    rw [heq]
+    exact hinv.polynomiallyBounded_mul hpoly_Q
+  have h42_neg : Negligible fun n => (42 : ℝ≥0) / 2 ^ n :=
+    negligible_const_div_two_pow 42
+  refine negligible_of_le
+    (((((hddh0.add hddh1).add hcr0).add hcr1).add hq_neg).add h42_neg) (fun n => ?_)
+  refine F.advantage_cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game_le_of_honest_bounds encodeMsg setup H isElem hmem
+    adversary n (Q₁ n) (Q₂ n) (m n) (hm0 n) (hm n) ?_ ?_
+  · intro d hd α δ δ₁ δ₂
+    have hd_le : (F.encDesc d).length ≤ Ld n := hdesc_le n d hd
+    have hB_le : ∀ x : F.Carrier d, (F.encode d x).length ≤ B n :=
+      fun x => (henc_le d x).trans (by dsimp only [B]; gcongr)
+    have hpk :
+        (F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d (F.encode d (α • F.generator d))
+          (F.skNatOfZMod d δ 0 δ₁ 0 δ₂ 0)).length ≤ Lpk n :=
+      (F.length_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_le hB_le α _).trans (by dsimp only [Lpk]; gcongr)
+    exact (hQ₁_raw n _).mono (by dsimp only [Q₁]; gcongr)

+    rw [ProbOracleComp.eval_run_interpret] at hchoice
+    have hd_le : (F.encDesc d).length ≤ Ld n := hdesc_le n d hd
+    have hB_le : ∀ x : F.Carrier d, (F.encode d x).length ≤ B n :=
+      fun x => (henc_le d x).trans (by dsimp only [B]; gcongr)
+    have hpk :
+        (F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d (F.encode d (α • F.generator d))
+          (F.skNatOfZMod d δ 0 δ₁ 0 δ₂ 0)).length ≤ Lpk n :=
+      (F.length_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_le hB_le α _).trans (by dsimp only [Lpk]; gcongr)
+    have hst : choiceOut.1.2.length ≤ Lst n :=
+      (hstate n _ Unit _ () choiceOut.2 choiceOut.1 hchoice).trans (by dsimp only [Lst]; gcongr)
+    have hct :
+        (encBits4
+          (F.encode d (β • F.generator d),
+           F.encode d (γ • F.generator d),
+           F.encode d (projHash F d (δ - α * τ) τ (β • F.generator d) (γ • F.generator d) + mElem),
+           F.encode d ((β * (δ₁ + F.cramerShoupHashMod H d
+             (encBits3 (F.encode d (β • F.generator d), F.encode d (γ • F.generator d),
+               F.encode d (projHash F d (δ - α * τ) τ (β • F.generator d) (γ • F.generator d) +
+                 mElem))) * δ₂) + (γ - α * β) * ξ) • F.generator d))).length ≤ Lct n :=
+      F.length_encBits4_encode_le hB_le _ _ _ _
+    exact (hQ₂_raw n choiceOut.1.2 _).mono (by dsimp only [Q₂]; gcongr)

+private theorem advantage_four_le_eight (g₁ g₂ g₃ g₄ : Game) {n : ℕ}
+    (h₁ : Game.advantage g₁ g₂ ≤ 1 / 2 ^ n)
+    (h₂ : Game.advantage g₂ g₃ ≤ 6 / 2 ^ n)
+    (h₃ : Game.advantage g₃ g₄ ≤ 1 / 2 ^ n) :
+    Game.advantage g₁ g₄ ≤ 8 / 2 ^ n := by
+  have htri1 := Game.advantage_triangle g₁ g₂ g₄
+  have htri2 := Game.advantage_triangle g₂ g₃ g₄
+  calc Game.advantage g₁ g₄
+      ≤ Game.advantage g₁ g₂ + (Game.advantage g₂ g₃ + Game.advantage g₃ g₄) :=
+        htri1.trans (add_le_add le_rfl htri2)
+    _ ≤ 1 / 2 ^ n + (6 / 2 ^ n + 1 / 2 ^ n) :=
+        add_le_add h₁ (add_le_add h₂ h₃)
+    _ = 8 / 2 ^ n := by ring

+private noncomputable def cramerShoupCCA2InnerB

+    (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ : ZMod (F.order d))
+    (choiceOut : ((List Bool × List Bool) × List Bool) × Unit)
+    (β : ZMod (F.order d)) : Game :=
+  let sk := F.skNatOfZMod d σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂
+  let pkVal := F.cramerShoupPublicKey d α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂
+  let m := if bit then choiceOut.1.1.2 else choiceOut.1.1.1
+  let ct := F.encodeCramerShoupEncrypt H d
+    (F.encode d pkVal.1, F.encode d pkVal.2.1,
+      F.encode d pkVal.2.2.1, F.encode d pkVal.2.2.2) m β.val
+  (ProbComp.eval ((OracleComp.interpret
+    (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun m => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin m))
+      (F.cramerShoupPhase2Oracle H isElem d sk ct))
+    (adversary.guess n choiceOut.1.2 ct)).run ())).bind (fun guessOut => PMF.pure guessOut.1)
+
+private noncomputable def cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool)
+    (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (d : F.Desc) (adversary : WordCCA2Adversary) (bit : Bool) (n : ℕ)
+    (α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ : ZMod (F.order d)) (useExactB : Bool) : Game :=
+  let sk := F.skNatOfZMod d σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂
+  let pk := F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey d (F.encode d (α • F.generator d)) sk
+  (ProbComp.eval ((OracleComp.interpret
+    (ProbOracleComp.handler (fun m => StateT.lift (ProbComp.unifFin m))
+      (F.cramerShoupPhase1Oracle H isElem d sk))
+    (adversary.choose n pk)).run ())).bind fun choiceOut =>
+    if isElem (d, choiceOut.1.1.1) && isElem (d, choiceOut.1.1.2) then
+      if useExactB then
+        (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))).bind fun β =>
+          F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerB H isElem d adversary bit n α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ choiceOut β
+      else
+        (ProbComp.eval (F.sampleCramerShoupExp n d)).bind fun b =>
+          F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerB H isElem d adversary bit n α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ choiceOut
+            (b : ZMod (F.order d))
+    else
+      PMF.pure false
+
+/-- The `Encryption.cca2GameOn` experiment for `(cramerShoupValid, cramerShoupKeyGenProb,
+cramerShoupEncryptProb, cramerShoupDecryptOpt)` is within statistical distance `8 / 2 ^ n` of
+`cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game (fun n => PMF.pure (d n))` (accounting for the eight `sampleModNat`
+exponent draws in `cramerShoupKeyGenProb` and `cramerShoupEncryptProb`). -/
+theorem advantage_cca2GameOn_cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game_le
+    (H : F.Desc × List Bool → List Bool)
+    (isElem : F.Desc × List Bool → Bool)
+    (hmem : ∀ d x, isElem (d, x) = true ↔ x ∈ Set.range (F.encode d))
+    (d : ℕ → F.Desc) (adversary : WordCCA2Adversary) (bit : Bool) (n : ℕ) :
+    Game.advantage
+      (ProbComp.eval
+        (cca2GameOn (F.cramerShoupValid isElem d) encBits (F.cramerShoupKeyGenProb d)
+          (F.cramerShoupEncryptProb H d) (F.cramerShoupDecryptOpt H isElem d) adversary bit n))
+      (F.cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game (fun n => PMF.pure (d n)) H isElem adversary bit n) ≤
+      8 / 2 ^ n := by
+  have hgame0 :
+      ProbComp.eval
+        (cca2GameOn (F.cramerShoupValid isElem d) encBits (F.cramerShoupKeyGenProb d)
+          (F.cramerShoupEncryptProb H d) (F.cramerShoupDecryptOpt H isElem d) adversary bit n) =
+      (ProbComp.eval (F.sampleCramerShoupExp n (d n))).bind fun a =>
+        (ProbComp.eval (F.sampleCramerShoupSK n (d n))).bind fun sk =>
+          F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK H isElem (d n) adversary bit n
+            (a : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+            (sk.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+            (sk.2.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+            (sk.2.2.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.2.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) false := by
+    simp only [cca2GameOn, cramerShoupKeyGenProb, cramerShoupEncryptProb, cramerShoupValid,
+      ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.bind_bind, PMF.pure_bind, F.smul_encode,
+      F.cca2Phase1Oracle_cramerShoupDecryptOpt]
+    refine congrArg _ (funext fun a => congrArg _ (funext fun sk => ?_))
+    dsimp only [cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK]
+    rw [F.encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_eq_skNatOfZMod (d n) (a : ZMod (F.order (d n))) sk,
+      F.cramerShoupPhase1Oracle_eq_skNatOfZMod H isElem hmem (d n) sk]
+    refine congrArg _ (funext fun choiceOut => ?_)
+    by_cases h : (isElem (d n, choiceOut.1.1.1) && isElem (d n, choiceOut.1.1.2)) = true
+    · simp only [h, ↓reduceIte, Bool.false_eq_true, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure,
+        PMF.bind_bind, PMF.pure_bind, F.cca2Phase2Oracle_cramerShoupDecryptOpt,
+        F.decodeBits4_dropFrame_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey, cramerShoupCCA2InnerB]
+      refine congrArg _ (funext fun b => ?_)
+      have hct :=
+        F.encodeCramerShoupEncrypt_skNatOfZMod H (d n) (a : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (sk.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (sk.2.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (sk.2.2.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.2.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (if bit then choiceOut.1.1.2 else choiceOut.1.1.1) b
+      rw [hct, F.cramerShoupPhase2Oracle_eq_skNatOfZMod H isElem hmem (d n) sk]
+    · simp only [h, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, ProbComp.eval_pure]
+  have hgame1 :
+      F.cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game (fun n => PMF.pure (d n)) H isElem adversary bit n =
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun α =>
+        (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun σ =>
+          (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun τ =>
+            (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun σ₁ =>
+              (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun τ₁ =>
+                (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun σ₂ =>
+                  (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun τ₂ =>
+                    F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK H isElem (d n) adversary bit n
+                      α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ true := by
+    simp only [cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game, cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game, PMF.monad_bind_eq_bind,
+      PMF.monad_pure_eq_pure, PMF.pure_bind]
+    refine congrArg _ (funext fun α => congrArg _ (funext fun σ =>
+      congrArg _ (funext fun τ => congrArg _ (funext fun σ₁ =>
+        congrArg _ (funext fun τ₁ => congrArg _ (funext fun σ₂ =>
+          congrArg _ (funext fun τ₂ => ?_)))))))
+    simp only [cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK, cramerShoupCCA2InnerB, ↓reduceIte,
+      encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_encode, skNatOfZMod, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
+  rw [hgame0, hgame1]
+  refine advantage_four_le_eight _
+    ((PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun α =>
+      (ProbComp.eval (F.sampleCramerShoupSK n (d n))).bind fun sk =>
+        F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK H isElem (d n) adversary bit n α
+          (sk.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (sk.2.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (sk.2.2.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.2.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) false)
+    ((PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun α =>
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun σ =>
+        (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun τ =>
+          (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun σ₁ =>
+            (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun τ₁ =>
+              (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun σ₂ =>
+                (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order (d n)))).bind fun τ₂ =>
+                  F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK H isElem (d n) adversary bit n
+                    α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ false) _
+    (F.advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupExp_le n (d n) (fun α =>
+      (ProbComp.eval (F.sampleCramerShoupSK n (d n))).bind fun sk =>
+        F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK H isElem (d n) adversary bit n α
+          (sk.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (sk.2.1.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.1.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n)))
+          (sk.2.2.1 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) (sk.2.2.2 : ZMod (F.order (d n))) false))
+    (advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun α =>
+      F.advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupSK_le n (d n) _ (fun σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ =>
+        F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK H isElem (d n) adversary bit n
+          α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ false) (fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => rfl)) ?_
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun α => ?_
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun σ => ?_
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun τ => ?_
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun σ₁ => ?_
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun τ₁ => ?_
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun σ₂ => ?_
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun τ₂ => ?_
+  dsimp only [cramerShoupCCA2InnerSK]
+  refine advantage_bind_le_nnreal _ _ _ fun choiceOut => ?_
+  by_cases h : (isElem (d n, choiceOut.1.1.1) && isElem (d n, choiceOut.1.1.2)) = true
+  · simp only [h, ↓reduceIte, Bool.false_eq_true]
+    exact F.advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupExp_le n (d n)
+      (F.cramerShoupCCA2InnerB H isElem (d n) adversary bit n α σ τ σ₁ τ₁ σ₂ τ₂ choiceOut)
+  · simp only [h, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, Game.advantage_self, zero_le]
+
+/-- **Theorem 12.9 & Exercise 12.27 via `Encryption.INDCCA2On`**: for any polynomial-time group
+description family `d : ℕ → F.Desc`, the probabilistic polynomial-time Cramer–Shoup encryption
+scheme `(cramerShoupKeyGenProb d, cramerShoupEncryptProb H d, cramerShoupDecryptOpt H isElem d)`
+satisfies `Encryption.INDCCA2On` with respect to the group-membership admissibility predicate
+`cramerShoupValid isElem d` under DDH and collision resistance of `cramerShoupHashMod H`. -/

title: feat(Crypto/Computational/CramerShoup): prove Cramer-Shoup 1CCA and INDCCA2On security under DDH
body:
## Summary

Completes **#1000 Step 3** (Cramer–Shoup CCA2-secure public-key encryption from DDH in the standard model), proving concrete and asymptotic single-challenge 1CCA security (both for the **ideal exact-uniform PMF** games and for the **native strict-PPT** `Encryption.INDCCA2On` notion) for the **Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup public-key encryption scheme** ($\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$, [Boneh and Shoup, Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 521–522](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf), specialized to associated data $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$) over a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, under:
1. the Decisional Diffie–Hellman (`PrimeOrderGroupFamily.DDH`) assumption,
2. collision resistance (`CollisionResistantFor`) of the $\mathbb{Z}_q$-valued hash family `cramerShoupHashMod`, and
3. a positive group-order lower bound $m(n) > 0$ with $m(n) \le q$ and negligible inverse order $1 / m(n)$,

following the Games 0–6 proof template of [Boneh and Shoup, Section 12.5.3, Theorem 12.9 and Remark 12.3, printed pp. 488–493](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf). Stacked on merged #1096, #1193, #1169, #1207 (`UntilBad` witness-finding oracle supplier PR), #1208 (`CramerShoup/Reductions.lean`), and #1214 (`DiffieHellman/EncodingBounds.lean` supplier PR):

1. **Ideal exact-uniform PMF Games 0–2 and 1CCA security definitions (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CramerShoup.lean`)**:
   - `cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupGroupINDCCA2`, `cramerShoupCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupINDCCA2`, `cramerShoupGame1`, and `cramerShoupGame2` (in which key and challenge exponents are sampled from `PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))`).
2. **Game-hop reductions (Game 0 $\to$ Game 3)**:
   - `cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game_eq_game1`: Game 0 = Game 1 (eq. (12.21), printed p. 490).
   - `advantage_cramerShoupGame1_game2_le`: Game 1 $\to$ Game 2 bound reducing to the DDH advantage of `cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher` plus `12 / 2 ^ n` (eq. (12.22), printed p. 492).
   - `advantage_cramerShoupGame2_game3_le`: Game 2 $\to$ Game 3 bound reducing via `runStatelessOracle_le_runFinderOracle` to the `collisionGameFor` success probability of `cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder` plus `9 / 2 ^ n` (eqs. (12.24)–(12.25), printed p. 492).
3. **Concrete and asymptotic ideal-game 1CCA security theorems**:
   - Concrete ideal-game bounds: `advantage_cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game_game5_le`, `advantage_cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game_le_of_honest_bounds`, `advantage_cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game_le`, `advantage_cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game_le`, and `advantage_cramerShoupCCA2Game_le` (where `42 / 2 ^ n` is the reduction loss from the `ProbComp.sampleModNat` exponent draws inside the reductions).
   - Asymptotic ideal-game 1CCA security under `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.DDH`, `CollisionResistantFor` of `cramerShoupHashMod`, a positive group-order lower bound `m n > 0` with `Negligible (fun n => (1 / m n : ℝ≥0))`, and polynomially bounded group description bit-length (using `exists_length_encode_le` from #1214): `DDH.cramerShoupMsgINDCCA2`, `DDH.cramerShoupGroupINDCCA2`, and `DDH.cramerShoupINDCCA2`.
4. **Native strict-PPT `Encryption.cca2GameOn` and `Encryption.INDCCA2On` instantiation**:
   - `advantage_cca2GameOn_cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game_le`: bounds the statistical distance between the native `ProbComp.eval (cca2GameOn (F.cramerShoupValid isElem d) encBits (F.cramerShoupKeyGenProb d) (F.cramerShoupEncryptProb H d) (F.cramerShoupDecryptOpt H isElem d) adversary bit n)` experiment and the ideal exact-uniform PMF game `F.cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game (fun n => PMF.pure (d n)) H isElem adversary bit n` by `8 / 2 ^ n` per challenge bit (`16 / 2 ^ n` across both challenge bits, accounting for the eight `ProbComp.sampleModNat` exponent draws in `cramerShoupKeyGenProb` and `cramerShoupEncryptProb`).
   - `DDH.indcca2On_cramerShoup`: proves the native `INDCCA2On (F.cramerShoupValid isElem d) encBits encBits (F.cramerShoupKeyGenProb d) (F.cramerShoupEncryptProb H d) (F.cramerShoupDecryptOpt H isElem d)` notion under `F.DDH (fun n => PMF.pure (d n))`, `CollisionResistantFor F.encDesc (fun n => PMF.pure (d n)) (F.cramerShoupHashMod H)`, and a positive group-order lower bound `m n > 0` (`m n ≤ F.order (d n)`) with `Negligible (fun n => (1 / m n : ℝ≥0))`.

## Source Statements ([Boneh and Shoup, v0.6](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf), Section 12.5.3 & Exercise 12.27)

Verbatim from Boneh and Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography* (Version 0.6, Section 12.5.3, printed pp. 489–492):

> **Theorem 12.9.** If the DDH assumption holds in $\mathbb{G}$, $\mathcal{E}_s$ is 1CCA secure, $H$ is a secure KDF, and $H'$ is collision resistant, then $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$ is CCA secure.
>
> In particular, for every 1CCA adversary $\mathcal{A}$ that attacks $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$ as in Definition 12.2, and makes at most $Q_d$ decryption queries, there exist a DDH adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{ddh}}$ for $\mathbb{G}$ as in Attack Game 10.6, a 1CCA adversary $\mathcal{B}_s$ that attacks $\mathcal{E}_s$ as in Definition 9.6, a KDF adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{kdf}}$ that attacks $H$ as in Attack Game 11.3, and a collision-finding adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}$ that attacks $H'$ as in Attack Game 8.1, where $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{ddh}}, \mathcal{B}_s, \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{kdf}}, \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}$ are elementary wrappers around $\mathcal{A}$, such that
> $$\text{1CCAadv}[\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}] \le 2\left(\text{DDHadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{ddh}}, \mathbb{G}] + \text{KDFadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{kdf}}, H] + \text{CRadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}, H'] + \frac{Q_d + 1}{q}\right) + \text{1CCAadv}[\mathcal{B}_s, \mathcal{E}_s]. \quad (12.19)$$
> …
> **Game 1.** We replace the lines marked (2) and (3) in Fig. 12.3 as follows:
> $$(2) \qquad z \leftarrow f(v, w)$$
> $$(3) \qquad z' \leftarrow f'(v, w, \rho)$$
> Here, instead of using the auxiliary information that allows us to compute $f$ on $L_u$ and $f'$ on $L_u \times \mathbb{Z}_q$, we compute them directly, using the secret key $\mathit{sk}$. This does not change the result of the computation in any way. Therefore,
> $$\Pr[W_1] = \Pr[W_0]. \quad (12.21)$$
> …
> **Game 2.** We replace the line marked (1) in Fig. 12.3 with
> $$(1) \qquad \gamma \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q$$
> …
> It is easy to see that
> $$|\Pr[W_1] - \Pr[W_2]| \le \text{DDHadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{ddh}}, \mathbb{G}] \quad (12.22)$$
> for an efficient DDH adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{ddh}}$ …
>
> **Game 3.** We replace the line marked (1) in Fig. 12.3 with
> $$(1) \qquad \gamma \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q \setminus \{\alpha\beta\}$$
> Since the statistical distance between the uniform distribution on all triples and the uniform distribution on all non-DH-triples is $1/q$ (see Exercise 10.7), it follows that:
> $$|\Pr[W_2] - \Pr[W_3]| \le \frac{1}{q}. \quad (12.23)$$
>
> **Game 4.** We now play our “CR card”. Let us define $\mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{v}, \hat{w})$ to be true if $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \ne (v, w)$ and $H'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) = H'(v, w)$, and to be false, otherwise. In this game, we “widen” the rejection rule at line (5), replacing it with
> $$(5) \qquad \text{if } \mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v}) \text{ or } z' \ne f'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{\rho})$$
> Let $Z_4$ be the event that in Game 4, some decryption query, which would not have triggered the rejection rule of Game 3, does trigger the wider rejection rule in Game 4. Clearly, Games 3 and 4 proceed identically unless event $Z_4$ occurs. By the Difference Lemma, we have
> $$|\Pr[W_3] - \Pr[W_4]| \le \Pr[Z_4]. \quad (12.24)$$
> It should be clear that
> $$\Pr[Z_4] \le \text{CRadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}, H']. \quad (12.25)$$
> for an efficient collision-finding adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}$. Indeed, adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}$ just plays Game 4 and waits for the event $Z_4$ to happen.

Verbatim from Boneh and Shoup (Version 0.6, Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 521–522):
> … Show that $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$ is CCA secure, provided $H'$ is collision resistant and the DDH assumption holds for $\mathbb{G}$.

**Scope and Quantitative Adaptation Note**:
- The scheme is specialized to associated data $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$ and proved secure in the single-challenge 1CCA game (`Definition 12.2`, printed p. 468).
- **Adaptation of Game 4 from $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$ to $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$**: in Theorem 12.9 ($\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{CS}}$), $H'$ hashes the pair $(v, w)$ and $\mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{v}, \hat{w})$ tests $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) \ne (v, w) \land H'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}) = H'(v, w)$. In Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$ (Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 521–522, with $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$), $H'$ hashes the triple $(v, w, e) \in \mathbb{G}^3$ (`encBits3`), so the Game 4 collision predicate is originally adapted to $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{e}) \ne (v, w, e) \land H'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{e}) = H'(v, w, e)$ (while Phase 2 decryption already rejects the full challenge ciphertext $(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{e}, \hat{z}') = (v, w, e, z')$).
- **Ideal exact-uniform PMF games vs. native `Encryption.INDCCA2On`**: `cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupGroupINDCCA2`, `cramerShoupCCA2Game`, and `cramerShoupINDCCA2` are **ideal exact-uniform PMF** 1CCA experiments and security definitions. In `advantage_cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game_le` (an **original quantitative adaptation** of `(12.19)` to $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$ in the library's uniform strict-PPT model), the two fixed-bit DDH distinguishers (`cramerShoupToDDHDistinguisher`) and two fixed-bit collision finders (`cramerShoupToCollisionFinder`) contribute `42 / 2 ^ n` from their internal `ProbComp.sampleModNat` exponent draws, and `(2 * Q₁ n + 2 * Q₂ n + 2) / m` combines the non-DH triple exclusion (`1 / m`) and the adaptive Lemma 12.8 bound (`(Q₁ n + Q₂ n) / m`) across `bit = false` and `bit = true`. The **native strict-PPT** security theorem `DDH.indcca2On_cramerShoup` instantiates `Encryption.INDCCA2On` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/CCA.lean`), bridging from `cramerShoupKeyGenProb` and `cramerShoupEncryptProb` to the ideal game via `advantage_cca2GameOn_cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game_le` with an additional `8 / 2 ^ n` statistical loss per challenge bit (`16 / 2 ^ n` across both bits).
- **Group-order growth premise**: the asymptotic theorems (`DDH.cramerShoupMsgINDCCA2`, `DDH.cramerShoupGroupINDCCA2`, `DDH.cramerShoupINDCCA2`, and `DDH.indcca2On_cramerShoup`) assume a positive lower bound `m : ℕ → ℕ` on `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.order` with `Negligible (fun n => (1 / m n : ℝ≥0))`.

## Existing Notions Considered

| New or Reused Declaration | Existing Notion Checked | Why Reused or Added |
|---|---|---|
| `cramerShoupMsgCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupGroupINDCCA2`, `cramerShoupCCA2Game`, `cramerShoupINDCCA2`, `cramerShoupGame1`, `cramerShoupGame2` | `cramerShoupGame3`, `cramerShoupGame4`, `cramerShoupGame5` (#1169), `Game.Indistinguishable` (`Complexity/Crypto/Game.lean`), `Encryption.cca2GameOn`, `Encryption.INDCCA2On` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/CCA.lean`, #1096) | Defines the **ideal exact-uniform PMF** Games 0–2 of Boneh–Shoup Section 12.5.3 with `PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))` exponents (matching `cramerShoupGame3`–`cramerShoupGame5` from #1169 and `ddhRealGame` / `ddhIdealGame`), as an intermediate step before bridging to the **native strict-PPT** `Encryption.cca2GameOn` / `Encryption.INDCCA2On` notions in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/CCA.lean`. |
| `advantage_cca2GameOn_cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game_le`, `DDH.indcca2On_cramerShoup` | `Encryption.cca2GameOn`, `Encryption.INDCCA2On` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/CCA.lean`, #1096) | Instantiates the library's native strict-PPT PKE 1CCA game `Encryption.cca2GameOn` and security notion `Encryption.INDCCA2On` with group-membership admissibility `cramerShoupValid`, bridging from `cramerShoupKeyGenProb` / `cramerShoupEncryptProb` to `cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game` with an `8 / 2 ^ n` per-bit `ProbComp.sampleModNat` approximation bound. |
| `exists_length_encode_le` | `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/DiffieHellman/EncodingBounds.lean` (#1214) | **Reused directly** from shared supplier PR #1214 to bound the bit-length of encoded group elements in `DDH.cramerShoupMsgINDCCA2`. |

## Framework friction and abstract-impact assessment

- **Framework friction**:
  1. Because `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.DDH` samples group exponents with exact `PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))` inside `ddhRealGame` / `ddhIdealGame` while `IsPPTOn` reductions (`cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher`, `cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder`) and `ProbComp` scheme operations (`cramerShoupKeyGenProb`, `cramerShoupEncryptProb`) sample exponents inside `ProbComp` over dyadic coin tosses via `ProbComp.sampleModNat`, each reduction and `cca2GameOn` bridge carries an explicit `c / 2 ^ n` statistical-distance tail (`12 / 2 ^ n` in Game 1 $\to$ Game 2, `9 / 2 ^ n` in Game 2 $\to$ Game 3, and `8 / 2 ^ n` per bit between `cca2GameOn` and `cramerShoupGroupCCA2Game`).
  2. Bridging per-input polynomial query bounds (`IsOraclePPT.query_bounds`) to the experiment-level query bounds (`HonestPhase1QueryBound`, `HonestPhase2QueryBound`) in `DDH.cramerShoupMsgINDCCA2` uses the shared group-element encoding bound `exists_length_encode_le` (#1214) derived from `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.order`, `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.generator`, and `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.smul`.
- **Abstract-impact assessment**: None. All declarations are additive in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CramerShoup.lean`, with no breaking changes to existing public APIs.

---

title: feat(threshold): strengthen support-three lower bound to 2/3
body:
This follow-up to #1185 strengthens the support-three coefficient from **4/7 to 2/3**. For weighted threshold programs whose gates each read at most three original input coordinates, it proves $q>(2/3-\varepsilon)n$ eventually when both Boolean fibers are rectangle-free with a sublinear logarithmic threshold. Here $q$ counts input-reading gates; internal predecessor fan-in, depth, fan-out, real weights, and the Boolean readout of gate values remain unrestricted. Supports use the existing aggregated coefficients.

This is a stacked PR against `feat/threshold-direct-support-b5179`, dependent on #1185. Refs #1203.

### Mathematical change

For both fibers $K$-rectangle-free across every coordinate partition, $K\le2^k$, and every natural cutoff $T$, the new finite theorem is

$$
2n < \left(3+\frac{6}{T+1}\right)q
+\max(3,T)\operatorname{Nat.log}_2(n+q)+6k+1.
$$

The original derivation fixes high-incidence inputs, bounds the width of the residual incidence graph using the existing cycle-rank layout theorem, and finds a prefix cut with an exact deficit. A hereditary obstruction on arbitrary disjoint input sets combines the connected components without multiplying the error by their number. The result is exposed for native programs and single-output circuits, and the existing support-three asymptotic theorem is strengthened in place. The general-support random-cut theorem is unchanged.

At the first PR's witnessed parameters $n=2{,}000{,}000$, $K=32{,}000{,}016$, $k=25$, the new theorem with $T=255$ forces **1,321,177** input-reading gates, versus **1,052,028** from that PR's finite random-cut bound. A concrete circuit regression also checks cutoff zero with an empty residual input type and an input-free internal gate.

### Comparison and scope

The classical rank-three transversal bound [Theorem 1, p. 2, in Thomassé–Yeo](https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/stephan.thomasse/liste/strondom.pdf), combined with the existing support-two transfer, implies $q>(3n-8k)/5$. This **3/5 comparison is our inference from those results**; the 2/3 coefficient improves it. The near-$n$ result for [oblivious local decision trees](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/195/download) assumes the same query function at each depth. Earlier gate outputs can change the effective threshold in the present model, so that result does not directly cover these programs.

Literature-wide priority is not established. The hypotheses have a nonconstructive witness, but this PR does not supply an explicit polynomial-time hard family. The broader objective remains open in #1203 and ROADMAP.

The new incidence graph reuses `Frontier.Multigraph`; the existing threshold `supportGraph` is a clique expansion and does not retain the required membership-edge accounting. The input-prefix definition bridges layouts to the existing finite-set cut language. The unchanged subset-sum lemma is moved to `Finset.exists_subset_sum_ge`, removing the generic graph proof's dependency on threshold-circuit semantics; both clients are updated.

### Validation and review

Published revision: `567548a35dabcce7d21f5075d6426b9f2d1f2b22`. The published commit, local validation commit, and CI merge commit have the same source tree.

- [Full Lean CI passed](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40368053655): library build, complete tests, lint, documentation checks, import aggregate, style, and initialization imports. The tests include both regressions and the global axiom audit, which allows only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
- All seven changed library modules also pass local checks with the pinned Lean toolchain, the repository's strict linter settings, and zero warnings. Source hygiene and compiled-declaration documentation checks pass locally as well.
- The required local six-gate `scripts/check.sh` was attempted but stopped before compilation at dependency materialization; downloads were disabled on the full shared disk. Targeted checking used source-verified, read-only artifacts with identical toolchain and dependency pins. Duplicate local checks were stopped under memory pressure; CI provides the completed regression and axiom checks.

Ready for coordinator review.

Formal-abstract assessment: the selected headline statements, catalogue, and rendering are unaffected; no abstract changes are needed. Internal read-only reviews found no mathematical or model mismatch. Independent coordinator review outside the authoring fleet is still required.

AI-authored with ChatGPT, session `chatgpt-b5179-lower-bound-round2`.

title: feat(Crypto/Computational/DiffieHellman): add polynomial bit-length bound for encoded group elements
body:
## Summary

Shared `#733` supplier PR requested during the review of [#1209](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1209) ([review comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1209#pullrequestreview-5656993716)). Extracts the general polynomial bit-length bound for encoded elements of a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily` into `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/DiffieHellman/EncodingBounds.lean`.

### Main Declarations (`Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily`)

- `exists_length_encode_le`: from the polynomial-time certificates `computableInPolyTime_order`, `computableInPolyTime_generator`, and `computableInPolyTime_smul` on a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, together with generator surjectivity `smul_generator_surjective`, every encoded group element `encode` has bit-length bounded by a fixed polynomial in the group description length `encDesc`.

### Existing Notions Considered

| Existing Declaration / Module | Role | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `PrimeOrderGroupFamily` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/DiscreteLog.lean`) | Prime-order cyclic group family with certified polynomial-time operations (`computableInPolyTime_order`, `computableInPolyTime_generator`, `computableInPolyTime_smul`) and `smul_generator_surjective` | **Reused directly**; `exists_length_encode_le` derives a uniform polynomial bit-length bound on `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.encode` from these fields |
| `PolynomiallyBounded`, `polynomiallyBounded_iff_le` (`Complexity/Asymptotics/PolyBounded.lean`) | Polynomial growth predicates | **Reused directly** |
| `schnorrGroups` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/DiscreteLog/SchnorrGroup.lean`) | Concrete prime-order subgroup family | **Reused directly** in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/DiffieHellman.lean` |

### Framework Friction and Abstract Impact Assessment

- **Framework friction:** None; `ComputableInPolyTime.tidy`, `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.polyBounded_length`, `PolyBounded.exists_le`, and `fun_prop` compose cleanly with `smul_generator_surjective`.
- **Abstract impact assessment:** None. No declaration in `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/` is modified or weakened.

### Validation

[Hosted Lean CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40378284354). The [author's focused-check record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1214#issuecomment-6424169282) includes the concrete Schnorr-family instantiation.

Part of [#1000](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1000) (Step 3, shared `#733` supplier for [#1209](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1209)).

body:
The original Liu–Pass threshold arithmetic still exhausted its 200,000-heartbeat budget because generic composition explored an unconstrained intermediate encoding. Add `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_add'`, `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_sub'` and `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_mul'`: computed-operand rules that require both operands in unary under the complete common input encoding. Each proof uses only the existing plain operation certificate, composition and pairing. Existing definitions, proofs, resource contracts, composition registrations and search backend are unchanged.

They also cover the full supplied-leaf positive and three operator positives/six missing-left/right controls. The direct operator controls explicitly use `fun_prop (maxSteps := 256)` on both sides; they are configured-search controls, not default rejection parity. **The full missing-leaf negative still times out under both default and 256-step search and remains OPEN in #1155.** [Preserved failed/prototype sources and logs](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/tree/7c2a9fdb5d5de8c745476c8e0f3b0649e788b45f/evidence/1155-regression-559). author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Coordinator `coordinator-integration-review-20261020`: independent review of head `654402c6ea6a8efa89fa3eb29afcbf31da622045`, with the three new modules and `ComplexityTests/Iteration.lean` verified byte-for-byte identical to source `077363a05aef29152639cedb3b4fc995981fe2fc`. Scope: full UniversalMap and SequentialSquaring correctness; whole-batch API/reuse, source credit, proof hygiene and client coverage. Root separately owns full InPlace correctness/model and final index/artifact review. **Changes requested** for the concrete items below; no mathematical defect found in the two fully reviewed modules.

1. **[must-fix] `UniversalMap.lean:24–29,285–306,459–470` and the universal-map index bullet:** preserve the model boundary requested in [the issue's design review](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/issues/117#issuecomment-6303410643). The global configuration type has natural-number operand indices and program counter; it is not a finite Boolean state space or the native certified universal TM. A gate interpretation and the simultaneous copy/reset each count as one semantic step. The circuit theorem assumes the encoding/start-state and powered-circuit equations; it constructs neither a global finite encoding nor a circuit for one universal step. State these limits explicitly in the module/index. The generic carrier also needs a chosen default (`[Inhabited V]`, line 285); the index currently says “any … carrier V” without that premise.
2. **[must-fix] `ComplexityTests/Iteration.lean:139–177`: add the promised nonvacuity/boundary evidence.** The new clients are one unpadded `flip` round, an all-halting idle machine's cardinality/stability, and the generic squarefree-15 theorem. They do not instantiate the conditional universal circuit-transfer hypotheses, exercise zero gates/padding, or cover the explicitly requested `M = 1`, `T = 0`, concrete non-unit residue and non-squarefree boundary. Add a small concrete transfer client and those boundary cases. The prior design review also requested actual InPlace encoding/step/initial circuits and clamped/colliding-write clients; the current idle examples do not supply them. Root is checking that part independently. Named axiom guards are present and pass, but are not those client witnesses.
3. **[must-fix] PR description:** reconcile it with the actual reviewed source rather than the earlier proposed API. `GateDesc`, a `pairAction` definition, `InPlace.IsHalting`, `InPlace.HaltsWithin`, `InPlace.RoundsCompute`, `squareMap`, `powerMap`, `reducedExponent_pos` and `pow_reducedExponent` are absent. The actual interfaces include `Universal.Description`, `pairAction_iterate`, `Machine.HaltingAbsorbing`, explicit time/round premises and the conjunctive `reducedExponent_le`. The primary file is `lean/Proofs/InPlace.lean`, not `InPlaceMachine.lean`; the source bibliography key is `Schlesinger2026IteratedFunctions`, not `Schlesinger2026Iterating`. Describe the actual tests and limits accurately, and align the inconsistent 34/33 declaration-link counts. There is no code dependency on #122: this branch is based on main `a9b72ca0`, and the InPlace result transfers an assumed hardness bound; it does not yet instantiate the modulus counter from #107.
4. **[should-fix] `UniversalMap.lean:213–215` and `SequentialSquaring.lean:120–124`: reuse the upstream public lemmas.** `smul_iterate_eq` duplicates Mathlib `smul_iterate`, and `iterate_square` specializes Mathlib `pow_iterate`. In the isolated exact-head checkout, MCP checks the direct `smul_iterate` substitution at the first consumer with no remaining goals, and `rw [pow_iterate]` at the second consumer gives the required power equality without diagnostics. Use those existing lemmas directly instead of adding redundant public circuit-namespace APIs. These declarations are new in this unmerged branch, so no deprecated alias is needed.

Checked and sound: the two-constant hardwiring charge and free projections, both product-factor orientations, integer/natural/inverse group actions, earlier-gate invariant with harmless padding and final reset, the squarefree prime-factor argument for every residue, positivity of both exponents, reduction at zero squarings, and the arithmetic-only table. The code makes no VDF security proof. All three source headers preserve Samuel Schlesinger's authorship from primary revision `c4cfa198a241b3d2cc3bfa5f744a68a66f49be8b`; the source references are accurate. Fresh private-cache Lean MCP diagnostics are clean for UniversalMap, SequentialSquaring and the complete Iteration test module; `git diff --check` is clean. I did not rerun the six full author gates or review the generated PDF. Re-review the fixes at their exact new revision before approval.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Coordinator `coordinator-ops-20261020`: **changes requested** at head `654402c6ea6a8efa89fa3eb29afcbf31da622045`, source `077363a05aef29152639cedb3b4fc995981fe2fc`. I read the complete InPlace module, its clients, the two changed index entries, and the existing native `Turing.Action`/`Turing.Cfg` conventions. InPlace source bytes are unchanged between these revisions. This complements the [independent UniversalMap/SequentialSquaring and batch API review](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/123#issuecomment-6303924475).

1. **[must-fix] `paper/sections/iteration.tex:349–351`: state the output-projection premise of round hardness transfer.** The theorem requires `tape : Fin m → Fin w` and `∀ x, e (M.init x) ∘ tape = x` (`InPlace.lean:389–400,405–420`). Its lower bound is inherited by composing with this zero-gate wiring. Injectivity of `e` on reachable configurations alone supplies no free decoder. State the projection condition and the transferred bound at time `τ*T`; keep the separate upper bound with storage `2^m*τ` under positive rounds and the supplied step/initial circuits.
2. **[must-fix] `InPlace.lean:27–37,51–52,242–249`: qualify stabilization by eventual halting.** Absorbing halting does not make every run stabilize after the configuration count. I checked a finite counterexample in a private Lean file: `Q = Bool`, `Γ = Unit`, one cell, zero heads, `δ` toggles the state and `halting := False`. `HaltingAbsorbing` holds, the configuration count is two, and the configurations after two and three steps differ. The actual theorem is sound: the count-time configuration is halting iff the run ever halts, and equals a halting configuration whenever one is reached. Use that conditional wording in the module and index (lines 343–345). Likewise describe `embed : Bool → Γ` at line 102 as an input map, not an inclusion, and remove the unsupported “valid encodings” gloss from `card_config` at line 154; neither fact needs an injective input map.
3. **[must-fix] model scope and completion record:** explain why this finite configuration-map example is separate from the shared native machine core. Here the input tape is writable, all heads share its `n` cells, moves clamp, and the highest-index colliding write wins. Native `Turing.Cfg` has a read-only input, separate unbounded work tapes, and a write-only output. The new circuit results assume an injective-on-reach encoding plus correct step/initial circuits and charge their sizes; they do not compile the local table or establish a native simulation. `inplace_halting` outputs an encoded configuration with a semantic equivalence, not a separately costed halting-test bit. Preserve those boundaries in the module/index and record the native adapter/step-circuit construction and concrete modulus-counter round instantiation as outstanding in ROADMAP or a linked follow-up. The generic conditional round theorem can be delivered independently of #107; the concrete sharpness instance is absent from this PR.

The independent review's client request also applies here: supply an actual encoding, step circuit and initial circuit witnessing a headline bound, with clamped-boundary/colliding-write behavior. The current idle-machine cardinality example does not instantiate those circuit hypotheses. My private boundary probes confirm the stated clamp/collision convention and show that the input map can collapse inputs.

Checked and sound: reachable-state covering and cardinality bounds, positive-round remainder decomposition, absorbing-halting argument, injectivity-based encoding width, both charged initialization/circuit bounds and the zero-gate lower-bound transfer. Fresh private Lean MCP checks are clean for InPlace and all boundary probes; `git diff --check` passes. I found no defect in those Lean statements/proofs. Author CI is green, but the generated PDF is not approved while these statement/model corrections remain. Re-review the fixes at the new exact revision before integration. This is an AI coordinator verdict, not a platform approval or human editorial approval.

body:
## Summary

Ports the universal-map simulation, product-factor, and group-action hardwiring reductions, the in-place multi-head machine reachability/power/halting bounds, and the Carmichael sequential-squaring reduction from `SamuelSchlesinger/iterating-functions` (`lean/Proofs/{UniversalMap,InPlace,SequentialSquaring}.lean`), closing #117:

- **`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Iteration/UniversalMap.lean`**:
  - Generic simulation transfer `iterate_simulation`, Boolean input-wire placement `hardwired`, `exists_hardwired_comp`, `exists_hardwired_projection`, and circuit transfer `simulation_circuit`.
  - Product-map projections `prodMap`, `prodMap_power_circuit`, and `prodMap_power_circuit_left`.
  - Group-action hardwiring `smul_perm_symm`, `smul_zpow_circuit`, `smul_iterate_circuit`, `smul_inverse_circuit`, and `pairAction_iterate`.
  - Straight-line step interpreter `Universal.Description`, `Universal.Config`, `Universal.read`, `Universal.step`, `Universal.wireIndex`, `Universal.describe`, `Universal.start`, `Universal.run`, `Universal.step_round`, `Universal.step_iterate`, and `Universal.universal_power_circuit` (with explicit documentation of the unbounded mathematical `Universal.Config` model boundaries).
- **`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Iteration/InPlace.lean`**:
  - Standalone fixed-length multi-head machine `InPlace.Move`, `InPlace.Move.apply`, `InPlace.Machine`, `InPlace.Config`, `InPlace.writeHeads`, `InPlace.Machine.step`, `InPlace.Machine.init`, `InPlace.Machine.HaltingAbsorbing`, and `InPlace.card_config`.
  - Reachable-set cardinality bounds `InPlace.reach`, `InPlace.reach_card_le_configs`, `InPlace.reach_card_le_of_cover`, `InPlace.reach_card_le_time`, `InPlace.iterate_rounds`, `InPlace.reach_card_le_round`, and `InPlace.iterate_card_halting`.
  - Circuit upper/lower transfer theorems `InPlace.inplace_fixed_power`, `InPlace.inplace_fixed_power_optimized`, `InPlace.inplace_configs_optimized`, `InPlace.inplace_time_optimized`, `InPlace.inplace_halting`, `InPlace.round_lower_bound_of_hard`, and `InPlace.round_bounds_of_hard` (with explicit documentation of the standalone `InPlace.Machine` model boundaries).
- **`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Iteration/SequentialSquaring.lean`**:
  - Carmichael exponent `SequentialSquaring.carmichael`, `SequentialSquaring.carmichael_pos`, squarefree Euler-totient power identity `SequentialSquaring.pow_carmichael_succ` / `SequentialSquaring.pow_add_mul_carmichael` / `SequentialSquaring.pow_eq_pow_of_modEq` on all of `ZMod M` (units and non-units), and sequential-squaring reduction `SequentialSquaring.reducedExponent`, `SequentialSquaring.reducedExponent_le`, `SequentialSquaring.iterate_square_reduced`, and `SequentialSquaring.crypto_table_entries`.
- **`ComplexityTests/Iteration.lean`**, **`ROADMAP.md`**, and **`paper/sections/iteration.tex`**:
  - Concrete non-vacuous and boundary tests (`Universal.step_round` for `G = 0, 1, 3`, `Universal.universal_power_circuit`, `InPlace.inplace_halting` on `idleMachine`, 2-head clamped/colliding `collideMachine`, and `SequentialSquaring` on `ZMod 1`, zero-divisor `3 : ZMod 15` including `T = 0`, and non-squarefree `ZMod 4`), `#print axioms` guards, roadmap updates, and theorem-index entries.

ok    mk_all --check

`python3 scripts/build_paper.py` succeeded cleanly.

title: feat(counting): characterize GapP by native finite machines
body:
Every verifier-defined GapP difference now has an actual fixed finite native List-choice machine with a polynomial all-branches clock. A true verifier result produces one chosen-sign leaf; a false result produces a balanced accepting/rejecting pair. A one-step, two-occurrence selector adds independently prepared witness families, including unequal lengths. This proves the bidirectional GapP machine characterization with exact signed counts.

Closes #120. Closes #106.

- Source/test checkpoint: `6457c0f3730a38a0d0866a440b51c04ef57caacd`; integrated source head `b21f6e4cab93863ae072e2293f7dc8dc4b8c8217` includes main `a9b72ca0` without source conflicts.
- Headline endpoints: `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.exists_signed_verifier_machine`, `Turing.MultiTapeCTM.exists_verifier_difference_machine`, and `Cslib.Complexity.mem_GapP_iff_exists_machine`.
- Exact routed count pairs are `(N, N-f)` and `(N-f, N)`. The native selector count law adds both component counts; the List/native bridge preserves occurrences even when outputs coincide.
- Routing a verifier with clock `T` costs `T + (T + 4 + 1)`; combining routed clocks `S+`, `S-` costs `S+ + S- + 1`. Existing unary preparation, framing, buffers, copying/rewinding and tidy restoration remain charged. Halted padding adds no choices.
- Fixed finite state type, tape count, machine and clock precede every input. Constructed tables are globally nonblocking. Halting is required on encoded instances; `encBits` covers all binary inputs. This is a closed-machine result, without oracle channels or a runtime bound uniform in a supplied machine description.
- Concrete adversarial clients prove buffered/selected counts `2/1`, `1/2`, and `2/2`, plus first-halt clock padding, retained dirty scratch and input head, live-selector versus halted control, zero-bit witnesses, unequal witness lengths and cancellation. Three headline axiom guards report only the standard allowed axioms.
- Reuses the existing shared core, FreeM/List execution, singleton lift, scanner and buffered compiler. The former private enumeration-count helper is shared in `BitString.Enumeration`; no public declaration is renamed or removed.

ROADMAP leaves UP/FewP ambiguity-restricted characterizations open. The displayed entry count is automatic; no PDF is committed. Author checks passed on the [CI PDF artifact](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/actions/runs/39514685003/artifacts/12308160231): 144 entries/76 pages, pages 1 and 29–31 inspected, all six embedded declaration URLs verified against exact live GitHub source. body:
Closes #125.

> **Note:** Stacked on PR #122 (`work/hard-power-counting-20261020`, which introduces `ModulusCounter.lean`).

### Summary
Ports the remainder-power equivalence and batched modular-counter upper and lower bounds from `SamuelSchlesinger/iterating-functions` (`c4cfa198`, `lean/Proofs/{CounterRemainders,CounterBatch}.lean`) into `Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Iteration/CounterBatch.lean`:

1. **Remainder-power equivalence (`CounterBatch.lean:75–110`)**:
   - Defines `counterRemainder` and proves `word_counterRemainder`, `addResidue_eq_addWrapSpec`, `counterRemainder_of_power` (`≤ c.size + 1`), and `counterPower_of_remainder` (`≤ c.size + 100 * (k + 1)`).
2. **Batched modular-counter upper bound (`CounterBatch.lean:111–303`)**:
   - Defines `counterBlock`, `counterBatchPower`, `residueKeys`, and `residueValues`.
   - Proves `counterBatchPower_apply`, `counterBlock_counterBatchPower`, `iterate_counterBatchPower`, `counterStep_iterate_left`, `counterStep_iterate_joinState_zero`, `joinState_zero_zero`, `residueKeys_injective`, `clog_two_pow_add_le`, and `batched_counter_power` (size `≤ 40000 * (k + 1) ^ 3 * (2 ^ k + r)` for `r ≤ 2 ^ (k + k)` using one shared dictionary `lookupOr` and `r` parallel `addResidue` circuits).
3. **Batched modular-counter lower bounds (`CounterBatch.lean:304–440`)**:
   - Proves `counterPower_of_batched` (size `≤ c.size` by duplicating one state across all `r` blocks), `counterBatch_size_ge_of_ne_id` (`r ≤ c.size` whenever `ModulusCounter.power T ≠ id`), `counterBatch_lower_bounds`, and `batched_hard_counter_power` (for `64 ≤ k`, some `T < ModulusCounter.period k` simultaneously satisfies the shared-dictionary upper bound and both lower bounds `lowerBudget k < c.size ∧ r ≤ c.size` for all `0 < r ≤ 2 ^ (k + k)`).
4. **Tests & Documentation**:
   - Adds nonvacuous regression tests and `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/Iteration.lean`.
   - Updates `ROADMAP.md` and `paper/sections/iteration.tex` (`Batched modular-counter powers and lower bounds`) with 15 `\declat{f4dad04ef6c6adef3a5289df7c653a43e75228bf}{...}` declaration links.

### Validation
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`
- `python3 scripts/build_paper.py` (76 pages, 0 `Overfull \vbox` / `Overfull \hbox` warnings, visual inspection of rendered page 66)

### Independent Reviews
- **CSLib API Review (`14919544-d52b-40a4-aa1f-d7fa16f654b7`):** Reviewed revision `f4dad04ef6c6adef3a5289df7c653a43e75228bf`. Checked naming conventions, headers, `-- upstream: candidate`, `public import` vs `import`, module docstring, citations (`[Schlesinger2026IteratedFunctions]`), reuse of `ResidueAdd.lean`, `ModulusCounter.lean`, and `SharedDictionary.lean`, and proof hygiene. Verdict: **APPROVED** with 0 blocking issues.
- **Mathematical Correctness Review (`0cdeb10e-3db3-44c3-81d1-6ef4f4507c85`):** Reviewed revision `f4dad04ef6c6adef3a5289df7c653a43e75228bf`. Checked all definitions, hypotheses, quantitative bounds (`c.size + 1`, `c.size + 100*(k+1)`, `40000*(k+1)^3*(2^k+r)`, `lowerBudget k < c.size ∧ r ≤ c.size`), and edge cases (`k = 0`, `r = 0`, `a = 0`, `b ≥ a`, `64 ≤ k`). Verdict: **APPROVED** with 0 blocking issues.
- **Theorem Index Review (`bbf779fa-0ff8-44cc-9a13-d5cbbbf120ba`):** Reviewed `paper/sections/iteration.tex` and `ROADMAP.md` against `f4dad04ef6c6adef3a5289df7c653a43e75228bf`, verifying all 15 `\declat` line numbers, declaration names, quantifiers, and scope boundaries. Verdict: **APPROVED**.

**Exact head:** `4f4634e648c13e5aa73cd56170f6c17f65c8ae39`. **Verdict: changes requested. Source mathematics remains approved; final API/documentation/client and integration approval waits for the following fixes.**

1. **[must-fix] State the supplied selector contracts in the index** (`paper/sections/iteration.tex:307–311`). `forest_navigation_spec` receives sound/complete flagged selections of a prefix mark and an anchor candidate. The long-range alternative requires both selections to succeed and the candidate to pass the final short verification prefix before applying the interval test. It does not construct a first-hit selector, and anchor existence/uniqueness is guaranteed on the checkpoint hull, not for every arbitrary off-hull transient target. Please make those success/failure and soundness/completeness hypotheses explicit while retaining the final verification. Also replace “first-hit mark” in `ForestNavigation.lean:23` with a selected/sound prefix mark: the theorem intentionally permits any such mark.
2. **[should-fix] Correct the path orientation wording** (`paper/sections/iteration.tex:298–299`). `forestPath` is already the root-to-vertex reversal of the forward orbit prefix. “Ranking the reversed root-to-vertex paths” reverses the description a second time. Say “ranking the root-to-vertex paths” or “ranking the reversed forward-orbit prefixes.”
3. **[should-fix] Reuse Mathlib's orbit-list API** (`ForestIntervals.lean:65–89`). `forestTrace` and its length/membership proofs duplicate `List.iterate`, `List.length_iterate` and `List.mem_iterate`. I privately checked equality to the current trace and the replacement length/membership statements under MCP. After importing `Mathlib.Data.List.Iterate`, membership with the current equality orientation is `by simpa only [eq_comm] using (List.mem_iterate (f := f) (a := x) (n := k) (b := y))`. Use the upstream API, with a thin domain wrapper only if useful. These names are new in this unmerged branch, so no deprecated alias is required.
4. **[should-fix] Add actual navigation and rejection clients** (`ComplexityTests/FunctionalGraph.lean:15–17,45–78`). The header claims concrete `ForestAnchor` and `forest_navigation_spec` coverage, but those endpoints are only axiom-guarded. The supplied edge/table instances are nonvacuous. Please additionally exercise a nontrivial compressed-edge interior and an actual navigation call, including an off-hull side branch that matches a last-predecessor key but fails the final short verification. This checks the essential distinction behind item 1 rather than merely reapplying an existence theorem.

What was checked and is sound: the `2|H|` mark bound; root-path/interval orientation in the actual Lean statements; positive compressed-edge lengths bounded by `2L`; nonmerging interiors and unique last-predecessor keys; depth-filtered anchors; and both directions of the supplied-selector transient navigation theorem. No source edits were made by this reviewer. This development depends on merged `Cycle`/`Checkpoints`, not the pending #114 batch, and the roadmap correctly leaves compressed-forest circuit synthesis open.

All 31 new index pins hit the stated declarations and all 34 inherited pinned links in `iteration.tex` remain. The PR body accurately inventories the actual APIs, and Samuel Schlesinger's authorship/source credit matches the four primary modules at `c4cfa198a241b3d2cc3bfa5f744a68a66f49be8b`. Re-pin affected declarations after fixes and request exact-revision review. title: feat(counting): characterize UP and FewP by native machines
body:
The verifier-defined UP and FewP classes now have exact native finite-machine characterizations. Both directions reuse the actual parsimonious #P bridge: a bound of one or a polynomial on accepting witness counts becomes the same bound on accepting occurrence traces, with a polynomial all-branches clock.

Closes #131.

- Endpoints: `Cslib.Complexity.mem_UP_iff_exists_machine` and `Cslib.Complexity.mem_FewP_iff_exists_machine`. The fixed tape count, finite control, closed List-choice machine and polynomial clock precede every input; FewP has a separate ambiguity polynomial in encoded input length. Tables are globally nonblocking, while the halting/correctness contract is on the encoding image (`encBits` covers all binary inputs).
- Ambiguity bounds accepting branches only. Rejecting and total branch counts are unrestricted by that bound. Repeated equal transition occurrences count separately; early-halt clock padding introduces no new paths. No new machine semantics, compiler or shared counting helper was needed.
- Actual 0-tape Unit-state clients have 0, 1 or 3 copied possible accepting occurrences plus two always-rejecting occurrences. They prove exact accept/reject counts, nonblocking and one-step all-branches halting for arbitrary inputs, clock padding, a nonconstant language in UP/FewP and the zero ambiguity polynomial. A multiply accepting machine is not a language separation claim. Both headline axiom guards use only the standard allowed axioms.

Validation: all six local gates passed on immutable source/test checkpoint `72e6465f1f456ccc6080e3bd65a6fb322468ad84`, based on merged main `037c95e4b81733937618ceeb20531423b6e273ac`. Log: `/private/tmp/counting-ambiguity-131-check.log`. Three fresh author MCP checks were clean. Subsequent commits change only the index/roadmap and one module-docstring sentence clarifying global nonblocking versus encoded-image halting; that module's fresh MCP check also passes. Remote CI and artifact checks are separate.

body:
Closes #128.

Proves native logarithmic-space model checking for every fixed first-order sentence over a finite relational input vocabulary expanded by canonical `0`, `1`, `max`, order and BIT. `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.queryLanguage_mem_L` concerns the actual `encStructure` query language: it checks table shapes, rejects cardinalities below two, and evaluates genuine numeric atoms even inside quantified formulas. Numeric tables and an efficient-evaluator certificate are not supplied by clients.

The compiler shares the original equality/implication/quantifier control through narrow term and relation handlers. Existing order-free public names, code lengths and empty-universe behavior are preserved. Native-costed `Expr.sub` and `Expr.bit` reuse proved arithmetic; focused prerequisite commit `9bf2748f` moves Christian Reitwiessner's unchanged binary digit certificate into shared `InSpace.Bit` and preserves its old full name as a dated deprecated alias.

The vocabulary and sentence are fixed. Work space is logarithmic in full encoded input length, using the existing unary cardinality and framed input tables in `tupleIndex` order. The contract is at `encStructure`, with no claim about raw words outside its image. Ordered interpretation transducers, reduction closure, projections and capture remain open. The documented #86 upstream exception is unchanged.

body:
Closes #137.

### Summary
- Factors shared output routines (`tupleReg`, `coordinatesCode`, `length_coordinatesCode`, `reaches_coordinatesCode`, `tupleReg_ne`, `flatMap_range_pair_append_false`, `rejectCode`, `reachesOut_rejectCode`, `encStructure_reject`) into `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/LogSpace/FirstOrder/Output.lean` (`97622143391f6777b14b832420787b5a79d7109d`).
