title: feat(stateful): certify resource bounds across interface refinements
body:
Stateful clients already had separate semantic Hoare rules and per-operation resource bounds, but no client contract that carried a budget through interface implementations. This adds `Spec.CostHoare`, separate `Module.ChargeBound` certificates, and compositional transport through adaptive linking and native realizations.

The `stateful` Aesop rule set supports pure/call contracts and named routine reuse. Intermediate assertions, budgets and implementations are explicit proof inputs. An adaptive counter client is implemented through a mutable cell and paired storage: the zero branch costs seven, the nonzero branch two, and budget six is refuted. A parametric test charges the continuation at its updated state.

This first milestone of #274 follows #160 and supports the architecture intended for #273. Total controller-time certificates, `polytime` integration, argument delivery/decoding and vEB remain subsequent work. The native example is a primitive evidence interpretation, not a newly implemented RAM backend. Existing `WordRAM/Dynamic` realization contracts can supply native-operation bounds separately.

Validation: complete actual-file Lean MCP diagnostics; all six strict local checks passed on the original source (session38388) and again on the combined current-main tree (session73491); global axiom audit and three named guards. Independent correctness review by `/root/ordered_fagin_recovery`; independent API/tactic/final tests and index review by `/root/recovery_integration`. No source findings; index wording was corrected to state the native initial representation and contract-precondition hypotheses explicitly. Local PDF pages82–83 and all three new declaration annotations were inspected and independently approved. CI and its PDF artifact provenance remain coordinator gates; no maintainer approval is implied.

Source credits: reuse the existing Stateful calculus and Quang Dao's upstream `PFunctor.FreeM`; preserve its source documentation and CLRS citation in the index. AI assistance: OpenAI Codex worker `worker-refinement-20261021` authored the change and coordinated independent nonauthor reviews. No author approval or merge.

Theorem-index impact: updated the existing Stateful result with precise quantifiers, initial-state-dependent budgets, module-cost refinement and native-execution scope; three exact source pins. ROADMAP and UPSTREAM describe remaining controller certification work.

Published source `5d9eefc4f20726054a71df3539c2471f1c18712c` has exactly the tested local `e4539513` tree `61377bf7b2d7e0210250df65a78d50b604b8079b`. Only publication metadata and the three resulting documentation SHA pins changed. The repinned PDF and remotely resolved source links were independently rechecked; final PDF SHA256 `73a514399409c9bb08145918945d9eb961645da3f1df373e8fc94b4d514f87fd`.

Current head `3ebc658f3916a7d0cf247d04cfcd4be7b76069ef` incorporates main `c7d0d1da`; its full tree `78a27edcae8e2223ba0fbe0454be28aeac785315` exactly matches the tested local merge. Only the independent review-log additions conflicted, and both were preserved. Implementation/tests and the Stateful result prose are unchanged. The combined rendering and all source pins received fresh independent review. CI and coordinator integration remain pending; this is a review handoff.

title: feat(proof-complexity): Haken's pigeonhole lower bound for resolution
body:
Closes #271

## Summary

Formalizes the propositional pigeonhole formula $\mathrm{PHP}^m_n$ (`Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF.pigeonhole m n`) and Haken's (1985) exponential lower bound on the size of resolution refutations of $\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n$, following the Beame–Pitassi (1996) / Jukna (2012, Section 18.6) critical-assignment bottleneck and greedy matching-restriction proof.

### Added modules and declarations

1. **`Complexity/Logics/Propositional/Pigeonhole.lean`** (`Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF`):
   - `pigeonClause n i`, `holeClause i i' j`, `pigeonhole m n : CNF (Fin m × Fin n)`
   - `mem_pigeonhole`, `eval_pigeonClause`, `eval_holeClause`, `eval_pigeonhole_eq_true_iff`
   - `satisfiable_pigeonhole_iff : (pigeonhole m n).Satisfiable ↔ m ≤ n`
   - `not_satisfiable_pigeonhole (h : n < m) : ¬ (pigeonhole m n).Satisfiable`
   - `length_le_of_mem_pigeonhole`, `length_pigeonhole_le`, `card_toFinset_vars_pigeonhole_le`

2. **`Complexity/Logics/Propositional/Resolution/Proof.lean`** (`Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF`):
   - `CNF.restrictBy (ρ : V → Option Bool) (f : CNF V) : CNF V`
   - `CNF.IsProof.restrictBy`: restricting a resolution proof of `c` from `f` by `ρ` produces either `true` (if `ρ` satisfies `c`) or a resolution proof of a subclause `c' ⊆ c.restrictBy ρ` from `f.restrictBy ρ` whose lines are line-by-line subclauses of the `ρ`-unsatisfied lines of the original proof.

3. **`Complexity/Logics/Propositional/Resolution/Pigeonhole.lean`**:
   - Sub-instance formulation `Pigeonhole.pigeonClauseOn`, `Pigeonhole.pigeonholeOn P H` and single-pair matching restriction `Pigeonhole.matchPair i₀ j` with `Pigeonhole.restrictBy_pigeonholeOn_subset`
   - Critical assignments `Pigeonhole.IsCrit P H g` and `Pigeonhole.critAssign H g`, falsified-pigeon set `Pigeonhole.falsifiedPigeons P H c`, and critical-satisfaction pair witnesses `Pigeonhole.satPairs P H c`
   - Bottleneck counting lemma `Pigeonhole.exists_le_card_falsifiedPigeons_mul`: in any refutation of `pigeonholeOn P H` with `#P = #H + 1`, some line falsifies at least `#P / 3` critical assignments (i.e. `#P ≤ 3 * #(falsifiedPigeons P H c)`)
   - Width-in-critical-pairs lower bound `Pigeonhole.exists_le_card_satPairs` and `CNF.exists_le_card_satPairs_pigeonhole`: every resolution refutation of `pigeonhole (n + 1) n` contains a clause `c` with `2 * n ^ 2 ≤ 9 * #(Pigeonhole.satPairs univ univ c)`
   - Greedy matching-restriction induction `Pigeonhole.exists_restrict_countP_satPairs` and `Pigeonhole.pow_le_mul_countP_satPairs`
   - Headline lower bounds (`Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF`):
     - `pow_le_mul_of_refutableInSize_pigeonhole (hn : 8 ≤ n) : (pigeonhole (n + 1) n).RefutableInSize s → 12 ^ (n / 3) ≤ 11 ^ (n / 3) * s`
     - `two_pow_le_of_refutableInSize_pigeonhole : (pigeonhole (n + 1) n).RefutableInSize s → 2 ^ (n / 24) ≤ s`
     - `not_refutableInSize_pigeonhole (hs : s < 2 ^ (n / 24)) : ¬ (pigeonhole (n + 1) n).RefutableInSize s`
     - `Derivation.two_pow_le_size_pigeonhole (d : (pigeonhole (n + 1) n).Derivation []) : 2 ^ (n / 24) ≤ d.size`

4. **Tests & Documentation**:
   - `ComplexityTests/ProofComplexity/Pigeonhole.lean` and updates to `ComplexityTests/ProofComplexity/Resolution.lean` (including `#print axioms` guards and concrete refutations for `n = 0, 1`)
   - `references.bib`: `Haken1985` and `BeamePitassi1996`
   - `ROADMAP.md` and `paper/sections/proofs.tex` theorem-index entry.

## Scope Limitations

- Covers the standard non-onto $(n+1)$-to-$n$ pigeonhole formula (`pigeonhole (n + 1) n`), without hole-surjectivity clauses or weak PHP ($m \gg n$).
- Uses the direct Beame–Pitassi bottleneck + restriction argument rather than the Ben-Sasson–Wigderson size–width tradeoff (since the pigeon clauses of $\mathrm{PHP}^{n+1}_n$ already have initial width $n$).
- Bounds resolution proof size (number of lines in a DAG proof or nodes in a tree derivation), not solver runtime.

## Theorem Index Assessment

Added the "Haken's pigeonhole lower bound for resolution" entry in `paper/sections/proofs.tex` linking `satisfiable_pigeonhole_iff`, `not_satisfiable_pigeonhole`, `exists_le_card_satPairs_pigeonhole`, `pow_le_mul_of_refutableInSize_pigeonhole`, `two_pow_le_of_refutableInSize_pigeonhole`, and `Derivation.two_pow_le_size_pigeonhole` at commit `c9fdac891ad75dfbf23952ced1a54b2c62a68401`.

## Validation

Ran `scripts/check.sh` in the worktree:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`: ok
- `lake exe mk_all --check`: ok
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`: ok
- `lake lint`: ok
- `lake exe lint-style`: ok
- `lake exe checkInitImports`: ok

## AI Assistance Disclosure

Authored with AI assistance: Antigravity agent (Claude and Gemini), worker `agy-worker-f29e46b2` / `agy-worker-f29e46b2/php-resolution`.

title: feat(circuit/rational): certify staged integer determinant in polynomial time
body:
Part of #201

## Summary

Proves Milestone 1 of #201: the staged division-free Bird integer determinant `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.detRows` on framed lists of rows of binary sign-magnitude integers (`encList (encList encIntBin)`) is computable tidily in polynomial time (`detRows_polytime`), using the existing stage bit-length invariant `intBits_le_of_mem_stagesRows` and `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.iterateWith`.

All existing copyright and author credit headers (`Copyright (c) 2026 OpenAI, Samuel Schlesinger` and `Authors: OpenAI, Samuel Schlesinger, Karn Seth`) are preserved.

## Headline declarations (`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Rational/Runtime/Determinant.lean`)

```lean
namespace Cslib.Circuits.Rational

def stageEntryBound (L k : ℕ) : ℕ := L + k * (2 * L + 1) + 1
def stageRowBound (L k : ℕ) : ℕ := L * (2 * stageEntryBound L k + 1)
def stageTableBound (L k : ℕ) : ℕ := L * (2 * stageRowBound L k + 1)

theorem length_encList_stagesRows_le (A : List (List ℤ)) {i k : ℕ} (hik : i ≤ k) :
    (encList (encList encIntBin) (stagesRows A i)).length ≤
      stageTableBound (encList (encList encIntBin) A).length k

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_rowEntry {rows : α → List (List ℤ)} {i j : α → ℕ}
    (hrows : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime rows encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hi : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime i encIn encUnary)
    (hj : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime j encIn encUnary) :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => rowEntry (rows x) (i x) (j x)) encIn encIntBin

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_tabulateRows {d : α → ℕ} {g : α → ℕ → ℕ → ℤ}
    (hd : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime d encIn encUnary)
    (hg : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : (α × ℕ) × ℕ => g p.1.1 p.1.2 p.2)
      (encPair (encPair encIn encUnary) encUnary) encIntBin) :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => tabulateRows (d x) (g x))
      encIn (encList (encList encIntBin))

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_squareRows :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime squareRows
      (encList (encList encIntBin)) (encList (encList encIntBin))

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_traceTerms {A F : α → List (List ℤ)} {i : α → ℕ}
    (hA : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime A encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hF : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime F encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hi : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime i encIn encUnary) :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => traceTerms (A x) (F x) (i x))
      encIn (encList encIntBin)

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_productTerms {A F : α → List (List ℤ)} {i j : α → ℕ}
    (hA : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime A encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hF : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime F encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hi : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime i encIn encUnary)
    (hj : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime j encIn encUnary) :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => productTerms (A x) (F x) (i x) (j x))
      encIn (encList encIntBin)

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_stepEntryRows {A F : α → List (List ℤ)} {i j : α → ℕ}
    (hA : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime A encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hF : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime F encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hi : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime i encIn encUnary)
    (hj : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime j encIn encUnary) :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => stepEntryRows (A x) (F x) (i x) (j x))
      encIn encIntBin

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_stepRows :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List (List ℤ) × List (List ℤ) => stepRows p.1 p.2)
      (encPair (encList (encList encIntBin)) (encList (encList encIntBin)))
      (encList (encList encIntBin))

@[program_certificate]
theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_stagesRows {A : α → List (List ℤ)} {k : α → ℕ}
    (hA : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime A encIn (encList (encList encIntBin)))
    (hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime k encIn encUnary) :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => stagesRows (A x) (k x))
      encIn (encList (encList encIntBin))

@[program_certificate]
theorem detRows_polytime :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime detRows (encList (encList encIntBin)) encIntBin
```

## Validation

No Lean MCP server was available; iterated with targeted `lake env lean` checks and ran `scripts/check.sh` once at completion:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`: ok
- `lake exe mk_all --check`: ok
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`: ok
- `lake lint`: ok
- `lake exe lint-style`: ok
- `lake exe checkInitImports`: ok

`ComplexityTests/RationalHitting/Determinant.lean` instantiates `detRows_polytime`, `length_encList_stagesRows_le`, `detRows_eq`, `detRows_eq_det_ofRows`, compositional `fun_prop` examples, and `#print axioms` guards (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

## Theorem-index assessment & remaining limitations

- Added `\subsection{Polynomial-time division-free integer determinant}` in `paper/sections/synthesis.tex` with `\declat` links pinned to `72da75e2041012a90b95a0d49e6a8cfbbf7d4d8f` and updated `ROADMAP.md`.
- Scope limitation: this PR completes Milestone 1 (`detRows_polytime`) of #201; Milestones M2–M5 of #201 (binary `divMod`/`gcd` and canonical rational serialization, certified integer lift tables, per-point Cramer output words, and grid enumeration for the full `hittingGenerator` endpoint) remain open.

## AI assistance disclosure

Antigravity agent (Claude and Gemini), worker `agy-worker-f29e46b2` / `agy-worker-f29e46b2/detrows-m1`.

body:
## Coordinator Review — `agy-coordinator-d55a006b`

- **Verdict**: **CHANGES REQUESTED**
- **Reviewed head SHA**: `82c298d9222c610eb5e5c63e9a4e0e8e29957a5d`
- **Independent review subagent**: `b5ba017b-5970-4e22-ad8e-da6c97531dfa` (`FO Composite Simp Reviewer`, Antigravity, Gemini 4 Argon)

The `tupleStructure` / `tupleInputStructure` design, the `dsimproc → simproc` upgrade in `Complexity/Tactic/FirstOrder.lean`, and the client proof reductions (-43 net proof lines across FO modules) are sound and pass CI (`39657734315`). Before integration, please address the following API, `simp`-hygiene, and documentation polish items identified by `b5ba017b-5970-4e22-ad8e-da6c97531dfa`:

1. **Avoid global default-`simp` pollution on `Unit → α` (`Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Interpretation/Tuple.lean:92-94`)**:
   - `fun_unit_eq_iff` is currently tagged `@[simp, fo_realize]`, which registers a global default-`simp` rule on `@Eq (Unit → α)` in every module transitively importing `Interpretation/Tuple.lean`.
   - **Fix**: Tag `fun_unit_eq_iff` with `@[fo_realize]` only (without `@[simp]`), matching `Model.ext_iff` in `Interpretation.lean`.
2. **Fix nonexistent declaration reference in docstring (`Complexity/Tactic/FirstOrder.lean:38` & `Interpretation.lean:64`)**:
   - Line 38 of `Complexity/Tactic/FirstOrder.lean` lists `Interpretation.realize_comp_rel`, which does not exist (only `Interpretation.realize_comp_rel_tupleStructure` exists, cited on line 43). Remove `Interpretation.realize_comp_rel` from line 38 (and mention `Projection.comp_numeric_domain` alongside `Projection.comp_numeric_rel`).
   - In `Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Interpretation.lean` (`## Main results`, lines 64–65), list `Cslib.Logic.FO.Interpretation.realize_comp_domain` alongside `relMap_comp_model`.
3. **API symmetry & term-mode definition in `Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Projection.lean:256-271`**:
   - Write `Projection.tupleModelEquiv` directly as a term (`letI ... { ... }`) without `by ... exact`, matching `Interpretation.tupleModelEquiv`.
   - Add `@[simp] theorem tupleModelEquiv_apply` after `Projection.tupleModelEquiv` to match `Interpretation.tupleModelEquiv_apply` (`Interpretation/Tuple.lean:87`) and `Interpretation.unitModelEquiv_apply` (`Interpretation/Unit.lean:75`).
4. **Tag `realize_successor` and `realize_tupleSucc` with `@[simp, fo_realize]` (`Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Ordered/TupleSuccessor.lean:202, 242`)**:
   - Matches `realize_tupleLt` and `realize_tupleLe` in `TupleInterpretation.lean` so downstream `fo_simp` clients don't need to pass them manually.

<details><summary>Complete reproducible harness (place beside baseline/ and candidate/ clean checkouts)</summary>

Run `python3 benchmark.py > results-v2.jsonl 2> errors-v2.log` after building dependencies in both variants. Host/toolchain description in the harness records this measured machine and should be updated when reproducing elsewhere. A single profiler file can be re-read using `python3 benchmark.py <profile.json>`.

```python
"""Paired, read-only Lean client profiling for Complexitylib2 issue 272."""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
VARIANTS = {
    "A": (ROOT / "baseline", "23d97bee81664dbda4fd948ea2ce64c8f4dd8155"),
    "B": (ROOT / "candidate", "7ebefd57bbcfcaa138b3f094d63ae763bd17dd41"),
}
TARGETS = [
    "Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Ordered/TupleInterpretation.lean",
    "Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Ordered/TupleSuccessor.lean",
    "Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Problems/ColoringReduction.lean",
]
ORDER = "ABBAABBAABBA"


def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.check_output(["git", *args], cwd=repo, text=True).strip()


def metrics(path):
    profile = json.loads(path.read_text())
    assert profile["meta"]["sampleUnits"]["time"] == "ms"
    command_ms = frontend_ms = kernel_in_command_ms = 0.0
    command_threads = []
    negative_weights = []
    for thread in profile["threads"]:
        samples = thread["samples"]
        assert samples["weightType"] == "tracing-ms"
        if not samples["length"]:
            continue
        thread_command_ms = 0.0
        stack = thread["stackTable"]
        frame = thread["frameTable"]
        funcs = thread["funcTable"]
        labels = thread["stringArray"]
        ancestors = {}

        def names(index):
            if index not in ancestors:
                label = labels[funcs["name"][frame["func"][stack["frame"][index]]]]
                parent = stack["prefix"][index]
                ancestors[index] = (label,) + (() if parent is None else names(parent))
            return ancestors[index]

        for index, weight in zip(samples["stack"], samples["weight"], strict=True):
            # Lean exports signed gaps between nested trace children. Summing all
            # descendants telescopes to the enclosing trace duration; do not clamp.
            if weight < 0:
                negative_weights.append(weight)
            if thread.get("isMainThread", False):
                frontend_ms += weight
            trace = names(index)
            if any(name.startswith("Elab.command") for name in trace):
                command_ms += weight
                thread_command_ms += weight
                if "Kernel" in trace:
                    kernel_in_command_ms += weight
        if thread_command_ms:
            command_threads.append(thread["name"])
    assert len(command_threads) == 1, command_threads
    assert command_ms > 0
    return {
        "command_ms": command_ms,
        "kernel_in_command_ms": kernel_in_command_ms,
        "frontend_ms": frontend_ms,
        "command_threads": command_threads,
        "negative_gap_count": len(negative_weights),
        "min_negative_gap_ms": min(negative_weights, default=0),
    }


def validate_repos():
    for label, (repo, revision) in VARIANTS.items():
        assert git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD") == revision
        assert not git(repo, "status", "--porcelain"), label


def run(label, target, sequence, warmup=False):
    repo, revision = VARIANTS[label]
    name = Path(target).stem
    profile = ROOT / f"{name}-{sequence:02d}-{label}-{'warm' if warmup else 'sample'}.json"
    command = [
        "lake", "env", "lean", "-j1", "-DElab.async=false",
        "-Dtrace.profiler=true", "-Dtrace.profiler.threshold=0",
        f"-Dtrace.profiler.output={profile}", target,
    ]
    env = dict(os.environ, LEAN_NUM_THREADS="1")
    start = time.perf_counter()
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=repo, env=env, capture_output=True)
    wall_s = time.perf_counter() - start
    assert result.returncode == 0, (command, result.stdout.decode(), result.stderr.decode())
    assert not result.stdout.strip() and not result.stderr.strip(), (
        result.stdout.decode(), result.stderr.decode()
    )
    row = {
        "kind": "warmup" if warmup else "sample", "target": target,
        "variant": label, "revision": revision, "sequence": sequence,
        "source_blob": git(repo, "rev-parse", f"HEAD:{target}"),
        "wall_s": wall_s, "exit_code": result.returncode,
        "output_sha256": hashlib.sha256(result.stdout + result.stderr).hexdigest(),
        "profile": str(profile), **metrics(profile),
    }
    print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
    return row


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) == 2:
        print(json.dumps(metrics(Path(sys.argv[1])), indent=2))
        return
    validate_repos()
    print(json.dumps({
        "kind": "method", "order": ORDER, "samples_per_variant_per_target": 6,
        "threads": 1, "Elab.async": False, "profiler_threshold_ms": 0,
        "metric": "signed trace-weight sum beneath Elab.command; gaps telescope to command duration",
        "scope": "synchronous command elaboration including kernel checking; import/startup separate",
        "host": "Mac16,8 arm64, 14 logical CPUs, 48 GiB; other worker builds active",
        "toolchain": subprocess.check_output(["lake", "env", "lean", "--version"],
                                             cwd=VARIANTS["A"][0], text=True).strip(),
    }), flush=True)
    rows = []
    for target in TARGETS:
        for i, label in enumerate("AB"):
            run(label, target, i, warmup=True)
        for i, label in enumerate(ORDER):
            rows.append(run(label, target, i))
    validate_repos()
    for target in TARGETS:
        summary = {"kind": "summary", "target": target}
        for label in VARIANTS:
            group = [r for r in rows if r["target"] == target and r["variant"] == label]
            summary[label] = {
                key: {"median": statistics.median(r[key] for r in group),
                      "min": min(r[key] for r in group),
                      "max": max(r[key] for r in group)}
                for key in ["command_ms", "wall_s"]
            }
        print(json.dumps(summary), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

</details>

body:
Closes #272

### Summary
Extends the first-order reduction automation (`fo_simp`, `fo_reduction`, `fo_qf`, and the `fo_realize` simprocs) to simplify composite interpretations (`J.comp I`), higher-dimensional full-domain interpretations (`tupleStructure`), and composite projections (`J.comp I`):

- **`Complexity.Logics.FirstOrder.Interpretation.Tuple`**:
  - Defines `Interpretation.tupleStructure`, `Interpretation.tupleModelEquiv`, `relMap_tupleStructure` (`@[fo_realize]`), and `realize_onFormula_tupleStructure`.
  - Proves `realize_comp_domain_tupleStructure` and `realize_comp_rel_tupleStructure` (`@[fo_realize high]`) to rewrite the domain and relation formulas of `J.comp I` directly to `J` on `I.tupleStructure M` whenever `I.domain` holds of every tuple.
- **`Complexity.Logics.FirstOrder.Interpretation`**:
  - Adds `Interpretation.Model.mk` and `Model.val_mk` (`@[simp, fo_realize]`), and tags `realize_comp_domain` with `@[fo_realize]` so restricted-domain composite interpretations simplify cleanly without subtype predicate rewrite mismatches.
- **`Complexity.Logics.FirstOrder.Projection`**:
  - Adds `comp_numeric`, `comp_numeric_domain` (`@[fo_realize]`), `comp_numeric_rel` (`@[fo_realize]`), `compEquiv_numeric_symm_apply_val_val` (`@[simp, fo_realize]`), and `relMap_comp_inputStructure` (`@[fo_realize high]`).
  - Defines `Projection.tupleInputStructure`, `relMap_tupleInputStructure` (`@[fo_realize]`), `Projection.tupleModelEquiv`, `realize_onFormula_tupleStructure`, and `realize_comp_rel_tupleStructure` (`@[fo_realize high]`).
- **`Complexity.Logics.FirstOrder.Reduction` & `Reduction.QuantifierFree`**:
  - Adds `coe_bundledOf` (`@[fo_realize]`), `Interpretation.mem_iff_tupleStructure`, `Reduces.of_tupleStructure`, and `QFReduces.of_tupleStructure`.
- **`Complexity.Tactic.FirstOrder`**:
  - Upgrades `reduceInterpretationDomain`, `reduceInterpretationRel`, `reduceProjectionNumeric`, and `reduceProjectionRel` from `dsimproc` to `simproc` with an explicit expected-type equality proof `mkExpectedTypeHint (← mkEqRefl e') (← mkEq e e')`, allowing `simp` to discharge conditional domain hypotheses (`∀ x, I.domain.Realize x`) at reducible transparency without unfolding composites into raw pullback formulas.
  - Extends `fo_reduction` to apply `QFReduces.of_tupleStructure` and `Reduces.of_tupleStructure` after `of_unitStructure` and before `of_interpretation`.
- **Client refactorings & proof-length metrics**:
  - Refactored manual formula/interpretation realization and quantifier-freeness proofs in `ColoringToCNF`, `ColoringReduction`, `TupleInterpretation`, `TupleSuccessor`, and `BitArithmetic` to use `fo_simp` and `fo_qf`.
  - `python3 scripts/proof_lengths.py` measurements:
    - `First/second-order logic`: 510 proofs / 3,965 body lines (median 3.0, P90 19) → **533 proofs (+23) / 3,922 body lines (-43 lines net; median 3, P90 17)**.
    - `TOTAL`: 17,623 proofs / 138,223 body lines → **17,646 proofs (+23) / 138,180 body lines (-43 lines net)**.

### Theorem Index Assessment
No impact on `paper/main.tex`: this PR adds tactic and structural simplification helpers for first-order interpretations and projections and refactors internal proof scripts without changing any headline theorem statement, assumption, model, or quantitative bound in the curated theorem index.

### Validation
Ran `./scripts/check.sh` on commit `82c298d9`:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail` (ok)
- `lake exe mk_all --check` (ok)
- `lake test --wfail --iofail` (ok)
- `lake lint` (ok)
- `lake exe lint-style` (ok)
- `lake exe checkInitImports` (ok)

title: feat(stateful): certify adaptive RAM controllers and charged calls
body:
Stateful operation budgets previously left client control flow, initialization, and argument delivery outside the RAM execution. This adds fixed-code `Refines` certificates with charged sequencing, branches, pure results, preparation and initialization, plus a uniform word-valued RAM-time predicate. Named certificates are reusable through `stateful`, `polytime`, and the demonstrated `fun_prop` registration.

The complete adaptive client reuses the existing bounded stack: push/pop the input, observe the answer, and push/pop one if it was zero. One fixed nine-register program returns `max n 1`, leaves its stack empty, and takes exactly 49 instructions for zero or 29 otherwise, including setup, argument writes, dispatch, control and halt. Every input fits its stated logarithmic numerical-magnitude width threshold. Standard input placement is the machine convention; arbitrary continuation synthesis, general allocation, Turing-machine simulation, and vEB remain subsequent work.

Closes #280. Follow-up to #278 and #160; supports #273.

Validation and review:
- All six strict project checks passed on final source over main `9e161a05` (session 50678, exit 0), plus complete Lean MCP diagnostics, global/named axiom audits, and documentation configuration checks.
- Tests exercise actual adaptive argument passing, charged call/bind/branch/pure/initialization rules, both exact paths and minimum width, insufficient-budget rejection, conditional-budget certificate lookup with competing certificates, and RAM/TM predicate separation.
- Independent nonauthor `/root/controller_review` approved API, correctness, tests, index prose, exact published source, and rendered pages 84–85 with five checked declaration links. Two documentation nits and a source-link nit were resolved; no blocking findings. The full API-documentation build and `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` passed: 1,572 modules, all four new module source links, and four headline search entries verified at head `071b80e0`. The isolated clone remote and an obsolete reused-cache module were corrected locally; no source changes were needed.
- Theorem-index impact: added the precise controller result and clarified the earlier operation-cost boundary. Local PDF SHA256 `583aaca3cfffc9693bed4b9bf796de9f52695403bca272c05abcdb83436dafe2`. Coordinator `agy-coordinator-d55a006b` independently approved exact head `071b80e0`, inspected the CI PDF artifact and its provenance/pages/links, and merged the PR as `8540156a0ee8b96dbdb8f543e47d80b2907b4ad9`; see [coordinator review](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/284#issuecomment-6324445136). All PR CI checks passed.

Source credit is retained for Quang Dao's upstream FreeM and the existing stack/lean-trominoes-based RAM substrate. No author approval or merge.

title: feat(circuit): AC^i[q] ⊆ TC^i, threshold/majority in NC^1, and fan-in-bounded TC^i in NC^(i+1)
body:
Closes #269 (for the `AC^i[q] ⊆ TC^i`, `threshold`/`majority ∈ NC^1`, and fan-in-bounded `TC^i ⊆ NC^{i+1}` milestones).

## Summary

1. **Wire-multiplicity collapsing & $\mathsf{AC}^i[q] \subseteq \mathsf{TC}^i$** (`Multiplicity.lean`, `ModMajority.lean`, `Smolensky/Majority.lean`):
   - `Unbounded.multCircuit`: collapses repeated input wires of symmetric gates $f_m(x) = G(m, \operatorname{weight}(x))$ into distinct wires with multiplicity weights while deduplicating `.ac` gates, preserving computed functions (`eval_multCircuit`) and size (`size_multCircuit`), non-increasing depth (`depth_multCircuit_le`), and bounding gate arity by $n + |C|$ (`fanInAtMost_multCircuit`).
   - `modCircuitOfMajority` & `Unbounded.modMultCircuit`: simulates an $n$-input $\mathrm{MOD}_q$ gate using $(2n + 2)$-input majority in size $\le 1 + (n + 1)(2(2 + |M|) + 2)$ and depth $\le \operatorname{depth}(M) + 4$, reduces wire multiplicities modulo $q$ (or $\min(k, 1)$ when $q = 0$) to bound expanded fan-in by $\max(q, 1)(n + |C|)$, and proves `Unbounded.exists_majority_simulation_modGate`, `ACMod_subset_TC`, `AC0Mod_subset_TC0`, and `Smolensky.AC0Mod_ssubset_TC0` ($\mathsf{AC}^0[p] \subsetneq \mathsf{TC}^0$ for every odd prime $p$).

2. **Carry-save bit counting, threshold/majority in $\mathsf{NC}^1$, and fan-in-bounded $\mathsf{TC}^i$ in $\mathsf{NC}^{i+1}$** (`CarrySave.lean`, `ThresholdNC1.lean`):
   - `csa3to2` and `csa4to2`: $3$-to-$2$ and $4$-to-$2$ carry-save adders over the De Morgan basis preserving unsigned $w$-bit sums modulo $2^w$ (`val_csaSum_add_val_csaCarry_mod`, `pairVal_eval_csa4to2_mod`) in constant depth ($\le 6$ and $\le 12$) and linear size ($\le 20w$ and $\le 40w$).
   - `finishCircuit` and `weightCircuit`: balanced binary tree of $4$-to-$2$ reducers over $k$ input bits followed by $w = \lceil \log_2(k + 1) \rceil$ carry-clearing steps, computing the exact $w$-bit binary numeral of $\operatorname{weight}(x)$ (`val_eval_weightCircuit`) in depth $\le 1 + 19w$ and size $\le \max(1, k) + 40kw + w(20w + 1)$.
   - `thresholdDeMorganCircuit` and `majorityDeMorganCircuit`: compose `weightCircuit k` with the $w$-bit comparator `leCircuit w` to compute $\mathrm{Th}^k_j$ and $k$-bit majority in depth $\le 2 + 23\lceil \log_2(k + 1) \rceil$ and size $\le 4 + k + 40kw + w(20w + 6)$.
   - `threshold_mem_NC_one`, `majority_mem_NC_one`, `strictMajority_mem_NC_one`, `Threshold.exists_deMorgan_simulation_of_fanInAtMost`, `Unbounded.exists_deMorgan_simulation_majority_of_fanInAtMost`, `mem_NC_succ_of_threshold_fanInAtMost`, and `mem_NC_succ_of_majority_fanInAtMost`.

3. **Tests & Documentation**:
   - Added `#print axioms` guards for all 15 headline theorems in `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean` and non-vacuity checks in `ComplexityTests/NonVacuity.lean`.
   - Added two curated entries in `paper/sections/circuits.tex` and updated `ROADMAP.md`.

## Remaining Limitations

- All inclusions are nonuniform.
- In `Unbounded.extSignature`, a majority gate `.gate m` can repeat the same wire with unbounded multiplicity $m$ not bounded by $n + |C|$. Eliminating unbounded wire multiplicities in unrestricted $\mathsf{TC}^i$ without a polynomial fan-in hypothesis requires Muroga's threshold weight-bounding theorem and is recorded as open work in `ROADMAP.md`.

## Validation

Ran in `/private/tmp/complexitylib2-tc-nc` with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4`:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail` (passed)
- `lake exe mk_all --check` (passed)
- `lake test --wfail --iofail` (passed)
- `lake lint` (passed)
- `lake exe lint-style` (passed)
- `lake exe checkInitImports` (passed)
- `python3 scripts/build_paper.py` (passed)

## Independent Reviews

- **Reviewer**: `agy-worker-b24933fa/review-269` (`4e654662-524a-4e00-bc8c-a06feec99fc8`, independent research subagent)
- **Reviewed revisions**: `28552bfdfffefcb2e4c4783735a10be85aadd5c0` and `0df188f8d24ac5aabca97e2f0c102cf6dddcb077`
- **Scope**: `Multiplicity.lean`, `ModMajority.lean`, `CarrySave.lean`, `ThresholdNC1.lean`, `Smolensky/Majority.lean`, `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean`, `ComplexityTests/NonVacuity.lean`, `paper/sections/circuits.tex`, `ROADMAP.md`.
- **Findings & resolutions**:
  1. *cslib-style & API review*: Passed with 0 issues.
  2. *Mathematical correctness review*: Passed with 0 issues; verified definitions, resource bounds, edge cases ($q = 0, 1$, $k = 0$, $k < j$), and non-vacuity examples.

title: perf(tactic): speed up polytime and ppt proof search
body:
Closes #267

## Summary

Optimizes the `polytime` and `ppt` Aesop rule engines across `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean`, `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.lean`, and `Complexity/Tactic/PPT.lean`:

1. **`applyKnownCall` identity-argument fast path (`Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean`)**:
   - When a local routine certificate `hf` matches a direct call with an identity argument (`fun x => x`, checked after `!(← instantiateMVars argument).hasExprMVar`), assign `input.goal.assign decl.toExpr` directly after `withReducible (isDefEq decl.type target)` rather than applying `.comp` / `.comp_polytime` and generating redundant identity composition subgoals.
   - Reject local certificates whose encoding differs from the target call rather than falling through to redundant identity `.comp`.
2. **`solveTagged` rule-set selection and reducible `assumption` (`Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean`)**:
   - Use `[PolyTime]` alone for deterministic goals and `[PPT, PolyTime]` only for `IsPPTOn` / `IsPPT` goals, with `terminal := true, assumptionTransparency := .reducible`.
3. **Syntactic head guards before `withoutLocalCall` / `withLocalCall` (`Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.lean`)**:
   - Check the body head (`BitString.append`, `List.cons`, `List.foldl`, `Nat.iterate`) before running `withoutLocalCall`/`withLocalCall` and `etaExpand` in `polytimeConstructFast`, `polytimeFold`, and `polytimeIterate`.
   - Hoist `case hlist => polytime_step` outside the zero-growth probe in `polytimeFold` so `hlist` is discharged once rather than inside both the zero-growth and fallback branches.
4. **Reducible `assumption` in `polytime` and `ppt`, plus input-encoding mvar guard in `pptFunProp` (`Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.lean`, `Complexity/Tactic/PPT.lean`)**:
   - Add `assumptionTransparency := .reducible` (and `terminal := true` in `ppt`) so Aesop's built-in `assumption` rule does not perform `.default`-transparency unfolding of local hypotheses against every subgoal.
   - Skip `pptFunProp` when the input encoding (`target.getAppArgs[2]!`) still contains metavariables (e.g. on monadic continuation goals before the sampler determines the intermediate encoding).

## Benchmarks (`LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 lake env lean` wall time, base `5464e455` vs branch)

| Benchmark file | Base (s) | After (s) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `ComplexityTests/PolyTimeContracts.lean` | 26.23 | 15.02 | **-11.21s (-42.7%)** |
| `ComplexityTests/PPTTactic.lean` | 13.15 | 11.06 | **-2.09s (-15.9%)** |
| `ComplexityTests/PolyTimeTactic.lean` | 14.33 | 14.66 | +0.33s |
| `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/CookLevin/Tableau.lean` | 3.75 | 3.84 | +0.09s |
| `Complexity/Computability/Probabilistic/Repeat.lean` | 3.43 | 3.55 | +0.12s |
| `Complexity/Computability/NP/CanonicalComplete.lean` | 2.13 | 2.13 | 0.00s |
| `Complexity/Computability/Encoding/Graph.lean` | 2.86 | 2.88 | +0.02s |
| `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/CircuitEval.lean` | 3.63 | 3.50 | -0.13s |
| `Complexity/Computability/Padding.lean` | 2.80 | 2.91 | +0.11s |
| `Complexity/Computability/Space/Savitch.lean` | 1.98 | 2.04 | +0.06s |
| `Complexity/Computability/Reduction.lean` | 2.68 | 3.55 | +0.87s |
| `Complexity/Tactic/MemoizePPT.lean` | 2.50 | 2.84 | +0.34s |
| **Total (12 files)** | **79.47s** | **67.98s** | **-11.49s (-14.5%)** |

On `ComplexityTests/PolyTimeContracts.lean`, total `aesop` proof-search time (`trace.profiler`) dropped by >4x to **3.47s** across the entire file.

## Theorem Index Assessment

No theorem statements, definitions, hypotheses, or scope changed (tactic-only performance optimization). Checked `paper/main.tex`: no impact.

## Independent Review

- **Reviewer**: `agy-worker-b24933fa/review-267` (independent research subagent `44487e95-fe03-4a71-a4b4-9c7538cc7d37`)
- **Reviewed revision**: `b6cb6f607a4febe9fbb7666a9378fd36b4f56e9c` (with polish applied in `22927a0aa0214045f3ce3368cf9908b0830ddac3`)
- **Scope**: cslib-style, API, soundness/completeness, and theorem-index impact review of `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean`, `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.lean`, and `Complexity/Tactic/PPT.lean`.
- **Findings & resolutions**:
  1. Update `solveTagged` docstring to reflect that `[PPT, PolyTime]` runs on PPT goals and `[PolyTime]` runs otherwise — resolved in `22927a0aa0214045f3ce3368cf9908b0830ddac3`.
  2. Guard `applyKnownCall`'s identity-argument fast path with `!argument.hasExprMVar` so an under-constrained tuple component metavariable is not unified with `idArg` — resolved in `22927a0aa0214045f3ce3368cf9908b0830ddac3`.

## Validation

All 6 validation checks pass cleanly:
- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`

title: feat(computability): add binary division, GCD, and rational encoding certificates
body:
Closes #283
Part of #201

## Summary

Implements Milestone 2 of #201 (#283): polynomial-time certificates for binary division, remainder, Euclidean greatest common divisor, and canonical natural and reduced-rational encodings (`encodeNat` and `encodeRat (Rat.divInt p q)`).

* **`Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Nat/BinaryDiv.lean`**:
  * `Turing.MultiTapeTM.BinaryDiv.divModStep`: one shift-and-subtract step of binary long division.
  * `BinaryDiv.foldl_divModStep`, `BinaryDiv.divMod_eq`, `BinaryDiv.length_encPair_foldl_divModStep_le`: folding `divModStep` over `a.bits.reverse` from `(0, 0)` computes `(a / b, a % b)` (including `a / 0 = 0` and `a % 0 = a`) with encoded pair length at most `3 * word.length + 1`.
  * `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_divMod`, `.binary_div`, `.binary_mod`, `.binary_div'`, `.binary_mod'`: `@[fun_prop, program_certificate]` rules for binary division and remainder on `encNat`.
* **`Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Nat/Gcd.lean`**:
  * `Turing.MultiTapeTM.BinaryGcd.gcd_product_halving`: for `0 < a ≤ b`, `2 * (a * (b % a)) ≤ a * b`.
  * `BinaryGcd.gcdStep`, `BinaryGcd.gcdCount`, `BinaryGcd.iterate_gcdStep_eq`, `BinaryGcd.length_encPair_iterate_gcdStep_le`: iterating `gcdStep` for `a.bits.length + b.bits.length + 1` steps reaches `(Nat.gcd a b, 0)` with intermediate pair encodings bounded by `3 * (encPair encNat encNat p).length`.
  * `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_gcd`, `.binary_gcd'`: `@[fun_prop, program_certificate]` rules for `Nat.gcd` on `encNat`.
* **`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Rational/Runtime/Encode.lean`**:
  * `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.digits_two_map_bne_zero`, `.encodeNat_eq`: `encodeNat a = List.replicate a.bits.length true ++ false :: a.bits`.
  * `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.encodeNat_polytime`, `.encodeNat_polytime'`: `@[fun_prop, program_certificate]` certificates for `encodeNat`.
  * `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.divInt_num_abs`, `.divInt_den`, `.divInt_sign`, `.encodeRat_divInt`: reduced numerator magnitude, denominator, and sign bit of `Rat.divInt a b` via `Nat.gcd a.natAbs b.natAbs` (including `b = 0`).
  * `Cslib.Circuits.Rational.encodeDivInt_polytime`, `.encodeDivInt_polytime'`: `@[fun_prop, program_certificate]` certificates for `(p, q) ↦ encodeRat (Rat.divInt p q)` on `encPair encIntBin encIntBin`.
* **`ComplexityTests/RationalHitting/Encode.lean`**:
  * Concrete examples and kernel evaluations, `fun_prop` composition tests, and `#print axioms` guards for `binary_div`, `binary_mod`, `binary_gcd`, `encodeNat_polytime`, and `encodeDivInt_polytime`.
* **`ROADMAP.md` & `paper/sections/synthesis.tex`**:
  * Updated the rational hitting-list runtime roadmap bullet and added a curated theorem-index entry with exact `\declat{20c7c1390afb0a50fd39759e3010e668a620678c}{...}` declaration links.

## Source credit & AI disclosure

* `gcd_product_halving` and the reduced-rational component lemmas `digits_two_map_bne_zero`, `divInt_num_abs`, `divInt_den`, and `divInt_sign` are adapted from OpenAI's formalization (`[OpenAI2026RationalHitting]` at `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`) via the complexitylib port (`[Schlesinger2026RationalHitting]` at `add0aca8ee0d71e68969f2cb45cf91554a50f787`).
* Authored with AI assistance (`agy-worker-f29e46b2/rational-m2`).

## Validation

* `./scripts/check.sh` passed on `2da7c2e7f84827b7f96d34b884f969198fecd92a`:
  * `lake build --wfail --iofail`
  * `lake exe mk_all --check`
  * `lake test --wfail --iofail`
  * `lake lint`
  * `lake exe lint-style`
  * `lake exe checkInitImports`
* `python3 scripts/build_paper.py` succeeded cleanly (113 pages, 0 errors).

## Remaining limitations

* Certifies individual natural and reduced-rational encodings; polynomial-time certification of the full rational matrix hitting-list generator `encodeOutput (hittingList n s)` remains in Milestones 3–5 of #201.

title: feat(ram): certify sparse memory on native multitape TMs
body:
Closes #293; implements the finite-memory component of #292.

Sparse RAM reads and replacement writes now have actual native binary multitape-machine certificates. The implementation reuses Mathlib's `AList` and Christian Reitwiessner's certified equality/search/filter calculus. It proves functional-update semantics, distinct stored-cell bounds, encoded-size/max-word invariants, and parameterized `ComputableTidilyInO` time/space bounds including argument preparation and an input-supplied read default. Separate corollaries give cubic time and linear workspace in full encoded input length, with `fun_prop` polynomial-time rules.

This does not yet simulate whole RAM programs: checked primitives, finite control, initialization/output and whole-run transport remain in #292. Default-valued writes retain a binding, so cardinality counts stored addresses rather than nondefault support.

Validation: all six local gates passed (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`). Tests cover absent/default reads, overwrites, a two-cell store containing address `2^128`, distinct address/value types, native write→read composition, automation, an actual finite-state witness, and headline axiom guards.

Independent review by `/root/controller_review` approved source/API/correctness, index statements, exact declaration pins and the locally rendered entry (page 82); initial documentation findings were resolved. title: feat(counting): prove LWPP reduction closure and multiple-target robustness
body:
## Summary

Implements polynomial-time many-one reduction closure for `LWPP`, unary-indexed target normalization, and finite-family multiple-target robustness for `WPP` and `LWPP` (#26).

### Main additions
- **[`Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Int/Binary.lean`](Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Int/Binary.lean)**:
  - `Int.size_natAbs_prod_le`: binary length bound on the magnitude of a list product of integers.
  - `@[fun_prop] theorem Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.intBin_prod`: polynomial-time list product of binary integers (`encList encIntBin → encIntBin`), proved via `foldlWith_of_bounded_growth`.
- **[`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/WPP.lean`](Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/WPP.lean)**:
  - Subclass containments: `UP_subset_LWPP`, `UP_subset_WPP`, `coUP_subset_LWPP`, `coUP_subset_WPP`, `FewP_subset_LWPP`, `FewP_subset_WPP`.
  - Remaining Boolean closures: `diff_mem_WPP`, `symmDiff_mem_WPP`, `diff_mem_LWPP`, `symmDiff_mem_LWPP`.
  - Finite multiple-target robustness (`mem_WPP_of_finset_targets`, `mem_LWPP_of_finset_targets`): if a `GapP` function takes `0` outside `A` and one of a fixed finite family (`s : Finset ι`) of nonzero polynomial-time binary-integer targets on `A`, then $\prod_{i\in s} f_i - \prod_{i\in s}(f_i - g) \in \mathsf{GapP}$ witnesses membership with single nonzero target $\prod_{i\in s} f_i$.
  - Unary-indexed target normalization (`mem_LWPP_of_polyTime_index`) and many-one reduction closure (`PolyTimeReducible.mem_LWPP`): if a `GapP` function takes `0` outside `A` and $f(k(a))$ on `A` for a nonzero unary-input target $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and unary polynomial-time index $k : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ bounded by $p(|a|)$, multiplying the gap by the filtered product $\prod_{i \le p(|a|),\, i \ne k(a)} f(i)$ normalizes the target to $\prod_{i \le p(|a|)} f(i)$, yielding reduction closure for `LWPP` by taking $k(a) = |r(a)|$.
- **[`ComplexityTests/WPP.lean`](ComplexityTests/WPP.lean)**:
  - Nonvacuous tests (including length-altering reductions and signed multiple-target families) and `#print axioms` guards for all headline theorems.
- **Documentation & Theorem Index**:
  - Updated [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md), Section 4.15 ("Wide counting gaps") of [`paper/sections/randomness.tex`](paper/sections/randomness.tex) pinned to `f2409a4a13c9e6b67a22ede3eb3ef963ddf9401c`, and rebuilt [`paper/main.pdf`](paper/main.pdf).

### Scope & Limitations
- Uses the library's verifier-based `#P` and `GapP` definitions; nondeterministic counting-machine characterizations and oracle lowness of `WPP`/`LWPP` are not claimed.
- `mem_WPP_of_finset_targets` and `mem_LWPP_of_finset_targets` cover fixed finite target families (`s : Finset ι`), while `mem_LWPP_of_polyTime_index` normalizes a polynomial-time unary-computable target index $k(a)$; polynomial-cardinality target families where the accepting target index is not polynomial-time computable from the input (`Poly-LWPP = LWPP`, `Poly-WPP = WPP`) remain open in `ROADMAP.md`.

### Validation
All six checks in `scripts/check.sh` passed on `0180e770`:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`

### AI Assistance & Independent Reviews
- **Authoring agent**: Google DeepMind Antigravity (`worker-agy-20261020`, session `f04f33f1-0933-4580-9dd9-aafb408a4017`).
- **Independent cslib-style API review** (subagent `14919544-d52b-40a4-aa1f-d7fa16f654b7`, reviewed `f2409a4a`): **Approved**. Recommended making `Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.SPP.FewP` a private `import` in `WPP.lean` (with `public import Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.FewP`); applied in `f2409a4a`.
- **Independent mathematical correctness review** (subagent `0cdeb10e-3db3-44c3-81d1-6ef4f4507c85`, reviewed `f2409a4a`): **Approved**. Verified truth of statements, edge cases (`s = ∅`, negative targets, `n = 0`, length-altering reductions), and nonvacuity tests; recommended explicitly distinguishing fixed-`Finset` multiple-target robustness and known-index normalization from polynomial-family robustness (`Poly-LWPP = LWPP`, `Poly-WPP = WPP`) in docstrings; applied in `f2409a4a`.
- **Independent theorem-index review** (subagent `bbf779fa-0ff8-44cc-9a13-d5cbbbf120ba`, reviewed `0180e770` against `f2409a4a`): **Approved**. Verified all quantifiers, models, resource bounds, scope limitations, and all 22 `\declat` line numbers and declaration names in `paper/sections/randomness.tex`, and inspected rendered Page 21 of `paper/main.pdf`.

Closes #26

title: feat(ram): certify encoded primitives with native resource bounds
body:
Adds native TM certificates for the scalar primitives of a generic RAM model, as the model layer of #292. Each fixed symbol has one machine handling every encoded configuration and operand tuple. The certificate records arbitrary input-dependent time/space bounds and charges output length; forgetting bounds yields exactly native computability, while polynomial time follows only under separate polynomial-bound hypotheses.

The bundle covers checked literals/ALU results, optional Boolean tests, address conversion, move validity and PC validity. Checked results are connected to existing instruction evaluation, preserving faults. A complete bounded-natural addition/order model instantiates every field. A separate checked standard WordRAM-add certificate handles all unary-encoded widths with binary operands. Both reuse Christian Reitwiessner's native arithmetic/encoding calculus.

This does not certify memory access, arbitrary-program dispatch, complete RAM steps/runs, the full standard word basis, or exact real values as bit strings. Configuration encoding remains selectable. Input-only complexity results still require charged computable width selection and input fit. Sparse memory is #293; the fixed-program step interpreter is #298.

Validation and review:

- All six strict project gates passed with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2`: build, import inventory, tests/global axiom audit, environment lint, style lint and init imports. Documentation configuration and `git diff --check` passed.
- Tests instantiate the complete bundle, extract actual native machines, check arbitrary computability and quantitative/polynomial composition, reuse `polytime`, and exercise scalar/instruction rejection paths plus zero-width and overflow boundaries.
- Independent nonauthor `controller_review` approved exact source/API/correctness/tests and index prose without findings. Source commit 0e4ef81e8eb56c42a280f1223dd4d28ddf4486e0 (tree 3827454eb423947f1630588e5a8c1200ce3d61bc); final documentation head 915660b9a223478aa40b458970c514d9962b607b.
- The theorem index adds the primitive result with explicit quantifiers, models, resource bounds, encoding conventions, source credit and limitations. All five links pin 0e4ef81e8eb56c42a280f1223dd4d28ddf4486e0. Independently inspected local rendered page 82 of 115 and exact declaration links; actual CI artifact review is now independently approved in [review 6327630636](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/303#issuecomment-6327630636), covering artifact 12383540126 from run 39678547035, provenance, rendered page 82 and all five declaration links. title: feat(tm): add parameterized tuple and option resource rules
body:
Adds native resource rules needed to compose an encoded fixed-program RAM step. Fixed tuple
selection, gathering (including repeated indices), and update have linear time and space in the
full encoded input; finite-family construction retains arbitrary component time/space bounds
as E + sum_i T_i and E + sum_i S_i. Option elimination retains the original input and charges
tag/payload extraction, repeated option computation, and the selected handler.

The proofs reuse Christian Reitwiessner's native tidy calculus and the existing encPi finite-table
encoding directly. No arbitrary-bound result is obtained by choosing an opaque polynomial-time
witness. Dimensions are fixed; constants may depend on them. Empty dimensions and value/payload
types are covered. This is a compositional prerequisite for #298, not an encoded RAM simulator
or whole-run theorem transport.

Closes #301. Supports #298 and #292.

Validation: all six repository checks passed on main 1e2dcd0c plus the source change. Lean MCP
checks are clean. Tests cover empty types/products, repeated gathering, updates, concrete tuple
construction, read-after-update, and both branches of a client using input and payload. Named
axiom guards use only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

Independent API/correctness/index review: controller_review approved source 798d9514 and final
local docs head 0a70be7e. Its sole test-header finding was fixed and rechecked. The theorem index
states the exact hypotheses, arbitrary bounds, output-size accounting, and remaining simulator
boundary; source links are pinned to the source commit. Independent local rendering review
checked page 84 of the 116-page PDF and all six declaration annotations. Final local provenance

- `Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/{Model,Program,Member,Call}.lean` all reside in `namespace Cslib.Algorithms.WordRAM.VanEmdeBoas`, with exact 5-line Apache 2.0 headers, `module`, `-- upstream: candidate`, `@[expose] public section`, transitive `public import Complexity.Init`, and complete module docstrings (`## Main definitions`, `## Main results`, `## References` citing `[Demaine2015VanEmdeBoas]` and `[VanEmdeBoasKaasZijlstra1977]`).
- Zero `sorry`, zero custom `axiom`, zero `native_decide`, zero `maxHeartbeats` / `maxRecDepth` overrides, no `@[simp]` on machine step functions or transition tables, and all non-terminal `simp` calls use `simp only`.

#### 2. Mathematical Correctness & Non-Vacuity Review
- `Header` and `Rep` (`Model.lean:58–66`) recursively refine `Tree d` in actual RAM memory over `[p, p + span d)`, permitting stale empty extrema (`True` on `mem (p + 1)` and `mem (p + 2)` when `b = none`) and arbitrary surrounding memory (`rep_congr` / `rep_frame`).
- `member_descent_safe` (`Model.lean:107`) and `member_descendant_read_safe` (`Model.lean:125`) prove that whenever `(Tree.node (some (m, M)) s c).Valid` and `Rep` hold and the runtime maximum guard `x < mem (p + 2)` passes, `x < M < universeSize d * universeSize d` follows automatically—even for out-of-universe queries—so child header addresses lie strictly inside `[p, p + span (d + 1))`.
- `program` (`Program.lean:240`) is a single fixed 32-register `.standard` WordRAM program (`program.size = 212`, `(program.program out).length = 213`, `program_not_readsWidth`) independent of `d, U, query, w`.
- `member_call` (`Call.lean:98`), `member_executes` (`Call.lean:112`), `member_executes_generic` (`Call.lean:123`), and `member_executes_log` (`Call.lean:138`) prove exact execution within `28 * (d + 1) + 18 = 28 * (Nat.log 2 (Nat.log 2 (universeSize d)) + 1) + 18` instructions (including setup, dispatch, loop control, and halt), preserving all memory (`z.mem = s.mem`) and `z.regs root = base`.
- `ComplexityTests/VanEmdeBoasRAM.lean` witnesses non-vacuity on a multi-level tree (`fixtureTree : Tree 1`) in `poisonedMemory` across all 256 8-bit queries, `staleEmptyMemory`, adaptive multi-call sequences, and `#print axioms` guards (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`).

#### 3. Theorem Index & Documentation Review

title: feat(fo): ordered first-order reductions are logspace reductions, on a uniform many-one core
body:
Closes milestones 1 and 2 of #309 (milestone 3 migrations stay open; recorded in `ROADMAP.md`).

## Summary

**Ordered first-order reductions are logspace reductions** — `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.Reduces.logSpaceReducible`, with `L`/`P` closure of encoded ordered queries (Immerman, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.10).

- **Many-one core** (`Reduction/ManyOne.lean`): `ManyOneReducibleBy Good A B` with `refl`/`trans` from identity/composition closure, `mono`, `compl` and `lift` (transfer along partial decodings), plus generic `HardUnder`/`CompleteUnder`. `PolyTimeReducible`/`LogSpaceReducible` keep their literal `∃` bodies with `Iff.rfl` bridges, so `⟨f, by fun_prop, h⟩` still elaborates without `beta_reduce` (regression-tested); `PolyTimeHard`/`LogSpaceHard`/`…Complete` are `HardUnder`/`CompleteUnder` instances, definitionally their previous statements.
- **Level 1, semantic map** (`Ordered/DomainInterpretation*.lean`): ordered interpretations with a domain formula; image = φ₀-tuples, lexicographically ordered, renumbered by rank. Admissible when every image has ≥ 2 elements — the library's convention after Proviso 1.15 (Immerman's Definition 1.26 does not discuss smaller domains). Encoded map, partial decoding, and the decoding commutation consumed by `lift`.
- **Level 2, `≤_fo`** (`Ordered/DomainInterpretation/Certificate.lean`, `Composition.lean`, `Ordered/Reduction.lean`): numeric certificates (formulas defining the image's ≤, BIT, 0/1/max — Remark 1.32's requirement; without φ₀ ≡ true BIT need not be definable, per the paragraph after Exercise 1.33). `Ordered.Reduces` with `refl`, `trans` (certified composition, Proposition 1.28 / Exercise 2.15(1)), `compl`, `Definable.of_reduces`; full-tuple interpretations embed with their native certificate (`FullTupleInterpretation.reduces`).
- **One domain-counting transducer** (`LogSpace/FirstOrder/Transducer.lean`), parametrized by a `FormulaCompiler`, computes order-free interpretations, ordered interpretations with a domain formula (new: `DomainInterpretation.computableInLogSpace_encodedMap`), and full-tuple interpretations as the `domain = ⊤` instance. The old order-free and full-tuple programs are deleted (all private). Both logspace theorems are direct `ManyOneReducibleBy.lift` applications through one simulation lemma; the level-1 theorem needs no certificate (ranks are computed by counting).

Size: 23 files, +3459/−1313 (`Complexity/` +2742/−1285, tests +577). The three transducer files went 1414 → 1349 lines while gaining restricted domains; the rest is new semantics, the core and tests.

## Preserved API

No public declaration on `main` was removed or renamed. Statements unchanged: `PolyTimeReducible`, `LogSpaceReducible`, `PolyTime/LogSpace{Hard,Complete}` (definitionally), `FO.Interpretation.computableInLogSpace_encodedMap`, `FO.Reduces.logSpaceReducible`/`queryLanguage_mem_L`/`_mem_P`, `FullTupleInterpretation.computableInLogSpace_encodedMap`/`mem_queryLanguage_encodedMap_iff`/`logSpaceReducible_onSentence`, `Vocabulary.decoded_encode`.

## Limitations

Fixed vocabularies and interpretation; relational targets; lexicographic image order (Remark 1.32's default). Certificates are supplied explicitly; the library builds them for full-tuple interpretations of positive dimension, the identity, and certified composites. The certified restricted-domain test client has ranks equal to a coordinate; an input-dependent domain covers the level-1 logspace claim. Projections, completeness results and the remaining reduction-notion migrations are out of scope.

## Validation

`scripts/check.sh` on code revision `834487c0`: build `--wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, test `--wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports` — all ok. Headline theorems' axioms: `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` (guards in `ComplexityTests/OrderedFOReduction.lean`, `ComplexityTests/ManyOne.lean`, `ComplexityTests/OrderedReduction.lean`). Paper builds locally (`scripts/build_paper.py`); entries on pages 19–21 fit; 28/28 links verified at their revisions. The only overfull vbox (page 100) predates this change.

## Theorem index

New entry "Ordered first-order reductions are logspace reductions"; "Canonical full-tuple ordered interpretations as logspace transducers" and "Order-free interpretations induce logspace reductions" updated (shared transducer; links repointed to `834487c0`); stale "restricted-domain … remain open" sentence in the preceding entry fixed. Reductions-core refactor: no index impact (statements unchanged).

## Reviews (all independent of authoring; AI reviewers)

Authoring: main session `claude-opus-5-5-48cb80c1` (core, headline corollaries, integration, roadmap/index draft) and delegated worker subagents (PolyTime/LogSpace migration; ordered semantics; transducer unification; fix batch). An Immerman fact-check subagent checked Definitions 1.26/2.11, Proviso 1.15, Remark 1.32, Exercise 1.33, Propositions 1.28/3.5/3.10, Exercise 2.15 and Theorem 3.1 against the hosted chapters.

Revision `d3840a07`:
- Correctness/nonvacuity (adversarial): APPROVE WITH NITS — no blocking or should-fix; verified certificates force canonical numerics, no sentinel/encoding vacuity, preserved statements unchanged, axioms clean. Nits (lexicographic/relational scope, citation, "strictly more general", duplicated helper, weak client) → fixed or documented.
- cslib API/style (adversarial): APPROVE WITH NITS — no blocking; should-fix: unused witness structure (removed), contrived `lift` use (both theorems now direct `lift` applications), missing full-tuple constructor (added), misplaced general lemmas (moved), deferred migrations in ROADMAP (added); nits applied except renaming `lift` and moving the core to `Foundations` (kept; documented in #309).
- Theorem index: REQUEST CHANGES (prose only; 31/31 links OK) — stale neighbouring disclaimer, certificate-scope sentence, fixed-interpretation caveat → fixed; nits applied.

Revision `5e78416e` (fix batch, 4 commits on `d3840a07`): **not yet independently reviewed** — an independent re-review was started and stopped before reporting. Independent re-review of this exact revision is requested before integration.

body:
Closes #273

## Summary

Completes the full Word-RAM van Emde Boas tree certification (#273) on top of #291 and #302:

1. **`Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/Program.lean`**:
   - Factors out `insertBody`, `successorDescentBody`, and `successorUnwindBody` while keeping the single 32-register dispatcher `program` (`213` compiled instructions including `halt`) and its exact size/preservation lemmas unchanged.

2. **`Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/Insert.lean`**:
   - Proves single-step execution (`insertBody_exec`, at most `37` instructions per loop body) and the full loop certificate `insertLoop_spec` (`39 * (d + 1) + 2` instructions) establishing `Rep (tree.insert key) base z.mem` for any `key < universeSize d` and preserving all memory outside `[base, base + span d)`.

3. **`Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/Successor.lean`**:
   - Proves descent (`successorDescentBody_exec`), cluster unwind (`successorUnwindBody_cluster_exec`), and summary unwind (`successorUnwindBody_summary_exec`) step certificates.
   - Proves `successor_some_spec`, `successor_none_spec`, and unified `successor_loop_spec` (`65 * (d + 1) + 4` instructions) for any fitting query (including queries `≥ universeSize d`), using the `4 * d`-word scratch stack at `[stackBase₀, stackBase₀ + 4 * d)` with `base + span d ≤ stackBase₀`, preserving `Rep tree base z.mem`, restoring `z.regs sp = stackBase₀`, and preserving all memory outside `[stackBase₀, stackBase₀ + 4 * d)`.

4. **`Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/Init.lean`**:
   - Defines the uniform 32-register initializer `initProgram` (computing `(universeSize d, span d)`, building the `(splitSize k, childSpan k)` lookup table at `base + span d`, and traversing the tree in DFS order to initialize all headers while leaving stale empty extrema untouched).
   - Proves `init_dispatch_spec` (`8 * span d + 20 * d + 24` instructions), `init_call`, `init_executes` (`8 * span d + 20 * d + 25` instructions including `halt`), `init_executes_generic`, `init_executes_universe` (`80 * universeSize d + 20 * d` instructions), and `init_space_le` (`span d + 4 * (d + 1) ≤ 10 * universeSize d + 4 * (d + 1)`).

5. **`Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/Call.lean`**:
   - Proves complete call, flat `Executes`, `GenericRAM.Executes`, and `Nat.log 2 (Nat.log 2 (universeSize d))` bounds for all three operations on `program`:
     - Insertion (`tag = 0`): `insert_dispatch_spec`, `insert_call`, `insert_executes`, `insert_executes_generic`, `insert_executes_log` (`39 * (d + 1) + 16` instructions).
     - Membership (`tag = 1`): `member_dispatch_spec`, `member_call`, `member_executes`, `member_executes_generic`, `member_executes_log` (`28 * (d + 1) + 18` instructions).
     - Strict successor (`tag = 2`): `successor_dispatch_spec`, `successor_call`, `successor_executes`, `successor_executes_generic`, `successor_executes_log` (`65 * (d + 1) + 22` instructions).
   - Packages the finite-set `Stateful.Spec` (`Operation`, `spec`, `dynamicProgram`, `SetRep`, `certificate`) and proves `instruction_bound`, `instruction_bound_log`, `execOp_frame`, `executes_client_frame`, `client_spec`, and `run_initialized` (combining `initProgram` from arbitrary bounded memory with arbitrary admissible adaptive clients).

6. **`ComplexityTests/VanEmdeBoasRAM.lean`, `ROADMAP.md`, and `paper/sections/query.tex`**:

   - `MappingReducible` (`Halting/Reduction.lean`): add `mappingReducible_iff_manyOneReducibleBy := Iff.rfl`, delegate `.refl`, `.trans`, `.compl`, and `IsDecidable.of_mappingReducible` to `ManyOneReducibleBy`, and add `PolyTimeReducible.mappingReducible` (`Reduction.lean`) via `ManyOneReducibleBy.mono`.

   - `SharpPHard` / `SharpPComplete` (`SharpP/Completeness.lean`), `SearchHard` / `SearchComplete` (`TFNP.lean`), and `PromiseProblem.NPHard` (`PCP/Approximation.lean`): express via generalized `HardUnder`/`CompleteUnder`, add `_iff_hardUnder` / `_iff_completeUnder := Iff.rfl` bridges, and delegate `.trans` to `HardUnder.trans`.

title: refactor(machines): modularize GenericRAM simulation/transport and deduplicate TM plumbing
body:
## Summary

Implements #316 (`refactor(machines): modularize GenericRAM simulation/transport and deduplicate multi-tape TM plumbing`):

1. **Modularize `Complexity/Computability/GenericRAM/Simulation/Run.lean` (1,616 → 1,226 lines)**:
   - **Break `GenericRAM` → `WordRAM` dependency inversion**: Move the `Cslib.WordRAM` whole-run transport adapter (`executes_iff_exists_finiteRun`, `WordRAM.transportCertificate`, `WordRAM.transport_inO`, `WordRAM.transport_polyTime`) into `Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Native.lean`, removing `public import Complexity.Computability.WordRAM.Generic` (and `Complexity.Computability.GenericRAM.Native.Nat`) from `GenericRAM/Simulation/Run.lean`.
   - **Relocate general `NativeCertificate` combinators and polynomiality predicates**: Move `maxRoundTime`, `maxRoundSpace`, `maxStateLength`, `NativeCertificate.iterate`, `iterate_time`, `iterate_space`, and all 15 `*_isPolynomial` combinator lemmas into `Complexity/Computability/GenericRAM/Native/Combinators.lean`; move `Model.NativePrimitives.IsPolynomial` into `Complexity/Computability/GenericRAM/Native.lean`; and move `BoundedNat.nativePrimitives_isPolynomial` into `Complexity/Computability/GenericRAM/Native/Nat.lean`. All full declaration names and namespaces are preserved unchanged.
   - **Deduplicate `transportCertificate_isPolynomial`**: Refactor `transportCertificate_isPolynomial` in `GenericRAM/Simulation/Run.lean` to reuse `iterate_isPolynomial` directly instead of repeating the 65-line `maxStateLength_le` / `maxRoundTime_le` / `maxRoundSpace_le` bound derivation.
   - **Add `FiniteState.transport_polyTime_of_le_const` & `WordRAM.transport_polyTime_of_le_const`**: Discharge `hOutLen` automatically for constant step-budget bounds `∀ a, steps a ≤ K` by induction on `K` using `roundCertificate_isPolynomial`, simplifying the 6-step client example in `ComplexityTests/GenericRAMSimulation.lean`.
2. **Multi-Tape TM & Tidy Calculus Consolidation (`ROADMAP.md:1010`, `UPSTREAM.md:148-154`)**:
   - Extract `clearedCfg_nil`, `clearedCfg_cons`, `Sequential.rightCfg_clearedCfg`, and `PairReady.clearedCfg` in `Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Combinators/TidyNormalForm.lean` to simplify `exists_runPath_clearList`.
   - Move general tape-visit lemmas `exists_visitedByTapeHead_eq_Icc` and `workTapes_runFrom_eq_of_notMem_visitedByTapeHead` from `Plumbing/Shadow.lean` into a candidate section in `TapeLemmas.lean` (`UPSTREAM.md:148`).
   - Simplify `ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace.runFrom_initCfg_eq` in `Plumbing/Tidy/Run.lean` to a 1-line term proof via `computesTidily_iff_runFrom` and `initCfg_eq_wordsCfg`.
   - Add public `@[simp] lemma streamEmit_const_nil` to the candidate section of `Encodings/StreamFold.lean` and delete the duplicate private copies in `Complexity/Streaming.lean` and `Complexity/LogSpace/QueryMachine.lean`.

## Theorem Index Assessment

No impact on `paper/main.tex`: this PR is a structural modularization and proof-deduplication refactor that preserves all existing public declaration names, namespaces, theorem statements, and quantitative bounds.

## Validation

All 6 checks in `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 ./scripts/check.sh` pass at `a37de6a2`:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`

## AI Assistance Disclosure

Authored by Antigravity (`worker-consolidation-316`, Gemini) under coordinator review.

Closes #317.

## Summary

- **Module splits & placement**:
  - Added general finite-type expectation helpers (`Fintype.expect_unique`, `Fintype.expect_expect_update`, `Fintype.expect_bool`, `Fintype.expect_sub_expect_fiber`, `Fintype.expect_add_sq_of_expect_fiber_eq_zero`, `Fintype.exists_eq_add_expect_fiber_eq_zero`, `Fintype.expect_sq_le_of_expect_mul_le`, `Fin.expect_univ_cons`) to `Complexity/Foundations/Data/Finset/Expect.lean`, and deduplicated private copies in `Expander/{Products,Power,Walk,Hitting}.lean` and `Crypto/Primitives/PRG/Circuit.lean`.
  - Extracted the general finite-type harmonic-mean theory (`harmonicMean`, variational formula, monotonicity, concavity, Jensen, light-fraction Markov bound, pair decomposition) into `Complexity/Foundations/Analysis/HarmonicMean.lean` in namespace `Cslib`, retaining `@[deprecated (since := "2026-10-21")] alias` in `Cslib.BitString` in `Complexity/Foundations/BooleanAnalysis/HarmonicMean.lean`.
  - Extracted the cover-coding and Hamming-ball combinatorics (`coverCard`, `coverIndex`, `coverRank`, `ballSize`, `coverEntropy`, and all properties) into `Complexity/Foundations/Data/BitString/CoverCoding.lean` in namespace `Cslib.BitString`, retaining `@[deprecated (since := "2026-10-21")] alias` in `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.WeightedThreshold` in `ScalarActivity.lean`, updating `ComplexityTests/WeightedThresholdBounds.lean`, and simplifying `Justesen.lean`'s `card_filter_hammingNorm_le_eq_sum_choose` via `BitString.card_filter_weight_le`.
- **Foundational, circuit & crypto helper deduplication**:
  - Added `Finset.exists_median` to `Complexity/Foundations/Data/Finset/Quantile.lean` and deduplicated `WeightedThreshold/Cut.lean` and `Expander/Cheeger.lean`.
  - Consolidated binomial-product bounds (`Nat.descFactorial_mul_pow_le`, `Nat.choose_mul_pow_le`, `Nat.choose_mul_sub_mul_pow_le`, `Nat.two_mul_pred_pow_le`, `Nat.two_pow_mul_choose_sub_le`) in `Complexity/Foundations/Data/Nat/Choose.lean` and deduplicated `PartialAssignment.lean` and `Expander/Random.lean`.
  - Reused `Cslib.BitString.one_sub_pow_mul_one_add_mul_le_one` from `Bernoulli.lean` in `Expander/TowerBase.lean`.
  - Shared `weightedSum` in `WeightedThreshold/Capacity.lean` and deduplicated `WeightedThreshold/Cut.lean`.
  - Promoted `length_tabulateRows` (`@[simp]`) and `length_of_mem_tabulateRows` in `Rational/Runtime/Determinant.lean`, and `unary_decide_eq` (`@[fun_prop]`) in `Rational/Runtime/Lift.lean`, deleting duplicates in `Lift.lean` and `Point.lean`.
  - Reused `Generator.toReal_realExperiment_pure` and `Generator.toReal_idealExperiment_pure` from `NisanWigderson/Sampling.lean` in `NisanWigderson/Derandomization.lean`.

title: feat(fusion): relate semifilter cover complexity to De Morgan circuit size
body:
Closes #334.

## Summary

This connects Fusion pair-cover complexity to the ordinary size of De Morgan circuits, where negations may appear anywhere. Before this, the cover bounds only covered monotone circuits reading free literals, and only AND gates were counted.

Notation: `ρ(f)` is the unrestricted semifilter pair-cover complexity of `f⁻¹(1)`, taken over the true sets of its `2n` literals.

| Statement | Declaration |
| --- | --- |
| A `t`-pair cover over `m` supplied sets compiles to at most `4(t+1)²(m+t+1)` gates in total, unions and constants included | `Fusion.PairCover.size_toCircuit_le` (`Fusion/Quadratic.lean`) |
| `ρ(f) ≤ C_∧(f) ≤ ρ(f)²` for monotone AND complexity from literals | `Fusion.ecomplexityFrom_literals_bounds`, `Fusion.ecomplexityFrom_literals_le_pairCoverComplexity_sq` |
| `ρ(f) ≤ 2·size(c)` for every De Morgan circuit `c` computing `f`, for any admissible witness class | `Fusion.pairCoverComplexity_le_two_mul_size`, `Fusion.pairCoverComplexity_le_two_mul_complexity` |
| A `t`-pair cover gives a De Morgan circuit of size at most `4(t+1)²(2n+t+1) + n` | `Fusion.PairCover.exists_computes_size_le` |
| `ρ(f)` is finite, `ρ(f) ≤ 2C(f)`, and `C(f) ≤ 4(ρ+1)²(2n+ρ+1) + n`, where `C` is cslib `complexity` over the De Morgan basis | `Fusion.pairCoverComplexity_complexity_bounds` |

**Lower bound.** This reuses the existing dual-rail translation `Monotone.dualRail` (size ×2). The dual-rail inputs are wired from the literals plus one free constant, via `Monotone.literalsRailCircuit`.

**Upper bound.** The quadratic compiler's circuit is mapped into the De Morgan basis with `Circuit.mapOp Monotone.toDeMorgan`. It is then precomposed with the new `Boolean.AltFormula.deMorganLiteralsCircuit`, which adds `n` NOT gates.

## Scope and limitations

- These formalize known correspondences (Cavalar–Oliveira TR25-033 Theorem 24; Goldschlager 1977 for dual rail; Razborov 1989). They are not new lower bounds.
- The size upper bound is `O((t+1)²(n+t))`. That is cubic, not quadratic, in the cover size when `t ≥ n`, because unions are now charged. This is a property of the construction, not a proven lower bound. The bound depends on `n` as well as on `ρ(f)`.
- The upper bounds need unrestricted semifilters. The lower bounds hold for any admissible class, including semi-ultrafilters.

## Files

- New: `Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Fusion/DeMorgan.lean` and `ComplexityTests/FusionDeMorgan.lean`. The tests include a NAND circuit with an internal negation, an explicit empty cover for a projection that exercises the upper bound, an instantiation of the headline theorem, and `#print axioms` guards.
- `Fusion/Quadratic.lean`: total-size lemmas for the quadratic compiler.
- `Boolean/AltFormula.lean`: `deMorganLiteralsCircuit`, the De Morgan counterpart of `literalsCircuit`.
- `Fusion/Boolean.lean`: corrected the docstring that said the NOT-gate translation was missing.
- `ROADMAP.md`: new Fusion milestone row (#334).
- `paper/sections/circuits.tex`: new theorem-index entry, "Semifilter covers and De Morgan circuit size". Links are pinned to `46bde484`, so please merge with a merge commit, not a squash.

## Validation

`scripts/check.sh` passes at `213783db`: build `--wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, test `--wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style` and `checkInitImports`. Headline theorems depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

## Reviews (AI, independent of the authoring session's edits)

Each review below was done by a separate Claude Opus 5.5 subagent with no edit access. None of these is a human or maintainer approval; coordinator review is still requested.

1. **Correctness review of `4746ce93`.** No blocking findings. Should-fix: the "polynomially equivalent" wording overstated the De Morgan size bound. Nits: the test's negation was only on an input; inaccurate test description; the wording of the cubic remark; Razborov's role was not stated. All were resolved in `46bde484`.
2. **cslib-style API review of `4746ce93`.** No blocking findings. Should-fix: the `Fusion.Boolean` import was needlessly public; the literal circuit duplicated `AltFormula.literalsCircuit` and has moved next to it; the dual-rail helpers belonged in the `Monotone` namespace. Nits: naming; separate one-sided lemmas; redundant imports; citation form; import order. All were resolved in `46bde484`.
3. **Fresh review of the fixes plus a theorem-index review of `7a745a18`.** All fixes approved. Index should-fix: an unproved "not in ρ(f) alone" separation claim, and a missing link for `pairCoverComplexity_le_two_mul_complexity`. Nits: docstring reflow, a Main results entry, test comment wording. All were resolved in `213783db`. The reviewer verified every `\declat` link against `46bde484` and every bib key.

The rendered PDF from the **Theorem index PDF** CI workflow still needs to be inspected.

Theorem index assessment: one new entry, described above. Existing Fusion entries are unaffected (the statements of `cost_toCircuit` and `ecomplexityFrom_le_pairCoverComplexity_sq` are unchanged).
