author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent API/style review — reviewer `coordinator-reviewer-wordram430-api-01a1658b`, exact head `e621d62248c3e86225e56b6aa68840c69378216c`. I authored none of this PR. Read-only review of the exact committed Time/Function/Compile/MapOp API, the full changed-file patch, migrated clients/tests, documentation and compatibility scope.

**Findings: none. Approve API/style at this exact revision within the intentional WordRAM redesign.** This is a shared-account AI review verdict, not GitHub platform approval, human editorial approval or integration approval.

Checked:
- `WordRAM/Time.lean:129–320`: width chooses code only through `ℕ → Program B r`, with one fixed register count and one instruction-list bound across all widths in the existential nonuniform predicates. `Uniform` retains a single finite program and permits reading the width. Ordinary `allowed a w`, `encode w a` and `time a w` contracts expose their quantifiers directly; `InputFits` is a separate premise. Positive logarithmic-threshold constants do not silently assert fit. `InO` preserves correctness on every admitted fitting input and makes only the shared runtime estimate eventual.
- `WordRAM/Function.lean:59–125,188–370`: function arguments, encodings and budgets are consistent with the decision API; the function is placed early for `fun_prop`. Raw family contracts and bounded existential classes remain distinct. Fixed-code/family introduction, recoding and basis transfer preserve the same allowed widths and encoded inputs; structured introductions explicitly add final halt. Uniform-to-nonuniform conversion supplies the constant family and its code bound without extra caller bookkeeping.
- Public visibility: all new ordinary API declarations remain inside the exposed public sections, and Function publicly imports the API dependencies it exposes. The real-Archimedean proof import in Time is proof-only; the asymptotics interface is already public through cslib PolynomialBound. No new local-only library module or downstream prefix exception is introduced.
- Migrated clients retain their actual contracts: element distinctness has explicit fixed-program uniform results at `16*(n+1)` instructions plus nonuniform corollaries, and the stack controller retains the 49-instruction uniform certificate. Basis translation preserves code size. Separate automation keys prevent a WordRAM function certificate from becoming a Turing-machine certificate.
- Concrete API clients exercise width-indexed literals and bounded code, fixed code reading width, fitting upper/lower width conditions, width-dependent inputs/budgets, uniform/nonuniform automation, empty/nonfitting cases and all-input asymptotic correctness. The documented encoding/width advice and vacuity boundaries agree with these examples.
- Compatibility assessment compared against base `db7d324dd3d92798e7b35fd75aa223c838b3e2e7`: removed prescribed-width names and the old `ComputableInPolyTime.of_program` are within the stated redesign, with prescribed-width conditions expressible by equality and fixed-program conveniences provided under `Uniform`. The underlying `Program.Answers.mono_width` and operational/fault semantics are retained. I found no lost contract outside that intentional scope. The maintainer-submitted PR and dated UPSTREAM exception expressly describe omission of aliases; I did not locate a separately linked original human instruction, and this review does not extend that exception beyond this redesign.
- Existing authors/license/upstream markers are preserved, including lean-trominoes/Erik Demaine credit. The documentation distinguishes uncharged mathematical encoding and code selection from actual machine execution, does not identify these classes with Turing complexity, and does not claim the motivating data-structure algorithms were proved here. The changed index text reflects the actual uniform/nonuniform and fitting-width contracts; rendered-PDF/provenance acceptance remains separate.

Limits: static source/API/style review only; no source edits or build runs by this reviewer. Correctness review, final CI/current-main validation and actual rendered-artifact checks remain separate.

Checked:
- `Time.lean:130–203,259–320`: family code depends only on width; register count and instruction-list bound are selected outside all input/width quantifiers. Raw family execution contracts intentionally omit a code bound; existential nonuniform classes include it. Uniform conversion uses constant families without changing width conditions or time.

Existing element-distinctness and adaptive-stack programs retain actual input-fit certificates and their instruction bounds.
- `paper/sections/query.tex:86–175,522–546` independently against final definitions/proofs: uniform/nonuniform quantifiers, logarithmic threshold, all-input asymptotic correctness, shared constants, charged halt, element-distinctness promise, basis-transfer scope, and controller bound agree. title: feat(wordram): support word-size-dependent programs and time bounds
body:
## Change

Generalize Word RAM complexity predicates to support arbitrary admissible word sizes, time bounds depending on both input and word size, and programs whose code or constants depend on word size. Nonuniform predicates are primary; explicit `Uniform` predicates provide the common fixed-program case.

Throughout, `n = size a`. The existing helper, defined in `WordRAM/Time.lean`, is:

```lean
def logWidth (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  k * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)
```

Thus `logWidth k n` means `k (⌊log₂ max(1,n)⌋ + 1)`, including `logWidth k 0 = k`.

### Motivation

Standard Word RAM bounds depend on word size:

- Van Emde Boas priority-queue operations take `O(log log U)` time for universe size `U`, giving `O(log w)` when `U = 2^w`. ([van Emde Boas–Kaas–Zijlstra, abstract](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/6885/6885D.pdf))
- Pătraşcu–Thorup's dynamic fusion trees support predecessor, rank, select, insertion, and deletion in `O(log n / log w)` time. These examples motivate retaining both parameters and imposing no monotonicity requirement in `w`. ([Pătraşcu–Thorup 2014](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.3045))

Some results also explicitly permit word-size-dependent constants. Fredman–Willard assume a fixed number of constants depending on word size, supplied with the algorithm without charging for their computation. Hagerup–Miltersen–Pagh formalize this convention as weak nonuniformity; their dictionary constructions use constants not known to be computable in polynomial time in `w`. ([Fredman–Willard 1993, p. 427](https://users.cs.utah.edu/~pandey/courses/cs6968/spring23/papers/fusiontree.pdf#page=4), [Hagerup–Miltersen–Pagh 2001, introduction](https://www.rasmuspagh.net/papers/det-jour.pdf))

Word-size-dependent lookup tables also occur in succinct data structures. Navarro–Sadakane explicitly separate universal tables from the input-dependent representation and account for constructing them once. The present predicates accommodate word-size-dependent code and constants; growing tables still require charged construction or an additional table/advice contract. ([Navarro–Sadakane, Theorem 4.11](https://users.dcc.uchile.cl/~gnavarro/ps/talg12.pdf#page=16))

These results motivate the definitions; this PR does not prove the cited algorithmic bounds.

### Word-size-dependent programs and general contracts

```lean
abbrev WordSizeDependentProgram (B : Basis) (r : ℕ) :=
  ℕ → Program B r
```

`P w` selects a program using only the word size. The register count `r` is fixed. The primary existential predicates additionally require:

```lean
P.BoundedCode := ∃ L, ∀ w, (P w).length ≤ L
```

Thus one instruction-count bound applies to the code at every word size, while literals and instruction choices may depend on `w`.

The contract parameters are ordinary functions:

```lean
encode  : ℕ → α → List ℕ
time    : α → ℕ → ℕ
allowed : α → ℕ → Prop
```

For decision, the program must satisfy:

```lean
∀ a w, allowed a w → InputFits w (encode w a) →
  (P w).Answers w (encode w a) (a ∈ A) (time a w)
```

Function computation analogously requires output `f a` within `time a w` instructions. Instruction counts include the final halt.

Admissible widths use ordinary predicates, for example:

```lean
fun a w => logWidth k (size a) ≤ w
fun a w => lo a ≤ w ∧ w ≤ hi a
fun a w => logWidth 1 (size a) ^ 2 ≤ w
fun a w => w = width a
```

These can express lower bounds, upper bounds, intervals, prescribed widths, or other input-dependent conditions.

### Complexity predicates

| Nonuniform | Uniform |
|---|---|
| `DecidableInTime` | `UniformDecidableInTime` |
| `ComputableInTime` | `UniformComputableInTime` |
| `DecidableInTimeLogWord` | `UniformDecidableInTimeLogWord` |
| `ComputableInTimeLogWord` | `UniformComputableInTimeLogWord` |
| `DecidableInO` | `UniformDecidableInO` |
| `ComputableInO` | `UniformComputableInO` |
| `LinearTime` | `UniformLinearTime` |
| `PolynomialTime` | `UniformPolynomialTime` |
| `ComputableInPolyTime` | `UniformComputableInPolyTime` |

The `LogWord` wrappers package the transdichotomous word-size assumption: there exists a positive constant `k` such that correctness and the time bound hold at every fitting width satisfying:

```lean
logWidth k (size a) ≤ w
```

`LogWord` constrains word size; its time bound may still depend on `w`. The linear and polynomial classes specialize the time bound to a function of input size alone.

The `InO` predicates accept a bound `T n w`. They retain correctness on **every admitted fitting input**, while requiring one positive multiplicative constant and one input-size threshold such that:

```lean
time a w ≤ c * T (size a) w
```

for all sufficiently large admitted inputs and all their admitted widths. Only the runtime estimate is eventual. The constants cannot vary with `w`.

### Convenience for uniform programs

A uniform program is one fixed finite program for every admitted width. It may read `w`, branch on it, and execute for different amounts of time at different widths. The uniform predicates impose no requirement that the program avoid reading word size.

For a flat program, an existing execution proof packages directly:

```lean
-- hp : p.DecidesInTime encode A time allowed
have hu : UniformDecidableInTime B A encode time allowed :=
  ⟨r, p, hp⟩

have h : DecidableInTime B A encode time allowed :=
  hu.decidableInTime
```

The conversion constructs the constant word-size-dependent program and proves its code-length bound automatically. The user supplies neither a family nor a separate bounded-code proof.

Structured programs have direct introduction rules:

- `UniformDecidableInTime.of_code`
- `UniformComputableInTime.of_code`
- `UniformComputableInPolyTime.of_program`
- `UniformComputableInPolyTime.of_code`

The structured-code rules compile one fixed program and charge the final halt. Existing sequential, conditional, and loop execution proofs remain usable, including programs containing the word-size instruction.

Uniform certificates convert to their nonuniform counterparts without weakening the width conditions or increasing the runtime bounds. Conversions are provided for exact time, `LogWord`, asymptotic time, linear time, and polynomial time.

Width-independent encodings and budgets remain simple special cases:

```lean
encode := fun _ a => inputWords a
time   := fun a _ => T (size a)
```

### Supporting results and migrated users

The API supports increasing time bounds, restricting admitted widths, specializing to width schedules, discharging input-fit premises, recoding inputs, and transferring programs along meaning-preserving maps of operation bases. Basis translation preserves executions, instruction counts, and program-length bounds.

Existing fixed-program clients now establish uniform results:

- Element distinctness retains its `16 * (n + 1)` instruction bound and input-fit guarantee, with uniform linear-time theorems and nonuniform corollaries.
- The stack controller retains its uniform polynomial-time certificate and bound of at most 49 instructions.
- `polytime` and `fun_prop` support the appropriate uniform and nonuniform function predicates.

This is an intentional breaking API revision. In-repository users are migrated; deprecated compatibility aliases are omitted as authorized.

### Scope and tests

Input fitting remains a separate premise. A logarithmic bound derived from word-count size alone does not guarantee that every encoded input word fits. Tests include concrete fitting instances and examples exposing vacuous contracts.

Code selection and mathematical input encoding are uncharged. No computability requirement is imposed on selecting width-dependent code, and input-dependent width choices can convey advice. These predicates therefore make no automatic identification with Turing-machine complexity.

Tests cover width-dependent literals, fixed programs reading word size, upper/lower width predicates, width-dependent encodings and instruction budgets, uniform-to-nonuniform conversions, automation, and all-input correctness of asymptotic certificates. The underlying machine's overflow and fault semantics are unchanged.

Both TM2 library files have byte-identical noncomment source. The listed `cfg_label`, `cfg_var`, `cfg_stacks`, `cfg_mk`, `stepAux_polyTime` and `pushBound` names match their actual configuration projections/construction, fixed-statement evaluator and syntactic bound; no declaration moves, renames or compatibility aliases are needed.

This charges initial, intermediate and final stacks without adding a larger bound merely for halted padding. It does not change the adapter's hypotheses or claim linear simulation space.
- `MathlibTM2Space.lean:216–316` supplies a real fixed two-stack Boolean machine on the infinite domain `List Bool`. The first transition peeks without consuming the input, saves exactly its emptiness answer on the other stack, resets the finite variable and enters the clearing state. Each clearing transition pops one symbol; the empty-stack transition resets the variable and halts. Thus `[]` accepts, every nonempty word rejects, and the final label, variable, input stack and one-bit output stack match `haltList`, rather than only an output marginal.

It assumes neither a target PSPACE certificate nor an unproved source correctness field. `empty_bound` proves both stacks are bounded by `xs.length + 1` for every iterate, including initialization and all halted padding. The final client applies the adapter using identity input coding, injective Boolean output coding and a genuine linear source-space bound. This is meaningful adapter/nonvacuity coverage, not a new complexity separation or runtime-lower-bound claim.

title: ci(abstracts): require exact-source Lean success before publication
body:
Abstract PDFs can currently reach the release before Lean CI validates their source commit. This change requires successful **Lean Action CI** for the artifact's exact SHA before any release creation, asset deletion/replacement or release edit. Closes #432.

The gate uses the authoritative workflow-file/ID API, requires this repository's `push` to `main`, selects the latest workflow run and checks its current attempt. It never searches only for green runs. Missing or pending validation can wait up to 20 minutes; failed, cancelled or mismatched evidence denies publication. The run listing and current main are checked again, and each release mutation repeats the gate. Existing artifact provenance, PDF digests, current-main checks and PR review artifacts remain. Only the publication job has release-write permission; its added Actions permission is read-only.

Publication retries download the immutable artifact ID exported by the successful PDF build, so a failed-publish-only rerun does not assume that its new attempt number produced another artifact. No second Lean build is started by the gate.

Validation at exact tree `57aa48eba0aed825d0c9b4cc9a210c54b6a88c27` (public head `4687c9c9c1948b4b6d57d4d9d856b71724ccbf67`, identical to clean private checkpoint `a6bf96e4`):

- All **67 Python tests** pass without skips, including 18 new policy/workflow regressions. They cover wrong SHA/workflow/repository/event/branch, stale green runs/attempts, pagination, unsuccessful conclusions, missing/pending completion/timeout and API errors. The real publication shell, provenance verifier and gate execute against a fake GitHub process boundary; each release mutation is independently blocked when validation is denied.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/abstracts.yml` passes.
- Catalogue selection (12 abstracts/16 headlines), documentation configuration, hygiene and diff checks pass.
- No Lean source or abstract/bridge/catalogue semantic input changes, so no duplicate local six-gate Lean run. Fresh PR CI remains a separate check.

**Abstract impact:** none on selected definitions, statements, bounds, selection or rendered content; this changes release eligibility only. No obsolete paper artifacts are generated or required.

**Limits and review:** GitHub's API checks and release writes are not one atomic transaction. A concurrent main update or rerun can still occur after a check; every subsequent mutation rechecks, but an already-started mutation cannot be rolled back atomically with CI state. Independent exact-revision workflow/security [review by worker_time408](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6354294869) and [coordinator review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6354337252) approve the exact source/tree with no findings. Main-only publication cannot run in PR CI: the postmerge audit must verify actual Lean-success-before-write ordering, released provenance/source/digests and publication retry behavior. Mocked policy tests and PR artifact generation are not that end-to-end publication claim.

**Sources and AI:** addresses the two codebase reviews supplied by Samuel and recorded in #432. Implementation follows the [workflow-run REST API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs), [run/attempt semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables), [CLI GET/pagination](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api) and [immutable artifact-ID interface](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/tree/v4). OpenAI Codex worker `worker-codex-abstract-ci432-01a1658b` implemented the workflow, helper, tests and focused documentation. Original renderer/model source credit is unchanged. No author approval or merge is implied.

Adding this PR produces exact combined tree `5e3be0601e9f02d8caf9e919f7f106641fcf92ee`, already validated with all six strict gates and all 67 Python tests ([combined record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6354368913)). Materializing the connector download is DNS-blocked, so no independent new archive-byte or rendered-page audit is claimed. No source head changes or unresolved source-review findings. See [prior coordinator checkpoint](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6355888246).

title: feat(wordram): undefined operations fault, an exact basis, and a formal abstract
body:
## Change

This PR has two parts: (1) word-RAM operations can be undefined, and an undefined operation
faults, with a new basis `Basis.exact`; (2) a formal abstract of the word RAM over that basis.

### Part 1: undefined operations fault, and an exact basis

A word-RAM operation can now be undefined, and an undefined operation faults. `Basis.exact` is a
basis whose operations fault on subtraction below zero and on division or remainder by zero.

Why: until now every basis had to give every operation a value, so no basis could make
subtraction below zero or division by zero an error. Programs over the standard basis go on with
`0` for `x - y` when `y > x`, `0` for `x / 0` and `x` for `x % 0`. With this change a basis can
leave such a value undefined, and the machine treats it like overflow: the run faults and gives no
answer. Over `Basis.exact`, a run that succeeds never relies on these conventions, just as it
never relies on wrap-around.

Samuel Schlesinger and Erik Demaine agreed to this change before this PR was opened.

What changes (`Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/`):

- `Basis.interp : ℕ → (f : Op) → (Fin (Arity f) → ℕ) → Option ℕ`. `none` means undefined.
- The field `interp_eq_of_not_readsWidth` becomes `interp_mono_of_not_readsWidth`: an operation
  that does not read the word size keeps each value that fits a word at every larger word size.
  The old field said the value (now an `Option`) is the same at every word size. `Basis.exact`
  would meet it too; the new field is weaker and is exactly what `Executes.mono_width` needs. It
  also admits operations that are undefined when their value does not fit the word, which the old
  field would exclude. `Executes.mono_width` still holds for every basis, with the same
  statement. The old name stays as a deprecated alias.
- `Basis.Hom.preserves` is now an explicit equation. It used `Signature.Hom.Preserves`, whose
  interpretations take values in the same type as their arguments; that does not fit
  `Option`-valued operations.
- `Op.eval_alu`: `(Op.alu f d args).eval w x = (B.interp w f (x.regs ∘ args)).bind (x.put w d)`.
  `Exec.alu` and `ExecWithin.alu` take `hf : B.interp w f (x.regs ∘ args) = some v` and
  `Fits w v`. New lemma `Op.eval_alu_eq_some`.
- New: `BinOp.evalExact`, `StandardOp.evalExact`, `Basis.exact` with its `simp` lemmas, and
  `Op.exactBin`, `Op.exactWidth` with `Op.eval_exactBin`, `Op.eval_exactWidth`.
- `Basis.standard`, `Basis.additive` and `Basis.arithmetic` keep their values (now wrapped in
  `some`): truncated subtraction and Lean's `x / 0 = 0`, `x % 0 = x`. Their programs keep the
  same runtime behaviour; callers of the changed APIs (for example `Exec.alu` and
  `ExecWithin.alu`, which now take `hf`) may need proof updates.
- `Generic.lean`, `MapOp.lean`, `Structured.lean`, `Trace.lean`: proofs adapted. No other file
  needed a change, including the code of #430.
- Module docstrings (`Basis.lean`, `Defs.lean`) record the deviation from the source,
  [edemaine/lean-trominoes](https://github.com/edemaine/lean-trominoes) @6d5b36c1: there, a
  negative difference or a zero divisor is not rejected as such. Subtraction is on signed words,
  and division and remainder by zero follow Lean's integer conventions `x / 0 = 0`, `x % 0 = x`
  (`LeanTrominoes/ComplexityAbstract.lean`, lines 129–139); only the usual check that the result
  fits a signed word applies (lines 153–154, 176–177). In `Basis.exact` these cases fault.
  Source credit and `Authors:` lines are unchanged.
- `ComplexityTests/WordRAMBasis.lean`: the exact basis faults on `3 - 5`, `7 / 0` and `7 % 0`
  where the standard basis gives `0`, `0` and `7`; it computes `5 - 3` and `7 / 2`; and
  `Executes.mono_width` applies to an exact-basis program.
- `UPSTREAM.md` records the API change under "Word-RAM bases with undefined values".

### Part 2: a formal abstract of the exact word RAM

- `ComplexityTests/Abstracts/WordRAMAbstract.lean` restates the machine and the decision
  definitions locally: ten binary operations with exact values (`none` where undefined), ten
  instructions, states, one step, halting runs with their length, the start state, and decision in
  time `T` from a word-size threshold on. Only its last section (`OutcomeAgrees`, `Same` and the
  two theorems) refers to the library's word RAM. Each theorem is proved by one call into the
  bridge:
  - `runsAgree r`: every program of the abstract runs alike with some
    `Cslib.WordRAM.Program .exact r`, and conversely (same one-step outcomes, same halting runs
    with the same output and length).
  - `decidableInTime_iff`: `DecidableInTime A encode T bits` of the abstract is equivalent to
    `Cslib.WordRAM.UniformDecidableInTime .exact A (fun _ => encode) (fun a _ => T a)
    (fun a w => bits a ≤ w)`.
- `ComplexityTests/Abstracts/WordRAMBridge.lean` proves both, following the `Presentation` /
  `Laws` pattern of the TQBF bridge: the program translation is instruction by instruction, and
  surjective in both directions.
- `#check_abstract` allows the modules `Defs`, `Basis` and `Time` of
  `Complexity/Computability/WordRAM`. These are the library's word RAM, the model that the
  theorems compare against, and only the last section uses them.
- `scripts/abstract_to_tex.py` maps `ₖ`, which the abstract's docs use, with a test sample.

Scope that the abstract states: `decidableInTime_iff` covers one fixed program at every word size
from a threshold on, with encodings and times that do not depend on the word size. It does not
cover the nonuniform `Cslib.WordRAM.DecidableInTime` or classes built on it, nor word-size
dependent encodings or time bounds. The abstract's `DecidableInTime` corresponds to the library's
`UniformDecidableInTime`, not to the library definition of the same name; the abstract keeps its
name because it predates the uniform/nonuniform split and was read under it.

Some prose is in both a section doc and a declaration doc comment. The section docs carry the
explanation of a write-up that was reviewed with these definitions, and are kept close to it.

The abstract is a port of a reading abstract on our fork,
`Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Abstract.lean` with its bridge `AbstractBridge.lean`, at
[orbitingflea/complexitylib2@17b72db3](https://github.com/orbitingflea/complexitylib2/tree/17b72db3).
All definitions keep their names, bodies and doc comments. The differences, with their reasons:

1. No `module`, `public import` or `@[expose] public section`: upstream `ComplexityTests` files
   are not modules.
2. The namespace is `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.WordRAMAbstract` (the layout of the other
   abstracts).
3. The imports are `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.Check` and `WordRAMBridge`: the abstract imports its
   bridge and runs `#check_abstract`, as the other abstracts do.
4. The marker is `-- upstream: local-only (formal abstract tests)`, as in the other abstracts; it
   was `-- upstream: local-only (reading abstract …)`.
5. Module doc: the sentence that the file imports only Mathlib and `Cslib.Init` is removed, since
   it now imports its bridge. A trust paragraph is added, as `.agents/skills/lean-abstract/SKILL.md`
   asks: a reader only needs to inspect the definitions and statements, Lean checks the proofs
   through the bridge, and `#check_abstract` audits the dependency boundary. It also names the
   three axioms the proofs use.
6. A new `## References` section (CLRS, Fredman–Willard, the tromino formalization), for source
   credit: CSLib `CODESTYLE.md:95` asks to "please reference the resource in your documentation".
7. The prose of the fork's hand-written section is now in `/-! ## … -/` section docs, so that the
   rendered abstract carries it. The bullets on `step` became sentences, since the renderer shows
   no lists in section docs.
8. `OutcomeAgrees`, `Same`, `runsAgree` and `decidableInTime_iff` moved from the bridge into the
   abstract, as in the other abstracts:
   - library names have the full `Cslib.WordRAM.` prefix, since no `open` is allowed;
   - each proof gives the `Presentation` literal inline, since `#check_abstract` rejects a shared
     definition. The literal is an anonymous constructor in the order of the fields (three lines),
     so the last section, from `## Main theorems`, is 72 lines. One auxiliary theorem that proves
     both statements from one literal is also legal, but that section is then 80 lines;
   - the `Laws` are proved by `constructor <;> simp_all [step, Halts, OutcomeAgrees, AluOp.eval]`,
     not `rfl`, since the step laws have hypotheses.
9. The file ends with the audit, `#check_abstract … allowing [Defs, Basis, Time]` pinned by
   `#guard_msgs`, as in the other abstracts.
10. The right side of `decidableInTime_iff` is `Cslib.WordRAM.UniformDecidableInTime .exact …`:
    since #430, the library's `DecidableInTime` is nonuniform. The theorem doc names what it does
    not cover. The abstract keeps its own name `DecidableInTime`, for the reason above.
11. The "Main theorems" prose speaks of "this file" and of names with the prefix
    `Cslib.WordRAM.`, since there is no `Abstract.` prefix now.
12. Kept: the theorem's `{α : Type u}` with `universe u`, as in the old bridge; the definitions
    keep `Type*`, as in the old abstract.

## Validation and review

Tested source revision: `d19d8508`. The public head `c3c38afa267ed9ce9dbe92f21c82864a11c58684` adds only an empty CI-rerun commit and has the identical source tree; independent coordinator review [5626159204](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/442#pullrequestreview-5626159204) verifies that identity, the exact-head CI logs, and all six locally rendered model-abstract pages. Merged with commit `1dc68abee2e1aafe86f6cd5f154a10ae380c41af`. Part 1 is `b64602fa` (two commits on upstream
`main` at `403ea745`, #439) and the doc fixes of `bbd06793`; part 2 is the three commits between
them and `d19d8508`.

- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 scripts/check.sh`: all six checks passed (`build --wfail --iofail`,
  `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`).
- `lake build`: passed.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py`: `All hygiene checks passed.`
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: `Catalogue selects 12 abstracts and 16 headline
  theorems.`
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 49 tests, OK.
- The abstract's audit, pinned by `#guard_msgs`: `abstract audit passed for
  ComplexityTests.Abstracts.WordRAMAbstract: 234 root declarations, 338 dependencies checked`.
- `#print axioms`:
  - `runsAgree` and `decidableInTime_iff`: `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
  - Part 1, checked at `b64602fa`: `Executes.mono_width`, `Op.eval_mono_width`,
    `Op.eval_alu_eq_some`, `Exec.alu`, `ExecWithin.alu`, `Op.eval_exactBin`, `Op.eval_exactWidth`
    and the `Basis.exact_*` lemmas depend on `[propext]`; `executes_mapOp_iff` and
    `Op.eval_toGeneric` on `[propext, Quot.sound]`; `Basis.Hom.interp_map` on none. The test
    suite's axiom audit passed.

Independent review of part 1: Codex (OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning effort high), a read-only
review of the diff at `c90e9586` against the request. Verdict: pass, with no blocker or major
finding. Two minor findings, both fixed in `b64602fa`:

1. The docstrings said the source does not fault on a negative difference or a zero divisor. It
   still faults when the signed result does not fit a word (at width 4, `-8 - 1 = -9` faults).
   They now say the source does not reject these cases as such, and its signed-range check still
   applies.
2. This description said the programs and proofs of the existing bases run as before. Proofs that
   call `Exec.alu` or `ExecWithin.alu` now need the extra `hf` argument; the text now says so.

Coordinator review of part 1: Samuel Schlesinger's Codex review of `b64602fa` (review 5623184291),
verdict approve, with two nonblocking doc nits, both fixed in `bbd06793`.

Independent reviews of part 2:

- Claude Opus 5.5 (a separate agent) reviewed the abstract, the bridge and the script change in
  the working tree before `9b560414`. It found no soundness problem. Its findings and the fixes,
  all in `9b560414`:
  - the docs said the theorem equates the library's `DecidableInTime`: now "uniform decidability
    (`UniformDecidableInTime`)", and the theorem doc names what is not covered;
  - the `#check_abstract` description left out upstream CSLib and placed the library modules
    wrongly: fixed;
  - no source credit: a References section now cites CLRS, Fredman–Willard and the tromino
    formalization, as `WordRAM/Time.lean` does;
  - three dropped phrases restored; the `Laws` discharge is one `simp_all` call; the bridge uses
    `Type*` instead of a named universe, and `executes_succ_iff` holds for any basis.
- Codex (OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning effort high), round 1, a read-only review at `9b560414`.
  Verdict: fail. Findings on this PR and their resolution:
  - Major: `UPSTREAM.md` had no record of the `Option`-valued bases. Fixed in `b40c40fe`; the
    entry was checked against `b64602fa` (the deprecated alias has the new signature, and
    `Op.eval_alu` propagates an undefined value before the word check).
  - The description said that no class definition or construction of a result is allowed, called
    TQBF and SubsetSum model abstracts, and said no workflow runs for this abstract. All three
    were wrong; this text replaces them.
  - The abstract's theorem had changed `{α : Type u}` to `{α : Type*}`, which no upstream rule
    asks for. `Type u` is restored in `9b995dc5`.
  - The other findings were about files outside this PR.
- Codex, round 2, at `9b995dc5`. Verdict: fail, on three minor doc points: this description had
  no full list of the differences from the fork's abstract (now above), it gave `Op.eval_alu`
  without `x.regs ∘` (now the exact equation), and a fork-only README misdescribed the catalogue
  workflow (fixed on the fork).
- Codex, round 3, at `9b995dc5`: pass, no findings.
- Codex, round 4, at `bbd06793`, after the fixes for the coordinator review: pass, no findings.
- Codex, round 5, at `d19d8508` (only the two proof bodies change): pass, no findings; source
  inspection, field order checked against `WordRAMBridge.Presentation`.
- Each Codex round was an independent agent (OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning effort high), reading
  only.
- No human review yet: the coordinator review of part 1 above was a Codex review.

Limitations:

- `Basis.standard` is unchanged, so programs over it still see truncated subtraction and Lean's
  division by zero. No simulation between `Basis.exact` and `Basis.standard` is proved, and there
  is no `Basis.Hom` between them (their values differ).
- The `ram_eval` tactic's simp set has the standard-basis lemmas only; exact-basis programs are
  checked here with `run` and `decide`.
- The deprecated alias `Basis.interp_eq_of_not_readsWidth` points to the new field, whose
  statement differs; code that used the old field must be updated.

## Headline abstracts

- Affected abstracts/catalogue entries, or reason the selection is unaffected: no catalogue entry
  is added, and no existing entry is affected. No entry of `abstracts/catalogue.json` is about
  the word RAM, and no other `*Abstract.lean` or `*Bridge.lean` imports a changed module. The new
  abstract states definitions and their equality with the library, with no headline complexity
  theorem, so it is not proposed for the selection.
  **Question for @SamuelSchlesinger:** should a model abstract like this one be listed in
  `abstracts/catalogue.json`?
- Independent abstract review (reviewer, exact source revision, findings/resolutions): the reviews
  of part 2 above: Claude Opus 5.5 on the working tree before `9b560414`, and Codex round 1 at

title: feat(crypto): construct and certify homomorphic refresh
body:
Construct Gentry's identity and NAND refresh from bit encryption, evaluation, and actual decryption circuits. Correctness covers every well-sized old ciphertext, including outputs of earlier evaluations, and permits the same encrypted secret key in both NAND input blocks. The refreshed ciphertext keeps the base scheme's fixed width.

This is the first bounded recovery milestone for #322. `Bootstrappable` requires only that the concrete decryption and NAND-augmented circuits belong to the base evaluator's permitted family. Uniform strict-PPT refresh is derived from certificates for the base encryption/evaluation algorithms and uniform decryption-circuit generation. The NAND augmentation itself is constructed in native polynomial time, with exact gate count `2 * size(D) + 2`.

Reusable additions include strict-PPT list traversal with captured inputs, native sequential composition of circuit codes, typed Boolean circuit evaluation with explicit input padding/truncation, and a generic NAND circuit. The three commits separate these prerequisites, the refresh development, and source credit/roadmap updates.

The regression scheme is explicitly insecure. Its fresh ciphertexts have tag false and evaluated ciphertexts have tag true; direct base evaluation on an evaluated encryption of true produces false. Tests prove different-key switching, shared encrypted-key inputs, two successful refreshes, fixed widths, and an actual instance of every refresh-efficiency hypothesis.

The full objective remains open: depth-layered DAG evaluation without tree expansion, its uniform resource bounds, the acyclic key-chain IND-CPA reduction, and the separately assumed circular-security fixed-key result. This milestone uses perfect correctness and fixed-width padded representations; it establishes no concrete LWE scheme or encryption-security theorem. Mathematical source: [Craig Gentry, STOC 2009, §§1–2](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/hits09/gentry-homomorphic-encryption.pdf), credited in `references.bib`.

title: refactor(hierarchy): decouple the space hierarchy from the time hierarchy
body:
Closes #415 (from the #404 survey).

## Summary
This moves generic helpers out of the time-hierarchy module. No full names or statements change, so no aliases are needed.
- `Turing.MultiTapeTM.length_unframe_le` → `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Encodings/Frame.lean`
- `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesInTimeAndSpace.runFrom_of_le` → `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Run.lean`. It keeps the same implicit order by using that file's section variables. It is now reused in `not_computableInTimeAndSpace_diagonal` (`Classes/Hierarchy.lean`), replacing an inlined copy of its proof.
- `Cslib.Complexity.Diagonal.shortDesc`, `shortDesc_eq_decide` and `computableTidilyInO_shortDesc` → a new `Classes/Hierarchy/ShortDesc.lean` (code by Samuel Schlesinger; credit kept).
  - **This differs from the issue text,** which proposed `Classes/Hierarchy.lean`. A separate leaf module avoids adding `Classes/Constructible` to the import closure of `Classes/Hierarchy.lean`. That file is imported by Ladner/PolyTime, Parameterized/Kernelization and several tests.
- `Hierarchy/Space.lean` and `Hierarchy/SpaceUniversal.lean` no longer import `Hierarchy/Time`, even transitively. SpaceUniversal imports `Classes/Constructible` instead, which cuts its closure from 196 to 83 Complexity modules.

**Formal abstracts: no impact.** The selected catalogue contains no hierarchy headline; this refactor preserves declaration names, statements, hypotheses and bounds. No selected abstract or bridge changes.

- `Hierarchy/Time.lean` and `Hierarchy/Space.lean` `public import` `MultiTape/Run`, so `runFrom_of_le` remains reachable from clients that import only one of them, as before the move (must-fix from the preliminary review on #415). `Hierarchy/Space` no longer re-exports the time hierarchy theorem module; that is the intended decoupling.

## Validation
- Rebased onto main `403ea745`.
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates pass at the head `7deddbb4`.
- A scratch client importing only `Hierarchy/Time` resolves the four declarations the reviewer listed:
  - `runFrom_of_le`
  - `length_unframe_le`
  - `shortDesc`
  - `computableTidilyInO_shortDesc`
- Independent AI review of `fb32c717`: **APPROVE**. It checked:
  - that names, statements and implicit binder order are identical against `origin/main`;
  - that nothing is lost or duplicated;
  - the template and credit of the new file;
  - the import graph has no cycles;
  - the vendored-file rules.
  Its import-order nit is applied in `c52f3687`. The final `public import` delta in `7deddbb4` is independently approved by coordinator reviewer `review-hierarchy-20261023`; the review verifies unchanged declarations/binder order, public reachability, the smaller Space/SpaceUniversal import closures, and the existing minimal-import client in successful exact-head CI.

title: feat(crypto): certify Gentry key chains and layered evaluation
body:
Construct an actual acyclic key-chain sampler and a public evaluator for consecutive-layer Boolean programs. For L scheduled layers the sampler generates L + 1 independent key pairs and L encrypted links. Every supported evaluation of a well-formed program preserves the exact wire count, ciphertext width, and plaintext values under the next key; intermediate ciphertexts need not be fresh.

The complete sampler and evaluator have native uniform strict-PPT certificates. Binary wire indices are handled without unary expansion. Every node branch truncates at the generated base decryption circuit's arity: this leaves valid outputs unchanged and bounds the loop on malformed public inputs too. Runtime inputs contain only public keys, encrypted links, ciphertexts and the program.

This completes the bounded milestone in #447 and advances #322. General-circuit conversion with size/depth bounds, a leveled encryption interface normalizing the final key for shorter circuits, the acyclic IND-CPA reduction, and circular-security bootstrapping remain open. This is neither a concrete LWE scheme nor an encryption-security theorem.

Tests use a deliberately insecure tagged scheme whose base evaluator rejects evaluated ciphertexts. They check two key transitions with a repeated key value, shared/repeated wires, constants mixed with copies, zero layers, empty inputs/layers, an asymmetric link-direction fixture, actual truncation of an oversized malformed encryption, disagreeing invalid-index defaults, and inhabitants of every native efficiency premise.

title: feat(crypto): compile circuits for layered homomorphic evaluation
body:
Ordinary shared Boolean circuits can now use the encrypted layered evaluator directly. The compiler computes the actual wire-depth table, emits exactly two layers per designated-output depth, and retains ordered output selection as wiring. The encrypted adapter executes that compiler and evaluator along the generated key chain.

Closes #455. This completes the compiler milestone of #322; the full Gentry objective remains open.

For a typed De Morgan circuit with n inputs, s stored gates, m outputs and depth d, the proofs establish:
- Exactly 2d consecutive NAND/copy/constant layers, each of width n + 3s; dead gates do not inflate the output depth.
- Well-formed references, valid final output selection, and preservation of the original circuit semantics, including zero-depth wiring and repeated outputs.
- A complete encoded-size bound: writing W = n + 3s and B = log2 W + 1, the emitted artifact has at most 4d(2W(6B + 21) + 1) + m(2B + 1) + 1 bits.
- Uniform native polynomial-time compilation on arbitrary raw code, charging binary references, unary depth-table entries, all framing, and output selection.
- Correct ordinary-circuit encrypted evaluation on every supported generated chain of 2d + 1 keys, retaining the base ciphertext width. Its strict PPT certificate composes the actual compiler, layered evaluator, and output selector.

Correctness is stated for typed circuits. Malformed raw codes have total polynomial-time behavior but need not preserve another raw interpreter's fallback semantics; a negative regression documents that boundary. Runtime statements do not assume validity, correctness, or an externally supplied depth/runtime certificate.

The final key still depends on actual depth. A depth-budgeted scheme with a common final key, the acyclic IND-CPA reduction, and the additional circular-security theorem remain open. This does not construct a concrete LWE scheme or prove encryption security.

Validation on tree `575b0aaa4196680d28115a36c23fb4bfd600a934`:
- All six AGENTS gates passed: strict build, import aggregation, strict tests, lint, style, and Init imports. The initial strict test run caught seven unguarded axiom messages; a separate fix adds exact guards and the full strict test rerun passed.
- Hygiene, abstract catalogue check, and diff whitespace check passed.
- Compiler regressions cover dead gates, no outputs, no-input constants, shared OR/AND/NOT gates, skipped depths, repeated outputs, and huge malformed binary indices.
- The explicitly insecure tagged-scheme fixture exercises actual refresh: generated-chain OR correctness, the exact final ciphertext distribution, and depth-zero permutation/duplication under the original key. Named axiom guards allow only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Independent reviews at published head `8c58aef9e28a87adaaeb7dcd76ac83bd421bb49f`:
- `/root/library_map`: API/style, documentation, tests and catalogue assessment — approve.
- `/root/refactor_plan_review`: mathematical correctness, runtime bounds and catalogue assessment — approve.
- Both identified the missing axiom guards at the earlier revision, reviewed the separate correction, and verified the published tree against the corrected local revision. These are independent AI review verdicts, not platform or human maintainer approvals.

Catalogue assessment: selected HILL/GGM abstracts and bridges are unchanged. No full-FHE abstract is introduced; ROADMAP records the bounded result and remaining obligations. There are no changed abstract pages requiring PDF review.

Sources: Gentry, *Fully homomorphic encryption using ideal lattices* (2009), Section 2; Arora and Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach* (2009), Section 6.1; existing cslib/Mathlib APIs. AI-assisted implementation by Codex `/root` and `/root/maintenance_audit`, under Samuel Schlesinger. The reviewers did not author the changes.

Ready for coordinator review and integration after current CI and maintainer requirements. The author has not approved or merged this PR.

# Independent final committed-revision review for #453

No unresolved source blocker.** This reconciles the five prior independent reports against the final committed sources. The parent owns the pending final six gates.

## Identity and method

Base: `403ea745ab0e866c9f62f18abc2fd46fdddf4f2f`. Pinned cslib: `1ade21e1bd8d03a4ca9f6f632a15c032926054f7`. Toolchain: `leanprover/lean4:v4.36.0-rc1`.

Their path set exactly equals the base-to-HEAD changed path set. V4 manifest SHA256: `aa48102ec1a290c750bccd04d8383e55722d23808f01ecb7377fe75a4c079bfe`. The tracked tree was clean. I inspected final definitions, statements, native control and concrete clients, and independently generated the complete v1-to-final Lean diff from actual `.lake/nl-v1-source-preimages/` files. Each preimage matches its original manifest SHA256 AND raw blob. Of 31 v1 Lean paths, 21 are byte-identical, two are LF-only, and eight have the explicit text deltas below. No source, GitHub content, commit, ref, Git object, main checkout or build/cache configuration was edited. No Lake build, cache repair, global gate or compiler output write was requested. The only intentional write is this ignored report. No additional agents were spawned.

## Actual theorem, semantics and limits

`MultiTapeNTM.exists_decidesInLogSpace_compl` takes one native binary NTM, fixed tape count, finite control, arbitrary embedding `enc : α ↪ List Bool`, language A and constant c. Its premise is actual recognition of A and an every-prefix native visited-work-cell bound `c * (log2 |enc a| + 1)`. It constructs one fixed finite-state binary native NTM, tape count and c' deciding A's complement on the SAME encoding, with the same every-prefix space convention and a common finite native clock for all branches on each encoded instance. No source termination premise occurs. `compl_mem_NL`, double complementation and `NL_eq_coNL` prove closure/equality for the existing native class; `mem_NL_of_recognizesInSpace` removes the recognizer/decider distinction at logarithmic space.

I reread Accepts/RecognizesInSpace/DecidesInSpace/NL and upstream RunsInSpace/RunPath.space/RunsInTime. Acceptance is existence of a halted path outputting exactly `[true]`. Space sums distinct visited work-head positions over tapes on EVERY prefix; read-only input and append-only output are uncharged. RunsInTime permits short stuck paths, but the constructed driver has `Native.exists_step`, so that concession does not weaken its actual halting guarantee.

This is the conventional native NL-complement endpoint under these explicit multitape/encoding conventions. The endpoint supplies actual native query/next/halt/verdict certificates, exact graph correspondence, every-replay storage and a common abstract clock to the proved compiler. No graph-only endpoint or assumed compiler-correctness conclusion replaces the native witness.

Limits: contracts concern encoded instances; no computable inverse or decidable encoding range is assumed, and the statement promises no behavior outside that range. Classical enumeration fixes finite tables/constants once, independently of runtime input. This is existential machine construction, not effective extraction from an arbitrary Lean transition predicate. No general space-constructible complementation theorem or compiler polynomial-time bound is asserted. Ghost clocks/maxima and replay lists are proof data, not stored state.

The final controller still has ten binary registers, two flags and ten phases. Included candidates require streamed padded walks; ordered selection and checked census equality force exhaustiveness. The initial census is proved. `advance` checks bounded storage and decreasing rank, rejecting dishonest/malformed live transitions. The three-index BinaryExtension and constructor-local binders retain the approved correction; width zero and counts equal to N keep their intended meanings.

The compact graph still represents actual reachable native views. IDs exclude the input word, request one original symbol, preserve boundaries/movement, summarize output as empty/exactly-true/rejecting and guard overflow. Source prefix-space supplies fitting configurations without a clock. Malformed unrelated IDs cannot introduce spurious reachable acceptance.

Runtime bootstraps with n+1 queries including an empty-input end marker, then executes the controller. Its invariant covers all choice prefixes, rejecting and post-halting included; `length_run_le` bounds encoded storage by `storageConstant k D * (log2 n + 1)`. `runtimeNext_budget` composes actual graph/advance routines. `sizeUnary_inSpace` emits one bit per digit of binary N, rather than expanding N in unary.

I reinspected Native.State/instruction/table, exists_routines and compiler space/time/acceptance proofs. Native control is the finite sum of initializer, two pass routines, finalizer and choose/check routing states. Only a boundary choice selects a pass; subsequent coins cannot change that deterministic pass. Abstract state is framed on work tapes. Tidy routines reset work origins, giving the SAME workspace window across arbitrarily many passes and every internal prefix; `k*(2*s+1)` is absorbed into a constant times the positive budget. Remaining abstract steps give a decreasing ghost rank; finite routine runs and maxima over both choices yield a common native clock. Forward/reverse simulations preserve exactly existential acceptance, including initially halted abstract states.

## Complete delta and findings reconciliation

1. Core explicit binders, including BinaryExtension indices, are the independently approved v1 content; only the root's line endings changed. No new hypothesis or restriction.
2. Graph Basic names/documents the existing anonymous action Fintype as `instFintypeActionBool`; its type/body are unchanged.

I inspected Mathlib's actual natural-number recursion: it is exactly the old recursion for EVERY base/list. At base zero it returns the head (zero for empty); at base one it returns the sum. Recovery/capacity still require positive B; at B=1 bounded digits are all zero and the claims remain true. Unrestricted base-one injectivity is not asserted. Every hunk was inspected in context. No definition, public statement, hypothesis, quantitative bound or import changes.
5. Query Routines adds ten field docstrings. Together with the action-instance name/doc, these account for the 12 lint findings. The heartbeat reason is now on the SAME LINE after `in`, before the declaration docstring. Mathlib's actual linter reads `in`'s trailing comments; this resolves the earlier warning, and static hygiene passes. The prior independent focused inline probe passed. No heartbeat limit change or linter disabling.
6. Actual hash-verified v1 preimages prove the previously uncertain `synthInstance.maxSize 1024` inside finiteP was ALREADY in v1. It is not an unreviewed late delta. The Routines construction otherwise stays unchanged.
7. Native now says two routing states, matching choose/check; Routines says finalizer instead of final_specr. Both earlier typo notes are resolved.

title: feat(logspace): prove NL = coNL
body:
## Change

Prove native `NL = coNL` for every injective instance encoding. Closes #453. `MultiTapeNTM.exists_decidesInLogSpace_compl` turns an all-prefix logarithmic-space recognizer into a complement decider with logarithmic visited work-cell space and a common finite halting bound for every branch. Source branches may loop; input and write-only output follow the existing uncharged convention.

The construction checks streaming inductive-counting certificates without storing a path or reachable set, enumerates compact native configuration IDs with actual read-only input queries, and compiles binary choices through finite native control and common-origin tidy routines. It also proves that logarithmic-space recognizers and the existing all-branches-halting `NL` definition give the same class. General space-constructible complementation is outside this result.

Reusable pieces include the bounded counting controller, compact configuration graph and native binary-choice query-machine compiler. Tests cover singleton/cyclic/disconnected graphs, invalid guesses and census mismatches, branching and initially halted compiler instances, a genuinely looping zero-tape source, empty input and all-prefix bounds. Sources are Immerman (1988), Szelepcsényi (1987) and Sipser §8.6; adapted native calculus retains Christian Reitwiessner and Samuel Schlesinger credit.

## Validation and review

Frozen head: `5c8198c81ea5c2812f5c69b7c5aa11b9a969ad36`.

All six gates passed in a fresh serial run of `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2 bash scripts/check.sh`: strict build, `mk_all --check`, strict tests, `lint`, `lint-style` and `checkInitImports`. Scoped hygiene, static catalogue validation and documentation consistency also pass. The test suite audits all imported library declarations and guards the native/class headline axioms. [Exact validation, environment and recovery record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/465#issuecomment-6363476251).

Independent nonauthor review **approves this exact commit** for mathematical correctness and cslib API/style. All 35 source identities, earlier review scopes and final deltas are reconciled in the [complete review record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/465#issuecomment-6363460407). It records actual theorem semantics, limitations, concrete nonvacuity cases, resolved findings and the distinction between reviewer checks and author validation. This is not platform or maintainer approval.

The generic radix API extraction remains a [nonblocking follow-up in #404](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/404#issuecomment-6363294352); current code reuses Mathlib's `Nat.ofDigits`. The native theorem and compiler are fully constructed; no native realization premise remains as a hypothesis. Maintainer approval and integration remain separate.

No selected abstract, bridge or catalogue entry changes. Existing class/model definitions are preserved; the adjacent `LogSpace` change is documentation. title: feat(crypto): prove IND-CPA for acyclic leveled encryption
body:
## Change

Prove IND-CPA security for the actual serialized acyclic leveled scheme constructed in #469. The adversary sees the complete public key, including encrypted key links, before choosing its two challenge messages, and carries arbitrary polynomial saved state into its second stage.

`Leveled.indCPA_scheme` assumes base IND-CPA, native uniform polynomial-time key generation and encryption, a fixed supported secret-key length at each security parameter, and an efficiently computed unary depth budget. Explicit reductions replace links in reverse order and bits in forward order, then simulate the zero-link challenge using a base adversary. The executable hybrid capacity comes from the key-generator certificate; the semantic secret-width function need not be computable.

Also expose indistinguishability of the serialized public artifact and assemble correctness, budget-independent polynomial secret/ciphertext widths, and security for the same constructed scheme in `Leveled.correct_fixedWidth_indCPA`. The latter additionally uses the existing base correctness, fixed-width and bootstrappable decryption-circuit hypotheses. Evaluator efficiency remains the separate native theorem with its stated base-evaluator premise.

This is qualitative single-challenge security, without a claim to Gentry's exact concrete loss. Fixed-key circular-security FHE, a concrete LWE scheme, and arbitrary reuse of evaluated wrapper ciphertexts remain outside this milestone. #322 stays open.

Sources: [Craig Gentry (2009), Section 2, Theorems 3–4](https://doi.org/10.1145/1536414.1536440); [Dan Boneh and Victor Shoup (2023), Section 11.2](https://crypto.stanford.edu/~dabo/cryptobook/BonehShoup_0_6.pdf).

Closes #472.

## Validation and review

- All six `scripts/check.sh` gates pass at `4c1fcab82e8f21418c9b394f6830b8e89b50e97b` (tree `45ccc893b643c5d0236ea18819b72f9a8557c453`): strict build, aggregate check, strict tests, lint, style and Init imports. Hygiene and whitespace checks pass.
- Regressions cover leaking encryption, correlated repeated keys and retained nonces, adaptive messages/saved state, zero depth and empty secrets, padded coordinates, malformed saved-state decoding, and native nonconstant budgets. Named axiom guards cover the headline security and assembly theorems.
- The shared list-slicing certificates support the hybrid reductions and replace the duplicate private Nisan–Wigderson helper without changing its clients.
- Independent API, correctness and documentation review: `/root/library_map` approves the exact commit above; `/root/refactor_plan_review` independently reviewed the generic game, key-chain reductions, native helpers and regressions. A proof-only import nit and the duplicate-helper integration failure were fixed and reviewed. No outstanding findings. These are AI reviews, not platform or human approval.
- Local and published commit/tree match. Validation used an isolated checkout based on the merged #469 head; current-main integration and CI remain coordinator checks.

## Headline abstracts

- No selected abstract or catalogue entry changes: the current HILL/GGM cryptography selection is unaffected. This conditional construction milestone is documented in `ROADMAP.md`.
- `/root/library_map` independently confirmed that no-impact assessment against the exact final commit.
- Abstract sources and rendering are unchanged; no new PDF artifact or rendered-page review is needed.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex authored the implementation with Lean MCP inspection and shell validation. Worker `worker-codex-gentry-security-20261023` and author subagent `/root/maintenance_audit` implemented the changes; independent nonauthor agents `/root/library_map` and `/root/refactor_plan_review` reviewed them. title: feat(crypto): construct fixed-key FHE under circular security
body:
## Change

Construct fixed-key fully homomorphic encryption from a bootstrappable bit-encryption scheme with explicit circular security. Key generation samples one base key and publishes encryptions of its secret bits under that key. It takes no circuit or depth budget.

`FixedKey.evaluate_spec` proves that every finite Boolean DAG circuit can be evaluated under this same public artifact, including on previous evaluation outputs. Ciphertexts retain exactly the base width. `FixedKey.fullyHomomorphic` combines correctness for all circuits, polynomial secret/ciphertext widths and decryption-circuit size, native certificates for all four actual algorithms, and IND-CPA for that same constructed scheme.

The premises are base perfect correctness and fixed widths, actual bootstrappable decryption circuits with a uniform native generator, native base key generation/encryption/evaluation, base IND-CPA, and the separate `Encryption.CircularSecure` experiment. The latter compares the public key and complete self-encrypted secret vector jointly against equal-length zero encryptions. The security reduction preserves adaptive message choice and saved state; its zero-world simulator obtains the supported secret length from an independent key sample.

This is the generic conditional construction. A concrete LWE instantiation, general adaptive KDM security, circuit privacy, and Gentry's exact concrete-security loss are not established here. #322 remains open.

Sources: [Craig Gentry (2009), Section 2, self-loop construction](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/hits09/gentry-homomorphic-encryption.pdf); [Boneh–Halevi–Hamburg–Ostrovsky (2008), Section 2.1](https://crypto.stanford.edu/~dabo/papers/circular.pdf). Follows merged #478. Closes #479.

## Validation and review

- All six `scripts/check.sh` gates passed: strict build, aggregate check, strict tests, lint, style and Init imports. Whitespace and proof-hygiene checks passed.
- Tested and reviewed head: `4034a1521c4533b7f92948e9313f8618680d32e4`; tree `e42508d11d59d911fb66e12c5d6b4c14fcdbef48`. Local and published source match, with a clean isolated checkout. Code/tests and bibliography/roadmap are separate commits.
- Regressions cover actual repeated evaluation despite base-evaluator rejection, arbitrary encrypted wires, unchanged widths, constants, dead gates, repeated output wiring, malformed inputs and native algorithm fields. Security tests reject joint leakage despite identical ciphertext marginals; a security-only fixture explicitly fails correctness. Named axiom guards cover the headline theorems.
- Independent API/correctness/documentation approval: nonauthor `/root/library_map` on the exact final tree. `/root/refactor_plan_review` independently checked construction, native efficiency and assembly. The circular-experiment literature qualification was corrected and re-reviewed; no outstanding findings.

## Headline abstracts

The selected HILL/GGM abstracts and catalogue are unaffected; no new headline is selected. `/root/library_map` independently confirmed this no-impact assessment against the final tree. Abstract sources/rendering are unchanged, so no new PDF artifact review is required.

OpenAI Codex worker `worker-codex-gentry-fixedkey-20261023` and author subagent `/root/maintenance_audit` implemented this change using Lean MCP inspection and isolated shell validation. Independent nonauthor agents `/root/library_map` and `/root/refactor_plan_review` reviewed it. Mathematical source credit is retained in the modules and bibliography.

title: feat(crypto): prove GSW hiding with a shared public matrix
body:
Proves the statistical-hiding step for actual GSW ciphertexts when the public matrix is uniform. The first adversarial stage sees that matrix, chooses two messages, and retains arbitrary randomized state; the two challenge acceptance probabilities differ by at most `N * sqrt(2^(w*(n+1)) / 2^m)`, with `N = (n+1)*w`.

The proof uses exact subset-sum collision probabilities for every positive modulus and a shared-public-sample product bound. Tests include composite moduli, empty dimensions, repeated sampled rows, a counterexample to whole-matrix two-universality, and an adaptive game with exact acceptance probabilities 1/4 and 3/4. Mathematical source: [Gentry, Sahai and Waters (2013), §3.2](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/340); the general distance argument also credits Boneh and Shoup, §3.11.

Closes #494. The decision-LWE reduction for generated public keys, native runtime certificates, admissible parameter families, and bootstrappability remain open under #486. The selected HILL/GGM abstract catalogue is unchanged; this supporting theorem does not promote the FHE headline.

All six `scripts/check.sh` gates passed together on the final source tree. Independent API, correctness, and documentation review by `/root/library_map` found no issues; the reviewed source tree is `5dec7e46840321c61e240724e221628adcc2d5bc`. Review is by an AI agent, not a platform or human approval.

AI-assisted implementation and tests by `worker-codex-gsw-hiding-20261023`, coordinated by `/root`.

title: feat(crypto): sample GSW keys with supported correctness
body:
Constructs the actual finite GSW key-generation and encryption programs using uniform `w`-bit residues, independent binary coins, and errors given by the difference of two independent `η`-bit counts. Proves correctness for every supported generated key and fresh ciphertext under `w > 0` and `4*m*η < 2^w`, and for NAND of two fresh ciphertexts under `4*(1+N)*m*η < 2^w`, where `N=(n+1)*w`.

One flat tape of `n*w + m*n*w + 2*m*η + N*m` fair bits realizes the complete joint public-key, secret-key and ciphertext distribution. Serialized random-input samplers have uniform native PPT certificates, including all list framing, with unary dimensions and binary residues/errors. Exact distribution bridges and total decoder round trips connect those programs to the typed mathematical samplers. Reusable vector, finite-seed and uniform-support lemmas keep the client proofs compositional.

Tests cover exact nontrivial noise masses, signed endpoints, excluded errors, actual generated keys, both message bits and NAND, zero dimensions and widths, decoder normalization, growing native inputs and headline axiom guards. Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013) and NIST FIPS 203 Algorithm 8 are credited; the latter supplies the scalar noise construction, without a Gaussian-equivalence or hardness claim.

Closes #495. The full generated-key decision-LWE security reduction and admissible parameter families are tracked in #501; native certificates for modular matrix algorithms are tracked in #500. Full bootstrappability remains open in #486. This milestone certifies random-input generation, not complete encryption runtime. The selected formal abstract catalogue and existing headline statements are unaffected; the final FHE endpoint will receive its own checked abstract.

All six `scripts/check.sh` gates and `git diff --check` pass on the final integration source tree `b0508ed95ee0d7f676037414c7f4bbb633824cff`, published at `14f944215584f80090b89e45fc23b888675bc9b0`. title: feat(crypto): certify native GSW key generation and encryption
body:
GSW key generation and encryption now have native polynomial-time certificates for the actual serialized algorithms. Dimensions use unary encodings; residues and signed errors use binary encodings. Exact bridges identify the total computations with the existing typed construction, including the full joint public/secret-key law and the encryption distribution.

The representation is fixed-width, row-major and little-endian. Public keys contain `m*(n+1)*w` bits, secret keys `n*w` bits, and ciphertexts `((n+1)*w)^2` bits. The algorithms specify padding, truncation and modular normalization for arbitrary inputs. Generic matrix encodings, signed remainder and traversal certificates live below crypto; the moved bit-reconstruction lemmas retain deprecated aliases.

Closes #500. This completes the key-generation/encryption efficiency milestone under #486. Native decryption/NAND, cryptographic security, parameter selection and bootstrappability remain separate work. This PR builds on #502's tested sampling revision `14f9442`, now merged, and targets `main`. Integration against the newer main remains required before merge.

title: feat(fo): prove arbitrary-base lexicographic tuple order
body:
Adds arbitrary-base lexicographic numbering of full tuple universes, with the first coordinate most significant. The rank bijection, weighted digit formula, inverse and first-difference order are proved by reusing the existing colexicographic enumeration through coordinate reversal. Native quantifier-free strict/weak order formulas have exact rank semantics. Positive-dimensional full tuple interpretations also have uniquely defined canonical target constants with ranks 0,1,n^k−1.

Closes #43. Parent coordination #30. Integration preserves the reviewed PR #52 head `70766f5b29c1fd2fa83cba5d04d6e83d569c5962` and current main including PR #46; this PR follows #52 in the merge queue.

The first commit factors the existing generic tuple helpers out of machine-heavy Encoding into a lightweight module, preserving every public name and import compatibility. The second commit adds the new results. No binary-concatenation assumption or power-of-two base restriction is used.

Validation: all six gates pass separately after the refactor and after source revision `51e253c1e9d3b0ea81512eb7ff0fe830a00435bc`; MCP diagnostics are clean. All six gates also pass on the combined PR #52 integration tree. Tests distinguish base-three dimension-two lexicographic/colexicographic order, check base-five rank and inverse, zero-dimensional tuples, exact canonical ranks, quantifier-free order, and native constant-aware sentence pullback. Headline axiom guards use only the allowed axioms.

The index adds a curated tuple prerequisite entry (124 entries in the combined index). All five declaration links were verified against the pinned source. The PDF was rebuilt, and the tuple entry on page 9 and preserved two-sided counting entry on page 25 were rendered and inspected. The roadmap keeps successor/BIT lifting, numeric-preserving composition and the ordered complexity/capture endpoints open. The primary source warns that BIT on arbitrary definable restricted domains need not be first-order definable; no such general lifting is claimed.

Sources: Immerman, *Descriptive Complexity*, Remark 1.32 and Exercise 1.33(1), with the full-domain hypothesis; Mathlib's tuple bijection and Pi.Lex; existing Samuel Schlesinger tuple-index helpers. Exercise 1.33(3) remains open.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex worker `ordered-tuples-20261020` authored the refactor, new proofs, tests and documentation. Independent parent coordinator review found no API, correctness or index findings in refactor `b231228b`, source `51e253c1`, tests and the draft entry, and independently checked MCP diagnostics and page 9. title: feat(crypto): prove generated-key GSW security from exact decision LWE
body:
Proves single-challenge IND-CPA for the actual serialized GSW key generator and encryption program, assuming decision LWE for their exact centered-binomial error distribution. The public-key marginal is identified with the LWE experiment, and one uniform strict-PPT reduction retains the adversary's complete saved state. Its bound is `AdvCPA ≤ 2·AdvLWE + N·sqrt(2^N / 2^m)`, where `N = (n+1)w`.

The explicit family `n = η = λ+1`, `w = 16+8⌈log₂(λ+1)⌉`, and `m = N+2λ` supplies native parameter routines, negligible statistical error, and strict fresh/one-NAND correctness margins. The endpoint `GSW.Parameters.indCPA` therefore leaves only its specified LWE premise. Reusable additions cover public-key replacement, encoded LWE experiments, dyadic negligibility, and independent replicated sampling.

Closes #501 as a security milestone within #486. This does **not** establish LWE hardness, circular security, native decryption/evaluation, shallow decryption, or bootstrappability. The current parameter family is not claimed to support full FHE. The native honest algorithms come from merged #519.

Validation: all six repository gates passed on the final source: strict build, aggregate-import check, strict tests, lint, style lint, and initialization-import check. Regressions exercise adaptive message selection and saved public-key state, attain the reduction's factor-two loss, and check actual honest/reduction efficiency certificates. The checked abstract has 40 roots, 164 audited dependencies, no internal-definition allowlist, and headline axiom guards containing only the three permitted standard axioms.

Independent source/API/correctness review by `/root/maintenance_audit` approved published head `a406f81f19d5cb9c7383cacc1ca37e3d82e60eae` (tree `d79a101d3483da59b6edbf0740152d288e4a828a`); [review record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/524#issuecomment-6372185014). `/root/refactor_plan_review` independently reviewed the abstract/bridge and all six rendered PDF pages. The final standalone PDF has SHA256 `529a806df8e52120c9fcc98e58b052b4a5ae7390d9fcfb8b44930d650e270017`; its statement links resolve to this head at [native_algorithms](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/blob/a406f81f19d5cb9c7383cacc1ca37e3d82e60eae/ComplexityTests/Abstracts/GSWSecurityAbstract.lean#L231) and [indCPA](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/blob/a406f81f19d5cb9c7383cacc1ca37e3d82e60eae/ComplexityTests/Abstracts/GSWSecurityAbstract.lean#L240). Local PDF layout adjustments keep explanations with declarations and reserve footer space; the repository renderer is unchanged. Remote CI is separate from these completed local checks.

Documentation/index assessment: the roadmap records this result and its remaining gaps; the new supporting formal abstract is intentionally outside the curated headline catalogue while full FHE remains open. Catalogue and selected-headline documentation are unchanged.

Mathematical credit: Gentry, Sahai and Waters, [GSW 2013](https://courses.csail.mit.edu/6.857/2021/files/Gentry-Sahai-Waters13.pdf), §§3.1–3.2; additional sources are cited in the modules and abstract. +# Build caches
+
+Complexitylib's build has two caches. Both are optional: `lake build` without them compiles
+everything it needs.
+
+**Local artifact cache.** `lakefile.toml` enables Lake's content-addressed artifact cache, so a
+module built in one checkout (a worktree, an agent sandbox, a second clone) is reused by every
+other checkout on the same machine with the same inputs. Outputs are hard-linked back into
+`.lake/build`. `lake cache clean` empties it; it lives in the Lean toolchain's directory under
+`~/.elan` unless `LAKE_CACHE_DIR` says otherwise.
+
+**Remote cache.** CI uploads the build outputs of every commit on `main`; `scripts/cache/get.sh`
+downloads them for the nearest cached ancestor of your `HEAD`:
+
+```bash
+scripts/cache/get.sh   # Mathlib's cache, then Complexitylib's outputs
+lake build             # compiles only what you changed
+```
+
+A complete set of library and test outputs is about 70 MB compressed. Outputs are platform
+independent (`platformIndependent = true`), so Linux CI builds serve macOS checkouts.
+`COMPLEXITYLIB_CACHE_URL` overrides the location; set it to an empty string to skip the
+Complexitylib download.
+
+## Trust and privacy
+
+Downloaded `.olean` files are trusted by Lean: imported modules are not re-checked by the
+kernel, and their compiled code (tactics, macros, initializers) runs during your build. Whoever
+can write to the cache could therefore make a false theorem appear proved or run code on your
+machine. The cache is set up so that this is no more trust than building `main` already
+requires:
+
+- Only the `main` push job of this repository can write. It authenticates with GitHub's OIDC
+  token through Workload Identity Federation, restricted to this repository's numeric id, the
+  `main` ref and the `push` event; no credentials are stored in GitHub. Pull requests, forks and
+  other workflows cannot obtain write access.

+| `project` | the project, billing link and APIs |
+| `bucket` | `gs://complexitylib-lake-cache` (`us-east1`), public read by object name without listing, no soft delete or versioning, revision mappings expire after 180 days |
+| `writer` | the GitHub identity pool and provider, and the `lake-cache-writer` service account (create + read on the bucket only) |
+| `budget` | a monthly budget (default 10 USD) with alerts at 50/90/100 % and a Pub/Sub topic |
+| `killswitch` | a Cloud Run function that removes public read when the budget is reached or the egress alert fires |
+| `alert` | an alert on more than 20 GB sent per hour, to the kill switch and `ALERT_EMAIL` |
+| `variables` | prints the `gh variable set` commands for the three repository variables |
+
+CI skips the upload until the repository variable `LAKE_CACHE_BUCKET` is set.
+
+**Costs.** Storage and egress are small at this size: each `main` push uploads only modules whose
+outputs changed, and Cloud Storage's free tier covers 5 GB of storage and 100 GB of egress per
+month in `us-east1`. The budget alerts and the kill switch bound abuse of the public bucket.

+# One-time maintainer setup of the remote build cache on Google Cloud. See scripts/cache/README.md.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   PROJECT=<new-project-id> BILLING_ACCOUNT=<id> [ALERT_EMAIL=<address>] \
+#     scripts/cache/setup-gcs.sh [step...]
+#
+# Steps (default: all, in order): project bucket writer budget killswitch alert variables.
+# Each step can be rerun on its own. Optional settings: BUCKET (complexitylib-lake-cache),
+# REGION (us-east1, inside Cloud Storage's free tier), BUDGET_USD (10), EGRESS_ALERT_GB (20 per
+# hour). Billing account and e-mail are arguments so that they never enter the repository.
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")"
+
+: "${PROJECT:?set PROJECT to the id of a new, dedicated Google Cloud project}"
+BUCKET="${BUCKET:-complexitylib-lake-cache}"

+BUDGET_USD="${BUDGET_USD:-10}"
+EGRESS_ALERT_GB="${EGRESS_ALERT_GB:-20}"

+REPO_ID="1420662136"          # `gh api repos/cslib-community/complexitylib --jq .id`
+WRITER="lake-cache-writer@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
+KILLER="lake-cache-kill-switch@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
+TOPIC="lake-cache-limits"
+POOL="github"
+PROVIDER="complexitylib"
+
+gc() { echo "+ gcloud $*" >&2; gcloud "$@"; }
+project_number() { gcloud projects describe "$PROJECT" --format='value(projectNumber)'; }
+
+step_project() {
+  gcloud projects describe "$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1 || gc projects create "$PROJECT"
+  gc billing projects link "$PROJECT" --billing-account="${BILLING_ACCOUNT:?set BILLING_ACCOUNT}"
+  gc services enable --project="$PROJECT" storage.googleapis.com iam.googleapis.com \
+    iamcredentials.googleapis.com sts.googleapis.com pubsub.googleapis.com \
+    billingbudgets.googleapis.com monitoring.googleapis.com cloudfunctions.googleapis.com \
+    run.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com \
+    eventarc.googleapis.com
+}
+
+step_bucket() {
+  gcloud storage buckets describe "gs://$BUCKET" >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
+    gc storage buckets create "gs://$BUCKET" --project="$PROJECT" --location="$REGION" \
+      --uniform-bucket-level-access --soft-delete-duration=0 --default-storage-class=STANDARD
+  # Revision mappings older than 180 days are dropped; artifacts are shared between revisions

+  local lifecycle

+  rm -f "$lifecycle"
