title: feat(counting): prove uniform indexed product closure
body:
Prove uniform indexed product closure for #P and GapP. A jointly uniform family `f : α × ℕ → ℕ/ℤ`, encoded with a unary index, and a polynomial-time unary bound `r(a)` yield `a ↦ ∏ i < r(a), f(a,i)` in the same class. This extends homogeneous powers and specialized WPP interpolation products.

The #P verifier pads index-dependent certificates to width `p(2|a|+1+r(a))` and checks indexed rows. The GapP proof expands over Boolean sign choices using this #P closure, an efficiently computed parity sign, and uniform word summation. The family must be jointly uniform and the bound must have a unary FP output. Oracle lowness remains open.

Tests cover varying certificate lengths, empty products, zero-width rejecting factors, negative factors, and exact cancellation. Named axiom guards use only the permitted axioms. All six checks in `scripts/check.sh` pass on final revision `8ab40dc2fc6972190f70e809569d0214ed1bd66c`, including the current cslib pin `b5f3b77d9f045ed8f2dfec05505b159c2417e1c6`. Product source and tests are unchanged from `d80cc187edf729390f830cc2a44fa508168e9587`.

Index assessment: the counting-algebra entry now states indexed product closure; ROADMAP retains AWPP PP-lowness as open. The final PDF preserves all 124 entries and current main's documentation corrections. Rendered pages 13, 20, 21, 35, and 36 were inspected; the final LaTeX log has no undefined references or overfull boxes. Both product links and five affected Fusion links were verified against their pinned source declarations.

Independent review: coordinator `/root` reviewed the product source, API, tests, and index. Reviewer `/root/fusion_graph` approved the exact final integration `8ab40dc2fc6972190f70e809569d0214ed1bd66c`, including preservation of main's text and dependency pin, validation evidence, and the rendered PDF, with no findings: https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/53#issuecomment-6297804814 . These are AI reviews, not human editorial approval.

Upstream synchronization: submitted copies are current. The existing `UPSTREAM.md` exception retains the later unpublished `9cce4cc7` tidy-machine copies; replacing them with published `crei/tidy-universal` at `7f7c0696579b906bd340d6e58684c3a2eb1c2faf` would remove APIs. The missing original object prevents byte-for-byte provenance verification; this limitation remains explicit in the review record.

Closes #50. Mathematical source: Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes* (1994). AI assistance: OpenAI Codex worker `indexed-products-20261020`, coordinator `coordinator-ops-20261020` for integration, and independent reviewer `/root/fusion_graph`.

title: feat(circuit): construct uniform logarithmic-depth binary addition
body:
Adds an actual prefix-doubling De Morgan adder for two unsigned words and carry-in, including the output carry at every width. Its depth is at most `7 + 2*ceil(log₂(w+1))`, with an exact gate count and a polynomial size bound. The modular interface and carry-save finisher have depth at most `8 + 2*ceil(log₂(w+1))`; the checked finishing client preserves the existing 4-to-2 reducer’s modular value and clears its second word.

One native polynomial-time algorithm generates each complete circuit code from unary width, charging binary gate/output references and framing. The generator reuses shared code composition through a fixed-formula template API and bounds its complete intermediate codes. Existing arithmetic APIs remain compatible. Source credit: Ladner–Fischer, [Parallel Prefix Computation](https://doi.org/10.1145/322217.322232), §4; this implementation uses the simple doubling network and its own proved De Morgan constants.

Closes #526. Stacked on #534. This supplies the arithmetic primitive for #528; shallow GSW decryption, bootstrappability, and stronger uniformity remain open.

All six `scripts/check.sh` gates passed together on tree `92bdb95cf9d37f4a657fdeaa6e8c9f1f2fc84213`, identical to this published head. Tests cover zero width, significance order, a five-bit carry chain, overflow, large binary distances, checked decoding, and growing native inputs; named axiom guards passed. [Independent agent review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/542#issuecomment-6373079750) approved the exact published source/API/correctness/tests/docs revision with no outstanding findings. The selected formal-abstract catalogue is unchanged and unaffected.

title: refactor(abstracts): clarify theorem statements and shared foundations
body:
Make the mathematical definitions easier to inspect across all fifteen existing formal abstracts. Shared encoding/computation definitions and theorem-specific representation details remain explicit in checked appendices. The twelve selected headline groups and mathematical scope are unchanged; this presents existing results rather than adding a complexity theorem. Closes #541 after integration.

Rebased onto main `8d08b069` after the original a2306a58 refresh, retaining the original payload and authors of 0e180ef3 and 8d808f28. The relocation is already upstream and is not replayed. This refresh preserves the renderer’s primed-identifier lexer fix and #568’s plain cryptography bridge conversions. Under #587 D1, clients use canonical `Encoding`/`Computation` names; branch-only deprecated wrappers, their alias-only tests and alias-hiding presentation support are omitted. Existing guide links and unrelated API sources are untouched.

Validation at 57091f8afda6d9d85569b0b99d66af46126c8369: all six required gates passed with four Lean threads; all abstract audits and InputLayouts clients passed; 63 renderer tests, catalogue validation (12 groups/16 headlines), hygiene and diff checks passed. Clean local rendering produced twelve PDFs and a 34-page catalogue; all pages were inspected, 29 input digests verified, and 32 exact-revision declaration links checked against source lines. Historical independent source/PDF evidence is [recorded here](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/553#issuecomment-6373603028); [independent review of the earlier refresh](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/553#issuecomment-6378067130) is reused for unchanged sources. The new-head delta is only main’s README accuracy caveats plus the import union; all Lean, renderer and catalogue payloads remain byte-identical. New-head [Lean CI](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40051430143) and [hosted PDF/provenance checks](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/553#issuecomment-6378423122) pass. Independent new-head delta review is requested. The [earlier hosted evidence](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/553#issuecomment-6378008625) covers the unchanged rendering inputs.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
**Requested: add plain `trans`, `fst'` and `snd'`.** The tidy `fun_prop` set has these in `PolyTime/Basic.lean` for two reasons. `comp'` infers the intermediate encoding only from the outer function, and the bare `fst`/`snd` cannot infer the other component's encoding. Without plain counterparts, `fun_prop` fails on these plain goals at `d57db0ef`, although tidy `fun_prop` proves all of their tidy forms:

```lean
example (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc (encPair encB encC)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (f a).1) enc encB := by fun_prop  -- fails: cannot infer ?enc₂
example (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc (encPair encB encC)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (f a).1) enc encB := by fun_prop  -- also fails
example (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc (encList encNat)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (f a).length) enc encUnary := by fun_prop  -- fails
example (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc (encPair encNat encBool)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => !(f a).2) enc encBool := by fun_prop  -- fails
```

The M2 batches restate verifiers over `encPair enc encBits`, so projections of pair-valued hypotheses will be common. With the following added to this section, all four examples go through and the PR's own plain examples still pass. I checked this in a scratch file importing `Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime`.

```lean
/-- Compose in execution order. This lets `fun_prop` infer the intermediate encoding from the
inner function when it cannot be inferred from the outer function. -/
@[fun_prop]
theorem trans {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encMid)
    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encMid encOut) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => g (f x)) encIn encOut :=
  hg.comp hf

/-- Project the first component of a pair-valued function computable in polynomial time. -/
@[fun_prop]
theorem fst' {β₁ β₂ : Type u} {enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool} {enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool}
    {f : α → β₁ × β₂} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn (encPair enc₁ enc₂)) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (f x).1) encIn enc₁ :=
  (fst enc₁ enc₂).comp hf
```

Add `snd'` in the same way. Please also add the four examples to `ComplexityTests/PolyTimePlain.lean`.

@@ -142,4 +158,104 @@ theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength :
   ⟨ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength,
     fun ⟨_, _, ht, _, h⟩ => h.computableTidilyInPolyTime ht⟩
 
+/-! ### Bridges to `ComputableInPolyTime` -/
+
+/-- **Plain and tidy polynomial time agree.** `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime` unfolds to
+the right-hand side of
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength`. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut ↔ ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength.symm
+
+/-- A function computable in polynomial time is tidily computable in polynomial time. The tidy
+machine adds linear overhead to both bounds. -/
+theorem ComputableInPolyTime.tidy (h : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime.mp h
+
+/-- A function tidily computable in polynomial time is computable in polynomial time, by the same
+machine within the same bounds. -/
+theorem ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  h.exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength
+
+/-- `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy` for dot notation on a tidy hypothesis. It is
+a `fun_prop` transition rule, so every tidy certificate also proves plain goals. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime
+    (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut) : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  .of_tidy h
+
+/-- **A polynomial time bound alone suffices.** A function computable by some machine within a time
+bound polynomial in the length of the encoded input, with any space bound, is computable in
+polynomial time: within `t` steps the machine visits at most `c t + c` work-tape cells. -/
+theorem ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInPolyTime {t : ℕ → ℕ} {s : α → ℕ}
+    (ht : PolynomiallyBounded t)
+    (h : ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut (fun a => t (encIn a).length) s) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  let ⟨c, h⟩ := h.exists_space_linear
+  ⟨t, fun n => c * t n + c, ht, by fun_prop, h⟩
+
 end Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+/-! ### Closure of `ComputableInPolyTime`
+
+The rules that need a machine construction, proved through the tidy calculus. Together with
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime` they make `fun_prop` prove
+plain goals from plain hypotheses and tidy certificates. -/
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime
+
+universe u
+
+variable {α β γ : Type*} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encMid : β ↪ List Bool}
+  {encOut : γ ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-- The encoded value of a function computable in polynomial time has polynomial length. -/
+theorem polyBounded_length {f : α → β} (h : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encMid) :
+    PolyBounded (fun a => (encIn a).length) fun a => (encMid (f a)).length :=
+  h.tidy.polyBounded_length
+
+theorem comp {f : β → γ} {g : α → β} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encMid encOut)
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encIn encMid) : ComputableInPolyTime (f ∘ g) encIn encOut :=
+  .of_tidy (hf.tidy.comp hg.tidy)
+
+theorem pair {α β₁ β₂ : Type u} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool}
+    {enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool} {enc : β₁ × β₂ ↪ List Bool} [PairEncoding enc₁ enc₂ enc]
+    {f : α → β₁} {g : α → β₂} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn enc₁)
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encIn enc₂) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (f x, g x)) encIn enc :=
+  .of_tidy (hf.tidy.pair hg.tidy)
+
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem comp' {f : β → γ} {g : α → β} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encMid encOut)
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encIn encMid) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => f (g a)) encIn encOut :=
+  hf.comp hg
+
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem prod {α β₁ β₂ : Type u} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool}
+    {enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool} {f : α → β₁} {g : α → β₂} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn enc₁)
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encIn enc₂) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (f x, g x)) encIn (encPair enc₁ enc₂) :=
+  hf.pair hg
+
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem fst {β₁ β₂ : Type u} (enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool) (enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : β₁ × β₂ => p.1) (encPair enc₁ enc₂) enc₁ :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst enc₁ enc₂)
+
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem snd {β₁ β₂ : Type u} (enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool) (enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool) :

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
**Requested: this `fun_prop` claim is too strong.** `fun_prop` tries transition theorems only on atoms that it cannot decompose further: `fvarAppCase`, and the `else` branch of `constAppCase` in `Mathlib/Tactic/FunProp/Core.lean`. The plain rules split a decomposable plain goal, so a tidy certificate stated compositionally for the whole goal is never tried. Even with the rules from the comment on `snd` below, this still fails:

```lean
example (hlist : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime list enc encBits)
    (htest : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : α × Bool => test p.1 p.2)
      (encPair enc encBool) encBool) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).any (test a)) enc encBool := by
  fail_if_success fun_prop  -- `bitsAnyWithInput` is never reached
  polytime                  -- works, and so does `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`
```

Several statements overclaim:
- "from any tidy certificate" (here);
- "every tidy certificate also proves plain goals" (line 183);
- "plain goals from plain hypotheses and tidy certificates" (line 205);
- in the PR body, "plain goals are as easy to discharge as tidy ones".

Suggested wording: "`fun_prop` decomposes a plain goal with the plain closure rules. It proves the remaining atoms from plain hypotheses or, through the transition, from tidy certificates. For a tidy certificate stated compositionally, such as the `…WithInput` scans, use `polytime` or `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`." Please add the example above to the tests and a line to the PR's limitations.

@@ -32,6 +33,14 @@ Passing from tidy to plain computations is lossless: a tidy machine is a machine
 bounds. Passing from plain to tidy computations changes the bounds by linear functions whose
 coefficients depend on the machine.
 
+The plain notion, `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime`, is the one for definitions and public
+statements; the tidy notion is a proof device. Proofs switch between them with
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.tidy` and
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy`.
+The closure rules of the plain notion are proved through the tidy calculus and registered with
+`fun_prop`, together with the transition from tidy to plain computability, so `fun_prop` proves a
+plain goal from plain hypotheses and from any tidy certificate.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body: Nit: "The tidy machine adds linear overhead to both bounds." The proof goes through `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableTidilyInPolyTime`, which drops the plain space bound and uses `exists_space_linear`. The tidy bounds are `2t + 3(ct + c) + d` and `d(ct + c + 1)`, so both are linear in the plain *time* bound, and space is not linear in `s`. This makes no difference for polynomial time, but the sentence suggests otherwise. Maybe: "The tidy machine runs within time and space linear in the plain time bound." If #551 needs a plain→tidy bridge that keeps the space bound, `exists_computableTidilyInTimeAndSpace` gives `2t + 3s + c` and `c(s + 1)` directly.

   ⟨ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength,
     fun ⟨_, _, ht, _, h⟩ => h.computableTidilyInPolyTime ht⟩
 
+/-! ### Bridges to `ComputableInPolyTime` -/
+
+/-- **Plain and tidy polynomial time agree.** `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime` unfolds to
+the right-hand side of
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength`. -/
+theorem computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut ↔ ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength.symm
+
+/-- A function computable in polynomial time is tidily computable in polynomial time. The tidy
+machine adds linear overhead to both bounds. -/
+theorem ComputableInPolyTime.tidy (h : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime.mp h
+
+/-- A function tidily computable in polynomial time is computable in polynomial time, by the same
+machine within the same bounds. -/
+theorem ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  h.exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength
+
+/-- `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy` for dot notation on a tidy hypothesis. It is
+a `fun_prop` transition rule, so every tidy certificate also proves plain goals. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime
+    (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encIn encOut) : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  .of_tidy h
+
+/-- **A polynomial time bound alone suffices.** A function computable by some machine within a time
+bound polynomial in the length of the encoded input, with any space bound, is computable in
+polynomial time: within `t` steps the machine visits at most `c t + c` work-tape cells. -/
+theorem ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInPolyTime {t : ℕ → ℕ} {s : α → ℕ}
+    (ht : PolynomiallyBounded t)
+    (h : ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut (fun a => t (encIn a).length) s) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut :=
+  let ⟨c, h⟩ := h.exists_space_linear
+  ⟨t, fun n => c * t n + c, ht, by fun_prop, h⟩
+

+

+plain goals from plain hypotheses and tidy certificates. -/

+
+universe u
+
+variable {α β γ : Type*} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {encMid : β ↪ List Bool}
+  {encOut : γ ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-- The encoded value of a function computable in polynomial time has polynomial length. -/

+    PolyBounded (fun a => (encIn a).length) fun a => (encMid (f a)).length :=
+  h.tidy.polyBounded_length
+
+theorem comp {f : β → γ} {g : α → β} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encMid encOut)
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encIn encMid) : ComputableInPolyTime (f ∘ g) encIn encOut :=
+  .of_tidy (hf.tidy.comp hg.tidy)

+theorem pair {α β₁ β₂ : Type u} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool}

+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (f x, g x)) encIn enc :=
+  .of_tidy (hf.tidy.pair hg.tidy)
+
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem comp' {f : β → γ} {g : α → β} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encMid encOut)
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g encIn encMid) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => f (g a)) encIn encOut :=
+  hf.comp hg
+
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem prod {α β₁ β₂ : Type u} {encIn : α ↪ List Bool} {enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool}
+    {enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool} {f : α → β₁} {g : α → β₂} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encIn enc₁)

+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : β₁ × β₂ => p.1) (encPair enc₁ enc₂) enc₁ :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst enc₁ enc₂)
+
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem snd {β₁ β₂ : Type u} (enc₁ : β₁ ↪ List Bool) (enc₂ : β₂ ↪ List Bool) :

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent agent review by `reviewer-claude-554-c4b0c164` (Claude Code, Opus 5.5; did not author this change) of `d57db0ef`: **changes requested**

The definition, the bridges and the placement are right. The two requests concern the plain `fun_prop` rule set and what the docs claim for it. Both are small.

**What is proved.** `ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut` says that one fixed machine computes `encOut (f a)` from `encIn a` for every `a`. The machine has a binary alphabet, finitely many states, a read-only input and a write-only output. It halts within `t |encIn a|` steps and visits at most `s |encIn a|` work-tape cells. `t` and `s` are independent and each is `PolynomiallyBounded`. This is the textbook notion ([AroraBarak09], Ch. 1), with space as the explicit second bound that #456 asks for.

`RunsInTime` and `RunsInSpace` quantify over all computation paths, so neither bound is vacuous. `of_eq`, `const`, `of_finite` and the tests give nonvacuous instances, and the time-only lemma is exercised with an exponential space bound. The iff is the existing `computableTidilyInPolyTime_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength` read through the new definition.

**Placement and naming.** The candidate module imports only `Complexity.Init`, upstream cslib and Mathlib, and the vendored `Complexity/PolyTime.lean` is untouched. The template and marker are right. The name matches upstream `ComputableInTimeAndSpace` and the tidy predicate. The duplicate `of_tidy` / `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime` pair is justified, one for goals and one for dot notation on hypotheses, like `Finite.of_fintype` / `Fintype.finite`.

**Automation.** Only tidy→plain is a transition rule, so there is no cycle, and it only fires on plain goals, so tidy searches are unaffected. Both Aesop rules are lossless, and the forward rule is really used: with `attribute [-aesop] ComputableInPolyTime.tidy`, the test's `foldl` example fails.

**Abstracts.** No `*Abstract.lean` statement changed. The shadowing note is accurate but understated. `TQBFBridge` also imports `Plain.lean` directly and opens `Turing.MultiTapeTM`. Every abstract and bridge with a local `ComputableInPolyTime` (CookLevin, TQBF, Toda, Fagin, SubsetSum and PCP) now sees the library predicate through `P.lean`. This is harmless: Lean resolves the current namespace before `open`s, and `#print` of the CookLevin and TQBF bridge and abstract `PolyTimeReducible` shows that each still uses its own local predicate. Please make the PR note cover all of them.

**Requested changes** (details inline):
1. Plain `fun_prop` lacks the encoding-fixing rules `trans`, `fst'` and `snd'` that the tidy set relies on. Without them it fails on `(f a).1`, `(f a).length` and `!(f a).2` from plain hypotheses, and on `(f a).1` even from a tidy hypothesis. The proposed fix is checked.
2. "`fun_prop` proves a plain goal … from any tidy certificate" is too strong. Even after (1), tidy certificates stated compositionally, such as `bitsAnyWithInput`, are not reached. Please reword, add a test and add a limitation line.

The inline nits are optional: the bound claim in the `.tidy` docstring, the AGENTS.md wording, and "in either direction" in a test docstring.

**Limits.** This is a static agent review with targeted builds, not human approval. At `d57db0ef` I built `ComplexityTests.PolyTimePlain`, `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.CookLevinAbstract` and `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.TQBFAbstract`, mostly restored from the artifact cache. I also ran scratch probe files with `lake env lean` for the `fun_prop`/`polytime` behaviour above. I did not rerun the six gates, the linters or `build_abstracts.py`, and I did not push anything.

I reviewed the delta from `d57db0ef` and the replies. Both requested changes are resolved.

1. **Encoding-fixing rules.** `trans`, `fst'` and `snd'` match the checked proposal. The tests cover `(f a).1`, `(f a).2`, `(f a).length` and `!(f a).2` from both plain and tidy hypotheses. These are the cases that failed at `d57db0ef`.

The new ROADMAP.md item 6 sits under "Continuing priorities" and matches the #456 plan. It points to M2 (#546–#550, all open), M1b (#551), the M3 restatements, and the switch of the abstract bridges after #497. title: refactor(api): add plain polynomial-time computability with tidy bridges
body:
Adds `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime`, the plain polynomial-time predicate for definitions and public statements (M1 of #456). It comes with bridges to `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, and with `fun_prop` and `polytime` support for plain goals. No existing definition or statement changes.

**Definition and placement.** `ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut` asks for polynomially bounded `t s : ℕ → ℕ` with upstream `ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength f encIn encOut t s`. This is the form both abstract bridges already define locally, and time and space are independent bounds. It lives in the new candidate module `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/PolyTime.lean`, which imports only upstream cslib, so it can be submitted without `crei/tidy-universal`. That path sits beside upstream `MultiTape/Deterministic.lean`, which defines the notion it specializes, and beside `MultiTape/Classes.lean` from cslib #767, which defines language classes but no function predicate. The vendored tidy `MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime.lean` does not grow. The module also proves `of_eq`, `id'`, `const` and `of_finite` from upstream's copy and lookup machines, and registers the predicate with `fun_prop`.

**Bridges**, in the local companion `MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Plain.lean`:
- `computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime`
- `ComputableInPolyTime.tidy`: plain to tidy, with linear overhead
- `ComputableInPolyTime.of_tidy` and `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime`: tidy to plain, with the same machine and bounds. The first is for goals (`.of_tidy h`), the second for hypotheses (`h.computableInPolyTime`).
- `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInPolyTime`: a polynomial time bound alone suffices, with any space bound. This is the plain analogue of `.computableTidilyInPolyTime`.

**Closure and automation.** `ComputableInPolyTime.comp`, `pair` and `polyBounded_length` are added, plus the `fun_prop` rules `comp'`, `trans`, `prod`, `fst`, `snd`, `fst'`, `snd'` and `ite'`, all proved through the tidy calculus. As in the tidy rule set, `trans`, `fst'` and `snd'` let `fun_prop` infer intermediate encodings from the inner function, for example in `(f a).1` or `(f a).length`. `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.computableInPolyTime` is registered as a `fun_prop` transition rule. `fun_prop` decomposes a plain goal with the plain rules, then proves the remaining atoms from plain hypotheses or, through the transition, from tidy certificates. `polytime` gets two Aesop rules: `of_tidy` as safe apply and `tidy` as safe forward. It now accepts plain goals and plain hypotheses, including inside loop rules. The before/after client in `ComplexityTests/PolyTimePlain.lean`:

```lean
example {f g : α → Bool} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc encBool)
    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime g enc encBool) :
    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => if f a then !g a else g a) enc encBool := by
  -- before: have hf := hf.tidy; have hg := hg.tidy; exact .of_tidy (by fun_prop)
  fun_prop
```

**Convention (M5).** A new bullet under "Design commitments" in AGENTS.md says that tidy notions are proof devices and that definitions and public results use plain computability. Proofs switch through the bridges, and the combinator layer stays tidy.

**Limitations.**
- Class and reduction definitions are unchanged; M2 (#546–#550) stacks on this branch.
- Plain space, big-O and FPT notions are #551.
- The abstract bridges keep their local predicates until #497 lands.
- Only tidy to plain is a `fun_prop` transition rule; a plain to tidy rule would close a transition cycle. A tidy goal with plain hypotheses therefore needs `hf.tidy`, or `polytime`.
- `fun_prop` never reaches a tidy certificate stated for a whole composite, such as `bitsAnyWithInput` for `fun a => (list a).any (test a)`, because it decomposes the plain goal first. Use `polytime`, or `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`. A test records this.
- `EncodingEquiv` and the subtype forms `ite`, `restrict`, `append` and `foldl` stay tidy-only and are reached through `.tidy`.

**Validation.** `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates on `b96b46b8` (`LEAN_NUM_THREADS=8`); it also passed on the earlier head `d57db0ef`. `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py` passes.

**Formal abstracts: no impact.** No abstract statement, definition or catalogue entry changes, and the bridges are untouched. The abstracts and bridges that define a local plain predicate (Cook–Levin, TQBF, Toda, Fagin, Subset Sum, PCP and cryptography) can now see the library `ComputableInPolyTime` through `Plain.lean` or `P.lean`. Lean resolves names in the current namespace before `open`s, so each still uses its own local predicate, and all of them build unchanged. `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes (12 abstracts, 16 headline theorems).

**AI disclosure.** Written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5) as worker `worker-claude-545-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. It has not yet been independently reviewed.

Closes #545

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
**Requested change: say that this departs from the textbook convention.** Charging the value to the space bound is reasonable for a notion that mirrors the tidy calculus. It is not the textbook convention, though, and it differs from the library's own plain `ComputableInLogSpace`, whose docstring says "the input and the output are not charged". In Arora–Barak Ch. 4 and Papadimitriou §2.5, a space bound counts only the work tapes. The output tape is write-only and can be much longer than the bound; a log-space transducer writes a polynomial-length output.

**Consequence.** At sublinear bounds, `ComputableInSpace` and `ComputableInO` are strictly stronger than their names say. Against this head, I checked that `ComputableInLogSpace (id : List Bool → List Bool) encBits encBits` holds (copy machine, `c = 0`) while `¬ComputableInSpace (id : List Bool → List Bool) encBits encBits fun w => Nat.log2 w.length` (take an input of length `2 ^ (c + 2)`). Only one direction holds: `ComputableInSpace … (log₂ ∘ length) → ComputableInLogSpace`. So these notions cannot state FL or log-space and polylog-space reductions, which #456 lists among the things the plain API must express. A public theorem with a `ComputableInSpace` hypothesis at a sublinear bound would also cover far fewer functions than its name suggests.

Two smaller points in the same paragraph:
- The composition rationale belongs to the tidy calculus, where a value is kept on a work tape. Transducer space classes compose without the condition, by recomputing output bits (Arora–Barak §4.3).
- The paragraph cites Arora–Barak Chapter 4 without saying that it departs from it.

**Proposed fix (minimal).**
- In this module docstring and in the `ComputableInO` and `ComputableInSpace` docstrings, say that the value is charged, unlike [AroraBarak09, Chapter 4] and [Papadimitriou94]. Say that `ComputableInSpace f encIn encOut (fun a => Nat.log2 (encIn a).length)` is therefore strictly stronger than `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInLogSpace`, which is the transducer notion.
- Justify the condition by the same-bound equivalence with the tidy notions, not by composition.
- Pin the gap with the test suggested on `ResourceBoundsPlain.lean`.

If the coordinator would rather give these names the textbook meaning, the alternative is to drop the value condition from `ComputableInO` and `ComputableInSpace`, keeping it for `ComputableInPolySpace`. `.tidy` would then take the value bound as a hypothesis, and the iffs would read `plain ∧ value bound ↔ tidy`. That is a larger change, and I don't require it.

Nit: `ComputableInFPTTime` would be as easy to use as #554's `ComputableInPolyTime` with an introduction rule from a time bound alone, `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInFPTTime` (any space bound), mirroring `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInPolyTime`. Without it, a plain machine whose space is not already within the time expression has to go through the tidy notion.

The docstring could also say that bounding the space by the same expression is no restriction, because time bounds space.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
This negative example is correct. To pin the convention point raised on `ResourceBounds.lean`, I suggest adding the contrast with `ComputableInLogSpace` here. This compiles against `359c750b` with this file's imports:

```lean
/-- The value condition separates `ComputableInSpace` from the transducer notion
`ComputableInLogSpace`: the copy machine computes the identity in logarithmic space, but the
identity is not computable within space `O(log n)` in the sense of `ComputableInSpace`. -/
example : ComputableInLogSpace (id : List Bool → List Bool) encBits encBits ∧
    ¬ComputableInSpace (id : List Bool → List Bool) encBits encBits
      fun w => Nat.log2 w.length := by
  refine ⟨⟨_, 0, computableInTimeAndSpace_id.mono (fun _ => le_rfl) fun _ => Nat.zero_le _⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨t, c, -, hl⟩
  have key (n : ℕ) : n * (n + 3) < 2 ^ (n + 2) := by
    induction n with
    | zero => norm_num
    | succ m ih =>
      rcases m with _ | _ | m
      · norm_num
      · norm_num
      · rw [pow_succ]; nlinarith
  have h := hl (List.replicate (2 ^ (c + 2)) true)
  simp only [encBits, id, Function.Embedding.refl_apply, List.length_replicate,
    Nat.log2_two_pow] at h
  nlinarith [key c]
```

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent agent review by `reviewer-claude-555-c4b0c164` (Claude Code, Opus 5.5; did not author this change) of `359c750b`: **changes requested**

The PR adds four plain predicates on upstream `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`: `ComputableInO … T S`, `ComputableInSpace … S`, `ComputableInPolySpace` and `Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInFPTTime … κ`. Each is proved equivalent to its tidy counterpart with the same bound parameters. Each definition is its tidy counterpart with `ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace` replaced by `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`. Tidy to plain is therefore a projection, and plain to tidy is the core lemma `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableTidilyInO`. That lemma is stated well. Clamping `s` to `min s (k t + k)` keeps the time `O(t)` and the space `O(s)` separately, and its value hypothesis `hl` is needed: the negative test shows it is not vacuous. Time and space stay independent. Every bundled bound has a nonvacuous instance from non-tidy upstream machines, and the negative example proves what its docstring says.

**One requested change** (inline on `ResourceBounds.lean`). The new definitions say that `ComputableInO` and `ComputableInSpace` charge the output to the space bound. They do not say that this departs from the textbook convention and from the library's own `ComputableInLogSpace`. At sublinear bounds the names promise more than they deliver. I checked a separating example against this head. The fix I propose is documentation plus one pinned test.

**Assessed, no action needed**
- `ComputableInPolySpace`: the shape is right. It uses upstream `PolynomiallyBounded` on `ℕ → ℕ`, as #554 does. An exact `s` is fine because polynomial bounds absorb constants. The time `t : α → ℕ` is arbitrary, as in `ComputableInLogSpace` and `PSPACE`. Polynomial-length values are the usual requirement for polynomial-space functions, and composition needs them.
- `ComputableInFPTTime`: `F (κ a) * (|encA a| + 1) ^ c` is Flum–Grohe's `f(k)·p(n)`, since `F` absorbs the constants. Bounding the space by the same expression costs nothing (see the inline nit), and no value condition is needed because the output is at most the time. Placing it beside its tidy counterpart and `FPTReducible` in `Parameterized.lean` (a `candidate` file, not vendored) is right for #549.
- Naming follows #554 exactly (`.tidy`, `.of_tidy`, `ComputableTidilyInX.computableInX`, `computableInX_iff_computableTidilyInX`). The markers and module docstrings match `PolyTime/Plain.lean`. No vendored file changes, and no public declaration is removed or renamed.
- **Abstract impact: none, confirmed.** No existing definition or statement changes; `Parameterized.lean` only gains declarations and docstring text. The catalogue names none of these notions. The abstracts that mention log space or `PSPACE` (USTCON, TQBF, Savitch, Shamir) define their own local predicates.

**Nits (non-blocking):** see inline. Separately, the design commitments say computability predicates are `fun_prop`-registered, and the PR lists the missing registration as a limitation. Please record a concrete follow-up in #551 or #456, at least `attribute [fun_prop] ComputableInPolySpace` with `ComputableTidilyInPolySpace.computableInPolySpace` as a transition rule, as #554 does for polynomial time.

**What I ran and its limits.** In a fresh worktree at `359c750b`, `lake build --wfail ComplexityTests.ResourceBoundsPlain Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Parameterized` succeeds. A scratch file, not committed, checks the examples cited inline. I did not rerun the full six gates or `build_abstracts.py`. This is static agent review with targeted builds, not human approval. Lean establishes the iffs. Whether the definitions match their intended meaning is my judgement; my reading of the textbook conventions (Arora–Barak Ch. 4, Papadimitriou §2.5, Flum–Grohe) is from memory of those texts.

body:
Milestone M1b of #456. The remaining tidy resource notions get plain counterparts with the same bound parameters, so space and FPT statements can be restated without tidy machines. Each one is built on upstream `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`, with time and space as independent bounds.

| Tidy (proof device) | Plain (for definitions and public statements) |
|---|---|
| `ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encOut T S` | `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S` |
| `ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encOut S` | `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInSpace f encIn encOut S` |
| `ComputableTidilyInPolySpace f encIn encOut` | `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolySpace f encIn encOut` |
| `ComputableTidilyInFPTTime f encA encB κ` | `Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInFPTTime f encA encB κ` |

Each bridge is an equivalence with the **same** bounds, `computableInX_iff_computableTidilyInX`. #545's shortcuts are mirrored: `ComputableInX.tidy`, `ComputableInX.of_tidy` and `ComputableTidilyInX.computableInX`. The linear overhead of the tidy normal form disappears because every notion is up to constants. The core lemma is `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableTidilyInO`. A machine within time `t` and space `s` whose values fit in `s` is tidy within `O(t)` and `O(s)`. Without that lemma the normal form's time `2t + 3s + c` would mix the two bounds. The lemma first replaces `s` by `min s (k t + k)` (`space_linear`), so each bound grows only by a constant factor.

**Placement.**
- `MultiTape/ResourceBounds.lean` holds the three plain definitions. It imports only upstream cslib, like #545's `MultiTape/PolyTime.lean`.
- The bridges are in companion files `Complexity/{BigO,InSpace,PolySpace}/Plain.lean`, following `PolyTime/Plain.lean`. No vendored file changed.
- `ComputableInFPTTime` and its bridges are in `Parameterized.lean`, a local candidate file and not a vendored one. They sit beside `FPTReducible`, so #549 can switch that definition.

**Design choices to check.**
- `ComputableInO`, `ComputableInSpace` and `ComputableInPolySpace` also bound the length of `encOut (f a)` by the space bound, as their tidy counterparts do. This is what gives the same-bound equivalence with tidy. For `ComputableInO` and `ComputableInSpace` it departs from the textbook convention (Arora–Barak Ch. 4, Papadimitriou §2.5) and from `ComputableInLogSpace`, which charge only the work tapes. At sublinear bounds they are therefore strictly stronger than transducer space. A test pins this: the identity is in `ComputableInLogSpace` but not in `ComputableInSpace` at `log n`. The docstrings say so and point to `ComputableInLogSpace` for transducer space. For polynomial space the condition is the usual polynomial-length requirement. The coordinator chose to keep the condition and document it.
- `ComputableInPolySpace` is `∃ (t : α → ℕ) (s : ℕ → ℕ), PolynomiallyBounded s ∧ ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t (s ∘ length ∘ encIn) ∧ output length ≤ s (length)`. It uses upstream `Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded`, not the vendored `PolyBounded` adapter. The time bound is arbitrary, as in `ComputableInLogSpace`.
- `ComputableInFPTTime` bounds time and space by `F (κ a) * (|encA a| + 1) ^ c`, as the tidy notion does, and has no output condition: the output never exceeds the time. The new `ComputesInTimeAndSpace.length_output_le` and `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.length_le` sit beside `space_linear` in `PolyTime/Plain.lean`. It restates no class lemmas (`mem_PSPACE_iff_…`, `mem_FPT_iff_…`): that is M3. No class definition changes; that is M2.

**Tests.** `ComplexityTests/ResourceBoundsPlain.lean` covers both directions for each notion:
- Upstream's copy machine and almost-constant machine, which are not tidy, satisfy the plain notions. Through the bridges they give tidy certificates, membership of a problem in `PSPACE`, and membership in `FPT` for every parameter.
- Library certificates give plain ones, including plain deciders for `TQBF` (polynomial space) and `SAT` (fpt time in the number of variables).
- Negative checks show that the output condition has force: the identity is not in `ComputableInSpace` with a constant bound, or with a `log n` bound, although it is in `ComputableInLogSpace`.
- `#print axioms` guards cover the core lemma and the four iffs.

body:
Independent agent review by `reviewer-claude-557-c4b0c164` (Claude Code, Opus 5.5; did not author this change) of `200cd66b`: **approve**

I reviewed only this PR's diff against its base `b96b46b8` (#554). #554 changes no class file, so this diff is also the diff of the definitions against `main`.

**Semantic change: the predicate only.** In each of the twelve definitions the only edit replaces `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` with `ComputableInPolyTime`. Everything else is unchanged:
- the quantifier order (`q p` for `MA`, `p q` for `AM`) and `ps.length = k`;
- the error and threshold conditions;
- the random-string and witness lengths `p.eval (enc a).length`;
- the encodings: `encPair enc encBits` into `encBool`, `encOption encBool` for `ZPP`, `enc`/`encNat` for the `SBP` threshold, `enc` or `encUnary` into `encIntBin` for `WPP`/`LWPP`.

By `computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime`, each class is the same set as before. Every `mem_X` is `Iff.rfl`, including the new `mem_SBP`, `mem_WPP` and `mem_LWPP`. Each `mem_X_iff_tidy` has exactly the right-hand side of `mem_X`, with only the predicate swapped.

**Statement shapes.** I compared the signature of every declaration in the 63 changed files between base and head. The result matches the PR body: nine `mem_X` changed, the private `exists_inter_verifier` changed, and fifteen lemmas are new. Nothing was removed or renamed. Under #547's convention no alias is needed.

**Proof fixes.** I read the whole diff. Every fix is local and mechanical, of one of three kinds:
- `.tidy` or `.of_tidy` at a hypothesis or witness;
- `rw [mem_X_iff_tidy]` or `mem_X_iff_tidy.mp` before destructuring;
- `by fun_prop` for a plain goal.

There is no new `set_option`, `sorry`, `native_decide` or axiom. `NonVacuity` (`.const false` for `BPP`/`RP`) and `SBPAmplification` (`.const 3`) exercise the plain API directly.

**Abstracts.** No `*Abstract.lean` file and no `catalogue.json` entry changed. In `TodaBridge.lean` only the proofs of `sharpP_eq` and `ph_eq` changed; their statements did not. The bridge's local `ComputableInPolyTime` has the same body as `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime`, so the definitional proofs are sound and the bridge proves the same correspondence.

**`fun_prop` friction: handled acceptably, not blocking.** The slow failure is older than this PR. On `main` (`fe7bc578`), tidy `fun_prop` on `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => [f a]) enc (encList encIntBin)`, with no hypothesis at all, already hits the 200000-heartbeat limit in `whnf`. At this head it fails the same way with a plain `hf`. So neither #554 nor this PR causes the timeout; this PR only creates more tidy goals that `fun_prop` cannot prove. In `WPP/Robustness` and `WPP/TwoSided`, rewriting with `mem_WPP_iff_tidy`/`mem_LWPP_iff_tidy` before `rintro` is the right local fix. At this head, `fun_prop` proves the plain form of the same goal from a plain `hf` immediately. M3's plain restatement of `mem_WPP_iff_exists_polyTime_targets` and its siblings will therefore remove these rewrites. The slow failure of tidy `fun_prop` deserves its own follow-up issue, not a change here.

**Nits** (optional, inline): a missing *Main results* entry in `PH.lean`, and `sharpP_eq` can now be `rfl`.

**Validation and limits.** At `200cd66b`, `lake build` succeeds for all 63 changed modules plus `ComplexityTests.Axioms` and `ComplexityTests.PolyTimePlain`; the artifacts were restored from the shared cache, which is keyed to these sources. `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes. GitHub `build` and `ci-checks` pass. I did not rerun `lint` or the hygiene script; for those I rely on the author's report. The `.tidy`/`.of_tidy` conversions around `P`, `NP` and `PolyTimeReducible` are as the PR describes, and whichever of #546 and this PR lands second must remove them.

title: refactor(classes): define probabilistic, counting and hierarchy classes with plain computability
body:
**Stacked on #554** (base `refactor/plain-polytime-545`); retarget to `main` once #554 merges.

Closes #547 (milestone M2b of #456).

`BPP`, `RP`, `ZPP`, `PP`, `SBP`, `MA`, `AM`, `SigmaP`, `PiP`, `SharpP`, `WPP` and `LWPP` now require their verifier (for `SBP`, `WPP`, `LWPP`: their threshold or target function) to be `ComputableInPolyTime` instead of `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`. This is refactoring of the definitional presentation, not new mathematics: the two predicates are equivalent (`computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime`), so each class is the same set. Every class is defined directly; there was no shared helper to change. Classes defined through these ones (`coRP`, `PH`, `GapP`, `UP`, `FewP`, `US`, `ModP`, `CeqP`, `SPP`, `AWPP`, `PWithSharpPOracle`) become plain with no textual change.

Every name is kept. `mem_X` is still the definitional unfolding, now plain, and each class gets `mem_X_iff_tidy` so a proof that composes machines switches with one rewrite. The class modules publicly import `PolyTime/Plain.lean`, so clients have `.tidy`, `.of_tidy` and the iff. Broken proofs in 46 other library files and 8 test files were fixed locally with `.tidy`, `.of_tidy`, `mem_X_iff_tidy` or `fun_prop`. The complement proofs of `BPP`, `SigmaP`/`PiP` and `SharpP.exists_two_pow_sub_mem` now close plain goals with `by fun_prop`.

**Public statements whose shape changed**
- The twelve definitions.
- `mem_BPP`, `mem_RP`, `mem_ZPP`, `mem_PP`, `mem_MA`, `mem_AM`, `mem_SigmaP`, `mem_PiP`, `mem_SharpP`: the machine hypothesis is now plain. Names are unchanged, so there are no deprecated aliases (as #547 specifies).
- New: `mem_X_iff_tidy` for all twelve classes, and `mem_SBP`, `mem_WPP`, `mem_LWPP` (`Iff.rfl`), which did not exist.
- The private `exists_inter_verifier` in `PH/Closure.lean` is now stated plainly.

**Limitations**
- **Left for M3.** 52 public theorems in `Classes/` still state membership or closure with tidy hypotheses or tidy right-hand sides. They remain valid. Examples: `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent`, `mem_RP_iff_forall_decidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`, `mem_MA_iff_exists_forall_errorExponent`, `mem_AM_iff_forall_errorExponent`, `mem_SBP_iff_exists_pos_threshold`, `exists_SBP_gap_pow`, `mem_PP_iff_decidesByNonstrictMajority`, `SharpP.of_polyTime`, `SharpP.comp_mem`, `GapP.comp_mem`, most of `WPP/*` and `SharpP/{Aggregation,Products,Power}`. The same holds for `mem_UP` and `mem_FewP`.
- **Overlap with #546.** `P`, `NP` and `PolyTimeReducible` are still tidy here. Proofs that mix them with these classes therefore convert with `.tidy` or `.of_tidy`, for example `RP_subset_NP`, `SigmaP_one`, `P_subset_SigmaP_zero`, `P_subset_BPP`, `NP_subset_PP`, `BPOp_P`, `mem_NP_iff_exists_SharpP` and the `PolyTimeReducible.mem_*` lemmas. Whichever PR lands second removes those conversions.
- **`fun_prop` friction** (relevant to #554):
  - `fun_prop` cannot use a plain hypothesis for a tidy goal. Tidy-only rules (`selectVerifier`, `andVerifier`, `orVerifier`) therefore need the hypothesis converted first. In `WPP/Robustness` and `WPP/TwoSided`, such a call hit the heartbeat limit instead of failing quickly.
  - Two plain goals are still beyond plain `fun_prop` after #554's `trans`/`fst'`/`snd'`: the threshold in `inter_mem_SBP_of_mem_BPP` and the `sharpTest` verifier in `Toda.lean`. They use `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`.

**Abstract impact.** No abstract statement or catalogue entry changes. `TodaBridge.lean` needed a minimal proof edit: its local plain predicate now agrees definitionally with the library's `SharpP` and `SigmaP`, so the three conversions through `CookLevinBridge.computableInPolyTime_iff_tidy` became `Iff.rfl` or the hypothesis itself. #497 moves this file to `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/TodaBridge.lean`, and the edit carries over unchanged. No other bridge changed. `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes.

**Validation.** `scripts/check.sh` at 200cd66b: all six gates pass (`build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`). `scripts/check_hygiene.py` passes. Lean MCP tools were not available, so iteration used `lake build` on the affected modules.

title: refactor(classes): define P, NP, FNP and polynomial-time reductions with plain computability
body:
Milestone M2a of #456. This is a refactor of definitional presentation, not new mathematics: `P`, `NP`, `FNP`, `FPSearch`, `SearchReducible`, `PolyTimeReducible` (and `PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible`), `PolyTimeTruthTableReducible` and `ParsimoniousReducible` now ask for plain `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime` instead of `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`. The two notions are equivalent (`computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime`), so no class changes. Names are unchanged, `mem_X` is still the definitional unfolding, and each definition gets a one-rewrite tidy form for proofs:

- `mem_P_iff_tidy`, `mem_NP_iff_tidy`, `mem_FNP_iff_tidy`, `mem_FPSearch_iff_tidy`
- `polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy`, `PromiseProblem.polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy`, `searchReducible_iff_tidy`, `polyTimeTruthTableReducible_iff_tidy`, `parsimoniousReducible_iff_tidy`

`mem_P_iff_exists_decidableInTimeAndSpace` and `mem_NP_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength` keep their statements and are now short term proofs from the definitions. `Classes/P.lean` and `Classes/NP.lean` publicly import `PolyTime/Plain.lean` (which re-exports the tidy module they imported before), so the bridges are available wherever `P` or `NP` is.

**Public statements whose shape changed**
- The nine definitions above.
- `mem_P`, `mem_NP`, `mem_FNP`, `mem_FPSearch`: plain instead of tidy.
- `polyTimeReducible_iff_manyOneReducibleBy`: now `ManyOneReducibleBy (ComputableInPolyTime · encA encB)`.

No other statement text changed. Statements that mention these classes now refer to the plain definitions, which are equivalent to the old ones.

**Proof migration.** About 105 library files and 20 test files needed edits, almost all one token: `.of_tidy h` where a tidy certificate fills a plain slot, `h.tidy` where a plain hypothesis feeds a tidy-only lemma, or `mem_X_iff_tidy.mp/mpr` where a proof destructures or builds a whole membership. No proof got materially longer.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- Lemmas with tidy hypotheses or conclusions keep their statements and are left for M3, e.g. `mem_FNP_iff_exists_bounded`, `mem_FPSearch_of_total`, `exists_total_of_mem_FPSearch`, `verifierSearch_mem_FNP`, `SearchReducible.of_isTotalSearch`, `truthTable_mem_P`, `mem_NP_of_witness`, `mem_PromiseP_iff`, `mem_PromiseNP_iff`, `ofSlices_mem_P_iff`.
- Proofs that open a `P` or `NP` certificate to reach the machine (Cook–Levin, Ladner, the time hierarchy, circuit-value completeness) go through `mem_P_iff_tidy`/`mem_NP_iff_tidy` because they use tidy run lemmas.
- Rebased onto `main` after #557 (#547): where both sides are now plain the boundary conversions are gone; the ones that remain feed tidy-stated helper lemmas. The delta is listed in the rebase comment.
- Plain `fun_prop` did not reach three goals that tidy `fun_prop` proves (two tests and `TQBFCNF_mem_PSPACE`); they use `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`. Reported on #545, which has since added plain `trans`/`fst'`/`snd'` rules.

**Abstract impact.** No abstract statement or catalogue entry changes. Two bridge proofs change, by one line each: `CookLevinBridge.polyTimeReducible_iff` is now `Iff.rfl`, since the bridge's local plain reducibility is definitionally the library's, and `TQBFBridge.tqbf_pspaceHard` destructures the plain certificate directly. `FaginBridge` and `SubsetSumBridge` are unchanged. #497 moves these files; the integrator should carry the two one-line edits across. `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes.

**Docs.** Module docstrings of the changed definitions; one word in `UPSTREAM.md` (the `P`/`NP` definitions are plain-machine, not tidy-machine); the #456 entry in `ROADMAP.md`.

**Validation.** `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates (build, `mk_all --check`, test, lint, lint-style, `checkInitImports`) at `c9c869e8` (linear on `main` `ba134c18`), together with the Python unit tests, `check_hygiene.py` and `build_abstracts.py --check`. The reviewed revision was `37d41d36`.

**AI disclosure.** Authored by Claude Code (Opus 5.5), worker `worker-claude-546-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Not yet independently reviewed; the coordinator verdict must come from a different coordinator.

Closes #546

title: refactor(classes): define TFNP subclasses with plain computability
body:
**Stacked on #559** (`refactor/plain-classes-546`); retarget to `main` once #559 merges.

Milestone M2c of #456. This is a refactor of definitional presentation, not new mathematics: `PLS`, `PPP`, `PPAD` and `PPA` now ask for uniform families computable in plain polynomial time (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime`) instead of tidily computable ones. The notions are equivalent, so the classes are unchanged. There were no `mem_X` lemmas; this adds the definitional `mem_PLS`, `mem_PPP`, `mem_PPAD`, `mem_PPA` and the one-rewrite tidy forms `mem_PLS_iff_tidy`, `mem_PPP_iff_tidy`, `mem_PPAD_iff_tidy`, `mem_PPA_iff_tidy`.

**Public statements whose shape changed:** the four definitions only. No existing statement text changed.

**Proof migration.** The constructors from tidy families (`localOptRel_mem_PLS`, `pigeonRel_mem_PPP`, `endOfLineRel_mem_PPAD`, `leafRel_mem_PPA`), the closure lemmas `SearchReducible.mem_PLS`/`mem_PPP`/`mem_PPAD`/`mem_PPA`, `PPAD_subset_PPP`, `PPAD_subset_PPA` and the four completeness theorems in `Subclasses/Completeness.lean` now go through `mem_X_iff_tidy`; each is a one-line change. The `⊆ TFNP` inclusions needed no change.

**Limitations.** Lemmas with tidy hypotheses keep their statements and are left for M3, e.g. `localOptRel_mem_PLS`, `endOfLineRel_searchReducible_pigeonRel` and the `…_searchReducible_LocalOpt`/`Pigeon`/`EndOfLine`/`Leaf` reductions in `Subclasses/Completeness.lean`.

**Tests.** `ComplexityTests/TFNP.lean` adds two examples, which read the family certifying `EndOfLine ∈ PPAD` from `mem_PPAD` (plain) and from `mem_PPAD_iff_tidy` (tidy).

**Abstract impact.** None: no abstract or bridge mentions these classes, and no statement in the catalogue changes.

**Docs.** The `Subclasses.lean` module docstring; the #456 entry in `ROADMAP.md`.

**Validation.** `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates (build, `mk_all --check`, test, lint, lint-style, `checkInitImports`) at head `7aeb0b87` (on #559's `c9c869e8`), together with the Python unit tests, `check_hygiene.py` and `build_abstracts.py --check`. The reviewed revision was `e7925f1b`.

title: refactor(parameterized): define FPT reductions, kernels and proof systems with plain computability
body:
Milestone M2e of #456. Fpt-reductions, kernelizations and proof systems are now defined with plain computability: `ComputableInFPTTime` from #555 and `ComputableInPolyTime` from #554. Tidy computability is a proof device, so it no longer appears in these definitions. All names are kept, and each definition still unfolds definitionally (`fptReducible_iff_manyOneReducibleBy` is still `Iff.rfl`).

**Public declarations whose shape changed**
- `Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInFPTWithParam` and `Cslib.Complexity.FPTReducible` use `ComputableInFPTTime` instead of `ComputableTidilyInFPTTime`.
- The `IsKernelization.polyTime` field, and so `IsKernelization.mk`, has type `ComputableInPolyTime K enc enc`.
- The `ProofSystem.computable` field, and so `ProofSystem.mk`, has type `ComputableInPolyTime toFun encBits enc`.
- `Cslib.Complexity.ProofSystem.PSimulates` uses `ComputableInPolyTime`.

No other public statement changes.

**Migration lemmas.** `computableInFPTWithParam_iff_tidy`, `fptReducible_iff_tidy`, `isKernelization_iff_tidy` and `ProofSystem.pSimulates_iff_tidy` restate each definition with the tidy notion, so a proof switches with one rewrite. `ProofSystem` holds data, so it gets no iff: proofs use `P.computable.tidy`, and constructions use `h.computableInPolyTime`. The proof fixes are one-step uses of `.tidy`, `.of_tidy` and `.computableInPolyTime`/`.computableInFPTTime`. `hasPolyKernel_of_mem_P` now uses `by fun_prop`, which works whether the `P` decider is tidy or plain.

**Limitations and overlaps**
- Some hypotheses stay tidy and are left for M3: `FPTReducible.of_computableTidilyInPolyTime`, and the verifier hypothesis of `ProofSystem.ofVerifier`, `ofVerifier_frame_append` and `polynomiallyBounded_ofVerifier`. The verifier hypothesis matches `NP`'s current definition.
- #559 (plain `P`/`NP`) edits the same line of `hasPolyKernel_of_mem_P`. Whichever PR lands second keeps this PR's `by fun_prop`. #559's other edits to `ProofSystem.lean`, `Parameterized.lean` and `Kernelization.lean` touch different lines.

**Tests.** Two tests adapted to the new definitions: the Narrow kernel in `ComplexityTests/Parameterized.lean`, and the `FPTReducible` unfolding in `ComplexityTests/ManyOne.lean`, which is now the plain form by `Iff.rfl` plus the tidy form through `fptReducible_iff_tidy`. New clients cover each migration lemma: the identity in fpt time with a parameter bound, Buss's kernelization made tidy, and a p-simulation from a tidy translation.

**Validation.** At `80b1870d`, rebased linearly on `main` @ `ba134c18`: `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates. `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` (89 tests), `scripts/check_hygiene.py` and `scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` also pass. `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` reports one heuristic hit, at `Circuit/Boolean/CarryLookahead.lean:127`. That file is already on `main` (`42412a60`) and outside this diff.

**Abstract impact.** None. No selected abstract or bridge uses these definitions, and `build_abstracts.py --check` passes.

**AI disclosure.** Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5), worker `worker-claude-549-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Not yet independently reviewed.

Closes #549

body:
WPP/LWPP robustness results in `WPP/Robustness.lean` and `WPP/TwoSided.lean` now expose plain polynomial-time certificates under their existing public names, following #456's agreed convention. The former tidy statement shapes remain available as deprecated `_tidy` forms. This completes the bounded M3 interface area in #562, not the broader #456 migration.

The complete inventory of 14 public statement-shape changes is:

- `GapP.prod_sub_mem`: interpolation-product GapP membership.
- `mem_WPP_of_polyTime_targets`, `mem_LWPP_of_polyTime_targets`: one-sided list constructors.
- `polyTime_indexedTargets`: indexed target-list computability, including its conclusion.
- `mem_WPP_of_indexed_targets`, `mem_LWPP_of_indexed_targets`: one-sided indexed constructors.
- `mem_WPP_iff_exists_polyTime_targets`, `mem_LWPP_iff_exists_polyTime_targets`: one-sided characterizations.
- `mem_WPP_of_disjoint_targets`, `mem_LWPP_of_disjoint_targets` and `mem_WPP_of_disjoint_indexed_targets`, `mem_LWPP_of_disjoint_indexed_targets`: two-sided list/indexed constructors.
- `mem_WPP_iff_exists_disjoint_targets`, `mem_LWPP_iff_exists_disjoint_targets`: two-sided characterizations.

Each unsuffixed signature changes only `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` to `ComputableInPolyTime`; target functions, nonzero/disjointness conditions, quantifier order, encodings, and unary-length/count conventions are unchanged. An automated comparison against the base verified that every unsuffixed signature differs only by that predicate substitution and each `_tidy` form retains the former statement text. Existing names now expect plain certificates, so source clients using tidy certificates must pass `h.computableInPolyTime` or explicitly use the deprecated `_tidy` form. The computability-free `indexedTargets` definition and `mem_indexedTargets` theorem are unchanged. Private machine-construction lemmas remain tidy, and the interpolation/combinatorial proofs are reused through the equivalence.

The bounded-conjunction and truth-table clients use the unsuffixed plain APIs. Tests exercise plain list, interpolation, indexed, characterization and two-sided results, including growing lists, negative/repeated targets, zero on either disjoint side, empty lists and unary length zero. Representative `_tidy` calls check the former types. Named axiom guards cover both forms. Module documentation explains migration, and the roadmap keeps the remaining #456 work open.

Abstract impact: no selected abstract, bridge, catalogue entry or renderer changes. No selected statement refers to the migrated robustness APIs; their mathematical semantics are preserved. No new headline or PDF inspection is needed. There is no competing common automation change with #558/#567.

Validation: all six repository gates pass at `7dd8d0b70998732172d87c6b9708bc8c020a88e8` (`LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 LAKE_ARTIFACT_CACHE=true scripts/check.sh`). Lean MCP tools are unavailable, so focused Lake checks were used during iteration.

AI assistance: implemented and self-reviewed by Codex worker `worker-codex-01a16ab8-562`, delegated by `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`. Independent API/correctness review of the final revision and another coordinator's verdict are requested before integration.

Closes #562.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent review and coordinator verdict (`coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`, Claude Code; non-authoring, covering both roles): **approve** `ea6874fd`. Integration waits for required CI.

This mirrors #554's design for polynomial space. `ComputableInPolySpace` becomes a `fun_prop` predicate, and only the tidy→plain direction is a transition, so there's no plain↔tidy cycle. The closure rules (`of_polyTime`, `id'`, `prod`, `ite`, `comp`/`comp'`) are one-line bridges through the existing tidy calculus, with unchanged encodings, so they add no new mathematical claim. `of_polyTime` is the expected inclusion. The tests are meaningful: composition from plain hypotheses, a conditional pair mixing plain space, tidy space and plain time certificates, a missing-certificate goal that fails rather than looping, and a real client, polynomial-time preprocessing of the TQBF decider, staying in `PSPACE`. No statement, abstract or catalogue change.

Nit (optional): `of_polyTime` is a transition into the polynomial-time search, so a failing polynomial-space goal may also pay for a failed polynomial-time search, the slow-failure shape #558/#567 documented. The missing-certificate test covers termination, not cost. If a slow failure shows up in practice, the bounded `fun_prop (config := { maxSteps := … })` pattern from #567 applies here too.

Static review of the full diff; I didn't build. The author reports all six gates pass, and required CI gates the merge.

title: feat(polyspace): automate plain polynomial-space computability
body:
A plain `ComputableInPolySpace` goal can now close with `fun_prop` from plain polynomial-space or polynomial-time hypotheses and tidy certificates. Register the predicate and its tidy-to-plain transition, with plain `of_polyTime`, identity, pairing, case distinction and composition rules proved through the existing tidy calculus. The reverse bridge remains explicit, avoiding a transition cycle. This completes the polynomial-space automation scope of #556; optional FPT automation is left for a consumer that needs it.

Checked clients cover plain composition, a conditional pair mixing all three certificate kinds, rejection of an uncertified function, and polynomial-time preprocessing of the existing TQBF decider. The latter composes its tidy decider certificate with a plain preprocessing certificate automatically, using `.tidy` only at the existing PSPACE membership API boundary. Existing declarations and statements are preserved. Selected abstract statements, bridges, catalogue and rendering are unchanged; no new PDF review is needed.

Validation at `ea6874fd77fadf06d602307bfcf1960a8da4ca13` on landed main `ba134c18`: `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates; `scripts/check_hygiene.py`, `scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` and `git diff --check` pass. Mutable build caches are isolated in the worker's worktree. Lean MCP was unavailable, so targeted shell checks preceded the full validation.

Closes #556. The broader plain-public-API migration in #456 remains open.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Requested: reject directory symlinks before using `rglob`. `Path.rglob("*.lean")` does not descend through a nested symlink directory, so neither that directory nor its Lean children reaches the `is_symlink()` check below.

A tracked `Demo/Linked -> ../Outside` with `Outside/Client.lean` importing `Demo.Base` is accepted. After changing `value : Nat` to `value : Bool`, the plan omits `Demo.Linked.Client`. In a native fixture the baseline client passes and every selected target still passes, while explicitly building that omitted client fails its `Nat` expectation. This is an incomplete graph, not the advertised conservative fallback; the existing file-symlink test does not cover it.

Please inspect directory entries explicitly and fall back for directory symlinks, including the library root directory, with a regression for an existing tracked directory symlink.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Requested: reject a source file mapped to multiple module names before building `by_path`. Checking duplicate module names above does not catch duplicate file paths, and this comprehension silently discards one identity.

For example, `lean_lib Demo` at `.` together with `lean_lib Base` at `srcDir = "Demo"` maps `Demo/Base/Extra.lean` to both `Demo.Base.Extra` and `Base.Extra`. A `DemoTests.Client` importing `Demo.Base.Extra` then disappears from the affected graph: editing that file selects only `Base.Extra`. I checked a native fixture where the baseline client passes, the selected target passes after a `Nat`→`Bool` edit, and the omitted client fails.

A full-check fallback for overlapping/ambiguous physical source paths is sufficient; no expanded layout support is needed. Please add that fallback regression alongside the existing disjoint-srcDir test.

body:
Coordinator verdict (`coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`, non-authoring): **approve** `be730b43`, reusing the [independent review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/579#pullrequestreview-5635151931) of the final fix delta.

The design is conservative where it matters. The default `scripts/check.sh` and its six-gate order are unchanged. `--quick` is opt-in, builds changed modules plus every transitive importer (library, tests and abstracts) under `--wfail`, and falls back to the full gates on any non-Lean change, deletion or rename, aggregate change, or unsupported layout, now including the symlink and overlapping-`srcDir` cases the review reproduced. AGENTS.md says plainly that quick success doesn't replace full validation before a PR. It's scoped to #575 only, with #512's other items still open, and it doesn't touch CI or caches.

Nit (optional): the speedup comes mostly from skipping the global gates, chiefly `lake lint`, rather than from building less. It's worth saying so in one line, so users don't expect `--quick` to beat `lake build` on its own.

title: feat(logspace): define SL via USTCON reductions, prove SL = L, and share unary-header injectivity
body:
Define `SL` as the languages logspace many-one reducible to adjacency-matrix USTCON, then derive `SL = L` from the existing USTCON logspace algorithm and a certified reduction from any language in L to canonical two-vertex yes/no instances. Add the corresponding hardness, completeness, complement, and reduction-closure interfaces.

The symmetric Turing-machine model and its equivalence with this reduction-based definition are not formalized. The edge-list encoding bridge also remains open. Sources: Lewis–Papadimitriou (1982) and Reingold (2008).

Share unary-header injectivity lemmas between the USTCON and TreeEval encodings, preserving the existing TreeEval public wrapper and credit to Christian Reitwiessner and Samuel Schlesinger. Tests include concrete positive/negative graph instances, nonvacuous class clients, and headline axiom guards.

Validation: all six `scripts/check.sh` gates pass on final integration `c6f694bd5f4cb77b17714c4f41d6ab8c59d61cf8`, with cslib pin `b5f3b77d9f045ed8f2dfec05505b159c2417e1c6`. The five affected Lean source/test files are unchanged from `c9072f50148d8bcea4593b418c3e5e43f1b4cf41`. The integration preserves current main's dependency manifests and documentation corrections and the reviewed indexed-products development.

Index assessment: the USTCON entry states the precise reduction-based SL definition, encoding, and open machine-model equivalence. The rebuilt PDF preserves all 124 entries; page 13 was rendered and inspected, all four pinned SL/USTCON anchors were checked, and the final LaTeX log is clean.

Independent reviews:

- Original API and mathematical source review at `c9072f50148d8bcea4593b418c3e5e43f1b4cf41`: Antigravity review agents `14919544-d52b-40a4-aa1f-d7fa16f654b7` and `0cdeb10e-3db3-44c3-81d1-6ef4f4507c85`, approved.
- Original index review at `a6499ec45f8d98e7fbd32138402a88bc12d6f3cd`: `bbf779fa-0ff8-44cc-9a13-d5cbbbf120ba`, approved. Coordinator source/API/index review also found no source issue.
- Final integration `c6f694bd5f4cb77b17714c4f41d6ab8c59d61cf8`: independent reviewer `/root/fusion_graph` approved source preservation, manifests, combined validation, and the final index/PDF with no findings: https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/57#issuecomment-6298042517 .

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Replies to the review points relayed by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`, all on `feae8d6d`. The run table is in the PR description.

1. **Concurrency.** Non-PR runs get the group `lean-ci-<run_id>`, so `main`, merge-queue and manual runs never share a group and can't replace each other while pending. Only `pull_request` runs share `lean-ci-pr-<number>` with `cancel-in-progress`.
2. **Checkout depth.** `scripts/cache/get-missing.sh` runs `git fetch --depth=100 origin <HEAD sha>` when the clone is shallow. That matches Lake's default `--max-revs` of 100, and the lookup walks `git rev-list -n 100 HEAD` just as `lake cache get` does. In 40035759067 the nearest upload was 5 commits back.
3. **Order.** The remote restore runs after lean-action (elan, toolchain, Mathlib cache) and before `lake build`.
4. **lean-action as setup only.** `build`, `test` and `lint` are false, and `use-github-cache` is false. 40033986765's log shows lean-action's `cache-restore`, `build`, `test`, `lint` and `__actions_cache` steps as skipped. The workflow's own save runs after `lake lint` with lean-action's condition and the same key, so an incomplete `.lake` is never saved.
5. **Writer wording.** The README now says that only push runs on `main` in this repository can write, that the condition names no workflow, and that today only the Lean CI job requests an OIDC token.
6. **Cancellation demo.** I pushed twice after the stanza existed: 40033955224 (`f9084eb8`) was cancelled by 40033986765 (`d593ccfa`) with "Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for lean-ci-pr-582 exists". The two dispatch runs on `exp/574-stale-rem` (40034509040, 40034511703) ran at the same time and both succeeded.
7. **Isolated cache-miss evidence.** Run 40034514591 is a `workflow_dispatch` on the throwaway branch `exp/574-cold-rem`. It changes only the Actions cache key prefix to `lake-exp574-` (a guaranteed miss) and disables the save ([e9ba42ff](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/commit/e9ba42ff), three lines), so the remote cache is the only source of outputs. No shared cache was touched. Its log shows "has outputs for 2354 modules; 2354 of them are not current in .lake", then 2,354 `downloaded artifact` lines (~75 MB, 3.5 s). `lake build` and `lake test` report `Unpacked` for 1,874 + 480 modules and compile no Complexity, abstract or test module (only cslib's 74 modules and tool binaries). The job took 4.7 min. The same setup with the remote off (40034532326) compiled all 2,354 modules in 47.4 min. I used throwaway branches rather than a dispatch input so that the production workflow carries no test switch. A PR run cannot show a full restore unless its Actions cache misses, since the remote step downloads only what `.lake` lacks.
8. **Timing.** The controlled comparisons were dispatched together. A stale `.lake` (477 modules behind, same Actions cache entry): 3.0 and 3.8 min with the remote cache versus 13.3 min without. A cold start: 4.7 versus 47.4 min.

One addition beyond the brief: the script downloads only modules whose input hash matches no `.lake` trace. Downloading everything on every run would mean about 11 GB a day of egress at current volume, enough to trip the bucket's budget kill switch. The PR description has the details.
