title: ci: cancel superseded PR runs and restore from the remote build cache
body:
Closes #574.

Lean CI now cancels a pull request's superseded run, and before building it downloads from the remote cache the outputs that `main` CI already built, so a run whose GitHub Actions copy of `.lake` is stale or evicted no longer recompiles them. This is infrastructure only; no Lean source changes.

**Concurrency.** Pull-request runs share the group `lean-ci-pr-<number>` and cancel the run they supersede. Every other run (`main` pushes, merge-queue groups, manual runs) is alone in `lean-ci-<run_id>`, so none of them is cancelled, or replaced while pending as a shared group would do even without `cancel-in-progress`. The `ci-checks` job name is unchanged.

**Remote restore.** lean-action has no hook between installing the toolchain and building, so it now only installs elan and fetches Mathlib's cache (`build`, `test`, `lint` and `use-github-cache` set to false; its own cache restore, build, test, lint and cache save are skipped in the logs). The workflow restores and saves `.lake` itself with lean-action's key, path and save condition (`actions/cache` pinned to the SHA lean-action uses), and runs `lake build`, `lake test` and `lake lint` with the same arguments. The save still runs only after the build succeeds, so an incomplete `.lake` is never saved. Between the two, the new `scripts/cache/get-missing.sh`:

- deepens the depth-1 checkout to 100 generations, since Lake's lookup walks the first 100 commits of `git rev-list HEAD`;
- finds the nearest uploaded revision, as `lake cache get` does;
- drops mapping entries whose input hash already matches a trace in `.lake/build`;
- downloads the rest with `lake cache get <mapping> --repo=cslib-community/complexitylib`.

A miss, a timeout (10 minutes) or an unreachable bucket only leaves the build colder (`continue-on-error`). The filter matters because Lake consults its artifact cache before `.lake` traces, and that cache starts empty on every runner. A plain `lake cache get` would therefore download a complete set (about 75 MB) on every run. At 150–200 runs a day that comes to about 11 GB a day, several times the 100 GB-a-month free egress tier, and it would hit the 10 USD budget whose kill switch makes the bucket private.

**Evidence.** All runs below use this PR's workflow. The `exp/574-*` runs are `workflow_dispatch` runs on throwaway branches. Each differs from the PR only by the toggles shown, and none saves to the Actions cache. Times are `ci-checks` job durations.

| Scenario | Run | `.lake` from the Actions cache | Remote cache | Compiled (build + test) | Restored from remote | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Actions cache miss, remote on | [40034514591](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034514591) | none (forced miss) | 2,354 artifacts, ~75 MB in 3.5 s | no Complexity modules (74 cslib modules, plus native code for lint tools) | 2,354 | **4.7 min** |
| Actions cache miss, remote off | [40034532326](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034532326) | none (forced miss) | disabled | all 2,354 library, abstract and test modules (plus the same cslib and tooling) | 0 | **47.4 min** |
| Stale `.lake`, remote on (×2) | [40034509040](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034509040), [40034511703](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034511703) | `fd5c03e5`, 477 modules behind | 477 artifacts, 12.5 MB | 0 | 477 | **3.0, 3.8 min** |
| Stale `.lake`, remote off | [40034506321](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034506321) | `fd5c03e5`, same | disabled | 477 | 0 | **13.3 min** |
| This PR, current `.lake` | [40033986765](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033986765) | `0a3b3f66` | 0 missing, nothing downloaded | 6 tooling jobs | 0 | 4.1 min |
| This PR, `main` ahead of its uploads | [40035759067](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40035759067) | `fd5c03e5` | newest upload `fd5c03e5`, 0 missing | 428 | 0 | 13.6 min |

The stale pair builds `a029f89c`'s sources (an uploaded `main` commit) against the newest `main` copy of `.lake`; in recent PR runs a stale copy recompiled 250–480 modules, taking 11–20 minutes. The four controlled runs were dispatched together; the stale ones restored the same Actions cache entry. Toggles: forced miss = cache key prefix `lake-exp574-`; remote off = `COMPLEXITYLIB_CACHE_URL: ""` on the restore step; no save = `if: false` on the save step (e.g. [e9ba42ff](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/commit/e9ba42ff), the forced-miss run with remote on). For reference, recent PR runs under the old workflow took 11–15 minutes (#563 11m10s, #559 11m41s, #497 14m38s), and cold ones 31–47 minutes (40025177553, 40024674388, 40017135006).

Concurrency on real runs: this PR's [40033955224](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033955224) was cancelled by [40033986765](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033986765) ("Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for lean-ci-pr-582 exists"). The two dispatch runs on `exp/574-stale-rem` above ran at the same time and both succeeded. `actionlint` 1.7.12 with shellcheck 0.11.0 passes on the workflow, and shellcheck passes on the script.

**Trust.** CI now reuses outputs that `main` CI produced, so a restored module is not re-checked by the kernel in that run. `scripts/cache/README.md` explains why this adds no party to trust. The Actions cache CI already restores holds copies saved by runs on `main`, a superset of the remote cache's writers, and Lake reuses them in the same way. The README also says what still compiles: every module whose input hash differs from what `main` built, which covers everything a PR changes and every module that imports it. It also corrects the writer description: Workload Identity Federation admits any push run on `main` that requests an OIDC token, not one named workflow, and today only Lean CI requests one.

**Limitations.**
- The remote cache helps only up to the newest commit that `main` CI has finished uploading. During a burst of merges, PR runs still compile the gap, as in 40035759067. `main` runs now restore too, which shortens that lag.
- PR and merge-queue runs still save 2.8 GB `.lake` copies to the Actions cache, unchanged from before. With five entries filling a 13.9 GB cache, they evict `main`'s copies within minutes. Saving only on `main` may now be better; that is left as a follow-up.
- `get-missing.sh` reads Lake's trace (`depHash`) and mapping formats. If they change, the filter keeps every entry and CI downloads a complete set, which stays correct but costs more egress. Like `get.sh`, it passes endpoints by environment variable, which Lake reports as deprecated.
- cslib has no prebuilt cache, so a run without a `.lake` copy still compiles cslib's 74 modules (within the 1.7-minute build step of 40034514591).
- Lake replays no warnings for restored modules. This loses nothing for `--wfail`, because `main` uploads only outputs that passed `--wfail` (see the README).
- The `exp/574-*` branches can be deleted once this is reviewed.

**Abstracts.** No impact: workflow, cache script and documentation only; no Lean statement, definition or catalogue entry changes.

title: ci(docs): publish the API documentation to GitHub Pages
body:
Publishes the doc-gen4 API documentation to GitHub Pages at https://www.cslib.io/complexitylib/ and points README "Start here" at its search. The organisation's Pages domain applies, so `cslib-community.github.io/complexitylib/` redirects there. Until now, users looking for a definition or tool were sent to `Complexity.lean`, a flat list of about 1,870 imports; `Complexity.lean` stays linked for the full module list. This is item 1 of #578, which Samuel approved there. Infrastructure and documentation only: no Lean changes, no mathematical progress, and no effect on the abstracts catalogue.

**Workflow.** `docs.yml` keeps its build and the `check_docs.py` gate. It then checks the site size and uploads the Pages artifact. A separate `deploy` job runs `configure-pages` and `deploy-pages` into the `github-pages` environment, only for builds of `main`. That job alone has `pages: write` and `id-token: write`; the build job keeps `contents: read`. The three Pages actions are pinned to full commit SHAs (configure-pages v6.0.0, upload-pages-artifact v5.0.0, deploy-pages v5.0.1). A manual run on another branch builds and checks the docs, uploads `api-docs` as before, and skips the deploy job. Pull requests don't trigger the workflow, so they can't deploy.

**Triggers.** Nightly (03:17 UTC) and `workflow_dispatch`, without `push`. `main` received 64 pushes in the 24 hours before this PR and a build takes about an hour, so nearly every push-triggered build would be cancelled by the next merge after spending most of a runner-hour. Nightly keeps the site at most a day behind; a dispatch on `main` refreshes it at once. A per-ref `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: true` lets a newer build supersede an older one, so only the latest build of `main` deploys.

**Size: the main limitation.** Pages caps a published site at 1 GB, and the docs are close to it. The 22 October build (1,647 modules, run 39794423110) is 55 MB compressed but 962,395,848 bytes uncompressed in 8,260 files: Mathlib pages 570 MB, `Complexity` 106 MB, Std 94 MB, Init 74 MB, the search index 48 MB and Lean 46 MB. The 18 October build (703 modules) was 807 MB. The validation run below (current `main`, 1,874 modules) measured 973,243,475 bytes: 90.6 % of 1 GiB, about 100 MB of headroom. `main` gained about 135 modules a day over the past three days, roughly 6.5 MB a day at the recent per-module cost, so at that pace the limit is about two weeks away, sooner if new modules pull in more of Mathlib. The workflow fails before deploying if the site exceeds 1 GiB (the value `deploy-pages` uses for "1 GB"), warns above 90 %, and writes the size to the job summary; after a failed run Pages keeps serving the previous deployment. Keeping the site under the limit needs a follow-up. Measured options: `DISABLE_EQUATIONS=1` removes about 48 MB (equation blocks), and dropping the 829 Lean/Std/Lake modules outside the library's import closure (doc-gen4 always documents them) about 37 MB. Together they would add about two more weeks at that pace. A lasting fix would link Mathlib declarations to an external Mathlib docs site instead of hosting its 570 MB of pages, or host the docs somewhere without the 1 GB cap.

**Subpath and search.** No base-path setting is needed. Every page sets a relative `SITE_ROOT`, the search index stores relative `docLink`s (all 320,004 entries), and a scan of the 3.9 million `href`/`src` attributes found no root-relative links. The leanprover-community `mathlib4_docs` site runs the same doc-gen4 `search.js` and `declaration-data.js` (byte-identical) from a Pages subpath, and its `.//declarations/declaration-data.bmp` request resolves there. Two small caveats are unrelated to the subpath. `404.html` uses relative asset paths, so it is unstyled when GitHub serves it for a missing deep URL. And 404 links on 323 library pages already point at pages that don't exist, wherever the site is hosted, for example `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.html` → `Cslib/Tactic/PolyTime.html`.

**Pages enablement.** Enabled at 23:28 UTC on 23 October with `POST /pages build_type=workflow`, after the validation run passed; nothing blocked it. That also created the `github-pages` environment with a deployment branch policy allowing only `main`, so a branch run could not deploy even without the job condition. I also turned on "Enforce HTTPS", matching the organisation's other Pages sites (AlgoLib, CSwL, fad, bignum). The site returns 404 until the first deployment, from the first nightly run or a dispatch on `main` after merge.

**Validation.** [Run 40033874751](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033874751) (`workflow_dispatch` on e95f28b3) passed in 59 minutes. It covered the docs build, `check_docs.py` (1,874 modules), the size check with the expected 90 % warning, the `api-docs` artifact (56.5 MB) and the `github-pages` artifact (49.3 MB). The deploy job was skipped, as intended for a branch. The later commit e1787207 changes only the URL in the README and a workflow comment. `actionlint` 1.7.12 with shellcheck 0.11.0 reports no findings for `docs.yml`. `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --config-only` and the script unit tests pass. title: feat(crypto): Sigma protocols with Schnorr, linear relations and AND/OR composition
body:
Milestone 1 of #581: the exact algebraic core of Boneh–Shoup Chapter 19, checked against the book (v0.6, §§19.1, 19.4, 19.5, 19.7). Refs #581; milestones 2 and 3 remain open.

**Mathematical progress**

`Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/SigmaProtocol/` (namespace `Cslib.Crypto.Protocols`, next to upstream's `Protocols/Commitment`):

- **`Basic`.** `SigmaProtocol X Y T C Z` has a probabilistic commitment (`PMF`) with an explicit prover state, a deterministic response, and a deterministic verifier. Each property carries its algorithm explicitly:
  - `Complete R` (Def. 19.3).
  - `SpecialSoundness R extract` (Def. 19.4): a deterministic extractor that works for every statement, from any two accepting conversations with a common commitment and distinct challenges.
  - `SpecialHVZK R simulate` (Def. 19.5): simulated conversations always accept, and for `R x y` the simulation equals the honest `(t, z)` law at *each* fixed challenge. `SpecialHVZK.conversation_eq` derives the book's uniform-challenge form.
- **`Linear`.** One protocol, `linear ψ u ι`, for preimages of `ZMod q`-linear maps `ψ y : M →ₗ N` at `u y`. Challenges come from any `C ↪ ZMod q`. This is Thm 19.12 in prime order:
  - `linear_complete` and `linear_specialHVZK` hold for every `q`.
  - `linear_specialSoundness` needs `[Fact q.Prime]`; its extractor is `(ι c − ι c')⁻¹ • (z − z')`.
  - The instances `schnorr`, `okamoto`, `chaumPedersen` and `linearSystem` (§19.5.3, `m` equations in `n` unknowns) get all three properties stated with their own relations (Examples 19.1–19.3, Thms 19.9–19.11).

  Groups are additive `ZMod q`-modules, so the book's `g^α` is `α • g`. No cyclicity is assumed.
- **`Composition`.** `andProof`/`andExtract`/`andSimulate` (Thm 19.18) and `orProof`/`orExtract`/`orSimulate` (Thm 19.19). The OR-proof's challenges form any finite additive group, which generalizes the book's `{0,1}ⁿ` with XOR. Its witnesses are `X₀ ⊕ X₁` and its relation is `orRelation`. OR completeness uses the simulators' acceptance, as the book notes.

Everything here is exact and finite. Nothing claims efficiency or makes an asymptotic statement.

**Infrastructure and documentation**
- `references.bib` gains `[Schnorr1991]` and `[CramerDamgardSchoenmakers1994]`. The existing `[BonehShoup2023]` is reused.
- `ROADMAP.md` gets an entry recording what remains of #581.
- `ComplexityTests/Crypto/SigmaProtocol.lean` runs concrete cases by `decide`, with `decide +kernel` where `ZMod` inversion is involved:
  - Schnorr in `ZMod 11`, and in the order-11 subgroup of `(ZMod 23)ˣ` through `Additive` and `AddCommGroup.zmodModule`.
  - Okamoto, Chaum–Pedersen (including a non-DH triple with no two accepting conversations), a 2×2 linear system, AND, and OR.
  - Extractor runs that recover the witness, simulator support and law checks, and `#print axioms` guards.

**Design notes for review**
- `PMF`, not `ProbComp`, following upstream's `Commitment.Scheme`. A strict-PPT machine cannot sample `ZMod q` exactly (its probabilities are dyadic), so the computational milestones need a separate efficient realization in any case.
- The extractor signature `Y → T → C → Z → C → Z → X` is fixed by `SpecialSoundness`. `linearExtract` therefore ignores the statement and commitment.

**Not in this PR (remaining milestones, see the plan in #581)**
- The rewinding lemma and the extraction bound `ε' ≥ ε² − ε/N`.
- A discrete-log assumption for a group family with native polynomial-time operations.
- Schnorr identification against direct and eavesdropping attacks.
- Fiat–Shamir/Schnorr signatures in the ROM with the Thm 19.16 bound.
- GQ (§19.5.5) and §§19.8–19.9.

**Validation** at `07241b59`:
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates pass.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: passes.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 101 tests OK.
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: passes.

**Abstract assessment.** No catalogue change. These are foundational definitions and exact protocol lemmas, not a headline endpoint; the security theorems of milestones 2–3 are the candidates.

title: doc(paper): expand the theorem index into a comprehensive tour
body:
## Change

Expand the theorem index from 16 to 48 entries across 12 subjects, giving a broader tour of the significant results already formalized. Add cryptographic constructions, Fagin and Barrington, structural complexity, circuit lower bounds and natural proofs, proof complexity, communication, hypercontractivity, expander walks, decoding, sharp mass production, and general fixed-power circuits.

Each entry states the proved guarantee with its hypotheses, model and quantitative bounds. Preserve the distinction between uniform and nonuniform results, security assumptions and conclusions, formula and circuit cost conventions, and correctness versus certified constructor/decoder runtime. All 62 declaration links now target library revision `cec38657ddf1b93dd1be123e86d0ecdd9728c610`.

Split the source into subject files, add a clickable contents list, and keep statements with their declaration links. The resulting PDF has 16 pages and 53 references. No Lean source, dependencies or mathematical endpoints change.

## Accuracy review and validation

- Three independent Codex reviewers (`proof_correctness`, `proof_api`, `resume_alternation`) compared all 48 entries with the actual Lean statements and definitions. All approve; no findings remain. Scope and exact source SHA-256 hashes are recorded in `paper/review.md`.
- Resolved findings clarify the OWF experiment, PRF query/output lengths and auxiliary input, Fagin's encoding, and formula leaf counting including Spira's zero case. A stale cross-reference was corrected.

Confirmed 48 entries, 12 subject sections and 53 bibliography entries. `git diff --check` passes.
- Local Lean builds were not repeated for these documentation-only changes. The underlying library revision passed the six project gates; this PR also runs repository CI. title: refactor(logics): make propositional proof helpers private
body:
Makes 101 proof helpers in 15 `Logics/Propositional` modules private. This is item 1 of #596, under #587's surface standard. Statements and proofs are unchanged; only the `private` modifier and signature line breaks change.

**Rule.** A theorem becomes private when it is one step of a proof in its own module. That means:

- no other library module, test or abstract references it;
- no module doc names it;
- it is in no `simp`, `fun_prop` or `aesop` set.

Lemmas that state the semantics or basic structure of a public definition stay public even when nothing uses them yet. Examples are `Derives.mono`, `RefutableInSize.mono`, `QBF.closed_*`, `CNF.eval_compact`, `Clause.eval_exclude_eq_true_iff`, `Pigeonhole.mem_pigeonholeOn`, the `Derivation` API and `ProofSystem` soundness and completeness. Four helpers stay public because exposed definition bodies use them: `exists_choice`, `choice_chooseBranch`, `normalized_next` and `toClauseSet_next`. There are no aliases (D1, #588).

**Main groups:**

| Group | Theorems |
|---|---|
| Sparsification list layer | 26 |
| Sparsification path, tree, search, bounds and step | 27 |
| Intermediate sparsification certificates `computableTidilyInPolyTime_{reduce,flower,heavy,candidates,choice}` | 5 |
| Haken bottleneck lemmas in `Resolution/Pigeonhole` | 19 |
| Coding-lemma steps | 6 |
| `splitAux` | 4 |
| Tseitin parity and width steps | 8 |

`QBF/Arithmetization` and `Resolution/TseitinExpander` are left for a follow-up, because the deprecation sweep edits them.

**Why.** It gives users and agents about 100 fewer public names to navigate. Editing these proof steps also no longer changes the module interfaces that downstream builds depend on.

**Risk.** Low. The build rejects any private name that another module or an exposed body uses. That check is how the four exceptions above were found.

**Validation:**
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`

**Abstract impact:** none. The Cook–Levin, TQBF and Resolution bridges use no changed declaration. The Resolution bridge uses `CNF.IsProof`, `CNF.RefutableInSize`, `CNF.Satisfiable`, the `eval_eq_true_iff` lemmas, `satisfiable_pigeonhole_iff` and `two_pow_le_of_refutableInSize_pigeonhole`, all unchanged and public.

This adds the missing "find the declaration" step of the NP-completeness path. A block in `ComplexityTests/NPCompleteness.lean` that references each one (`example := @Cslib.Complexity.Clique_npComplete` and so on) would make the index checked. That fits the program's checked-documentation rule (#587). Separately, the remaining mention of `polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy` in the module doc goes away with #456's T2/T3.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Thanks for the review and the reproductions. All three points are fixed in `e8977be8`. Before that, I rebased onto `main` `cded1fc9` with no conflicts; the reviewed `bcc94648` is now `5362980e`, unchanged.

1. **Stale custom build directory.** Lake checks only the default build directory, so `check_outputs` now runs `lake build --no-build` and then requires any other `--build-dir` to hold exactly the same report inputs as the checked default outputs. The inputs are every `.ilean`, `.olean`, `.olean.server` and `.olean.private` under the three libraries; a missing, extra or changed file is refused. `--no-build-check` still reports on such a directory, but the header says "build outputs not checked against the sources". The JSON records `build_dir`, `outputs` and the limitations (`notes`), as you suggested.
   - Regressions in `OutputCheckTests`: a copy missing a newly added declaration's outputs is refused, an identical copy passes, stale default outputs are refused, and unchecked reports say so.
   - End to end on the real outputs: a hard-linked copy passes. After I removed three references from one `.ilean` in the copy, the report exits with "differs from the current build outputs in 1 file(s) (e.g. `Complexity/Foundations/Data/List/BalancedFold.ilean`)". With `--no-build-check` it is labelled unchecked.
2. **Area ownership.** `AREAS` now follows #587's table and the [assignment of the remaining paths](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/587#issuecomment-6376302681):
   - Machines gains RAM, GenericRAM and Tactic.
   - Circuit gains BranchingProgram.
   - Classes gains Kolmogorov, MCSP, USTCON, Computability/Languages and MachineLearning.
   - Foundations gains Computability/BitString.

   Only `Init` remains in Other. The GenericRAM-is-Other test is replaced by `test_areas_assigned_after_the_program_table`, which covers every reassigned path; the area legend in the output changed to match. WordRAM and Algorithms has 112 modules.
3. **Cross-module documented API.** Backquoted names from every module docstring and from the READMEs are pooled before candidates are computed. A name protects every declaration it could denote: the name itself, or a suffix of it on a component boundary. An ambiguous short name like `mono` therefore protects all its matches. `test_documentation_in_another_module_protects` is your A/B fixture as a unit test: B's docstring names `Cslib.Fixture.docApi`, which is protected while A's undocumented `helper` is not. At `2549de63`, cross-module mentions protect 133 more candidates: 2 through qualified names and 131 through short names.

**Also fixed.** The rebase brought in the Sigma-protocol modules (#581), whose statements use `let x ← e` inside `do`. Both the old and the new `scripts/proof_lengths.py` rejected them: `body_offset` counted those `let`s as awaiting a `:=`. Such `let`s no longer count, and a `do_let` case is added to the self-check. Results on the other 1,875 modules are identical to before. The report now records modules the proof scanner can't parse (`proofs_unparsed`) instead of stopping.

**Validation at `e8977be8`.**
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` passes, including 16 report tests.
- `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` passes.
- `quality_report.py` runs checked on fresh outputs in about 19 s.

Ready for re-review.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent cross-fleet agent review (`reviewer-codex-audit-01a16ab8`, with `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8` covering the Lean extractor and proof-length optimization): **CHANGES REQUESTED** at `bcc94648c071d9dd007d6ecb7736b07dd00db0ce`.

Three correctness issues affect the shared baseline/candidate output:

1. **Selected artifacts are not what the freshness guard validates** (`quality_report.py:878–884`). Build a small two-module project, copy its build outputs elsewhere, add a public declaration and rebuild/commit the default outputs. Running the report with `--build-dir` pointing to the old copy passes its default-directory Lake check, reports the current revision with `dirty: false`, and silently omits the new declaration. I reproduced this end to end. Validate the selected artifact tree against its source snapshot/expected coverage, or restrict normal checked reports to the default build directory. Add a regression that cannot label stale custom artifacts as current checked output. The default Lake check correctly rejects a missing `.ilean`; that case is not the bug.

2. **Area ownership is outdated** (`AREAS`, lines 49–62). `Computability/RAM/`, `Computability/GenericRAM/` and `Tactic/` currently go to Other, but #587 assigns them to Machines; `Computability/BranchingProgram/` belongs to Circuit. Update the mapping and explanatory text to the resolved charter, and replace the test explicitly expecting GenericRAM to be Other with regressions for all four assignments.

3. **Cross-module documentation does not protect intended API** (`check_module_docs`, lines 537–562). In the fresh native fixture, module A defines public `Cslib.Fixture.docApi`; module B's module docstring explicitly names `Cslib.Fixture.docApi` without a code reference. The report still emits `doc_named: false`, `candidate: true`, contrary to the documented candidate exclusion. Documentation tokens are only applied to declarations in the module containing the docstring. Resolve fully qualified mentions across all module docstrings before finding candidates, conservatively handling ambiguous short names, and add this two-module regression.

Validation/review scope: all ten supplied Python tests pass. The coordinator independently ran the pinned Lean extractor on the A/B fixture and obtained the expected three records with kinds/ranges; no additional extractor blocker was found. The coordinator also differentially compared `proof_lengths.masks` with its parent on all 2,358 tracked Lean files at this revision plus five delimiter/error cases, with identical output. No costly six-gate rerun was duplicated, and no shared build outputs were modified. Native reproductions and report artifacts are retained for the author handoff.

Optional: include guide omission, implicit/tactic-reference limits, and the selected build directory/check status in emitted report metadata/Markdown, so reports remain understandable outside this PR. These are separate from the three requested correctness fixes; restricting the override is a sufficient bounded approach to the first issue. Counts remain review signals, not deletion authority. This is agent review, not human approval.

title: feat(scripts): report public surface and quality signals per area
body:
Adds `scripts/quality_report.py`, the shared instrument for #584 and #587. At a built revision it classifies every public declaration written in `Complexity/` by where it is referenced (other library modules, only tests or abstracts, never outside its module), and reports the #587 signals per area: tidy predicates in public statements, missing docstrings, module-doc drift, duplicate statements, hub fan-out and proof-length outliers. It prints markdown tables and writes a per-declaration JSON file.

```bash
lake build Complexity ComplexityTests ComplexityAbstracts   # or scripts/cache/get.sh first
python3 scripts/quality_report.py --json report.json        # about 20 s; refuses stale outputs
```

**Method.** References come from the `.ilean` files Lake writes beside each `.olean`. They record every identifier written in the source, proofs included, as a full constant name, so namespaces, `open` and dot notation don't matter. `scripts/QualityReport.lean` reads the exported and private `.olean` parts directly, without importing them. It supplies kinds, export status, docstrings, declaration ranges, statement types (for duplicate detection by alpha-equivalence) and the same-module constants that each exported statement or exposed body mentions. References to constants Lean generates (constructors, recursors, equation lemmas, `simps` lemmas) count for the declaration they come from. Structure fields and constructors count for their type. Privatization candidates exclude declarations with implicit-use attributes (`simp`, `fun_prop`, `aesop`, instances, notation, …) and declarations named in module docstrings or READMEs. They also exclude declarations that a staying-public statement or exposed body mentions, computed as a fixed point. "Unfolded elsewhere" means named in `unfold`/`delta`, as an element of a `simp`/`rw` lemma list, or through an equation lemma.

**Validation.**
- Unit tests for the parsing and graph helpers (`scripts/test_quality_report.py`) pass.
- `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` passes, and the six gates passed before rebasing.
- 20 sampled declarations across the categories were checked with `grep`, and all classifications held. One apparent cross-module use turned out to be a different declaration with the same short name.
- Systematic text check: 82% of the declarations never referenced outside their module have no occurrence of their final name component in the code of any other file. A sample of 25 of the rest found only name collisions (`mono`, `refl`, `run`, …).
- `proof_lengths.masks` now jumps between delimiters. Its output is identical on 3,310 Lean files, and it runs about five times faster, which keeps the report fast.

**Limitations.** These are review signals, not rules. Uses through simp sets, instances, `fun_prop`, Aesop, notation and macros leave no reference. Such declarations are flagged and kept out of the candidates, not counted as unused. Definitional unfolding without naming the definition (`rfl`, `decide`) is invisible, so the exposure figures bound evidence rather than prove a body unneeded. Zero in-repository references doesn't mean an API is unwanted. The guide (#585) isn't scanned yet.

matching_paragraphs: **Method.** References come from the `.ilean` files Lake writes beside each `.olean`. They record every identifier written in the source, proofs included, as a full constant name, so namespaces, `open` and dot notation don't matter. `scripts/QualityReport.lean` reads the exported and private `.olean` parts directly, without importing them. It supplies kinds, export status, docstrings, declaration ranges, statement types (for duplicate detection by alpha-equivalence) and the same-module constants that each exported statement or exposed body mentions. References to constants Lean generates (constructors, recursors, equation lemmas, `simps` lemmas) count for the declaration they come from. Structure fields and constructors count for their type. Privatization candidates exclude declarations with implicit-use attributes (`simp`, `fun_prop`, `aesop`, instances, notation, …) and declarations named in module docstrings or READMEs. They also exclude declarations that a staying-public statement or exposed body mentions, computed as a fixed point. "Unfolded elsewhere" means named in `unfold`/`delta`, as an element of a `simp`/`rw` lemma list, or through an equation lemma.

**Limitations.** These are review signals, not rules. Uses through simp sets, instances, `fun_prop`, Aesop, notation and macros leave no reference. Such declarations are flagged and kept out of the candidates, not counted as unused. Definitional unfolding without naming the definition (`rfl`, `decide`) is invisible, so the exposure figures bound evidence rather than prove a body unneeded. Zero in-repository references doesn't mean an API is unwanted. The guide (#585) isn't scanned yet.

title: refactor(logics): make first-order proof helpers private
body:
Makes 35 proof helpers in 15 `Logics/FirstOrder` and `Logics/SecondOrder` modules private. This is item 2 of #596, following the rule of #601. Statements and proofs are unchanged.

**What becomes private:**

| Group | Theorems |
|---|---|
| Steps of the CNF-structure and graph copy-invariance proofs (`*_copies_iff`, `literals_copies`) | 5 |
| Interpretation of the local sum-language symbols (`relMap_{pos,neg,true}Sym`, `relMap_edge`, `relMap_color`) | 5 |
| Realization of the ESO matrices (`realize_satMatrix`, `realize_colorableMatrix`, `realize_independentSetMatrix`, `realize_iExs_fourLiteralsFormula`) | 4 |
| 3SAT→3COL gadget lemmas | 7 |
| `*_rel_lit` and subsingleton-case lemmas in `ColoringToCNF` and `Grounding` | 4 |
| `TaggedInterpretation.coords_*` | 3 |

The remaining seven are `flatMap_frame_drop`, `sumElim_comp_snocVar`, `mem_domainRanks`, `isCarrySuccessor_of_lexRank_succ`, `pairwise_not_adj_iff_compl` and the `flatten`/`modelRel` bijectivity lemmas in `SecondOrder/Reduction`.

**What stays public:**

- The semantic and closure API, even where nothing outside the module uses it yet: the `Interpretation`, `DomainInterpretation`, `Certificate` and `FullTupleInterpretation` API, `QFReduces.{isoClosed, compl, of_interpretation}`, `ReducesNontrivial.compl`, `Satisfiable.of_equiv`, the ESO `realize_*`/`*_isExpansionOn` lemmas, the encoding layout lemmas and `tupleIndex_snoc`.
- Six `TaggedInterpretation` lemmas, because the exposed bodies of `ofCopies`, `copiesEquiv` and `subsingletonEquiv` use them.

The #596 audit counted about 95 unreferenced theorems in these directories; most of them are API under this rule. No aliases (D1, #588).

**Why.** Fewer public names, and editing these proof steps no longer changes module interfaces. **Risk:** low; the build rejects any private name that another module or an exposed body uses.

**Validation:**
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`

**Abstract impact:** none. The Fagin bridge uses `ESO.Definable` and the Fagin class theorems, which are unchanged.

Checked: this has exactly the shape of `DecryptionCircuits.correct` in `Refresh.lean`, with the same input order and widths, quantified over all raw words.

Optional, non-blocking: typed GSW clients would benefit from a public corollary on canonical encodings. This compiles at `ee20f997`:
```lean
theorem eval_serialize {n w : ℕ} (t : Fin n → ZMod (2 ^ w)) (C : Ciphertext n w) :
    (circuit n w).eval interpretation
      (BitString.ofList (inputWidth n w) (serializeSecret t ++ serializeCiphertext C)) 0 =
      decrypt t C := by
  rw [correct n w _ _ (length_serializeSecret t) (by simp [pow_two]),
    decryptSerialized_serialize]
```

@@ -0,0 +1,282 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.Homomorphic.GSW.Serialized.Evaluation
+public import Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Boolean.Modular.InnerProduct
+public import Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Boolean.Modular.Subtract
+import Complexity.Foundations.Data.Nat.Bits
+import Mathlib.Data.List.GetD
+
+/-!
+# Selected-row GSW decryption circuits
+
+The input order is the complete serialized secret followed by the complete serialized ciphertext.
+The row selected by the existing total decoder is used on every input, without a key-generation
+or noise hypothesis. Arithmetic circuits preserve residues modulo the word modulus.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.inputWidth`: the complete raw input length.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.circuit`: the actual total raw-input decryptor.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.correct`: agreement with serialized decryption
+  on every well-sized raw input, including widths zero and one and both half-open decoder ties.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.depth_circuit_le`: explicit logarithmic depth.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit.size_circuit_le`: explicit polynomial gate count.
+
+## References
+
+* [C. Gentry, A. Sahai, B. Waters][GentrySahaiWaters2013], Sections 3.1 and 3.4.
+* [C. Gentry][Gentry2009], Definition 4: augmented decryption takes all key and ciphertext bits.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DecryptionCircuit
+
+open Cslib.Circuits Cslib.Circuits.Boolean Cslib.BitString
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+variable {n w : ℕ}
+
+/-- Secret bits precede all square-matrix ciphertext bits. -/
+abbrev inputWidth (n w : ℕ) : ℕ := n * w + ((n + 1) * w) * ((n + 1) * w)
+
+/-- Interpret the raw first block with the same total decoder as the serialized scheme. -/
+private def inputSecret (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) : Fin n → ZMod (2 ^ w) :=
+  decodeSecret n w (List.ofFn (fstBits x))
+
+/-- Interpret every raw ciphertext bit, including ciphertexts outside encryption support. -/
+private def inputCiphertext (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) : Ciphertext n w :=
+  decodeCiphertext n w (List.ofFn (sndBits x))
+
+private theorem inputSecret_apply (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (j : Fin n) :
+    inputSecret x j = ((BitString.equivFin w (block (fstBits x) j) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) := by
+  simp only [inputSecret, decodeSecret, Cslib.Matrix.ofBinary_apply,
+    Cslib.Matrix.binaryEntry, Fin.val_zero, zero_mul, zero_add,
+    listRow_eq_ofFn w j, ofList_ofFn, Nat.foldr_bit_ofFn, BitString.val_equivFin_eq_sum]
+
+/-- Recompose any row's binary word by the same place values as the circuit word convention. -/
+private theorem rowWord_cast (C : Ciphertext n w) (row : Fin (n + 1) × Fin w) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
+    ((BitString.equivFin w (fun l => C row (j, l)) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      recomposeMatrix w (bitMatrix (ZMod (2 ^ w)) C) row j := by
+  simp only [BitString.val_equivFin_eq_sum, Nat.cast_sum, Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_pow,
+    Nat.cast_ofNat, recomposeMatrix, bitCompose, bitMatrix_apply]
+
+private theorem inputCiphertext_apply (x : BitString (inputWidth n w))
+    (i j : Fin (n + 1)) (k l : Fin w) :
+    inputCiphertext x (i, k) (j, l) = x (Fin.natAdd (n * w)
+      (finProdFinEquiv (finProdFinEquiv (i, k), finProdFinEquiv (j, l)))) := by
+  rw [inputCiphertext, decodeCiphertext_apply]
+  let p := finProdFinEquiv (finProdFinEquiv (i, k), finProdFinEquiv (j, l))
+  have hp : (i.val * w + k.val) * ((n + 1) * w) + j.val * w + l.val = p.val := by
+    simp only [p, finProdFinEquiv, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Fin.val_mk]
+    ring
+  rw [hp, List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ (by simp), List.getElem_ofFn]
+  rfl
+
+/-- The selected row is the last binary digit of the leading expanded-secret coordinate. -/
+private def selectedRow (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Fin (n + 1) × Fin w :=
+  (0, ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩)
+
+/-- Wire one selected-row word directly out of the complete ciphertext input. -/
+private def rowInputs (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
+    Fin w → Fin (inputWidth n w) :=
+  fun l => Fin.natAdd (n * w)
+    (finProdFinEquiv (finProdFinEquiv (selectedRow n w hw), finProdFinEquiv (j, l)))
+
+private theorem eval_rowInputs (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
+    (Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw j)).eval interpretation x =
+      fun l => inputCiphertext x (selectedRow n w hw) (j, l) := by
+  funext l
+  rw [Circuit.eval_wiring]
+  exact (inputCiphertext_apply x 0 j ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩ l).symm
+
+/-- Consecutive selected-row words paired with the unexpanded secret, omitting column zero. -/
+private def rowTail (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) : BitString (n * w) :=
+  fun i => inputCiphertext x (selectedRow n w hw)
+    ((finProdFinEquiv.symm i).1.succ, (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).2)
+
+private theorem block_rowTail (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) (j : Fin n) :
+    block (rowTail x hw) j = fun l => inputCiphertext x (selectedRow n w hw) (j.succ, l) := by
+  funext l
+  simp only [rowTail, block, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]
+
+/-- Feed the complete secret and the non-leading selected-row words to the inner product. -/
+private def productInputs (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Fin (n * w + n * w) → Fin (inputWidth n w) :=
+  Fin.append (m := n * w) (n := n * w)
+    (Fin.castAdd (((n + 1) * w) * ((n + 1) * w)))
+    (fun i => rowInputs n w hw (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).1.succ (finProdFinEquiv.symm i).2)
+
+private theorem append_comp_productInputs (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) :
+    x ∘ productInputs n w hw = Fin.append (fstBits x) (rowTail x hw) := by
+  funext i
+  refine Fin.addCases (fun j => ?_) (fun j => ?_) i
+  · simp only [Function.comp_apply, productInputs, Fin.append_left, fstBits]
+  · simp only [Function.comp_apply, productInputs, Fin.append_right, rowTail]
+    exact (inputCiphertext_apply x 0 (finProdFinEquiv.symm j).1.succ
+      ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩ (finProdFinEquiv.symm j).2).symm
+
+/-- The actual selected-row modular inner product, reading directly from raw inputs. -/
+private def productSum (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Circuit signature (inputWidth n w) w :=
+  (Modular.innerProduct n w).comp (Circuit.wiring signature (productInputs n w hw))
+
+private theorem productSum_cast (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) :
+    ((BitString.equivFin w ((productSum n w hw).eval interpretation x) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      ∑ j : Fin n, recomposeMatrix w (bitMatrix (ZMod (2 ^ w)) (inputCiphertext x))
+        (selectedRow n w hw) j.succ * inputSecret x j := by
+  rw [productSum, Circuit.eval_comp, Circuit.eval_wiring, append_comp_productInputs,
+    Modular.val_eval_innerProduct, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_sum]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro j _
+  rw [Nat.cast_mul, ← inputSecret_apply, block_rowTail, rowWord_cast, mul_comm]
+
+/-- Subtract the selected row's inner product from its leading word, modulo `2 ^ w`. -/
+private def phase (n w : ℕ) (hw : 0 < w) : Circuit signature (inputWidth n w) w :=
+  (Modular.subtract w).comp
+    ((Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)).append (productSum n w hw))
+
+/-- The raw circuit phase is exactly the original selected-row residue on every input. -/
+private theorem phase_cast (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) (hw : 0 < w) :
+    ((BitString.equivFin w ((phase n w hw).eval interpretation x) : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      decryptionPhase (inputSecret x) (inputCiphertext x) (selectedRow n w hw) := by
+  let a := (Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)).eval interpretation x
+  let b := (productSum n w hw).eval interpretation x
+  have ha : ((BitString.equivFin w a : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) =
+      recomposeMatrix w (bitMatrix (ZMod (2 ^ w)) (inputCiphertext x)) (selectedRow n w hw) 0 := by
+    dsimp only [a]
+    rw [eval_rowInputs]
+    exact rowWord_cast _ _ _
+  have hb := productSum_cast x hw
+  change ((BitString.equivFin w b : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) = _ at hb
+  have hv : (BitString.equivFin w ((phase n w hw).eval interpretation x) : ℕ) =
+      (2 ^ w - (BitString.equivFin w b : ℕ) + (BitString.equivFin w a : ℕ)) % 2 ^ w := by
+    simpa only [phase, Circuit.eval_comp, Circuit.eval_append] using Modular.val_eval_subtract a b
+  rw [hv, ZMod.natCast_mod, Nat.cast_add,
+    Nat.cast_sub (Nat.le_of_lt (BitString.equivFin w b).isLt), ZMod.natCast_self]
+  simp only [ha, hb, decryptionPhase, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm, zero_add]
+
+private theorem testBit_wordValue (x : BitString w) (i : Fin w) :
+    (BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ).testBit i.val = x i := by
+  simpa only [BitVec.getLsbD, toNat_word_eq_equivFin] using getLsbD_word x i
+
+/-- Implement the actual width-zero, width-one and top-two-bit decoder cases. -/
+private def decodeWord (w : ℕ) : Circuit signature w 1 :=
+  if h₀ : w = 0 then Circuit.oneGate (.const false) Fin.elim0
+  else if h₁ : w = 1 then Circuit.wiring signature (fun _ => ⟨0, by omega⟩)
+  else ((Formula.input ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩).xor (.input ⟨w - 2, by omega⟩)).toCircuit
+
+/-- The scalar decoder is computed on every modular word, including both quarter ties. -/
+private theorem eval_decodeWord (x : BitString w) :
+    (decodeWord w).eval interpretation x 0 =
+      decode w ((BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)) := by
+  have hv : (((BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) : ZMod (2 ^ w)).val) =
+      (BitString.equivFin w x : ℕ) := by
+    rw [ZMod.val_natCast, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (BitString.equivFin w x).isLt]
+  by_cases h₀ : w = 0
+  · subst w
+    simp [decodeWord, interpretation]
+  · by_cases h₁ : w = 1
+    · subst w
+      simp only [decodeWord, Nat.one_ne_zero, ↓reduceDIte, Circuit.eval_wiring,
+        Function.comp_apply, decode_one, hv]
+      exact (testBit_wordValue x 0).symm
+    · have hw : 2 ≤ w := by omega
+      rw [decode_eq_xor_highBits hw, hv]
+      simp only [decodeWord, h₀, h₁, ↓reduceDIte, Formula.eval_toCircuit,
+        Formula.eval_xor, Formula.eval_input]
+      rw [testBit_wordValue x ⟨w - 1, by omega⟩,
+        testBit_wordValue x ⟨w - 2, by omega⟩]
+
+private theorem depth_decodeWord_le (w : ℕ) : (decodeWord w).depth ≤ 3 := by
+  unfold decodeWord
+  split_ifs
+  · simp
+  · simp
+  · exact (Formula.depth_toCircuit_le _).trans
+      ((Formula.depth_xor_le _ _).trans (by simp))
+
+private theorem size_decodeWord_le (w : ℕ) : (decodeWord w).size ≤ 5 := by
+  unfold decodeWord
+  split_ifs <;> simp
+
+/-- The actual total GSW decryptor, with all raw secret and ciphertext bits as inputs. -/
+def circuit (n w : ℕ) : Circuit signature (inputWidth n w) 1 :=
+  if hw : 0 < w then (decodeWord w).comp (phase n w hw)
+  else Circuit.oneGate (.const false) Fin.elim0
+
+/-- All raw inputs agree with typed GSW decryption, without generation or noise hypotheses. -/
+private theorem eval_circuit (x : BitString (inputWidth n w)) :
+    (circuit n w).eval interpretation x 0 = decrypt (inputSecret x) (inputCiphertext x) := by
+  by_cases hw : 0 < w
+  · rw [circuit, dite_eq_left hw, Circuit.eval_comp, eval_decodeWord, phase_cast x hw,
+      decrypt_eq_decode_decryptionPhase hw]
+    rfl
+  · have hz : w = 0 := by omega
+    subst w
+    simp [circuit, interpretation]
+
+/-- The selected-row construction has logarithmic depth in both parameter dimensions. -/
+theorem depth_circuit_le (n w : ℕ) :
+    (circuit n w).depth ≤ 28 + 18 * Nat.clog 2 (w + 1) + 12 * Nat.clog 2 n := by
+  have hp : ∀ hw, (productSum n w hw).depth ≤
+      17 + 16 * Nat.clog 2 (w + 1) + 12 * Nat.clog 2 n := by
+    intro hw
+    exact (Circuit.depth_comp_le _ _).trans (by
+      simpa only [Circuit.depth_wiring, add_zero] using Modular.depth_innerProduct_le n w)
+  have hphase : ∀ hw, (phase n w hw).depth ≤
+      25 + 18 * Nat.clog 2 (w + 1) + 12 * Nat.clog 2 n := by
+    intro hw
+    have ha := Circuit.depth_append_le
+      (Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)) (productSum n w hw)
+    simp only [Circuit.depth_wiring, zero_max] at ha
+    have hc := Circuit.depth_comp_le (Modular.subtract w)
+      ((Circuit.wiring signature (rowInputs n w hw 0)).append (productSum n w hw))
+    have hs := Modular.depth_subtract_le w
+    have hi := hp hw
+    change (phase n w hw).depth ≤ _ at hc
+    omega
+  unfold circuit
+  split_ifs with hw
+  · have hc := Circuit.depth_comp_le (decodeWord w) (phase n w hw)
+    have hd := depth_decodeWord_le w
+    have hp := hphase hw
+    omega
+  · simp only [Circuit.depth_oneGate]
+    omega
+
+/-- Polynomial gate count includes all unused fallback gates in the balanced construction. -/
+theorem size_circuit_le (n w : ℕ) :
+    (circuit n w).size ≤ 131 * (n + 1) * (w + 1) ^ 2 := by
+  unfold circuit
+  split_ifs with hw
+  · simp only [Circuit.size_comp, phase, productSum, Circuit.size_append,
+      Circuit.size_wiring, zero_add]
+    have hd := size_decodeWord_le w
+    have hs := Modular.size_subtract_le w
+    have hi := Modular.size_innerProduct_le n w
+    nlinarith [Nat.zero_le n, Nat.zero_le (n * w), Nat.zero_le (n * w ^ 2)]
+  · simp only [Circuit.size_oneGate]
+    nlinarith [Nat.zero_le n, Nat.zero_le (n * w), Nat.zero_le (n * w ^ 2)]
+
+/-- The serialized contract required by generic refresh: every well-sized raw pair is covered. -/
+theorem correct (n w : ℕ) (secret ciphertext : List Bool)

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent cross-fleet review by `reviewer-claude-607-c4b0c164` (Claude Code, Opus 5.5; did not author this change) of `ee20f997`: **approve** (mathematics and API; integration still awaits the tidy-surface fix)

Scope: the whole PR except the #594 prerequisite. `BalancedCode.lean`, the `Balanced.lean` hunk and `ComplexityTests/BalancedCode.lean` are byte-identical to `main` and were not re-reviewed. The six tidy-stated public certificates are the known blocker and are not repeated here.

**What is proved**
- `DecryptionCircuit.correct`: for all `n w` and every raw `secret`/`ciphertext` of lengths `n*w` and `((n+1)*w)^2`, the circuit applied to `ofList (secret ++ ciphertext)` outputs `decryptSerialized n w secret ciphertext`. #537's `decryptSerialized_eq` identifies that with typed `decrypt` of the decoded inputs. There is no key-generation, support or noise hypothesis. Every circuit input is such an `ofList`, so the theorem is total, and it has exactly the shape of `DecryptionCircuits.correct` in `Refresh.lean`. **The statement is faithful.**
  - Construction: take row `(0, w-1)`, subtract the modular inner product of the secret with the row's other words from its leading word, then decode.
  - Decoder: `false` at `w = 0`, the sole bit at `w = 1`, and the XOR of bits `w-1, w-2` otherwise, via `decode_eq_xor_highBits` (both ties covered). `n = 0` goes through the empty-sum fallback inside the same theorem.
- `depth_circuit_le` gives `28 + 18·clog₂(w+1) + 12·clog₂ n` and `size_circuit_le` gives `131(n+1)(w+1)²`, for all `n w`. I rechecked the chain: inner product `17+16c_w+12c_n`, subtract `8+2c_w`, decoder 3.
- **Depth against the budget:** `layers_augment_le_depthBudget` holds at every λ, including 0, with no asymptotic step. The compiled layer count is `2·depth(augmentNand) ≤ 2(30 + 18(15+2t) + 12t) = 600 + 96t ≤ 512t = L`. This uses `clog₂(16384t²+1) ≤ 15+2t`, `clog₂(λ+1) ≤ t` and `t ≥ 2`. The slack is at least 232 layers at `t = 2` and grows linearly.
  - Counting NAND layers rather than De Morgan depth is the right unit against `noise_margin`, which charges one `(N+1)` factor per NAND level. The input count is the two-copy `inputWidth + inputWidth` that `refreshNand` evaluates. **The "shallow" claim holds.**
- **Generator:** `computableInPolyTime_code` and `computableInPolyTime_circuit` take unary `(n, w)` to the full binary `encCode`. Unary input is right here because the output size is polynomial in `n` and `w`.
  - `code_eq_code` holds exactly, including the `w = 0` fallback, and `computableInPolyTime_layeredAugment` also emits the compiled layered NAND augmentation.
  - The raw pieces are total on out-of-range data: a shift `i ≥ w`, or arbitrary leaf codes passed to `sumPairsCode`. I found no per-parameter shortcut and no assumed bound field.
- **Arithmetic:** each block states exact agreement on every word.
  - `partialProduct`: `if bᵢ then a·2^i mod 2^w else 0`, depth 1, size `w`.
  - `reducePairs`/`sumPairs`: the pair sum mod `2^w`, empty list included.
  - `multiply`: `ab mod 2^w`, depth `9+14c_w`, size `63(w+1)²`.
  - `subtract`: `(2^w − b + a) mod 2^w` with no truncated subtraction, depth `8+2c_w`, size `21(w+1)²`.
  - `innerProduct`: `Σ aⱼbⱼ mod 2^w` including `k = 0` and `w = 0`, depth `17+16c_w+12c_k`, size `105(k+1)(w+1)²`.
- **Scope:** the ROADMAP and the PR text claim no bootstrappability, hardness transfer or FHE endpoint, and #486 stays open. No formal abstract is affected (`GSWSecurityAbstract` is unrelated), so I agree with the no-impact assessment.
- **API:** construction helpers are private, `import all` appears only in the companion `PolyTime` modules, and `code` hides its body with `private_decl%`, the same pattern as #594. No private declaration still carries `@[fun_prop]`: ee20f997 removed the attribute from `computableTidilyInPolyTime_falseWordCode`, whose uses are explicit. Axiom guards cover the three headline theorems.

**Checks run**
- `lake build ComplexityTests.Crypto.GSWDecryptionCircuit` at `ee20f997` succeeds.
- Independent of the proofs: I compiled the native `DecryptionCircuit.code n w` with `Layered.compile`, ran `Layered.eval` on pseudo-random raw inputs and compared the result with `decryptSerialized`. All 78 inputs matched, over `(n,w) ∈ {(1,2),(2,3),(0,3),(3,1),(2,0),(3,5)}`, and the spec outputs were mixed rather than constant (5 of 20 true at `(2,3)`).
- Actual size against the stated bounds: depth 37 of 64 and 251 of 2358 gates at `(1,2)`; depth 99 of 124 and 11459 of 53055 gates at `(4,8)`.

**Findings**
1. **The PR description gives the wrong delta range; please fix it before the final-delta review.** `c9e74315..HEAD` is not the #528-only delta. `0b945318` (circuit and arithmetic) and `f1619be5` (budget fit and `PartialProduct/PolyTime`) come before the cherry-picked `c9e74315` in history, so that range leaves out all of `DecryptionCircuit/Parameters.lean`. It also shows only about 50 lines of churn in `DecryptionCircuit.lean` and the arithmetic files instead of their content. A reviewer using the link would miss the budget theorem entirely.
   - #594 is merged and its files match `main` byte for byte, so rebase onto `main`. The PR diff then is the #528 delta, and the link can go.
   - The rebase will conflict in `ROADMAP.md`, where main's #543 sentence still says the circuit, generator and fit "remain the separate #528 objective", and in `Complexity.lean`. Keep this PR's wording.
2. The nits are inline:
   - the `Parameters.lean` docstring says "fewer" where the theorem proves `≤`;
   - two private `Subtract` lemmas carry a redundant `@[simp]`;
   - one ROADMAP sentence is stale;
   - an optional typed corollary for canonical encodings, checked to compile.
3. Optional, after #608: the family generator `security ↦ code (dimension λ) (width λ)` exists only as a test `example` built with `.tidy.comp`. Once the plain calculus composes it directly, consider stating it in the library, since #486 will consume it.

**Limits**
- I did not re-review #594, #537's `decryptSerialized`, #552's `noise_margin` or `Layered.compile`.
- Showing that a future GSW evaluator spends exactly one `(N+1)` noise factor per layered NAND level is #486's work. This PR shows only that the layer count fits `L`.
- I took the cost charged by `encCode` as given by the existing encoding.

title: feat(crypto): construct native shallow GSW decryption circuits
body:
Construct the actual selected-row GSW decryption circuit on the complete serialized secret followed by the complete square-matrix ciphertext. Evaluation agrees with total `decryptSerialized` for every well-sized raw pair, without key-generation, encryption-support or noise hypotheses. Shifted partial products, the exact half-split carry-save tree and carry-lookahead finishing compute the phase modulo `2^w`; the decoder covers widths zero and one and both half-open boundary ties.

The proved depth is at most `28 + 18 clog₂(w+1) + 12 clog₂(n)` and gate count at most `131(n+1)(w+1)²`. A native polynomial-time generator charges the full code, matrix selectors and wiring, and also constructs the complete layered NAND augmentation. Its actual compiled layer count fits the existing `DepthParameters.depthBudget` at every security parameter. Public generator statements are plain; construction helpers are private, with narrow companion `import all` access. Checked clients exercise decoder ties, negative wraparound, boundary widths, empty arrays, the uniform parameter family, compiler semantics/encoded-size overhead and audited axioms.

Rebased onto main `7122d105`; #594 is already present and its duplicate cherry-pick is removed. All eight original #528 commits are retained, including the two that preceded that cherry-pick. The independent mathematical/API review at `ee20f997` remains [review 5635643747](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/607#pullrequestreview-5635643747). The rebase preserves that source, and the subsequent [plain API delta](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/compare/71aa74e9...93e2da84) replaces six public tidy constructor certificates with plain hypotheses and conclusions, updates their clients, and keeps tidy inside proofs/private construction helpers. The circuit definitions, evaluation, depth/size bounds and budget proofs are unchanged. Prior unavailable private-machine checkpoints and earlier contributions remain credited in #528; this implementation does not claim to recover those files.

Closes #528. The broader #486 objective remains open: this proves the actual decryption circuit, native construction and budget fit, not bootstrappability, a transfer of a decision-LWE premise, circular security or the concrete FHE endpoint. Existing selected abstract statements and catalogue entries are unchanged; no new headline is proposed and no PDF rendering changes.

Validation: all six required gates passed at `93e2da84c0f36ff7e86e20a135de83e05f7efac2` (strict build, generated imports, tests, lint, style and init imports). Focused plain-client and ordinary-import API checks, hygiene including changed-source `--check-simp`, and the abstract catalogue check passed. The six old public tidy certificate names are removed without aliases; no global private `fun_prop` registration is added. The earlier six-gate result at `ee20f997` remains valid for the independently reviewed mathematical checkpoint. Final independent delta review is requested before integration; the authors do not approve or merge this work.

title: doc(contributing): state the public-surface rules of the module system
body:
Adds a short "Public surface under the module system" subsection to CONTRIBUTING's library quality standard. It turns the #584 findings into rules.

- **What invalidates importers.** Only a change to a module's exported `.olean`. That file holds public statements, exposed bodies, attributes of public declarations, and each public declaration's axiom set. Docstrings, private declarations, proofs and non-exposed bodies are not part of it, unless a proof edit changes the axiom set.
- **Rules.**
  - Helpers are private by default.
  - `@[expose]` stays on bodies that downstream proofs unfold.
  - A private `@[fun_prop]` theorem uses `attribute [local fun_prop]`, because the extension exports the rule anyway and `fun_prop` then fails in importers with "Unknown constant `_private…`".
  - Tests and abstracts can't name private declarations, so they are updated in the same PR.
  - `scripts/quality_report.py` supplies the evidence, and its counts are signals, not rules.

The evidence is in the [#584 measurement](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/584#issuecomment-6376568560): the Lean and Lake source, plus scratch modules whose exported `.olean` hashes were compared before and after each kind of edit. It references `scripts/quality_report.py`, so it should merge after or together with #604.

title: feat(counting): prove uniform bounded wide-gap closure
body:
Closes #55. Includes refreshed PR53, PR57 and PR59 at the current cslib pin; preserve ancestry with a merge commit because PR61 stacks on this head.

Prove uniform bounded conjunction and disjunction closure for both WPP and LWPP. The input is one jointly uniform language on `(x,i)`, encoded with a unary index, and any polynomial-time unary bound `r(x)`. This does not replace joint membership with separate slice membership, and `r` may vary between inputs of the same length.

Conjunction multiplies the indexed gaps using PR53's certified product theorem. For WPP, multiply the corresponding FP targets. For LWPP, joint encoded length is `2|x|+1+i`; all possible targets are `T(n,k) = product_{i<k} f(2n+1+i)` for `0 ≤ k ≤ p(n)`, where a fixed polynomial bounds `r`. This nonzero, uniformly FP family permits polynomial-family robustness to normalize the selected input-dependent index `k=r(x)`. Complement closure gives disjunction. Empty ranges produce the full and empty languages respectively.

Source credit: this is a formalized deduction from Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz counting algebra and the polynomial-family robustness theorem of Edith Hemaspaandra, Lane A. Hemaspaandra, Holger Spakowski and Osamu Watanabe, *The Robustness of LWPP and WPP, with an Application to Graph Reconstruction*, Theorem 3.1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.01250. It does not claim that source states these exact encoded interfaces. The classes retain the verifier model; adaptive oracle closure, PP-lowness and counting-machine characterization remain separate.

body:
States the verifier proof system with plain computability. This is item 3 of #596 and part of #456's direction that tidy notions stay inside proofs.

- **Plain verifier:** `ProofSystem.ofVerifier`, `ofVerifier_frame_append` and `polynomiallyBounded_ofVerifier` now take a plain `ComputableInPolyTime` verifier. This matches `NP`'s plain verifiers since #559. The tidy certificate for the composed machine is built inside the `computable` proof with `hV.tidy`.
- **One less conversion:** `exists_polynomiallyBounded_iff_mem_NP` now passes `NP`'s verifier through directly, without `.tidy`.
- **Removed `pSimulates_iff_tidy`:** its only client was one test example. That example now gives the plain translation `⟨id, .id', fun _ => rfl⟩` to `PSimulates` directly.

title: feat(polytime): certify negation and list membership for automation
body:
Adds `fun_prop` certificates for `decide (¬p)` and for membership of a computed value in a computed list, so tests written as on paper, such as `(u, v) ∉ G.2`, need no rewriting into Boolean scans before `fun_prop` or `polytime` runs. Found while writing #585's NP-completeness chapter: a newcomer's natural graph complement defeated both tactics, and the library's own proof needed a hand-proved rewrite.

Before, `Graph.computableTidilyInPolyTime_compl` needed an 8-line lemma that rewrites `decide (u ≠ v ∧ (u, v) ∉ G.2 ∧ (v, u) ∉ G.2)` into `!decide (u = v) && !G.adjBool u v`, followed by `simp_rw` and unfolding `adjBool`. On `main`, `unfold Graph.compl; polytime` on the plain goal fails on `decide ((u, v) ∈ G.2)`. After:

```lean
example : ComputableInPolyTime Graph.compl encGraph encGraph := by
  unfold Graph.compl
  polytime
```

and the library certificate is `unfold compl encGraph; fun_prop`. `Clique.mem_NP` now proves its verifier's cost with `by fun_prop` instead of `.of_tidy computableTidilyInPolyTime_verifier`, so the worked example that #603 and the guide point to shows no plain/tidy plumbing.

**Placement.** Both rules (`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.decide_not`, `.decide_mem`) live in a new narrow module, `PolyTime/Membership`, rather than in the `PolyTime/Basic` and `PolyTime/List` hubs. `Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime` imports it, so `polytime` users get the rules, and `Clique.lean` imports it privately. Membership is decided by an `anyWithInput` scan for an equal element. The instance argument is generic, so the rule matches whichever `Decidable` instance the goal uses.

**Scope.** No statements change, and no definitions or abstracts are touched. Other `mem_NP` proofs still use `.of_tidy …_verifier`; that, and whether per-problem certificates should be stated plainly, is an NP-area question I'm recording in #585's friction log rather than changing here. #603 has since merged; the second commit drops its `PolyTimeReducible` docstring's advice to rewrite `decide` expressions into Boolean tests, which pointed at the rewrite this PR removes.

**Validation.** Rebased on `main` after #603. `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates, and `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` passes. New checked examples in `ComplexityTests/PolyTimeTactic.lean`: `decide (3 ∈ l)`, a filter by `x ∉ p.2`, and the complement map, all plain and proved by `polytime`. `ComplexityTests/KarpReductions.lean` still checks the complement and verifier certificates and their axioms.

**Abstracts.** No impact: proof-only changes, plus two new automation lemmas; no selected statement or definition changes.

Refs #585

title: fix(reduction): let hardness proofs chain along reductions
body:
Hardness proofs couldn't be chained with dot notation. Writing #585's NP-completeness chapter, the natural way to derive Clique's hardness from Cook–Levin failed:

```lean
example : NPHard (encPair encGraph encNat) Clique :=
  (CookLevin.SAT_npHard.trans polyTimeReducible_SAT_IndependentSet).trans
    polyTimeReducible_IndependentSet_Clique
-- error: Invalid field `trans`: The environment does not contain `Function.trans`
```

`HardUnder`, which `NPHard`, `coNPHard`, `PolyTimeHard`, `LogSpaceHard`, `SearchHard` and the promise-problem `NPHard` all unfold to, began with `∀ {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) …`. Lean instantiates a leading implicit binder as soon as a term of that type is produced, so `h.trans r` had type `∀ (enc : ?α ↪ List Bool), …` rather than `NPHard encB B`, and the second `.trans` had nothing to resolve against. A single `.trans` on a named theorem worked, which is why the library never hit this. Users composing results do.

This makes the binder strict-implicit, `∀ ⦃α : Type⦄ …`, which is instantiated only when an explicit argument follows. Applying a hardness proof, `h enc A hA`, is unchanged, and the example above now elaborates. Term-mode constructions no longer get an automatic implicit lambda, so the 14 sites written `fun enc A hA => …` (3 in `ManyOne.lean`, 10 in other library modules, 1 in a test) now read `fun _ enc A hA => …`. Tactic proofs (`rintro α enc A …`) are unaffected. `HardUnder`'s docstring records why the binder is strict, and `ComplexityTests/KarpReductions.lean` checks the chained example.

**Scope.** No statement changes meaning: binder annotations don't affect what a proposition says. The definitions' displayed types change only in the annotation.

**Validation.** `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates. `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` and `build_abstracts.py --check` (12 abstracts, 16 headlines) pass.

**Abstracts.** No impact. The Cook–Levin and subset-sum abstracts define their own `NPComplete`; their bridges to the library's notions build unchanged.

Refs #585

title: doc(guide): add the NP-completeness chapter
body:
Adds the guide's NP-completeness chapter, #585's M1. It is written as a newcomer meets the area:
- problems as sets with explicit encodings;
- polynomial time with `fun_prop` and `polytime`;
- `P`, verifiers and `NP`;
- reductions as map, cost and correctness;
- hardness and completeness, and Cook–Levin;
- the catalogue of proved NP-complete problems, as a reduction tree from SAT;
- a five-step proof that `Clique` is NP-complete, following `Problems/Clique.lean`.

Every example is checked against the library, and each of the catalogue's 35 names is resolved and linked to the API documentation. First Steps becomes orientation (package, imports, namespaces, finding declarations) instead of previewing the NP results. Documentation only, with no mathematical progress.

**Base.** #599, #612 and #621 have merged, and this is rebased onto `main`; the PR is the chapter commit alone.

**Friction log.** Writing the chapter is the instrument #585 describes. Each place an example needed plumbing, and what happened to it:

| | Friction | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Membership tests written as on paper (`(u, v) ∉ G.2`, `0 ∈ l`) defeated `fun_prop` and `polytime`: there was no rule for `decide ¬p` or list membership, and `Clique.lean` hand-proved an 8-line Boolean rewrite | Fixed in #612 |
| 2 | `(SAT_npHard.trans r).trans r'` failed with "`Function.trans`": `HardUnder`'s implicit type binder was instantiated as soon as a hardness proof was produced | Fixed in #621 |
| 3 | `mem_NP` proofs bridge tidy verifier certificates with `.of_tidy`. `Problems/` states 96 public certificates tidily, against the quality standard's plain statements | `Clique` fixed in #612; the rest is #626 |
| 4 | After `import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime`, `polytime` fails on `n % 2`, `n / 2` and `testBit` (binary division is never imported) and on list length into binary | #627 |
| 5 | Plain `fun_prop` cannot certify list scans whose body uses the rest of the input; `polytime` can | Already documented in `PolyTime/Plain`; the chapter teaches `polytime` for these |
| 6 | No single import for the NP-complete problems | By design (narrow modules); the chapter imports each, and #603's index names their modules |
| 7 | `Clique.isVerifier` needs Mathlib unfoldings (`isNClique_iff`, `IsClique`) to meet `Graph.isVerifier_verifySubset`'s statement | Minor; recorded only |
| 8 | `VertexCover.verifier` tests `any (decide (w = u))` rather than `u ∈ …`, shaped by item 1 | In #626 |
| 9 | Verso's 60-column limit for code does not fit encodings such as `encPair (encPair encGraph encNat) encBits` | Guide-side: chapters allow 80 columns |
| 10 | Plain versus tidy: every cost obligation in the chapter is stated and proved with plain `ComputableInPolyTime`, and no example names a tidy notion, as #671 asks. Tidy names remain only in library certificate names that readers meet in the API docs | Plain throughout the chapter; library side in #626 |

The chapter shows the improved API: the complement map is certified by `unfold Graph.compl; polytime`, `Clique ∈ NP` by `⟨Polynomial.X, Clique.verifier, by fun_prop, Clique.isVerifier⟩`, and hardness chains from Cook–Levin with `.trans`. It links #603's checked client and `Reduction.lean`'s index rather than duplicating them, and the Cook–Levin abstract for the self-contained statement.

**Limitations.** README "Start here" doesn't link the guide yet. The live site is the deployment from before #599 merged, so `https://www.cslib.io/complexitylib/guide/` still returns 404; I'll add the link once a docs run on `main` publishes it. #626 and #627 are open, so other problem modules still show tidy certificate names.

**Validation.** On `beb22083`:
- `scripts/guide.sh` builds and renders the guide; every example and `leanOutput` expectation checks, with chapter warnings as errors.
- All 122 of the guide's API links, on 41 pages, resolve with their anchors against the live API documentation at `https://www.cslib.io/complexitylib/`, the latest docs output. The full `check_docs.py --guide` gate also re-inventories modules against current sources, and runs in the next docs build.
- `scripts/check.sh --quick` fell back to the six full gates, and all pass; `check_docs.py --config-only` passes.

**Abstracts.** No impact: the new commit changes only the guide.

Refs #585

title: refactor(classes): make proof helpers private across the classes area
body:
Makes 734 proof helpers private, in 129 modules of the classes area. This is item 2 of #610, sized as one mechanical PR following Samuel's rule change on #587. Statements and proofs are unchanged. The only edits are the `private` modifier, line breaks in signatures that it pushed past 100 columns, and five `@[expose]` attributes removed from definitions that became private (they are redundant there, and `--wfail` rejects them).

**Rule.** A declaration becomes private when all of the following hold:
- `scripts/quality_report.py` (#604, run at d52fd12c) lists it as a privatization candidate. That means:
  - no other library module, test or abstract references it;
  - no module doc or README names it;
  - it has no implicit-use attribute (`simp`, `fun_prop`, `aesop`, instance, …);
  - no statement or exposed body that stays public mentions it.
- Its own module uses it, so it is a step of a proof there. Unused candidates stay public for a separate review.
- Its name is not API-shaped.

The following stay public even when they meet the rule:
- names ending in `_iff`, `mono`, `anti`, `nonneg`, `pos`, `apply`, `ext`, `comm`, `congr`, `symm`, `trans`, `refl`, `def`, `injective` and the like;
- names that contain a class or problem name (`mem_BPP`, `UP_subset_ModP`, `inter_mem_ParityP`, `SATH_notMem_P`) or are `isVerifier`;
- the definitional modules of communication, decision-tree and query complexity, Kolmogorov complexity and learning, except their proof developments (`DecisionTree/Switching`, `DecisionTree/CanonicalTree`, `SensitivitySeparation/Internal`) and nine Huang and sensitivity proof steps;
- a few modules whose lemmas are the basic API of their definitions (`TFNP`, `PH`, `ZPP`, `RP`, `BooleanHierarchy`, `Alternation`, `Constructible`, `Parameterized`, `FineGrained`, `FineGrained/Exponents`, `Reduction/TruthTable`, `Classes/PCP`, `MIP/Defs`, `TFNP/Subclasses/Principles`, `TreeEval/Instance`), and the PCP modules whose fate #610 leaves open (`ConstraintGraph`, `RegularConstraintGraph`, `LocalTest`, `Amplification`, `Amplifier`, `GapTheorem`, `Approximation`).

**Build exceptions.** Nine more declarations stay public because the build needs them public:
- seven are reached through dot notation or namespace resolution, which does not find private names: `iffTokens`, `Graph.vertexEquiv`, `mod_lt_of_lt_mul`, `Interaction.pushStep`, `natDegree_minpoly_of_aeval_eq_zero`, `ModelChecker.tupleExpr` and `Encoded.Graph.readLabel`;
- two are used by an exposed public body: `USTCON.Reader.card_label_eq_numLabels` and `walkFrom`.

**Scope.** Files touched by an open PR or by the deprecation sweep (#631) are left out, for example `Hierarchy`, `Ladner/PolyTime`, `MIP/NEXP`, `ValiantVazirani/Reduction` and `TreeEval/Reader/Cert/Weight`. That covers 201 candidates, plus the 12 modules that #632 and #621 also edit (124 declarations, dropped in 8bca8c48). These files follow in a second pass once those PRs land.

| Subtree | Declarations made private |
|---|---|
| Classes | 285 |
| TreeEval | 108 |
| PCP | 70 |
| QueryComplexity | 47 |
| Problems | 44 |
| Parameterized | 38 |
| FineGrained | 34 |
| Fagin | 28 |
| DecisionTree | 26 |
| AffineDisperser | 21 |
| CookLevin | 14 |
| HardnessEncoding | 10 |
| USTCON | 5 |
| Communication, MCSP | 2 each |

105 of them have tidy statements, so #456's S2 sweep has 105 fewer public statements to rename.

**Why.** Users and agents get about 730 fewer public names to navigate. Editing these proof steps also no longer changes the exported module interfaces that downstream builds depend on (#609).

**Review.** Check against the rule above, with spot checks. Proof steps such as `Reader.hTup`, `IP.PSPACE.pushStep` and the `Switching` encode/decode lemmas illustrate the rule, while a result that a module's doc should list would be an exception.

**Risk.** Low. The build rejects any private name that another module, a test, an abstract or an exposed body uses; that check found the nine exceptions above. No aliases are needed (#588).

**Validation** at 8bca8c48 (on 375ea689):
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates;
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`;
- the Python unit tests;
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`.

**Abstract impact.** None. Abstracts and bridges reference no changed declaration, which the report confirms (zero abstract references) and the build of `ComplexityAbstracts` checks.

@@ -0,0 +1,337 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.DiscreteLog
+public import Complexity.Probability.BitString
+public import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.BitString
+public import Cslib.Foundations.Data.BitString
+import Complexity.Crypto.Negligible.Basic
+import Complexity.Crypto.Protocols.SigmaProtocol.Identification
+import Complexity.Foundations.Data.BitString.Counter
+import Complexity.Foundations.Data.Nat.Bits
+import Complexity.Probability.PMF
+import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Basic
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Nat.BinaryDiv
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Nat.PowMod
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Plain
+import Complexity.Tactic.PPT
+
+/-!
+# Schnorr identification under the discrete-logarithm assumption
+
+Schnorr's identification scheme ([BonehShoup2023], Section 19.1) over a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`:
+the key is a description `d`, drawn from a setup law, a uniform secret `α` and the public key
+`u = α • g`. An impersonator sees the description and the encoded public key and sends a
+commitment word `t`; the verifier draws a uniform challenge word `c` of `k n` bits; the
+impersonator answers with a word `z`. Challenges and responses are read as binary numbers modulo
+the group order `q`, and the verifier accepts when `t` encodes `z • g - c • u`; on genuine group
+elements this is Schnorr's check `z • g = t + c • u`.
+
+Rewinding an impersonator gives a discrete-logarithm adversary, `SchnorrImpersonator.rewind`. It
+runs the impersonator to its commitment, answers two independent uniform challenges from the same
+state, and computes `(c - c')⁻¹ (z - z')` modulo `q`, inverting by Fermat's little theorem. For each
+security parameter, if `2 ^ k ≤ q` for every description the setup can produce,
+
+  `ε ≤ 1 / 2 ^ k + √ε'`,
+
+where `ε` is the impersonator's success probability and `ε'` the discrete-logarithm success
+probability of the rewinding adversary (`succProbability_schnorrDirectGame_le`, Theorem 19.1).
+The rewinding adversary is uniform strict PPT whenever the impersonator is and `k` is computable
+in polynomial time. Under the discrete-logarithm assumption, with negligible `1 / 2 ^ k`, every
+uniform strict PPT impersonator therefore succeeds with negligible probability
+(`negligible_schnorrDirectGame`).
+
+The impersonator may use fresh randomness in its second stage; its state is a word. Challenges
+are bit strings because strict PPT machines sample them exactly; they cannot sample `ZMod q`
+exactly, which matters for the honest prover and for simulation but not for this reduction.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.SchnorrImpersonator`: a two-stage word adversary.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.schnorrDirectGame`: the direct impersonation attack.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.SchnorrImpersonator.rewind`: the rewinding
+  discrete-logarithm adversary.
+
+## Main results
+

+  at each security parameter.

+  PPT.
