+# --- Report -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+AREA_ORDER = [name for name, _, _ in qr.AREAS] + [qr.OTHER_AREA]
+
+
+def summary(entries: list[Entry]) -> dict:
+    by_area: dict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
+    reasons: Counter = Counter()
+    for e in entries:
+        by_area[e.area]["total"] += 1
+        by_area[e.area][e.case] += 1
+        if e.case == "unclassifiable":
+            reasons[e.reason] += 1
+    total = Counter()
+    for counts in by_area.values():
+        total.update(counts)
+    return {"areas": {a: dict(by_area[a]) for a in AREA_ORDER if a in by_area},
+            "total": dict(total), "unclassifiable_reasons": dict(reasons.most_common())}
+
+
+def markdown_report(report: dict, limit: int = 40) -> str:
+    s = report["summary"]
+    dirty = " with uncommitted changes" if report["dirty"] else ""
+    twins = ", ".join(f"{n} {k}" for k, n in sorted(report["twins"].items())) or "none"
+    registry = (f" (`{report['registry']}`: {report['registry_size']} pairs)"
+                if report["registry"] else "")
+    out = [f"Revision `{report['revision']}`{dirty}; build outputs {report['outputs']}. "
+           f"Allowlist: {report['allowlist_size']} modules. Plain twins of tidy theorems: "
+           f"{twins}{registry}.", ""]
+    if report.get("missing") is not None:
+        by_area = Counter(qr.area_of(m.removeprefix("Complexity.").replace(".", "/") + "/")
+                          if m.startswith("Complexity.") else qr.module_role(m)
+                          for m in report["missing"])
+        out += [f"**Partial build:** {len(report['missing'])} modules have no build outputs and "
+                "are not analysed (" + ", ".join(f"{a} {n}" for a, n in by_area.most_common())
+                + "). Their declarations, and references from them, are missing below.", ""]
+    out += ["### Public declarations whose statement mentions a tidy predicate", "",
+            "| Area | Total | (1) Plain twin | (2) Rename and restate | "
+            "(3) Definition or field | Unclassifiable |", "|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|"]
+    for area, c in list(s["areas"].items()) + [("Total", s["total"])]:
+        out.append(f"| {area} | {c.get('total', 0):,} | {c.get('1', 0):,} | {c.get('2', 0):,} | "
+                   f"{c.get('3', 0):,} | {c.get('unclassifiable', 0):,} |")
+    out += ["", "Unclassifiable, by reason: " + "; ".join(
+        f"{r} ({n})" for r, n in s["unclassifiable_reasons"].items()) + "."]
+    collisions = [e for e in report["entries"] if e["collision"]]
+    if collisions:
+        out += ["", "### Collisions", "",
+                "| Declaration | Target | Target module | Why |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
+        for e in collisions[:limit]:
+            c = e["collision"]
+            out.append(f"| `{e['name']}` | `{c['target']}` | `{c['module']}` | {e['detail']} |")
+        if len(collisions) > limit:
+            out.append(f"| … {len(collisions) - limit} more in the JSON report | | | |")
+    unsupported = Counter(t for e in report["entries"] for t in e["unsupported"])
+    if unsupported:
+        out += ["", "Tidy notions without a same-bound plain equivalence, by declarations "
+                "mentioning them: " + ", ".join(f"`{t}` ({n})" for t, n in
+                                                unsupported.most_common()) + "."]
+    third = [e for e in report["entries"] if e["case"] == "3"]
+    if third:
+        out += ["", "### Case 3: definitions and structure fields", ""]
+        out += [f"* `{e['name']}` ({e['kind']}, {e['area']})" for e in third[:limit]]
+        if len(third) > limit:
+            out.append(f"* … {len(third) - limit} more in the JSON report")
+    if report["registry_problems"]:
+        out += ["", "Registry problems: " + "; ".join(report["registry_problems"][:limit])]
+    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"

+# --- Lean source helpers (unit-tested in scripts/test_tidy_sweep.py) ----------------------------
+
+OPENERS, CLOSERS = "([{⦃⟨‹", ")]}⦄⟩›"
+IDENT = re.compile(qr.IDENT.pattern)
+KEYWORDS = {"by", "fun", "λ", "with", "at", "using", "from", "then", "else", "do", "in", "if",
+            "match", "show", "have", "let", "calc", "only", "generalizing", "says", "where",
+            "deriving", "termination_by", "decreasing_by", "obtain", "rcases", "refine", "exact"}
+COMMAND_KEYWORD = re.compile(r"#?[A-Za-z_]+")
+NAME_ONLY_COMMANDS = {"#print", "#check", "#guard_msgs", "attribute", "open", "export", "#eval",
+                      "#reduce", "#synth", "add_decl_doc", "#lint", "#help"}
+LEMMA_LIST_TACTIC = re.compile(
+    r"\b(?:simp|simp_all|dsimp|simp_rw|rw|rwa|rewrite|erw|nth_rewrite|nth_rw|simpa|fun_prop|"
+    r"aesop|norm_num|field_simp|grind|polytime|positivity|unfold|delta|gcongr|subst_vars|"
+    r"continuity|measurability|bound|decide|omega|linarith|nlinarith|exact\?|apply\?|"
+    r"rw_mod_cast|push_cast|norm_cast|simp_arith|conv)\b[^\[\]\n]*$")
+
+
+def match_bracket(mask: str, i: int, limit: int | None = None) -> int:
+    """The index of the bracket closing the one at `mask[i]`, or -1."""
+    depth, end = 0, len(mask) if limit is None else limit
+    for j in range(i, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+            if depth == 0:
+                return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def find_top_level(mask: str, start: int, end: int, token: str) -> int:
+    """The first `token` at bracket depth 0 in `mask[start:end]`, or -1. `:` excludes `:=`."""
+    depth = 0
+    for j in range(start, end):
+        char = mask[j]
+        if char in OPENERS:
+            depth += 1
+        elif char in CLOSERS:
+            depth -= 1
+        elif depth == 0 and mask.startswith(token, j):
+            if token == ":" and (mask.startswith(":=", j) or mask.startswith("::", j)
+                                 or (j and mask[j - 1] == ":")):
+                continue
+            return j
+    return -1
+
+
+def line_indent(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    start = text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+    return len(text[start:]) - len(text[start:].lstrip(" "))
+
+
+def column(text: str, offset: int) -> int:
+    return offset - (text.rfind("\n", 0, offset) + 1)
+
+
+def atom_end(mask: str, i: int, limit: int) -> int:
+    """The end of the atom (identifier, number, `?_`, bracket group, `.ident`) at `i` together
+    with directly attached projections (`.field`, `.1`), or `i` when no atom starts there."""
+    if i >= limit:
+        return i
+    char = mask[i]
+    if char in OPENERS:
+        end = match_bracket(mask, i, limit)
+        if end < 0:
+            return i
+        j = end + 1
+    elif char == "." and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char == "?" and mask.startswith("?_", i):
+        j = i + 2
+    elif char == "@" and i + 1 < limit and IDENT.match(mask, i + 1):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, i + 1).end()
+    elif char.isdigit():
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and (mask[j].isalnum() or mask[j] == "."):
+            j += 1
+    else:
+        match = IDENT.match(mask, i)
+        if not match or match[0].rstrip(".") in KEYWORDS:
+            return i
+        j = match.end()
+    while j < limit and mask[j] == "." and j + 1 < limit and (
+            mask[j + 1].isdigit() or IDENT.match(mask, j + 1)):
+        j = IDENT.match(mask, j + 1).end() if IDENT.match(mask, j + 1) else j + 2
+    return min(j, limit)
+
+
+NAMED_ARG = re.compile(r"\(\s*[^\W\d][\w'₀-₉]*\s*:=")
+
+
+def parse_args(mask: str, pos: int, limit: int, count: int, base_indent: int,
+               named: list[tuple[int, int]] | None = None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    """Up to `count` positional application arguments after `pos`: atoms separated by blanks,
+    continuing onto lines indented more than `base_indent`. Named arguments `(x := e)` are
+    skipped and, when `named` is given, appended to it."""
+    args = []
+    i = pos
+    while len(args) < count and i < limit:
+        j = i
+        while j < limit and mask[j] in " \t":
+            j += 1
+        if j < limit and mask[j] == "\n":
+            k = j
+            while k < limit and mask[k] in " \t\n":
+                k += 1
+            if k >= limit or line_indent(mask, k) <= base_indent:
+                break
+            j = k
+        if j == i and args:
+            break  # no blank after the previous argument
+        end = atom_end(mask, j, limit)
+        if end == j:
+            break
+        if NAMED_ARG.match(mask, j):
+            if named is not None:
+                named.append((j, end))
+        else:
+            args.append((j, end))
+        i = end
+    return args
+
+
+def strip_space(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    while start < end and mask[start].isspace():
+        start += 1
+    while end > start and mask[end - 1].isspace():
+        end -= 1
+    return start, end
+
+
+def is_atomic_application(mask: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
+    """For text `P args` in `mask[start:end]` made of atoms only, the span of `P`; else None."""
+    start, end = strip_space(mask, start, end)
+    head = atom_end(mask, start, end)
+    if head == start:
+        return None
+    args = parse_args(mask, head, end, 10 ** 6, -1)
+    last = args[-1][1] if args else head
+    return (start, head) if strip_space(mask, last, end)[0] == end else None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Binder:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    bracket: str
+    names: list[str]
+    type_start: int
+    type_end: int
+    default: bool
+
+
+@dataclass
+class DeclText:
+    start: int
+    sel_start: int
+    sel_end: int
+    end: int
+    binders: list[Binder]
+    colon: int  # the `:` before the type, or -1
+    assign: int  # the `:=` before the body, or -1
+    problems: list[str]
+
+
+def parse_decl(mask: str, start: int, sel_start: int, sel_end: int, end: int) -> DeclText:
+    """Binders, type and body of the declaration whose name ends at `sel_end`."""
+    assign = find_top_level(mask, sel_end, end, ":=")
+    stop = assign if assign >= 0 else end
+    binders, problems, colon = [], [], -1
+    i = sel_end
+    if mask.startswith(".{", i):
+        i = match_bracket(mask, i + 1, stop) + 1
+    while i < stop:
+        char = mask[i]
+        if char.isspace():
+            i += 1
+        elif char in "([{⦃":
+            close = match_bracket(mask, i, stop)
+            if close < 0:
+                problems.append("unbalanced binder")
+                break
+            inner = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":")
+            default = find_top_level(mask, i + 1, close, ":=")
+            if inner < 0:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:close].split(), close
+            else:
+                names, type_start = mask[i + 1:inner].split(), inner + 1
+            type_end = default if default >= 0 else close
+            binders.append(Binder(i, close + 1, char, names, type_start, type_end,
+                                  default >= 0))
+            i = close + 1
+        elif char == ":":
+            colon = i
+            break
+        else:
+            problems.append("binder without brackets")
+            break
+    if assign < 0:
+        problems.append("no `:=` (pattern-matching definition)")
+    return DeclText(start, sel_start, sel_end, end, binders, colon, assign, problems)
+
+
+def proof_parts(text: str, assign: int, end: int) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    """The text after `:=` and whether it is a tactic block."""
+    body = text[assign + 2:end]
+    return body, re.match(r"\s*by(?:\s|$)", body) is not None
+
+
+def collapse(text: str) -> str:
+    return " ".join(text.split())
+
+
+# --- Scopes and names ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+SCOPE_COMMAND = re.compile(
+    r"^(?P<mods>(?:@\[[^\]\n]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:public|private|noncomputable|protected|meta)\s+)*)"
+    r"(?P<kw>namespace|section|end|open|mutual|variable|export)\b", re.M)
+NOTATION_COMMAND = re.compile(
+    r"(?:@\[[^\]\n]*\]\s*)*(?:(?:local|scoped|private|public|meta)\s+)*"
+    r"(?:notation3?|infixl?|infixr|prefix|postfix|syntax|macro|elab|binder_predicate)\b")
+STRING_LITERAL = re.compile(r'"((?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*)"')
+
+
+def notation_tokens(text: str, mask: str) -> set[str]:
+    """The tokens the notation, syntax and macro commands of a source declare: the string
+    literals of each whole command, across continuation lines."""
+    starts = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(mask)] + [len(mask)]
+    tokens = set()
+    for start, end in zip(starts, starts[1:]):
+        if NOTATION_COMMAND.match(mask, start):
+            tokens.update(t.strip() for t in STRING_LITERAL.findall(text, start, end))
+    return tokens - {""}
+
+
+def token_capture(written: str, following: str, tokens) -> str | None:
+    """A token that Lean's tokenizer reads instead of the identifier `written` followed by
+    `following`: a token wins over an identifier at least as short as it. `tokens` maps first
+    characters to tokens."""
+    text = written + following
+    lexeme = IDENT.match(text)
+    length = lexeme.end() if lexeme else len(written)
+    for token in tokens.get(written[:1], ()):
+        if len(token) >= length and text.startswith(token):
+            return token
+    return None
+
+
+def by_first(tokens) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+    out: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
+    for token in tokens:
+        out[token[:1]].append(token)
+    return out
+
+
+def namespaces_of(names) -> set[str]:
+    """Every name and every proper prefix of a name, as namespaces."""
+    out = set()
+    for name in names:
+        parts = name.split(".")
+        for i in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+            out.add(".".join(parts[:i]))
+    return out
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Open:
+    """An opened namespace: all of it, only the names `only` (`open N (x y)`), or all but the
+    names `hiding`."""
+    namespace: str
+    only: frozenset[str] | None = None
+    hiding: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Scope:
+    namespace: str
+    opens: tuple[Open, ...] = ()
+    aliases: frozenset[str] = frozenset()  # short names from `open … renaming` and `export`
+    variables: frozenset[str] = frozenset()  # names bound by `variable` commands
+
+
+def binder_names(text: str) -> set[str]:
+    """The names bound by the top-level binder groups of a `variable` command (masked)."""
+    names, i = set(), 0
+    while i < len(text):
+        if text[i] in "([{⦃":
+            close = match_bracket(text, i)
+            if close < 0:
+                break
+            inner = text[i + 1:close]
+            colon = find_top_level(inner, 0, len(inner), ":")
+            if colon >= 0:
+                names.update(inner[:colon].split())
+            elif text[i] != "[":
+                names.update(inner.split())
+            i = close + 1
+        else:
+            i += 1
+    return {n for n in names if IDENT.fullmatch(n) and n != "_"}
+
+
+class Scopes:
+    """The namespace, opened namespaces, aliases and section variables at each offset of a
+    masked source, and the tokens its notations, syntax and macros declare."""
+
+    def __init__(self, mask: str, namespaces: set[str], text: str | None = None):
+        self.points: list[tuple[int, Scope]] = [(0, Scope(""))]
+        self.once: list[tuple[int, int, tuple[Open, ...], frozenset[str]]] = []
+        # frames: [kind, name, opens, aliases, variables]
+        stack: list[list] = [["file", "", [], set(), set()]]
+        starts = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(mask)] + [len(mask)]
+        self.tokens = by_first(notation_tokens(text if text is not None else mask, mask))
+
+        def namespace() -> str:
+            return ".".join(f[1] for f in stack if f[0] == "namespace" and f[1])
+
+        def resolve(word: str, earlier: list[Open]) -> list[str]:
+            ns = namespace()
+            parts = ns.split(".") if ns else []
+            prefixes = [".".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(len(parts), -1, -1)]
+            prefixes += [o.namespace for f in stack for o in f[2]]
+            prefixes += [o.namespace for o in earlier]
+            found = [p + "." + word if p else word for p in prefixes
+                     if (p + "." + word if p else word) in namespaces]
+            return list(dict.fromkeys(found)) or [word]
+
+        for match in SCOPE_COMMAND.finditer(mask):
+            kw = match["kw"]
+            end = next((x for x in starts if x > match.start()), len(mask))
+            rest = mask[match.end():end]
+            words = rest.split()
+            if kw == "namespace" and words:
+                stack.append(["namespace", words[0], [], set(), set()])
+            elif kw in ("section", "mutual"):
+                stack.append([kw, words[0] if words and kw == "section" else "", [], set(),
+                              set()])
+            elif kw == "end":
+                if len(stack) > 1:
+                    stack.pop()
+            elif kw == "variable":
+                stack[-1][4].update(binder_names(rest))
+            elif kw in ("open", "export"):
+                one_shot = bool(words) and words[-1] == "in"
+                body = " ".join(words[:-1] if one_shot else words)
+                opens, aliases = self.parse_open(body, resolve, kw == "export")
+                if one_shot:
+                    following = next((x for x in starts if x > end), len(mask))
+                    self.once.append((match.start(), following, tuple(opens),
+                                      frozenset(aliases)))
+                    continue
+                stack[-1][2].extend(opens)
+                stack[-1][3].update(aliases)
+            self.points.append((match.end(), Scope(
+                namespace(), tuple(o for f in stack for o in f[2]),
+                frozenset().union(*(f[3] for f in stack)),
+                frozenset().union(*(f[4] for f in stack)))))
+        self.offsets = [point for point, _ in self.points]
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def parse_open(body: str, resolve, export: bool) -> tuple[list[Open], set[str]]:
+        """The namespaces an `open` (or `export`) command makes visible, and the short names it
+        introduces as aliases. `open scoped` opens no names."""
+        words = body.replace("(", " ( ").replace(")", " ) ").replace(",", " ").split()
+        if not words or words[0] == "scoped":
+            return [], set()
+        if words[0] == "private":
+            words = words[1:]
+        if "renaming" in words:
+            pairs = words[words.index("renaming") + 1:]
+            return [], {pairs[i + 2] for i in range(len(pairs) - 2) if pairs[i + 1] == "→"}
+        if "hiding" in words:
+            k = words.index("hiding")
+            return [Open(ns, hiding=frozenset(words[k + 1:]))
+                    for w in words[:k] for ns in resolve(w, [])], set()
+        if "(" in words:
+            k = words.index("(")
+            names = frozenset(w for w in words[k + 1:] if w != ")")
+            opens = [Open(ns, only=names) for w in words[:k] for ns in resolve(w, [])]
+            return ([] if export else opens), (set(names) if export else set())
+        opens: list[Open] = []
+        for w in words:  # a later name may be relative to an earlier one
+            opens += [Open(ns) for ns in resolve(w, opens)]
+        return opens, set()
+
+    def at(self, offset: int) -> Scope:
+        i = bisect.bisect_right(self.offsets, offset) - 1
+        scope = self.points[i][1] if i >= 0 else Scope("")
+        for start, end, opens, aliases in self.once:
+            if start <= offset < end:
+                scope = Scope(scope.namespace, scope.opens + opens, scope.aliases | aliases,
+                              scope.variables)
+        return scope
+
+    def chain(self, offset: int) -> list[str]:
+        """The enclosing namespaces, innermost first, ending with the root `""`."""
+        ns = self.at(offset).namespace
+        parts = ns.split(".") if ns else []
+        return [".".join(parts[:i]) for i in range(len(parts), -1, -1)]
+
+    def prefixes(self, offset: int) -> list[str]:
+        """Namespaces a written name may be relative to, innermost first (`""` is the root);
+        selective opens count as whole ones (an over-approximation)."""
+        return self.chain(offset) + [o.namespace for o in self.at(offset).opens]
+
+
+def written_name(target: str, prefixes: list[str], known: set[str]) -> str:
+    """The shortest suffix of `target` that resolves to it, and to nothing else, from a position
+    whose namespace prefixes and opened namespaces are `prefixes`."""
+    parts = target.split(".")
+    for k in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
+        suffix = ".".join(parts[-k:])
+        hits = {p + "." + suffix if p else suffix for p in prefixes}
+        resolved = {h for h in hits if h in known or h == target}
+        if resolved == {target}:
+            return suffix
+    return target
+
+
+def renamed_token(token: str, old: str, new: str) -> str | None:
+    """`token` (a written form of `old`) with the renamed part, when the written prefix still
+    resolves the same way (`old = P.token` and `new = P.result`); otherwise None."""
+    at = "@" if token.startswith("@") else ""
+    bare = token[len(at):]
+    root = "_root_." if bare.startswith("_root_.") else ""
+    bare = bare[len(root):]
+    if not (old == bare or old.endswith("." + bare)):
+        return None
+    prefix = old[:len(old) - len(bare)]
+    if not new.startswith(prefix):
+        return None
+    result = new[len(prefix):]
+    if not result or (prefix and result.startswith(".")):
+        return None
+    return at + root + result
+
+
+# --- Edits --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Replace:
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    text: str
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Wrap:
+    """Text inserted before `open` and after `close`; `site` orders wraps with equal spans (the
+    wrap of the site that starts first is outermost)."""
+    open: int
+    close: int
+    before: str
+    after: str
+    site: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Region:
+    """A span whose edited text is then transformed by `build`."""
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    build: object
+    decl: str
+
+
+def render(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap], lo: int, hi: int) -> str:
+    """`text[lo:hi]` with the replacements and wraps inside it applied. At one position, wraps
+    close (innermost first) before others open (outermost first), then a replacement starts."""
+    reps = sorted((r for r in replaces if lo <= r.start and r.end <= hi),
+                  key=lambda r: (r.start, r.end))
+    ws = [w for w in wraps if lo <= w.open and w.close <= hi]
+    points = sorted({r.start for r in reps} | {w.open for w in ws} | {w.close for w in ws})
+    starting = defaultdict(list)
+    for r in reps:
+        starting[r.start].append(r)
+    out, cur = [], lo
+    for p in points:
+        if p < cur:
+            continue  # inside a replaced span
+        out.append(text[cur:p])
+        out += [w.after for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.close == p),
+                                        key=lambda w: (-w.open, -w.site))]
+        out += [w.before for w in sorted((w for w in ws if w.open == p),
+                                         key=lambda w: (-w.close, w.site))]
+        cur = p
+        for r in starting.get(p, []):
+            out.append(r.text)
+            cur = max(cur, r.end)
+    out.append(text[cur:hi])
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+def apply_edits(text: str, replaces: list[Replace], wraps: list[Wrap],
+                regions: list[Region]) -> str:
+    out, cur = [], 0
+    for region in sorted(regions, key=lambda r: r.start):
+        out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, region.start))
+        out.append(region.build(render(text, replaces, wraps, region.start, region.end)))
+        cur = region.end
+    out.append(render(text, replaces, wraps, cur, len(text)))
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+# --- Round trips --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+OF_TIDY = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.'])(?:(?:[\w.']*\.)?Computable(?:In(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|"
+                     r"FPTTime))\.|\.)of_tidy\b")
+DOT_ROUND_TRIP = re.compile(r"\.tidy\.computableIn(?:PolyTime|PolySpace|Space|O|FPTTime)\b")
+
+
+def cancel_round_trips(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
+    """Remove `of_tidy (x.tidy)`, `of_tidy <| x.tidy` and `x.tidy.computableIn…` round trips,
+    where `x` is an atom. Returns the new text and the number of removals."""
+    count = 0
+    while True:
+        mask = masks(text)[1]
+        change = None
+        for match in DOT_ROUND_TRIP.finditer(mask):
+            change = (match.start(), match.end(), "")
+            break
+        if change is None:
+            for match in OF_TIDY.finditer(mask):
+                i = match.end()
+                while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                    i += 1
+                pipe = mask.startswith("<|", i)
+                if pipe:
+                    i += 2
+                    while i < len(mask) and mask[i] in " \t":
+                        i += 1
+                end = atom_end(mask, i, len(mask))
+                if end == i:
+                    continue
+                inner = (i, end)
+                if mask[i] == "(" and match_bracket(mask, i) == end - 1:
+                    inner = strip_space(mask, i + 1, end - 1)
+                start, stop = inner
+                if not mask[start:stop].endswith(".tidy") or atom_end(mask, start, stop) != stop:
+                    continue
+                core_end = stop - len(".tidy")
+                if atom_end(mask, start, core_end) != core_end:
+                    continue
+                if pipe:
+                    after = end
+                    while after < len(mask) and mask[after] in " \t":
+                        after += 1
+                    if after < len(mask) and mask[after] not in CLOSERS + "\n,":
+                        continue
+                change = (match.start(), end, text[start:core_end])
+                break
+        if change is None:
+            return text, count
+        start, end, new = change
+        new_mask = masks(new)[1]
+        if (start > 0 and text[start - 1] == "(" and end < len(text) and text[end] == ")"
+                and atom_end(new_mask, 0, len(new)) == len(new) and not new.startswith("@")):
+            start, end = start - 1, end + 1
+        text = text[:start] + new + text[end:]
+        count += 1
+
+
+# --- Wrapping -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Hyp:
+    names: list[str]
+    old_type: str  # one line
+    simple: bool
+
+
+def reindent(lines: list[str], delta: int) -> list[str] | None:
+    """Shift lines by `delta` columns; None when that would remove non-blank text."""
+    out = []
+    for line in lines:
+        if not line.strip():
+            out.append("")
+        elif delta >= 0:
+            out.append(" " * delta + line)
+        elif len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" ")) >= -delta:
+            out.append(line[-delta:])
+        else:
+            return None
+    return out
+
+
+def wrap_proof(body: str, body_column: int, decl_indent: int, hyps: list[Hyp],
+               conclusion: str | None, simple_conclusion: bool, iffs: str) -> str | None:
+    """The new text after `:=` for a proof `body` of the old (tidy) statement, now stated plainly:
+    tidy hypotheses are recovered, and the old conclusion converted. `body_column` is the column
+    of the first character of `body`. None when the layout cannot be preserved."""
+    stripped = body.lstrip()
+    lead = body[:len(body) - len(stripped)]
+    first_col = body_column + len(lead) if "\n" not in lead else len(lead.rsplit("\n", 1)[1])
+    stripped = stripped.rstrip()
+    tactic = re.match(r"by(?=\s|$)", stripped) is not None
+    if not hyps and simple_conclusion and not tactic:
+        return f"{lead}.of_tidy ({stripped})"
+    k = decl_indent + 2
+    rebind = []
+    for hyp in hyps:
+        for name in hyp.names:
+            rebind.append(f"have {name} := {name}.tidy" if hyp.simple else
+                          f"have {name} : {hyp.old_type} := by simpa only [{iffs}] using {name}")
+    if tactic:
+        rest = stripped[2:]
+        if rest.lstrip(" \t").startswith("\n") or not rest.strip():
+            lines = rest.lstrip(" \t")[1:].split("\n")
+            nonblank = [ln for ln in lines if ln.strip()]
+            if not nonblank:
+                return None
+            k = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        else:
+            first_line, _, tail = rest.lstrip(" \t").partition("\n")
+            tactic_col = first_col + 2 + (len(rest) - len(rest.lstrip(" \t")))
+            shifted = reindent(tail.split("\n"), k - tactic_col) if tail else []
+            if shifted is None:
+                return None
+            lines = [" " * k + first_line] + shifted
+        pad = " " * k
+        out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+        if conclusion is None:
+            out += lines
+        elif simple_conclusion:
+            out += [pad + "refine .of_tidy ?_"] + lines
+        else:
+            inner = reindent(lines, 2)
+            out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} := by"] + inner + \
+                [pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+        return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+    first, _, tail = stripped.partition("\n")
+    tail_lines = tail.split("\n") if tail else []
+    nonblank = [ln for ln in tail_lines if ln.strip()]
+    shift = 0
+    if nonblank:
+        least = min(len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip(" ")) for ln in nonblank)
+        shift = max(0, k + 2 - least)
+    tail_lines = reindent(tail_lines, shift) or tail_lines
+    pad = " " * k
+    out = [pad + line for line in rebind]
+    term = "\n".join([first] + tail_lines)
+    if conclusion is None:
+        out.append(pad + "exact " + term)
+    elif simple_conclusion:
+        out.append(pad + "exact .of_tidy (" + term + ")")
+    else:
+        out += [pad + f"have this : {conclusion} :=", pad + "  " + term,
+                pad + f"simpa only [{iffs}] using this"]
+    return " by\n" + "\n".join(out)
+

+# --- Planning -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@dataclass
+class Manual:
+    path: str
+    line: int
+    decl: str
+    kind: str
+    detail: str = ""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Ref:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+    decl: str | None
+
+
+class SourceFile:
+    def __init__(self, path: Path, namespaces: set[str]):
+        self.path = path
+        self.text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.code, self.mask = masks(self.text) if path.suffix == ".lean" else (self.text,) * 2
+        self.lines = self.text.split("\n")
+        self.starts = [0]
+        for line in self.lines:
+            self.starts.append(self.starts[-1] + len(line) + 1)
+        self.commands = [m.start() for m in qr.COMMAND_START.finditer(self.mask)]
+        self._namespaces = namespaces
+        self._scopes: Scopes | None = None
+
+    @property
+    def scopes(self) -> Scopes:
+        if self._scopes is None:
+            self._scopes = Scopes(self.mask, self._namespaces, self.text)
+        return self._scopes
+
+    def at(self, line: int, column16: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 0-based line and UTF-16 column (`.ilean` positions)."""
+        return self.starts[line] + qr.utf16_index(self.lines[line], column16)
+
+    def at_range(self, line: int, column: int) -> int:
+        """The offset of a 1-based line and code-point column (declaration ranges)."""
+        return self.starts[line - 1] + column
+
+    def line_of(self, offset: int) -> int:
+        """The 1-based line of an offset."""
+        return self.text.count("\n", 0, offset) + 1
+
+    def command_keyword(self, offset: int) -> str:
+        starts = [s for s in self.commands if s <= offset]
+        if not starts:
+            return ""
+        match = COMMAND_KEYWORD.match(self.mask, starts[-1])
+        return match[0] if match else ""
+
+    def comment_spans(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+        if self.path.suffix != ".lean":
+            return [(0, len(self.text))]
+        spans, i = [], 0
+        while i < len(self.text):
+            if self.code[i] != self.text[i]:
+                j = i
+                while j < len(self.text) and self.code[j] != self.text[j] or (
+                        j < len(self.text) and self.text[j] == "\n" and j + 1 < len(self.text)
+                        and self.code[j + 1] != self.text[j + 1]):
+                    j += 1
+                spans.append((i, j))
+                i = j
+            else:
+                i += 1
+        return spans
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FileEdits:
+    replaces: list[Replace] = field(default_factory=list)
+    wraps: list[Wrap] = field(default_factory=list)
+    regions: list[Region] = field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class Planner:
+    """The edits of one area's batch: case 2 declarations restated and renamed, the references
+    to them converted, and case 1 twins used in proofs that become plain.
+
+    No edit is made at a span whose text does not spell the referenced constant, and a
+    replacement is written only when it resolves to its intended target, and nothing else, from
+    its position. A declaration with a reference that cannot be converted completely is deferred
+    (left tidy), so that skipped references stay unchanged."""
+
+    def __init__(self, model: Model, entries: list[Entry], twins: dict[str, str], area: str,
+                 force_wrap: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+                 bridge: frozenset[tuple[str, str]] = frozenset()):
+        self.model, self.area, self.force_wrap = model, area, force_wrap
+        self.bridge = bridge
+        self.entries = {e.name: e for e in entries}
+        self.batch = {e.name: e for e in entries if e.area == area and e.case == "2"}
+        self.twins = {o: p for o, p in twins.items() if p in model.constants}
+        self.privates = private_by_module(model.constants)
+        self.known = model.known | {e.target for e in self.batch.values()}
+        self.namespaces = namespaces_of(self.known)
+        self.sources: dict[Path, SourceFile] = {}
+        self.deferred: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        self._refs: dict[str, list[Ref]] = {}
+        self._locals: dict[tuple[str, int, int], set[str]] = {}
+        self._decl_spans: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {}
+        self.tokens = by_first(model.tokens)
+        self.reset()
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        """Forget the edits of a planning pass."""
+        self.renames = {n: e.target for n, e in self.batch.items() if n not in self.deferred}
+        self.files: dict[Path, FileEdits] = defaultdict(FileEdits)
+        self.manual: list[Manual] = []
+        self.decls: dict[str, dict] = {}
+        self.spans: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, str]]] = defaultdict(list)
+        self.needs: dict[str, dict[str, bool]] = defaultdict(dict)
+        self.sites: Counter = Counter()
+        self.twin_refs: Counter = Counter()
+        self.imports: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
+        self.blockers: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
+        self.bridged: list[str] = []
+        self.round_trips = 0
+
+    # Sources and references.
+
+    def source(self, path: Path) -> SourceFile:
+        if path not in self.sources:
+            self.sources[path] = SourceFile(path, self.namespaces)
+        return self.sources[path]
+
+    def refs(self, module: str) -> list[Ref]:
+        if module not in self._refs:
+            src = self.source(qr.source_path(module))
+            out = []
+            for name, _, info in self.model.lib.references(module):
+                for u in info["usages"]:
+                    out.append(Ref(name, src.at(u[0], u[1]), src.at(u[2], u[3]),
+                                   u[4] if len(u) == 5 else None))
+            self._refs[module] = sorted(out, key=lambda x: x.start)
+        return self._refs[module]
+
+    def ref_kind(self, name: str) -> str:
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return "pred"
+        if owner in self.renames:
+            return "renamed"
+        if name in self.twins:
+            return "twin"
+        if name in BRIDGES:
+            return "bridge"
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        if const.get("tidy") or const.get("tb") or is_tidy_constant(name):
+            return "tidy"
+        return "plain"
+
+    def new_name(self, name: str) -> str:
+        if name in BY_TIDY:
+            return BY_TIDY[name].plain
+        owner = qr.owner_of(name, self.model.owners) or name
+        if owner in self.renames and (name == owner or name.startswith(owner + ".")):
+            return self.renames[owner] + name[len(owner):]
+        return self.twins.get(name, name)
+
+    def note(self, path: Path, offset: int, decl: str | None, kind: str, detail: str = ""):
+        src = self.source(path)
+        self.manual.append(Manual(str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), src.line_of(offset), decl or "",
+                                  kind, detail))
+
+    def where(self, path: Path, offset: int) -> str:
+        return f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{self.source(path).line_of(offset)}"
+
+    def need(self, module: str, constant: str, public: bool) -> None:
+        defining = self.model.constants.get(constant, {}).get("m")
+        if defining and defining != module:
+            self.needs[module][defining] = self.needs[module].get(defining, False) or public
+
+    def notions_of(self, name: str) -> list[Notion]:
+        const = self.model.constants.get(name, {})
+        return [BY_TIDY[t] for t in const.get("tidy", []) if t in BY_TIDY]
+
+    # Names.
+
+    def local_names(self, module: str, src: SourceFile, offset: int) -> set[str]:
+        """Identifiers of the declaration (or command) around `offset` that are not references
+        to constants: binders, local hypotheses, tactic names. A written name whose first
+        component is one of them could be captured by a local."""
+        if module not in self._decl_spans:
+            ranges = self.model.lib.ileans.get(module, {}).get("decls", {}).values()
+            self._decl_spans[module] = [(src.at(r[0], r[1]), src.at(r[2], r[3]))
+                                        for r in ranges]
+        span = next(((a, b) for a, b in self._decl_spans[module] if a <= offset < b), None)
+        if span is None:
+            starts = src.commands + [len(src.mask)]
+            start = max([s for s in starts if s <= offset], default=0)
+            span = (start, min(s for s in starts if s > offset) if offset < len(src.mask)
+                    else len(src.mask))
+        key = (module, *span)
+        if key not in self._locals:
+            refs = [(x.start, x.end) for x in self.refs(module)
+                    if span[0] <= x.start < span[1]]
+            names = set()
+            for match in IDENT.finditer(src.mask, *span):
+                if not any(a <= match.start() < b for a, b in refs):
+                    names.add(match[0].split(".")[0])
+            self._locals[key] = names - KEYWORDS
+        return self._locals[key]
+
+    def resolves(self, module: str, src: SourceFile, offset: int, written: str,
+                 following: str = "") -> set[str]:
+        """Everything `written` (without `@`, followed by `following`) might denote at
+        `offset`, over-approximated: constants reached through the enclosing namespaces and
+        every opened namespace (selective and hiding opens counted whole), private constants of
+        the module, `"<local>"` when its first component is a local binder, a section variable
+        or an alias from `open … renaming` or `export`, and `"<token>"` when the tokenizer would
+        read a notation, syntax or macro token there instead (from the import closure, scoped
+        ones included, or from the module's own commands). Names come from the whole import
+        closure, not only the referenced ones."""
+        privates = self.privates.get(module, set())
+
+        def exists(name: str) -> bool:
+            return name in self.known or name in privates
+        if written.startswith("_root_."):

title: feat(scripts): plan and rewrite the S2 tidy sweep
body:
Adds `scripts/tidy_sweep.py`, the tooling for S2 of #456 (the [S2 design](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/456#issuecomment-6376748411)). It removes tidy computability from public statements one #587 area at a time, following Samuel's direction: plain is the API, and tidy is how proofs are done. Tidy reasoning is fine inside proofs, never in a theorem statement or a definition's public type. This is infrastructure only: no library declaration changes here. The first area batch, Logics, is prepared separately and opens once this is accepted.

```bash
python3 scripts/tidy_sweep.py report [--area A] [--partial] --json r.json --markdown r.md   # dry run, ~40 s
python3 scripts/tidy_sweep.py rewrite --area Logics --diff plan.patch                       # preview
python3 scripts/tidy_sweep.py rewrite --area Logics --verify                                # rewrite, strict build
```

**Classification.** It reuses #604's extractor. `QualityReport.lean` additionally reports tidy constants in exposed definition bodies and, when asked, two more things: a statement hash that identifies each tidy predicate with its plain counterpart, and per-binder tidy flags. Its `--names` mode lists every constant, `export` alias and parser token of the import closure. The cases:
1. A theorem with a committed plain twin: the public plain theorem named by the plain rename, either `exact` or broader. `--registry` adds pairs from a migration script, validated strictly; nothing is checked in.
2. Any other theorem. It is renamed `computableTidily…` → `computable…` for the five same-bound notions, after checking the target against public and same-module private names.
3. Definitions, instances and structure fields.

Everything else is unclassifiable: an unsupported notion, a bridge, a tidy-notion definition, or a collision.

**Rewrite.** Edits go at the exact `.ilean` reference spans; a span that does not spell the referenced constant is never edited. A replacement name is written only if Lean surely resolves it to its target from that position and nothing else can bind it there. The check covers:
- namespaces, and `open`s by kind (selective, hiding, `scoped`, renaming);
- every constant and alias of the import closure;
- same-module private names, local binders and section variables;
- notation, syntax and macro tokens: imported, multiline, rooted, and the dotted `.tidy`/`.of_tidy` spellings the rewrite inserts itself.

Field and leading-dot references are kept only when the namespace changes with the tidy predicate itself. A rename whose new name could capture another reference is deferred.

Each case 2 declaration of the area is handled in one of three ways:
- *Deferred*, left tidy with its references unchanged. A reference to it that cannot be converted completely defers it, so skipped sites stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
- *Translated*: the proof's names are swapped in place.
- *Wrapped*: the old proof runs on `.tidy` hypotheses under `.of_tidy`. This is a fine permanent state.

A call site in a proof that stays tidy keeps its old type: `(lemma args).tidy`, with `.of_tidy` on tidy arguments. The tool also adds imports, cancels round trips, and renames docs and `#guard_msgs` text.

**Verification.** `--verify` builds the three libraries strictly (`--wfail --iofail`). A translated proof that fails is wrapped. A wrapped proof or client that fails gets `attribute [local fun_prop] ComputableInPolyTime.tidy in`, scoped to its declaration. That is proof-local tidy reasoning, reported for information as a plain-calculus gap. Remaining failures give status `failed` and exit 1; nothing is patched with `sorry`. Lines the rewrite pushes past 100 characters (with code) are listed. `report --partial` analyses a tree that does not build completely, and requires the loaded outputs to be current.

**Dry run on `main` `c85201e0`.** 2,077 declarations; 25 committed twins; 1,779 to restate (510 translate, 601 wrap, 668 deferred); 14 definitions or fields; 259 unclassifiable. On Codex's staging tree `83401205`, with S1's committed plain calculus, it gives 413 twins and 616 translate, 248 wrap, 180 deferred over the modules that build there (numbers on #456 after acceptance).

**Logics, prepared on `refactor/tidy-sweep-logics`.** All 20 Logics certificates are restated plainly, and no public Logics statement mentions tidy. The six gates pass. Twelve declarations needed the scoped local transition, and six needed hand-written certificates inside the proof.

**Limitations.**
- Uses that leave no reference (`fun_prop`, simp sets, Aesop) are found only by the strict build.
- Unconvertible call sites defer their lemma rather than being patched.
- Case 3, internalizing case 1 originals, and docstring wording are left to people.
- The `polytime` Aesop set still reduces plain goals to tidy ones.

**Validation.** At `2b847828`: all Python tests (61 for this tool) and `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` pass. The six gates last passed at `fc2f8a0c`; the commits since change only Python. #604's report output is unchanged.

Abstracts: no impact. Only scripts change.

Refs #456

Reviewed exact PR head b5329faa7824d73e2d7721ca0dbe7453c2980aba, with Lean source 3f273bbfa63b964c32474cd341e253ddcf466fb0. No mathematical-correctness or API finding in the source; two bounded presentation/coverage findings follow.

1. [must-fix] PR description, Summary and `padMajority` bullet: shell expansion has corrupted the mathematical statement (`PP569Xcompleteness`, missing `2`/`Q`/`j`, selector variable `zsh`, dangling dollar signs). Replace the body through a literal body file or structured API field. State the odd relabeling `2v+1`, positive even dummies `2j+2` for `j<Q`, selector `0`, and the exact count/threshold identities in plain code or correctly escaped math. The current description is not a reliable review record even though the Lean statements are correct.

2. [should-fix] `ComplexityTests/CountingCompleteness.lean:62`: the claimed tie-rejection and zero-boundary padding coverage is not present. The two-unit-clause example has one satisfying assignment out of four, not a tie; the padding examples use Q=1 and Q=2 with a nonempty variable set. Add a genuine tie (`[[(0,true)]]` is not in MAJSAT), plus direct zero-boundary padding clients such as `SharpSAT (padMajority [] 0) = 1`, `(padMajority [] 0).vars.toFinset.card = 1`, and rejection of that padded formula (one of two assignments). A nonempty Q=0 tie client is also useful. I checked these proposed clients in an isolated MCP snippet: all compile using direct `decide` after exposing the MAJSAT inequality. This is a coverage/reporting correction, not evidence of a theorem bug.

Checked and sound: firstPositions bijects first occurrences with distinct occurring variables and its unary-output runtime is certified. Strict majority uses `2^k < 2*count`; ties reject. The padding partitions variables into selector 0, positive evens and injectively shifted odds. Selector false contributes exactly the original model count with all dummies fixed false; selector true contributes `2^Q*(2^k-1)`, including k=0 and Q=0. The natural subtraction is justified by `2^Q ≤ 2^(Q+k)`. Hardness feeds the parsimonious formula for twice the #P count into padding, with the exponent computed in unary, so the polynomial-time certificate is genuine and there is no hidden exponential unary input. The finite-map counting interface requires both injectivity on occurring-variable assignments and realizability of every selected image; the proof supplies both.

Fresh MCP diagnostics are clean for CountingSAT, SharpSAT and CountingCompleteness. I did not repeat the six-gate build; the author reports it passed. The index matches the occurring-variable, strict-majority and verifier-based model, all 12 changed declaration links resolve to the named statements at the pinned source, and the rendered changed page 2 is clean. Source is unchanged between the cited source and document heads. Simon's thesis metadata matches the Cornell primary repository (https://ecommons.cornell.edu/entities/publication/8b5105ee-7c85-435b-b4bf-86bade8ecf9d); source credit/AI disclosure are present. I made no repository edits. Please refresh the exact review after the bounded fixes; dependency-stack/PDF integration remains the coordinator's separate step.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
**Samuel's direction for S1 and S2** (relayed by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`; Samuel chose this option in conversation). Tidy is a proof technique for the machine layer. It is not a public abstraction: **plain is the API, and tidy is how it's proved.**

The 412 kernel-checked transports in this PR are the right proofs. What needs to change is how they're packaged:

1. **Plain rules are ordinary source declarations,** with docstrings, each proved by a short transport from the internal tidy rule. The mirror tool may generate that source once, as a migration script under `scripts/`. It doesn't remain library infrastructure, so the library ships no `@[plain_mirror]`, `plain_mirror_sources` or `plain_mirror_registrations` and no checked-in registry JSON. A reader or grep should find every plain rule in the source.
2. **Only plain rules are registered publicly with `fun_prop` and Aesop.** Tidy registrations become local or scoped to the machine-construction modules, so client automation never produces a tidy goal. The S2 pilot needed an `attribute [local fun_prop] ComputableInPolyTime.tidy in` fallback; that should disappear.
3. **Tidy declarations move into an internal namespace,** allowed only in the 23 allowlisted machine-construction files (comment 6376743596 on #608). S3's guard enforces this as a ratchet down to zero.
4. **New machine rules are exported only as plain.** Tidy may be used in their proofs. Contributors outside the machine layer never need to know tidy exists.
5. **The 159 bound-sensitive statements** (`…InDegree`, `…InTimeAndSpace`, `…InLinearTimeAndSpace`, `IsTidyOraclePPTOn`, `…InBigO`, `ComputesTidily…`) get one decision per notion. Each either gets a plain public form with the clean-up overhead stated, or stays inside the machine layer.

Removing tidy from the machine layer altogether is **not** the goal. Composition needs the clean-tape invariant, and the base definitions live upstream in cslib.

`coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`, please revise #671 along these lines, or reply here if one of the points has a technical problem. #666 (S2) will consume committed plain declarations instead of a registry.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Agreed (`coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`). Both S1 workers have switched to this direction. #671 is being converted to ordinary typed plain declarations with docstrings, retaining the checked proofs and existing broader canonical rules. The shipped attribute/derivation commands and registry JSON will be removed. The inventory will inspect the actual declarations and kernel-check compatibility from a script, rather than depend on library derivation infrastructure. The 412-pair checkpoint `c8096188` is preserved separately; all six gates passed there, but that does not validate the new packaging or complete the boundary migration.

There is one concrete sequencing/layering problem with applying point 3 literally as a packaging change: the transport proofs currently depend on tidy calculus/equivalence declarations in roughly 44 generic topic modules outside the 23 raw-construction files. For example, `PolyTime/Basic.lean` and `PolyTime/Plain.lean` sit above the encoding/primitives layer. Moving their bodies into the raw combinator files would reverse dependencies or create cycles. Merely renaming those declarations `Internal` in their current files would not meet the stated file boundary.

The endpoint should instead make the canonical generic rules plain **in their existing topic modules**, move their old proof bodies behind those plain statements, retire superseded tidy declarations, and migrate references. Removing global tidy automation also has to be checked together with those clients: the earlier S2 pilot already demonstrated failures when domain proofs still ask for tidy certificates. I will keep #671 a draft while doing the source conversion and coordinate that cutover with S2; I will not claim the 23-file/public-automation endpoint from ordinary wrappers alone, widen the allowlist silently, or scatter client fallbacks as a substitute.

For bound-sensitive notions, the decision must preserve the actual quantitative information. Existing `TidyNormalForm` gives plain `(t,s)` to tidy `(2*t + 3*s + c, c*(s+1))`; the zero-space construction has the separate `(2*t+2, 0)` bound. Degree certificates retain their independent output bound, and `InBigO` lacks the output-length premise of `InO`. We are enumerating the affected declarations and their overlaps, then choosing a stated-overhead plain theorem or internal machine use per notion. No same-bound blanket rename is being applied. Fixed-machine `ComputesTidily…` predicates are internal candidates; oracle normalization must retain the joint stateful law.

title: refactor(calculus): prove the canonical plain core directly
body:
Plain PT/O/Degree/linear proofs now use canonical machine-witness rules directly, with existing entry modules reexporting their names. The included closure and primitive rules preserve generic encodings, complete callback contexts, independent time/workspace/output bounds and the distinction between charged O and uncharged time/space bounds. Superseded same-name plain wrappers are removed.

Both composition alternatives live in the raw-free core. Inner-first inference avoids the original Extraction test's 12,000-heartbeat timeout; outer-first inference remains available to standalone clients. One private Liu–Pass certificate explicitly composes arithmetic after that ordering exposed expensive search. Its program, statement and resource limit are unchanged. Claude's #1039 supplies direct binary-index lookup without expanding a binary index to unary.

**This is a core milestone; S1 and S4 remain open.** Decoder/Native/StepMachine field and API changes, strict PPT activation and the whole Crypto public-surface sweep are a subsequent delivery with their consumers. Tidy codec capability fields, four conversion bridges and framed-word conversion proofs remain transitional. No mirror attribute, derivation command, registry or compatibility alias ships here.

The sole allowlist addition is the exact `Internal/NormalForm.lean` path: five statements return bare normalized machines, rather than a high-level tidy calculus. [Boundary rationale](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6400704445). There is no wildcard or baseline increase; the final zero boundary remains #862's objective.

<details>
<summary>32 legacy plain wrappers still deferred</summary>

All names below are in `ComputableInPolyTime`:

- Basic: `bool_or`, `decide_eq'`, `beq`.
- List: `anyWithInput`, `bitsAppend`, `bitsTakeWithInput`, `encoding_length`, `filterWithInput`, `flatMapWithInput`, `headD`, `length_list`, `length_bits`, `bitsDropWithInput`, `length_bits_comp`.
- Nat: `unary_add`, `unary_eval`, `unary_mul`, `unary_pow`.
- Nat/Binary: `binary_bitwise`, `binary_and`, `binary_or`, `binary_xor`, `binary_and'`, `binary_or'`, `binary_xor'`, `binary_size`, `binary_min_unary`, `binary_min_unary'`, `binary_shiftRight`, `binary_shiftRight'`, `binary_mul'`, `binary_two_pow`.

`bits_encList_polyTime` and `trans_encList_polyTime` also retain raw construction dependencies. `PairEncoding`, `ListEncoding` and `OptionEncoding` still expose tidy linear capability fields. This is not a claim of transitive plain compliance.

</details>

**New definitions: existing notions considered.** The existing plain `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`, `ComputableInBigO` and `ComputableInDegree` remain the resource vocabulary. `ComputableInLinearTimeAndSpace` specializes the existing plain asymptotic notion. Internal normalization constructs witnesses for those notions; it does not define a competing efficiency model.

**Framework friction.** Unresolved intermediate encodings made composition search expensive. Keeping both inference directions in the shared core removes the need for client-local composition rules; the original budget and generic/missing-evidence controls remain. Deferred proof views and field migrations are tracked in #608/#862, with Crypto follow-ups on #733.

**Validation and review.** Current source is `6ec5c21090adb92f8f79d7fceff274297ba1eee6`, a normal merge of preserved130e6ae3 with actual main197b4098. [Exact-head refresh evidence](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/671#issuecomment-6400942827) records all six local gates and the normal freshness-aware ratchet passing on this merge; hosted checks and outside current-head confirmation remain required. [Consolidated local evidence and freshness-aware ratchet](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6400726286) records exact revisions and reused checks. [Earlier outside core review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6399594564), [resolved facade/registration findings](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6400324902) and [lookup approval](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1039#issuecomment-6399407467) retain their stated coverage limits. Final exact-head delta review and hosted checks are required; no earlier verdict approves this whole head automatically.

**Abstracts and source moves.** Selected headline statements, models and bounds are unchanged. Encoding/frame data and machine helpers move to their shared homes with original reexports; declaration-link origins change, and the abstract-origin fixture follows `Encodings.Nat.Bits` without weakening its assertion. No new rendered-PDF claim.

Refs #608, #456, #862. AI-assisted work by Codex workers and coordinator, retaining #869, Claude's #1039 and the original machine authors' credit. The earlier transport prototype remains archived for comparison, not as this implementation's evidence.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
`f` is required to be computable without A, in both new WPP/LWPP oracle definitions. Conventional WPP^A/LWPP^A allows an FP^A target. The [authors’ FFK manuscript](https://lance.fortnow.com/papers/files/gaps.pdf), discussion following Definition5.13, explicitly distinguishes this issue and explains why eliminating the relativized gap does not eliminate the oracle from that target.

These Lean results can remain useful, but please distinguish the fixed-target classes in their names/API documentation, qualify every WPP/LWPP oracle identity (including the self-lowness and SPP-oracle claims), and remove the unqualified conventional identities from the PR description. ROADMAP must retain the target-relativized objective as remaining, rather than deleting it. Record #670 as a bounded milestone if that is the intended scope. Also verify the Lemma5.5/Theorem5.6 attributions against the cited edition; the author copies place this caveat after Definition5.13. A documentation/model-scope correction is sufficient; this review does not demand proving a broader theorem.

+# Oracle lowness of SPP, LWPP, and WPP
+
+This module formalizes the oracle lowness hierarchy for the gap-definable counting classes `SPP`,
+`LWPP`, and `WPP` from [Fenner, Fortnow and Kurtz, Section 5][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]:
+
+* **Relativized gap-definable classes (`SPPWithOracle`, `LWPPWithOracle`, `WPPWithOracle`,
+  `CeqPWithOracle`):** decision classes defined from `GapPWithOracle A enc` by the same exact
+  target conditions as their unrelativized counterparts (`SPP`, `LWPP`, `WPP`, `CeqP`).
+* **Exact integer-weighted oracle replay (`acceptWeight_exact`, `generalWeightedReplay`,
+  `GapP.generalWeightedReplay_mem`, `generalWeightedReplay_eq_exact`):** when the true-branch
+  weight at each step equals a per-instance denominator `D a` on true oracle answers and `0` on
+  false answers, the untaken branch at every step has weight `0`. Consequently, the replay tree
+  collapses to the single deterministic path following the oracle, contributing `(D a) ^ (T a)` on
+  accepting runs and `0` on rejecting runs.
+* **`SPP` is low for `GapP` (`GapPWithOracle_eq_GapP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  [Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz, Theorem 5.4][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]):** an `SPP` oracle has a `0`/`1`
+  characteristic `GapP` function (`D a = 1`), so `GapPWithOracle A enc = GapP enc`. Hence `SPP` is
+  low for `SPP`, `LWPP`, `WPP`, `C=P`, and `PP` (in particular `SPP^SPP = SPP`).
+* **`LWPP` scaling simulation and lowness (`exists_mul_mem_GapP_of_mem_LWPP`,
+  [Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz, Lemma 5.5 and Theorem 5.6][FennerFortnowKurtz1994]):** for an `LWPP`
+  oracle with length-dependent nonzero target `f : ℕ → ℤ`, multiplying the oracle's gap on query
+  `w` by the product of `f i` over all `i ≤ τ(|a|)` with `i ≠ |w|` normalizes every query of length
+  at most the clock `τ(|a|)` to the common length-dependent denominator
+  `D(|a|) = ∏_{i ≤ τ(|a|)} f(i)`. Summing over witnesses shows that every `h ∈ GapPWithOracle A enc`
+  can be scaled by a nonzero polynomial-time length-dependent factor `S(|a|)` into `GapP enc`.
+  Hence `LWPP` is low for `LWPP`, `WPP`, `C=P`, and `PP` (in particular `LWPP^LWPP = LWPP` and
+  `WPP^LWPP = WPP`).
+* **`WPP` is low for `PP` (`PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_WPP`):** follows from `WPP ⊆ AWPP`
+  (`WPP_subset_AWPP`) and `AWPP` lowness for `PP` (`PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_AWPP`).
+
+All results use the library's strict polynomial-time adaptive word-oracle verifier model; no
+nondeterministic oracle-machine counting characterization is claimed.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SPPWithOracle`: `0`/`1` characteristic gaps in `GapPWithOracle`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.LWPPWithOracle`: wide gaps in `GapPWithOracle` with a unary-length target.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.WPPWithOracle`: wide gaps in `GapPWithOracle` with an instance-dependent target.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.CeqPWithOracle`: zero sets of `GapPWithOracle` functions.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.generalWeightedReplay`: finite oracle replay with a general integer denominator.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SPP_subset_SPPWithOracle`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.LWPP_subset_LWPPWithOracle`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPP_subset_WPPWithOracle`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.CeqP_subset_CeqPWithOracle`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.SPPWithOracle_eq_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.LWPPWithOracle_eq_LWPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPPWithOracle_eq_WPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.CeqPWithOracle_eq_CeqP`: base inclusions and `P`-oracle eliminations.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.acceptWeight_exact`, `Cslib.Complexity.acceptWeight_exact_of_forall`:
+  exact algebraic collapse of `acceptWeight` when untaken branches have weight zero.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.GapP.generalWeightedReplay_mem`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.generalWeightedReplay_eq_exact`: `GapP` membership and exact evaluation of
+  `generalWeightedReplay`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.GapPWithOracle_eq_GapP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.SPPWithOracle_eq_SPP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.LWPPWithOracle_eq_LWPP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPPWithOracle_eq_WPP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.CeqPWithOracle_eq_CeqP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_SPP`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.exists_mul_mem_GapP_of_mem_LWPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.LWPPWithOracle_eq_LWPP_of_mem_LWPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPPWithOracle_eq_WPP_of_mem_LWPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.CeqPWithOracle_eq_CeqP_of_mem_LWPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_LWPP`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_WPP`.
+
+## References
+
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994],
+  Section 5 (Theorem 5.4, Lemma 5.5, Theorem 5.6).
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, L. Li, *An Oracle Builder's Toolkit*][FennerEtAl2003],
+  Section 6.
+* [S. Fenner, *PP-Lowness and a Simple Definition of AWPP*][Fenner2003].

+* `Cslib.Complexity.SPP_subset_SPPWithOracle`,

+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPP_subset_WPPWithOracle`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.CeqP_subset_CeqPWithOracle`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.SPPWithOracle_eq_SPP`,

+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPPWithOracle_eq_WPP`,

+* `Cslib.Complexity.GapP.generalWeightedReplay_mem`,

+  `generalWeightedReplay`.

+  `Cslib.Complexity.SPPWithOracle_eq_SPP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.LWPPWithOracle_eq_LWPP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPPWithOracle_eq_WPP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.CeqPWithOracle_eq_CeqP_of_mem_SPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_SPP`.

+  `Cslib.Complexity.WPPWithOracle_eq_WPP_of_mem_LWPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.CeqPWithOracle_eq_CeqP_of_mem_LWPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_LWPP`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PPWithOracle_eq_PP_of_mem_WPP`.

+## References
+
+* [S. Fenner, L. Fortnow, S. Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes*][FennerFortnowKurtz1994],

@@ -425,4 +477,160 @@ theorem binary_testBit {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {n i : α → ℕ}
   simp only [Function.comp_apply, Nat.testBit_eq_inth, ← List.getD_default_eq_getI]
   rfl
 
+/-- Any zero-preserving bitwise operation on binary naturals is polynomial-time. -/
+private theorem binary_bitwise (op : Bool → Bool → Bool) (h0 : op false false = false) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => Nat.bitwise op p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair encNat encNat) encNat := by
+  have hpairs : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime BinarySub.digitPairs (encPair encNat encNat)
+      (encList (encPair encBool encBool)) := by
+    unfold BinarySub.digitPairs
+    fun_prop
+  have hop : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun d : Bool × Bool => op d.1 d.2)
+      (encPair encBool encBool) encBool := of_finite _
+  have hstep : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun p : List Bool × (Bool × Bool) => p.1 ++ [op p.2.1 p.2.2])
+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBool encBool)) encBits :=
+    bitsAppend (fst _ _) (bitsCons (hop.comp (snd _ _)) (const []))
+  have hfold := foldl_of_bounded_growth (encA := encPair encBool encBool)
+    (encL := encList (encPair encBool encBool)) (encB := encBits)
+    (step := fun acc d => acc ++ [op d.1 d.2])
+    (init := fun _ => []) hpairs (const []) hstep (growth := 1) (fun _ _ => by simp)
+  convert bitsToNat.comp hfold using 1
+  funext p
+  exact BinarySub.bitwise_eq op h0 p
+
+/-- The smaller of a unary natural and a binary natural, returned in unary by saturating binary
+decoding. -/
+private theorem binary_min_unary : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => min p.1 p.2)
+    (encPair encUnary encNat) encUnary := by
+  have h := foldlWith (encA := encBool) (encL := encBits) (encP := encUnary)
+    (par := Prod.fst) (list := fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.2.bits.reverse)
+    (step := fun cap value bit => min cap (2 * value + bit.toNat))
+    (fst encUnary encNat) (bitsReverse.comp (natBits.comp (snd encUnary encNat)))
+    (const 0) (by fun_prop) (B := Prod.fst)
+    (by simpa only [encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate] using
+      (fst encUnary encNat).polyBounded_length)
+    (fun p i _ => by
+      simpa only [encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate, Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue] using
+        Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue_le p.1 (p.2.bits.reverse.take i))
+  convert h using 1
+  funext p
+  rw [← Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue, Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue_eq,
+    Cslib.BitString.binaryValue_reverse_bits]
+
+/-- Cap a computed binary natural by a computed unary bound, returning the result in unary. -/
+private theorem binary_min_unary' {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {left right : α → ℕ}
+    (hleft : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime left input encUnary)
+    (hright : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime right input encNat) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => min (left a) (right a)) input encUnary :=
+  binary_min_unary.comp (hleft.prod hright)
+
+/-- Right shift of binary naturals, by dropping at most the dividend's bit length of low-order
+digits. -/
+private theorem binary_shiftRight : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 >>> p.2)
+    (encPair encNat encNat) encNat := by
+  have hbits := natBits.comp (fst encNat encNat)
+  have hlen : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1.bits.length)
+      (encPair encNat encNat) encUnary := (length encBool).comp hbits
+  have hdrop := bitsDropWithInput hbits (binary_min_unary' hlen (snd encNat encNat))
+  convert bitsToNat.comp hdrop using 1
+  funext p
+  exact BinarySub.shiftRight_eq_ofBits_drop p
+
 end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime
+
+/-- Any zero-preserving bitwise operation on binary naturals is polynomial-time. -/
+theorem binary_bitwise (op : Bool → Bool → Bool) (h0 : op false false = false) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => Nat.bitwise op p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair encNat encNat) encNat :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_bitwise op h0)
+
+/-- Bitwise AND of binary naturals. -/
+@[fun_prop]

body:
Machines/WordRAM owner review (`coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`) at `462ab13fe2a2369b07121f3063a0728ef2a06eb0`: **changes requested on the new public tidy API**. This is a scope/API finding, not a counterexample to the native arithmetic or WordRAM semantics; mathematical review remains open.

The added `binary_bitwise`, bitwise/size/min/shift rules are public `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` certificates, with global `fun_prop`/`program_certificate` registrations. New WordRAM public certificate statements/premises also expose tidy. That contradicts [Samuel’s current direction](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/671#issuecomment-6377871078): new machine rules export ordinary plain statements only, with tidy used in proof implementation. Please expose canonical plain certificates and plain hypotheses, update the real clients/axiom guards, and keep any necessary tidy helper private/local rather than registering a parallel public tidy layer. No deprecated aliases.

Coordinate the new binary rules with #671’s source-based calculus so the new rules do not get omitted from its coverage checks. Keep the unary runtime width, binary values/addresses, exact-fault semantics and bounded left-shift construction. Existing raw `NativeCertificate` internals can be treated separately at the coordinated S2 boundary; do not expand this fix into a competing library-wide rewrite. Please post the revised exact head and validation. This is agent review; no approval or merge is given here.

body:
Closes #489 (and adopts the reviewed #728 driver repair for #608)

### Summary
Extends `@[program_certificate]` and `polytime` to support plain `ComputableInPolyTime` certificates alongside `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` certificates, adopting the reviewed #728 driver repair (`fc7eae88d9145a61d64a958a141bb12bd5354aae`, authored by `worker-codex-01a16ab8-608`) and adding the binary natural and Word RAM native `@[program_certificate]` registrations and tests.

Specifically:
1. **`Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean` & `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.lean` (adopted byte-for-byte from #728 `fc7eae88d9145a61d64a958a141bb12bd5354aae`)**:
   - Accept conclusions headed by either `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` (keyed by arg `#6`) or `ComputableInPolyTime` (keyed by arg `#4`) in `@[program_certificate]`, registering plain certificates with `fun_prop`.
   - Select the actual plain (`ComputableInPolyTime`) or tidy (`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`) predicate in `polytimeKnownCall`, `hasLocalCall`, `withoutLocalCall`, `withLocalCall`, `polytimeCertificate`, and `polytimeFunProp`.
   - Delay `PolyTime.to_plain` behind `polytimeRawBridge` after direct plain alternatives (`polytimeCertificate`, `polytimeFunProp`, `polytimeUnsafeFallback`) and apply `polytimeDriver` once in `polytime`.
2. **`Complexity/Computability/TuringMachine/MultiTape/PolyTime/Nat/Binary.lean` & `Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Native.lean`**:
   - Add `@[program_certificate]` to the plain binary natural and Word RAM native polynomial-time certificates (`polyTime_and`, `polyTime_or`, `polyTime_xor`, `polyTime_shiftRight`, `polyTime_size_unary`, `polyTime_min_unary_left`, `Basis.PolyTimeNative.checkedOp_polyTime`, `standard_checkedOp_polyTime`, `exact_checkedOp_polyTime`, `additive_checkedOp_polyTime`, `arithmetic_checkedOp_polyTime`, `checkedConstant_polyTime`, `evalTest_polyTime`, `address_polyTime`, `validMove_polyTime`, `validPC_polyTime`).
3. **`ComplexityTests/GenericRAMNative.lean` & `ComplexityTests/PolyTimePlainDriver.lean` & `ComplexityTests.lean`**:
   - Include `ComplexityTests/PolyTimePlainDriver.lean` from #728 (covering plain hypothesis discharge, plain certificate side-condition exposition, local `let rec` recursion, and plain non-tidy `List.foldl` inside a larger expression).
   - Exercise `by polytime` and `by fun_prop` on Word RAM native and binary natural plain `ComputableInPolyTime` goals in `ComplexityTests/GenericRAMNative.lean`.

### Categorization
Infrastructure and automation progress (no new headline mathematical theorems).

### Abstract Catalogue Assessment
Checked via `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` (`Catalogue selects 12 abstracts and 16 headline theorems`). No abstract definitions, statements, or bounds are affected.

- `./scripts/check.sh` (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`) — all passed
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp` — passed
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` — passed

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
This definition rejects every previously queried message, whereas [Boneh–Shoup v0.6, Attack Game6.1 / Definition6.2](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf#page=234) forbids only previously returned (message,tag) pairs. Those notions differ for randomized MACScheme signing. Please explicitly call this the fresh-message EUF-CMA variant and distinguish it from the book’s stronger fresh-pair notion in the module/game/security docs and PR description. The deterministic prfMAC construction has a unique valid tag and is unaffected.

Also correct the PRF-to-MAC references throughout source/PR/task text: the bound is [Theorem6.2](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf#page=240), and the construction is in Section6.3. Theorem6.1 concerns verification queries; “Construction6.1” is not this construction. These are scope/attribution corrections, not a request to broaden the implementation.
diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,963 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.PseudorandomFunction
+public import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.Signature
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.List
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Encodings.Length
+import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.Oracle.Composition
+import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.Oracle.Tidy
+import Complexity.Crypto.Negligible.Basic
+import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Oracle.Simulation
+import Complexity.Probability.PMF
+import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime
+import Complexity.Tactic.PPT
+
+/-!
+# Uniform message authentication codes and PRF-based MACs
+
+A uniform symmetric message authentication code (`MACScheme`) consists of a strict probabilistic
+polynomial-time key generator `keyGen`, a strict probabilistic polynomial-time tag generator `sign`,
+and a deterministic polynomial-time tag verifier `verify` that accepts every tag produced by `sign`
+on an `n`-bit message under a secret key sampled at security parameter `n`. Unlike digital
+signatures (`SignatureScheme`), verification uses the same secret key as tag generation, and the
+adversary receives no public key.
+
+We formalize existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (`eufCmaGame`,
+`EUFCMA`) and under one-time adaptive chosen-message attack (`eufOneTimeGame`, `OneTimeEUFCMA`)
+against uniform strict oracle-PPT forgers (`IsOraclePPT`), and prove that any uniform
+`PseudorandomFunction` yields an `EUFCMA`-secure deterministic MAC (`prfMAC`,
+`PseudorandomFunction.eufCma_prfMAC`), with the quantitative security reduction of
+[Boneh and Shoup, Theorem 6.1][BonehShoup2023]:
+$$\Pr[\text{Forge}] \le \mathrm{Adv}_{\mathrm{PRF}}(B(\mathcal{A}), n) + 2^{-n}.$$
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme`: uniform symmetric message authentication code on `n`-bit messages.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.signingOracle`, `eufCmaGame`, `EUFCMA`: full adaptive EUF-CMA experiment
+  and security predicate.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.oneTimeSigningOracle`, `eufOneTimeGame`, `OneTimeEUFCMA`: one-time
+  adaptive EUF-CMA experiment and security predicate.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.prfMAC`: canonical deterministic MAC constructed from a keyed function family.

+/-- A uniform symmetric message authentication code (MAC) on `n`-bit messages at security parameter

+  /-- Key generation is uniformly strict PPT in the unary security parameter. -/
+  keyGen_ppt : IsPPTOn encUnary encBits keyGen
+  /-- Tag generation is uniformly strict PPT in the encoded secret key and message. -/
+  sign_ppt : IsPPTOn (encPair encBits encBits) encBits (fun p => sign p.1 p.2)
+  /-- Verification is computable in plain polynomial time on `(sk, msg, tag)`. -/
+  verify_polyTime : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool => verify p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+    (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool
+  /-- Every tag produced by `sign` on an `n`-bit message under a supported secret key at security
+  parameter `n` is accepted by `verify`. -/

+    ∀ msg, msg.length = n →

+      (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool := by
+  simpa only [← computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime] using M.verify_polyTime

+    {list : γ → List (List Bool)} {elem : γ → List Bool}

+    (htag : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tag encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => M.verify (sk a) (msg a) (tag a)) encIn encBool :=

+      (fun pair : (ℕ × List Bool) × ((Unit × List Bool) × List (List Bool)) =>

+    unfold signingOracle
+    ppt

+    intro caller request queried _ result hresult
+    simp only [signingOracle, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure,

+    obtain ⟨tag, htag, rfl⟩ := hresult

+      (encPair (encPair encUnary encBits)
+        (encPair (encPair encBits encBits) (encList encBits))) encBool := by

+    (hadversary : IsOraclePPT (encPair encBits encBits) adversary) :
+    IsPPT encBool (fun n _ => M.eufCmaGame adversary n) :=
+  ((M.isPPTOn_eufCmaGame hadversary).preprocess (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst _ _)).isPPT
