+/-- Existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (EUF-CMA) for a symmetric MAC
+against uniform strict oracle-PPT adversaries [Boneh and Shoup, Definition 6.2][BonehShoup2023]. -/

title: feat(crypto): formalize uniform MAC schemes and PRF-to-MAC EUF-CMA reduction (#668)
body:
Closes #668 (part of #640 Track D item 2a).

## Summary

This PR formalizes uniform symmetric Message Authentication Codes (`MACScheme`) on `n`-bit messages at security parameter `n`, fresh-message existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (`EUFCMA`) and one-time adaptive chosen-message attack (`OneTimeEUFCMA`), the canonical PRF-based deterministic MAC construction (`prfMAC`), and the quantitative security reduction of Boneh and Shoup (*A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*, Section 6.3, Theorem 6.2).

### Mathematical Progress (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MAC.lean`)
* **`MACScheme` and Fresh-Message EUF-CMA / One-Time EUF-CMA Security**:
  * `MACScheme` bundles strict PPT `keyGen`, strict PPT `sign`, deterministic polynomial-time `verify` (`ComputableInPolyTime`), and perfect completeness on supported keys, `n`-bit messages, and tags.
  * `MACScheme.signingOracle`, `MACScheme.eufCmaGame`, `MACScheme.EUFCMA` (`isPPTOn_eufCmaGame`, `isPPT_eufCmaGame`). As in `SignatureScheme.eufCmaGame`, `eufCmaGame` enforces fresh-message unforgeability (`!queried.contains msg`), whereas Boneh–Shoup Attack Game 6.1 / Definition 6.2 forbids only previously returned `(message, tag)` pairs (fresh-pair / strong unforgeability). For general randomized `sign` algorithms the two notions differ; for deterministic canonical MACs with a unique valid tag per message (such as `prfMAC`), fresh-message and fresh-pair unforgeability coincide.
  * `MACScheme.oneTimeSigningOracle`, `MACScheme.eufOneTimeGame`, `MACScheme.OneTimeEUFCMA` (`isPPTOn_eufOneTimeGame`, `isPPT_eufOneTimeGame`).
  * `MACScheme.EUFCMA.oneTimeEUFCMA`: full EUF-CMA security implies one-time EUF-CMA security via `SignatureScheme.limitToOneQuery`.
* **Canonical PRF-based MAC (`prfMAC`) and Quantitative Forgery Reduction (Boneh–Shoup Section 6.3, Theorem 6.2)**:
  * `prfMAC family hpoly`: constructs a deterministic `MACScheme` from any polynomial-time keyed family `family`, sampling an `n`-bit key uniformly via `BitString.sampleList n`, tagging via `prfOracle family sk.length sk msg`, and verifying via `(msg.length == sk.length) && (family sk msg == tag)`.
  * `macLogHandler` and `macToPrfDistinguisher`: strict oracle-PPT reduction (`isOraclePPT_macToPrfDistinguisher`) that simulates the MAC tagging oracle using the external PRF/random-function oracle, logs queried messages, and uses one additional oracle query to test a candidate unqueried `n`-bit forgery.
  * `eval_prfRealGame_macToPrfDistinguisher`: exact distributional equivalence between `prfRealGame family (macToPrfDistinguisher adversary) n` and `(prfMAC family hpoly).eufCmaGame adversary n`.
  * `succProbability_prfIdealGame_macToPrfDistinguisher_le`: in the ideal random-function game, any unqueried `n`-bit forgery message misses the lazy random-oracle cache and draws a fresh uniform `n`-bit tag, succeeding with probability at most $1 / 2^n$.
  * `succProbability_eufCmaGame_prfMAC_le`: quantitative security bound
    $$\Pr[\text{Forge}] \le \mathrm{Adv}_{\mathrm{PRF}}(\text{macToPrfDistinguisher}(\mathcal{A}), n) + 2^{-n}.$$
  * `PseudorandomFunction.eufCma_prfMAC` and `PseudorandomFunction.oneTimeEUFCMA_prfMAC`: any uniform `PseudorandomFunction` yields an `EUFCMA`-secure (and `OneTimeEUFCMA`-secure) `MACScheme`.

### Tests and Nonvacuity (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/MAC.lean`)
* Concrete witnesses (`trivialMACScheme` and `echoPrfMAC`), evaluation tests for valid/invalid tags and one-time query slot consumption, nonvacuity refutation (`not_oneTimeEUFCMA_trivialMACScheme`, `not_eufCMA_trivialMACScheme`), and `#print axioms` guards for all 7 headline declarations.

### Formal Abstract Assessment
* No impact on existing selected headline abstracts in `abstracts/catalogue.json` (`python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes).

## Validation & Review
* Built and checked `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MAC` and `ComplexityTests.Crypto.MAC` (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, 6508 jobs), `lake exe mk_all --check`, `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`, and `python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`.
* Pre-PR independent review conducted by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-mac668` on `e874e9a2`; all 3 documentation/example items addressed in `b677a7db`.
* Addressed coordinator review (`pullrequestreview-5636168295`) in `d5776322` by explicitly documenting fresh-message vs. fresh-pair EUF-CMA for randomized MAC signing and updating the Boneh–Shoup PRF-to-MAC references to Section 6.3 and Theorem 6.2.

*AI disclosure: Authored by `worker-jetski-5950b838` (Gemini) with independent pre-PR review by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-mac668`.*

body:
`@[local fun_prop, program_certificate]` makes only the first attribute local. The `program_certificate` handler in `Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean` uses its global attribute kind for both `certificateExt.add` and `Attribute.add ... fun_prop`; `hasGlobalFunProp` deliberately ignores the local entry. Consequently these private tidy certificates still become global automation after importing the module.

Please make the program-certificate registrations local as well (or remove them from private helpers), preserving the public plain certificates. This occurs in both `CollisionResistant.lean` helpers and seven `MerkleDamgard.lean` helpers. Verify that ordinary importing clients retain the plain API without globally registering those private tidy rules. This applies Samuel’s plain-only global automation direction without changing the mathematical construction.

+module
+-- upstream: candidate

+public import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.CollisionResistant
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.BitString
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.List
+import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime
+import Complexity.Tactic.PPT
+
+/-!
+# The Merkle–Damgård transform
+
+Given a keyed `2n → n` collision-resistant compression family
+`h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, the Merkle–Damgård transform ([BonehShoup2023],
+Section 8.4, Construction 8.1 and Theorem 8.3) constructs a collision-resistant hash family on
+arbitrary-length messages by iterating `h k` over a sequence of `n`-bit blocks starting from a
+fixed `n`-bit initialization vector `0^n`.
+
+We formalize the transform and its collision-extraction reduction at two levels:
+
+1. **Block-chain level (`merkleDamgardChain`, `extractChainCollision`)**:
+   Iterating `h k` over a list of `n`-bit blocks produces an `n`-bit digest. Whenever two block
+   lists `bs₁` and `bs₂` of `n`-bit blocks produce the same final digest under `merkleDamgardChain`
+   and neither block list is a suffix of the other (`¬ (bs₁ <:+ bs₂) ∧ ¬ (bs₂ <:+ bs₁)`), scanning
+   the compression inputs backward from the final step (`extractChainCollision`) deterministically
+   finds a `2n`-bit collision `(x₁, x₂)` for `h k` in polynomial time. In particular, this covers
+   both cases of the classical length-strengthened Merkle–Damgård proof ([BonehShoup2023],
+   Theorem 8.3):
+   * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`: the final (length-encoding) blocks of
+     `bs₁` and `bs₂` differ;
+   * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: `bs₁` and `bs₂` have the same number of
+     blocks and `bs₁ ≠ bs₂`.
+   Consequently, any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding turns a `CompressionFamily` into a
+   collision-resistant hash family (`CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`).
+
+2. **Unrestricted bit-string level (`mdBlocks`, `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`)**:
+   Encoding an arbitrary bit string `msg : List Bool` as the initial marker block `0^n` followed by
+   one `n`-bit data block `1 ‖ b ‖ 0^{n-2}` per bit `b` of `msg` produces a suffix-free block
+   encoding of **all** bit strings for every `n ≥ 2`, with no upper bound on message length.
+   Iterating `h` over `mdBlocks k.length msg` yields
+   `merkleDamgard h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, which is collision-resistant on all
+   arbitrary-length bit strings (`CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+   `CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`).
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.padOrTake`: fixed-width bit-string normalization to exact length `n`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgardChain`: block-level iterated compression
+  `blocks.foldl (fun acc b => h k (acc ++ b)) iv`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.chainTraceStep`, `Cslib.Crypto.chainTrace`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.extractChainCollision`: polynomial-time backward scan extracting a `2n`-bit
+  compression collision from colliding block chains.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdEndBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdDataBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks`: suffix-free
+  `n`-bit block encoding of arbitrary bit strings.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgard`, `Cslib.Crypto.extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: domain-extended
+  keyed hash family and its deterministic collision extractor.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgardChain`, `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgard`: digest length
+  preservation.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_not_suffix`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: fundamental Merkle–Damgård chain
+  collision extraction lemmas.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`: collision resistance
+  for any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks_suffix_iff`: suffix-freeness of `mdBlocks n` for `n ≥ 2`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: deterministic collision extraction for
+  `merkleDamgard`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`: any `2n → n` collision-resistant
+  compression family yields an unrestricted collision-resistant hash family on `List Bool`.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023],
+  Section 8.4 (Construction 8.1 and Theorem 8.3).
+* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020], Section 5.2.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+/-! ### Fixed-width normalization -/
+
+/-- Normalize a bit string to exact length `n` by right-padding with `false` or truncating.
+On words already of length `n`, this is the identity. -/
+def padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (w ++ List.replicate n false).take n
+
+@[simp]
+theorem length_padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : (padOrTake n w).length = n := by
+  simp only [padOrTake, List.length_take, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]
+  omega
+
+@[simp]
+theorem padOrTake_eq_self {n : ℕ} {w : List Bool} (hw : w.length = n) :
+    padOrTake n w = w := by
+  subst hw
+  simp [padOrTake]
+

+
+2. **Unrestricted bit-string level (`mdBlocks`, `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`)**:
+   Encoding an arbitrary bit string `msg : List Bool` as the initial marker block `0^n` followed by
+   one `n`-bit data block `1 ‖ b ‖ 0^{n-2}` per bit `b` of `msg` produces a suffix-free block
+   encoding of **all** bit strings for every `n ≥ 2`, with no upper bound on message length.
+   Iterating `h` over `mdBlocks k.length msg` yields
+   `merkleDamgard h : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool`, which is collision-resistant on all
+   arbitrary-length bit strings (`CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+   `CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`).
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.padOrTake`: fixed-width bit-string normalization to exact length `n`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgardChain`: block-level iterated compression
+  `blocks.foldl (fun acc b => h k (acc ++ b)) iv`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.chainTraceStep`, `Cslib.Crypto.chainTrace`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.extractChainCollision`: polynomial-time backward scan extracting a `2n`-bit
+  compression collision from colliding block chains.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdEndBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdDataBlock`, `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks`: suffix-free
+  `n`-bit block encoding of arbitrary bit strings.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.merkleDamgard`, `Cslib.Crypto.extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: domain-extended
+  keyed hash family and its deterministic collision extractor.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgardChain`, `Cslib.Crypto.length_merkleDamgard`: digest length
+  preservation.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_not_suffix`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: fundamental Merkle–Damgård chain
+  collision extraction lemmas.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`: collision resistance
+  for any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.mdBlocks_suffix_iff`: suffix-freeness of `mdBlocks n` for `n ≥ 2`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.isCollision_extractMerkleDamgardCollision`: deterministic collision extraction for
+  `merkleDamgard`.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`: any `2n → n` collision-resistant
+  compression family yields an unrestricted collision-resistant hash family on `List Bool`.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*][BonehShoup2023],
+  Section 8.4 (Construction 8.1 and Theorem 8.3).
+* [J. Katz, Y. Lindell, *Introduction to Modern Cryptography*][KatzLindell2020], Section 5.2.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Crypto
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+/-! ### Fixed-width normalization -/
+
+/-- Normalize a bit string to exact length `n` by right-padding with `false` or truncating.
+On words already of length `n`, this is the identity. -/
+def padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (w ++ List.replicate n false).take n
+
+@[simp]
+theorem length_padOrTake (n : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : (padOrTake n w).length = n := by
+  simp only [padOrTake, List.length_take, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]
+  omega
+
+@[simp]
+theorem padOrTake_eq_self {n : ℕ} {w : List Bool} (hw : w.length = n) :
+    padOrTake n w = w := by
+  subst hw
+  simp [padOrTake]
+
+@[local fun_prop, program_certificate]

title: feat(Crypto): keyed collision-resistant hash families and the Merkle-Damgard transform
body:
Closes #669 (part of #640 Track D).

## Summary

This PR formalizes keyed collision-resistant hash families and compression functions (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CollisionResistant.lean`) and the Merkle–Damgård iterated-compression transform and deterministic collision-extraction reduction (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MerkleDamgard.lean`, Boneh–Shoup Section 8.4, Figure 8.5 and Theorem 8.3).

### Mathematical Progress

1. **Keyed Collision-Resistant Hash Families (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CollisionResistant.lean`)**:
   * `isCollision H valid n k m₁ m₂`, `collisionGame H valid adversary n` (`isPPTOn_collisionGame`, `isPPT_collisionGame`), and `CollisionResistantOn H valid` / `CollisionResistant H`.
   * `succProbability_collisionGame_le_of_extract`, `CollisionResistantOn.of_extract`, and `CollisionResistantOn.mono`: deterministic polynomial-time collision extraction transfers collision resistance between hash families.
   * `not_collisionResistantOn_of_le_succProbability`: general nonvacuity lemma showing that any strict PPT collision finder with success probability bounded away from zero refutes `CollisionResistantOn`.
   * `CompressionFamily` (`2n → n` collision-resistant compression families) and `HashFamily` (unrestricted collision-resistant hash families on arbitrary-length bit strings `List Bool`).

2. **The Merkle–Damgård Transform and Collision Reduction (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MerkleDamgard.lean`)**:
   * **Block-chain level**: `merkleDamgardChain`, `chainTraceStep`, `chainTrace`, and `extractChainCollision` (polynomial-time backward trace scan, `computableInPolyTime_extractChainCollision`), together with:
     * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_not_suffix`: fundamental suffix-free chain collision lemma;
     * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`: Boneh–Shoup Theorem 8.3 Case 1 (distinct final blocks);
     * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: Boneh–Shoup Theorem 8.3 Case 2 (equal block counts);
     * `CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`: any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding turns a `CompressionFamily` into a collision-resistant hash family.
   * **Unrestricted bit-string level**: `mdEndBlock`, `mdDataBlock`, `mdBlocks` (suffix-free `n`-bit block encoding of arbitrary bit strings for `n ≥ 2`, `mdBlocks_suffix_iff`), `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`, `isCollision_extractMerkleDamgardCollision`, and `CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard` / `CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`.

### Tests and Nonvacuity (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/MerkleDamgard.lean`)
* Concrete `2n → n` XOR compression function (`xorCompress`) and checked examples of `mdBlocks`, `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`, and both cases of `extractChainCollision` (Theorem 8.3 Cases 1 and 2).
* Client checks verifying that ordinary importing clients retain the public plain `ComputableInPolyTime` API without globally registering private tidy helpers.
* Nonvacuity refutation (`not_collisionResistant_constHash`) via an explicit zero-coin PPT collision finder.
* `#print axioms` guards for all 12 headline declarations.

### Formal Abstract Assessment
* No impact on existing selected headline abstracts in `abstracts/catalogue.json` (`python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes).

## Validation & Review
* Built and checked `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.CollisionResistant`, `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MerkleDamgard`, and `ComplexityTests.Crypto.MerkleDamgard` (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, 6496 jobs), `lake exe mk_all --check`, `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`, and `python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`.
* Pre-PR independent review conducted by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-md669` on `ec5de574`; all 3 items (module docstring coverage, `private` internal helpers / plain `@[program_certificate]` attributes, and Boneh–Shoup section locators) addressed in `483287ce`.
* Addressed coordinator review (`pullrequestreview-5636180774`) in `da71993b` by removing global `program_certificate` attributes from the private tidy helpers in `CollisionResistant.lean` and `MerkleDamgard.lean`, updating "Construction 8.1" citations to Section 8.4 / Figure 8.5 / Theorem 8.3, and adding plain-API client examples in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/MerkleDamgard.lean`.

*AI disclosure: Authored by `worker-jetski-5950b838` and subagent `1a2b8286-7df4-4f01-af32-7c3474556ff0` (Gemini), with independent pre-PR review by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-md669`.*

title: feat(counting): define MAJSAT and prove PP-completeness
body:
## Summary

Closes #48.

Defines `MAJSAT` (strict majority satisfiability over the occurring variables of a general CNF formula) and proves that it is `PP`-complete (`MAJSAT_ppComplete`) following Simon [Simon1975]:

- **`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Problems/SharpSAT.lean`**:
  - Defines `SharpSAT.firstPositions` (filtering the variable list to first occurrences via `List.idxOf`) and proves `length_firstPositions : (firstPositions φ).length = φ.vars.toFinset.card`.
  - Certifies `computableTidilyInPolyTime_firstPositions` and `computableTidilyInPolyTime_card_vars` (`@[fun_prop]`) so that `φ ↦ φ.vars.toFinset.card` is polynomial-time computable in unary.
- **`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Problems/CountingSAT.lean`**:
  - Defines `MAJSAT : Set (CNF ℕ) := {φ | 2 ^ φ.vars.toFinset.card < 2 * SharpSAT φ}`.
  - Proves `two_pow_card_vars_mem_SharpP` and `MAJSAT_mem_PP : MAJSAT ∈ PP encCNF` via `GapP.natCast_sub_natCast_mem`.
  - Defines the odd/even variable-shifting majority-padding transformation `shiftOdd` (relabeling variable `v` to `2 * v + 1`), `dummyClauses Q` (clauses `[(0, true), (2 * j + 2, false)]` for `j < Q` forcing the `Q` positive even dummy variables `2, 4, ..., 2 * Q` to `false` when the selector variable `0` is `false`), and `padMajority φ Q`.
  - Certifies `computableTidilyInPolyTime_padMajority` (`@[fun_prop]`) and proves:
    - `card_vars_padMajority : (padMajority φ Q).vars.toFinset.card = 1 + Q + φ.vars.toFinset.card`
    - `sharpSAT_padMajority : SharpSAT (padMajority φ Q) = SharpSAT φ + (2 ^ (Q + φ.vars.toFinset.card) - 2 ^ Q)`
    - `padMajority_mem_MAJSAT_iff : padMajority φ Q ∈ MAJSAT ↔ 2 ^ Q < SharpSAT φ`
  - Proves `MAJSAT_ppHard : PolyTimeHard PP encCNF MAJSAT` and `MAJSAT_ppComplete : PolyTimeComplete PP encCNF MAJSAT`.
- **`ComplexityTests/CountingCompleteness.lean`**:
  - Exercises `MAJSAT` on `[]`, `[[(0, true), (1, true)]]`, `[[(0, true)], [(0, false)]]`, genuine tie `[[(0, true)]]`, and `[[(0, true)], [(1, true)]]`, plus zero-boundary padding clients `padMajority [] 0` and `padMajority [[(0, true)]] 0`, `padMajority_mem_MAJSAT_iff`, and `#print axioms` guards for `MAJSAT_mem_PP`, `MAJSAT_ppHard`, and `MAJSAT_ppComplete`.
- **`references.bib`, `ROADMAP.md`, and `paper/sections/completeness.tex` (§1.2)**:
  - Adds `[Simon1975]`, updates `ROADMAP.md`, and updates §1.2 of `paper/sections/completeness.tex` with `\declat{3f273bbfa63b964c32474cd341e253ddcf466fb0}{...}` links and rebuilt `paper/main.pdf`.

## Validation

Ran `./scripts/check.sh` in `/tmp/complexitylib-agy-majsat`:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`

All 6 gates pass with zero warnings or errors.

## Independent Reviews & AI Disclosure

AI-assisted implementation (`worker-agy-majsat-20261020`, Claude Opus 4.6). Independent reviews conducted on Lean source commit `3f273bbfa63b964c32474cd341e253ddcf466fb0` and updated test suite:
- **cslib-style API review** (`14919544-d52b-40a4-aa1f-d7fa16f654b7`): Approved with no findings.
- **Mathematical correctness & test coverage review** (`0cdeb10e-3db3-44c3-81d1-6ef4f4507c85`): Approved with no findings.
- **Theorem-index review** (`bbf779fa-0ff8-44cc-9a13-d5cbbbf120ba`): Approved with no findings; verified all 12 `\declat{3f273bbfa63b964c32474cd341e253ddcf466fb0}` links and inspected rendered PDF page 2.

## Final current-pin integration

Final revision: `45fd65f150b9daaccc09c3b8dbea88ebbeac6aea`, incorporating independently reviewed PR66 `49b13382a079632ef215a4d23692c9cdd1170311` and its PR58/61 predecessors. Coordinator `fusion_quadratic` performed integration only in `.worktrees/ops-majsat-refresh` with OpenAI Codex; original author branch/worktree and Claude Opus 4.6 implementation credit are preserved. MAJSAT source and tests are byte-identical to author head `f8c10c46`.

All six combined gates pass on cslib `b5f3b77d9f045ed8f2dfec05505b159c2417e1c6` (`.worktrees/ops-coordinator-logs/majsat-final-check.log`); fresh MCP diagnostics for both source modules and tests are clean. Documentation configuration and whitespace checks pass. The roadmap preserves both MAJSAT completeness and the newer Boolean-hierarchy milestones. The combined PDF retains all 127 entries; the counting entry text is unchanged, all 12 updated source anchors were rechecked, and rendered pages 2/4 are clean with no undefined citations or overfull boxes.

Independent root coordinator approved the exact final integration/API preservation/index revision with no findings: https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/67#issuecomment-6299544649 . This shared-account review is distinct from GitHub platform approval. Final CI and merge remain coordinator actions; the theorem is general-CNF completeness, not restricted-width completeness.

body:
The sparse-synthesis parameter lemma ran nonlinear arithmetic over a large accumulated context. Restrict its searches to the facts each step uses and spell out one multiplication bound. This changes only the private `parameters_spec` proof body; its eleven-conjunct statement and every source byte outside that body are unchanged. Closes #679; the broader #622 performance work remains open.

Controlled whole-module Lean elaboration and checking against baseline `5897d88b97ef9578af1a7942795733f4a6aa0401`:

| Variant | CPU seconds | Wall seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 24.194, 23.314 | 24.742, 23.320 |
| After | 15.887, 15.820 | 15.900, 15.825 |

The mean CPU reduction is 33.3%. Runs used before/after/after/before order, the same core (23), one Lean thread (`-j1`), Lean v4.36.0-rc1, the same source filename and warm imported artifacts. Direct Lean runs wrote no build outputs; no profiler was enabled during timing. The host is shared, and this measures one module on one machine, not end-to-end CI wall time. The preliminary profiler attributed the dominant cost to `nlinarith`; heartbeat counts selected the proof rather than serving as the speedup measurement.

title: feat(crypto): commitment hiding against a randomized stateful receiver (#682)
body:
Closes #682 (Item 2 of #680).

### Summary

This PR formalizes commitment hiding against a two-stage randomized stateful PPT receiver in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Commitment.lean` ([Naor 1991; Goldreich 2001, Section 4.4.1]), following the `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.Adversary` pattern:

- **`CommitmentReceiver` and `CommitmentReceiver.IsPPT`:** Two-stage stateful receiver where `choose n aux` outputs `((r, (b₀, b₁)), state)` and `guess n state c` outputs a distinguishing bit, with uniform strict PPT admissibility charging the full encoded input (including `aux` in `choose` and `(state, c)` in `guess`).
- **`commitmentHidingGame` and `StatefulHiding`:** The two-stage commitment-hiding experiment and security definition against all strict PPT stateful receivers for every plain polynomial-time auxiliary input family `aux : ℕ → List Bool`, along with strict PPT certificates (`isPPTOn_commitmentHidingGame`, `isPPT_commitmentHidingGame`, `isPPTOn_commitmentHidingGame_aux`).
- **Deterministic-family bridge (`StatefulHiding.computational_hiding`):** Packages deterministic polynomial-time families `(r, b₀, b₁)` and a `Distinguisher` `D` into `CommitmentReceiver.ofDeterministic` and derives the existing deterministic-family hiding interface (`BitCommitmentScheme.computational_hiding`).
- **Naor stateful-receiver hiding reduction (`naorReceiverDistinguisher`, `advantage_commitmentHidingGame_naorCommit_le`, `PseudorandomGenerator.naorStatefulHiding`):** Commutes seed sampling with `receiver.choose`, shows that a uniform pad yields identical `false` and `true` experiments conditioned on every stage-1 output `(r, (b₀, b₁), state)`, bounds the stateful-receiver advantage by the sum of two PRG distinguishing advantages, and upgrades `BitCommitmentScheme` (`stateful_hiding : StatefulHiding commit`) and `PseudorandomGenerator.naorBitCommitment`.
- **Tests (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/Commitment.lean`):** Exercises a genuinely randomized stateful receiver (`statefulReceiver`) whose stage-1 challenge bits `(m, !m)` are marginally uniform without the saved state `[m]`, proves `not_statefulHiding_leakCommit`, checks public plain/PPT certificates, and adds `#print axioms` guards.

### Curated Abstracts Assessment

No curated formal abstract in `abstracts/catalogue.json` is affected (`python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes).

### Validation & Review

- `lake build Complexity.Crypto.Computational.Commitment ComplexityTests.Crypto.Commitment ComplexityTests.Crypto.ZeroKnowledge --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`
- `python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`
- `#lint in Cslib.Crypto` (0 errors in 62 declarations)
- Independent pre-PR review by `reviewer-jetski-commitment-682` at `8b76fcd2` (with `ROADMAP.md` nit addressed in `99eaf73a`): **Approved** (0 blocking findings).

*AI disclosure: Authored by `worker-jetski-5950b838` (Gemini) and independently reviewed by `reviewer-jetski-commitment-682` (Gemini).*

title: refactor(logics): move the QBF derived connectives into the QBF module
body:
Moves the derived connectives of quantified Boolean formulas from the classes area into the Logics module that defines `QBF`. This is item 4 of #596; #610 item 7 records this move as Logics work.

**What moves.** The connectives are `QBF.exs`, `alls`, `conj`, `imp`, `iff`, `lit`, `ofClause` and `ofCNF`, together with their evaluation and free-variable lemmas:
- `eval_exs_eq_true_iff`, `eval_alls_eq_true_iff`, `eval_conj`, `eval_ofCNF`, …;
- `freeVars_exs`, `freeVars_alls`, `mem_freeVars_ofCNF`, ….

title: refactor(problems): give the graph toolkit its own module
body:
Gives the graph toolkit its own module (#610 item 4, first step). Placement only: names, statements and proofs are unchanged, apart from one new lemma.

**Why.** The list-based `Graph`, its encoding `encGraph`, the simple-graph reading `Graph.toSimpleGraph`, the executable adjacency `Graph.adjBool` and the subset verifier `Graph.verifySubset`, with their certificates, lived in `Problems/IndependentSet.lean`. Meanwhile `Problems/Graph.lean` publicly imported `IndependentSet`. So every graph problem that imports `Graph.lean` (Coloring, Hamiltonian, GraphIsomorphism, VertexCover) also pulled in Karp's SAT-to-independent-set reduction and Cook–Levin.

**Change.**
- The toolkit moves into `Problems/Graph.lean`, which now imports only the verifier layer (`Classes/NP/Witness`) and Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Basic`.
- `IndependentSet` imports `Graph`, rather than the reverse.
- `VertexCover`, which uses `IndependentSet` for its reduction, imports it directly. `GraphIsomorphism` imports Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Maps` for `induce`, which it used to get transitively.
- `Graph.lean`'s module doc now describes the representation and the shared tools.
- New: `Graph.toSimpleGraph_adj : G.toSimpleGraph.Adj u v ↔ u ≠ v ∧ ((u, v) ∈ G.2 ∨ (v, u) ∈ G.2)`, for the clients that unfold `toSimpleGraph` and `SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj` (13 sites). It is deliberately **not** `simp`: as a `simp` lemma it changed normal forms and broke `Hamiltonian/Undirected`. The clients switch to it in a later step of item 4.

**Later steps of item 4:**
- stating independent set, clique and vertex cover through `Graph.induced`;
- using Mathlib's `indepNum`, `cliqueNum` and `vertexCoverNum`;
- the vertex-cover verifier via `subsetVerifier`;
- deleting the unused `selectVertices` family, whose test file is in other PRs.

**Overlap.** #685 (opened meanwhile) edits one line in `computableTidilyInPolyTime_verifySubset`, which this PR moves to `Graph.lean`, and an import plus one line in `VertexCover`. If #685 lands first, I'll rebase and carry its edit into the moved proof in `Graph.lean`, then ask for a delta review. If this PR lands first, #685 needs the same one-line edit in `Graph.lean` instead.

**Validation** at 619ca405, on `main`:
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates;
- `check_hygiene.py --check-simp`;
- `build_abstracts.py --check`.

**Abstract impact.** None. No abstract imports these modules, and names are unchanged.

title: feat(tree-eval): prove O(log n * log log n) input-size space bound for Cook-Mertz Tree Evaluation
body:
## Summary

Closes #62.

Proves the input-size `O(log n * log log n)` space bound corollary for the Cook–Mertz Tree Evaluation algorithm (`Cslib.TreeEval`) in `O(b(n) * b(b(n))) = O(log n * log log n)` space where `b(n) := (encNat n).length` and `n = (encNontrivialInstance I).length`:

- **`Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/Encoding.lean`**:
  - Proves lower bounds on `tableLength` and `bodyLength`: `two_pow_le_tableLength`, `two_pow_mul_le_bodyLength`, `tableLength_le_bodyLength_of_pos`, `two_pow_ell_le_bodyLength` (`2 ^ ℓ ≤ bodyLength ℓ H` when `1 ≤ ℓ` and `1 ≤ H`), and `two_pow_height_le_bodyLength` (`2 ^ H ≤ bodyLength ℓ H` when `1 ≤ ℓ`), plus `@[simp] theorem Tree.length_encode`.
- **`Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/Instance.lean`**:
  - Proves `length_encInstance`, `two_le_length_encInstance`, `ell_lt_length_encNat_length_encInstance` (`I.ell < (encNat (encInstance I).length).length` when `1 ≤ I.height`), and `height_lt_length_encNat_length_encInstance` (`I.height < (encNat (encInstance I).length).length` when `1 ≤ I.ell`).
- **`Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/Space.lean`**:
  - Defines `NontrivialInstance := {I : Instance // 1 ≤ I.ell ∧ 1 ≤ I.height}` and `encNontrivialInstance : NontrivialInstance ↪ List Bool`.
  - Proves `spaceBound_add_length_le_log_mul_log_log`: for `1 ≤ I.ell` and `1 ≤ I.height`, `spaceBound I.ell I.height + (encNat ((encInstance I).length + 1)).length ≤ 6 * ((encNat (encInstance I).length).length * (encNat (encNat (encInstance I).length).length).length)`.
  - Proves `computableTidilyInSpace_eval_log_mul_log_log`: the Cook–Mertz evaluator on `NontrivialInstance` runs tidily in space `O(b(n) * b(b(n))) = O(log n * log log n)` in the total encoded instance length `n = (encNontrivialInstance I).length`, where `b(m) := (encNat m).length`.
- **`ComplexityTests/TreeEval.lean`**:
  - Exercises `sampleNontrivial`, `ell_lt_length_encNat_length_encInstance`, `height_lt_length_encNat_length_encInstance`, `spaceBound_add_length_le_log_mul_log_log`, and `computableTidilyInSpace_eval_log_mul_log_log`, with `#print axioms` guards.
- **`ROADMAP.md` & `paper/sections/space.tex` (§3.12)**:
  - Updates the Tree Evaluation roadmap entry and theorem-index entry with `\declat{3a10a7a7c55bc0b5ec4588e369ab19daf66418f7}{...}` links and rebuilt `paper/main.pdf`.

## Source Credit

Preserves source credit for Christian Reitwiessner (`Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Reitwiessner, Samuel Schlesinger`, `Authors: Christian Reitwiessner, Samuel Schlesinger`) across the touched `TreeEval` modules and cites `[CookMertz2024]` and `[Goldreich2024TreeEval]`.

## Validation

Ran `./scripts/check.sh` in `/tmp/complexitylib-agy-treeeval`:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`

All 6 gates pass with zero warnings or errors.

## Independent Reviews & AI Disclosure

AI-assisted implementation (`worker-agy-treeeval-20261020`, Claude Opus 4.6). Independent reviews conducted on exact commit `3a10a7a7c55bc0b5ec4588e369ab19daf66418f7` (Lean) / `b110fbb558d07b1d5597a62b5828bbe568e8a998` (docs):
- **cslib-style API review** (`14919544-d52b-40a4-aa1f-d7fa16f654b7`): Approved with no findings.
- **Mathematical correctness review** (`0cdeb10e-3db3-44c3-81d1-6ef4f4507c85`): Approved with no findings.
- **Theorem-index review** (`bbf779fa-0ff8-44cc-9a13-d5cbbbf120ba`): Approved with no findings; verified all `\declat{3a10a7a7c55bc0b5ec4588e369ab19daf66418f7}` links and inspected rendered PDF page 16.

## Final current-pin integration

Final revision: `f5f986b4f5dd2bb4af2b1248d85dfddd23fa0b72`, incorporating approved MAJSAT PR67 `45fd65f150b9daaccc09c3b8dbea88ebbeac6aea` and its PR66/58/61 predecessors. Coordinator `fusion_quadratic` performed integration only in `.worktrees/ops-treeeval-refresh` with OpenAI Codex. The original author branch/worktree, Claude Opus 4.6 implementation credit, and Christian Reitwiessner's earlier formalization credit are preserved.

The author's new bounds and clients are unchanged. The only additional TreeEval source difference from author head `b110fbb5` is main's existing refactor of unary-block decoding to a shared list helper, with its public statement preserved. All six combined gates pass on cslib `b5f3b77d9f045ed8f2dfec05505b159c2417e1c6` (`.worktrees/ops-coordinator-logs/treeeval-final-check.log`). Fresh MCP diagnostics for Encoding, Instance, Space and the TreeEval tests are clean; documentation configuration and whitespace checks pass.

The combined PDF preserves all 127 entries. The TreeEval entry text and six new pinned source anchors are unchanged and rechecked; rendered pages 18 (TreeEval) and 2 (MAJSAT) are clean, with no undefined citations or overfull boxes in the final LaTeX log. The result retains positive value length and height, valid encoded instances, and no asserted asymptotic time bound. The sharp Cook–Mertz parameter bound, malformed-input recognition and Williams simulation remain open.

Independent root coordinator approved the exact final integration and index with no findings: https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/68#issuecomment-6299713367 . This shared-account review is distinct from GitHub platform approval. Final CI and merge remain coordinator actions.

title: doc(site): trim unimported core docs, disable equations, and fix broken links
body:
Closes #624 (Part 1: Option B + source docstring link fixes).

### Summary
1. **Disable equation/code-block sub-accordions in `doc-gen4` (`DISABLE_EQUATIONS=1` in `.github/workflows/docs.yml`):**
   - Avoids generating `equations` HTML lists for every definition while keeping every imported declaration's type signature, docstring, and source link intact.
2. **Trim unimported dependency HTML pages and search-index declaration bloat (`scripts/check_docs.py --trim`):**
   - Prunes generated HTML pages (and matching `nav.js` sidebar entries) for dependency modules outside the transitive import cone of `Complexity` (derived from `declaration-data.bmp`'s `modules` import graph), while preserving any core module pages linked from retained pages.
   - Filters `declarations/declaration-data.bmp` `declarations` and `find/header-data.bmp` down to local `Complexity.*` declarations while keeping retained dependency modules in `modules`, shrinking `declaration-data.bmp` from ~194 MB to ~7.7 MB (`7,744,484` bytes, `29,113` local declarations across `7,746` retained modules).
   - Enforces a hard `MAX_DOCS_BYTES = 950_000_000` (950 MB) size gate in `check_docs.py --trim` so the deployed artifact stays comfortably under GitHub Pages' 1 GB limit (measured output on current tree: **`859,168,765` bytes / ~859.2 MB**).
3. **Fix broken internal links at the source and enforce internal link integrity in `check_docs.py`:**
   - Adds `check_internal_links(docs)` to `scripts/check_docs.py` to verify that every relative internal link across all retained HTML pages resolves to an existing published file (properly rejecting external schemes, protocol-relative `//...` URLs, and any `..` traversal escaping the `doc` root).
   - Fixes all 342 `.lean` files whose docstrings had backticked file paths (`Foo/Bar.lean` without `.html`) that `doc-gen4`'s markdown renderer auto-linked as relative broken URLs:
     - Local `complexitylib` module paths are qualified with `Complexity/...` so `doc-gen4` rewrites `.lean` -> `.html` relative to the site root.

body: [P2] Preserve the generic promise-monotonicity rule. `PolyTimeReducible.of_subset` directly constructs a reduction between arbitrary promise problems from yes/no inclusions, just as the neighboring public refl/trans rules construct other basic reductions. Making it private removes the normal client `PolyTimeReducible.of_subset hyes hno` and forces repetition of the function/certificate/MapsTo tuple. This is an API-shaped closure rule under the PR's exception policy; keep it public.

 /-- A promise problem reduces, by the identity, to any problem with more yes-instances and more
 no-instances: enlarging the promise can only make a problem harder. -/

title: refactor(probability): split the PMF hub into topic modules
body:
This splits the `Probability/PMF.lean` hub by topic (#614 item A3, #569, #587). This is a refactor, not new mathematics. Statements, names, attributes and proofs are unchanged. Only the declarations' modules and the clients' imports change.

**What moves**
- `Probability/PMF.lean` now holds only the two vendored upstream blocks: the `do`-notation simp lemmas (cslib #1129) and the real-valued masses (cslib #1062). Their declarations and markers are unchanged. The module docstring now says what the file holds and points to the topic modules. Two block comments no longer refer to "the lemmas below".
- New `Probability/PMF/Event` covers event probabilities:
  - the `toOuterMeasure_*` lemmas and `filter_apply_toReal`;
  - the failure-composition and rate lemmas;
  - the Boolean `toReal_*` masses.
- New `Probability/PMF/Bind` covers two-stage experiments: `bind_congr_on_support`, `bind_apply_of_forall`, `le_bind_apply_on_support`, `bind_apply_mono_on_support`, `exists_bind_apply_le`, `tsum_mul_le_*` and `bind_sigma_apply`.
- New `Probability/PMF/Uniform` covers uniform distributions and resampling: `mem_support_uniformOfFintype`, `uniformOfFintype_*` and `toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFintype{,_toReal}`.
- `map_injective` moves into the existing `Probability/PMF/Map`. `PMF/Map` now imports `PMF/Bind`, because its `map_congr_on_support` proof uses `bind_congr_on_support`.

**Clients.** Every module that uses a moved lemma now imports the topic module that defines it. That is 95 files, each with one or two added `import` lines and no other edits:

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| `Crypto` | 36 |
| `Computability` | 24 |
| `Probability` | 17 |
| `Languages/Probabilistic` | 5 |
| `MachineLearning` | 3 |
| `ComplexityTests` | 10 |

By topic module, 43 files gained `PMF/Event`, 41 gained `PMF/Bind`, 16 gained `PMF/Uniform` and 2 gained `PMF/Map`.

A script generated the list on this PR's base. For each module, it adds a plain `import` when the module uses a moved name and cannot see its topic module through its direct imports or their public re-exports. The build confirms the list. `Complexity.lean` is regenerated by `mk_all`.

**Why.** On the base, `PMF.lean` had 55 direct and 474 transitive library importers. It is publicly re-exported, notably by `Languages/Probabilistic/Basic`, so 455 of those modules depend on its exported interface. Any edit to a candidate lemma that changed the hub's interface, such as adding a lemma or changing a statement, invalidated all 455. Such an edit now reaches only the importers of one topic module. Proof-only and docstring edits leave the exported interface unchanged, so they did not reach these importers before either.

The table counts library modules, using `scripts/quality_report.py`'s `transitive_importers` and `rebuild_fanout` (#604). These are static counts of import and public-re-export reach, not measured rebuilds:

| Module | Transitive importers, base → head | Interface-dependency fan-out, base → head |
|---|---|---|
| `Probability/PMF` (vendored blocks only) | 474 → 477 | 455 → 458 |
| `Probability/PMF/Event` (new) | — → 323 | — → **40** |
| `Probability/PMF/Bind` (new) | — → 420 | — → **39** |
| `Probability/PMF/Uniform` (new) | — → 107 | — → **12** |
| `Probability/PMF/Map` (now with `map_injective`) | 272 → 276 | 150 → 152 |

How the numbers were measured:
- The head numbers come from `quality_report.py --json` on the head build.
- The base numbers apply the same two functions to the base's import graph, parsed from source.
- That source parse reproduces the head's `.ilean` import graph exactly.
- Tests and abstracts are not counted.

**Declaration preservation**
- I checked by script that each of the old hub's 35 theorem blocks appears verbatim in the hub or a topic module, with its docstring, attributes, statement and proof, under the same `variable`/`omit` context.
- No name is defined twice.
- The only elaborated difference is an auto-generated universe name. `bind_sigma_apply`'s dependent family `β : α → Type*` is now `u_3` instead of `u_6`, because the module's `variable` line is shorter. Universe order is unchanged, and the change is invisible to clients.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body: [P2] Complete or explicitly delimit the canonical-encoding endpoint before closing #683. That issue requests `BH encBits (k+1) = BH encBits k` (or `coBH encBits k ⊆ BH encBits k`) as the collapse premise. Here, and in the full consecutive-level/DP wrappers, the premise instead quantifies over every type and every injective encoding. The fixed-level theorem additionally asks for the paired encoding; Tests/Kadin:61,66,71 repeat paired/universal assumptions rather than checking the canonical-only client. Existing Decoder and BH reduction-closure APIs transport canonical collapse to decodable encodings, including paired bit strings, but do not by themselves supply a Decoder or the required collapse premise for arbitrary encodings in this quantifier or PH/Collapse:212. Please provide a checked public corollary/client whose only collapse hypothesis is the encBits one (including general k), or make this an explicitly scoped milestone and retain #683's canonical endpoint as unfinished in the PR/ROADMAP instead of Closes #683. The universal-encoding theorem and single-DP-complete-problem corollaries remain valid useful results.

+/-

+module
+-- upstream: candidate

+public import Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.BooleanHierarchy.PH
+public import Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.PH.Collapse
+public import Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Problems.SATUNSAT
+import Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.NP.Witness
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.BitString
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.List
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Nat
+
+/-!
+# Kadin's Theorem
+
+If the Boolean hierarchy over `NP` collapses at any finite level `k` (`coBH k ⊆ BH k`, or
+equivalently `BH (k + 1) = BH k`), then the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its third level
+`Σ₃ᴾ ∩ Π₃ᴾ` (`PH = Σ₃ᴾ`) [Kadin][Kadin1988]. In particular, if `DP = coDP` (or `SATUNSAT ∈ coDP`),
+then `PH = Σ₃ᴾ`.
+
+## Proof overview
+
+To place a language `A ∈ Π₃ᴾ` in `Σ₃ᴾ`, peel off its first two quantifier blocks of lengths `p₁`
+and `p₂`; the negated inner quantifier defines a language `E ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)` such that
+`a ∈ A ↔ ∀ u₁ (|u₁| = p₁(n)), ∃ u₂ (|u₂| = p₂(n)), (a, u₁ ++ u₂) ∉ E`, where every queried word
+`u₁ ++ u₂` has fixed length `m(n) = (p₁ + p₂)(n)`.
+
+For each `r ≤ k`, an `r`-tuple of words of length `m(n)` is represented as a single concatenated
+bit string `s` of length `r * m(n)` paired with `a` under `encPair enc encBits`. The canonical
+alternating languages `kadinChain enc m E r ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) r` satisfy
+`(a, s ++ y) ∈ kadinChain enc m E (r + 1) ↔ (a, y) ∈ E ∧ (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r` whenever
+`|s| = r * m(n)`. Assuming `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k`, the
+complement `(kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ` lies in `BH (encPair enc encBits) k`. Stepping down the nested
+difference representation of `(kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ` from `r = k` to `r = 0` yields at each level
+either a hard prefix `s` of length `r * m(n)` that reduces `(a, y) ∉ E` on words of length `m(n)`
+to an existential check over `NP`, or completeness for the next level down. Taking the union of
+these `k` hard-prefix branches places `A` in `Σ₃ᴾ`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Complexity.kadinChain`: the canonical `BH r` language on concatenated `r`-tuples of fixed
+  polynomial word length.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.allWordsIn`: the `NP` language checking that `d` concatenated words of fixed
+  polynomial length all belong to a given language.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH`:
+  `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k → PiP 3 enc ⊆ SigmaP 3 enc`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.SigmaP_three_eq_PiP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH`:
+  `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k → SigmaP 3 enc = PiP 3 enc`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH`: Kadin's theorem for `coBH k ⊆ BH k`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_BH_succ_eq`: Kadin's theorem for `BH (k + 1) = BH k`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_DP_eq_coDP`: Kadin's theorem for `DP = coDP`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.DPComplete.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_mem_coDP` and
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_SATUNSAT_mem_coDP`: collapse from a single `DP`-complete
+  language in `coDP`.
+
+## References
+
+* [J. Kadin, *The Polynomial Time Hierarchy Collapses if the Boolean Hierarchy
+  Collapses*][Kadin1988]
+* [J.-Y. Cai et al., *The Boolean Hierarchy I: Structural Properties*][CaiEtAl1988]
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Complexity
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM ComputableTidilyInPolyTime Polynomial
+
+variable {α β : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-! ### Alternating verifiers on fixed-length bit-string slices -/
+
+/-- The encoded length of `(a, s)` under `encPair enc encBits` when `s` has length `q |enc a|`. -/
+private noncomputable def pairPoly (q : Polynomial ℕ) : Polynomial ℕ := 2 * X + 1 + q
+
+private theorem length_encPair_eq_eval_pairPoly {q : Polynomial ℕ} {a : α} {s : List Bool}
+    (hs : s.length = q.eval (enc a).length) :
+    (encPair enc encBits (a, s)).length = (pairPoly q).eval (enc a).length := by
+  simp [pairPoly, hs]
+
+/-- Shift the first `p |enc a|` certificate bits from the quantifier stream onto the accumulated
+bit-string prefix `s`. -/
+private def shiftVerifier (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool) (x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool) : Bool :=
+  let n := p.eval (enc x.1.1).length
+  V ((x.1.1, x.1.2 ++ x.2.take n), x.2.drop n)
+
+@[simp]
+private theorem shiftVerifier_append {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool}
+    {a : α} {s u v : List Bool} (hu : u.length = p.eval (enc a).length) :
+    shiftVerifier enc p V ((a, s), u ++ v) = V ((a, s ++ u), v) := by
+  simp [shiftVerifier, ← hu]
+
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_shiftVerifier (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    {V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (shiftVerifier enc p V)
+      (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encBool := by
+  have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool => p.eval (enc x.1.1).length)
+      (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encUnary :=
+    (unary_eval p).comp ((encoding_length enc).comp (fst _ _).fst')
+  exact hV.comp (((fst _ _).fst'.prod
+    (bitsAppend (fst _ _).snd' (bitsTakeWithInput (snd _ _) hn))).prod
+    (bitsDropWithInput (snd _ _) hn))
+
+private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_splitAlternatingBlocks' {γ : Type}
+    {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} (ps : List (Polynomial ℕ × Polynomial ℕ)) {N : γ → ℕ}
+    (hN : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime N encIn encUnary) {W : γ → List Bool}
+    (hW : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime W encIn encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun x => splitAlternatingBlocks (ps.map fun pq => (pq.1.eval (N x), pq.2.eval (N x)))
+        (W x)) encIn (encPair encBits encBits) := by
+  induction ps generalizing W with
+  | nil => exact .const ([], [])
+  | cons pq ps ih =>
+    have hp := (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval pq.1).comp hN
+    have hq := (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval pq.2).comp hN
+    have ht := ih (hW.bitsDropWithInput (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_add.comp
+      (hp.prod hq)))
+    exact ((hW.bitsTakeWithInput hp).bitsAppend ht.fst').prod
+      (((hW.bitsDropWithInput hp).bitsTakeWithInput hq).bitsAppend ht.snd')
+
+/-- `R : α → List Bool → Prop` is verified at `(b, k)` on prefixes `s` of length `q |enc a|` by a
+polynomial-time alternating verifier whose certificate block lengths are polynomials in
+`|enc a|`. -/
+private def OnSliceAlt (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (b : Bool) (k : ℕ) (q : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (R : α → List Bool → Prop) : Prop :=
+  ∃ (ps : List (Polynomial ℕ)) (V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool),
+    ps.length = k ∧
+    ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encBool ∧
+    ∀ a : α, ∀ s : List Bool, s.length = q.eval (enc a).length →
+      (R a s ↔ Alternation b (ps.map fun p => p.eval (enc a).length) fun v => V ((a, s), v) = true)
+
+namespace OnSliceAlt
+
+variable {b : Bool} {k : ℕ} {p q : Polynomial ℕ} {R R₁ R₂ : α → List Bool → Prop}
+
+private theorem congr (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₁)
+    (hR : ∀ a s, s.length = q.eval (enc a).length → (R₁ a s ↔ R₂ a s)) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂ := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, fun a s hs => (hR a s hs).symm.trans (hA a s hs)⟩
+
+private theorem congr_poly (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) {q' : Polynomial ℕ}
+    (hq : ∀ n, q.eval n = q'.eval n) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q' R := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, fun a s hs => hA a s (hs.trans (hq _).symm)⟩
+
+/-- At slice length `0`, an existential `OnSliceAlt` relation defines a `SigmaP k` language on
+`α`. -/
+private theorem mem_SigmaP (h : OnSliceAlt enc true k 0 R) : {a | R a []} ∈ SigmaP k enc := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine mem_SigmaP_iff_tidy.mpr ⟨ps, fun x => V ((x.1, []), x.2), hk, ?_, fun a => ?_⟩
+  · exact hV.tidy.comp (((fst enc encBits).prod (.const [])).prod (snd enc encBits))
+  · exact hR a [] (by simp)
+
+/-- Negating the verifier swaps quantifier polarities. -/
+private theorem not (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) : OnSliceAlt enc (!b) k q (fun a s => ¬R a s) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨ps, fun x => !V x, hk, by fun_prop, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  dsimp only
+  rw [hR a s hs, not_alternation]
+  exact alternation_congr fun v => by simp
+
+/-- Prepending a length-zero block flips the leading quantifier polarity and increments the
+level. -/
+private theorem zero_cons (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) : OnSliceAlt enc (!b) (k + 1) q R := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨0 :: ps, V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  rw [hR a s hs, List.map_cons, Polynomial.eval_zero, alternation_zero_cons, Bool.not_not]
+
+/-- Appending a length-zero block increments the level without changing the leading polarity. -/
+private theorem append_zero (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) : OnSliceAlt enc b (k + 1) q R := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨ps ++ [0], V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  rw [hR a s hs, List.map_append, List.map_singleton, Polynomial.eval_zero, alternation_append_zero]
+
+/-- Conjoining two `OnSliceAlt` relations at the same polarity and level. -/
+private theorem and (h₁ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₁) (h₂ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => R₁ a s ∧ R₂ a s) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hp, hV, hR₁⟩ := h₁
+  obtain ⟨qs, W, hq, hW, hR₂⟩ := h₂
+  have hlen : ps.length = qs.length := hp.trans hq.symm
+  let pqs := ps.zip qs
+  refine ⟨pqs.map fun pq => pq.1 + pq.2,
+    fun x =>
+      let w := splitAlternatingBlocks
+        (pqs.map fun pq => (pq.1.eval (enc x.1.1).length, pq.2.eval (enc x.1.1).length)) x.2
+      V (x.1, w.1) && W (x.1, w.2),
+    by simp [pqs, hp, hq], ?_, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  · have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+        (fun x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool => (enc x.1.1).length)
+        (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encUnary :=
+      (encoding_length enc).comp (fst _ _).fst'
+    have hs := computableTidilyInPolyTime_splitAlternatingBlocks' pqs hn (snd _ _)
+    exact .of_tidy <|
+      (hV.tidy.comp ((fst _ _).prod hs.fst')).bool_and'
+        (hW.tidy.comp ((fst _ _).prod hs.snd'))
+  · dsimp only
+    rw [hR₁ a s hs, hR₂ a s hs]
+    have hfst : pqs.map Prod.fst = ps := List.map_fst_zip hlen.le
+    have hsnd : pqs.map Prod.snd = qs := List.map_snd_zip hlen.ge
+    rw [← hfst, ← hsnd]
+    simp only [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, Polynomial.eval_add, Bool.and_eq_true]
+    simpa only [List.map_map, Function.comp_def] using (alternation_splitAlternatingBlocks
+      (pqs.map fun pq => (pq.1.eval (enc a).length, pq.2.eval (enc a).length)) b
+      (fun v => V ((a, s), v) = true) (fun v => W ((a, s), v) = true)).symm
+
+/-- Disjoining two `OnSliceAlt` relations at the same polarity and level. -/
+private theorem or (h₁ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₁) (h₂ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => R₁ a s ∨ R₂ a s) := by
+  have h : OnSliceAlt enc (!!b) k q (fun a s => ¬(¬R₁ a s ∧ ¬R₂ a s)) := (h₁.not.and h₂.not).not
+  rw [Bool.not_not] at h
+  exact h.congr fun a s _ => by tauto
+
+/-- Implication from a negated `OnSliceAlt` relation to a positive one at the same polarity. -/
+private theorem imp (h₁ : OnSliceAlt enc (!b) k q R₁) (h₂ : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R₂) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => R₁ a s → R₂ a s) := by
+  have h₁' : OnSliceAlt enc b k q (fun a s => ¬R₁ a s) := by
+    simpa using h₁.not
+  refine (h₁'.or h₂).congr fun a s _ => ?_
+  tauto
+
+/-- Embed a `SigmaP k (encPair enc encBits)` language at any slice polynomial `q`. -/
+private theorem of_mem_SigmaP {C : Set (α × List Bool)} (hC : C ∈ SigmaP k (encPair enc encBits))
+    (q : Polynomial ℕ) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc true k q (fun a s => (a, s) ∈ C) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := hC
+  refine ⟨ps.map fun p => p.comp (pairPoly q), V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  dsimp only
+  rw [hA (a, s), length_encPair_eq_eval_pairPoly hs]
+  simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, Polynomial.eval_comp]
+
+/-- Embed a `PiP k (encPair enc encBits)` language at any slice polynomial `q`. -/
+private theorem of_mem_PiP {C : Set (α × List Bool)} (hC : C ∈ PiP k (encPair enc encBits))
+    (q : Polynomial ℕ) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc false k q (fun a s => (a, s) ∈ C) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hA⟩ := hC
+  refine ⟨ps.map fun p => p.comp (pairPoly q), V, by simp [hk], hV, fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  dsimp only
+  rw [hA (a, s), length_encPair_eq_eval_pairPoly hs]
+  simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, Polynomial.eval_comp]
+
+/-- Drop the first `p |enc a|` bits of the slice prefix before evaluating `R`. -/
+private theorem drop (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc b k q R) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc b k (p + q) (fun a s => R a (s.drop (p.eval (enc a).length))) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨ps, fun x => V ((x.1.1, x.1.2.drop (p.eval (enc x.1.1).length)), x.2), hk, ?_,
+    fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  · have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+        (fun x : (α × List Bool) × List Bool => p.eval (enc x.1.1).length)
+        (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encUnary :=
+      (unary_eval p).comp ((encoding_length enc).comp (fst _ _).fst')
+    exact .of_tidy <| hV.tidy.comp (((fst _ _).fst'.prod
+      (bitsDropWithInput (fst _ _).snd' hn)).prod (snd _ _))
+  · refine hR a (s.drop (p.eval (enc a).length)) ?_
+    simp [hs]
+
+/-- Prepend an existential quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` to a universal relation. -/
+private theorem exists_append_flip (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc false k (q + p) R) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc true (k + 1) q
+      (fun a s => ∃ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ R a (s ++ u)) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p :: ps, shiftVerifier enc p V, by simp [hk],
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_shiftVerifier p hV.tidy), fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  simp only [List.map_cons, alternation_true_cons]
+  refine exists_congr fun u => and_congr_right fun hu => ?_
+  have hsu : (s ++ u).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by
+    simp [hs, hu]
+  rw [hR a (s ++ u) hsu]
+  exact alternation_congr fun v => by rw [shiftVerifier_append hu]
+
+/-- Prepend a universal quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` to an existential relation. -/
+private theorem forall_append_flip (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc true k (q + p) R) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc false (k + 1) q
+      (fun a s => ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length → R a (s ++ u)) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p :: ps, shiftVerifier enc p V, by simp [hk],
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_shiftVerifier p hV.tidy), fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  simp only [List.map_cons, alternation_false_cons]
+  refine forall_congr' fun u => imp_congr_right fun hu => ?_
+  have hsu : (s ++ u).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by
+    simp [hs, hu]
+  rw [hR a (s ++ u) hsu]
+  exact alternation_congr fun v => by rw [shiftVerifier_append hu]
+
+/-- Merge an existential quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` into the leading existential
+block. -/
+private theorem exists_append_same (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc true (k + 1) (q + p) R) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc true (k + 1) q
+      (fun a s => ∃ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ R a (s ++ u)) := by
+  obtain ⟨ps, V, hk, hV, hR⟩ := h
+  rcases ps with _ | ⟨p₁, ps⟩
+  · cases hk
+  refine ⟨(p + p₁) :: ps, shiftVerifier enc p V, by simpa using hk,
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_shiftVerifier p hV.tidy), fun a s hs => ?_⟩
+  simp only [List.map_cons, Polynomial.eval_add, alternation_true_cons]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨u, hu, hRu⟩
+    have hsu : (s ++ u).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by simp [hs, hu]
+    obtain ⟨w₁, hw₁, hA⟩ := (hR a (s ++ u) hsu).1 hRu
+    refine ⟨u ++ w₁, by simp [hu, hw₁], ?_⟩
+    refine hA.mono fun v hv => ?_
+    simpa only [List.append_assoc, shiftVerifier_append hu] using hv
+  · rintro ⟨w, hw, hA⟩
+    let n := p.eval (enc a).length
+    have hu : (w.take n).length = n := by simp [n, hw]
+    have hw₁ : (w.drop n).length = p₁.eval (enc a).length := by simp [n, hw]
+    have hsu : (s ++ w.take n).length = (q + p).eval (enc a).length := by simp [hs, hu, n]
+    refine ⟨w.take n, hu, (hR a (s ++ w.take n) hsu).2 ⟨w.drop n, hw₁, ?_⟩⟩
+    refine hA.mono fun v hv => ?_
+    have htake : (w.take n ++ (w.drop n ++ v)) = w ++ v := by
+      rw [← List.append_assoc, List.take_append_drop]
+    rw [← htake, shiftVerifier_append hu] at hv
+    exact hv
+
+/-- Merge a universal quantifier over words of length `p |enc a|` into the leading universal
+block. -/
+private theorem forall_append_same (p : Polynomial ℕ) (h : OnSliceAlt enc false (k + 1) (q + p) R) :
+    OnSliceAlt enc false (k + 1) q
+      (fun a s => ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length → R a (s ++ u)) := by
+  have hnot : OnSliceAlt enc (!!false) (k + 1) q
+      (fun a s => ¬∃ u : List Bool, u.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ ¬R a (s ++ u)) :=
+    (h.not.exists_append_same p).not
+  exact hnot.congr fun a s _ => by simp
+
+end OnSliceAlt
+
+/-! ### Kadin's alternating tuple chain and word-tuple predicates -/
+
+/-- The canonical `BH r` language on concatenated `r`-tuples of words of length `m |enc a|`:
+`(a, s ++ y)` belongs to `kadinChain enc m E (r + 1)` when `(a, y) ∈ E` and
+`(a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r`. -/
+def kadinChain (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+    ℕ → Set (α × List Bool)
+  | 0 => ∅
+  | r + 1 =>
+    {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} \
+      {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.take ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ kadinChain enc m E r}
+
+@[simp]
+theorem kadinChain_zero (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+    kadinChain enc m E 0 = ∅ := rfl
+
+theorem mem_kadinChain_succ_append {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)} {r : ℕ}
+    {a : α} {s y : List Bool} (hs : s.length = (r • m).eval (enc a).length) :
+    (a, s ++ y) ∈ kadinChain enc m E (r + 1) ↔
+      (a, y) ∈ E ∧ (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r := by
+  have hs' : s.length = r * m.eval (enc a).length := by simpa using hs
+  simp [kadinChain, ← hs']
+
+theorem kadinChain_mem_BH {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)}
+    (hE : E ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)) (r : ℕ) :
+    kadinChain enc m E r ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) r := by
+  induction r with
+  | zero => simp [kadinChain]
+  | succ r ih =>
+    have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+        (fun x : α × List Bool => (r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)
+        (encPair enc encBits) encUnary :=
+      (unary_eval (r • m)).comp ((encoding_length enc).comp (fst _ _))
+    have hdrop : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+        {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} E :=
+      ⟨fun x => (x.1, x.2.drop ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)),
+        .of_tidy ((fst _ _).prod (bitsDropWithInput (snd _ _) hn)), fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+    have htake : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+        {x : α × List Bool |
+          (x.1, x.2.take ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ kadinChain enc m E r}
+        (kadinChain enc m E r) :=
+      ⟨fun x => (x.1, x.2.take ((r • m).eval (enc x.1).length)),
+        .of_tidy ((fst _ _).prod (bitsTakeWithInput (snd _ _) hn)), fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨_, hdrop.mem_NP hE, _, htake.mem_BH ih, rfl⟩
+
+/-- The `NP` language checking that each of the first `d` consecutive blocks of length `m |enc a|`
+in `z` belongs to `E`. -/
+def allWordsIn (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+    ℕ → Set (α × List Bool)
+  | 0 => Set.univ
+  | d + 1 =>
+    {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.take (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} ∩
+      {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d}
+
+@[simp]
+theorem allWordsIn_zero (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool)) :
+    allWordsIn enc m E 0 = Set.univ := rfl
+
+theorem mem_allWordsIn_succ_append {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)} {d : ℕ}
+    {a : α} {y z : List Bool} (hy : y.length = m.eval (enc a).length) :
+    (a, y ++ z) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E (d + 1) ↔
+      (a, y) ∈ E ∧ (a, z) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d := by
+  simp [allWordsIn, ← hy]
+
+theorem allWordsIn_mem_NP {m : Polynomial ℕ} {E : Set (α × List Bool)}
+    (hE : E ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)) (d : ℕ) :
+    allWordsIn enc m E d ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits) := by
+  induction d with
+  | zero => exact ⟨0, fun _ => true, .const _, by simp [IsVerifier]⟩
+  | succ d ih =>
+    have hn : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+        (fun x : α × List Bool => m.eval (enc x.1).length)
+        (encPair enc encBits) encUnary :=
+      (unary_eval m).comp ((encoding_length enc).comp (fst _ _))
+    have htake : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+        {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.take (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ E} E :=
+      ⟨fun x => (x.1, x.2.take (m.eval (enc x.1).length)),
+        .of_tidy ((fst _ _).prod (bitsTakeWithInput (snd _ _) hn)), fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+    have hdrop : PolyTimeReducible (encPair enc encBits) (encPair enc encBits)
+        {x : α × List Bool | (x.1, x.2.drop (m.eval (enc x.1).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d}
+        (allWordsIn enc m E d) :=
+      ⟨fun x => (x.1, x.2.drop (m.eval (enc x.1).length)),
+        .of_tidy ((fst _ _).prod (bitsDropWithInput (snd _ _) hn)), fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+    exact inter_mem_NP (htake.mem_NP hE) (hdrop.mem_NP ih)
+
+/-- Unpack a `BH (r + 1)` language `D ⊆ U` (where `U ∈ NP`) into `D = B \ D₁` with
+`D₁ ⊆ B ⊆ U`, so that `D₁ = B \ D ⊆ U \ D`. -/
+private theorem mem_BH_succ_subset {γ : Type} {encγ : γ ↪ List Bool} {r : ℕ}
+    {U D : Set γ} (hU : U ∈ NP encγ) (hD : D ∈ BH encγ (r + 1)) (hDU : D ⊆ U) :
+    ∃ B ∈ NP encγ, ∃ D₁ ∈ BH encγ r,
+      B ⊆ U ∧ D₁ ⊆ B ∧ D = B \ D₁ ∧ D₁ ⊆ U \ D := by
+  obtain ⟨B', hB', D', hD', rfl⟩ := hD
+  refine ⟨B' ∩ U, inter_mem_NP hB' hU, D' ∩ (B' ∩ U),
+    inter_mem_BH_of_mem_NP hD' (inter_mem_NP hB' hU),
+    Set.inter_subset_right, Set.inter_subset_right, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · ext x
+    have hxU : x ∈ B' \ D' → x ∈ U := fun h => hDU h
+    simp only [Set.mem_sdiff, Set.mem_inter_iff] at hxU ⊢
+    tauto
+  · intro x hx
+    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_sdiff] at hx ⊢
+    tauto
+
+/-! ### Hard-prefix branch at level `r` -/
+
+/-- A prefix `s` of `r` words of length `m |enc a|` is `r`-hard for `D₁` on instance `a` if
+`(a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r` and no extension by `y` (of length `m |enc a|`) and `z` (of `d`
+words in `E` of length `m |enc a|`) places `(a, s ++ y ++ z)` in `D₁`. -/
+private def kadinIsHard (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool))
+    (r d : ℕ) (D₁ : Set (α × List Bool)) (a : α) (s : List Bool) : Prop :=
+  (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r ∧
+    ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = ((1 + d) • m).eval (enc a).length →
+      (a, w.drop (m.eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d →
+      (a, s ++ w) ∉ D₁
+
+/-- Given a hard prefix `s`, the main `Π₂` check for `a ∈ A`: for every `u₁` of length `p₁ |enc a|`,
+there exist `u₂` of length `p₂ |enc a|` and `z` of `d` words in `E` (packed as `w = u₂ ++ z` of
+length `(p₂ + d • m) |enc a|`) such that `(a, s ++ u₁ ++ w) ∈ B`. -/
+private def kadinMain (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p₁ p₂ m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool))
+    (d : ℕ) (B : Set (α × List Bool)) (a : α) (s : List Bool) : Prop :=
+  ∀ u₁ : List Bool, u₁.length = p₁.eval (enc a).length →
+    ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = (p₂ + d • m).eval (enc a).length ∧
+      (a, w.drop (p₂.eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d ∧
+      (a, s ++ u₁ ++ w) ∈ B
+
+/-- The level-`r` hard-prefix branch of Kadin's `Σ₃ᴾ` simulation. -/
+private def kadinHardBranch (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p₁ p₂ m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool))
+    (r d : ℕ) (D₁ B : Set (α × List Bool)) : Set α :=
+  {a | ∃ s : List Bool, s.length = (r • m).eval (enc a).length ∧
+    kadinIsHard enc m E r d D₁ a s ∧
+    kadinMain enc p₁ p₂ m E d B a s}
+
+private theorem kadinHardBranch_mem_SigmaP_three {p₁ p₂ m : Polynomial ℕ}
+    {E : Set (α × List Bool)} (hE : E ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)) (r d : ℕ)
+    {D₁ B : Set (α × List Bool)} (hD₁ : D₁ ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) r)
+    (hB : B ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)) :
+    kadinHardBranch enc p₁ p₂ m E r d D₁ B ∈ SigmaP 3 enc := by
+  have hLr_compl : (kadinChain enc m E r)ᶜ ∈ PiP 2 (encPair enc encBits) :=
+    (BooleanHierarchy_subset_SigmaP_two_inter_PiP_two
+      (compl_mem_BooleanHierarchy
+        (BH_subset_BooleanHierarchy r (kadinChain_mem_BH hE r)))).2
+  have hD₁_compl : D₁ᶜ ∈ PiP 2 (encPair enc encBits) :=
+    (BooleanHierarchy_subset_SigmaP_two_inter_PiP_two
+      (compl_mem_BooleanHierarchy (BH_subset_BooleanHierarchy r hD₁))).2
+  have hAll : allWordsIn enc m E d ∈ SigmaP 1 (encPair enc encBits) :=
+    SigmaP_one (enc := encPair enc encBits) ▸ allWordsIn_mem_NP hE d
+  have hB' : B ∈ SigmaP 1 (encPair enc encBits) :=
+    SigmaP_one (enc := encPair enc encBits) ▸ hB
+  -- `kadinIsHard` is `OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m)`
+  have hHard1 : OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m) (fun a s => (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r) :=
+    OnSliceAlt.of_mem_PiP hLr_compl (r • m)
+  have hAll_drop1 : OnSliceAlt enc true 2 ((r • m + m) + d • m)
+      (fun a sw => (a, sw.drop ((r • m + m).eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d) :=
+    ((OnSliceAlt.of_mem_SigmaP hAll (d • m)).append_zero).drop (r • m + m)
+  have hAll_drop1' : OnSliceAlt enc (!false) 2 (r • m + (1 + d) • m)
+      (fun a sw => (a, sw.drop ((r • m + m).eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d) :=
+    hAll_drop1.congr_poly fun n => by simp [add_smul, one_smul, add_assoc]
+  have hD₁_slice : OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m + (1 + d) • m) (fun a sw => (a, sw) ∉ D₁) :=
+    OnSliceAlt.of_mem_PiP hD₁_compl (r • m + (1 + d) • m)
+  have hHard2_body : OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m + (1 + d) • m)
+      (fun a sw =>
+        (a, sw.drop ((r • m + m).eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d →
+          (a, sw) ∉ D₁) :=
+    hAll_drop1'.imp hD₁_slice
+  have hHard2 : OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m)
+      (fun a s => ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = ((1 + d) • m).eval (enc a).length →
+        (a, w.drop (m.eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d →
+        (a, s ++ w) ∉ D₁) := by
+    refine (hHard2_body.forall_append_same ((1 + d) • m)).congr fun a s hs => ?_
+    refine forall_congr' fun w => imp_congr_right fun _ => ?_
+    have hlen : (r • m + m).eval (enc a).length = s.length + m.eval (enc a).length := by
+      rw [Polynomial.eval_add, hs]
+    have hdrop : (s ++ w).drop ((r • m + m).eval (enc a).length) =
+        w.drop (m.eval (enc a).length) := by
+      rw [hlen, ← List.drop_drop, List.drop_left]
+    rw [hdrop]
+  have hIsHard : OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m) (kadinIsHard enc m E r d D₁) :=
+    hHard1.and hHard2
+  -- `kadinMain` is `OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m)`
+  have hAll_drop2 : OnSliceAlt enc true 1 ((r • m + p₁ + p₂) + d • m)
+      (fun a suw =>
+        (a, suw.drop ((r • m + p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d) :=
+    (OnSliceAlt.of_mem_SigmaP hAll (d • m)).drop (r • m + p₁ + p₂)
+  have hAll_drop2' : OnSliceAlt enc true 1 ((r • m + p₁) + (p₂ + d • m))
+      (fun a suw =>
+        (a, suw.drop ((r • m + p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d) :=
+    hAll_drop2.congr_poly fun n => by simp [add_assoc]
+  have hB_slice : OnSliceAlt enc true 1 ((r • m + p₁) + (p₂ + d • m))
+      (fun a suw => (a, suw) ∈ B) :=
+    OnSliceAlt.of_mem_SigmaP hB' ((r • m + p₁) + (p₂ + d • m))
+  have hMain_exists : OnSliceAlt enc true 1 (r • m + p₁)
+      (fun a su₁ => ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = (p₂ + d • m).eval (enc a).length ∧
+        (a, (su₁ ++ w).drop ((r • m + p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length)) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d ∧
+        (a, su₁ ++ w) ∈ B) :=
+    (hAll_drop2'.and hB_slice).exists_append_same (p₂ + d • m)
+  have hMain : OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (r • m) (kadinMain enc p₁ p₂ m E d B) := by
+    refine (hMain_exists.forall_append_flip p₁).congr fun a s hs => ?_
+    refine forall_congr' fun u₁ => imp_congr_right fun hu₁ => ?_
+    refine exists_congr fun w => and_congr_right fun _ => ?_
+    have hsu₁ : (r • m + p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length =
+        (s ++ u₁).length + p₂.eval (enc a).length := by
+      simp [hs, hu₁]
+    have hdrop : (s ++ u₁ ++ w).drop ((r • m + p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length) =
+        w.drop (p₂.eval (enc a).length) := by
+      rw [hsu₁, ← List.drop_drop, List.drop_left]
+    rw [hdrop]
+  -- Combine `kadinIsHard` and `kadinMain`, then existentially quantify over `s`
+  have hBoth : OnSliceAlt enc false 2 (0 + r • m)
+      (fun a s => kadinIsHard enc m E r d D₁ a s ∧ kadinMain enc p₁ p₂ m E d B a s) :=
+    (hIsHard.and hMain).congr_poly fun n => by simp
+  have hBranch : OnSliceAlt enc true 3 0
+      (fun a s => ∃ u : List Bool, u.length = (r • m).eval (enc a).length ∧
+        kadinIsHard enc m E r d D₁ a (s ++ u) ∧ kadinMain enc p₁ p₂ m E d B a (s ++ u)) :=
+    hBoth.exists_append_flip (r • m)
+  exact hBranch.mem_SigmaP
+

+variable (enc) (p₁ p₂ m : Polynomial ℕ) (E : Set (α × List Bool))

+private def kadinTarget : Set α :=
+  {a | ∀ u₁ : List Bool, u₁.length = p₁.eval (enc a).length →
+    ∃ u₂ : List Bool, u₂.length = p₂.eval (enc a).length ∧ (a, u₁ ++ u₂) ∉ E}

+private def kadinSoundD (r d : ℕ) (D : Set (α × List Bool)) : Prop :=
+  ∀ a : α, ∀ s z : List Bool,
+    s.length = (r • m).eval (enc a).length →
+    z.length = (d • m).eval (enc a).length →
+    (a, z) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d →
+    (a, s ++ z) ∈ D →
+    (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r
+
+private def kadinSoundDiff (r d : ℕ) (U D : Set (α × List Bool)) : Prop :=
+  ∀ a : α, ∀ s z : List Bool,
+    s.length = (r • m).eval (enc a).length →
+    z.length = (d • m).eval (enc a).length →
+    (a, z) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d →
+    (a, s ++ z) ∈ U \ D →
+    (a, s) ∈ kadinChain enc m E r
+
+private def kadinComp (r d : ℕ) (D : Set (α × List Bool)) (a : α) : Prop :=
+  ∀ s : List Bool,
+    s.length = (r • m).eval (enc a).length →
+    (a, s) ∉ kadinChain enc m E r →
+    ∃ z : List Bool,
+      z.length = (d • m).eval (enc a).length ∧
+      (a, z) ∈ allWordsIn enc m E d ∧
+      (a, s ++ z) ∈ D

+      kadinSoundDiff enc m E r d U D →

+        exact hD₁UD hmem

+          not_not] at hnotHard
+        obtain ⟨w, hw, hwE, hmemD₁⟩ := hnotHard
+        have hw' : w.length = m.eval (enc a).length + (d • m).eval (enc a).length := by
+          simpa [add_smul, one_smul] using hw
+        let y := w.take (m.eval (enc a).length)
+        let z := w.drop (m.eval (enc a).length)
+        have hy : y.length = m.eval (enc a).length := by simp [y, hw']
+        have hz : z.length = (d • m).eval (enc a).length := by simp [z, hw']
+        have hsplit : y ++ z = w := List.take_append_drop _ _
+        rw [← hsplit] at hmemD₁
+        have hyE : (a, y) ∈ E := (hStrongD₁ a s y z hs hy hz hwE hmemD₁).1
+        refine ⟨w, by simpa [add_smul, one_smul, Nat.add_comm] using hw, ?_, by rwa [← hsplit]⟩
+        rw [← hsplit, mem_allWordsIn_succ_append hy]
+        exact ⟨hyE, hwE⟩
+
+end KadinInduction
+
+/-! ### Kadin's collapse theorems -/
+
+/-- **Kadin's theorem at level `3`** [Kadin][Kadin1988]: if `coBH k ⊆ BH k` holds for the pair
+encoding `encPair enc encBits`, then `PiP 3 enc ⊆ SigmaP 3 enc`. -/
+theorem PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH {k : ℕ}
+    (h : coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k) :
+    PiP 3 enc ⊆ SigmaP 3 enc := by
+  rintro A ⟨ps, V, hps, hV, hAV⟩
+  rcases ps with _ | ⟨p₁, _ | ⟨p₂, _ | ⟨p₃, _ | _⟩⟩⟩ <;> try cases hps
+  let E : Set (α × List Bool) :=
+    {y | ∃ u₃ : List Bool, u₃.length = p₃.eval (enc y.1).length ∧ (!V (y.1, y.2 ++ u₃)) = true}
+  have hE : E ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits) :=
+    mem_NP_setOf_exists_append (V := fun x => !V x)
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bool_not.comp hV.tidy) p₃
+  let m := p₁ + p₂
+  have hLk_compl : (kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) k :=
+    h (compl_mem_coBH_iff.mpr (kadinChain_mem_BH hE k))
+  have hU : (Set.univ : Set (α × List Bool)) ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits) :=
+    ⟨0, fun _ => true, .const _, by simp [IsVerifier]⟩
+  have hSoundD : kadinSoundD enc m E k 0 (kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ := by
+    intro a s z hs hz _ hmem
+    have hz0 : z = [] := List.length_eq_zero_iff.1 (by simpa using hz)
+    subst hz0
+    simpa using hmem
+  have hSoundDiff : kadinSoundDiff enc m E k 0 Set.univ (kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ := by
+    intro a s z hs hz _ hmem
+    have hz0 : z = [] := List.length_eq_zero_iff.1 (by simpa using hz)
+    subst hz0
+    simpa using hmem
+  obtain ⟨H, hH_mem, hH_sub, hH_comp⟩ :=
+    exists_kadin_sigmaP_three enc p₁ p₂ m E rfl hE k 0 hU hLk_compl (Set.subset_univ _)
+      hSoundD hSoundDiff
+  have hA_eq : A = kadinTarget enc p₁ p₂ E := by
+    ext a
+    rw [hAV a]
+    simp only [kadinTarget, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, List.map_cons, List.map_nil,
+      alternation_false_cons, alternation_true_cons, alternation_nil]
+    refine forall_congr' fun u₁ => imp_congr_right fun _ => ?_
+    refine exists_congr fun u₂ => and_congr_right fun _ => ?_
+    simp [E, List.append_assoc]
+  have hH_eq : A = H := by
+    rw [hA_eq]
+    refine Set.Subset.antisymm (fun a ha => hH_comp a ha fun s _ hs => ?_) hH_sub
+    exact ⟨[], by simp, trivial, by simpa using hs⟩
+  rwa [hH_eq]
+
+/-- **Kadin's theorem at level `3`** [Kadin][Kadin1988]: if `coBH k ⊆ BH k` holds for the pair
+encoding `encPair enc encBits`, then `SigmaP 3 enc = PiP 3 enc`. -/
+theorem SigmaP_three_eq_PiP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH {k : ℕ}
+    (h : coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k) :
+    SigmaP 3 enc = PiP 3 enc := by
+  have hsub := PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH h
+  refine Set.Subset.antisymm (fun A hA => ?_) hsub
+  simpa using compl_mem_PiP_of_mem_SigmaP (hsub (compl_mem_PiP_of_mem_SigmaP hA))
+
+/-- **Kadin's theorem** [Kadin][Kadin1988]: if `coBH k ⊆ BH k` for all encodings, the polynomial
+hierarchy collapses to `Σ₃ᴾ`. -/
+theorem PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH {k : ℕ}
+    (h : ∀ {β : Type} (enc' : β ↪ List Bool), coBH enc' k ⊆ BH enc' k) :
