author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent correctness/model/index review of exact `47ccf008f813eb5f7baaa3d21bc1afe6a7723a4d`, reviewer `fusion_barrier` (not an author). **Changes requested for contract/documentation precision.** These supplement the separate API/source-credit review; they do not request a different machine definition.

1. **[must-fix] Describe the generic time classes as their actual all-fitting-width contracts.** `Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Time.lean:17` and `:46` describe logarithmic-width operation, but `LinearTime`/`PolynomialTime` at `:172`/`:178` choose a logarithmic **lower threshold** and require success at every larger width **conditional on `InputFits`**. They do not ensure that the input fits at any `O(log(size a))` width. For example, the allowed encoding `encode n = [2^(n+1)]`, with `size n = n`, requires at least `n+2` bits regardless of the chosen logarithmic lower threshold. Keep the useful general contracts, but state this distinction explicitly, including the extra input-word/encoding-size assumptions needed for a logarithmic-width specialization or a TM comparison. Likewise replace `Defs.lean:21`'s unqualified “bounded, so unit cost is sound” with the precise instruction-count convention; neither a bit-cost equivalence nor a simulation is proved here. This is **not** a vacuity finding about element distinctness: its proof derives the required word bounds directly and works at the advertised logarithmic threshold.
2. **[must-fix] Do not list the unrestricted converse of `DecidesInTime.at` as merely open.** `ROADMAP.md:501` (and the PR's follow-up list) must qualify this proposed theorem. The literal `DecidesInTimeAt` at `Time.lean:118` permits a counterexample: both Boolean instances encode the empty list; choose width `1` for false and `2` for true. The four instructions `width r0; const r1 1; sub r0 r0 r1; halt r0` return the Boolean predicate, and both inputs fit. But any uniform decider must handle the two instances at the same width `max (bits false) (bits true)`, on identical initial data, contradicting `Executes.unique`. This is a static argument against the exact definitions; a separate Lean probe is not yet successfully compiled. A sensible follow-up must specify width selection and its computability/resource assumptions, input-fit guarantees, encoding/size conventions, and the permitted simulation overhead. A logarithmic band alone does not prevent the exhibited input-dependent-width leakage.
3. **[should-fix] Make the empty-input word-size bound defined in the index.** `paper/sections/query.tex:88` writes `floor(log₂ n)` while the theorem and tests include `n=0`. Lean's `Nat.log 2 0` is zero; ordinary real logarithm at zero is undefined. State the binary-digit convention explicitly (one digit at zero), or use `floor(log₂(max(1,n)))+1`, preserving the actual `w ≥ 2` empty-list threshold.
4. **[should-fix] Reconcile the index count.** `paper/main.tex:31` still says 124 entries, but this exact revision contains 125 `result` blocks after adding the word-RAM entry. Recount against the final integrated tree and rebuild the PDF.

The separate model is reasonable for the intended client, but its operational choices matter. It has a fixed finite register file plus indirect memory, unit-cost primitive operations including multiplication/division/shifts, an unbounded program counter over a fixed program, explicit halting, and faults on oversized arithmetic results. It is a fault-on-overflow variant: for example at width 3, `5+5` faults instead of returning the modular result 2; a left shift that discards high bits in a wrapping model may fault here. The existing test already exercises this distinction. Successful runs from `InputFits` inputs maintain word bounds, so removing redundant bounds checks on copy/load/store is justified. No transfer to wrapping arithmetic, existing `Cslib.RAM`, Turing machines, or cell-probe bounds is established by these files. The existing RAM also offers both cost measures, as the API reviewer noted.

The general word-RAM literature does not require a universal logarithmic upper bound on `w`: [MIT 6.006's model description, page 4](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-006-introduction-to-algorithms-spring-2020/c6d8f06c6f11e3342633dec85498f551_MIT6_006S20_r01.pdf) explicitly requires enough bits to address the input and includes unit-cost multiplication/division. Thus finding 1 asks for accurate parameterized-model documentation, not restriction of the general API. I compared the pinned `lean-trominoes@6d5b36c1` machine/uniform-decision and allocation/structured definitions: the signed-to-unsigned change, overflow faults, input convention, uniform fitting-width implication, and charged allocation/control flow are traceable, with the stated deviations. I did not establish a new equivalence with the cited literature's other instruction/overflow variants.

Checked all seven modules and tests: flat/interpreter correspondence and determinism; word-bound preservation and width monotonicity; branch/loop counts including final halt; compiler placement; invariant/measure termination; allocator register separation and empty blocks; renaming/frame behavior; and the distinctness invariant/bounds. No core correctness finding remains from that read. The distinctness advantage is properly restricted to values below the list length and a non-comparison algorithm; it does not claim unrestricted distinctness or a formalized comparison lower bound. Nonvacuous tests execute yes/no/empty inputs and check actual counts; named axiom guards cover the major endpoints. Four pinned index links were checked, and rendered page 43 fits cleanly apart from the semantic wording above. This is independent static source/index review; the author's six-gate report is not represented as a fresh reviewer run. The temporary review cache was lost during host recovery; any later probe result will be recorded separately.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Adversarial follow-up to the correctness review, still against exact `47ccf008f813eb5f7baaa3d21bc1afe6a7723a4d`. Reviewer `fusion_barrier` has now successfully checked the following five Lean probe theorems through MCP diagnostics in an isolated exact-revision checkout. Diagnostics report no errors or warnings; the axiom prints use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. This replaces the earlier “static only” status for these particular claims; it does not claim a fresh run of the six project gates.

- The first pair proves the unrestricted `At`-to-uniform converse fails, even though both advised widths fit the empty input. It rules out every uniform time/threshold function for this example.
- `at_vacuous` proves any predicate satisfies the low-level `At` contract at zero time when the chosen width fits no input. This is a consequence of its explicit implication, not an inconsistency; users need a domain-fit guarantee when interpreting it as decision on all instances.
- The last pair proves the existing `LinearTime` predicate on an injective encoding of arbitrary singleton natural words, with size equal to the actual one-word input length, while no width depending only on that constant size can fit all instances. Thus even an injective encoding and a natural word-count size do not imply logarithmic-bit-width execution. A promise bounding input magnitudes supplies the missing specialization. The actual element-distinctness domain supplies that promise.

No tracked source or author worktree was edited. The probe is review evidence, not a proposed implementation redesign. The code is reproduced here for a durable, independently reproducible record:

```lean
import Complexity.Computability.WordRAM.Time
open Cslib.WordRAM

namespace WordRAMReview

def probeProgram : Program 2 :=
  [.op (.width 0), .op (.const 1 1), .op (.bin .sub 0 0 1), .halt 0]

theorem at_can_read_predicate :
    DecidesInTimeAt (fun _ : Bool => []) (fun b => b = true)
      (fun _ => 4) (fun b => if b then 2 else 1) := by
  refine ⟨2, probeProgram, ?_⟩
  intro b _
  cases b
  · exact ⟨0, 4, .of_run (fuel := 4) (by decide), le_rfl, by decide, by decide⟩
  · exact ⟨1, 4, .of_run (fuel := 4) (by decide), le_rfl, by decide, by decide⟩

theorem no_uniform_decider (time bits : Bool → Nat) :
    ¬DecidesInTime (fun _ : Bool => []) (fun b => b = true) time bits := by
  rintro ⟨r, p, hp⟩
  let w := max (bits false) (bits true)
  have hi : InputFits w [] := ⟨fits_zero w, by simp⟩
  obtain ⟨v₀, n₀, he₀, _, _, hb₀⟩ := hp false w (le_max_left _ _) hi
  obtain ⟨v₁, n₁, he₁, _, _, hb₁⟩ := hp true w (le_max_right _ _) hi
  have hv := (he₀.unique he₁).1
  have h1 : v₁ = 1 := hb₁.mpr rfl
  have : false = true := hb₀.mp (hv.trans h1)
  cases this

theorem at_vacuous (P : Bool → Prop) :
    DecidesInTimeAt (fun _ : Bool => [1]) P (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) := by
  refine ⟨0, [], ?_⟩
  intro b hi
  have h := hi.1
  change 1 < 1 at h
  exact False.elim (Nat.lt_irrefl 1 h)

def acceptProgram : Program 1 := [.op (.const 0 1), .halt 0]

theorem linearTime_arbitrary_singleton :
    LinearTime (fun n : Nat => [n]) (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => True) := by
  refine ⟨1, 0, 1, acceptProgram, ?_⟩
  intro n w _ hi
  have h1 : Fits w 1 := hi.1
  refine ⟨1, 2, .of_run (fuel := 2) ?_, le_rfl, le_rfl, by simp⟩
  simp [run, step, acceptProgram, Op.eval, Data.put, h1, Data.set, State.init]

theorem no_fixed_width_for_singletons (w : Nat) : ¬∀ n, InputFits w [n] := by
  intro h
  have hi := (h (2 ^ w)).2 (2 ^ w) (by simp)
  exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ hi

end WordRAMReview

#print axioms WordRAMReview.at_can_read_predicate
#print axioms WordRAMReview.no_uniform_decider
#print axioms WordRAMReview.at_vacuous
#print axioms WordRAMReview.linearTime_arbitrary_singleton
#print axioms WordRAMReview.no_fixed_width_for_singletons
```

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Independent model-review follow-up by fusion-barrier, exact PR revision `47ccf008f813eb5f7baaa3d21bc1afe6a7723a4d`; its existing RAM modules are identical to current main `0bef073f`.

The same input/model scrutiny applies to the existing RAM. [Cook and Reckhow (1973), §1/Table I and Theorem 2](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~sacook/homepage/rams.pdf) use integer registers, no multiplication, charged READ/PRINT, finite-alphabet input strings, and a bound T(input length) at least the input length. Their TM simulation bounds are quadratic for logarithmic cost and cubic for unit cost; controlled number growth is essential to the latter.

Our RAM instead preloads arbitrary natural numbers without charge, extracts register 0 without charge, adds multiplication, and indexes `ComputesInTime` bounds by the raw input tuple. These are legitimate contracts, but the paper's simulation theorem does not transfer automatically. In particular, the following witnesses have been checked with Lean MCP (no errors/warnings; only standard allowed axioms):

- `ComputesInTime logCost 1 [] (fun x => x 0) (fun _ => 0)`: arbitrary preloaded identity costs zero.
- For the fixed multiplication-free program `[.add 0 0 0]`, one step costs exactly 1 under `unitCost` and `2 * bitLength n` under `logCost` on input `[n]`. Taking `n = 2^B` makes the latter exceed any proposed bound B while unit time stays 1.

Thus the existing `RAM/Squaring.lean` prose claiming an unconditional multiplication-free polynomial relation also needs an initial-bitlength/charged-input qualification. The actual bound `bitLength_read_run_le` correctly retains the initial-size term; no theorem flaw was found. Cleanup #79 will qualify that prose and add these regression clients, preserving APIs. Neither this cleanup nor the present WordRAM PR proves RAM/TM simulation or a P equality. This is a symmetric model audit, not a demand that all machines share one operational semantics.

body:
Completes the `RotationMap` rotation-simplification set and moves `spectralExpansion_eq_of_walk_eq` into `Expander/Basic.lean` (Items D4 and E4 of #614, #587).

### Summary of Changes

1. **`Expander/Basic.lean` & `Expander/Loops.lean`**:
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem rot_ofInvolutive` in `Basic.lean`.
   - Moves `spectralExpansion_eq_of_walk_eq` from `Loops.lean` into `Basic.lean` (and lists it in `Basic.lean`'s `## Main results` docstring), so only `Basic.lean` unfolds `spectralExpansion`.
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem rot_addLoops_inl` and `@[simp] theorem rot_addLoops_inr` in `Loops.lean`.
2. **`Expander/Reindex.lean`**:
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem rot_reindex` (listed in `## Main results`) and marks `neighbor_reindex` `@[simp]`.
3. **`Expander/SlotGraph.lean`**:
   - Adds `rot_extendLabels_of_forall_ne` and simplifies `neighbor_extendLabels_of_forall_ne` to `congrArg Prod.fst (G.rot_extendLabels_of_forall_ne enc v hb)`.
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem rot_slotGraph_inl`, `@[simp] theorem rot_slotGraph_inr_false`, and `@[simp] theorem rot_slotGraph_inr_true`.
4. **`Expander/Contraction.lean`**:
   - Adds `rot_contract` and `@[simp] theorem rot_contract_contractDart`.
5. **`Expander/Lazy.lean`**:
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem rot_lazy_inl`, `@[simp] theorem rot_lazy_inr`, `@[simp] theorem neighbor_lazy_inl`, and `@[simp] theorem neighbor_lazy_inr`.
6. **`Expander/Hom.lean`**:
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem rot_restrict` and replaces the 8-line `change` in `Hom.powRot_map` with `rw [powRot_succ, powRot_succ, φ.rot_map, Prod.map_fst, Prod.map_snd, id_eq, powRot_map φ t]; rfl`.
7. **`Expander/LowerBound.lean`**:
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem rot_complete`.
8. **`Expander/Power.lean` & `Expander/Walk.lean`**:
   - Adds `@[simp] theorem powRot_zero`, makes `powRot_succ` public, and adds `@[simp] theorem rot_pow_zero` and `rot_pow_succ` (listed in `## Main results`).
   - Replaces the manual `have hrot : (G.pow (t + 1)).rot (v, k) = ... := rfl` in `Walk.walkDart_rot_pow` with `rw [rot_pow_succ]`.
9. **`Expander/Products.lean`, `Expander/Tower.lean`, & `Expander/AffinePlane.lean`**:
   - Marks `rot_zigzag` `@[simp]` in `Products.lean` and adds `rot_zigzagTower_succ` in `Tower.lean`.
   - Renames `affinePlane_rot` to `@[simp] theorem rot_affinePlane` in `AffinePlane.lean`.
10. **Client cleanups**:
    - `PolyTime/RotationMap/TowerTable.lean`: removes `private theorem reindex_rotation` in favor of `rot_reindex` and replaces unfolding `zigzag, zigzagRot` in `lookup_iterate_numbered` with `rot_zigzagTower_succ, rot_zigzag`.
    - `PolyTime/RotationMap/TowerTable/Family.lean`: uses `rot_contract` in `contract_eq` instead of unfolding `RotationMap.contract` and `contractRot`.
    - `PCP/Encoded/CloudRotation.lean` and `PCP/Encoded/Preprocess.lean`: replaces unfoldings of `RotationMap.reindex`, `RotationMap.reindexRot`, and `RotationMap.loops` with `rot_reindex`, `neighbor_def`, and `rot_loops`.
    - `USTCON/Reader/Correct.lean`: replaces manual unfoldings of `slotGraph`, `union`, `ofInvolutive`, `extendLabels`, and `decodeLabel_eq_none_iff` in `slotRotN_val` with `rot_slotGraph_inl`, `rot_slotGraph_inr_false`, `rot_slotGraph_inr_true`, and `rot_extendLabels_of_forall_ne`.

### Validation
- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 ./scripts/check.sh`: all 6 gates passed (`build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`).
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: passed (`All hygiene checks passed.`).
- `python3 -B scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`: passed (`2021 public tidy statement(s) in 423 module(s), matching the baseline.`).
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: passed (no impact on curated headline abstracts).

### AI Disclosure
- **Agent / Session:** `worker-jetski-73aa4b5a` (`73aa4b5a-fa3d-4195-8024-b19f43bfa557`, Gemini 3.1 Pro).
- **Self-reviewed revision:** `b31135c20ea0756aa6c46c3fb69b4a5a53166086`.

Refs #614, #587

body:
Independent coordinator verdict — `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023` (not Samuel): **APPROVED at exact head `1d9e882dc7bb9debdc53117a074d13f89c00dabe`.**

The relocations preserve effective hypotheses, universes, proofs and credit. Degree zero still selects `X`: irreducibility and monicity correctly become unconditional, while the basis, bit encoding and `2 ^ w` cardinality results retain `w ≠ 0`. The strengthened additive equivalence uses the same basis coordinates and coordinatewise bit conversion/inverse, with identical bit order. Schedule and the actual encoding clients retain their functions and resource bounds. The subfield specialization is valid.

The new lower modules have no Combinatorics/Computability dependency or cycle; BinaryField and Schedule lose the affine-disperser proof dependencies. No alias, stale moved name or public tidy surface is added. Nonblocking doc nit: qualify the opening search-interval description by `w ≠ 0`, consistent with the later zero-degree caveat.

Exact-head [CI40081209515](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40081209515), job120834978618, passes all six gates and the tidy statement ratchet. This is source/API and dependency review, reusing unchanged mathematics; no fresh full local build is claimed. Ready at this head under the coordinator’s integration order.

title: refactor(fieldtheory): separate binary-field and subfield infrastructure from affine disperser (#614)
body:
Implements Item **A5 (`Separate binary-field infrastructure from the affine-disperser proof`)** of #614 (under #587):

1. **`Complexity/Foundations/Data/BitString/ZModTwo.lean` (`Cslib.BitString`)**:
   - Moves `bitEquiv : ZMod 2 ≃+* Bool`, `bitEquiv_eq_ringEquivOfPrime`, `bitEquiv_symm_apply`, `bitEquiv_symm_false`, and `bitEquiv_symm_true` out of `Complexity/Foundations/Combinatorics/AffineDisperser/Bits.lean` into `Complexity/Foundations/Data/BitString/ZModTwo.lean`.
   - `FieldTheory/Finite/BinaryField.lean` and `HardnessAmplification/Schedule.lean` no longer transitively import `Combinatorics/AffineDisperser/Bits.lean` or the affine-disperser proof.

2. **`Complexity/Foundations/FieldTheory/Finite/BinaryField.lean` (`Cslib`)**:
   - Moves `polyOfCode`, `polyOfCode_zero`, `polyOfCode_two_mul_add`, `polyOfCode_ne_zero_and_natDegree`, `natDegree_polyOfCode`, `polyOfCode_surjective`, `exists_irreducible_natDegree_eq`, `leastIrreducible`, `leastIrreducible_zero`, `irreducible_leastIrreducible`, `natDegree_leastIrreducible`, `exists_code_leastIrreducible`, and `monic_leastIrreducible` from `Combinatorics/AffineDisperser/BinaryField.lean` into `FieldTheory/Finite/BinaryField.lean`.
   - Drops `hp : p ≠ 0` from `irreducible_leastIrreducible` and `monic_leastIrreducible` so they hold unconditionally for all degrees (including `0`), and deletes the primed duplicates `irreducible_leastIrreducible'` and `monic_leastIrreducible'`.
   - Promotes `BinaryField.equivBits` to an additive equivalence (`BinaryField w ≃+ BitString w`) and updates callers in `HardnessAmplification/Schedule.lean` and `HardnessEncoding/Program.lean`.

3. **`Complexity/Foundations/FieldTheory/Finite/Subfield.lean` (`Cslib`)**:
   - Moves `card_sq_le_of_ne_top`, `card_subfield_le_of_lt_prime`, and `card_subfield_le` (proved as `card_subfield_le_of_lt_prime (L := 1)`) into `Complexity/Foundations/FieldTheory/Finite/Subfield.lean`.
   - Moves `nonempty_addEquiv_bitString` and `exists_field_card_eq_two_pow` from `Combinatorics/LineCode/Field.lean` into `FieldTheory/Finite/Subfield.lean` and deletes `Combinatorics/LineCode/Field.lean`, updating callers in `MassProduction/Fine.lean`, `Probability/SmallBias/Powering.lean`, `ComplexityTests/Code/M3.lean`, and `ComplexityTests/MassProduction/HighRate.lean`.

### Validation
- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 ./scripts/check.sh` (all 6 gates: `build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`)
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
- `python3 -B scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`

Part of #614, #587.

body: [P2] This constructor, its two simp lemmas and `symmDiff_mem` depend only on general Boolean-algebra APIs, but are introduced in the upper complexity-reduction module. `Classes/P/Closure` and `Classes/ParityP/Closure` now import that module solely to obtain them. This preserves the public names and avoids touching any foundational hub while giving the generic API its shared lower home, as required by AGENTS.md’s placement rule.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
### Independent Review of `3d0c7d9bbefade9fb721dcf553f5827fad462e5e` (`reviewer-jetski-boolean-closure-610`, `d35b58a2-ae7a-4e41-9ea2-f9c8c2a78a42`)

**Verdict:** **APPROVED** (`3d0c7d9bbefade9fb721dcf553f5827fad462e5e`)

1. **Mathematical Correctness & Model Conventions**:
   - `BooleanSubalgebra.ofComplInf` and `BooleanSubalgebra.symmDiff_mem` (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Reduction/ManyOne.lean`) construct a `BooleanSubalgebra α` for any `[BooleanAlgebra α]` from `⊥ ∈ s`, complement closure, and meet (`⊓`) closure, deriving join (`⊔`) closure by De Morgan's law `x ⊔ y = (xᶜ ⊓ yᶜ)ᶜ`, and symmetric-difference closure via `S.sup_mem (S.sdiff_mem hx hy) (S.sdiff_mem hy hx)`.
   - `inter_mem_BPP` (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/BPP/Amplification.lean`) amplifies both `BPP` verifiers to error exponent `3` (`2 ^ (-3) = 1 / 8`) via `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent` and runs `andVerifier` on disjoint segments of the random string of length `(p₁ + p₂).eval (enc a).length` (`49 / 64 ≥ 3 / 4` on `a ∈ A ∩ B` and `≤ 1 / 8 ≤ 1 / 4` on `a ∉ A ∩ B`).
   - `inter_mem_PSPACE` (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/Space/Closure.lean`) uses `mem_PSPACE_iff_computableTidilyInPolySpace` and composes `hf.prod hg` with `ComputableTidilyInPolySpace.of_polyTime ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bool_and`.
   - Verified all 13 `BooleanSubalgebra (Set α)` bundles (`P`, `ZPP`, `BPP`, `PSPACE`, `PP`, `SPP`, `WPP`, `LWPP`, `AWPP`, `ParityP`, `ModP` for `hk : k.Prime`, `PH`, and `BooleanHierarchy`), their `@[simp]` `coe_booleanSubalgebra` and `mem_booleanSubalgebra` lemmas, and the uniform `union_mem_*`, `diff_mem_*`, and `symmDiff_mem_*` projections (`sup_mem`, `sdiff_mem`, `symmDiff_mem`).
   - Dual-class union/intersection closures (`union_mem_coRP`, `inter_mem_coRP`, `union_mem_SigmaP`, `union_mem_PiP`, `union_mem_BH`) are cleanly factored through `compl_union_mem`, `compl_inter_mem`, and `union_mem_differenceHierarchy`.
2. **API Quality, Placement, & Proof Hygiene**:
   - Placement of `BooleanSubalgebra.ofComplInf` and `BooleanSubalgebra.symmDiff_mem` in `ManyOne.lean` alongside existing De Morgan helpers (`compl_union_mem`, `compl_inter_mem`) avoids touching high-fanout foundational hubs or `Complexity.lean`.
   - Zero `sorry`, custom `axiom`, `native_decide`, or non-terminal bare `simp` calls in the diff.
3. **Tests & Axiom Guards**:
   - `ComplexityTests/ClassClosure.lean` exercises `diff_mem_P`, `inter_mem_BPP`, `union_mem_BPP`, `inter_mem_PSPACE`, and `union_mem_PSPACE` on concrete languages and includes `#print axioms` guards verifying only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

body:
Addressed the placement review (`https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/787#pullrequestreview-5637778843`) in `505fd7c45ff14f156819a612ae30e4a5e8c47c3e` (stacked directly on `3d0c7d9bbefade9fb721dcf553f5827fad462e5e` with no force-push):

- Moved `BooleanSubalgebra.ofComplInf`, `BooleanSubalgebra.coe_ofComplInf`, `BooleanSubalgebra.mem_ofComplInf`, and `BooleanSubalgebra.symmDiff_mem` out of `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Reduction/ManyOne.lean` into the narrow module `Complexity/Foundations/Order/BooleanSubalgebra.lean` (`-- upstream: candidate (Mathlib, Mathlib/Order/BooleanSubalgebra.lean)`).

title: refactor(complexity): bundle Boolean-closed classes into BooleanSubalgebra and add BPP/PSPACE intersection (#610)
body:
Completes the **Boolean closure of complexity classes** milestone in #610 (item 6):

1. **`BooleanSubalgebra` constructors and helpers (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Reduction/ManyOne.lean`, `Classes/P.lean`)**:
   - Adds `BooleanSubalgebra.ofComplInf` (constructing a `BooleanSubalgebra α` from `⊥ ∈ s`, complement closure, and meet `⊓` closure, deriving join `⊔` closure via De Morgan's law) and `BooleanSubalgebra.symmDiff_mem`.
   - Adds `empty_mem_P` and `univ_mem_P` in `Classes/P.lean`.
2. **Missing `inter_mem_BPP` and `inter_mem_PSPACE` (`Classes/BPP/Amplification.lean`, `Classes/Space/Closure.lean`)**:
   - Proves `inter_mem_BPP` by amplifying both verifiers to error exponent `3` (`2 ^ (-3) = 1 / 8`) via `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent` and running `andVerifier` on disjoint segments of the random string.
   - Proves `inter_mem_PSPACE` via `mem_PSPACE_iff_computableTidilyInPolySpace` and `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bool_and`.
3. **Uniform `BooleanSubalgebra (Set α)` bundles across 13 complexity classes**:
   - Bundles `P`, `ZPP`, `BPP`, `PSPACE`, `PP`, `SPP`, `WPP`, `LWPP`, `AWPP`, `ParityP`, `ModP` (for `hk : k.Prime`), `PH`, and `BooleanHierarchy` into `BooleanSubalgebra (Set α)` via `<Class>.booleanSubalgebra` (following `SharpP.subsemiring` and `GapP.subring`), deriving `union_mem_*`, `diff_mem_*`, and `symmDiff_mem_*` as 1-line projections (`sup_mem`, `sdiff_mem`, `symmDiff_mem`), and factoring dual-class closures (`union_mem_coRP`, `inter_mem_coRP`, `union_mem_SigmaP`, `union_mem_PiP`, `union_mem_BH`) through `compl_union_mem`, `compl_inter_mem`, and `union_mem_differenceHierarchy`.

### Validation & Review
- All 6 `./scripts/check.sh` gates (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`), `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `python3 -B scripts/check_tidy_surface.py` (`2020 public tidy statement(s) in 422 module(s)`), and `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passed on `3d0c7d9bbefade9fb721dcf553f5827fad462e5e`.
- Concrete examples and `#print axioms` guards added in `ComplexityTests/ClassClosure.lean`.
- Abstract catalogue assessment: internal refactoring and closure API completion; no change to `abstracts/catalogue.json`.
- Independently reviewed and approved at `3d0c7d9bbefade9fb721dcf553f5827fad462e5e` by `reviewer-jetski-boolean-closure-610` (`d35b58a2-ae7a-4e41-9ea2-f9c8c2a78a42`).

body: [P2] Deleting the existing destination before the rename makes replacement destructive on failure. With an existing valid destination and `Path.rename` raising OSError, this removes the old output and the finally block also removes the verified staging directory. +def verify_provenance(directory: Path, repository: str, sha: str) -> dict:
+    root = Path(directory).resolve()
+    prov_path = root / "provenance.json"
+    require(prov_path.is_file(), "Missing provenance.json in abstract artifact")

+    documents = [catalogue, *docs]
+    expected_pdfs = set()
+    for document in documents:
+        require(isinstance(document, dict) and isinstance(document.get("pdf"), str)
+                and isinstance(document.get("pdf_sha256"), str),

+    clock=time.monotonic,
+    sleep=time.sleep,

+    while True:
+        try:
+            lean_run = check_workflow_once(
+                repository, sha,

+            break

+            remaining = deadline - clock()
+            if remaining <= 0:

+    artifact_name = f"formal-abstracts-{sha}-{abstracts_run['run_attempt']}"
+    dest = Path(output_dir)
+    staging = dest.parent / f".{dest.name}-staging"

+        downloader(repository, abstracts_run["id"], artifact_name, staging)
+        verify_provenance(staging, repository, sha)

body:
Addressed all three findings from review `5637869383` in `dd194298068248acfb7fdf7812d7a83dbe3378ed`:

1. **Catalogue completeness, run metadata binding, and input digest checks (`discussion_r4366804715`)**:
   - `verify_provenance` now loads `abstracts/catalogue.json`, requires `catalogue.pdf` and an exact ordered match between `provenance.json`'s `documents` (`id` and `<id>.pdf`) and all 14 entries in `abstracts/catalogue.json`.
   - Binds `run_url` (`https://github.com/<repository>/actions/runs/<run_id>`) and `run_attempt` in `provenance.json` to the selected `Formal abstract PDFs` run and attempt.
   - Verifies `provenance.json`'s `inputs` list against the checked-out repository files (requiring `abstracts/catalogue.json`, `scripts/build_abstracts.py`, `scripts/abstract_to_tex.py`, and `scripts/proof_lengths.py`, plus matching SHA-256 digests for every recorded input and any document `source` / `source_sha256`).
   - Updated `write_fixture_artifact` to generate all 14 catalogue entries and real input digests, and added regression subtests for `incomplete catalogue` (`only_cook_levin=True`), `wrong run_attempt` (`99`), `wrong run_url`, `empty inputs`, and `tampered input digest`.
   - Updated the PR description to match the producer's actual `source_sha` / `inputs` schema.
2. **Non-destructive destination replacement (`discussion_r4366804718`)**:
   - `download_verified_abstracts` no longer deletes `dest` before `staging.rename(dest)`. Instead, an existing `dest` is moved to a sibling backup directory (`os.replace(dest, backup)`) only after download, provenance verification, and post-download CI revalidation succeed, and is restored automatically (`os.replace(backup, dest)`) if `staging.rename(dest)` fails.
   - Added `test_existing_destination_survives_rename_or_verification_failure` injecting `Path.rename` raising `OSError` and a provenance failure on an existing destination.
3. **Post-download workflow revalidation and rerun handling (`discussion_r4366804722`)**:
   - `download_verified_abstracts` now re-checks both `Lean Action CI` and `Formal abstract PDFs` via `check_both_workflows` immediately after downloading and verifying provenance, before installing `staging`.
   - `check_both_workflows` checks `Abstracts` even when `Lean` is `Pending`, so a terminal failure in `Abstracts` rejects immediately rather than waiting on a pending `Lean` attempt.
   - If a newer completed attempt appears during download, the loop re-downloads and verifies the new attempt's artifact (bounded by `authority_retries <= 3`) instead of installing the stale attempt.
   - Added `test_rerun_during_download_rejects_failure_and_installs_newer_attempt` covering both probes.

### Verification (`dd194298068248acfb7fdf7812d7a83dbe3378ed`)
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: `Ran 288 tests in 22.630s — OK`

title: feat(WordRAM): bounded-word RAM, structured programs, time classes and element distinctness
body:
Closes #63.

Adds `Cslib.WordRAM`, an unsigned bounded-word machine with explicit halting, overflow faults and unit-cost instructions. It supports certified word-level algorithms with a finite named register file and indirect memory. The existing `Cslib.RAM` has unbounded registers and both unit/logarithmic cost measures; a different cost function alone does not supply the new operational semantics.

The machine, uniform decision predicates, structured execution and allocation are adapted from [the lean-trominoes formalization at 6d5b36c1](https://github.com/edemaine/lean-trominoes/tree/6d5b36c1), under Apache-2.0. Adapted files preserve the collective lean-trominoes copyright notice and credit Erik Demaine alongside Samuel Schlesinger. Mathematical/model sources include Cook–Reckhow, CLRS, Fredman–Willard and Hagerup; notation work credits Algolean in the bibliography.

## Results and API

- The machine includes arithmetic, bitwise operations, shifts, memory access and reading the word size. A fuelled interpreter, determinism, word-bound preservation from fitting inputs, and width monotonicity for programs that do not read the width are proved.
- `Program.DecidesInTime` and `DecidableInTime` require one program to answer at every fitting width above the threshold. `LinearTime` and `PolynomialTime` put logarithmic lower thresholds on that contract. They do not themselves guarantee that inputs fit at logarithmic width, or identify a class with Turing-machine P.
- `Program.DecidesInTimeAt` and `DecidableInTimeAt` are conditional prescribed-width contracts. Their input-fit premise and arbitrary width function permit vacuity and width advice. The unrestricted converse to uniform decision is false, not an open theorem.
- Structured `Code` shares data-operation semantics with flat instructions and compiles with exact instruction counts (`Exec.runs`). The API includes invariant/measure loop rules, frames, injective register renaming, scoped `ram[...]` notation and symbolic execution with `ram_eval`.
- Allocation zeroes a block in `4k + 7` instructions; indexed reads/writes cost two. Register parameters avoid a fixed allocator layout.
- The element-distinctness client decides `List.Nodup` for lists of length `n` whose entries are below `n`, within `16(n + 1)` instructions including halt, at every width at least `2(floor(log2(max(1,n))) + 1)`. `inputFits` proves every promised instance fits at that threshold. This is direct addressing, not a comparison algorithm or a theorem about unrestricted distinctness.

## Model boundaries

Overflow faults rather than wrapping; subtraction is truncated, division by zero returns zero and remainder by zero returns the dividend. Initial input installation and output extraction are uncharged; halt is counted. Multiplication, division and shifts are primitive unit-cost operations. Bounds along runs assume the initial input fits. The program counter is not word-bounded. These are explicit model choices, not a proved bit-cost equivalence.

No wrapping-model, existing-RAM, TM, or cell-probe transfer is established. Follow-up #81 scopes a quantitative additive-fragment simulation to existing RAM under logarithmic cost. Any prescribed-width-to-uniform conversion needs input-fit, encoding and effective width-selection assumptions and an explicit overhead. The source's further algorithm clients remain in ROADMAP. UPSTREAM records source-author and CSLib algorithm-model coordination.

## Validation and review

Final integration revision: `822d6793cd9c37feefc3cfd1b40722c69e5da069`. It merges approved WordRAM revision `d56de97e` with approved PR69 wrapper `0d53e0f6`, which contains main `6c66a22b` through PR68 and PR83. All eight WordRAM source/test files are byte-identical to the independently approved source (`4d59a90c`); all other Lean source/test files match the approved dependency tree. The aggregate imports preserve both developments.

All six `scripts/check.sh` gates pass on the combined candidate: strict build, `mk_all --check`, strict tests, `lint`, `lint-style`, and `checkInitImports`. MCP diagnostics were clean during source development. The earlier source checkpoint's long docstring line was fixed before its passing rerun. Independent final integration review is approved below; required CI is checked separately before merge.

The regression suite covers overflow, halt/fault behavior, memory layout, division/bitwise conventions, symbolic execution, register renaming, loops and compiled distinctness on yes/no/empty inputs. Five adversarial contract checks show width advice despite fitting inputs, impossibility of a uniform decider for that example, prescribed-width vacuity, and arbitrary singleton inputs in the generic linear-time class despite no common fitting width. The real client separately tests its threshold certificate and the empty-input `w = 2` case. Existing named axiom guards are retained; no `sorry`, custom axioms or `native_decide` are introduced.

Independent API/source-credit review by `fusion-graph-20261020` and correctness/model/index review by `fusion_barrier` requested changes on `47ccf008`. The original author's unpublished fixes are preserved, and the takeover addresses the remaining contract/model/index findings. Independent coordinator `wordram-final-review-20261020` [approved the exact source and documentation with no findings](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/78#issuecomment-6299772589). Root coordinator `coordinator-ops-20261020` [approved the exact final integration and index at `822d6793` with no findings](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/78#issuecomment-6300088526); these agent verdicts are not platform or human approvals. [Initial API review](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/78#issuecomment-6298651629), [initial correctness/model/index review](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/78#issuecomment-6299200228), and [checked adversarial probes](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/78#issuecomment-6299258307) remain the durable review history.

## Theorem index

The query-complexity entry states the promise, exact time and width constants, counted halt, empty-input convention and non-comparison scope. All five declaration links, including `inputFits`, pin `4d59a90c` and were checked against the committed source lines and emitted PDF URLs. The integration preserves every approved dependency section and the approved WordRAM entry.

The combined index has 129 entries and a 312-key bibliography without duplicate keys. `latexmk` succeeds; the final LaTeX pass has no undefined citations, overfull boxes or warnings. Its BibTeX runs retain two existing metadata warnings for `ThresholdCircuitRepresentations2026` and `Fagin1974`. Rendered pages 1, 31 and 49 were inspected, including the combined count, truth-table closure dependency and WordRAM entry. Independent final integration/index review is approved at `822d6793`, as recorded above. This is an AI-reviewed statement index, not human editorial approval or a formal proof of prose equivalence.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5, worker `claude-0ee2da73`) authored/adapted the original implementation and its initial review fixes. After that worker exhausted credits, the human explicitly authorized takeover by Codex worker `wordram-takeover-20261020`, which preserved those commits and added the remaining model-contract documentation, adversarial regression tests, client input-fit certificate and index corrections. Coordinator agents arrange independent review and integration. Samuel Schlesinger directed the work.

title: refactor(circuit): expose plain certificates throughout Circuit APIs
body:
Circuit's 114 remaining public tidy computability statements now expose the same-bound plain predicates, with renamed certificates and all in-repository callers updated. Runtime functions, encodings, quantifiers and numerical bounds are preserved; no compatibility aliases are added. Refs #456 and #587.

The deterministic `tidy_sweep rewrite --area Circuit --verify --rounds 8` handles the mechanical portion. The nine manual cases are Layered `carry`, `prepareLayer`, `finishLayer`, `nodeEval`; fixed-formula `formulaCode`; Tableau `gfStart_inSpace`, `blockSize_inSpace`, `gateCode_inSpace`; and the computability conjunct of rational `hittingGenerator_spec`. Higher-order callers use explicit certificates where inference needs them. Tableau's shared section hypotheses become explicit plain premises, with three full-telescope regression fixtures covering arbitrary input encodings and workspace bounds. Existing positive/negative clients and axiom sets are retained; proof-local tidy reasoning remains an implementation detail while S1 proceeds separately.

Framework friction: Existing plain-resource equivalences and certificates suffice for the Crypto client migrations; no new shared machinery or unresolved framework friction is introduced.

Abstract meaning: No selected abstract headline changes meaning. The migration preserves its functions, encodings, hypotheses and resource bounds; the selected abstract statements and bridges require no changes.

Validation on base `8f81e195`:

- All six required gates passed on the final Lean sources, plus hygiene/simp and abstract catalogue checks (14 abstracts, 19 headlines).
- Strict three-root build passed (13,075 jobs); current Circuit report is **114 → 0**, with no manual or unclassifiable statements remaining. S3 matches the reduced baseline: 1,904 statements remain in other areas.
- Source comparison accounts for all 114 headers: 111 exact predicate/name substitutions and three compiler-checked Tableau telescope fixtures. This is source correspondence, not an old elaborated-type hash identity claim. All 176 runtime definitions across the 41 changed library files remain unchanged.

The only current overlap is #790's shared `tidy_surface_baseline.json`; this PR removes only the 20 Circuit entries totalling 114, so integration must retain both areas' reductions. Other areas' migrations and the Machines S1/S3 boundary remain separate. Original authorship is preserved. Implemented and checked using OpenAI Codex; independent review is requested before integration.

title: feat(machines): add independent plain polynomial-degree certificates
body:
Adds ordinary plain `ComputableInDegree f encIn encOut d e`: one machine has time and workspace of degree `d`, while encoded output has its separate degree `e`. Both degrees may be zero, input/output types may have unrelated universes, and output is not charged to workspace. Direct `mono`, `of_bounds` and `computableInPolyTime` rules need no normalization. Refs #456 and #608.

The pure `DegreeBounded` definition and ten algebra lemmas move unchanged into `ResourceBounds/Degree.lean`, retaining names and Christian Reitwiessner's credit; `polyBounded` stays in its existing higher home. The existing raw Degree implementation and three existing resource definitions are byte-identical. There is no new raw transport, normalizer, registration, alias or S1 backend dependency.

Framework friction (#733): Crypto's accepted quantitative Stretch migration needs this shared plain degree interface before its area sweep. This PR supplies that interface in Machines; it proves no new Crypto/security endpoint and does not complete S1 or the Crypto sweep.

All six required gates passed, followed by the strict three-root build (13,081 jobs), S3 (unchanged: 2,018 statements/421 modules), hygiene/simp and catalogue checks (14 abstracts/19 headlines). Fixtures cover constant-degree machines, unrelated universes, uncharged copy output, independent output-degree failure, and an inhabited cumulative Stretch-shaped bound with negative monotonicity checks. Existing ResourceBounds tests and the full PRGStretch test file, including their negative assertions, remain unchanged and pass. Abstract/catalogue sources and claims are unchanged. Final overlap check found only generated aggregate unions.

Implemented and validated using OpenAI Codex. Independent final review is requested before integration; the author will not approve or enqueue this PR.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
[P2] Certify the published destination rather than the local dependency snapshot

This inventory is populated from locally generated dependency pages, so accepting membership here does not verify the public URL it redirects readers to. Two links in the current frozen output pass this function but have missing public anchors: `Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Bird.html` links [Matrix/Defs.html#Matrix.ofArray](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Defs.html#Matrix.ofArray), while the published declaration lives at [Matrix/Array.html#Matrix.ofArray](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Array.html#Matrix.ofArray); `tactics.html` links [TautoSet.html#Mathlib.Tactic.TautoSet.specialize_all](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Tactic/TautoSet.html#Mathlib.Tactic.TautoSet.specialize_all), whose current public page has no such ID. Both destination pages return HTTP 200, so page-existence checks alone miss this.

Resolve against published target mappings or otherwise verify the actual destinations before pruning; remap moved declarations and provide a valid fallback for unavailable ones. Add regressions where the published inventory moves or omits a declaration that exists locally. Rechecking a local snapshot and its own cached manifest cannot catch these cases.

title: feat(logic): add compositional first-order projection core
body:
This adds the compositional semantic foundation for first-order projections on the path to Circuit Value completeness. Numeric tests and input relations have separate vocabularies: for a fixed numeric structure and assignment, one constant or signed input literal works for every interpretation of the input relations. Arbitrary quantifier-free formulas do not enforce that restriction.

The core is vocabulary-parametric and relativized. It reuses Mathlib formulas and the existing tuple-based `FO.Interpretation`, proves a finite mutually exclusive numeric-case normal form, truth-preserving substitution, identity/composition isomorphisms preserving both vocabularies, and quantifier-free closure under explicit numeric hypotheses. A graph-complement client reuses Mathlib's graph language. Tests include a concrete nonvacuous example, empty universes, composition, axiom guards, and a proof that two independent nullary input bits cannot be projected to their conjunction.

This is the first independently useful milestone. Classical positive-dimensional full tuple universes with canonical numeric predicates, projection reducibility on finite structure classes, a certified logspace encoding transducer, the alternating-logspace simulation, `REACHa → MCVP → CVP`, and the native Circuit Value P-completeness theorem remain outstanding in `ROADMAP.md`. No resource bound or completeness theorem is claimed here. The classical quantifier-free convention of the cited source excludes BIT.

Validation and reviews:

- All six project gates passed, including strict build/tests and the imported-declaration axiom audit. The final expected-output guards also passed strict tests after formatting.
- The upstream synchronization check reports CURRENT for the CSLib main pin and every copied dependency revision.
- Independent Codex API review (`proof_api`) and correctness review (`proof_correctness`) approved exact Lean revision `811ad02abdab6bc2b9f945d58d2a1ff2ed1c282b`. Findings about precise source credit and scope wording were fixed and re-reviewed; no findings remain.
- Independent statement-index review (`resume_alternation`) approved the new exposition against that Lean revision. The 19-page PDF was rebuilt and visually inspected; all 81 declaration names, source anchors, and actual PDF URLs were verified. The 50 numbered entries remain unchanged. Exact review evidence and source hashes are in `paper/review.md`.

Mathematical sources: [Immerman, Descriptive Complexity](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-0539-5) and [Immerman–Landau, The Complexity of Iterated Multiplication, Definitions 3.3–3.6](https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/pub/mult.pdf). The latter bibliography entry is a separate commit.

AI assistance: Codex implemented the modules and tests, prepared the documentation, and ran validation; separate Codex agents performed the API, correctness, and prose-to-Lean reviews described above. These reviews do not imply human editorial approval or a machine-checked equivalence between prose and Lean.

These support fixtures alone do not establish direct-driver parity: execution of the preserved growth/callback negatives and actual driver clients belongs to the separate driver handoff. [P2] Preserve universe polymorphism of the existing deterministic API

This shared context changed from `{α β γ : Type*}` to `{α β γ : Type}`. Consequently the pre-existing `PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible`, reflexivity, composition and related deterministic interfaces now accept only `Type 0`. A generic `universe u; example {α : Type u} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (X : PromiseProblem α) : PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible enc enc X X := .refl enc X` passes against the prior module and fails against this exact head with `PromiseProblem.{u}` versus `PromiseProblem.{0}`.

Retain the original `Type*` context for existing deterministic declarations and localize the `Type` restriction to new PPT-dependent declarations. This does not require generalizing the PPT framework.

@@ -37,46 +52,487 @@ Reductions of promise problems are Karp reductions in the sense of Goldreich's s
 asking every problem separating the yes-instances from the no-instances to be NP-hard, which
 `PromiseProblem.NPHard.npHard_of_subset` derives.
 
+For randomized hardness results in metacomplexity [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020],
+[Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022], a **randomized polynomial-time many-one
+reduction with one-sided error** (`PromiseProblem.RPReducible`, and the threshold-indexed
+`PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError`) is a uniform strict PPT program `R : α → ProbComp β` that
+maps every yes-instance of `X` exclusively into `Y.yes` and maps every no-instance of `X` into
+`Y.no` with probability at least `2 / 3` (or `s a`). This convention matches the metacomplexity
+sources, where upper bounds on circuit or Kolmogorov complexity hold deterministically for every
+random choice on yes-instances while lower bounds on no-instances hold with high probability.
+Equivalence bridges connect `RPReducible` to:
+
+* the `Pr[...]` event notation (`PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_probability`),
+* probability-one completeness (`PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one`),
+* explicit seeded polynomial-time functions reading a random string of polynomial length
+  (`PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_exists_seeded`), and
+* the dual one-sided error convention of Valiant and Vazirani [ValiantVazirani1986] through
+  promise-problem complement (`PromiseProblem.rpReducible_compl_iff`).
+
+The probabilistic promise classes `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP` and `PromiseCoRP` follow Goldreich's
+semantic definitions [Goldreich, Definition 1.2 and Section 5.1][Goldreich2006], requiring bounded
+or one-sided error only on instances in the promise, and `PromiseBPP` and `PromiseCoRP` are closed
+under `RPReducible` (`PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`,
+`PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`).
+
 ## Main definitions
 
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.SolvesWithBoundedError`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.SolvesWithOneSidedError`: Goldreich's bounded-error and
+  one-sided-error conditions on a promise problem.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseBPP`, `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseRP`, `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseCoRP`:
+  the probabilistic classes of promise problems.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible`: polynomial-time reductions of promise
   problems, which between gap problems are the gap-preserving reductions.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.NPHard`: every problem in `NP` reduces to the promise problem.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducible`: randomized polynomial-time many-one reductions
+  with one-sided error on promise problems.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.gapMax`, `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.gapMin`: the gap
   problems of a maximization and of a minimization objective.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.restrict`: a promise problem restricted to a set of instances.
 
 ## Main results
 
+* `Cslib.Complexity.ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP`, `Cslib.Complexity.ofSet_mem_PromiseRP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.ofSet_mem_PromiseCoRP`, `Cslib.Complexity.promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.promiseClass_coRP_subset_PromiseCoRP`: agreement with `BPP`, `RP` and `coRP`
+  on decision problems and inclusion of `promiseClass`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.mem_PromiseCoRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn`: characterizations by uniform strict PPT
+  programs.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.polyTimeReducible_ofSet_iff`,
   `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.npHard_ofSet_iff`: on decision problems, the notions are
   `Cslib.Complexity.PolyTimeReducible` and `Cslib.Complexity.NPHard`.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.trans`,
   `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.NPHard.trans`: reductions compose and transfer hardness.
-* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseP`: `PromiseP` is closed under
-  reductions.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseNP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseRP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`: closure of promise classes
+  under deterministic reductions.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.npHard_of_polyTimeReducible_SAT`: a reduction from `SAT`
   proves NP-hardness, by the Cook–Levin theorem.
 * `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.NPHard.P_eq_NP_of_mem_PromiseP`: an NP-hard promise problem
   solvable in polynomial time gives `P = NP`.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducible.refl`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError.trans`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError.trans_add`: reflexivity, lifting of
+  deterministic reductions, and composition of randomized reductions with multiplicative and
+  additive error accounting.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_probability`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_exists_seeded`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.rpReducible_compl_iff`: faithfulness and convention bridges.
+* `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`,
+  `Cslib.Complexity.PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_PromiseRP_of_compl`: closure of `PromiseBPP`,
+  `PromiseCoRP` and `PromiseRP` under randomized one-sided reductions.
 
 ## References
 
 * [S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Chapter 11][AroraBarak09]
 * [O. Goldreich, *On promise problems: a survey*][Goldreich2006]
 * [S. Even, A. Selman, Y. Yacobi, *The complexity of promise problems with applications to
   public-key cryptography*][EvenSelmanYacobi1984]
+* [R. Ilango, *Approaching MCSP from Above and Below: Hardness for a Conditional Variant and
+  AC⁰[p]*, Section 2][Ilango2020]
+* [R. Ilango, B. Loff, I. C. Oliveira, *NP-Hardness of Circuit Minimization for Multi-Output
+  Functions*, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020]
+* [S. Hirahara, *NP-Hardness of Learning Programs and Partial MCSP*, Section 8][Hirahara2022]
+* [L. G. Valiant, V. V. Vazirani, *NP is as Easy as Detecting Unique
+  Solutions*][ValiantVazirani1986]

 @[expose] public section
 
 namespace Cslib.Complexity
 
-open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM Probability PromiseProblem
+
+/-! ### Promise-BPP, promise-RP and promise-coRP -/
 
 namespace PromiseProblem
 
-variable {α β γ : Type*} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encC : γ ↪ List Bool}
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+  {Q : PromiseProblem α} {A : Set α}
+
+/-- `V` solves the promise problem `Q` with bounded error, using random strings whose length is `p`
+evaluated at the length of the encoded instance: for every yes-instance at least two thirds of the
+random strings are accepted, and for every no-instance at least two thirds are rejected
+[Goldreich, Definition 1.2][Goldreich2006]. Nothing is required on instances outside the
+promise. -/
+def SolvesWithBoundedError (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (Q : PromiseProblem α) : Prop :=
+  (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+    3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+      V (a, List.ofFn r) = true).card) ∧
+  ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+    3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+      V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card
+
+/-- `V` solves the promise problem `Q` with one-sided error, using random strings whose length is
+`p` evaluated at the length of the encoded instance: for every yes-instance at least half of the
+random strings are accepted, and for every no-instance none is
+[Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]. Nothing is required on instances outside the promise. -/
+def SolvesWithOneSidedError (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (p : Polynomial ℕ)
+    (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (Q : PromiseProblem α) : Prop :=
+  (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+    2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+      V (a, List.ofFn r) = true).card) ∧
+  ∀ a ∈ Q.no, ∀ r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (a, List.ofFn r) = false
+
+@[simp]
+theorem solvesWithBoundedError_ofSet_iff :
+    (ofSet A).SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V ↔ DecidesWithBoundedError enc p V A := by
+  simp only [SolvesWithBoundedError, DecidesWithBoundedError, yes_ofSet, no_ofSet,
+    Set.mem_compl_iff]
+  exact ⟨fun h a => ⟨h.1 a, h.2 a⟩, fun h => ⟨fun a => (h a).1, fun a => (h a).2⟩⟩
+
+@[simp]
+theorem solvesWithOneSidedError_ofSet_iff :
+    (ofSet A).SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V ↔ DecidesWithOneSidedError enc p V A := by
+  simp only [SolvesWithOneSidedError, DecidesWithOneSidedError, yes_ofSet, no_ofSet,
+    Set.mem_compl_iff]
+  exact ⟨fun h a => ⟨h.1 a, h.2 a⟩, fun h => ⟨fun a => (h a).1, fun a => (h a).2⟩⟩
+
+/-- Negating the verifier solves the complement promise problem with bounded error. -/
+theorem SolvesWithBoundedError.compl (h : Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V) :
+    Qᶜ.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p (fun x => !V x) := by
+  refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+  · simpa using h.2 a ha
+  · simpa using h.1 a ha
+
+/-- A one-sided-error solver for a promise problem is a polynomial-time verifier on the promise. -/
+theorem SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate (h : Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V) :
+    (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = p.eval (enc a).length ∧ V (a, w) = true) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, ∀ w : List Bool, w.length = p.eval (enc a).length → V (a, w) = false := by
+  refine ⟨fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha w hw => ?_⟩
+  · have hpos := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := p.eval (enc a).length)
+    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ : (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+        V (a, List.ofFn r) = true).Nonempty := by
+      rw [← Finset.card_pos]
+      have := h.1 a ha
+      omega
+    exact ⟨List.ofFn r, List.length_ofFn, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hr).2⟩
+  · have hno := h.2 a ha fun i => w[i.val]'(by omega)
+    rwa [show (List.ofFn fun i : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) => w[i.val]'(by omega)) = w from
+      List.ext_getElem (by simp [hw]) fun i _ _ => by simp] at hno
+
+end PromiseProblem
+
+section PromiseProbabilistic
+
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool} {Q : PromiseProblem α} {A : Set α}
+
+/-- The promise problems solved with bounded error by polynomial-time algorithms reading
+polynomially long random strings, with respect to the encoding `enc` of instances
+[Goldreich, Definition 1.2][Goldreich2006]. -/
+def PromiseBPP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (PromiseProblem α) :=
+  {Q | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+    ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V}
+
+/-- The promise problems solved with one-sided error (no false positives on no-instances) by
+polynomial-time algorithms reading polynomially long random strings
+[Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]. -/
+def PromiseRP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (PromiseProblem α) :=
+  {Q | ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+    ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V}
+
+/-- The promise problems solved with one-sided error (no false negatives on yes-instances) by
+polynomial-time algorithms reading polynomially long random strings: those whose complements are
+in `PromiseRP` [Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]. -/
+def PromiseCoRP (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (PromiseProblem α) :=
+  {Q | Qᶜ ∈ PromiseRP enc}
+
+theorem mem_PromiseBPP_iff : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+private theorem mem_PromiseBPP_iff_tidy : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithBoundedError enc p V := by
+  simp only [mem_PromiseBPP_iff, computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime]
+
+theorem mem_PromiseRP_iff : Q ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+private theorem mem_PromiseRP_iff_tidy : Q ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      Q.SolvesWithOneSidedError enc p V := by
+  simp only [mem_PromiseRP_iff, computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime]
+
+/-- A promise problem is in `PromiseCoRP` when a polynomial-time verifier accepts every random
+string on every yes-instance and rejects at least half on every no-instance. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseCoRP_iff : Q ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔
+    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (V : α × List Bool → Bool),
+      ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, ∀ r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool, V (a, List.ofFn r) = true) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+        2 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+          V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨p, fun x => !V x, .of_tidy (by have := hV.tidy; fun_prop),
+      fun a ha r => by simp [hno a ha r], fun a ha => by simpa using hyes a ha⟩
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨p, fun x => !V x, .of_tidy (by have := hV.tidy; fun_prop),
+      fun a ha => by simpa using hno a ha, fun a ha r => by simp [hyes a ha r]⟩
+
+@[simp]
+theorem ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP : ofSet A ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔ A ∈ BPP enc := by
+  simp only [PromiseBPP, BPP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, solvesWithBoundedError_ofSet_iff]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem ofSet_mem_PromiseRP : ofSet A ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔ A ∈ RP enc := by
+  simp only [PromiseRP, RP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, solvesWithOneSidedError_ofSet_iff]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem ofSet_mem_PromiseCoRP : ofSet A ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔ A ∈ coRP enc := by
+  rw [PromiseCoRP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, ← ofSet_compl, ofSet_mem_PromiseRP, mem_coRP]
+
+/-- Every promise problem separated by a language in `BPP` is in `PromiseBPP`. -/
+theorem promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP : promiseClass (BPP enc) ⊆ PromiseBPP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨B, ⟨p, V, hV, hB⟩, hyes, hno⟩
+  exact ⟨p, V, hV, fun a ha => (hB a).1 (hyes ha),
+    fun a ha => (hB a).2 (Set.disjoint_right.1 hno ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every promise problem separated by a language in `RP` is in `PromiseRP`. -/
+theorem promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP : promiseClass (RP enc) ⊆ PromiseRP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨B, ⟨p, V, hV, hB⟩, hyes, hno⟩
+  exact ⟨p, V, hV, fun a ha => (hB a).1 (hyes ha),
+    fun a ha => (hB a).2 (Set.disjoint_right.1 hno ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every promise problem separated by a language in `coRP` is in `PromiseCoRP`. -/
+theorem promiseClass_coRP_subset_PromiseCoRP : promiseClass (coRP enc) ⊆ PromiseCoRP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨B, hB, hyes, hno⟩
+  exact promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP ⟨Bᶜ, hB,
+    Set.subset_compl_iff_disjoint_left.2 hno, Set.disjoint_compl_left_iff_subset.2 hyes⟩
+
+/-- `PromiseBPP` is closed under complement. -/
+theorem compl_mem_PromiseBPP (hQ : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc) : Qᶜ ∈ PromiseBPP enc :=
+  let ⟨p, V, hV, h⟩ := hQ
+  ⟨p, fun x => !V x, by have := hV.tidy; exact .of_tidy (by fun_prop), h.compl⟩
+
+/-- A promise problem's complement is in `PromiseRP` exactly when the problem is in
+`PromiseCoRP`. -/
+theorem compl_mem_PromiseRP_iff : Qᶜ ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔ Q ∈ PromiseCoRP enc :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- A promise problem's complement is in `PromiseCoRP` exactly when the problem is in
+`PromiseRP`. -/
+theorem compl_mem_PromiseCoRP_iff : Qᶜ ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔ Q ∈ PromiseRP enc := by
+  rw [← compl_mem_PromiseRP_iff, compl_compl]
+
+theorem PromiseP_subset_PromiseRP : PromiseP enc ⊆ PromiseRP enc :=
+  (promiseClass_mono P_subset_RP).trans promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP
+
+theorem PromiseP_subset_PromiseCoRP : PromiseP enc ⊆ PromiseCoRP enc :=
+  (promiseClass_mono P_subset_coRP).trans promiseClass_coRP_subset_PromiseCoRP
+
+theorem PromiseP_subset_PromiseBPP : PromiseP enc ⊆ PromiseBPP enc :=
+  (promiseClass_mono P_subset_BPP).trans promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP
+
+theorem PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP : PromiseRP enc ⊆ PromiseNP enc := by
+  rintro Q ⟨p, V, hV, h⟩
+  exact mem_PromiseNP_iff.2 ⟨p, V, hV.tidy, h.exists_certificate⟩
+
+/-- A counted verifier's uniform rejection probability is its rejected fraction of all words. -/
+private theorem uniformList_rejectCount_toReal (V : α × List Bool → Bool) (a : α) (n : ℕ) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).map (fun word => V (a, word))) false).toReal =
+      ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin n → Bool => V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card : ℝ) /
+        2 ^ n := by
+  rw [BitString.uniformList_map_apply]
+  simp
+
+/-- Converting a polynomial-time seeded verifier into a uniform strict PPT Boolean program. -/
+private theorem isPPTOn_sampleList_verifier {p : Polynomial ℕ} {V : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hV : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool) :
+    IsPPTOn enc encBool (fun a => (fun w => V (a, w)) <$>
+      BitString.sampleList (p.eval (enc a).length)) :=
+  have hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) enc encUnary :=
+    (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval p).comp
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encoding_length enc)
+  hcount.sampleList.map_with hV
+
+/-- **Probabilistic-program characterization of `PromiseBPP`**: a promise problem is in
+`PromiseBPP` exactly when a uniform strict PPT Boolean program accepts every yes-instance with
+probability at least `2 / 3` and rejects every no-instance with probability at least `2 / 3`. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn : Q ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔
+    ∃ M : α → ProbComp Bool, IsPPTOn enc encBool M ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 2 / 3 ≤ Pr[M a]) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 2 / 3 ≤ (ProbComp.eval (M a) false).toReal := by
+  rw [mem_PromiseBPP_iff_tidy]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => (fun w => V (a, w)) <$> BitString.sampleList (p.eval (enc a).length),
+      isPPTOn_sampleList_verifier hV, fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [uniformList_acceptCount_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+          3 * (acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hyes a ha
+      linarith
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [uniformList_rejectCount_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+          3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool =>
+            V (a, List.ofFn r) = false).card : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hno a ha
+      linarith
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    obtain ⟨c, d, evalM, hevalM, hlaw⟩ := hM.exists_seeded_evaluator
+    refine ⟨Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d, fun x => evalM x.1 x.2, hevalM,
+      fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (enc a).length =
+          c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+      rw [hp]
+      have hprob := hyes a ha
+      rw [hlaw a, uniformList_acceptCount_toReal (V := fun x => evalM x.1 x.2),
+        le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+      have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+          3 * (acceptCount (fun x => evalM x.1 x.2) a (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) : ℝ) := by
+        linarith
+      exact_mod_cast h3
+    · have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (enc a).length =
+          c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+      rw [hp]
+      have hprob := hno a ha
+      rw [hlaw a, uniformList_rejectCount_toReal (V := fun x => evalM x.1 x.2),
+        le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+      have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+          3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) → Bool =>
+            evalM a (List.ofFn r) = false).card : ℝ) := by
+        linarith
+      exact_mod_cast h3
+
+/-- **Probabilistic-program characterization of `PromiseRP`**: a promise problem is in `PromiseRP`
+exactly when a uniform strict PPT Boolean program accepts every yes-instance with probability at
+least `1 / 2` and never accepts a no-instance. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn : Q ∈ PromiseRP enc ↔
+    ∃ M : α → ProbComp Bool, IsPPTOn enc encBool M ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, 1 / 2 ≤ Pr[M a]) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, true ∉ (ProbComp.eval (M a)).support := by
+  rw [mem_PromiseRP_iff_tidy]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => (fun w => V (a, w)) <$> BitString.sampleList (p.eval (enc a).length),
+      isPPTOn_sampleList_verifier hV, fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha hmem => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [uniformList_acceptCount_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h : (2 : ℝ) ^ p.eval (enc a).length ≤
+          2 * (acceptCount V a (p.eval (enc a).length) : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hyes a ha
+      linarith
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList,
+        PMF.mem_support_map_iff, BitString.mem_support_uniformList_iff] at hmem
+      obtain ⟨w, hw, hVw⟩ := hmem
+      have := (SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate ⟨hyes, hno⟩).2 a ha w hw
+      rw [this] at hVw
+      exact Bool.noConfusion hVw
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    obtain ⟨c, d, evalM, hevalM, hsupp, hlaw⟩ := hM.exists_total_seeded_evaluator
+    refine ⟨Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d, fun x => evalM x.1 x.2, hevalM,
+      fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha r => ?_⟩
+    · have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (enc a).length =
+          c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+      rw [hp]
+      have hprob := hyes a ha
+      rw [hlaw a _ le_rfl, uniformList_acceptCount_toReal (V := fun x => evalM x.1 x.2),
+        le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+      have h2 : (2 : ℝ) ^ (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+          2 * (acceptCount (fun x => evalM x.1 x.2) a (c * ((enc a).length + 1) ^ d) : ℝ) := by
+        linarith
+      exact_mod_cast h2
+    · rw [← Bool.not_eq_true]
+      intro htrue
+      exact hno a ha (htrue ▸ hsupp a (List.ofFn r))
+
+/-- **Probabilistic-program characterization of `PromiseCoRP`**: a promise problem is in
+`PromiseCoRP` exactly when a uniform strict PPT Boolean program never rejects a yes-instance and
+rejects every no-instance with probability at least `1 / 2`. -/
+theorem mem_PromiseCoRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn : Q ∈ PromiseCoRP enc ↔
+    ∃ M : α → ProbComp Bool, IsPPTOn enc encBool M ∧
+      (∀ a ∈ Q.yes, false ∉ (ProbComp.eval (M a)).support) ∧
+      ∀ a ∈ Q.no, 1 / 2 ≤ (ProbComp.eval (M a) false).toReal := by
+  rw [PromiseCoRP, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => Bool.not <$> M a, hM.map (by fun_prop), fun a ha hmem => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.mem_support_map_iff,
+        Bool.not_eq_false'] at hmem
+      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := hmem
+      exact hno a ha hb
+    · have h : (ProbComp.eval (Bool.not <$> M a) false).toReal = Pr[M a] := by
+        simp [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.map_apply]
+      rw [h]
+      exact hyes a ha
+  · rintro ⟨M, hM, hyes, hno⟩
+    refine ⟨fun a => Bool.not <$> M a, hM.map (by fun_prop), fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha hmem => ?_⟩
+    · have h : Pr[Bool.not <$> M a] = (ProbComp.eval (M a) false).toReal := by
+        simp [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.map_apply]
+      rw [h]
+      exact hno a ha
+    · simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.mem_support_map_iff,
+        Bool.not_eq_true'] at hmem
+      obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := hmem
+      exact hyes a ha hb
+
+theorem PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP : PromiseRP enc ⊆ PromiseBPP enc := by
+  intro Q hQ
+  obtain ⟨p, V, hV, hyes, hno⟩ := mem_PromiseRP_iff_tidy.mp hQ
+  have hk : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) enc encUnary :=
+    (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval p).comp
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encoding_length enc)
+  refine ⟨p + p, orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V,
+    .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_orVerifier hk hV hV), fun a ha => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+  · change 2 * 2 ^ (p + p).eval (enc a).length ≤
+      3 * acceptCount (orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V) a
+        ((p + p).eval (enc a).length)
+    rw [Polynomial.eval_add]
+    generalize hk₀ : p.eval (enc a).length = k
+    have hc := acceptCount_orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V a k
+    simp only [hk₀] at hc ⊢
+    have n₁ := acceptCount_add_acceptCount_not V a k
+    have hhalf : 2 ^ k ≤ 2 * acceptCount V a k := hk₀ ▸ hyes a ha
+    have hrej : 2 * acceptCount (fun x => !V x) a k ≤ 2 ^ k := by omega
+    have hprod : 4 * (acceptCount (fun x => !V x) a k * acceptCount (fun x => !V x) a k) ≤
+        2 ^ (k + k) := by
+      rw [pow_add]
+      nlinarith [Nat.mul_le_mul hrej hrej]
+    omega
+  · rw [Polynomial.eval_add]
+    have hall (r : Fin (p.eval (enc a).length + p.eval (enc a).length) → Bool) :
+        orVerifier (fun a => p.eval (enc a).length) V V (a, List.ofFn r) = false := by
+      simp only [orVerifier, Bool.or_eq_false_iff]
+      have hcert := (SolvesWithOneSidedError.exists_certificate ⟨hyes, hno⟩).2 a ha
+      exact ⟨hcert _ (by simp), hcert _ (by simp)⟩
+    rw [Finset.filter_true_of_mem fun r _ => hall r]
+    simp only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_bool, Fintype.card_fin]
+    omega
+
+theorem PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP : PromiseCoRP enc ⊆ PromiseBPP enc := fun Q hQ => by
+  simpa using compl_mem_PromiseBPP (PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP hQ)
+
+end PromiseProbabilistic
+
+namespace PromiseProblem
+
+variable {α β γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool} {encC : γ ↪ List Bool}

[P2] Reuse the existing support/probability-one equivalence

Pinned Mathlib already has `PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff` and `ENNReal.toReal_eq_one_iff`. I checked the exact proposed equivalence with pinned Lean and warnings as errors using:

```lean
by
  rw [ENNReal.toReal_eq_one_iff, PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff]
  rfl
```

Remove this newly introduced 22-line public duplicate and use those existing facts at its callers. No compatibility alias is needed for a declaration introduced in this unmerged PR.

body:
[P2] Put the reused generic event bound in its shared home

`toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul` is a statement about arbitrary PMFs, events and a restricted-event lower bound, with no promise-problem dependency. It is already reused by composition and both randomized class pullbacks (lines 915, 1062 and 1125). Move this small lemma to the existing `Complexity/Probability/PMF/Event.lean` API and consume it here. Existing Event/Bind and pinned upstream were checked; no equivalent with these restricted-event premises was found. Keep the same premises and proof; no new probability model or hierarchy is needed.
