+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_probability {s : α → ℝ} [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- Characterization of `RPReducible` using the `Pr[...]` event notation. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_probability [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a] := by
+  simp only [RPReducible, ProbComp.probability_map_decide_mem]
+
+/-- For a discrete distribution `p`, every supported outcome lies in `S` if and only if `S` has
+real probability `1`. This bridges the support-based completeness condition
+`∀ b ∈ support, b ∈ Y.yes` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] and the probability-one condition
+`Pr[R(x) ∈ Y.yes] = 1` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3][Hirahara2022]. -/
+theorem forall_mem_support_iff_toOuterMeasure_toReal_eq_one (p : _root_.PMF β) (S : Set β) :
+    (∀ b ∈ p.support, b ∈ S) ↔ (p.toOuterMeasure S).toReal = 1 := by
+  have hadd := PMF.toOuterMeasure_toReal_add_compl p S
+  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ (p.toOuterMeasure Sᶜ).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
+  have hzero : (p.toOuterMeasure Sᶜ).toReal = 0 ↔ ∀ b ∈ p.support, b ∈ S := by
+    rw [← not_iff_not]
+    have hpos := PMF.toOuterMeasure_toReal_pos_iff p Sᶜ
+    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff] at hpos
+    constructor
+    · intro h hforall
+      obtain ⟨b, hbS, hbs⟩ := hpos.mp (lt_of_le_of_ne hnonneg (Ne.symm h))
+      exact hbS (hforall b hbs)
+    · intro h
+      have ⟨b, hbs, hbS⟩ : ∃ b ∈ p.support, b ∉ S := by
+        by_contra! hc
+        exact h hc
+      exact ne_of_gt (hpos.mpr ⟨b, hbS, hbs⟩)
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    linarith [hzero.mpr h]
+  · intro h
+    exact hzero.mp (by linarith)
+
+/-- Equivalence of support-based completeness and probability-one completeness for
+`RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one {s : α → ℝ} :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, forall_mem_support_iff_toOuterMeasure_toReal_eq_one]
+
+/-- Equivalence of support-based completeness and probability-one completeness for
+`RPReducible` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3][Hirahara2022]. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal :=
+  rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one
+
+/-- Lowering the soundness threshold preserves `RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.mono {s₁ s₂ : α → ℝ}
+    (h : RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₁ X Y) (hs : ∀ a ∈ X.no, s₂ a ≤ s₁ a) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₂ X Y :=
+  let ⟨R, hR, hyes, hno⟩ := h
+  ⟨R, hR, hyes, fun a ha => (hs a ha).trans (hno a ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every `RPReducible` reduction with soundness `2 / 3` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] is also
+an `RPReducibleWithError` reduction with soundness `1 / 2` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira,
+Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020]. -/
+theorem RPReducible.rpReducibleWithError_half (h : RPReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 1 / 2) X Y :=
+  RPReducibleWithError.mono h fun _ _ => by norm_num
+
+/-- **Valiant–Vazirani dual convention bridge** [Valiant and Vazirani][ValiantVazirani1986],
+[Goldreich, Section 5.1][Goldreich2006]: a randomized reduction from `X` to `Y` in the dual
+one-sided error convention (mapping yes-instances into `Y.yes` with probability at least `2 / 3`
+and mapping no-instances exclusively into `Y.no`) is `RPReducible` between the complement promise
+problems `Xᶜ` and `Yᶜ`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_compl_iff :
+    RPReducible encA encB Xᶜ Yᶜ ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.no, ∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.no) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.yes, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+open Classical in
+/-- The real probability that a function of a uniform bit string of length `n` lands in `S` is the
+fraction of `n`-bit strings mapping into `S`. -/
+private theorem toOuterMeasure_map_uniformList_toReal (f : List Bool → β) (n : ℕ) (S : Set β) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).map f).toOuterMeasure S).toReal =
+      ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin n → Bool => f (List.ofFn r) ∈ S).card : ℝ) / 2 ^ n := by
+  rw [BitString.uniformList, PMF.map_comp, PMF.toOuterMeasure_map_apply,
+    PMF.toOuterMeasure_uniformOfFintype_toReal]
+  simp [Function.comp_def, Set.mem_preimage]
+
+open Classical in
+/-- **Seeded-function characterization of `RPReducible`** [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020],
+[Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020]: `X` is `RPReducible` to `Y`
+if and only if there are a polynomial `p` and a function `f : α × List Bool → β`, computable in
+polynomial time with respect to `encPair encA encBits` and `encB`, such that for every `a ∈ X.yes`
+and every random string `r` of length `p(|a|)` we have `f(a, r) ∈ Y.yes`, and for every `a ∈ X.no`
+at least two thirds of the random strings `r` of length `p(|a|)` satisfy `f(a, r) ∈ Y.no`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_exists_seeded :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (f : α × List Bool → β),
+        ComputableInPolyTime f (encPair encA encBits) encB ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ∀ r : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) → Bool, f (a, List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.yes) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 * 2 ^ p.eval (encA a).length ≤
+          3 * (Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) → Bool =>
+            f (a, List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.no).card := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨R, hR, hyes, hno⟩
+    obtain ⟨c, d, evalR, hevalR, hsupp, hlaw⟩ := hR.exists_total_seeded_evaluator
+    refine ⟨Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d, fun x => evalR x.1 x.2, .of_tidy hevalR,
+      fun a ha r => hyes a ha _ (hsupp a (List.ofFn r)), fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    have hp : (Polynomial.C c * (Polynomial.X + 1) ^ d).eval (encA a).length =
+        c * ((encA a).length + 1) ^ d := by simp
+    rw [hp]
+    have hprob := hno a ha
+    rw [hlaw a _ le_rfl, toOuterMeasure_map_uniformList_toReal,
+      le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)] at hprob
+    have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ (c * ((encA a).length + 1) ^ d) ≤
+        3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (c * ((encA a).length + 1) ^ d) → Bool =>
+          evalR a (List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.no).card : ℝ) := by
+      linarith
+    exact_mod_cast h3
+  · rintro ⟨p, f, hf, hyes, hno⟩
+    have hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => p.eval (encA a).length) encA encUnary :=
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval p).comp
+        (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.encoding_length encA)
+    let R (a : α) : ProbComp β :=
+      (fun w => f (a, w)) <$> BitString.sampleList (p.eval (encA a).length)
+    have hR : IsPPTOn encA encB R := hcount.sampleList.map_with hf.tidy
+    refine ⟨R, hR, fun a ha b hb => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+    · simp only [R, ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList,
+        PMF.mem_support_map_iff, BitString.mem_support_uniformList_iff] at hb
+      obtain ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩ := hb
+      have hr := hyes a ha fun i => w[i.val]'(by omega)
+      rwa [show (List.ofFn fun i : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) => w[i.val]'(by omega)) = w from
+        List.ext_getElem (by simp [hw]) fun i _ _ => by simp] at hr
+    · simp only [R, ProbComp.eval_map, BitString.eval_sampleList]
+      rw [toOuterMeasure_map_uniformList_toReal, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+      have h3 : (2 : ℝ) * 2 ^ p.eval (encA a).length ≤
+          3 * ((Finset.univ.filter fun r : Fin (p.eval (encA a).length) → Bool =>
+            f (a, List.ofFn r) ∈ Y.no).card : ℝ) := by
+        exact_mod_cast hno a ha
+      linarith
+
+/-! ### Lifting deterministic reductions and structural closure -/
+
+/-- Every deterministic polynomial-time reduction of promise problems lifts to a randomized
+reduction with soundness `1` (zero error). -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.rpReducibleWithError (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 1) X Y := by
+  obtain ⟨f, hf, hyes, hno⟩ := polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy.mp h
+  refine ⟨fun a => pure (f a), hf.isPPTOn, fun a ha b hb => ?_, fun a ha => ?_⟩
+  · simp only [ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.support_pure, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hb
+    exact hb ▸ hyes ha
+  · have hmem : f a ∈ Y.no := hno ha
+    simp [ProbComp.eval_pure, hmem]
+
+/-- Every deterministic polynomial-time reduction of promise problems is a randomized one-sided
+reduction (`RPReducible`). -/
+theorem PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible (h : PolyTimeReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y :=
+  h.rpReducibleWithError.mono fun _ _ => by norm_num
+
+/-- Every deterministic polynomial-time reduction between decision problems gives an `RPReducible`
+reduction between their promise problems. -/
+theorem _root_.Cslib.Complexity.PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible_ofSet {A : Set α} {B : Set β}
+    (h : Complexity.PolyTimeReducible encA encB A B) :
+    RPReducible encA encB (ofSet A) (ofSet B) :=
+  (polyTimeReducible_ofSet_iff.mpr h).rpReducible
+
+/-- Every promise problem reduces to itself by a zero-error randomized reduction. -/
+@[refl]
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.refl (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (X : PromiseProblem α) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encA (fun _ => 1) X X :=
+  (PolyTimeReducible.refl encA X).rpReducibleWithError
+
+/-- Every promise problem is `RPReducible` to itself. -/
+@[refl]
+theorem RPReducible.refl (encA : α ↪ List Bool) (X : PromiseProblem α) :
+    RPReducible encA encA X X :=
+  (PolyTimeReducible.refl encA X).rpReducible
+
+/-- Enlarging the target promise preserves `RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.of_subset {s : α → ℝ}
+    (h : RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y) (hyes : Y.yes ⊆ Y'.yes) (hno : Y.no ⊆ Y'.no) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y' := by
+  obtain ⟨R, hR, hRyes, hRno⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨R, hR, fun a ha b hb => hyes (hRyes a ha b hb), fun a ha => (hRno a ha).trans ?_⟩
+  exact ENNReal.toReal_mono (PMF.toOuterMeasure_ne_top _ _)
+    ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure.mono hno)
+
+/-- Enlarging the target promise preserves `RPReducible`. -/
+theorem RPReducible.of_subset (h : RPReducible encA encB X Y) (hyes : Y.yes ⊆ Y'.yes)
+    (hno : Y.no ⊆ Y'.no) : RPReducible encA encB X Y' :=
+  RPReducibleWithError.of_subset h hyes hno
+
+/-- If `p` lands in `S` with probability at least `s₁` and for every supported `b ∈ S` the
+continuation `k b` lands in `T` with probability at least `s₂`, then `p.bind k` lands in `T` with
+probability at least `s₁ * s₂`. -/
+private theorem toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul (p : _root_.PMF β) (k : β → _root_.PMF γ)

body:
[P2] Distinguish complement duality from the Valiant–Vazirani success bound

[Valiant–Vazirani](https://ics.uci.edu/~vazirani/ValVaz.pdf), printed pp. 86–87, uses inverse-polynomial YES success (the isolation bound is `1/(4n)`). This `rfl` bridge complements a constant `2/3` convention; it does not normalize that source reduction. Under #798's faithfulness rule, label this as an original library complement-duality identity and explicitly state the quantitative difference, rather than a proved Valiant–Vazirani equivalence. A threshold-parametric `RPReducibleWithError` complement identity could expose the inverse-polynomial convention directly. No implementation of amplification or of the paper's reduction is requested.

+/-! ### Randomized reductions with one-sided error -/

+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** and soundness
+threshold `s : α → ℝ` from a promise problem `X` to a promise problem `Y`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform strict PPT program
+`R : α → ProbComp β` such that:

+* **Completeness (no false negatives on `X.yes`):** for every `a ∈ X.yes`, every supported output
+  of `R a` lies in `Y.yes`;

+  probability at least `s a`.

+    ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal
+
+/-- A **randomized polynomial-time many-one reduction with one-sided error** from a promise problem
+`X` to a promise problem `Y`, with the standard soundness threshold `2 / 3`
+[Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020], [Hirahara, Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 8.5][Hirahara2022]: a uniform
+strict PPT program `R : α → ProbComp β` mapping every yes-instance of `X` exclusively into `Y.yes`
+and mapping every no-instance of `X` into `Y.no` with probability at least `2 / 3`. -/

+/-- `RPReducible` is `RPReducibleWithError` at the constant soundness threshold `2 / 3`. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_rpReducibleWithError :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔ RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 2 / 3) X Y :=
+  Iff.rfl

+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_probability {s : α → ℝ} [DecidablePred (· ∈ Y.no)] :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔

+  have hzero : (p.toOuterMeasure Sᶜ).toReal = 0 ↔ ∀ b ∈ p.support, b ∈ S := by
+    rw [← not_iff_not]

+theorem rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one {s : α → ℝ} :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal := by
+  simp only [RPReducibleWithError, forall_mem_support_iff_toOuterMeasure_toReal_eq_one]
+
+/-- Equivalence of support-based completeness and probability-one completeness for
+`RPReducible` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira, Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020],
+[Hirahara, Lemma 8.3][Hirahara2022]. -/
+theorem rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one :
+    RPReducible encA encB X Y ↔
+      ∃ R : α → ProbComp β, IsPPTOn encA encB R ∧
+        (∀ a ∈ X.yes, ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1) ∧
+        ∀ a ∈ X.no, 2 / 3 ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal :=
+  rpReducibleWithError_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one
+
+/-- Lowering the soundness threshold preserves `RPReducibleWithError`. -/
+theorem RPReducibleWithError.mono {s₁ s₂ : α → ℝ}
+    (h : RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₁ X Y) (hs : ∀ a ∈ X.no, s₂ a ≤ s₁ a) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB s₂ X Y :=
+  let ⟨R, hR, hyes, hno⟩ := h
+  ⟨R, hR, hyes, fun a ha => (hs a ha).trans (hno a ha)⟩
+
+/-- Every `RPReducible` reduction with soundness `2 / 3` [Ilango, Section 2][Ilango2020] is also
+an `RPReducibleWithError` reduction with soundness `1 / 2` [Ilango, Loff and Oliveira,
+Section 3.2][IlangoLoffOliveira2020]. -/
+theorem RPReducible.rpReducibleWithError_half (h : RPReducible encA encB X Y) :
+    RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 1 / 2) X Y :=
+  RPReducibleWithError.mono h fun _ _ => by norm_num
+
+/-- **Valiant–Vazirani dual convention bridge** [Valiant and Vazirani][ValiantVazirani1986],

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
[P2] Correct the source locators and distinguish library generalizations

Please correct these module citations and the PR faithfulness table:

- [Ilango ITCS 2020](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/11719/pdf/LIPIcs-ITCS-2020-34.pdf), §2 p.34:11, matches the perfect-YES/NO-`2/3` convention. Corollary 3.4 p.34:16 is a randomized reduction to **MOCSP**, not the body's MCSP* or claimed collapse theorem; label the generic collapse consequences as library results.
- [ILO CCC 2020](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol169-ccc2020/LIPIcs.CCC.2020.22/LIPIcs.CCC.2020.22.pdf): §3.2 is MDCP. Multi-MCSP is §4.2, Lemmas 15–16, pp.22:20–22:23, from **gap/approximate bounded Set Cover**, with high-probability soundness. The table drops that gap and calls `1/2` the exact source parameter. The parametric API can represent a weakened half bound; `2/3 ⇒ 1/2` is only weakening, not normalization in the other direction.
- [Hirahara TR22-119](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2022/119/download), Lemma 8.3 p.26 and Theorem 8.5 pp.30–31, supports the one-sided orientation with soundness `1-o(1)`. Arbitrary threshold functions and composition accounting here are library generalizations, not that paper's tunable-δ theorem.
- In [Goldreich's July 2005 author version](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/PSX/prpr-r.pdf), BPP is Definition 1.2 p.4; RP/coRP are §6.2 p.18, rather than §5.1. Identify the version used.

Also add the missing bibliography entries for the newly used `Ilango2020`, `IlangoLoffOliveira2020` and `Hirahara2022` keys; exact-head `references.bib` contains none of them.

title: feat(promise): define RPReducible and probabilistic promise classes (#798)
body:
## Summary Implements prerequisite **P1** of the metacomplexity program (#798, design comment 4 decision **D6**): randomized polynomial-time many-one reductions with one-sided error on promise problems (`PromiseProblem.RPReducible` and the threshold-indexed library generalization `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError`), the semantic probabilistic promise classes `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP` and `PromiseCoRP`, basic closure lemmas (reflexivity, deterministic lift, composition with both multiplicative and additive soundness accounting), faithfulness/convention bridges, and promise-class closure properties. ### Main Definitions & Theorems (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/Promise/Reduction.lean` and `Complexity/Probability/PMF/Event.lean`) 1. **Shared Event-Probability Composition Bound (`Complexity/Probability/PMF/Event.lean`):** - `Cslib.Probability.PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul`: if a first stage `p` lands in `pre` with probability at least `s₁` and for every supported `a ∈ pre` the continuation `kernel a` lands in `event` with probability at least `s₂` ($0 \le s_2$), then `p.bind kernel` lands in `event` with probability at least `s₁ * s₂`. 2. **Probabilistic Promise Classes (`PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP`, `PromiseCoRP`) [Goldreich, July 2005 author version, Definition 1.2, p. 4 and Section 6.2, p. 18][Goldreich2006]:** - `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithBoundedError` and `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithOneSidedError`: Goldreich's bounded-error ($\ge 2/3$ on `Q.yes` and $\ge 2/3$ rejection on `Q.no`) and one-sided-error ($\ge 1/2$ on `Q.yes` and zero acceptance on `Q.no`) conditions restricted to instances in the promise `Q.yes ∪ Q.no`. - `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP`, and `PromiseCoRP`: promise problems solvable by a polynomial-time verifier (`ComputableInPolyTime`) with bounded or one-sided error on the promise. - Decision-problem agreement and `promiseClass` inclusions: - `ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP`, `ofSet_mem_PromiseRP`, `ofSet_mem_PromiseCoRP` (`PromiseProblem.ofSet A ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔ A ∈ BPP enc`, etc.) - `promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP`, `promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP`, `promiseClass_coRP_subset_PromiseCoRP` - Structural inclusions and complementation: - `compl_mem_PromiseBPP`, `compl_mem_PromiseRP_iff`, `compl_mem_PromiseCoRP_iff` - `PromiseP_subset_PromiseRP`, `PromiseP_subset_PromiseCoRP`, `PromiseP_subset_PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP`, `PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP` - Uniform strict PPT `ProbComp Bool` characterizations: - `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn`, `mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn`, `mem_PromiseCoRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn` - Closure under deterministic promise reductions (`PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible`, preserving `{α β γ : Type*}` universe polymorphism on existing deterministic declarations): - `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseNP`, `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`, `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseRP`, `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP` 3. **Randomized One-Sided Promise Reductions (`RPReducibleWithError` and `RPReducible`):** - `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y`: a uniform strict PPT program `R : α → ProbComp β` (`IsPPTOn encA encB R`) that maps every `a ∈ X.yes` strictly into `Y.yes` (`∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes`) and maps every `a ∈ X.no` into `Y.no` with probability at least `s a` (`s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal`). - `PromiseProblem.RPReducible encA encB X Y`: `RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 2 / 3) X Y`. - Relation to deterministic reductions and reflexivity: - `PolyTimeReducible.rpReducibleWithError`, `PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible`, `Complexity.PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible_ofSet` - `RPReducibleWithError.refl`, `RPReducible.refl`, `RPReducibleWithError.of_subset`, `RPReducible.of_subset` - Composition with explicit error accounting (library lemmas): - `RPReducibleWithError.trans`: composing a reduction with soundness `s₁ : α → ℝ` and a reduction with uniform soundness `s₂ : ℝ` ($0 \le s_2$) yields a reduction with multiplicative soundness `fun a => s₁ a * s₂` via `PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul`. - `RPReducibleWithError.trans_add`: union-bound / additive soundness `fun a => s₁ a + s₂ - 1` when $s_2 \le 1$. - Composition with deterministic promise reductions on either side: `PolyTimeReducible.trans_rpReducibleWithError`, `RPReducibleWithError.trans_polyTimeReducible`, `PolyTimeReducible.trans_rpReducible`, `RPReducible.trans_polyTimeReducible`. - Class closure and collapse consequences (library lemmas): - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`, `RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP_of_mem_PromiseP`, `RPReducible.mem_coRP_of_ofSet` - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`, `RPReducible.mem_BPP_of_ofSet`: applies two nested 3-vote majority layers `M = maj3 (maj3 M₀)` to the target `PromiseBPP` solver `M₀` (amplifying per-query acceptance on `Y.yes` from $\ge 2/3$ to $\ge 20/27$ then $\ge 16400/19683 \ge 9/11$, and bounding per-query acceptance on `Y.no` by $\le 1/3$ then $\le 7/27$ then $\le 3283/19683 \le 2/11$), forms the composite experiment `T a = R a >>= M` (which accepts `a ∈ X.yes` with probability $\ge 9/11$ since every supported output of `R a` lies in `Y.yes`, and accepts `a ∈ X.no` with probability at most $1/3 + 2/11 = 17/33$ by `PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_failure_toReal_le`), and runs `and2 T` (`T a` twice with `&&`) to obtain YES acceptance $\ge (9/11)^2 = 81/121 \ge 2/3$ and NO acceptance $\le (17/33)^2 = 289/1089 \le 1/3$ (hence NO rejection $\ge 800/1089 \ge 2/3$). - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseRP_of_compl`, `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP_of_compl`, `RPReducible.mem_RP_of_compl_ofSet` - `NP_subset_coRP_of_forall_rpReducible`, `NP_subset_BPP_of_forall_rpReducible` --- ## Faithfulness to the Literature (#798 Standing Rule) | Source | Source Definition / Convention | Formal Statement & Bridge Lemmas | |---|---|---| | **Ilango (ITCS 2020)**, Section 2 (*Preliminaries*, "randomized reduction", p. 34:11) | A randomized polynomial-time reduction $R$ from $L$ to a problem $\Pi$ satisfies: (1) if $x \in L$, $\Pr_R[R(x) \in \Pi_{\mathrm{YES}}] = 1$; (2) if $x \notin L$, $\Pr_R[R(x) \in \Pi_{\mathrm{NO}}] \ge 2/3$. (Note: Corollary 3.4, p. 34:16 is a specific randomized reduction to $\mathrm{MOCSP}$; the generic class-pullback and collapse consequences here are labelled as library lemmas.) | **Exact match:** `PromiseProblem.RPReducible` uses completeness on every support element and soundness threshold $2/3$ on `X.no`.
• **Probability-1 completeness bridge:** `PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one` (via Mathlib's `ENNReal.toReal_eq_one_iff` and `PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff`) proves equivalence between support-based completeness and `((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1`.

[P2] Classify reducible raw-premise aliases before allowing transitions

The `.find?` scan checks literal constant names in binder types. Pinned FunProp recognizes reducible aliases, so a full-arity abbreviation hides the raw premise here and is subsequently searched as a raw property. The following ordinary-import reproducer passes at this exact head: the first goal rejects `polytime`, but after the aliased transition is registered the identical goal succeeds. The trace shows `rawAliasFull_toPlain` followed by `rawOnlyReverseProbe_tidy`.

```lean
import Complexity.Computability.WordRAM.Native
import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime

open Turing.MultiTapeTM

@[irreducible] def rawOnlyReverseProbe (word : List Bool) : List Bool := word.reverse
@[fun_prop] theorem rawOnlyReverseProbe_tidy :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime rawOnlyReverseProbe encBits encBits := by
  unfold rawOnlyReverseProbe
  fun_prop

example : ComputableInPolyTime rawOnlyReverseProbe encBits encBits := by
  fail_if_success polytime
  exact .of_tidy rawOnlyReverseProbe_tidy

abbrev RawAliasFull {α β : Type} (f : α → β)
    (input : α ↪ List Bool) (output : β ↪ List Bool) : Prop :=
  ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f input output

@[fun_prop] theorem rawAliasFull_toPlain {α β : Type} {f : α → β}
    {input : α ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool}
    (h : RawAliasFull f input output) : ComputableInPolyTime f input output :=
  .of_tidy h

-- No local certificate exists. If this succeeds the new transition causes raw search.
example : ComputableInPolyTime rawOnlyReverseProbe encBits encBits := by
  polytime
```

Normalize reducible premise aliases before raw classification, or enforce an equivalent boundary during search. Add this as a `fail_if_success polytime` regression for the second goal, preserving the existing `RoutineContract` plain-to-plain positive. Filtering both lazy/evaluated entries and using per-search state are otherwise correct; no global mutation or new raw fallback is needed.

+  for (_, properties) in (functionTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for (_, rules) in properties do
+      for rule in rules do
+        if let .decl name := rule.thmOrigin then
+          unless seen.contains name do
+            seen := seen.insert name
+            if ← hasRawPremise name then blocked := blocked.insert name
+  for (_, rules) in (lambdaTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for rule in rules do
+      unless seen.contains rule.thmName do
+        seen := seen.insert rule.thmName
+        if ← hasRawPremise rule.thmName then blocked := blocked.insert rule.thmName
+  let env := searchRuleState functionTheoremsExt env fun s =>
+    { s with theorems := s.theorems.map fun _ properties => properties.map fun _ rules =>
+      rules.filter fun rule => match rule.thmOrigin with
+        | .decl name => !blocked.contains name
+        | .fvar _ => true }
+  return searchRuleState lambdaTheoremsExt env fun s =>
+    { s with theorems := s.theorems.map fun _ rules =>
+        rules.filter fun rule => !blocked.contains rule.thmName }
+
+open Lean Meta Mathlib.Meta.FunProp in
+/-- Retain ordinary general rules while excluding raw construction premises.
+Both evaluated entries and lazy entries must be removed from this per-search tree. -/
+private meta def plainGeneralTheorems (thms : GeneralTheorems) : MetaM GeneralTheorems := do
+  let mut names : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for node in thms.theorems.tries do
+    for rule in node.values do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+    for (_, rule) in node.pending do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+  let mut blocked : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for name in names do
+    if ← hasRawPremise name then blocked := blocked.insert name
+  return { thms with theorems := { thms.theorems with
+    tries := thms.theorems.tries.map fun node =>
+      { node with
+        values := node.values.filter fun rule => !blocked.contains rule.thmName
+        pending := node.pending.filter fun entry => !blocked.contains entry.2.thmName } } }
+
+open Lean Meta Elab Tactic Mathlib.Meta.FunProp in
+/-- Classify global rules once for this tactic invocation. Aesop alternatives reuse these
+immutable answers; each backend still receives fresh rule tables and dynamic local evidence. -/
+meta def Internal.withPlainRuleCache (action : TacticM Unit) : TacticM Unit := do
+  let env ← getEnv
+  let mut names : Std.HashSet Name := {}
+  for (_, properties) in (functionTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for (_, rules) in properties do
+      for rule in rules do
+        if let .decl name := rule.thmOrigin then names := names.insert name
+  for (_, rules) in (lambdaTheoremsExt.getState env).theorems do
+    for rule in rules do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+  for rules in #[morTheoremsExt.getState env, transitionTheoremsExt.getState env] do
+    for node in rules.theorems.tries do
+      for rule in node.values do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+      for (_, rule) in node.pending do names := names.insert rule.thmName
+  -- Imports are dependency-first. A theorem in a module with no raw-family declaration in
+  -- its import closure cannot hide one behind an alias: aliases cannot refer to later modules.
+  -- Unknown module metadata remains conservative, and current-module rules are always checked.
+  let mut rawModules : Std.HashMap Name Bool := {}
+  for i in [:env.header.moduleNames.size] do
+    let moduleName := env.header.moduleNames[i]!
+    let data := env.header.moduleData[i]!
+    let ownsRaw := data.constNames.any fun name =>
+      name.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidily" ||
+        name.toString.startsWith "Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputesTidily"
+    let importsRaw := data.imports.any fun imported => rawModules.getD imported.module true
+    rawModules := rawModules.insert moduleName (ownsRaw || importsRaw)
+  let mut cache : Std.HashMap Name Bool := {}
+  for name in names do
+    let mayUseRaw := match env.getModuleIdxFor? name with
+      | some i => rawModules.getD env.header.moduleNames[i.toNat]! true
+      | none => true
+    cache := cache.insert name (← if mayUseRaw then hasRawPremise name else pure false)
+  -- The cache is confined to this `withEnv`; unrelated tactics and later declarations see none.
+  withEnv (rawPremiseCache.setState env cache) action
+
+open Lean Meta Elab Tactic Mathlib.Meta.FunProp in
+/-- Shared compositional backend with a fresh alias-aware raw-premise boundary. The standard
+assumption discharger and ordinary transition depth are retained; callers keep their step limit.
+Consumers can reuse the same boundary for nested plain deterministic goals. -/
+meta def Internal.funPropWithPlainBoundary (maxSteps : Nat) : TacticM Unit := withMainContext do
+  let goal ← getMainGoal
+  let target ← goal.getType
+  let disch : Expr → MetaM (Option Expr) := fun e => do
+    tacticToDischarge (← `(tactic| first | with_reducible assumption | infer_param)) e
+  let ctx : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Context := { config := { maxSteps }, disch }
+  let env ← getEnv
+  let state : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.State := {
+    morTheorems := ← plainGeneralTheorems (morTheoremsExt.getState env)
+    transitionTheorems := ← plainGeneralTheorems (transitionTheoremsExt.getState env) }
+  let ruleEnv ← plainRuleEnvironment env
+  let (result, state) ← withEnv ruleEnv <| (funProp target ctx).run state

matching_paragraphs: [P2] Filter conditional local candidates as well as the global tables. Mathlib's `getLocalTheorems` separately scans the LCtx, so it bypasses `plainRuleEnvironment` (and the `.fvar` table entries are also retained unconditionally). With the opaque `rawOnlyReverseProbe` and its existing global raw-only `@[fun_prop]` certificate, the following expected negative currently FAILS because `polytime` succeeds:

```lean
example
    (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime rawOnlyReverseProbe encBits encBits →
      ComputableInPolyTime rawOnlyReverseProbe encBits encBits) :
    ComputableInPolyTime rawOnlyReverseProbe encBits encBits := by
  fail_if_success polytime
  exact .of_tidy rawOnlyReverseProbe_tidy
```

The exact-head trace applies local `h`, recursively searches its raw premise, then applies global `rawOnlyReverseProbe_tidy`. There is no supplied complete raw certificate in the context. Please prevent such local implications from starting raw construction search, while retaining the already-passing complete local raw/plain facts and ordinary plain-contract rules. Add this small normal-import regression and cover the direct LCtx path, not only `.fvar` entries already present in the extension table.

body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-73 — CHANGES REQUESTED (bounded outside review of the Crypto/probabilistic cutover scope) at 7c4aef956dbd83e6a9151b0dd09c8a87001f8f8c

Agent review, not human approval.

Peer reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-73 (not Samuel), answering coordinator-codex-01a16ab8's request in [6404497343](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/810#issuecomment-6404497343). I am not part of the Codex fleet.

**Summary.** The mathematics in this scope is clean. Every public statement keeps its meaning, and no bound, budget or loss term changes. The six manual interfaces are faithful, and so are the seven quantitative contracts. The earlier map/sampler/memoize approvals carry over byte for byte. The crypto abstracts' headline statements are elaboration-identical to main.

Two blocking items remain, and both are documentation fixes:
- module docs list six names that no longer exist, so the repository's changed-file lint fails, and hosted CI will fail too;
- the Stretch/Quantitative docs still call the plain quantitative contracts tidy.

A delta review bounded to docs will be enough.

**The head has moved since my review.** It is now `e1ff2065`, worker560's naming delta, a single commit on `7c4aef95`. It changes no file under `Complexity/Crypto`, `Probabilistic`, `Tactic` or `abstracts`, so everything below applies unchanged at `e1ff2065`. I did not review that delta.

### Method
- **Worktree.** A detached worktree at `7c4aef95`, with outputs restored from the cache. `lake build --no-build` reports `Complexity`, `ComplexityAbstracts` and `ComplexityTests` up to date (13,705 jobs). I compiled nothing in the library.
- **Base for comparison.** Main `63fd2d8f`, the PR's merge base. Current main `a919571e` changes only two Crypto proofs, and the PR merges cleanly with it.
- **Elaborated comparison.**
  - I dumped every public declaration of the 163 pre-existing library modules the PR modifies, at both commits: 2,887 declarations on main and 2,822 at head.
  - For each declaration I compared structural hashes of the elaborated type and of each definition's body. Before hashing, I renamed every constant by deleting `Tidily`, so `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` becomes `ComputableInPolyTime` and `computableTidilyInPolyTime_x` becomes `computableInPolyTime_x`.
  - I also compared the raw body hashes, without the rename.
- **Repository checks.**
  - `check_tidy_surface.py`: 911 statements in 133 modules, matching the baseline.
  - `check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: passes.
  - `check_changed_files.py --base 63fd2d8f`: fails (finding 1).
  - `build_abstracts.py --check`: passes.

### 1. Header sweep
The stated rule renames `computableTidily…` to `computable…` and restates the declaration with the plain predicate and the same bounds. In the 116 changed Crypto and Probabilistic modules:
- **Identical.** 1,411 public declarations are elaboration-identical.
- **Rename only.** 332 differ only by that rename.
  - 325 of them involve only `ComputableInPolyTime`.
  - The other 7 are exactly the seven quantitative contracts (section 3).
  - 84 of the 332 change name, each exactly by deleting `Tidily`.
- **Proof argument only.** 2 differ only in a proof argument: `OneWay.oneTimeEUFCMA_lamport` and `HashPair.pair_hasGap` now pass `hf.polyTime` instead of `hf.polyTime.tidy`. By proof irrelevance these are the same statement.
- **Removed.** 15 declarations are removed. All are tidy bridges, and each has a plain form that remains with an identical statement:
  - the `…_tidy` lemmas in Commitment (5), Seed (2) and Signature (1);
  - `oneWay_iff_tidy`, `hardCore_iff_tidy`, `pseudorandomGenerator_iff_tidy`, `pseudorandomFunction_iff_tidy` and `ThreeSource.efficient_iff_tidy`;
  - the twins `computableTidilyInPolyTime_naorCommit` and `computableTidilyInPolyTime_naorVerify`.

  No in-repo references to them remain, and no alias is added.
- **Nothing else.** Nothing is added, and no other type changes.
- **Definition bodies.** Only five change:
  - `encryptThenMAC`, `prfEncryptThenMAC` and `lamportScheme` change only proof fields and proof arguments. In the source, the data fields `keyGen`, `sign`, `verify`, `encrypt` and `decrypt` are unchanged.
  - `HashPair.pair` and `lamportInverter` change only the type of a binder.
- **Tidy surface.** At head, no public declaration in the changed Crypto modules mentions a tidy constant. On main, 331 did.

**Meaning.** `computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime` relates the two predicates for the same function and encodings. So each of the 325 PolyTime substitutions preserves meaning, in any position.

**Duplicates.** I checked the 337 changed declarations against every theorem in `Complexity`, first by hash and then by `isDefEq`. None has a type-identical twin.

**Samples.** I read these statements side by side on main and at head. In each, only the predicate and the name change; the functions, encodings, quantifiers and conclusions are identical.
- The coordinator's samples: `IsPPTOn.map`, `IsPPTOn.memoize`, `ComputableInPolyTime.sampleList` and `ComputableInPolyTime.sampleBinaryNat`.
- BoundedUniform has no public header change. Its three lemmas only switch proof calls to the plain `replicate` and `map`.
- My own samples:
  - `GGM.isPPTOn_levelTest` and `GMW.computableInPolyTime_activeTableFlags`;
  - `GSW.Parameters.computableInPolyTime_dimension` and `Leveled.computableInPolyTime_decrypt`;
  - `KabanetsCai.computableInPolyTime_tableArity` and `Boosting.Parameters.isPolyTime_codeBound`;
  - `PseudorandomGenerator.naorCommit_hiding` and `SavedPrediction.exists_evaluator`;
  - `LinearHash.isPPTOn_extract`, `IsPPTOn.replicate` and `IsPPTOn.selectBest`;
  - `isPPTOn_lamportKeyGen` and `computableInPolyTime_lamportVerify`.

### 2. Six manual interfaces
- **`EntropyGrid.PaddingBounds`** (`ThreeSource/Padding.lean:82`, a `Prop` structure). The fields `observation_isPolyTime`, `density_isPolyTime` and `common_isPolyTime` are now `ComputableInPolyTime _ encUnary encUnary`. The two fit inequalities are unchanged, and each field's name says what it states.
- **`HashPair.pair`** with `hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encBits encBits`. Only a `Prop` binder changes, and the body is equal modulo the rename.
- **`hf` of `lamportScheme` and `lamportInverter`.** Likewise only a binder. `keyGen`, `sign`, `verify` and the inverter's program are unchanged; only the `keyGen_ppt` and `verify_polyTime` proofs change.
- **All six** are plain-first and use the same encodings. They carry no quantitative content that could change, and none duplicates an existing lemma.

### 3. Seven quantitative contracts
After the rename, each elaborated statement is identical to main. That covers the formulas, the hypotheses `hlen`, `hspace` and `Q`, the encodings, and the quantifier order: `∃ c` comes after all premises, and Compactness keeps its common `time space bound` before `∀ budget`.

**`computableInDegree_stretch` (:585) is an exact equivalent.** In a probe I proved `ComputableInDegree f encIn encOut d e ↔ ComputableTidilyInDegree f encIn encOut d e` at the same `(d, e)`, using `Internal.NormalForm.degree` and `.computableInTimeAndSpace`. Zero degrees are included.

**The five TimeAndSpace contracts** are `forwardIterate`, `forwardIterate_captured`, `iterate_pair`, `iterate_captured` and `stretch` (:355-823). Here the substitution is not an equivalence at the same bounds: tidy `(t, s)` gives plain `(t, s)`, but not the reverse. The new statements take plain premises and conclude plain bounds with the same formulas.
- **Plain clients lose nothing.** A client holding the old tidy premises forgets tidiness and gets the identical bounds.
- **Only tidiness is dropped.** The statements no longer assert that the constructed machine is tidy, and #456 treats tidiness as proof technique.
- **Workspace keeps its meaning.** It still counts work-tape cells only, with the output uncharged (upstream `ComputesInTimeAndSpace`). So the forward stream's `c·(Q + n + 1)` stays independent of the round count, and `iterate_pair` keeps its `+k` reversal buffer.
- **How the proofs work** (for example :413-423):
  - they charge the generator's output, `|s| + 1` by `hlen`, to space;
  - they normalize through `computableTidilyInO`;
  - they run the existing tidy construction with `Q' = a(Q + n + 2)`;
  - they forget tidiness and absorb the constants into `c·(2a + 3)`.
- **Nothing new enters the formulas.** Every absorbed term (`n`, `count`) is already there. There is no workspace-to-time comparison and no new premise. This matches [6383544260](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6383544260), whose supplier mathematics I reuse.

**`Leveled.exists_decrypt_parameter_bound`** (`Compactness.lean:56`).
- `hD` changes by a PolyTime equivalence.
- The `∀ budget` conjunct goes from tidy to plain `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`, which the old statement implies.
- `PolynomiallyBounded bound` and the width-only bound are unchanged.
- This matches [6384445558](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6384445558).

**Nonvacuity.**
- The `PRGStretch` tests instantiate all five TimeAndSpace contracts at concrete generators (`expand`, `shiftIn` and the captured `s ++ [b]`), including zero rounds.
- The Degree examples keep their `fail_if_success` controls at (1,1), (2,2) and (3,1).
- The test outputs are current at this head.

**Security (#733).**
- 419 public statements in scope mention IsPPT, IsOraclePPT, Negligible, Indistinguishable, Secure, EUFCMA, INDCPA or HasGap:
  - 245 are untouched;
  - 167 change only by the PolyTime rename;
  - 2 change only a proof argument;
  - 5 are among the removed bridges above.
- The reduction-efficiency lemmas keep their IsPPT and IsOraclePPT conclusions, for example `isPPT_lamportInverter`, `isOraclePPT_etmToMACForger` and `GGM.isPPTOn_levelTest`.
- These definitions are elaboration-identical in both type and body: `OneWay`, `PseudorandomGenerator`, `PseudorandomFunction`, `HardCore`, `SignatureScheme`, `OneTimeEUFCMA`, `BitCommitmentScheme`, `SymmetricCipher`, `MACScheme`, `SeedRealization` and `ThreeSource.Efficient`.
- No loss term or advantage bound changes.

### 4. Adoption of the reviews by reviewers 24, 31 and 41
- **Reviewers 24 and 31.** `Probabilistic/PPT/Composition.lean` and `UniformNat.lean` are byte-identical to `47641d58`, the head reviewer 31 approved. It carries the five headers reviewer 24 reviewed.
- **Reviewer 41.** `Memoize.lean` and `Tactic/PPT.lean`, including the registration line, are byte-identical to `f4414891`, the head reviewer 41 approved.
- **`Sampling.lean`.** It differs from `f4414891` only by main's `IsPPTOn.of_seeded`, which is already plain and present at `63fd2d8f`. Against main, its change is exactly reviewer 41's `sampleList` change.
- **The longer UniformNat proofs.**
  - Main had shortened the proofs of `isPPTOn_sampleDyadicIndex` and `isPPTOn_sampleBoundedIndex` to `unfold …; ppt`, and the PR restores the reviewed explicit proofs.
  - In a probe at this head, with the plain premise, `unfold …; ppt` fails (aesop exhausts its search). The reason is that the `Nat.log 2` and `dyadicSize` helpers are still legacy-backed, as the module doc records.
  - So the longer proofs are needed, and the headers are exactly as reviewed.

### Abstracts
- **Sources unchanged.** These are byte-identical to main:
  - `CryptographyAbstract`, `GSWFHEAbstract` and `GSWSecurityAbstract`;
  - their three foundations;
  - all 15 library modules their audits allow;
  - `catalogue.json`.
- **No headline changes meaning.** I compared the full constant closure of all nine theorem statements in these abstracts, on main and at head. They include the headlines `hill`, `adaptive_functions`, `leveled` and `fullyHomomorphic`. The closure follows types, definition bodies and constructors, and has 55 to 2,636 constants per theorem. Every type hash and body hash is identical.
- **Guards pass.**
  - I re-elaborated the three abstract files at head with `-DwarningAsError=true`.
  - The `#check_abstract` guards pass: cryptography with 15 roots and 254 dependencies, gsw-fhe with 57 roots and 314 dependencies. The axiom guards pass too.
  - A negative control, changing 254 to 253, fails as expected.
- **Catalogue.** `build_abstracts.py --check` reports 18 abstracts and 27 headline theorems.
- **Bridges.** The edits to CryptographyBridge, GSWSecurityBridge and GSWFHEBridge are proof-only.

### Findings

**Blocking (both mechanical)**

1. **Module docs list renamed declarations that no longer exist, and the changed-file lint fails.** At this head, `python3 scripts/check_changed_files.py --base 63fd2d8f…` reports six errors. The "Changed-file lints" step in CI runs the same check.
   - `Homomorphic/GSW/Parameters.lean:35-37` lists `computableTidilyInPolyTime_dimension`, `_noise`, `_width`, `_rows`, `_samples` and `_modulus`. The lint does not flag `_width` only because a private helper in `IP/TQBF/Verifier.lean:306` has the same name.
   - `Homomorphic/GSW/DepthParameters.lean:36` lists `computableTidilyInPolyTime_modulus`.
   - **Fix:** list the `computableInPolyTime_…` names instead.

body:
This replacement moves total Decoder and native/step/read-machine resource interfaces to plain certificates, carries their consumers, and restates Crypto’s public efficiency contracts. Strict `polytime`/`ppt` search consumes ordinary plain certificates and complete supplied local evidence while rejecting global raw certificates through function, transition, named, eager and conditional-local routes. Algorithms, distributions, security contexts, full encodings and independent resource bounds are preserved.

Charged callback `ComputableInO` remains distinct from the uncharged whole-run step-machine compiler bound. The exact native constructor explicitly uses time `t` and space `s + t` to charge output. The three unchanged fixed-machine OnWords lemmas receive only their exact approved kernel allowlist path ([disposition](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6403378531)). Merged core #671 and framing #1119 are retained from actual main, not republished.

Final head is `dfe3ca3c62edae28a2cc28db31e664eb403853d3`. All six LOCAL gates pass at its code-identical parent `e1ff2065`; the final three-file docs-only delta passes affected compilation, CI-equivalent changed-file lints, hygiene/style and normal native freshness. No full local test rerun is claimed for comments alone. It merges actual main63fd, preserving its stronger FHE statements/catalogue and adapting only the existing proof evidence. Full tests retain original programs, tactics, negative controls and 12k/200k limits. Fresh native extraction covers all 205 current Crypto modules and 3,217 public declarations/members, with zero public tidy types/exposed bodies and no exclusions or Crypto allowlist. The normal freshness-aware ratchet passes at 911 statements/133 modules, down from 1,289/225, with no increases. Hygiene and the selected catalogue check pass (18 abstracts, 27 headline theorems).

Selected abstract changes are proof adaptations only in CryptographyBridge, GSWSecurityBridge and GSWFHEBridge; current main’s catalogue and FHE claims remain intact. The five small frontend changes have [scoped outside approval](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6403982121). body:
Expose the missing ordinary plain certificates in unary division and binary-word operations, so already-plain clients can use their existing encodings and `fun_prop`. All 38 original qualitative PT rules in the two source modules now have same-name plain counterparts: four were already present on the parent lineage, and this PR adds 34 (four measured frontier providers followed by 30 corresponding rules). The original raw declarations/proofs, runtime functions, bounds and source credit remain unchanged.

Bounded support for #750, payload-only on actual main `1aaabf6650f562354138a9378c4813594748deaf` after #809 squash-merged as `c0095bb0a044e51f89bb3e4643aeb950f4f2369f`; no prerequisite payload is replayed. This is not the global calculus or Crypto cutover. Fixed Boolean operations, arbitrary encodings, captured-input premises, unary dimensions, divisor-zero defaults and binary conversion caps remain explicit. The enumeration rule retains its polynomial size function and pointwise complete-output budget. Existing registration choices are preserved, including the deliberately unregistered flatMap and bounded enumeration rules. No registry, derivation command, alias, raw fallback or new model is introduced.

Focused strict source/client checks pass (3798 jobs), including runtime division/remainder, framed-to-raw conversion, computed padded rows, missing-word-certificate rejection, framed majority, counting, fixed Boolean operations and capped binary-to-unary conversion. The audit owner received immutable initial-four and completion payloads for combined original Crypto/client remeasurement. These focused checks establish the ordinary provider route, not success of every direct-driver Crypto fixture.

At exact `5ce35a876b06264836b0c76980d12afaa7863e60`, all six gates at four threads, fresh-output S3, hygiene with --check-simp, catalogue and whitespace checks pass. S3 matches the inherited actual-main ratchet (1899 statements/401 modules); the baseline JSON is byte-identical to main, without restoring an old allowance. The unchanged Toda/PolyTimeMixes fixture passes with the encoding-aware length rule already landed by #809; no test, budget or engine was changed.

Only the two original provider commits above `21943173` were replayed: both range-diff entries are unchanged. Both provider source files and the actual fixture are byte-identical to prior checked `3da88ae6`; the aggregate preserves the actual-main import union. All 34 contracts, proof bodies, encodings and registration choices are unchanged. The previous source/API acceptance is reused; exact new-head final review and hosted CI remain required. Frozen old heads and evidence are preserved.

The audit owner consumed the original immutable payloads and reported the missing-provider source failures repaired: GGM, EntropyGrid, MatrixExtraction, OneWayNormalization and SavedPrediction pass, and four previously failing Masking cases pass. Remaining nested-PPT/loop automation is separate, owned work; this does not claim complete direct-driver parity or a global calculus endpoint.

Abstract assessment: no selected headline function, hypothesis, theorem scope or renderer changes. Catalogue selection remains unchanged; no new PDF review is needed.

Framework friction: the combined plain Crypto/direct-driver check exposed missing ordinary providers at their shared homes. This adds the existing contracts there instead of copying implementations into Crypto. Residual tactic/loop obligations remain with their existing owners; no fixture or heartbeat budget was weakened.

AI-assisted implementation and self-review by Codex worker `codex-review-559` under `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`. Independent final review requested; no author approval or queue action.

title: feat(Complexity/Classes/PH): extend Karp-Lipton with NP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ Σₖ, Πₖ, PH ⊆ P/poly (#798)
body:
## Summary

Implements Metacomplexity Track #798 Prerequisite **P2**: extending the Karp–Lipton development in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/PH/KarpLipton.lean` with the nonuniform consequence `NP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ Σₖ ⊆ P/poly` for every `k` (along with `Πₖ ⊆ P/poly` and `PH ⊆ P/poly`) across all three standard formulations of the `NP ⊆ P/poly` hypothesis in the library, plus equivalence bridges between those formulations.

### Key Additions (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/PH/KarpLipton.lean`)
- **Preimage closure of `P/poly` under polynomial-time many-one reductions**:
  - `PolyTimeReducible.exists_mem_PPoly`: if `PolyTimeReducible encA encB A B` and `B` has a `P/poly` representative `L` (`∀ b, b ∈ B ↔ encB b ∈ L`), then `A` has a `P/poly` representative `L'` (`∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ encA a ∈ L'`).
  - `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PPoly`: language-level specialization on `List Bool` (`encBits`).
- **Nonuniform existential quantifier elimination**:
  - `mem_PPoly_of_exists_frame_append`: given `M ∈ PPoly` and language-level `NP ⊆ P/poly` (`∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly`), the bounded existential projection `{x : List Bool | ∃ w : List Bool, w.length = p.eval x.length ∧ frame x ++ w ∈ M}` belongs to `PPoly` (proved via `familyAdvice`, `unframe`/`dropFrame`, `NP.of_verifier`, and `PPoly.of_advice`).
  - `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_NP` and `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_NP_of_SAT`: every `A ∈ NP enc` has a `P/poly` representative under language-level `NP encBits ⊆ PPoly` or `SAT ∈ P/poly`, without requiring a `Decoder` on `enc`.
- **Proved equivalence bridges for the `NP ⊆ P/poly` hypothesis**:
  - `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff`: `(∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), ∀ B ∈ NP encB, ∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ b, b ∈ B ↔ encB b ∈ L) ↔ (∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly)`
  - `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: `(∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), ∀ B ∈ NP encB, ∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ b, b ∈ B ↔ encB b ∈ L) ↔ (∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L)`
  - `forall_mem_NP_encBits_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: `(∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly) ↔ (∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L)`
  - `PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_encBits_subset_PPoly`: textbook language-level `NP encBits ⊆ PPoly` corollary for the existing collapse `PH enc = SigmaP enc 2`.
- **`NP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ Σₖ, Πₖ, PH ⊆ P/poly` for all `k : ℕ`**:
  - Under language-level `NP encBits ⊆ PPoly`: `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH` (for arbitrary `enc : α ↪ List Bool`), and set-inclusion rules `SigmaP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PiP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PH_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly` (for `Language Bool`).
  - Under arbitrary-encoding `NP ⊆ P/poly`: `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, and `mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH_of_NP_subset_PPoly`.
  - Under `SAT ∈ P/poly`: `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP_of_SAT`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP_of_SAT`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH_of_SAT`.

## Faithfulness

### Cited Sources
- **[KarpLipton1980, Section 3]**: the original collapse result. Arora–Barak's chapter notes (p. 120) credit the stronger second-level form used by the existing library theorem to Sipser.
- **[AroraBarak09, Section 6.3, Theorem 6.18; Section 6.4, Theorem 6.19]**: advice characterization and the collapse theorem. This PR derives the nonuniform closure consequence by existential projection and complement induction. Kannan's lower bound is Exercises 6.5–6.6; Theorem 6.21 is Shannon's counting bound. The broader #798 M5 objective remains open.

### Convention Differences and Proved Equivalence Bridges
In `complexitylib`, `PPoly : Set (Language Bool)` is a class of bit-string languages (`Language Bool = Set (List Bool)`), whereas `NP enc`, `SigmaP enc k`, `PiP enc k`, and `PH enc` are parameterized by an injective encoding `enc : α ↪ List Bool`. Accordingly, "a problem $A \subseteq \alpha$ belongs to $\mathrm{P/poly}$ under `enc`" is expressed either:
1. Directly as set membership `L ∈ PPoly` when `α = List Bool` and `enc = encBits` (`SigmaP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PiP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PH_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`); or
2. Via an explicit `P/poly` language representative `∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ enc x ∈ L` for general `enc : α ↪ List Bool` (matching the existing convention in `PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_SAT_mem_PPoly` and `PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_subset_PPoly`). Note that when `enc = encBits`, `(∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ encBits x ∈ L)` is equivalent to `(A : Language Bool) ∈ PPoly` because `Set.ext` identifies `A` and `L`.

Furthermore, we prove in `KarpLipton.lean` that the three ways of stating the hypothesis $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$ are mutually equivalent without requiring a `Decoder` on arbitrary encodings:
- `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff`: arbitrary-encoding `∀ {β} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), ∀ B ∈ NP encB, ∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ b, b ∈ B ↔ encB b ∈ L` $\iff$ textbook bit-string `∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly`.
- `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: arbitrary-encoding $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$ $\iff$ `∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L`.
- `forall_mem_NP_encBits_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: textbook bit-string $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$ $\iff$ `∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L`.

All public computability statements in this PR are plain (`ComputableInPolyTime`); `tidy` is used only inside proofs (`check_tidy_surface.py` remains unchanged at `1903 public tidy statement(s) in 401 module(s)`).

## Pre-Push Verification (`2fab74915aa89a1106c2d9b2ea11a44ea416bd12`)

- Author-reported local `./scripts/check.sh` success covers the repository's six gates: `lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, and `lake exe checkInitImports`.
- Independently verified [hosted CI 40106421407](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40106421407) at the exact head above passed all six gates and the tidy-statement ratchet (job 120908939004). The following additional local checks are author-reported:
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: `All hygiene checks passed.`
- `python3 -B scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`: `1903 public tidy statement(s) in 401 module(s), matching the baseline.`
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: `Catalogue selects 14 abstracts and 19 headline theorems.`
- `./scripts/guide.sh`: `Documentation configuration is consistent. Guide written to guide/.lake/build/site/html-multi`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: `Ran 295 tests in 22.719s — OK`

## Abstract-Impact Assessment

None (`abstract-none`). This PR extends `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/PH/KarpLipton.lean` with the nonuniform consequence `NP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ Σₖ, Πₖ, PH ⊆ P/poly` and hypothesis equivalence bridges; existing headline theorems (`PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_SAT_mem_PPoly`, `PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_subset_PPoly`) and `abstracts/catalogue.json` are unchanged, and `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes cleanly.

## AI Disclosure

Implemented by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity / Gemini, Google DeepMind), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. PR-description source locators and validation wording corrected with Codex reviewer assistance; no source changes.

Part of #798 (Prerequisite P2).

  - `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff`: `(∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), ∀ B ∈ NP encB, ∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ b, b ∈ B ↔ encB b ∈ L) ↔ (∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly)`
  - `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: `(∀ {β : Type} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), ∀ B ∈ NP encB, ∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ b, b ∈ B ↔ encB b ∈ L) ↔ (∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L)`
  - `forall_mem_NP_encBits_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: `(∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly) ↔ (∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L)`
  - `PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_encBits_subset_PPoly`: textbook language-level `NP encBits ⊆ PPoly` corollary for the existing collapse `PH enc = SigmaP enc 2`.
- **`NP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ Σₖ, Πₖ, PH ⊆ P/poly` for all `k : ℕ`**:
  - Under language-level `NP encBits ⊆ PPoly`: `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH` (for arbitrary `enc : α ↪ List Bool`), and set-inclusion rules `SigmaP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PiP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PH_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly` (for `Language Bool`).
  - Under arbitrary-encoding `NP ⊆ P/poly`: `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, and `mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH_of_NP_subset_PPoly`.
  - Under `SAT ∈ P/poly`: `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_SigmaP_of_SAT`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PiP_of_SAT`, `exists_mem_PPoly_of_mem_PH_of_SAT`.

### Convention Differences and Proved Equivalence Bridges
In `complexitylib`, `PPoly : Set (Language Bool)` is a class of bit-string languages (`Language Bool = Set (List Bool)`), whereas `NP enc`, `SigmaP enc k`, `PiP enc k`, and `PH enc` are parameterized by an injective encoding `enc : α ↪ List Bool`. Accordingly, "a problem $A \subseteq \alpha$ belongs to $\mathrm{P/poly}$ under `enc`" is expressed either:
1. Directly as set membership `L ∈ PPoly` when `α = List Bool` and `enc = encBits` (`SigmaP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PiP_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`, `PH_subset_PPoly_of_NP_subset_PPoly`); or
2. Via an explicit `P/poly` language representative `∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ enc x ∈ L` for general `enc : α ↪ List Bool` (matching the existing convention in `PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_SAT_mem_PPoly` and `PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_subset_PPoly`). Note that when `enc = encBits`, `(∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ encBits x ∈ L)` is equivalent to `(A : Language Bool) ∈ PPoly` because `Set.ext` identifies `A` and `L`.

Furthermore, we prove in `KarpLipton.lean` that the three ways of stating the hypothesis $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$ are mutually equivalent without requiring a `Decoder` on arbitrary encodings:
- `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff`: arbitrary-encoding `∀ {β} (encB : β ↪ List Bool), ∀ B ∈ NP encB, ∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ b, b ∈ B ↔ encB b ∈ L` $\iff$ textbook bit-string `∀ B : Language Bool, (B : Set (List Bool)) ∈ NP encBits → B ∈ PPoly`.
- `forall_mem_NP_exists_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: arbitrary-encoding $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$ $\iff$ `∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L`.
- `forall_mem_NP_encBits_mem_PPoly_iff_SAT`: textbook bit-string $\mathrm{NP} \subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$ $\iff$ `∃ L ∈ PPoly, ∀ φ, φ ∈ SAT ↔ encCNF φ ∈ L`.

All public computability statements in this PR are plain (`ComputableInPolyTime`); `tidy` is used only inside proofs (`check_tidy_surface.py` remains unchanged at `1903 public tidy statement(s) in 401 module(s)`).

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Focused #813 integration diagnosis (`codex-review-559`), not a readiness verdict. Exact failed queue prefix `3aca0095d43a266b8c8b822bc96d47f1a5d1bc69` and actual-main snapshot `545660c6a344e2d047d02d7b08b6111de6486ff2` were checked in separate isolated trees. Both original test files and Tactic/PPT are byte-identical across these snapshots; unlanded #824/#818 changes are excluded. Fresh unchanged main copies pass, while adding the exact plain provider reproduces both original 200,000-heartbeat failures.

Valid registration-only A/B uses a temporary unscoped environment FUNCTION-table filter, asserting the actual remaining names at key Pure.pure / property IsPPTOn. Results agree on both snapshots:

| Active pure-lift FUNCTION rules | GMWPointwise | OraclePPT |
|---|---|---|
| raw + plain | original timeout | original timeouts |
| raw only | pass | pass |
| plain only | original timeout | original timeouts |
| neither | pass | fails an earlier ordinary positive (not the original timeout result) |

Therefore removing the old raw registration alone does **not** resolve this interaction. The valid raw-only fresh runs take about 2.3–2.6s; plain-only failures about 13.2–13.8s. These are observed wall times on a shared node, not a controlled speedup benchmark. Every original assertion, tactic and heartbeat budget is preserved. Earlier attempts using unsupported attribute erasure, or a filter inside an open-in local scope, are invalid controls and are excluded from this conclusion.

The plain-only trace enters the new pure FUNCTION rule and requests plain deterministic certificates. GMW has no direct plain BEq rule, then composes with an unresolved intermediate encoding; later generic framed-list length and nested projections try to convert an actual raw word to encList encBool and exhaust whnf. Oracle goes through plain product/take, then the framed-length candidate before encoding-aware word length, ending at the same nested-projection encoding ambiguity. Logs: `/tmp/codex-813-plain-route-{GMW,Oracle}.log`; valid machine-readable runs: `/tmp/codex-813-ab-v3/{prefix,main}/results.json`. These paths are supporting audit artifacts, not shipped machinery.

No production source or registration change has been made. A diagnostic-only exact shared plain BEq preamble (common element encoding, LawfulBEq, proof `.of_tidy (hleft.tidy.beq hright.tidy)`) compiles but does not alone close either failing suite on either snapshot. Its trace selects the new BEq rule, then fails on RHS raw-word length being routed through a framed-list encoding and nested projections. This is a further encoding-inference obligation, not a reason to weaken the equality theorem or add assumptions. Exact logs `/tmp/codex-813-{prefix,main}-{GMWPointwise,OraclePPT}-plain-BEq.log`; remaining branch `/tmp/codex-813-prefix-GMW-BEq-trace.log`.

A separate small plain-only FUNCTION probe passes the supplied generic plain certificate, missing-premise rejection, and explicit raw-certificate method; the raw theorem remains available explicitly. This does not validate the final per-search backend, which remains owned by worker 560. The shared BEq/provider owner is separate. The theorem’s existing mathematical approval remains valid, but caller closure, final backend checks and green integration are still required. No global fallback, unsupported priority machinery, test weakening or CI restart is proposed.

**Reviewed-provider closure result:** a separate clean diagnostic checkpoint `46f3162c30436b2738bb14e37106d5e353b04a24` adds only #811’s two library files and #823’s 20-line library projection patch to the pinned main snapshot. It adds no producer test fixtures, aggregate imports or global test certificates. With the unchanged original test bodies/budgets, both suites pass in the plain-only pure FUNCTION route with the exact BEq preamble (3.840s/3.951s), and also WITHOUT BEq (2.665s/3.541s). Both production pure FUNCTION registrations together likewise pass without BEq. Thus this library-only #811+#823 package is sufficient for these regressions; a BEq landing is not established as an #813 prerequisite. These are fresh proof executions, not cached target successes.

The provider statement, proof, tests and registrations remain unchanged. Integration stays held until the actual shared-provider squash landings, payload-only rebase, fresh original sources/full checks and exact-new-head review. The separately owned final per-search backend still needs its own joined probe; this is not global S1/plain-only readiness. Local evidence: `/tmp/codex-813-provider-closure-{plain-results,controls,both-no-BEq-results}.json` and original-source probe logs. No production registration correction is justified by this evidence.

title: feat(ppt): lift plain deterministic certificates to pure programs
body:
Expose `ComputableInPolyTime.isPPTOn`: a deterministic function with a plain polynomial-time certificate gives a strict fair-coin program returning that function's value. The machine ignores its sampled bits. Types, encodings, uniform input scope and result distribution match the existing raw theorem; its construction is reused with proof-local `h.tidy`.

Bounded support for #750. Payload-only rebase onto actual main `60440a792ceac91ab7f524bcd197b044ecc56d62` after #811 and #823 squash-merged. The provider and test files are byte-identical to approved `11b13eea`; the aggregate adds only the original test import. Both original global registrations and the raw proof remain unchanged. No tactic-index change, callback batch, model change, alias or raw fallback is added.

The old queue prefix failed fresh GMWPointwise and OraclePPT proofs because the new plain route exposed missing encoding-conversion/projection support. [The corrected causal record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/813#issuecomment-6386870517) isolates the registration interaction and establishes the library-only #811+#823 context as sufficient; removing the raw rule alone was not a fix, and BEq is not a prerequisite for these regressions.

At exact `6b2fe277e4bbe7827a10a821d7efc1cc4a28312d`, strict provider/original-client targets pass (7318 jobs). Both original failure files were then executed directly in fresh Lean processes: GMWPointwise passes in 4.944s and OraclePPT in 6.796s, with unchanged source blobs and their original 200,000-heartbeat limits. No diagnostic preamble, attribute filter, budget increase or fixture change was used. These are fresh proof executions, not inferred from cached gate success.

All six local gates at four threads, fresh-output S3 (1899 statements/402 modules, matching the inherited baseline), hygiene with --check-simp, catalogue selection (14 abstracts/19 headlines) and whitespace checks pass. Ordinary-import named/automatic/missing-premise regressions remain intact. The earlier scoped [652 review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6382530362) and provider source approval are reused; exact-new-head integration review and hosted CI remain required. This does not claim the separately owned final per-search backend or global S1 parity.

Abstract assessment: no selected headline statement, model, encoding, bound or renderer changes; no new PDF inspection is needed.

Framework friction: pure-PPT lookup had only a raw deterministic premise even when an application had a plain certificate. This adds the shared ordinary provider without a local Crypto copy or a second efficiency model. The separate tactic index/filter work is not included.

AI-assisted implementation and self-review by Codex worker `codex-review-559`. Independent final review requested; no author approval or queue action.

title: refactor(expander): parameterize powRot by a raw rotation function and split Expander products (#614)
body:
## Summary

Implements the `powRot` raw-rotation refactor and the `Products`/`TowerBase`/`WithInput` module-structure slices of **Items D5 and A10** of #614 (under #587):

1. **Item D5 (`Let powRot take a raw rotation function` — milestone slice)**:
   - Parameterize `RotationMap.powRot` and `RotationMap.powRot_involutive` in `Complexity/Foundations/Combinatorics/Expander/Power.lean` by a raw rotation function `rotate : V × D → V × D`, matching `tensorRot` and `zigzagRot`.
   - Express `powRotWithInput` directly through `powRot (fun q => rotate (p.1, q))` and fold `Complexity/Foundations/Combinatorics/Expander/Walk/WithInput.lean` into `Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/RotationMap/Walk.lean`.
   - **Remaining open on #614 D5**: `walkAtWithInput` in `RotationMap/Walk.lean` remains a separate recursion rather than an instance of `walkAt`.

2. **Item A10 (`Expander module structure` — milestone slice)**:
   - Split `Complexity/Foundations/Combinatorics/Expander/Products.lean` into `Tensor.lean`, `Zigzag.lean`, and `Replacement.lean`.
   - Delete the superseded `Complexity/Foundations/Combinatorics/Expander/TowerBase.lean` and restate `exists_spectralExpansion_zigzagTower_le` in `Complexity/Foundations/Combinatorics/Expander/AffineTower.lean` from `affinePlaneTowerBase (ZMod 257)`.
   - **Remaining open on #614 A10**: the `ReingoldVertex` rename / `equivFin` helper bullet remains open.

Part of #614, #587.

## Validation
- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 ./scripts/check.sh` (all 6 gates pass)
- `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`
- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py`
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` (no headline abstract changes required)

body: [P2] Distinguish the two plain-complexity comparisons in this summary. The direct inequality is `plain x ≤ timeBounded t x`. +/-!
+# Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity (`K^t`) and Levin's `Kt`
+
+This module defines the universal multi-tape Turing machine description method
+`Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTM` for binary strings, the corresponding plain and
+time-bounded Kolmogorov complexities `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain` (`K`) and
+`Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded` (`K^t`), and Levin's time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity
+`Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKt` (`Kt`).
+
+## Modeling conventions (#798 Decisions D1–D3)
+
+* **D1 (clock counts steps of the described machine):**
+  A binary program `p : List Bool` is parsed into a multi-tape Turing machine description
+  `decodeDesc (unframe p)` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.decodeDesc`) and an input bit string
+  `dropFrame p` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.dropFrame`). At step bound `t`, `universalTM` runs the
+  described machine on `(dropFrame p).map eBit` for `t` steps (`Universal.Desc.runFor`).
+  In [Liu and Pass, Section 2.2][LiuPass2020], $U(\Pi, 1^t)$ denotes the output of $M(w)$ when
+  emulated for $t$ steps (whose proof of Theorem 5.2 requires counting steps of the described
+  machine $M$, or a constant-overhead universal simulator). Counting the steps of the described
+  multi-tape machine directly in `universalTM` makes $K^t$ exact at linear time scales while the
+  polynomial overhead of the universal simulator `Universal.universal` appears only in algorithmic
+  membership results such as `MINKT ∈ NP`.
+* **D2 (global output):**
+  When the described machine halts within `t` steps, the entire output tape contents are mapped back
+  to `List Bool` via `(· != 0)`, matching the global "print $x$" convention of
+  [Ko][Ko1986], [Liu and Pass, Section 2.2][LiuPass2020], and [Hirahara][Hirahara2018], as well as
+  `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFor_eq_simulate`.
+* **D3 (values in `ℕ∞` with finite-form bridges):**
+  `plain`, `timeBounded`, and `levinKt` take values in `ℕ∞` via
+  `DescriptionMethod.ecomplexity` and `DescriptionMethod.etimeBoundedComplexity`, accompanied by
+  `ℕ`-valued wrappers (`plainNat`, `timeBoundedNat`, `levinKtNat`) and proved equivalence bridges
+  (`timeBounded_le_natCast_iff`, `timeBoundedNat_le_iff`, `timeBoundedNat_eq_sInf`,
+  `levinKt_le_natCast_iff`) showing agreement with the literature's `min` over `ℕ` whenever a
+  witness exists.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTMRunFor`: clocked evaluation of a binary program
+  `p` for `t` steps of the described multi-tape machine.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTM`: the universal multi-tape description method on
+  `List Bool`.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plainNat`: plain Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ under
+  `universalTM` in `ℕ∞` and `ℕ`.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBoundedNat`: time-bounded Kolmogorov
+  complexity $K^t(x)$ for a time bound $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, in `ℕ∞` and `ℕ`.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKt`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKtNat`: Levin's time-bounded complexity
+  $\mathrm{Kt}(x) = \inf_{s \ge 1} (K^s(x) + \lceil \log_2 s \rceil)$, in `ℕ∞` and `ℕ`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTMSimulation`,
+  `Cslib.Kolmogorov.simulation_ofMultiTapeTM`: every finite-state binary `MultiTapeTM` is simulated
+  by `universalTM` with constant program overhead and zero time overhead.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded_anti`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded_mono_of_le`: monotonicity in
+  the time bound $t$.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded_le`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_timeBounded_le`:
+  $K^t(x) \le |x| + c$ whenever $t(|x|) \ge |x| + 1$ ([Liu and Pass, Fact 2.1][LiuPass2020] under
+  the multi-tape output convention).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain_le_timeBounded`,
+  `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_ecomplexity_universal_le_timeBounded`: $K(x) \le K^t(x)$ against both
+  `plain` (`universalTM.ecomplexity`) and `DescriptionMethod.universal.ecomplexity`.

The definitions and your conditional `GapMINKT.no_eq` agree; this requests citation precision, not a different problem. If using an extended version, identify and link that version explicitly.
