title: feat(LogSpace): directed s-t connectivity is NL-complete
body:
Item 1 of #885. Directed s–t connectivity is NL-complete under logspace many-one reductions [Sipser, Theorem 8.25], and its complement is in NL, and NL-complete, through `NL_eq_coNL`.

## What is proved

`STCON : Set STCONInstance` holds when there is a directed path from `s` to `t`, the empty path included. This is Sipser's `PATH`. An instance is an adjacency matrix on `Fin n` with two vertices. It is encoded by `encSTCON` as the unary header `1^n 0 1^s 0 1^t 0` followed by the matrix row by row, the same layout as `encUSTCON`. `USTCON` now encodes an instance as its directed graph, so that layout lives in one place.

- `STCON.mem_NL : STCON ∈ NL encSTCON` [Sipser, Example 8.19].
- `STCON.logSpaceReducible_of_mem_NL`, `STCON.logSpaceHard`, and `STCON.logSpaceComplete : LogSpaceComplete NL encSTCON STCON` [Sipser, Theorem 8.25].
- `STCON.compl_mem_NL` and `STCON.compl_logSpaceComplete`, through `NL_eq_coNL`, which rests on Erik Demaine's inductive-counting construction (#465). The second is the form used for 2SAT in item 2.
- `STCON.mem_L_iff_forall_NL_eq_L`: `STCON ∈ L` exactly when `NL = L` for every encoding [Sipser, Corollary 8.24].

The classes are the existing native ones. NL means one finite-state NTM with every-prefix work space `c * (log₂ n + 1)` that halts on every branch. The reductions are deterministic logspace functions (`LogSpaceReducible`).

## How

- **Membership.** `Machines/…/LogSpace/CounterProgram/Nondeterministic.lean` adds *nondeterministic counter programs*: a counter program whose register `0` receives a fresh choice bit after every step. `CounterProgram.exists_decidesInLogSpace` compiles one to a native NTM through `NondeterministicQueryMachine.exists_decidesInSpace`. The hypotheses are halting of every branch, polynomially bounded registers and correct acceptance. A rank and an invariant give the first two (`haltsWithin_of_rank`, `forall_run_of_rank`). `Problems/STCON/Search.lean` is the search: it reads the header, then guesses the next vertex by counting, and gives up after `n` steps. Its invariant records that the current vertex is reachable, which gives soundness. For completeness, a shortest path, with fewer than `n` arcs, is followed.
- **Hardness.** `Problems/STCON/Reduction.lean` maps an instance to the compact configuration graph of the decider (`ConfigurationGraph`), with one extra sink vertex and an arc to it from each accepting halted vertex. `configurationInstance_mem_iff` reduces correctness to the existing `accepts_iff_reachable_bad_of_runsInSpace`. A counter program with output writes the encoded instance; it stores the input length, two vertex identifiers and one symbol code. For that, `CounterProgram/Boolean.lean` and `ConfigurationGraph/Expr.lean` express the local edge test, `bad`, `startID`, `vertexBound` and `queryIndex` as counter-program expressions. Each comes with a lemma giving its value. The program runs on the framed input (`computableInLogSpace_frame`), so its registers stay below `(|input| + 1) ^ d` even on the empty encoding.

## Plain-first note

All new public statements are plain; the tidy ratchet is unchanged at 1301. The only tidy use is in the private compiler glue of `Nondeterministic.lean` (`withChoice_inSpace`, `next_inSpace`, `accept_inSpace`). It feeds `NondeterministicQueryMachine.exists_decidesInSpace`, whose callbacks are `ComputableTidilyInSpace` and which has no plain counterpart. The STCON program and the reduction use no tidy notion: the transducer uses the existing plain `CounterProgram.computableInLogSpace_of_reachesOut`. The missing plain rule is a plain-callback variant of `exists_decidesInSpace`, the Machines conversion of #862 step 5.

## Formal abstracts

No impact on statements. `USTCONBridge` used `USTCONInstance.matrix`, which moved to `STCONInstance.matrix`; I updated its proof. The abstract statement and its encoding are unchanged. `scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` selects 14 abstracts and 19 headline theorems, as before. Item 3 of #885 adds the NL = coNL headline.

## Validation

At 1e44041c: `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates. `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` and `check_tidy_surface.py` (1301, matching the baseline) pass, as does `build_abstracts.py --check`. `ComplexityTests/STCON.lean` exercises concrete instances: `0 → 1 → 2` is in `STCON`, the single arc `1 → 0` does not connect `0` to `1`, and the search accepts the first and rejects the second. It pins the encoding bit by bit, instantiates hardness on `USTCON ∈ L`, and guards the headline theorems with `#print axioms` (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).

Citations: Sipser, 3rd edition. Example 8.19 (p. 350), Theorem 8.23 (p. 352) and Theorem 8.25 (p. 353) were checked against course notes quoting those page numbers. Corollary 8.24 follows Theorem 8.23 in the same section.

title: feat(wordram): charge RAM preparation and derive element distinctness
body:
This completes the charged additive WordRAM-to-RAM bridge and derives a concrete logarithmic-cost element-distinctness decider. It composes the actual backward-copy/clearing program from #87 with the fixed compiler from #85; no simulation or setup certificate is assumed.

For a fixed source program with `r` named registers, let `R = r + 5`, `A = 8 * (bitLength R + 1)` and `B = (24 + R) * (bitLength (R + 5) + 2)`. Every successful `t`-instruction run on a fitting `w`-bit input is simulated within `(A + B) * (t + input.length + 1) * (w + 1)` logarithmic cost. The target program depends only on the source program. Its external input is `replicate 5 0 ++ input.length :: input`; installing that fixed convention is uncharged, while every subsequent relocation, clearing, initialization, simulation and output instruction is charged.

The twelve-register bounded-universe element-distinctness program compiles to one fixed target program with bound `2735 * (n + 1) * (Nat.log 2 (n + 1) + 1)`. Preparation contributes 287 and compiled execution 2448 times the same factor; the padded-input variant retains 2448. Every input entry must be below `n`, including the empty instance. This does not establish unrestricted element distinctness, source-fault reflection, a charged arbitrary-list encoding reduction, or a Turing-machine/class equivalence. Word-width access, multiplication, division, bitwise operations and shifts remain outside the supported fragment.

Tracked by #81. Preparation dependency: #87, whose final head `bb15478f78b7df389e1dbd0f91ce4cf21f23aeee` is included with its original source history preserved. The coordinator owns issue disposition and merge order.

Validation: all six project gates pass for final source/tests `aec70b38fb3158a09850dc3640fba31e8e312f1e` (`ed-prepared-check.log`), with fresh MCP diagnostics clean. Later dependency integration and this documentation commit leave all Lean source/tests unchanged. Tests cover charged width-zero execution, an aliased indirect load after overlapping relocation, actual empty/singleton/distinct/duplicate target executions, quantitative clients and guarded headline axiom checks.

Independent reviews: coordinator `coordinator-ops-20261020` approved [padded source 43cc1932](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/issues/81#issuecomment-6300510100); coordinator `ram-preparation-review-20261020` approved [exact charged source aec70b38](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/issues/81#issuecomment-6300618074) for API and correctness with no findings. Root coordinator `coordinator-ops-20261020` approved [exact final revision `3dd8f69e70bec1d0ebb88b1bc5f2551dc538bc10`](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/88#issuecomment-6300693546) after independent theorem-index, rendered-PDF and integration review. PR #87 is merged; this PR is ready for integration after required CI passes. These are agent review comments, not platform or human approvals.

Theorem-index assessment: extends the compiler entry with charged preparation and its explicit constant, and adds one logarithmic-RAM element-distinctness entry. The index has 131 entries; all eight declaration anchors were verified. The 65-page PDF builds without undefined citations or overfull boxes; rendered pages 1, 50 and 51 were inspected. A coordinator wording request distinguishing already-compiled code from runtime compilation was applied. The roadmap records the proved endpoint and retains the input-convention, larger-instruction-fragment and Turing-machine limitations.

Source credit: this composition and cost corollary are new code, using the existing local natural-number RAM adaptation of Cook–Reckhow, the lean-trominoes WordRAM formalization (including Erik Demaine and its other contributors), and the direct-addressing algorithm described by Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein. Existing headers and bibliographic credits are preserved; the target is not presented as literally Cook–Reckhow's original integer/I/O machine.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex worker `wordram-bridge-20261020` authored this branch; worker `ram-input-preparation-20261020` authored the dependency. The named independent Codex coordinators reviewed the source; `coordinator-ops-20261020` scoped and supervises final integration. No human editorial approval is implied.

Implements **Item 1 (Kolmogorov cleanup)** of the metacomplexity quality audit (#884), covering findings **F9**, **F11**, **F12**, **F13**, **F14**, **F15**, **F16**, **F17**, and **F19**:

- **F9 (Alias, duplicate, and placement cleanup):**
  - Removed the `simulation_ofMultiTapeTM` alias in `Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/TimeBounded.lean` and updated module docs and `ComplexityTests/KolmogorovTimeBounded.lean` to use `exists_simulation_ofMultiTapeTM`.
  - Removed duplicate `mem_universalTM_runFor_iff` and `mem_universalTM_runFor_iff_simulate` in `TimeBounded.lean` (keeping `mem_universalTMRunFor_iff`, `mem_universalTMRunFor_iff_simulate`, and `@[simp] theorem universalTM_runFor`).
  - Removed redundant `encard_setOf_length_eq_timeBounded_lt` in `TimeBounded.lean` (keeping `encard_setOf_timeBounded_lt`).
  - Extracted and generalized the seven public `Computable`/`Primrec` bridge lemmas (`ComputableInPolyTime.isComputable`, `computable_frame`, `primrec_encUnary`, `computable_encUnary`, `computable_encPair`, `IsComputable.computable_option`, `IsComputable.computable_option_bits`) from private helpers in `TimeBounded.lean` into `Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Halting/Partrec.lean` next to `IsComputable.computable`.
- **F11 (`MINKT` plain-first):**
  - Removed the 5 private `@[fun_prop]` tidy projection theorems, the 2 dead `attribute [local fun_prop] ... .tidy` lines, and the unused `PolySpace.Plain` import in `Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/MINKT.lean`.
  - Proved `Instance.computableInPolyTime_string`, `Instance.computableInPolyTime_time`, `Instance.computableInPolyTime_size`, and `Instance.computableInPolyTime_mk` directly in `ComputableInPolyTime` via `ComputableInPolyTime.of_eq`, `fst`, `snd`, and `comp`.
  - Replaced `.of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_eval p)` with plain `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_eval`.
  - Replaced the tidy round-trip in `MINKTAt.computableInPolyTime_toInstance` with plain `encoding_length`, `prod`, and `comp`.
  - Removed `private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_check` and proved `MINKT.computableInPolyTime_check` directly in plain `ComputableInPolyTime` (using `.of_tidy ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_le` only for the missing plain `unary_le` rule; the public tidy ratchet remains unchanged at 1301/225).
- **F12 (`Universal` plain wrappers and `computableInPolyTime_map_ne_zero` placement):**
  - Moved the four literal plain wrappers (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.Universal.computableInPolyTime_decodeDesc`, `computableInPolyTime_map_eBit`, `computableInPolyTime_eBit`, and `computableInPolyTime_universal`) together with `computableInPolyTime_map_ne_zero` (with `@[fun_prop, program_certificate]` registration) from `TimeBounded.lean` into `Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Universal/PolyTime.lean`.
- **F13 (`timeBoundedAt` and `timeBounded_antitone`):**
  - Added `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBoundedAt (t : ℕ) (x : List Bool) : ℕ∞ := universalTM.etimeBoundedComplexity t x` and `@[simp] theorem timeBounded_eq_timeBoundedAt (t : ℕ → ℕ) (x : List Bool) : timeBounded t x = timeBoundedAt (t x.length) x := rfl`.
  - Stated `levinKt`, `MINKT`, and `GapMINKT` through `timeBoundedAt` rather than `timeBounded (fun _ => ...)`.
  - Added `timeBoundedAt_antitone`, `timeBoundedAt_anti`, and `timeBounded_antitone`, and renamed `timeBounded_mono_of_le` / `timeBounded_mono` to `timeBounded_anti_of_le` / `timeBounded_anti` matching `etimeBoundedComplexity_antitone`.
- **F14 (Privatization):**
  - Privatized internal helpers in `TimeBounded.lean` (`universalTMRunFor_eq_ite`, `universalTMRunFor_mono`, `universalTMEval`, `mem_universalTMEval_iff`, `partrec_universalTMEval`, `machineHeader`, `universalTM_runFor_machineHeader_append`, `universalTMSimulation`), removed unused `universalTM_run_machineHeader_append`, and replaced `MINKT.Instance.equivTuple` in `MINKT.lean` with an inline embedding and private `Instance.computableInPolyTime_toTuple`.
- **F15, F16, F17 (Citations, module docs, and `levinKt` step-count note):**
  - Added `Ko1991` (Ko, *SIAM J. Comput.* 20(5):962–986, 1991) and `Levin1984` (Levin, *Inf. Control* 61(1):15–37, 1984) to `references.bib`; cited `[Ko1991]` for `MINKT` in `MINKT.lean`, cited `[Levin1973]`, `[Levin1984]`, and `[AllenderBuhrmanKouckyVanMelkebeekRonneburger2006]` on `levinKt` in `TimeBounded.lean`, and removed uncited `[AllenderBuhrmanKouckyVanMelkebeekRonneburger2006]` from `MINKT.lean`.
  - Consolidated modeling/threshold conventions into each module header (linking `#798` once per module header rather than repeating "Decision D1–D4" across individual docstrings), documented the constant-factor effect on $\lceil \log_2 s \rceil$ in `levinKt` from counting steps of the described multi-tape machine (`universalTM`) rather than the polynomial-overhead simulator (`Universal.universal`), and documented and listed all public declarations in `TimeBounded.lean` and `MINKT.lean`.
- **F19 (`KolmogorovTimeBounded` tests):**
  - Added non-vacuous concrete examples to `ComplexityTests/KolmogorovTimeBounded.lean`: a concrete `MINKT` yes-instance `⟨x, |x| + 1, |x| + copyOverhead⟩`, a no-instance from `exists_length_eq_forall_le_timeBounded`, a `GapMINKT` example with strict gap `σ(n, s) = 2 * s + 1` and `τ(n, t) = 2 * t + 2` exhibiting both yes- and no-instances, and `levinKt_le_length_add` on `[true, false, true, false]`.

## `abstracts/catalogue.json` Impact Assessment
This PR is an internal API, placement, plain-first, and documentation refactor of `Kolmogorov/{TimeBounded,MINKT}.lean` and `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/{Halting/Partrec,Universal/PolyTime}.lean` and does not add, remove, or alter any theorem referenced in `abstracts/catalogue.json`.

## Validation
- `./scripts/check.sh`:
  - `ok build --wfail --iofail`
  - `ok mk_all --check`
  - `ok test --wfail --iofail`
  - `ok lint`
  - `ok lint-style`
  - `ok checkInitImports`
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: `All hygiene checks passed.`
- `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`: `1301 public tidy statement(s) in 225 module(s), matching the baseline.`
- `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --config-only`: `Documentation configuration is consistent.`
- `./scripts/guide.sh --check`: `Guide written to guide/.lake/build/site/html-multi`

Refs #884

title: feat(classes): add basic closures UP exact counting and DP completeness
body:
This batch fills six basic class-theory gaps using the existing machine-certified verifier and reduction APIs:

- P, NP and coNP closure under union and intersection.
- Parity-P closure under union, intersection and symmetric difference.
- #P and GapP closure under polynomial-time precomposition, preserving the exact count by requiring padding bits to be false.
- Verifier-based UP, with P ⊆ UP ⊆ NP ∩ ⊕P and closure under polynomial-time reductions.
- C=P as GapP zero sets, equivalently equality of two #P functions; union/intersection/reduction closure and coNP ⊆ C=P ⊆ PP.
- DP and a generic theorem that an NP-complete language paired with a coNP-complete language is DP-complete. SAT–UNSAT completeness follows using the product CNF encoding.

The classes quantify over injectively encoded instances. UP and counting-class machine characterizations remain explicit roadmap work. No separation between DP and NP ∩ coNP is claimed. The source developments are separated into focused commits and modules.

The theorem index now has 68 entries and 26 pages, including three new entries and exact-count precomposition. All 17 new declaration links target reviewed Lean revision `4f6bdaf35ebe60aec6d1063ae513ac342df13589`.

Validation: all six project gates passed at `8c12d2a9` (build/test with `--wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, lint, lint-style, checkInitImports). The only subsequent Lean change is a reviewed docstring clarification. Tests include concrete yes/no instances, variable-length count precomposition, padding multiplicities and 16 headline axiom guards. The PDF rebuilt; all 26 rendered pages and 17 new source/PDF links were checked.

Independent Codex API and correctness reviews approved final Lean revision `4f6bdaf3`. The correctness review's DP wording nit was fixed and re-reviewed. An independent exposition review approved `683cfcf5` against that Lean revision. No outstanding findings. Exact scopes, revisions and artifact hashes are recorded in `paper/review.md`.

AI assistance: implementation and exposition by OpenAI Codex; independent reviews by Codex agents `proof_api`, `proof_correctness` and `resume_alternation`. Mathematical sources are credited in the modules and index, principally Arora–Barak, Papadimitriou, and Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz. These reviews do not imply human editorial approval.

title: refactor(counting): simplify wide-gap closure certificates
body:
The bounded and truth-table LWPP proofs repeat explicit certificate plumbing that existing automation can discharge. This proof-only cleanup uses `fun_prop` for the two unary-polynomial certificates, omits inferred range arguments from the two prefix-product certificates, and removes three redundant local `classical` commands. The product factor function remains explicit because automation alone cannot infer it reliably; no helper, public declaration, or global automation rule is added.

All theorem statements, names, hypotheses, bounds, mathematical arguments, and source credits are unchanged. The necessary `classical` command in the private answer-word argument remains. The existing named axiom guards continue to report `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`; removing a local command is not a claim of constructive independence.

Closes #89.

Validated revision: `708ad6d77622b7838c9b63cf1f033453cf306293` (base `eec59c2ad36d2116ae07defcbde802257fa211e6`).

Validation: fresh Lean MCP diagnostics are clean for both edited files. `scripts/check.sh` passed all six gates: `lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, and `lake exe checkInitImports`. Existing bounded/truth-table client tests and axiom guards are unchanged; no additional tests were needed for these proof-body edits.

Theorem-index assessment: no impact. Compared the final diff with the bounded and truth-table entries in `paper/sections/randomness.tex`; the jointly uniform hypotheses, input-dependent unary query count, verifier model, and nonadaptive scope remain identical. All eight immutable declaration anchors still resolve to their named declarations at their pinned revisions. No paper or PDF changes are needed.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex worker `wpp-proof-cleanup-20261020` inspected the existing API, made the proof edits, and ran validation. Independent exact-revision API/correctness and no-impact-index review is requested from the coordinator; the author has not approved or merged this change.

title: feat(LogSpace): 2SAT is NL-complete (#885)
body:
Item 2 of #885. 2SAT is NL-complete under logspace many-one reductions [Papadimitriou, Theorem 16.3]. Membership goes through the complement and `NL_eq_coNL`. Hardness comes from the NL-completeness of the complement of directed connectivity (#887).

## What is proved

`TwoSAT : Set (CNF ℕ)` is the set of satisfiable formulas whose clauses have at most two literals each. Formulas are the library's `Cslib.Logic.PL.CNF ℕ`, encoded by the existing `encCNF`, the same encoding SAT uses. Formulas with a wider clause are outside `TwoSAT`, so the problem is a promise-free language over all CNF formulas.

- `CNF.not_satisfiable_iff_of_width_le_two` (`Logics/Propositional/CNF/TwoCNF.lean`): when every clause has at most two literals, a formula is unsatisfiable exactly when it contains the empty clause, or some variable `x` has a path from `x` to `¬x` and one back in the implication graph `CNF.Implies` [Aspvall, Plass and Tarjan 1979]. A unit clause `ℓ` gives the arc `¬ℓ → ℓ`.
- `notMem_TwoSAT_iff`: the formulas outside `TwoSAT` are those with a clause of more than two literals, with the empty clause, or with such a cycle.
- `TwoSAT.compl_mem_NL : TwoSATᶜ ∈ NL encCNF` and `TwoSAT.mem_NL : TwoSAT ∈ NL encCNF`. The second follows from the first through `compl_mem_NL_iff`, that is, `NL = coNL`, which rests on Erik Demaine's inductive-counting construction (#465).
- `TwoSAT.logSpaceReducible_compl_STCON : LogSpaceReducible encSTCON encCNF STCONᶜ TwoSAT`.
- `TwoSAT.logSpaceHard` and `TwoSAT.logSpaceComplete : LogSpaceComplete NL encCNF TwoSAT`.

The classes are the native ones, as in #887. NL means one finite-state NTM with every-prefix work space `c * (log₂ n + 1)` that halts on every branch. The reductions are deterministic logspace functions.

## How

- **Every-branch reasoning** (`CounterProgram/AllBranches.lean`). The rank method of #887 needs one global rank, and that is awkward for a program with several loops. `AllBranches B Post Q s` is an inductive predicate. It says that every branch from `s` reaches `Q`, or halts in a configuration satisfying `Post`, with registers at most `B` along the way. It composes with `bind`. Code that never reads the choice register follows its deterministic `Reaches` run (`allBranches_of_oblivious`, `branches_of_oblivious`). `exists_decidesInLogSpace_of_allBranches` turns every-branch soundness and one accepting branch into a native logspace NTM, through #887's `exists_decidesInLogSpace`.
- **Membership** (`Problems/TwoSAT/Membership.lean`, `Routines.lean`, `Layout.lean`). `Layout.lean` unfolds the framed encoding into a flat bit layout, with positional reading lemmas (`InfixAt`, `LitsAt`, `ClausesAt`). The decider, a 104-instruction nondeterministic counter program with 16 registers, guesses one of two reasons a formula is outside `TwoSAT`. The first is a clause of width zero or more than two, which it finds by counting. The second is a variable `x` with both paths. For that it guesses an occurrence of `x` and walks the implication graph from `x` to `¬x`, then back to `x`, giving up after as many steps as the input has bits in each half. A literal is stored as the position of an occurrence of its variable together with a polarity bit. Variables are compared digit by digit through their positions (`cmpVarCode`), so every register stays at most the input length. Soundness is `allBranches_decider`. For completeness, `branches_modeA` handles the first reason, and `branches_modeB` follows paths shortened to at most the input length, via `Relation.ReflTransGen.relatesWithinSteps_of_encard_le`. `accepts_decider_iff` states the exact acceptance condition.
- **Hardness** (`Problems/TwoSAT/Reduction.lean`). An `STCON` instance becomes the formula with the unit clauses `x_s` and `¬x_t` and one clause `¬x_u ∨ x_v` per arc. It is in `TwoSAT` exactly when `t` is unreachable from `s` (`reachabilityFormula_mem_TwoSAT_iff`). A counter program with output, 109 instructions, writes its encoding. `computableInLogSpace_reachabilityFormula` then follows from the existing plain `computableInLogSpace_of_reachesOut`.

## Plain-first note

All new public statements are plain, and the tidy ratchet is unchanged at 1301/225. The new files contain no tidy notion, in statements or proofs. The only tidy use is transitive. `exists_decidesInLogSpace_of_allBranches` calls #887's `CounterProgram.exists_decidesInLogSpace`, whose private glue feeds `NondeterministicQueryMachine.exists_decidesInSpace`, and that theorem takes `ComputableTidilyInSpace` callbacks with no plain counterpart. The missing plain rule is the same as in #887: a plain-callback variant of `exists_decidesInSpace` (#862, step 5).

## Headline abstracts

- Affected abstracts or catalogue entries: none. No selected abstract mentions `TwoSAT`, `CNF.Implies` or the counter-program API, and no existing statement or definition changed. `scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` selects 14 abstracts and 19 headline theorems, as before. Item 3 of #885 adds the NL = coNL headline. 2SAT NL-completeness is a natural scope note for it, but I have not selected it as a headline here.
- Independent abstract review: not applicable, since no abstract changed.
- PDF artifact: not applicable.

## Validation

At f089e8c1, rebased on main 45f7a884 after #887 merged:
- `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates.
- `lake exe mk_all --check`, `check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `check_tidy_surface.py` (1301, matching the baseline), `check_docs.py --config-only` and `build_abstracts.py --check` all pass.

`ComplexityTests/TwoSAT.lean` exercises concrete instances:
- `(x₀ ∨ x₁) ∧ ¬x₀` is in `TwoSAT`. `x₀ ∧ ¬x₀`, `[[]]` and a three-literal clause are not.
- The arcs `¬x₀ → x₀` and `x₀ → ¬x₀` of the contradiction are checked, together with a non-arc of `x₀ ∨ x₁`, and the contradiction's cycle is shown to witness `notMem_TwoSAT_iff`.
- The decider accepts the contradiction, and no branch accepts the satisfiable formula.
- The reduction's formulas for the path `0 → 1 → 2` and the back arc `1 → 0` are pinned by `decide`, with membership checked for both.
- `#print axioms` guards `not_satisfiable_iff_of_width_le_two`, `exists_decidesInLogSpace_compl`, `mem_NL` and `logSpaceComplete` (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).

Citations:
- Papadimitriou, *Computational Complexity* (1994), Theorem 16.3, "2SAT is NL-complete". I checked this secondhand: Wikipedia's 2-satisfiability article cites "Papadimitriou 1994, Thrm. 16.3", and course notes describe the same reduction from reachability to 2-UNSAT. I could not check the book itself.
- Aspvall, Plass and Tarjan, *Information Processing Letters* 8(3):121–123 (1979), doi 10.1016/0020-0190(79)90002-4, for the implication-graph criterion. This PR adds the bib entry.
- The decider program, its register layout, the positional comparison of variables and the proof of the criterion are this library's own. The module docs label them that way and do not attribute them to a source.

Written by `worker-claude-nl-c4b0c164` (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. The author reviewed its own work; there has been no independent review.

title: chore(tests): build the test library from a Lake glob, removing ComplexityTests.lean
body:
Removes the most common source of merge conflicts and restacks.

**Problem.** Nearly every PR adds a test module, and the generated `ComplexityTests.lean` (506 imports) conflicted whenever two PRs added tests in the same alphabetical neighbourhood. Today that hit #813, #855, #864 (twice) and #883.
- **On GitHub:** the server ignores `.gitattributes` `merge=union`, so PRs show as **CONFLICTING** and get ejected from the merge queue.
- **Locally:** the union driver resolves the conflict but **concatenates unsorted**, which then fails `mk_all --check`. This happened to restacks of #855 and #883.

**Change.**
- `lakefile.toml`: `ComplexityTests` gets `roots = []` and `globs = ["ComplexityTests.+"]`, so Lake builds every module under `ComplexityTests/` and there is no aggregator to update or conflict on. `ComplexityTests.lean` is deleted, along with its `merge=union` line.
- **Abstracts are still built and tested.** `ComplexityAbstracts` is imported by `ComplexityTests/Abstracts/All.lean`, which the glob covers.
- **Scripts.** `scripts/quality_report.py` previously found modules by following imports from each library's root file. It now takes a glob-built library's modules from its source files (`GLOB_ROOTS`, `glob_modules`, `root_modules`). `check_tidy_surface.py` and `tidy_sweep.py` use the same functions. A new unit test covers seeding from sources and ignoring stale outputs.
- **Docs.** AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md now say tests need no aggregator entry, and new abstract tests are imported from `ComplexityTests/Abstracts/All.lean`.

**Validation** (local, base `45f7a884`):
- All six `scripts/check.sh` gates pass. `lake test` builds all 506 test modules through the glob; a `--no-build` plan includes every test, `Axioms` and `Smoke` among them.
- All 308 Python tests pass.

title: feat(abstracts): Immerman–Szelepcsényi headline abstract (#885)
body:
Item 3 of #885. This adds a headline formal abstract for the Immerman–Szelepcsényi theorem `NL = coNL`, with directed non-reachability in `NL` as a supporting corollary.

## Change

New `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/ImmermanSzelepcsenyiAbstract.lean` and `…Bridge.lean`, catalogue entry `immerman-szelepcsenyi`:

- `nl_eq_conl {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : NL enc = coNL enc` (headline).
- `stcon_compl_mem_nl : STCONᶜ ∈ NL encInstance` (supporting).

The abstract states the conventions explicitly:

- **Model.** Each problem has one fixed finite-state binary multi-tape `Turing.MultiTapeNTM` (upstream cslib). Acceptance means some computation path halts with output `[true]`.
- **Space.** Along every computation prefix, rejecting branches included, the machine visits at most `c * (floor(log₂ n) + 1)` work-tape cells (upstream `RunsInSpace`). Read-only input and write-only output are not charged.
- **Termination.** Every branch terminates: on each input some finite time bounds all paths (`RunsInTime`). A stuck branch rejects.
- **Encoding.** `NL = coNL` holds for an arbitrary injective encoding `enc`, and `coNL` uses the same encoding. The corollary uses the explicit adjacency-matrix encoding with unary header `1^n 0 1^s 0 1^t 0`, the same layout as the Reingold abstract, shown in the representation appendix.

`Accepts` and `DecidesInSpace` are copied verbatim from the Savitch abstract, and the bridge proves the public `NL` and `coNL` definitionally equal to the library's `Cslib.Complexity.NL` and `coNL` (`rfl`). The abstract and the new regression tests pin this. `#check_abstract` passes without an allowlist: 15 root declarations and 71 dependencies, all upstream (cslib, Mathlib).

The library proof is Erik Demaine's streaming inductive-counting construction (#465), and the abstract credits it. Directed connectivity's `compl_mem_NL` comes from #887.

Other edits:
- `abstracts/README.md`: a table row; fourteen → fifteen.
- `README.md`: the existing "Immerman–Szelepcsényi" selected-results bullet now links to the abstract rather than the library file.
- `ROADMAP.md`: one clause.
- `ComplexityTests/Abstracts/ImmermanSzelepcsenyiTests.lean`: concrete clients.
  - `rfl` checks that the public classes are the library's.
  - The single arc `1 → 0` is in `STCONᶜ`, and the path `0 → 1 → 2` is in `STCON`, so the corollary is nonvacuous.
  - The encoding of the path is pinned bit by bit.
  - `STCON ∈ NL` is derived by combining the two public theorems.

## Validation and review

At bcd454c8, on main 45f7a884:
- `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates, and `lake exe mk_all --check` passes.
- `check_tidy_surface.py` reports 1301/225, matching the baseline. `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` and `check_docs.py --config-only` pass.
- `build_abstracts.py --check` selects 15 abstracts and 20 headline theorems.
- `test_abstract_to_tex.py` (23 tests, including pdflatex) and `test_build_abstracts.py` pass. An earlier draft used `⌊ ⌋`, which the TeX renderer rejects, so it is now spelled `floor(…)` as in the Reingold abstract.
- A local `build_abstracts.py` run built all 15 PDFs. I inspected all three pages of `immerman-szelepcsenyi.pdf`: definitions, statements and the appendix render without clipping.

Citations: Sipser, 3rd edition, Section 8.6 ("NL equals coNL"), matching the existing library references; Immerman 1988; Szelepcsényi 1987. I could not check Sipser's exact theorem number for NL = coNL, so the abstract cites the section and gives no theorem number.

## Headline abstracts

- Affected abstracts or catalogue entries: new entry `immerman-szelepcsenyi`. No existing abstract or statement changes.
- Independent abstract review: requested from `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023`; not yet done. Please compare the quantifiers, the space and termination conventions, the encoding, nonvacuity and readability against `Cslib.Complexity.NL`/`coNL` and `STCON.compl_mem_NL` at the PR head.
- PDF artifact: the **Formal abstract PDFs** workflow run for this PR head will provide it. The local build is from source bcd454c8.

## AI assistance

Written by `worker-claude-nl-c4b0c164` (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. The author reviewed its own work; there has been no independent review. Adding a headline was requested in #885; this does not imply Samuel's editorial approval of the selection.

body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-02 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 954357793394cb3c3549f033b56fe2dbb7753751 (agent review)

**Classification.** This is not a pure move. It moves `familyAdvice`, `evalAdvice`, `length_familyAdvice` (with the private `length_familyAdvice_block` and `drop_familyAdvice`), `evalAdvice_familyAdvice` and `computableInPolyTime_evalAdvice` to `Advice.lean`, rewrites the last proof without tidy, and adds two new public theorems, `PPoly_subset_PAdvice` and `PPoly_eq_PAdvice`.
- **Move:** the five public declarations keep their namespace (`Cslib.Circuits.Boolean`), statements and privacy. The only clients outside the two files, `KarpLipton.lean` and `ComplexityTests/KarpLipton2.lean`, still resolve. No aliases are added. `computableInPolyTime_evalAdvice` is now a plain proof and its statement is unchanged.
- **New theorems:** `PAdvice` is the polynomial-time-with-polynomial-advice class (`x ∈ L ↔ (α |x|, x) ∈ A`, with `A ∈ P (encPair encBits encBits)` and `|α n|` polynomially bounded), and `PPoly_subset_PAdvice` is the faithful converse. The advice for length `n` lists the circuits `C 0 … C n`, padded to `certLength n (P n)` with `P = c (X + 1)^d`. The advice length is at most `(n + 1)·W(n)`, and the pair problem `evalAdvice (P |x|) (W |x|) u x` is polynomial-time by `computableInPolyTime_evalAdvice` with the size and width bounds in unary. `PPoly_eq_PAdvice` is the textbook equality. Both theorems have axiom guards. Hosted `ci-checks` passed on this head.

**Blocking**

1. `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/PH/KarpLipton.lean:66–77`: the module docstring still lists `familyAdvice` and `evalAdvice` under *Main definitions*, and `evalAdvice_familyAdvice` and `computableInPolyTime_evalAdvice` under *Main results*. These now belong to `Advice.lean`, which lists them. Remove them from KarpLipton's lists. The prose at `:43–47` that explains how the proof uses them can stay.
2. `Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Advice.lean:181` and `:233`: the new docstrings cite `[Arora and Barak, Theorem 6.11][AroraBarak09]`. In the published book, `P/poly = ⋃ DTIME(n^c)/n^d` is **Theorem 6.18** ("Polynomial-time TM's with advice decide P/poly", in the list of main theorems in the authors' front-matter excerpt, theory.cs.princeton.edu/complexity/excerpt.pdf). Theorem 6.11 is its number in the 2006 web draft. Please cite 6.18. The existing `Definition 6.10` / `Theorem 6.11` at `:21`, `:25`, `:166` and `:174` come from the same draft numbering and could be fixed in the same pass.

**Nonblocking**

- `KarpLipton.lean:10` keeps `public import …Encoding.Certificate`. It was needed for the exposed bodies that moved out, so check whether it can now be a plain `import` or be dropped.
- `PPoly_subset_PAdvice` repeats the size-polynomial and width scaffold (`c, d`, `P`, `W`, `hW`, `hsize_le`) that `KarpLipton.lean` already has three times (`:172–221`, `:269–309`, `:332–384`). The second bullet of #884 F12, one shared "advice string for `M ∈ PPoly` up to length `N`" lemma, would absorb all four copies. This fits a follow-up.

The PR merges cleanly with current main and does not touch `ComplexityTests.lean`.

title: feat(Space): NSPACE(s) = coNSPACE(s), with NL = coNL as the case s = log₂ (#885)
body:
Item 4 of #885. This proves `NSPACE(s) = coNSPACE(s)` for every bound `s` with `log₂ n ≤ s n` and re-derives `NL = coNL` as the case `s = log₂`. It generalizes the inductive-counting construction instead of copying it.

**Stacked on #918.** The base branch is `feat/nl-coNL-abstract`, so the diff shows only this item; the last commit extends #918's abstract. I will rebase onto `main` once #918 merges.

## What is proved

`Classes/Space/Nondeterministic.lean` defines the classes the same way as `NL`:
- `NSPACE enc s`: one finite-state native `MultiTapeNTM` decides the problem, using at most `c₁ * s n + c₂` work cells along every computation prefix, with every branch halting (`MultiTapeNTM.DecidesInSpace`).
- `coNSPACE enc s`: the complements of problems in `NSPACE enc s`, under the same encoding.

Main statements:
- `NSPACE_eq_coNSPACE (hs : ∀ n, Nat.log2 n ≤ s n) : NSPACE enc s = coNSPACE enc s` [Immerman 1988, Theorem 1].
- Supporting lemmas: `compl_mem_NSPACE`, `compl_mem_NSPACE_iff`, `compl_mem_NSPACE_of_recognizesInSpace` and `mem_NSPACE_of_recognizesInSpace`. The last two mean a recognizer with looping branches suffices, as before. Also `NSPACE_subset_of_le_mul_add`.
- `NL_eq_NSPACE : NL enc = NSPACE enc Nat.log2`.
- `NL_eq_coNL` keeps its name and is now derived from `NSPACE_eq_coNSPACE`. `compl_mem_NL` and `mem_NL_of_recognizesInSpace` are re-derived as well.
- The machine-level theorem is `Turing.MultiTapeNTM.exists_decidesInSpace_compl`. From a recognizer within space `c₁ * s n + c₂`, it builds a complement decider within space `c * (s n + 1)`, every branch halting.

**No constructibility hypothesis.** I checked the existing `SpaceConstructible`, and it is not needed. Immerman's paper says after Theorem 1 that he originally assumed `s` constructible, but because no sequence of choices may exceed `s(n)` cells, "the above proof works even if s(n) is not space constructible. We just let s(n) increase as needed." The construction does exactly that. I quoted this from the paper's PDF. The design note is in #885.

## How

1. **Radix-parametric compact graph** (`ConfigurationGraph/*`). Vertex identifiers are packed in an arbitrary radix `B` instead of `(n+2)^D`. The new `overflow` test marks represented views that have a step leaving the radix.
   - `fits_of_not_overflow`: if no vertex reachable in the graph overflows, every reachable view of the source fits, with no space assumption on the source.
   - `fits_of_runsInSpace_of_le`: a space bound makes large radices fit.
   - The logarithmic-space lemmas and the STCON reduction (#887) now instantiate `B = (n+2)^D`.
2. **Honest final scan** (`Algorithms/Reachability/InductiveCounting`).
   - `exists_replay_done_final`: honest choices reach the final count check with every reachable vertex selected, even when a bad vertex is reachable.
   - `invariant_replay`, `mem_roundSet_final` and `rank_initial_le_budget` are now public.
3. **Growing radix** (`InductiveCounting/Machine.lean`, `Bounds.lean`, `Callbacks.lean`). The query machine stores a radix `B`, starting at `(n+2)·2^(|Q|+3)`, and runs Erik's controller on the graph of `B` in two modes:
   - **Unchecked.** The bad set is the overflowing vertices. If the final count check is complete and has met one, that vertex is certifiably reachable (`not_closed_of_overflowed`), and the machine moves to `4B`. If the controller accepts, `B` is closed.
   - **Checked.** The bad set is the accepting vertices, and the controller's verdict is final.

   The radix grows only on a certified overflow, so under the source's space bound every branch stays at or below round `J₀ = 4(c₁ s n + c₂) + 1` (`round_le`, `closed_of_runsInSpace`). That gives every-branch halting within `abstractTime` and every-prefix storage `O(J₀ + log n)` (`storageBound`). Correctness is `queryMachine_accepts_iff_not_accepts`. Its soundness direction uses no space bound.
4. **Credit.** The construction is adapted from Erik Demaine's inductive-counting machine (#465). Every file derived from his keeps his name in `Copyright`/`Authors:`, with mine added beside it: `InductiveCounting.lean`, `InductiveCounting/{Machine,Bounds,Callbacks,Graph}.lean`, `Classes/LogSpace/Complement.lean`, `ComplexityTests/NLComplement.lean` and the new `Classes/Space/Nondeterministic.lean`.

The fixed-exponent machine and `exists_decidesInLogSpace_compl` are deleted, with no deprecated aliases. All clients are updated, including tests, docs and ROADMAP. The packaged `queryIndex_inSpace`/`edgeWithSymbol_inSpace`/… routines are replaced by budget-parametric versions that take the radix as an argument.

## Plain-first note

All new public statements are plain. Tidy now appears only in the native compiler callbacks. Their internal budget lemmas in `InductiveCounting/Callbacks.lean` are now private, and the unused or packaged routines in `ConfigurationGraph/Routines.lean` are removed. The ratchet drops from 1301 to **1289**, and `scripts/tidy_surface_baseline.json` is lowered with `--update`. The remaining callbacks feed `NondeterministicQueryMachine.exists_decidesInSpace`, whose interface is `ComputableTidilyInSpace`; the missing plain rule is the same as in #887 (#862 step 5).

## Headline abstracts

- **Affected entry:** `immerman-szelepcsenyi`, from #918.
  - New headline `nspace_eq_conspace (enc) (s) (hs : ∀ n, Nat.log2 n ≤ s n)`, with `NSPACE` and `coNSPACE` stated in the abstract.
  - `nl_eq_conl` becomes its corollary, and `stcon_compl_mem_nl` stays as the supporting theorem.
  - The title, summary and scope now state the general bound and that no constructibility is assumed.
  - `#check_abstract` passes without an allowlist: 18 roots, 75 dependencies. The tests check by `rfl` that `NSPACE` and `coNSPACE` equal the library's.
- **Independent abstract review:** requested from `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023`; not yet done.
- **PDF artifact:** a local `build_abstracts.py` run from 803151a7 built all 15 PDFs, and the 3 pages of `immerman-szelepcsenyi.pdf` render cleanly. CI will produce the artifact.

## Validation

At 803151a7, stacked on bcd454c8 (#918) on main 45f7a884:
- `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates.
- `lake exe mk_all --check`, `check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `check_tidy_surface.py` (1289, matching the lowered baseline), `check_docs.py --config-only` and `build_abstracts.py --check` (15 abstracts, 21 headline theorems) all pass.

Tests:
- `ComplexityTests/NSPACE.lean`:
  - The theorem is instantiated at `log₂`, `id` and `n²`; none needs constructibility.
  - The classes are nonvacuous: `STCON ∈ NSPACE encSTCON log₂`, `STCON ∈ NSPACE encSTCON id`, and the complements of both.
  - `#print axioms NSPACE_eq_coNSPACE` and `#print axioms NL_eq_coNL` guards.
- `ComplexityTests/NLComplement.lean` (Erik's) is updated to the new API. It keeps the looping-source correctness, bootstrap, storage, halting and native-decider checks.
- `ComplexityTests/ConfigurationGraph.lean` is updated to the radix API.

Scope: 30 files relative to #918, under the 40-file threshold, so I did not split this PR.

body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-01 — APPROVED at c8cf27bd7162a2b36fc288c2765c78f3adbe7f9d

Agent review, not human approval. Hosted `ci-checks` is green at this head.

**Algorithm against Paturi–Pudlák–Zane (FOCS 1997).** `round` is PPZ:
- a uniform order of the `n` variables;
- each variable is set to satisfy a unit clause on it under the values already chosen (`IsUnitOn` requires every literal on `x` to have one polarity, so a tautological clause never forces);
- otherwise it gets a uniform bit.

**Proof.**
- **`forced_eq`.** Forced values are correct along a run that agrees with a solution.
- **`run_apply_restrict`.** In a fixed order, the run produces `σ` with probability exactly `2^{−u}`.
- **`exists_critical`.** Flipping `x` falsifies some clause, whose only true literals under `σ` are on `x`.
- **`card_isLast_mul`.** A fixed member of `S` is last in exactly a `1/|S|` fraction of the `n!` orders.
- **`unforcedCount_le`.** With `|vars c| ≤ c.length ≤ k`, the average number of unforced variables is at most `(1 − 1/k)n`.
- **`round_success`.** Weighted AM–GM gives `2^{−(1−1/k)n} ≤ Pr[round = σ]` for the unique solution of a CNF with clauses of at most `k ≥ 1` literals. That is the PPZ bound for unique k-SAT, with the paper's constant and no extra polynomial factor.
- **Scope.** The scope stated in the PR is accurate: unique k-SAT only. Isolated solutions, PPSZ, amplification and the time model remain open on #894.

**Tests, scope and hygiene.** The tests are concrete: a uniquely satisfiable 2-CNF with bound `1/2`, the `1/3` fraction for `n = 3`, and axiom guards. Scope is only the claimed files and bib (FOCS 1997, pp. 566–574, doi `10.1109/SFCS.1997.646146`). Hygiene is clean; the scan's "axiom" hit is the phrase "axiom guards" in the test docstring.

Nonblocking:
1. `card_isLast_mul`, and `IsLast` with the swap argument, are general facts about uniform orders and would be reusable from Foundations (`Equiv.Perm`/`Finset`). The other lemmas are specific to PPZ.
2. The PR title says "satisfiability coding lemma", but the formal content is the algorithmic form (`unforcedCount_le` plus `round_success`). Consider mentioning that the coding-lemma encoding (the values of unforced variables in a random order) is what `unforcedCount_le` bounds, and cite the journal version (Chicago J. Theor. Comput. Sci. 1999) if you use its lemma numbers.
3. If both a `true` and a `false` unit clause are present, `forced` prefers `true`. That never happens along runs that agree with `σ`, but a one-line docstring note would help readers.

title: feat(FineGrained): the satisfiability coding lemma and PPZ for unique k-SAT (#894)
body:
This PR covers part of **M3 of #894**: the **PPZ satisfiability coding lemma and its unique k-SAT bound**, from R. Paturi, P. Pudlák and F. Zane, *Satisfiability Coding Lemma* (FOCS 1997). It is independent of #908 (Schöning).

**Algorithm** (`FineGrained/PPZ.lean`, namespace `Cslib.Complexity.PPZ`). `round φ` draws a uniformly random order `π` of the `n` variables and processes them in that order:
- if a clause becomes a unit clause on the current variable under the values chosen so far (`IsUnitOn`, `forced`), set the variable to satisfy it;
- otherwise draw a uniform bit.

Tautological clauses never force.

**Results:**
- `forced_eq`: along a run that agrees with a satisfying `σ`, forced values agree with `σ`.
- `run_apply_restrict`: in a fixed order, the run produces `σ` with probability exactly `2^{−u}`, where `u` (`unforcedCount`) is the number of unforced steps along the run that agrees with `σ`.
- `exists_critical`: if `σ` is the unique solution, every variable `x` has a **critical clause**, in which the literals on `x` are true under `σ` and every other literal is false.
- `forced_ne_none_of_isLast`: a variable that comes after the other variables of its critical clause is forced.
- `card_isLast_mul`: a fixed member of a set `S` comes last in exactly a `1/|S|` fraction of the `n!` orders. The proof uses swap involutions, plus the fact that every order has exactly one last element.
- `round_success`: for the unique solution of a CNF whose clauses have at most `k ≥ 1` literals, one round succeeds with probability at least `2^{−(1−1/k)n}`. On average at most `(1−1/k)n` steps are unforced, and the weighted AM–GM inequality gives `E[2^{−u}] ≥ 2^{−E[u]}`.

**Scope.** This is PPZ for **unique** k-SAT.
- The general (non-unique) PPZ bound via isolated solutions is a natural follow-up, and I plan it next.
- PPSZ's `s`-implication bound (the rest of M3), Hertli's general case (M4), and amplification and the time model (M2) remain open on #894.
- I'll add a `ROADMAP.md` line after #908 lands, to avoid conflicting edits to the same row.

**Faithfulness.** This follows the PPZ unique-SAT analysis. The algorithm processes variables in a random order with unit-clause forcing, and the bound `2^{−(1−1/k)n}` is the paper's.

**Abstracts.** No impact.

**Validation** at `c8cf27bd`:
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six strict gates pass.
- `scripts/check_hygiene.py` passes.
- `ComplexityTests/PPZ.lean`:
  - a uniquely satisfiable 2-CNF, where `round_success` gives at least `1/2`;
  - the `1/3` fraction of orders for `S = Fin 3`;
  - axiom guards.

Also adds the `PPZ1997` bibliography entry.

title: refactor(Circuit/Boolean): make 74 API and general declarations public again (#926)
body:
Makes 74 declarations in Circuit/Boolean public again (51 API, 23 general mathematics), across 42 files. Earlier passes made them `private` because nothing outside their module used them (#841 (73), 59149961 (1)). Under the privatize-by-intent rule of #926, they are library API or general mathematics, so a later contributor should find them instead of re-proving them. Part of the audit tracked on #587.

**Classification rule** (#926, CONTRIBUTING "Public surface under the module system"):

- **GENERAL** becomes public: general mathematics (lists, finsets, arithmetic, probability, linear algebra). These belong in `Complexity/Foundations` and are listed below as follow-ups, not moved here.

body:
Makes 42 declarations in Logics, Algorithms and Computability/WordRAM public again (37 API, 5 general mathematics), across 24 files. Earlier passes made them `private` because nothing outside their module used them (#868 (25), #601 (8), #606 (5), #634 (3), 036aad37 (1)). Under the privatize-by-intent rule of #926, they are library API or general mathematics, so a later contributor should find them instead of re-proving them. Part of the audit tracked on #587.

**Classification rule** (#926, CONTRIBUTING "Public surface under the module system"):

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-01 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 62b4c2243a15f0f9ff321d6881785badb4327098

Agent review, not human approval. This PR would qualify for the delegated-review exception (classification: tooling, statement-preserving) once CI is green; the only blocker is CI.

**Blocking.** Hosted `ci-checks` fails at this head ([run 40153606846](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40153606846), "Test documentation checker"). The new `test_repository_bibliography_is_sorted` reports ``references.bib:4093: entry `Schoening1999` comes after `Zhao2023` ``. CI tests the merge with current `main`, where #908 appended `Schoening1999` after this branch's sort. Because of that failure, the source-hygiene, build, ratchet and new "Changed-file lints" steps never ran, so CI has not yet exercised the new step. The PR body cites this run as validation without saying that it failed.

Fix: rebase onto `main`, re-sort so that the entries added since the sort (at least `Schoening1999`) take their key positions, and get a green run that includes the "Changed-file lints" step.

**Checked and fine at this head:**
- **Bibliography is a pure reorder.** Against the merge base `e6769b48`, the 378 entries are the same multiset, byte-identical apart from trailing blank lines, and the preamble is unchanged. Keys are unique and sorted case-insensitively by the checker's `BIB_KEY_RE`, which strips cslib's padded keys. `docbuild/docs/references.bib` is a symlink, so `check_docs.py`'s byte-equality still holds. Moving the duplicate-key check from `check_docs.py` (nightly) into `check_hygiene.py` (every PR) is an improvement.
- **The lints are narrow.** `check_changed_files.py` checks only modules under `Complexity/` that the change adds or modifies, and test files under `ComplexityTests/` that it adds. Nothing library-wide is swept: the scan over all of `Complexity/` only collects declared syntax names. The CI step runs only on `pull_request` and `merge_group` and diffs against the event's base SHA, which is appropriate for the shallow checkout.
- **No tactic-name false positives.** `polytime`, `ppt`, `program_certificate`, Aesop rule sets and simp attributes resolve through the `syntax`/`macro`/`elab`/`declare_aesop_rule_sets`/`register_simp_attr` scan, plus a short upstream allowlist. Non-identifier text such as notation and `foo_*` is skipped. Your full-`main` run reports no unresolved names, so it should not fire on existing docs.
- **The restatement rule is conservative.** A new test file fails only if every `example` is `:= name` or `:= by exact name`. `rfl`, `trivial` and similar are exempt, as are `where`/equation examples and abstract clients.
- **Unit tests are meaningful.** They cover suffix resolution on component boundaries, syntax names, sections outside "Main …", lazy loading of the `.ilean` files, restatement versus concrete examples, added versus modified files, and the shallow-checkout fallback.

Nonblocking: after this lands, every open PR that appends a `references.bib` entry (several open #886, #892, #894 and #896 milestones do) will fail hygiene until its entry is moved into key order. A short note in #949 or the coordination thread would save those authors a CI round.

title: ci(scripts): lint module-doc names and restatement-only tests in changed files
body:
Part of #949 (consolidation tooling). Two narrow, diagnostic lints that run in CI only on the files a pull request adds or changes, plus a sorted `references.bib`.

## Lints (`scripts/check_changed_files.py`)

- **Module-doc names.** In a changed module under `Complexity/`, each backquoted name that heads a bullet of a "Main …" section of the module docstring (the names before the bullet's first colon) must name a declaration. A name resolves when some library, test or abstract module defines or refers to it, according to the build's `.ilean` files, matched exactly or as a suffix on a component boundary. Tactic, attribute and rule-set names that the library declares (`syntax`, `macro`, `elab`, `declare_aesop_rule_sets`, `register_simp_attr`) also resolve, such as `polytime`, `ppt` and `program_certificate`. So does a commented allowlist of nine upstream tactic names (`fun_prop`, `simp`, …). Backquoted text that isn't an identifier, such as `Qᶜ` or `foo_*`, isn't checked.
- **Restatement-only tests.** A *new* file under `ComplexityTests/` fails when it has examples and every one is `example … := name` (or `:= by exact name`), unless it imports or names `ComplexityAbstracts`. The rule doesn't count `rfl`, `trivial` and similar terms as restatements, because they check a statement by evaluation. It doesn't police test quality beyond that.

The CI step "Changed-file lints" runs after the build on `pull_request` and `merge_group` events. It fetches the event's base commit and compares against it directly, because the checkout is shallow. Run locally, the script compares against the merge base with `origin/main`, including uncommitted and untracked files.

**Over all of current `main`** (not only changed files): the doc-name lint finds no unresolved names in 2,011 modules (14,624 listed names). Two existing test files consist only of restatements: `ComplexityTests/Smoke.lean` and `ComplexityTests/ListBasicImports.lean`, both import smoke tests. The lint applies only to new files, so they aren't flagged. This PR changes no Lean file, so nothing needed fixing or allowlisting.

## Sorted bibliography (separate commit)

`references.bib` is sorted by key, case-insensitively as BibTeX compares keys, with one blank line between entries. The multiset of the 379 entries is unchanged, including `Schoening1999` from #908, which landed after the first sort. The check compared entry texts before and after, and only one missing and one doubled blank line between entries changed. `scripts/check_hygiene.py`, which runs on every PR, now checks that keys are unique and sorted. It takes over the duplicate-key check that `scripts/check_docs.py` ran only in the nightly docs build. With entries placed by key, two PRs adding citations conflict only when their keys are adjacent.

**Once this lands, any open PR that appends a `references.bib` entry needs one re-sort:** a rebase that moves each new entry to its place in key order.

## Validation

- Hosted CI at `bfa72cfa`, rebased onto `main` `c89dd48c`: [Lean Action CI run 40154272379](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40154272379), success. Every step ran, including the new "Changed-file lints" step against base `c89dd48c`. The earlier run at `62b4c224` failed: the merge with `main` contained #908's `Schoening1999` out of order. The rebase re-sorts it.
- Unit tests in `scripts/test_check_changed_files.py` and new cases in `scripts/test_check_hygiene.py`.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-02 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 8055ecfe670b92569278c301762983af700b28f8 (agent review; classification: documentation-only, under the delegated-review exception. Samuel's editorial review still applies.)

I read all 1,724 old lines against the new file. Every open item in the old file has a home in the new one. The only dropped issue reference that is still open is #608, which is step 2 of the linked #862. Specific checks:
- **"Done by #121" is correct.** `Ordered/FullTuple.lean` builds the canonical numeric interpretation, and for `n ≥ 2` and positive dimension the result is isomorphic to the canonically ordered rank universe with genuine numeric constants. The old "Still outstanding" line was stale. The projection-specific remainder survives at new `:181–184`.
- **Dropping `P^PP = PP` is a fair call.** By Toda's theorem it would give PH ⊆ PP, so it is an open problem, not a library direction.
- **The recovered checklist items are real gaps:** there is no `WordRAM/Dynamic/Eval.lean`; `SensitivitySeparation/Internal/Defs.lean` exists; the guide has only `FirstSteps` and `NPCompleteness` (#585 is open).

**Blocking**

1. **Stale after #915.** Main's ROADMAP now records 2SAT as NL-complete (`Problems/TwoSAT/Completeness.lean`), and this head conflicts on `ROADMAP.md`. New `:141` still lists "2SAT NL-complete" as open. On restack, drop it so the line reads `NSPACE(s) = coNSPACE(s)` and general Savitch bounds.
2. **The FHE context is not held by #513.** #513 is a closed documentation issue whose deliverable *was* that ROADMAP section (merged in #515). Its body has no workload table, vendor paragraph, HEXL/OpenFHE references or eprint links. As written, new `:56–57` ("[#513] maps the schemes…") points at nothing that holds the content. Suggested fix: add one line near the top linking the pre-rewrite file at a fixed revision (e.g. `blob/c89dd48c/ROADMAP.md`). That one link also preserves the FO decision record, the repository-identity rationale and the "historical roadmap" link that the old file kept. Point the FHE sentence at that section, and keep the eprint links on the five scheme names (Ducas–Micciancio 2014/816, CGGI 2016/870, BGV 2011/277, FV 2012/144, CKKS 2016/421).
3. **The composite-moduli direction overreaches.** New `:159` reads "Boolean closures of the modular classes for composite moduli". For moduli that are not prime powers (e.g. Mod₆P), closure under complement is open. Barrington–Beigel–Rudich give an oracle relative to which ModₘP is closed under complement and union iff `m` is a prime power, so a relativizing proof cannot reach it. By the PR's own `P^PP = PP` criterion, narrow it, e.g. "the prime-power collapse `Mod_{p^e}P = Mod_pP` and union closure for composite moduli; complement closure for non-prime-power moduli is open".

**For Samuel: priority ordering.** I recommend restoring it. The old "Highest priorities" ranked ten landmarks: GMW, Rompel, Gentry, OT completeness, Håstad, Williams ACC, Valiant, Kabanets–Impagliazzo, MIP = NEXP, Regev. The PR body says priorities now live in #897's tiers, but #897 covers only Håstad, Williams, Kabanets–Impagliazzo and MIP = NEXP. It does not cover GMW, Rompel, the OT theorem, Regev or Valiant, and the file itself says nothing about where priorities live. The crypto section's numbering 1–5 now reads as a crypto-only order. A cheap fix is a 10-line "Landmark theorems, in priority order" index under *Programs*, one line each linking to its area entry or issue. Alternatively, add one sentence naming where the ranking lives.

**Nonblocking**

- New `:35–36`: "derive the advice-PRG premise … from uniform one-wayness". Goldreich proves the auxiliary-input theorem from *nonuniformly* one-way functions, and uniform one-wayness is not known to give an advice-secure PRG. Consider "state it under nonuniformly one-way functions (Goldreich, Theorem 4.4.11) and derive the advice-PRG premise from that".
- New `:356–358`: `Literal.eval` already has simp lemmas (`Literal.eval_mk`, `eval_eq_true_iff`, `eval_negate`, `CNF.lean:86–95`). `CNF/PolyTime.lean:202` passes `CNF.eval`/`Clause.eval`/`Literal.eval` to `fun_prop` as unfold hints, so the real gap is the `fun_prop` certificates.
- New `:305–306` lists "MINKT/MINCKT as independently scoped developments", but `Kolmogorov/MINKT.lean` already defines MINKT, proves MINKT ∈ NP and defines GapMINKT under #798. Name what remains (MINCKT, hardness) instead.
- FO: the dropped sentence "numeric predicates are computed from the universe size, not supplied as unverified input tables" is a standing convention for the restricted-domain certificate work (new `:188`), not history. It is worth keeping.
- The removed GSW limitations "no generator for the leveled scheme's wrapper decryption circuits" and "evaluated wrapper ciphertexts are not promised reusable as fresh inputs" read as open targets (uniform compactness, multi-hop evaluation). Either list them under the Gentry item or decide they are out of scope.
- Quantum (`:308–310`) lost "uniformity and approximation costs, amplification, containments and complete problems" from the old canon row.

title: doc(roadmap): rewrite as a short plan of open directions
body:
Part of #949 (R2). This is an editorial draft, so Samuel reviews it. It is rebased onto `main` after #915, which made 2SAT NL-complete, so that item is dropped.

`ROADMAP.md` goes from 1,724 lines to about 450. It is now a forward-looking plan of directions only, grouped by area, with links to the tracking issues: #897 and its tracks (#886, #888–#896, #459, #474), #862, #798, #486, #885 and #949. Status lines, completion notes, partial-progress paragraphs and per-PR records are gone; issues, PRs, module docstrings, the README and the curated abstracts hold those. Every open direction in the old file is kept. Open items with no issue stay as direction lines, and no issues are invented. A short ranked index under *Programs* keeps the old "Highest priorities" order of the ten landmark theorems. Each entry links to its area section; the file says that priorities live there and in #897's tiers. A link to the pre-rewrite file, pinned at `c89dd48c`, serves as the archive of past detail and design records.

## Removed, and not pure status (please check)
- **FHE industrial context:** the table of workloads and libraries, the vendor deployment paragraph, the Intel HEXL implementation target and the OpenFHE bootstrap reference. The FHE section links the pinned pre-rewrite section for this context. The five FHE directions keep their eprint links, and the per-scheme requirements are kept in shorter form.
- **Repository identity and home:** the name history, the rationale for the move to CSLib Community, and the four maintenance requirements: auditable claims, reproducible validation, a usable contribution path, one active project. Only the open direction, archiving `complexitylib-v1`, remains.
- **The measurement paragraph of "Measure reuse across papers":** measuring shared code, proof and interface size, and elaboration cost per paper. It is a metric target. The paper-sample direction is kept.
- **"Candidate proof improvements" guidance:** judging changes by proof burden and elaboration cost, comparing with `scripts/proof_lengths.py`, and the historical-roadmap link. The one candidate is kept.
- **The scope paragraph of "Approximation and Fusion milestones":** explicit source models, and where the counting barrier applies. Every milestone there is proved, and the module docstrings record their scope.
- **Process notes:** the preamble of "Finishing the recovered developments" (the six checks and independent reviews before closing a milestone), "upstream API coordination and coordinator review remain prerequisites" for stateful structures, and "the TQBF, PCP and GMW bridges are recorded on #643". The roadmap's intro keeps the rule that a direction is complete only with its machine, resource and quantitative conclusions.
- **First-order design history:** the 2026-10-19 decision record and its correction of `n ≥ 1`, and the rationale that order-free SAT-to-3SAT appears to need an order. The resulting convention is kept, including that numeric predicates are computed from the universe size.
- **Limitation statements** of the form "this does not establish X", unless they named an open target. The two GSW limitations are kept as Gentry targets: uniform compactness and multi-hop evaluation.
- **Rationale sentences:** existing cryptographic learners are not coverage of learning theory, the unrestricted prescribed-width-to-uniform converse is false, and no real-RAM/Turing-machine equivalence is claimed. Their directions are kept.

## Judgment calls (please check)
- **Dropped as apparently complete:** "the classical positive-dimensional full-universe specialization and canonical numeric preservation" under FO projections. The #121 FullTuple entry in the same file describes it as done.
- **Dropped as an open research problem, not a library direction:** "closure of PP under adaptive Turing reductions (`P^PP = PP`) … is open and not claimed."
- **Rephrased from a limitation into a direction:**
  - "The current modular Boolean closures require a prime modulus" became the prime-power collapse and union closure for composite moduli. Complement closure for moduli that are not prime powers is open, and relativizing proofs cannot give it (Barrington–Beigel–Rudich), so it is not a direction.
  - "No implication from uniform one-wayness/HILL to `GMW.AdvicePRG` is proved" became: state the theorem under nonuniformly one-way functions, as Goldreich does (Vol. 1, Section 4.4), and derive the nonuniform PRG premise from that.
- **Added from #897** but not in the old file: randomized logspace (#459, #474), lifting (#890), Limaye–Srinivasan–Tavenas lower bounds (#891), GKR (#892), quantum foundations (#896), and the note that 2-to-2 games waits for #886.

## Recovered from closed checklists
I scanned the bodies and last comments of #590, #591, #596, #610 and #614. Most items are done (for example `CNF.distinctVars`, `GapMCSP` as a `PromiseProblem`, `PolyTimeOracleProgram`, the PMF split, `BitString/Binary`). Others are process or metric items, or small refactors now covered by #949 and #939. These open directions are kept as roadmap lines:
- **Guide chapters (#585) per area:** Foundations (bit strings, Fourier analysis, PMF/`ProbComp`, codes), proof complexity, descriptive complexity, and Word RAM and algorithms. From #614 E9, #596 item 9 and #591. The guide now has only `FirstSteps` and `NPCompleteness`.
- **A typed-call evaluator for fixed-program Word-RAM clients**, returning the observation, final state and halt-inclusive cost. From #591's first candidate; `WordRAM/Dynamic/Eval.lean` does not exist.
- **One sensitivity API over any `Fintype`, in CSLib**, dropping the separate measures in `SensitivitySeparation/Internal/Defs.lean`. From #610 item 6.
- **CNF evaluation certificates:** `fun_prop` certificates for literal, clause and formula evaluation. From #596 item 6. `CNF/PolyTime.lean` still passes `CNF.eval`, `Clause.eval` and `Literal.eval` to `fun_prop` as unfolding hints; the `Literal.eval` simp lemmas already exist.

## Validation
Documentation only. Hosted CI at `2b55066a`: [Lean Action CI run 40156654904](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40156654904), success.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-02 — APPROVED at 0ee21837e9f41915603adc61ad4cf121fd4f4efb (agent review, not human approval)

The reftable copy can only write under `dst`. That directory was just removed and recreated by `isolate_git_dir`, and `shutil.copytree(..., symlinks=False)` copies file contents (not links or hardlinks) into `dst/reftable`. So ref updates in the copy rewrite private files and cannot reach the source, and nothing outside `dst` is deleted. The existing post-copy validation (toplevel, gitdir and commondir must equal the isolated directory) still runs. The new test checks both HEAD resolution and that the source is untouched after an `update-ref` in the copy. CI: https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40158112257.

Nit: as with `refs/`, the code copies `gitdir/reftable` *or* `commondir/reftable`. For a linked-worktree source, the shared branch refs live only in the common reftable. That case is out of scope for `.lake/packages` clones, but worth a comment.

title: fix(worktree): copy reftable refs when isolating dependency git dirs
body:
Fixes 966. `isolate_git_dir` now copies the dependency's `reftable/` directory when it exists. Without it, a package using the reftable ref format has no resolvable HEAD in the worktree copy, so Lake's checkout after a pin bump fails with a reftable I/O error.

The regression test `test_reftable_dependency_refs_are_copied` creates a reftable dependency, seeds a worktree and checks two things: HEAD resolves in the copy, and a ref update in the copy leaves the primary package unchanged. It is skipped when git lacks reftable support. It fails without the fix. The full `scripts/test_worktree.py` passes (28 tests).

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body: [P1] The pinned [Definition 2.5, p.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.11514v1#page=9) uses the symmetric event `|H(x) - f(x)| ≤ g(n)`. This definition uses `f(x)-g(n) ≤ v ∧ v ≤ f(x)`, so it rejects every overestimate. For example, f=0, H=1, g=1 is successful under the source event and unsuccessful here. Please make the canonical PPT approximation notion symmetric (e.g. `Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g n`) and derive the advertised theorem for it. The one-sided form can remain a clearly named helper: shifting a symmetric estimator down by g converts a g-error into a one-sided 2g-error when the shift is efficiently computable. Account for the rounded-log convention too. A docstring note alone does not supply this missing bridge.
