+/-!
+# Average-case hardness of time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity (`K^t`)
+
+This module formalizes the average-case hardness notions and information-theoretic building blocks
+from [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020]. All
+section, definition, theorem, lemma, and page locators follow the full version
+`arXiv:2009.11514v1` (and ECCC TR20-052), in which `Theorem`/`Definition` share one section
+counter while `Lemma`/`Fact` share a separate section counter.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverage`: mild average-case hardness of exact computation for
+  `List Bool → ℕ` against uniform strict PPT heuristics
+  ([Liu and Pass, Definition 2.4, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`: mild average-case hardness of $g(n)$-approximation
+  for `List Bool → ℕ` against uniform strict PPT heuristics
+  ([Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageDet`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`:
+  library specializations of `MildlyHardOnAverage` and `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` to
+  deterministic polynomial-time heuristics.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageIO`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`:
+  library infinitely-often (`∃ᶠ n in atTop`) companions.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageENat`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageIOENat`:
+  library `ℕ∞`-valued companions for `List Bool → ℕ∞` (such as `timeBounded t`).
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Probability.PMF.entropy_ge_of_dist_uniform_le`: if $X$ is a distribution on
+  $\{0, 1\}^n$ with $\mathsf{SD}(X, U_n) \le 1 / n^2$, then $H(X) \ge n - 2$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Lemma 2.2, §2.5, p. 9 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Probability.PMF.sum_filter_mass_le_ge_of_entropy_ge`: if $Y$ is a distribution on
+  $\{0, 1\}^m$ ($m \ge 1$) with $H(Y) \ge B \ge 3$, then the set of outcomes with point mass at
+  most $2^{-(B - 3)}$ has total probability at least $1 / m$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 5.2, Claim 2, §5.2, p. 12 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_timeBounded_generator_le`: for any length-nondecreasing
+  polynomial-time generator $G : \{0, 1\}^* \to \{0, 1\}^*$, there exist a polynomial $p_G$ and a
+  constant $c$ such that for all $t \ge p_G$ and all $z$, $K^t(G(z)) \le |z| + c$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 5.2, Equation (3), §5.2, pp. 11–12 of
+  arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.sum_uniform_timeBoundedNat_lt_le`: counting bound on the fraction of $n$-bit
+  strings with $K^t(x) < n - k$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 5.2, Equation (2), §5.2, p. 11 of
+  arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+
+## References
+
+* [Y. Liu, R. Pass, *On One-way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],
+  full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1` (Sections 2.3, 2.5, and 5.2).
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Probability.PMF
+
+open Cslib
+open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
+
+/-- Auxiliary bound: for any $q \in (0, 1]$, $-q \log_2 q \le 2$. -/
+private theorem mul_neg_logb_two_le_two {q : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) :
+    q * (-Real.logb 2 q) ≤ 2 := by
+  have hlog_half := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 2)
+  rw [one_div, Real.log_inv] at hlog_half
+  have hlog2 : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ Real.log 2 := by linarith
+  have hlog_inv : Real.log (1 / q) ≤ 1 / q - 1 :=
+    Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (one_div_pos.mpr hq0)
+  have hq_log : q * (-Real.log q) ≤ 1 - q := by
+    have h1 : -Real.log q = Real.log (1 / q) := by
+      rw [one_div, Real.log_inv]
+    rw [h1]
+    have hmul := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hlog_inv hq0.le
+    rwa [mul_sub, mul_one_div_cancel hq0.ne', mul_one] at hmul
+  rw [Real.logb, ← neg_div, ← mul_div_assoc]
+  have hnum : q * -Real.log q ≤ 1 := by linarith
+  calc
+    (q * -Real.log q) / Real.log 2 ≤ 1 / Real.log 2 :=
+      div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hnum (by linarith)
+    _ ≤ 1 / (1 / 2) := one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by norm_num) hlog2
+    _ = 2 := by norm_num
+
+/-- **General statistical-distance-to-entropy lower bound.**
+For any distribution $p$ on `BitString n`, the mass of outcomes with probability strictly above
+$2^{-(n - 1)}$ is at most $2 \cdot \mathsf{SD}(p, U_n)$, so
+$H(p) \ge (n - 1)(1 - 2 \cdot \mathsf{SD}(p, U_n))$. -/
+theorem entropy_ge_of_dist_uniform {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (p : PMF (BitString n)) :
+    ((n : ℝ) - 1) * (1 - 2 * dist p (PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString n))) ≤ entropy p := by
+  classical
+  let U := PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString n)
+  have hU_apply (x : BitString n) : (U x).toReal = (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) := by
+    rw [Real.rpow_neg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2), Real.rpow_natCast]
+    simp [U, uniformOfFintype_apply]
+  let S₁ : Finset (BitString n) :=
+    Finset.univ.filter fun x => (p x).toReal ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (-((n : ℝ) - 1))
+  let S₂ : Finset (BitString n) :=
+    Finset.univ.filter fun x => (2 : ℝ) ^ (-((n : ℝ) - 1)) < (p x).toReal
+  have htwo_pow : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-((n : ℝ) - 1)) = 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) := by
+    rw [show -((n : ℝ) - 1) = 1 + -(n : ℝ) by ring, Real.rpow_add (by norm_num), Real.rpow_one]
+  have hS₂_sub : S₂ ⊆ Finset.univ.filter fun x => (U x).toReal < (p x).toReal := by
+    intro x hx
+    simp only [S₂, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx ⊢
+    rw [hU_apply]
+    have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by norm_num) _
+    linarith [htwo_pow]
+  have hS₂_mass : ∑ x ∈ S₂, (p x).toReal ≤ 2 * dist p U := by
+    rw [dist_eq_sum_filter_lt p U, Finset.mul_sum]
+    calc
+      ∑ x ∈ S₂, (p x).toReal ≤ ∑ x ∈ S₂, 2 * ((p x).toReal - (U x).toReal) := by
+        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun x hx => ?_
+        simp only [S₂, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx
+        rw [hU_apply]
+        linarith [htwo_pow]
+      _ ≤ ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => (U x).toReal < (p x).toReal),
+            2 * ((p x).toReal - (U x).toReal) := by
+        refine Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg hS₂_sub fun x hx _ => ?_
+        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx
+        linarith
+  have hpart : (∑ x ∈ S₁, (p x).toReal) + ∑ x ∈ S₂, (p x).toReal = 1 := by
+    have hcompl : S₂ = S₁ᶜ := by
+      ext x
+      simp [S₁, S₂, not_le]
+    rw [hcompl, Finset.sum_add_sum_compl, sum_toReal]
+  have hS₁_mass : 1 - 2 * dist p U ≤ ∑ x ∈ S₁, (p x).toReal := by linarith
+  have hsurp (x : BitString n) (hx : x ∈ S₁) :
+      (p x).toReal * ((n : ℝ) - 1) ≤ (p x).toReal * surprisal p x := by
+    by_cases hp0 : (p x).toReal = 0
+    · simp [hp0]
+    · have hpos : 0 < (p x).toReal :=
+        lt_of_le_of_ne ENNReal.toReal_nonneg (Ne.symm hp0)
+      apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ hpos.le
+      simp only [S₁, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx
+      rw [surprisal, le_neg]
+      exact (Real.logb_le_iff_le_rpow (by norm_num) hpos).mpr hx
+  have hn_real : 1 ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
+  rw [entropy_eq_sum_surprisal]
+  calc
+    ((n : ℝ) - 1) * (1 - 2 * dist p U)
+      ≤ ((n : ℝ) - 1) * ∑ x ∈ S₁, (p x).toReal :=
+        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hS₁_mass (by linarith)
+    _ = ∑ x ∈ S₁, (p x).toReal * ((n : ℝ) - 1) := by
+        rw [Finset.mul_sum]
+        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => mul_comm _ _
+    _ ≤ ∑ x ∈ S₁, (p x).toReal * surprisal p x :=
+        Finset.sum_le_sum fun x hx => hsurp x hx
+    _ ≤ ∑ x, (p x).toReal * surprisal p x :=
+        Finset.sum_le_univ_sum_of_nonneg fun x =>
+          mul_nonneg ENNReal.toReal_nonneg (surprisal_nonneg p x)
+
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Lemma 2.2, §2.5, p. 9 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]: Statistical
+distance to uniform bounds Shannon entropy from below.**
+If $n \ge 4$ (and in fact for any $n$) and $\mathsf{SD}(p, U_n) \le 1 / n^2$, then
+$H(p) \ge n - 2$. -/
+theorem entropy_ge_of_dist_uniform_le {n : ℕ} (p : PMF (BitString n))
+    (hdist : dist p (PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString n)) ≤ 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) :
+    (n : ℝ) - 2 ≤ entropy p := by
+  rcases le_or_gt n 1 with hn1 | hn1
+  · have hent : 0 ≤ entropy p := entropy_nonneg p
+    have hn_le : (n : ℝ) ≤ 1 := by exact_mod_cast hn1
+    linarith
+  have hn_pos : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 0 < n)
+  have h1 := entropy_ge_of_dist_uniform hn1.le p
+  have hn_ge : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) - 1 := by
+    have : (2 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn1
+    linarith
+  have h2 : ((n : ℝ) - 1) * (1 - 2 * (1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) ≤
+      ((n : ℝ) - 1) * (1 - 2 * dist p (PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString n))) := by
+    refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ?_ (by linarith)
+    linarith
+  have h3 : (n : ℝ) - 2 ≤ ((n : ℝ) - 1) * (1 - 2 * (1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) := by
+    have hsq : 0 < (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := sq_pos_of_pos hn_pos
+    have hquad : 2 * ((n : ℝ) - 1) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
+      nlinarith [sq_nonneg ((n : ℝ) - 1)]
+    have hdiv : 2 * ((n : ℝ) - 1) * (1 / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) ≤ 1 := by
+      rw [mul_one_div]
+      exact (div_le_one hsq).mpr hquad
+    linarith
+  linarith
+
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 5.2, Claim 2, §5.2, p. 12 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]:
+High Shannon entropy implies non-negligible mass on low-probability outcomes.**
+For any distribution $p$ on `BitString m` with $m \ge 1$ and $B \ge 3$ such that $H(p) \ge B$,
+the set of outcomes $y$ with point mass $p(y) \le 2^{-(B - 3)}$ has total probability at least
+$1 / m$. -/
+theorem sum_filter_mass_le_ge_of_entropy_ge {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (p : PMF (BitString m))
+    {B : ℝ} (hB : 3 ≤ B) (hent : B ≤ entropy p) :
+    1 / (m : ℝ) ≤
+      ∑ y ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun y => (p y).toReal ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(B - 3))), (p y).toReal := by
+  classical
+  let S : Finset (BitString m) :=
+    Finset.univ.filter fun y => (p y).toReal ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(B - 3))
+  let q : ℝ := ∑ y ∈ S, (p y).toReal
+  change 1 / (m : ℝ) ≤ q
+  have hm_pos : (0 : ℝ) < m := by exact_mod_cast hm
+  -- Bound the contribution outside S: every y ∉ S has surprisal p y ≤ B - 3
+  have hout : ∑ y ∈ Sᶜ, (p y).toReal * surprisal p y ≤ B - 3 := by
+    have hterm (y : BitString m) (hy : y ∈ Sᶜ) :
+        (p y).toReal * surprisal p y ≤ (p y).toReal * (B - 3) := by
+      simp only [S, Finset.mem_compl, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, not_le] at hy
+      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (surprisal_le_of_mass_ge p y hy.le) ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
+    calc
+      ∑ y ∈ Sᶜ, (p y).toReal * surprisal p y
+        ≤ ∑ y ∈ Sᶜ, (p y).toReal * (B - 3) := Finset.sum_le_sum hterm
+      _ = (∑ y ∈ Sᶜ, (p y).toReal) * (B - 3) := (Finset.sum_mul _ _ _).symm
+      _ ≤ 1 * (B - 3) := by
+        refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ?_ (by linarith)
+        calc
+          ∑ y ∈ Sᶜ, (p y).toReal ≤ ∑ y : BitString m, (p y).toReal :=
+            Finset.sum_le_univ_sum_of_nonneg fun _ => ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
+          _ = 1 := sum_toReal p
+      _ = B - 3 := one_mul _
+  -- Bound the contribution inside S by q * m + 2
+  have hin : ∑ y ∈ S, (p y).toReal * surprisal p y ≤ q * (m : ℝ) + 2 := by
+    by_cases hq0 : q = 0
+    · have hall0 : ∀ y ∈ S, (p y).toReal = 0 :=
+        (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun _ _ => ENNReal.toReal_nonneg).mp hq0
+      have hsum0 : ∑ y ∈ S, (p y).toReal * surprisal p y = 0 :=
+        Finset.sum_eq_zero fun y hy => by simp [hall0 y hy]
+      rw [hsum0, hq0]
+      linarith
+    · have hq_nonneg : 0 ≤ q := Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
+      have hq_pos : 0 < q := lt_of_le_of_ne hq_nonneg (Ne.symm hq0)
+      have hex : ∃ y ∈ (S : Set (BitString m)), y ∈ p.support := by
+        by_contra! hno
+        have hzero : q = 0 := Finset.sum_eq_zero fun y hy => by
+          have := hno y hy
+          rw [PMF.mem_support_iff, not_not] at this
+          simp [this]
+        exact hq0 hzero
+      let pS := p.filter (S : Set (BitString m)) hex
+      have hmeas : (p.toOuterMeasure (S : Set (BitString m))).toReal = q := by
+        rw [toOuterMeasure_apply_toReal]
+        simp [q]
+      have hent_pS : entropy pS ≤ m := by
+        have hcard := entropy_le_log_card pS
+        rwa [show Fintype.card (BitString m) = 2 ^ m by simp, Nat.cast_pow, Nat.cast_ofNat,
+          Real.logb_pow, Real.logb_self_eq_one (by norm_num), mul_one] at hcard
+      have hident : ∑ y ∈ S, (p y).toReal * surprisal p y =
+          q * entropy pS + q * (-Real.logb 2 q) := by
+        rw [entropy_eq_sum_surprisal pS, Finset.mul_sum]
+        have hcompl0 : ∑ y ∈ Sᶜ, q * ((pS y).toReal * surprisal pS y) = 0 := by
+          refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun y hy => ?_
+          simp only [Finset.mem_compl] at hy
+          have hpSy : (pS y).toReal = 0 := by
+            simp [pS, hy]
+          simp [hpSy]
+        have hq_sum : q * (-Real.logb 2 q) = ∑ y ∈ S, (p y).toReal * (-Real.logb 2 q) :=
+          Finset.sum_mul S (fun y => (p y).toReal) (-Real.logb 2 q)
+        rw [← Finset.sum_add_sum_compl S, hcompl0, add_zero, hq_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y hy => ?_
+        by_cases hpy0 : (p y).toReal = 0
+        · have hpSy : (pS y).toReal = 0 := by
+            simp [pS, hy, hpy0]
+          simp [hpy0, hpSy]
+        · have hpy_pos : 0 < (p y).toReal :=
+            lt_of_le_of_ne ENNReal.toReal_nonneg (Ne.symm hpy0)
+          have hpSy : (pS y).toReal = (p y).toReal / q := by
+            dsimp [pS]
+            rw [filter_apply_toReal, ite_eq_left (Finset.mem_coe.mpr hy), hmeas]
+          have hq_mul : q * (pS y).toReal = (p y).toReal := by
+            rw [hpSy, mul_div_cancel₀ _ hq_pos.ne']
+          rw [← mul_assoc, hq_mul]
+          simp only [surprisal, hpSy, Real.logb_div hpy_pos.ne' hq_pos.ne']
+          ring
+      have hq_log := mul_neg_logb_two_le_two hq_pos
+      have hq_ent : q * entropy pS ≤ q * (m : ℝ) :=
+        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hent_pS hq_pos.le
+      linarith
+  have htotal : entropy p =
+      (∑ y ∈ S, (p y).toReal * surprisal p y) + ∑ y ∈ Sᶜ, (p y).toReal * surprisal p y := by
+    rw [entropy_eq_sum_surprisal, ← Finset.sum_add_sum_compl S]
+  have h1 : 1 ≤ q * (m : ℝ) := by linarith
+  exact (div_le_iff₀ hm_pos).mpr (by linarith)
+
+/-- Truncating an `m`-bit distribution to its first `k ≤ m` bits decreases Shannon entropy by at
+most `m - k` bits. -/
+theorem entropy_ofList_take_ge {m k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ m) (p : PMF (BitString m)) :
+    entropy p - ((m - k : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
+      entropy (p.map fun x => BitString.ofList k ((List.ofFn x).take k)) := by
+  let split (x : BitString m) : BitString k × BitString (m - k) :=
+    (BitString.ofList k ((List.ofFn x).take k),
+      BitString.ofList (m - k) ((List.ofFn x).drop k))
+  have hinj : Function.Injective split := by
+    intro x y hxy
+    have h1 := congrArg (List.ofFn ∘ Prod.fst) hxy
+    have h2 := congrArg (List.ofFn ∘ Prod.snd) hxy
+    dsimp only [Function.comp_apply, split] at h1 h2
+    rw [BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp [hk]), BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp [hk])] at h1
+    rw [BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp), BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp)] at h2
+    apply List.ofFn_inj.mp
+    rw [← List.take_append_drop k (List.ofFn x), ← List.take_append_drop k (List.ofFn y), h1, h2]
+  have hjoint : entropy (p.map split) = entropy p := entropy_map_of_injective p hinj
+  have hfst : (p.map split).map Prod.fst =
+      p.map fun x => BitString.ofList k ((List.ofFn x).take k) := by
+    rw [PMF.map_comp]
+    rfl
+  have hcond := conditionalEntropy_le_log_card (p.map split)
+  rw [conditionalEntropy, hjoint, hfst,
+    show Fintype.card (BitString (m - k)) = 2 ^ (m - k) by simp,
+    Nat.cast_pow, Nat.cast_ofNat, Real.logb_pow, Real.logb_self_eq_one (by norm_num),
+    mul_one] at hcond
+  linarith
+
+/-- Appending `k` independent uniform bits to an `m`-bit distribution increases Shannon entropy
+by exactly `k` bits. -/
+theorem entropy_append_uniform {m k : ℕ} (p : PMF (BitString m)) :
+    entropy (p.bind fun x => (PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString k)).map fun z =>
+      BitString.ofList (m + k) (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn z)) =
+      entropy p + (k : ℝ) := by
+  let join (xz : BitString m × BitString k) : BitString (m + k) :=
+    BitString.ofList (m + k) (List.ofFn xz.1 ++ List.ofFn xz.2)
+  have hinj : Function.Injective join := by
+    rintro ⟨x₁, z₁⟩ ⟨x₂, z₂⟩ hxy
+    have h := congrArg List.ofFn hxy
+    dsimp only [join] at h
+    rw [BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp), BitString.ofFn_ofList (by simp)] at h
+    obtain ⟨hx, hz⟩ := List.append_inj h (by simp)
+    exact Prod.ext (List.ofFn_inj.mp hx) (List.ofFn_inj.mp hz)
+  have hmap : (p.bind fun x => (PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString k)).map (x, ·)).map join =
+      p.bind fun x => (PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString k)).map fun z =>
+        BitString.ofList (m + k) (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn z) := by
+    simp only [PMF.map_bind, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, join]
+  rw [← hmap, entropy_map_of_injective _ hinj, entropy_prod, entropy_uniform,
+    show Fintype.card (BitString k) = 2 ^ k by simp,
+    Nat.cast_pow, Nat.cast_ofNat, Real.logb_pow, Real.logb_self_eq_one (by norm_num), mul_one]
+
+end Cslib.Probability.PMF
+
+namespace Cslib.Kolmogorov
+
+open Filter Cslib.Probability Cslib.Probability.PMF Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+/-! ### Average-case hardness definitions
+([Liu and Pass, Definitions 2.4 and 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]) -/
+
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.4, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]:
+Mildly hard on average (`MildlyHardOnAverage`).**
+A function $f : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathbb{N}$ is mildly hard on average if there exists a positive
+polynomial $p$ such that for every uniform strict PPT heuristic
+$\mathcal{H} : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathrm{ProbComp}\ \mathbb{N}$, for all sufficiently large
+$n \in \mathbb{N}$,
+$$\Pr_{x \leftarrow \{0, 1\}^n, v \leftarrow \mathcal{H}(x)}[v = f(x)] \le 1 - \frac{1}{p(n)}.$$ -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverage (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ, IsPPTOn encBits encNat H →
+      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+          (ProbComp.eval (H x)).map fun v => decide (v = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]:
+Mildly hard on average to $g$-approximate (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`).**
+A function $f : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathbb{N}$ is mildly hard on average to $g$-approximate if there
+exists a positive polynomial $p$ such that for every uniform strict PPT heuristic
+$\mathcal{H} : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathrm{ProbComp}\ \mathbb{N}$, for all sufficiently large
+$n \in \mathbb{N}$,
+$$\Pr_{x \leftarrow \{0, 1\}^n, v \leftarrow \mathcal{H}(x)}[f(x) - g(n) \le v \le f(x)]
+  \le 1 - \frac{1}{p(n)}.$$
+When instantiating Theorems 3.1 and 5.2 for natural-number-valued $K^t$, we take the integer
+window $g(n) = d \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$ (`d * Nat.log 2 n`), which is slightly smaller than
+the real-valued $d \log_2 n$ in the paper. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=

matching_paragraphs: [P1] The pinned [Definition 2.5, p.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.11514v1#page=9) uses the symmetric event `|H(x) - f(x)| ≤ g(n)`. This definition uses `f(x)-g(n) ≤ v ∧ v ≤ f(x)`, so it rejects every overestimate. For example, f=0, H=1, g=1 is successful under the source event and unsuccessful here. Please make the canonical PPT approximation notion symmetric (e.g. `Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g n`) and derive the advertised theorem for it. The one-sided form can remain a clearly named helper: shifting a symmetric estimator down by g converts a g-error into a one-sided 2g-error when the shift is efficiently computable. Account for the rounded-log convention too. A docstring note alone does not supply this missing bridge.

body: [P2] These are shared APIs in an application module. `entropy_ge_of_dist_uniform`, `entropy_ge_of_dist_uniform_le`, `sum_filter_mass_le_ge_of_entropy_ge`, `entropy_ofList_take_ge`, and `entropy_append_uniform` do not depend on Kolmogorov complexity. CondEPPRG currently imports this entire file solely for that probability machinery, and LiuPass needs the truncation lemma. Put them in a narrow shared Probability/Entropy topic module first. Likewise, the generic function-hardness predicates and their generic bridges belong in a shared complexity/average-case module; keep K^t-specific bounds here. #733's standing rule requires such machinery in shared prerequisite PRs before the Crypto consumer, with no local copy or deprecated aliases. Preserve the checked proofs and update imports/clients.

+/-!
+# Average-case hardness of time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity (`K^t`)
+
+This module formalizes the average-case hardness notions and information-theoretic building blocks
+from [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020]. All
+section, definition, theorem, lemma, and page locators follow the full version
+`arXiv:2009.11514v1` (and ECCC TR20-052), in which `Theorem`/`Definition` share one section
+counter while `Lemma`/`Fact` share a separate section counter.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverage`: mild average-case hardness of exact computation for
+  `List Bool → ℕ` against uniform strict PPT heuristics
+  ([Liu and Pass, Definition 2.4, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`: mild average-case hardness of $g(n)$-approximation
+  for `List Bool → ℕ` against uniform strict PPT heuristics
+  ([Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageDet`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`:
+  library specializations of `MildlyHardOnAverage` and `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` to
+  deterministic polynomial-time heuristics.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageIO`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`:
+  library infinitely-often (`∃ᶠ n in atTop`) companions.
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageENat`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MildlyHardOnAverageIOENat`:
+  library `ℕ∞`-valued companions for `List Bool → ℕ∞` (such as `timeBounded t`).
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Probability.PMF.entropy_ge_of_dist_uniform_le`: if $X$ is a distribution on
+  $\{0, 1\}^n$ with $\mathsf{SD}(X, U_n) \le 1 / n^2$, then $H(X) \ge n - 2$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Lemma 2.2, §2.5, p. 9 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Probability.PMF.sum_filter_mass_le_ge_of_entropy_ge`: if $Y$ is a distribution on
+  $\{0, 1\}^m$ ($m \ge 1$) with $H(Y) \ge B \ge 3$, then the set of outcomes with point mass at
+  most $2^{-(B - 3)}$ has total probability at least $1 / m$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 5.2, Claim 2, §5.2, p. 12 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_timeBounded_generator_le`: for any length-nondecreasing
+  polynomial-time generator $G : \{0, 1\}^* \to \{0, 1\}^*$, there exist a polynomial $p_G$ and a
+  constant $c$ such that for all $t \ge p_G$ and all $z$, $K^t(G(z)) \le |z| + c$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 5.2, Equation (3), §5.2, pp. 11–12 of
+  arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+* `Cslib.Kolmogorov.sum_uniform_timeBoundedNat_lt_le`: counting bound on the fraction of $n$-bit
+  strings with $K^t(x) < n - k$
+  ([Liu and Pass, Proof of Theorem 5.2, Equation (2), §5.2, p. 11 of
+  arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]).
+
+## References
+
+* [Y. Liu, R. Pass, *On One-way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],

+namespace Cslib.Probability.PMF

+open Cslib
+open scoped BigOperators ENNReal

+private theorem mul_neg_logb_two_le_two {q : ℝ} (hq0 : 0 < q) :
+    q * (-Real.logb 2 q) ≤ 2 := by
+  have hlog_half := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 2)
+  rw [one_div, Real.log_inv] at hlog_half
+  have hlog2 : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ Real.log 2 := by linarith
+  have hlog_inv : Real.log (1 / q) ≤ 1 / q - 1 :=
+    Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (one_div_pos.mpr hq0)
+  have hq_log : q * (-Real.log q) ≤ 1 - q := by
+    have h1 : -Real.log q = Real.log (1 / q) := by
+      rw [one_div, Real.log_inv]
+    rw [h1]
+    have hmul := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hlog_inv hq0.le

reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-01 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 504d359f7e90fc3f0b3a0e76fb2dfec819ae8976

Agent review, not human approval. Hosted `ci-checks` was still running when I reviewed. I checked the public statements against the source standard (AGENTS.md, #952); I did not audit the 3.5k-line private construction proof by proof.

**What is right.**
- The theorems use the library's existing `OneWay` and `timeBoundedNat`/`timeBounded` (#817), with no parallel notion.
- The quantifier order matches Theorems 3.1 and 3.4: `∀ d, ∃ p, ∀ t ≥ p`, with the uniform input distribution on `{0,1}ⁿ` and `∀ᶠ n`.
- The PPT forms, `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxPPT_timeBoundedNat` and `…PPT_timeBoundedNat`, state the forward direction of Liu–Pass.
- The OWF hypothesis keeps the theorems from being vacuous, and `not_hardOnAverage_zero` covers the negative side.
- The title and docs claim only the forward direction.

**Blocking**
1. **The source pins sit on weaker variants.**
   - Liu–Pass's mild average-case hardness quantifies over PPT heuristics, which is what `MildlyHardOnAveragePPT` and `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxPPT` formalize; the PR body's own source line says "PPT".
   - Yet the "[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.4/2.5]" pins sit on `MildlyHardOnAverage` and `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` (`AverageCase.lean:360, 387`), which allow only deterministic polynomial-time heuristics. That is a weaker notion.
   - Likewise "[Theorem 3.1 (a) ⇒ (b)]" is attached to `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverage_timeBoundedNat` and to the existential headline `exists_mildlyHardOnAverage_of_exists_oneWay`, both deterministic-heuristic and weaker than the cited theorem.
   - **Fix:** pin Definitions 2.4/2.5 and Theorem 3.1 to the PPT declarations, and ideally give them the unsuffixed names. Label the deterministic and `ℕ∞` versions as library corollaries.
   - `HardOnAverage` and `HardOnAverageToApprox` are an infinitely-often (`∃ᶠ n`) variant that the PR body says replaces the source's `∀ᶠ n`. Do not attribute them to Definition 2.4. Rename them, for example to `MildlyHardOnAverageIO`, because "hard on average" conventionally means a stronger notion.
2. **The locators are inconsistent, so please pin and verify one version.**
   - The bibliography entry `LiuPass2020` is the FOCS'20 proceedings, pp. 1243–1254. The PR body cites "pp. 1249–1260", with locators on pp. 1255–1259 and an "Appendix A".
   - The sources claim pairs that cannot both exist under shared numbering: "Lemma 5.2" (regularity buckets) and "Theorem 5.2"; "Definition 2.5" and "Lemma 2.5"; "Definition 5.1" and "Lemma 5.1".
   - Please check every number against one version and cite that version. If the numbering comes from the full version (ECCC TR20-051 or arXiv), add that bibliography entry and say so.
3. **The AI disclosure contradicts how this worker was launched.** The body says "under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`". If that is accurate, this review does not satisfy the independence rule; if it is not, please correct the line.

Nonblocking: the approximation window is `d·⌊log₂ n⌋`, slightly smaller than the source's `d log n`, so the formal claim is marginally weaker. This is immaterial, but worth one sentence in the docstring.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
Addressed review `5641640166` (inline comments `4369715844`, `4369715846`) and the #733 shared-prerequisite items at `df768b5c` (updated per review `5641774715` item 2):

1. **Symmetric PPT & Deterministic Approximation Hardness (Definition 2.5, inline comment `4369715844`):**
   - `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`) in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/AverageCase.lean` uses the paper's symmetric distance `Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g x.length` ($|H(x) - f(x)| \le g(|x|)$).
   - Added the one-sided underestimation helper `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox` (`f x - g x.length ≤ v ∧ v ≤ f x`) together with the certified uniform-PPT shift + gap-scaling bridge `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` (and `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet.mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`) reducing symmetric $g$-approximation hardness to one-sided $(2g)$-approximation hardness via $H'(x) = H(x) - g(|x|)$ when $x \mapsto g(|x|)$ is polynomial-time computable (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat`).
   - Proved `computableInPolyTime_mul_log_two_succ` (`LiuPass.lean:175`) via `polytime` and `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_to_binary`, and used `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` with stretch $\gamma \ge 4d + 3$ (`LiuPass.lean:549–563`) to establish symmetric uniform-PPT and deterministic approximation hardness for $K^t$:
     - `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` (`fun n => d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`, which upper-bounds the paper's real-valued $d \log_2 n$ for all $n \ge 1$),
     - `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_clog` (`fun n => d * Nat.clog 2 n`, i.e., $d \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$),
     - `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat` (`fun n => d * Nat.log 2 n`, i.e., $d \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$),
     - plus the direct real-valued log window corollary `OneWay.exists_eventually_real_abs_sub_le_timeBoundedNat` ($|(v : \mathbb{R}) - (K^t(x) : \mathbb{R})| \le d \log_2 |x|$),

title: feat(Kolmogorov,Crypto): prove OWF implies K^t is mildly hard on average (Liu-Pass FOCS'20 M2a, #798)
body:
Refs #798 (Milestone M2a: `OWF => K^t is mildly hard on average`), #733.

Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

### Summary

Implements Milestone M2a of #798: the forward direction of Liu and Pass (*On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*, 2020 IEEE 61st Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS), pp. 1243–1254, `LiuPass2020`), consuming the shared probability/entropy (#985, `Complexity/Probability/Entropy/BitString.lean`) and average-case hardness (#986, `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/AverageCase.lean`) modules tracked in #733:

> If one-way functions exist, then there exists a polynomial $p$ such that for every time bound $t(n) \ge p(n)$, the time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity $K^t$ is mildly hard on average (and mildly hard on average to $g$-approximate for $g(n) = d \cdot (\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$, $d \cdot \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$, $d \cdot \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, and the real-valued $d \log_2 n$ window).

### Mathematical Scope & Paper Attribution

- **Source:** Yanyi Liu and Rafael Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*, FOCS 2020 (`LiuPass2020`, pp. 1243–1254; full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1`):
  - **Definitions 2.4 & 2.5 ([Liu and Pass, §2.3, p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]) and library companions (from #986):**
    - Exact average-case hardness against uniform strict PPT (`MildlyHardOnAverage`), with `ENat`-valued library companion `MildlyHardOnAverageENat`; deterministic polynomial-time specialization `MildlyHardOnAverageDet`; and infinitely-often deterministic library companions `MildlyHardOnAverageIO` and `MildlyHardOnAverageIOENat`, over `BitString.uniformList n`.
    - Symmetric $g$-approximation hardness (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`) formalized via `Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g x.length`.
    - One-sided underestimation helper (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO`) replacing $|H(x) - f(x)| \le g(|x|)$ with $f(x) - g(|x|) \le H(x) \le f(x)$, together with the certified uniform-PPT shift + gap-scaling transfer theorem `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` deriving symmetric $g$-approximation hardness from one-sided $(2g)$-approximation hardness via $H'(x) = H(x) - g(|x|)$ when $x \mapsto g(|x|)$ is polynomial-time computable (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat`).
  - **Section 3.2 (pp. 1247–1248, PDF pp. 5–6):** *Warm-up: Hard-on-Average from Regular PRGs*. Constructs a length-doubling PRG $G : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^{2n}$ from any OWF (via HILL99) and uses the $K^t$ sparsity bound vs. generator output upper bound to distinguish $G(U_n)$ from $U_{2n}$.
  - **Theorem 3.1 (§3, p. 10 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`; FOCS pp. 1246–1247) & Theorem 5.2 (§5.2, p. 11 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`):** *OWFs Imply Mildly Hard-on-Average of $K^t$ (Full Proof from Conditionally Entropy-Preserving PRGs)*. Given any OWF, Theorem 5.5 (`OneWay.exists_condEPPRG` in `CondEPPRG.lean`) yields a conditionally entropy-preserving PRG $G : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^{n + \gamma \log n}$. Proving `computableInPolyTime_mul_log_two_succ` (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => d * (Nat.log 2 x.length + 1)) encBits encNat`, `LiuPass.lean:175`) via `polytime` and `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_to_binary`, `CondEPPRG.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` (`LiuPass.lean:549–563`) instantiates the one-sided theorem at gap $2d$ under stretch $\gamma \ge 4d + 3$ and applies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`. Monotonicity (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mono`) and rounded-log bridges then yield the ceiling ($d \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$), floor ($d \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$), and real-valued ($|v - K^t(x)| \le d \log_2 n$) approximation hardness endpoints.
- **M2a Polynomial-Overhead Scope vs. Source Rate-1 Universal Simulation:**
  - The source theorem (Theorem 3.1) states $t(n) \ge (1 + \varepsilon)n$ for all $\varepsilon > 0$ via a rate-$1$ universal Turing machine simulation of the polynomial-time PRG prefix evaluator (`LiuPass2020`, p. 1248, PDF p. 6).
  - Because `Kolmogorov.timeBounded` (`K^t`) in `Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/TimeBounded.lean` is defined on the fixed multi-tape `Turing.TuringMachine` model whose evaluator `TimeBounded.computableInPolyTime_eval` incurs polynomial step overhead $p(n)$, M2a proves the **M2a polynomial-overhead form** (`∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, n + 1 ≤ p.eval n) ∧ ∀ t : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, p.eval n ≤ t n) → ...`). All polynomial-threshold declarations and module docstrings are explicitly labeled as the M2a polynomial-overhead form.

### Architecture & Module Changes

1. **Shared Supplier Modules (#985 & #986, #733 items 6 & 7):**
   - `Complexity/Probability/Entropy/BitString.lean` (#985): reusable Shannon entropy and statistical distance lemmas on `BitString m` in `namespace Cslib.Probability.PMF`.
   - `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/AverageCase.lean` (#986): general average-case hardness definitions, monotonicity, the uniform-PPT shift + gap-scaling bridge (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`), rounded-logarithm comparisons, and negative-side nonvacuity lemmas on `fun _ => 0`.
2. **`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/AverageCase.lean` ($K^t$-specific bridges):**
   - Contains the $K^t$-specific bridges (`mildlyHardOnAverageENat_timeBounded_iff`, `mildlyHardOnAverageIOENat_timeBounded_iff`), generator description bounds (`exists_timeBounded_generator_le`, `timeBoundedNat_generator_le`, `exists_timeBounded_of_computableInPolyTime`), and uniform counting / threshold acceptance bounds (`card_filter_timeBoundedNat_lt`, `sum_uniform_timeBoundedNat_lt_le`, `uniformList_threshold_accept_ge`, `generator_threshold_accept_le`).
3. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/CondEPPRG.lean`:**
   - Imports `Complexity.Probability.Entropy.BitString` (#985).
4. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/LiuPass.lean`:**
   - Proves both one-sided (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`) and symmetric (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`) uniform-PPT and deterministic approximation hardness for `d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`, `d * Nat.clog 2 n`, `d * Nat.log 2 n`, and the direct real-valued $|v - K^t(x)| \le d \log_2 n$ corollary `OneWay.exists_eventually_real_abs_sub_le_timeBoundedNat`, as well as the exact Theorem 3.1 endpoints (`OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverage_timeBoundedNat`, `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageENat_timeBounded`, and `InhabitedOneWay` / deterministic / IO variants).
5. **`ComplexityTests/LiuPass.lean` & `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean`:**
   - Signature, non-vacuity, and `#guard_msgs in #print axioms` coverage.

### Framework friction

- **Uniform-PPT shift bridge and logarithmic-gap certificate:** The uniform-PPT shift bridge `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` (#986) reuses the existing binary subtraction certificate (`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_sub`, through a proof-local `.of_tidy` conversion) and `IsPPTOn.map_with`, taking an explicit `ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat` premise for the gap computation. In `LiuPass.lean:175`, `computableInPolyTime_mul_log_two_succ` proves this certificate for $g(n) = d(\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$ via `polytime` on unary output composed with `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_to_binary`, and `CondEPPRG.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` (`LiuPass.lean:549–563`) applies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` at gap $2d$ under stretch $\gamma \ge 4d + 3$.
- **Rate-1 universal simulation vs. fixed TM evaluator polynomial overhead:** As documented on #798 and in `LiuPass.lean`, closing the gap from $t(n) \ge p(n)$ to $t(n) \ge (1 + \varepsilon)n$ requires a linear-time universal simulation theorem for the machine model underlying `Kolmogorov.timeBounded`, which is orthogonal to the cryptographic COND-EP-PRG reduction and tracked separately from M2a.

matching_paragraphs:
- **Source:** Yanyi Liu and Rafael Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*, FOCS 2020 (`LiuPass2020`, pp. 1243–1254; full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1`):
  - **Definitions 2.4 & 2.5 ([Liu and Pass, §2.3, p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]) and library companions (from #986):**
    - Exact average-case hardness against uniform strict PPT (`MildlyHardOnAverage`), with `ENat`-valued library companion `MildlyHardOnAverageENat`; deterministic polynomial-time specialization `MildlyHardOnAverageDet`; and infinitely-often deterministic library companions `MildlyHardOnAverageIO` and `MildlyHardOnAverageIOENat`, over `BitString.uniformList n`.
    - Symmetric $g$-approximation hardness (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`) formalized via `Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g x.length`.
    - One-sided underestimation helper (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO`) replacing $|H(x) - f(x)| \le g(|x|)$ with $f(x) - g(|x|) \le H(x) \le f(x)$, together with the certified uniform-PPT shift + gap-scaling transfer theorem `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` deriving symmetric $g$-approximation hardness from one-sided $(2g)$-approximation hardness via $H'(x) = H(x) - g(|x|)$ when $x \mapsto g(|x|)$ is polynomial-time computable (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat`).
  - **Section 3.2 (pp. 1247–1248, PDF pp. 5–6):** *Warm-up: Hard-on-Average from Regular PRGs*. Constructs a length-doubling PRG $G : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^{2n}$ from any OWF (via HILL99) and uses the $K^t$ sparsity bound vs. generator output upper bound to distinguish $G(U_n)$ from $U_{2n}$.
  - **Theorem 3.1 (§3, p. 10 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`; FOCS pp. 1246–1247) & Theorem 5.2 (§5.2, p. 11 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`):** *OWFs Imply Mildly Hard-on-Average of $K^t$ (Full Proof from Conditionally Entropy-Preserving PRGs)*. Given any OWF, Theorem 5.5 (`OneWay.exists_condEPPRG` in `CondEPPRG.lean`) yields a conditionally entropy-preserving PRG $G : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^{n + \gamma \log n}$. Proving `computableInPolyTime_mul_log_two_succ` (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => d * (Nat.log 2 x.length + 1)) encBits encNat`, `LiuPass.lean:175`) via `polytime` and `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_to_binary`, `CondEPPRG.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` (`LiuPass.lean:549–563`) instantiates the one-sided theorem at gap $2d$ under stretch $\gamma \ge 4d + 3$ and applies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`. Monotonicity (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mono`) and rounded-log bridges then yield the ceiling ($d \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$), floor ($d \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$), and real-valued ($|v - K^t(x)| \le d \log_2 n$) approximation hardness endpoints.
- **M2a Polynomial-Overhead Scope vs. Source Rate-1 Universal Simulation:**
  - The source theorem (Theorem 3.1) states $t(n) \ge (1 + \varepsilon)n$ for all $\varepsilon > 0$ via a rate-$1$ universal Turing machine simulation of the polynomial-time PRG prefix evaluator (`LiuPass2020`, p. 1248, PDF p. 6).
  - Because `Kolmogorov.timeBounded` (`K^t`) in `Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/TimeBounded.lean` is defined on the fixed multi-tape `Turing.TuringMachine` model whose evaluator `TimeBounded.computableInPolyTime_eval` incurs polynomial step overhead $p(n)$, M2a proves the **M2a polynomial-overhead form** (`∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, n + 1 ≤ p.eval n) ∧ ∀ t : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, p.eval n ≤ t n) → ...`). All polynomial-threshold declarations and module docstrings are explicitly labeled as the M2a polynomial-overhead form.

1. **Shared Supplier Modules (#985 & #986, #733 items 6 & 7):**
   - `Complexity/Probability/Entropy/BitString.lean` (#985): reusable Shannon entropy and statistical distance lemmas on `BitString m` in `namespace Cslib.Probability.PMF`.

2. **`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/AverageCase.lean` ($K^t$-specific bridges):**
   - Contains the $K^t$-specific bridges (`mildlyHardOnAverageENat_timeBounded_iff`, `mildlyHardOnAverageIOENat_timeBounded_iff`), generator description bounds (`exists_timeBounded_generator_le`, `timeBoundedNat_generator_le`, `exists_timeBounded_of_computableInPolyTime`), and uniform counting / threshold acceptance bounds (`card_filter_timeBoundedNat_lt`, `sum_uniform_timeBoundedNat_lt_le`, `uniformList_threshold_accept_ge`, `generator_threshold_accept_le`).
3. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/CondEPPRG.lean`:**
   - Imports `Complexity.Probability.Entropy.BitString` (#985).
4. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/LiuPass.lean`:**
   - Proves both one-sided (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`) and symmetric (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`) uniform-PPT and deterministic approximation hardness for `d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`, `d * Nat.clog 2 n`, `d * Nat.log 2 n`, and the direct real-valued $|v - K^t(x)| \le d \log_2 n$ corollary `OneWay.exists_eventually_real_abs_sub_le_timeBoundedNat`, as well as the exact Theorem 3.1 endpoints (`OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverage_timeBoundedNat`, `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageENat_timeBounded`, and `InhabitedOneWay` / deterministic / IO variants).
5. **`ComplexityTests/LiuPass.lean` & `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean`:**
   - Signature, non-vacuity, and `#guard_msgs in #print axioms` coverage.

- **Uniform-PPT shift bridge and logarithmic-gap certificate:** The uniform-PPT shift bridge `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` (#986) reuses the existing binary subtraction certificate (`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_sub`, through a proof-local `.of_tidy` conversion) and `IsPPTOn.map_with`, taking an explicit `ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat` premise for the gap computation. In `LiuPass.lean:175`, `computableInPolyTime_mul_log_two_succ` proves this certificate for $g(n) = d(\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$ via `polytime` on unary output composed with `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_to_binary`, and `CondEPPRG.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` (`LiuPass.lean:549–563`) applies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` at gap $2d$ under stretch $\gamma \ge 4d + 3$.
- **Rate-1 universal simulation vs. fixed TM evaluator polynomial overhead:** As documented on #798 and in `LiuPass.lean`, closing the gap from $t(n) \ge p(n)$ to $t(n) \ge (1 + \varepsilon)n$ requires a linear-time universal simulation theorem for the machine model underlying `Kolmogorov.timeBounded`, which is orthogonal to the cryptographic COND-EP-PRG reduction and tracked separately from M2a.

body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-08 — CHANGES REQUESTED at 58abfc5e054c8cabc183bc7c0daf139feef20c85

The statements move unchanged, and all callers in `Runtime/Determinant.lean` and `Runtime/Lift.lean` are updated with no copies left behind. The new module imports only `Complexity.Init` and Mathlib. Mathlib has no direct equivalent of the list bounds. [Hosted ci-checks](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40172711056) is green at this head.

1. **The names conflict with Mathlib's conventions** (`Foundations/Data/Int/Order.lean:45,57,64`). This module is a Mathlib candidate.
   - Mathlib's `Int.natAbs_sum_le` is the triangle inequality `(∑ i ∈ s, f i).natAbs ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, (f i).natAbs`, and `GSW/Noise.lean:55` uses it. Under that convention, a `List.natAbs_sum_le` would be the list version of the same statement, not a bound by `length * C`. The length-times-bound form is what Mathlib calls `List.sum_le_length_nsmul`.
   - Mathlib writes `(l.take i).sum` as `sum_take`, as in `prod_take_succ` and `prod_take_mul_prod_drop`, not as `take_sum`.

   Suggested names: `List.natAbs_sum_le_length_mul`, `List.natAbs_sum_take_le_length_mul` and `List.natAbs_sum_take_le_of_length_le`. Update the body's list of names to match.

Nonblocking:
- The proofs are not verbatim: three `.trans` calls became `Nat.le_trans`. This is harmless, but the body should say so.
- `Int.natAbs_pow_le` is `Int.natAbs_pow` followed by Mathlib's `pow_le_pow` (`Algebra/Order/Monoid/Unbundled/Pow.lean:177`). Consider inlining it at the four call sites, as #989 did with `determinant_bound`, or prove it as that one-liner.
- `Int.size_natAbs_sum_le` (`PolyTime/Int/Binary.lean:86`) re-proves the list triangle inequality in a local `have habs`. A public `l.sum.natAbs ≤ (l.map Int.natAbs).sum` here would serve both places, with the length bound following from `List.sum_le_length_nsmul`. This could be a follow-up.
- `Determinant.lean` and `Lift.lean` can use a plain `import` of the new module, because none of their public statements mentions these lemmas.

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-07 — findings pre-check at b7fead6458e7fc89c115f750229791223c9ac99d (not an approval; the approving reviewer is coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023)

**What checks out.** I compared the code against Definition 2.2 on p. 7 of the arXiv:2009.11514v1 PDF.
- `WeakOneWay` quantifies as ∃q ∀A ∀ᶠn, with a strict `< 1 − α n`.
- It reuses `Inverter` and `inversionGame` from `OneWay`. That gives a uniform `BitString.sampleList n` input, accepts any preimage (`f candidate == f input`), and passes the inverter `n` and `f x`.
- `ComputableInPolyTime f encBits encBits` and `IsPPT encBits` are the same as in `OneWay`.
- A positive `q : ℕ[X]` is equivalent to the paper's "polynomial q > 0". `weakOneWay_iff_le` covers the "fails with probability ≥ 1/q" form.
- `OneWay.weakOneWay` is correct: q = 2, and the success probability is eventually ≤ 1/3 < 1/2.
- The reindex reduction loses nothing. It shares one coin tape and runs `findGreatest` over M ≤ m(n+1). `oneWay` gets M < m(n+1) from `comp_of_polynomial_bound`, and `weakOneWay` uses q(parameter) ≤ q(M).
- Reuse is fine: `OneWayNormalization.normalize`/`inversion_le`, the `GeneratorReindex.parameter` lemmas, `exists_total_seeded_evaluator` and `Negligible.comp_of_polynomial_bound`. There is no parallel PPT or negligible notion.
- No public statement mentions tidy. Tidy appears only in private helpers and proof terms, and `findGreatest` and `isPolyTime_parameter` exist only in tidy form on main.
- Every name in the module-doc Main lists is a real declaration.
- The tests have concrete negatives (`const`, `id`) and the conditional positive (`OneWay → WeakOneWay`, plus normalization).
- Hosted `ci-checks` passed at this exact head (run 40172808819).

**Findings**

1. **Goldreich pins are wrong** (`Weak.lean:34-35, 53, 91, 293-294, 568`).
   - Goldreich Vol. 1 defines weak one-way functions in §2.2.2, Definition 2.2.2. In §2.3, item 2.3.1 is Proposition 2.3.1 (a weak but not strong OWF), and there is no Definition 2.3.1.
   - Extending a (strongly or weakly) one-way function defined on a polynomial-time enumerable set of lengths to all lengths is §2.2.3, Proposition 2.2.3. That is the right pin, not the proof of Theorem 2.3.2.
   - Please re-pin. Check the page numbers against the printed 2001 edition or drop them; I could not confirm pp. 42/43.
2. **`reindex` differs from the paper's padding trick, and the docs don't say so** (`:46-53, :292-294, :307-312, :530-534`). Liu–Pass (proof of Thm 4.1, p. 10) truncate the input to the nearest valid length and output f(x) unchanged. `reindex` also pairs the output with the parameter `n` (`wrappedImage`). This is harmless and makes the lossless reduction easy, because images from different parameters are disjoint. Still, the citation should call it a variant, e.g. "the padding trick of …, with the parameter appended to the output".
3. **`familyInversionGame` docstring** (`:343-348`). The game scores `core n (candidate.take (m n))`, not `core n candidate`, and the docstring doesn't mention the truncation. The choice is fine: composing any inverter with `take (m n)` turns a win in this game into a win in the untruncated game. So the hypotheses of `OneWayReindex.weakOneWay`/`oneWay` are no stronger than the natural ones. A sentence saying so would help the M2b-2 and M2b-3 consumers.
4. **The PR body doesn't match the code.** AGENTS.md "New statements and definitions" asks the PR to quote the source and map its notation, and reviewers check that mapping. The current body says:
   - "0 ≤ α(n) ≤ 1 eventually". `WeakOneWayAt` has no such field; `α : ℕ → ℝ` is unconstrained.
   - `WeakOneWay.normalize_weakOneWay` and `normalize_preimage_iff`. Neither exists. The theorem is `WeakOneWay.normalize`, through the inequality `OneWayNormalization.inversion_le`.
   - "pads `true :: f x` … to exact length B(|x|)+1". `BitString.padWord` is `frame word ++ replicate (2*(B − |word|)) false`, so the length is 2B+1, the value `exists_fixedOutputLength` itself uses.
   - "`m` strictly increasing". The code needs only `∀ n, n + 1 ≤ m n`.
   - "M ∈ [m(n), m(n+1))". The search runs over every M ≤ m(n+1).

   Suggested fix: quote Definition 2.2 verbatim, map A(1^n, y), x ← {0,1}^n, "q > 0" and "sufficiently large" to the Lean, and add an explicit line saying no curated abstract changes.
5. *Nit:* the module doc (`:90`) gives Yao's title as "Theory and Applications of Trapdoor Functions", while `references.bib` `Yao1982` says "Theory and Application of …". Make them match.
6. *Nit, optional:* `WeakOneWay.exists_fixedOutputLength` (`:276-290`) repeats the bound construction of `OneWay.exists_fixedOutputLength` (`Normalize.lean:104-116`) line for line. A shared `OneWayNormalization` lemma returning the bound, its plain certificate and the length equation would remove the copy.

None of these change a statement's meaning. Findings 1, 2 and 4 are documentation and pin fixes.

title: feat(Crypto/OneWay): add WeakOneWay, output normalization, and schedule reindexing
body:
Refs #733 and #798. This is supplier M2b-1; Yao amplification (M2b-2) and the Liu–Pass converse (M2b-3) remain separate work.

Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

### What this supplies

- `WeakOneWayAt f α` uses the existing unrestricted-preimage `inversionGame`, polynomial-time evaluation of f, and eventual strict success `< 1 - α(n)` for every uniform strict PPT inverter. `WeakOneWay f` chooses one positive natural-coefficient polynomial q before the inverter, with gap `1/q(n)`, following Liu–Pass Definition 2.2, §2.1, p. 7 of arXiv:2009.11514v1. The parameterized helper does not impose additional range hypotheses on α.
- Strict/non-strict equivalence uses polynomial slack: `WeakOneWay.of_le` replaces q by `2*q`; `exists_monotone_poly` uses `q + X + 1`. Strong one-wayness implies weak one-wayness; efficient inverse and constant-function examples refute it.
- Weak normalization reuses `OneWayNormalization.normalize` and its self-delimiting `BitString.padWord`, with the existing `inversion_le` reduction. Under an honest polynomial image bound B, the output length is exactly `2*B(n)+1`, with a uniform polynomial-time unary length certificate. This adds no new padding implementation or claim of exact equality between inversion games.
- `OneWayReindex.reindex m core` wraps the greatest fitting parameter n together with `core n` of the input's `m(n)`-bit prefix. Its transfer theorems require unary polynomial-time m, `m(n) ≥ n+1`, and a joint polynomial-time core; monotonicity of m is not required. The finite initial lengths below `m(0)` are excluded from the reduction bound and do not affect eventual security.
- The reduction builds one uniform family inverter per global inverter. For each sampled shared coin tape it searches all auxiliary lengths `M ≤ m(n+1)` and checks candidate preimages, rather than choosing an optimal length by advice or success probabilities. Its success dominates every relevant M without a probability loss. Weak transfer uses polynomial monotonicity; strong transfer uses the polynomial bound relating M to its selected parameter.

### Framework friction

The implementation reuses the existing OneWay game, uniform PPT seeded evaluator, bounded search, GeneratorReindex parameter lemmas and negligible-function composition. `familyInversionGame` is the supporting parameter-indexed experiment: it samples an `m(n)`-bit input and checks `core n (candidate.take (m n)) = core n input`. Candidates may be shorter than `m(n)`; longer candidates are truncated. This explicit family contract is the premise for the shared reduction, while the final WeakOneWay/OneWay conclusions use the existing global inversion model.

### Validation and abstract impact

The author reports all six `scripts/check.sh` gates plus hygiene, tidy-surface, changed-file, docs and guide checks passing. The PR adds focused constant/identity negatives, a strong-to-weak/normalization client, a concrete schedule evaluation and eight axiom guards. Hosted validation is linked in the review.

No selected abstract statement, definition, scope, or catalogue entry changes. This is shared infrastructure for later M2b results, not completion of amplification or the converse.

body: [P2] Apply #733's shared-support rule before landing these generic bounds. `pmf_map_true_le_add`, `pmf_map_any_range_true_le_sum`, and `pmf_bind_true_le_of_le` have no cryptographic parameters; the geometric estimate `pow_one_sub_le_inv_one_add` is likewise general. Reuse existing Mathlib/shared event and bind interfaces where possible (in particular, `PMF.tsum_mul_le_of_forall_le` already exists in Probability/PMF/Bind), and publish genuinely missing general laws in their shared mathematical homes as a small preceding supplier PR. The two budget-specific geometric corollaries can remain local. Update Framework friction to link the reuse/supplier resolution. I reviewed the inequalities as sound; a preservation split does not need a fresh mathematical audit.

+/-!
+# Yao's Weak-to-Strong One-Way Function Hardness Amplification
+
+This module formalizes Yao's hardness amplification theorem ([Yao1982];
+[Goldreich, Vol. 1, §2.3, Theorem 2.3.2][Goldreich2001];
+[Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 7 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]):
+if there exists a weak one-way function (`WeakOneWay`), then there exists a strong one-way
+function (`OneWay`).
+
+## Construction Overview
+
+1. **Output-length normalization:** Given `hf : WeakOneWay f`, apply
+   `WeakOneWay.exists_fixedOutputLength` and `WeakOneWay.exists_monotone_poly` to obtain a weak
+   one-way function $g$ with a polynomial-time unary output-length schedule `outLen : ℕ → ℕ`
+   (`∀ x, (g x).length = outLen x.length`) and a monotone polynomial $q : \mathbb{N}[X]$
+   ($q(N) \ge N + 1$) such that `WeakOneWayAt g (fun N => 1 / (q.eval N : ℝ))`.
+2. **Parallel direct product on schedule $m(n)$:** At parameter $n \in \mathbb{N}$, set block width
+   $w(n) := n + 1$, block count $k(n) := 2 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot w(n)$, and input length
+   $m(n) := k(n) \cdot w(n)$. On an input $X \in \{0, 1\}^{m(n)}$, `parallelCore k w g n X` splits
+   $X$ into $k(n)$ blocks $x_0, \dots, x_{k(n)-1} \in \{0, 1\}^{w(n)}$ via `BitString.listRow` and
+   concatenates $g(x_0) \mathbin{\Vert} \dots \mathbin{\Vert} g(x_{k(n)-1})$.
+3. **Direct reduction and probability bound:** For any uniform strict PPT inverter $\mathcal{A}$
+   against `familyInversionGame m (parallelCore k w g)` and any target polynomial degree
+   $d \in \mathbb{N}$, running $t_d(n) := 4 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot k(n) \cdot p_d(n)$ independent
+   planted-slot trials (where $p_d(n) = (n + 1)^{d + 1}$) defines a uniform strict PPT inverter
+   $B_d$ against $g$. Using `BitString.uniformList_all_listRow_true` twice—once across the $k(n)$
+   input blocks of $X$ and once across the $t_d(n)$ independent seed blocks of $B_d$—together with
+   the exact single-slot planting law `uniformList_replaceRow`, the weak one-wayness bound on $g$
+   forces $\mathcal{A}$'s inversion probability at parameter $n$ to be at most
+   $(1/2)^{n+1} + \frac{1}{2 p_d(n)} \le \frac{1}{p_d(n)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
+4. **Length-universal extension:** Applying `OneWayReindex.oneWay` to the strictly increasing
+   schedule $m(n)$ extends `parallelCore k w g` to a single strong one-way function on all binary
+   strings.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.parallelCore`: evaluate $f$ in parallel on $k(n)$ blocks of
+  width $w(n)$ and concatenate the outputs.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.replaceRow`: replace block $j$ of a flat bit string with $x$.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.plantedImage`: form the $k(n)$-block parallel output with a
+  challenge $y$ planted in slot $j$.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.familyInversionGame_parallelCore_negligible`: any uniform strict
+  PPT adversary has negligible inversion probability against `parallelCore` on schedule
+  $m(n) = 2 q(n+1) (n+1)^2$.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWay.exists_oneWay`: every weak one-way function yields a strong one-way
+  function ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 7 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020];
+  [Yao1982]).
+* `Cslib.Crypto.exists_oneWay_of_exists_weakOneWay`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.exists_oneWay_iff_exists_weakOneWay`: existential and equivalence forms of
+  Theorem 2.3.
+
+## References
+
+* [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],
+  full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1` (Section 2.1, Theorem 2.3, p. 7).
+* [A. C. Yao, *Theory and Application of Trapdoor Functions*][Yao1982].
+* [O. Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography, Volume 1*][Goldreich2001],
+  Section 2.3, Theorem 2.3.2.
+-/
+

+namespace Cslib.Crypto
+
+open Probability BitString Filter Turing.MultiTapeTM
+open scoped NNReal BigOperators
+
+namespace OneWayAmplification
+
+/-! ### Elementary real-algebra bounds for geometric amplification -/
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_mul_one_add_le_one {α : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ α) (h1 : α ≤ 1) (m : ℕ) :
+    (1 - α) ^ m * (1 + (m : ℝ) * α) ≤ 1 := by
+  induction m with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ m ih =>
+    have hnonneg : 0 ≤ (1 - α) ^ m := pow_nonneg (by linarith) m
+    have hstep : (1 - α) * (1 + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α) ≤ 1 + (m : ℝ) * α := by
+      push_cast
+      have hsq : 0 ≤ ((m : ℝ) + 1) * (α * α) := by positivity
+      nlinarith
+    calc (1 - α) ^ (m + 1) * (1 + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α)
+      _ = (1 - α) ^ m * ((1 - α) * (1 + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α)) := by ring
+      _ ≤ (1 - α) ^ m * (1 + (m : ℝ) * α) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hstep hnonneg
+      _ ≤ 1 := ih
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_le_inv_one_add {α : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ α) (h1 : α ≤ 1) (m : ℕ) :
+    (1 - α) ^ m ≤ 1 / (1 + (m : ℝ) * α) := by
+  have hpos : 0 < 1 + (m : ℝ) * α := by positivity
+  exact (le_div_iff₀ hpos).mpr (pow_one_sub_mul_one_add_le_one h0 h1 m)
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_inv_two_mul_le {q : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (r : ℕ) :
+    (1 - 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ))) ^ (2 * q * r) ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ r := by
+  have hqR : (0 : ℝ) < q := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hq
+  have hα0 : 0 ≤ 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ)) := by positivity
+  have hα1 : 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ)) ≤ 1 := by
+    rw [div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ q := by exact_mod_cast hq
+    linarith
+  have hbase : (1 - 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ))) ^ (2 * q) ≤ 1 / 2 := by
+    have h := pow_one_sub_le_inv_one_add hα0 hα1 (2 * q)
+    have hmul : ((2 * q : ℕ) : ℝ) * (1 / (2 * (q : ℝ))) = 1 := by
+      push_cast
+      field_simp
+    rw [hmul] at h
+    linarith
+  rw [pow_mul]
+  exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (pow_nonneg (by linarith) _) hbase r
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_le_inv_two_mul {q m : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (hm : 0 < m) :
+    (1 - 1 / (2 * (m : ℝ))) ^ (4 * q * m) ≤ 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ)) := by
+  have hqR : (0 : ℝ) < q := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hq
+  have hmR : (0 : ℝ) < m := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hm
+  have hα0 : 0 ≤ 1 / (2 * (m : ℝ)) := by positivity
+  have hα1 : 1 / (2 * (m : ℝ)) ≤ 1 := by
+    rw [div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ m := by exact_mod_cast hm
+    linarith
+  have h := pow_one_sub_le_inv_one_add hα0 hα1 (4 * q * m)
+  have hmul : ((4 * q * m : ℕ) : ℝ) * (1 / (2 * (m : ℝ))) = 2 * (q : ℝ) := by
+    push_cast
+    field_simp
+    ring
+  rw [hmul] at h
+  refine h.trans ?_
+  exact one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by positivity) (by linarith)
+
+/-! ### PMF union and expectation bounds -/
+
+private theorem pmf_map_true_le_add {α : Type*} (p : PMF α) (E A B : α → Bool)

body: [P2] Put general row replacement and its uniform law in the BitString layers. `replaceRow`, `listRow_replaceRow`, and `uniformList_replaceRow` describe flat bit-string blocks independently of one-way functions. Reuse the existing blocksEquiv/uniform-update APIs directly or extract this API before the Crypto consumer: deterministic operations/laws alongside Foundations/Data/BitString/List, and the probability law alongside Probability/BitString/List/All. `parallelCore_replaceRow` remains an application lemma here. This is a concrete #733 prerequisite, not a request to redesign the amplification proof.

+/-! ### PMF union and expectation bounds -/
+
+private theorem pmf_map_true_le_add {α : Type*} (p : PMF α) (E A B : α → Bool)
+    (h : ∀ a, E a = true → A a = true ∨ B a = true) :
+    (p.map E) true ≤ (p.map A) true + (p.map B) true := by
+  rw [PMF.map_apply, PMF.map_apply, PMF.map_apply, ← ENNReal.tsum_add]
+  refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun a => ?_
+  by_cases hE : true = E a
+  · rcases h a hE.symm with hA | hB
+    · simp [← hE, hA]
+    · simp [← hE, hB]
+  · simp [hE]
+
+private theorem pmf_map_any_range_true_le_sum {α : Type*} (p : PMF α) (K : ℕ)
+    (F : ℕ → α → Bool) :
+    (p.map (fun a => (List.range K).any (fun j => F j a))) true ≤
+      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range K, (p.map (F j)) true := by
+  induction K with
+  | zero =>
+    simp [PMF.map_apply]
+  | succ K ih =>
+    have hsplit : ∀ a, ((List.range (K + 1)).any (fun j => F j a)) = true →
+        ((List.range K).any (fun j => F j a)) = true ∨ F K a = true := by
+      intro a ha
+      rw [List.range_succ, List.any_append, Bool.or_eq_true] at ha
+      simpa using ha
+    rw [Finset.sum_range_succ]
+    exact (pmf_map_true_le_add p _ _ _ hsplit).trans (add_le_add_left ih _)
+
+private theorem pmf_bind_true_le_of_le {α : Type*} (μ : PMF α) (r : α → PMF Bool)
+    {c : ENNReal} (h : ∀ x ∈ μ.support, (r x) true ≤ c) :
+    (μ.bind r) true ≤ c := by
+  rw [PMF.bind_apply]
+  calc ∑' x, μ x * (r x) true
+    _ ≤ ∑' x, μ x * c := ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun x => by
+        by_cases hx : μ x = 0
+        · simp [hx]
+        · exact mul_le_mul_right (h x ((PMF.mem_support_iff _ _).mpr hx)) (μ x)
+    _ = c := by rw [ENNReal.tsum_mul_right, PMF.tsum_coe, one_mul]

+/-! ### Parallel evaluation, row replacement, and planted challenges -/
+
+/-- Evaluate `f` in parallel on `k n` blocks of width `w n` extracted from `X` via
+`BitString.listRow`, concatenating the resulting bit strings. -/
+def parallelCore (k w : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool) :
+    List Bool :=
+  (List.range (k n)).flatMap (fun j => f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X))
+
+/-- When `f` has fixed output length `outLen |x|` on inputs of length `|x|`, `parallelCore`
+produces outputs of exact length `k n * outLen (w n)`. -/
+theorem length_parallelCore {k w outLen : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hlen : ∀ x, (f x).length = outLen x.length) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool) :
+    (parallelCore k w f n X).length = k n * outLen (w n) := by
+  simp [parallelCore, List.length_flatMap, hlen, BitString.length_listRow]
+
+/-- Extracting the `j`-th output block of width `outLen (w n)` from `parallelCore` recovers
+`f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X)`. -/
+theorem listRow_parallelCore {k w outLen : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hlen : ∀ x, (f x).length = outLen x.length) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool)
+    {j : ℕ} (hj : j < k n) :
+    BitString.listRow (outLen (w n)) j (parallelCore k w f n X) =
+      f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X) := by
+  have h := BitString.listRow_flatMap_append
+    (width := outLen (w n))
+    (fun i => f (BitString.listRow (w n) i X))
+    (List.range (k n))
+    (fun i _ => by simp [hlen])
+    [] j (by simpa using hj)
+  simpa [parallelCore] using h
+
+/-- Any preimage under `parallelCore k w f n` must invert every individual block `j < k n`. -/
+theorem parallelCore_eq_imp_row_eq {k w outLen : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hlen : ∀ x, (f x).length = outLen x.length) {n : ℕ} {X X' : List Bool}
+    (heq : parallelCore k w f n X' = parallelCore k w f n X) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < k n) :
+    f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X') = f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X) := by
+  rw [← listRow_parallelCore hlen n X' hj, ← listRow_parallelCore hlen n X hj, heq]
+
+/-- Truncating the input of `parallelCore k w f n` to `k n * w n` bits leaves the output
+unchanged. -/
+theorem parallelCore_take (k w : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool) :
+    parallelCore k w f n (X.take (k n * w n)) = parallelCore k w f n X := by
+  unfold parallelCore
+  refine List.flatMap_congr fun j hj => congrArg f ?_
+  have hj_lt : j < k n := List.mem_range.mp hj
+  apply List.ext_getElem (by simp)
+  intro i hi hi'
+  simp only [BitString.length_listRow] at hi
+  rw [BitString.getElem_listRow hi, BitString.getElem_listRow hi]
+  have hlt : j * w n + i < k n * w n := by
+    have hstep : j * w n + i < (j + 1) * w n := by ring_nf; omega
+    exact lt_of_lt_of_le hstep (Nat.mul_le_mul_right (w n) hj_lt)
+  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_take_of_lt hlt]
+

+/-!
+# Yao's Weak-to-Strong One-Way Function Hardness Amplification
+
+This module formalizes Yao's hardness amplification theorem ([Yao1982];
+[Goldreich, Vol. 1, §2.3, Theorem 2.3.2][Goldreich2001];
+[Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 7 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]):
+if there exists a weak one-way function (`WeakOneWay`), then there exists a strong one-way
+function (`OneWay`).
+
+## Construction Overview
+
+1. **Output-length normalization:** Given `hf : WeakOneWay f`, apply
+   `WeakOneWay.exists_fixedOutputLength` and `WeakOneWay.exists_monotone_poly` to obtain a weak
+   one-way function $g$ with a polynomial-time unary output-length schedule `outLen : ℕ → ℕ`
+   (`∀ x, (g x).length = outLen x.length`) and a monotone polynomial $q : \mathbb{N}[X]$
+   ($q(N) \ge N + 1$) such that `WeakOneWayAt g (fun N => 1 / (q.eval N : ℝ))`.
+2. **Parallel direct product on schedule $m(n)$:** At parameter $n \in \mathbb{N}$, set block width
+   $w(n) := n + 1$, block count $k(n) := 2 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot w(n)$, and input length
+   $m(n) := k(n) \cdot w(n)$. On an input $X \in \{0, 1\}^{m(n)}$, `parallelCore k w g n X` splits
+   $X$ into $k(n)$ blocks $x_0, \dots, x_{k(n)-1} \in \{0, 1\}^{w(n)}$ via `BitString.listRow` and
+   concatenates $g(x_0) \mathbin{\Vert} \dots \mathbin{\Vert} g(x_{k(n)-1})$.
+3. **Direct reduction and probability bound:** For any uniform strict PPT inverter $\mathcal{A}$
+   against `familyInversionGame m (parallelCore k w g)` and any target polynomial degree
+   $d \in \mathbb{N}$, running $t_d(n) := 4 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot k(n) \cdot p_d(n)$ independent
+   planted-slot trials (where $p_d(n) = (n + 1)^{d + 1}$) defines a uniform strict PPT inverter
+   $B_d$ against $g$. Using `BitString.uniformList_all_listRow_true` twice—once across the $k(n)$
+   input blocks of $X$ and once across the $t_d(n)$ independent seed blocks of $B_d$—together with
+   the exact single-slot planting law `uniformList_replaceRow`, the weak one-wayness bound on $g$
+   forces $\mathcal{A}$'s inversion probability at parameter $n$ to be at most
+   $(1/2)^{n+1} + \frac{1}{2 p_d(n)} \le \frac{1}{p_d(n)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
+4. **Length-universal extension:** Applying `OneWayReindex.oneWay` to the strictly increasing
+   schedule $m(n)$ extends `parallelCore k w g` to a single strong one-way function on all binary
+   strings.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.parallelCore`: evaluate $f$ in parallel on $k(n)$ blocks of
+  width $w(n)$ and concatenate the outputs.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.replaceRow`: replace block $j$ of a flat bit string with $x$.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.plantedImage`: form the $k(n)$-block parallel output with a
+  challenge $y$ planted in slot $j$.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Crypto.OneWayAmplification.familyInversionGame_parallelCore_negligible`: any uniform strict
+  PPT adversary has negligible inversion probability against `parallelCore` on schedule
+  $m(n) = 2 q(n+1) (n+1)^2$.
+* `Cslib.Crypto.WeakOneWay.exists_oneWay`: every weak one-way function yields a strong one-way
+  function ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 7 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020];
+  [Yao1982]).
+* `Cslib.Crypto.exists_oneWay_of_exists_weakOneWay`,
+  `Cslib.Crypto.exists_oneWay_iff_exists_weakOneWay`: existential and equivalence forms of
+  Theorem 2.3.
+
+## References
+
+* [Y. Liu and R. Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*][LiuPass2020],
+  full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1` (Section 2.1, Theorem 2.3, p. 7).
+* [A. C. Yao, *Theory and Application of Trapdoor Functions*][Yao1982].
+* [O. Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography, Volume 1*][Goldreich2001],
+  Section 2.3, Theorem 2.3.2.
+-/
+
