+/-! ### Elementary real-algebra bounds for geometric amplification -/
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_mul_one_add_le_one {α : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ α) (h1 : α ≤ 1) (m : ℕ) :
+    (1 - α) ^ m * (1 + (m : ℝ) * α) ≤ 1 := by
+  induction m with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ m ih =>
+    have hnonneg : 0 ≤ (1 - α) ^ m := pow_nonneg (by linarith) m
+    have hstep : (1 - α) * (1 + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α) ≤ 1 + (m : ℝ) * α := by
+      push_cast
+      have hsq : 0 ≤ ((m : ℝ) + 1) * (α * α) := by positivity
+      nlinarith
+    calc (1 - α) ^ (m + 1) * (1 + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α)
+      _ = (1 - α) ^ m * ((1 - α) * (1 + ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α)) := by ring
+      _ ≤ (1 - α) ^ m * (1 + (m : ℝ) * α) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hstep hnonneg
+      _ ≤ 1 := ih
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_le_inv_one_add {α : ℝ} (h0 : 0 ≤ α) (h1 : α ≤ 1) (m : ℕ) :
+    (1 - α) ^ m ≤ 1 / (1 + (m : ℝ) * α) := by
+  have hpos : 0 < 1 + (m : ℝ) * α := by positivity
+  exact (le_div_iff₀ hpos).mpr (pow_one_sub_mul_one_add_le_one h0 h1 m)
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_inv_two_mul_le {q : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (r : ℕ) :
+    (1 - 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ))) ^ (2 * q * r) ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ r := by
+  have hqR : (0 : ℝ) < q := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hq
+  have hα0 : 0 ≤ 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ)) := by positivity
+  have hα1 : 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ)) ≤ 1 := by
+    rw [div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ q := by exact_mod_cast hq
+    linarith
+  have hbase : (1 - 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ))) ^ (2 * q) ≤ 1 / 2 := by
+    have h := pow_one_sub_le_inv_one_add hα0 hα1 (2 * q)
+    have hmul : ((2 * q : ℕ) : ℝ) * (1 / (2 * (q : ℝ))) = 1 := by
+      push_cast
+      field_simp
+    rw [hmul] at h
+    linarith
+  rw [pow_mul]
+  exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (pow_nonneg (by linarith) _) hbase r
+
+private theorem pow_one_sub_le_inv_two_mul {q m : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (hm : 0 < m) :
+    (1 - 1 / (2 * (m : ℝ))) ^ (4 * q * m) ≤ 1 / (2 * (q : ℝ)) := by
+  have hqR : (0 : ℝ) < q := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hq
+  have hmR : (0 : ℝ) < m := Nat.cast_pos.mpr hm
+  have hα0 : 0 ≤ 1 / (2 * (m : ℝ)) := by positivity
+  have hα1 : 1 / (2 * (m : ℝ)) ≤ 1 := by
+    rw [div_le_iff₀ (by positivity)]
+    have : (1 : ℝ) ≤ m := by exact_mod_cast hm
+    linarith
+  have h := pow_one_sub_le_inv_one_add hα0 hα1 (4 * q * m)
+  have hmul : ((4 * q * m : ℕ) : ℝ) * (1 / (2 * (m : ℝ))) = 2 * (q : ℝ) := by
+    push_cast
+    field_simp
+    ring
+  rw [hmul] at h
+  refine h.trans ?_
+  exact one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by positivity) (by linarith)
+
+/-! ### PMF union and expectation bounds -/
+
+private theorem pmf_map_true_le_add {α : Type*} (p : PMF α) (E A B : α → Bool)
+    (h : ∀ a, E a = true → A a = true ∨ B a = true) :
+    (p.map E) true ≤ (p.map A) true + (p.map B) true := by
+  rw [PMF.map_apply, PMF.map_apply, PMF.map_apply, ← ENNReal.tsum_add]
+  refine ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun a => ?_
+  by_cases hE : true = E a
+  · rcases h a hE.symm with hA | hB
+    · simp [← hE, hA]
+    · simp [← hE, hB]
+  · simp [hE]
+
+private theorem pmf_map_any_range_true_le_sum {α : Type*} (p : PMF α) (K : ℕ)
+    (F : ℕ → α → Bool) :
+    (p.map (fun a => (List.range K).any (fun j => F j a))) true ≤
+      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range K, (p.map (F j)) true := by
+  induction K with
+  | zero =>
+    simp [PMF.map_apply]
+  | succ K ih =>
+    have hsplit : ∀ a, ((List.range (K + 1)).any (fun j => F j a)) = true →
+        ((List.range K).any (fun j => F j a)) = true ∨ F K a = true := by
+      intro a ha
+      rw [List.range_succ, List.any_append, Bool.or_eq_true] at ha
+      simpa using ha
+    rw [Finset.sum_range_succ]
+    exact (pmf_map_true_le_add p _ _ _ hsplit).trans (add_le_add_left ih _)
+
+private theorem pmf_bind_true_le_of_le {α : Type*} (μ : PMF α) (r : α → PMF Bool)
+    {c : ENNReal} (h : ∀ x ∈ μ.support, (r x) true ≤ c) :
+    (μ.bind r) true ≤ c := by
+  rw [PMF.bind_apply]
+  calc ∑' x, μ x * (r x) true
+    _ ≤ ∑' x, μ x * c := ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun x => by
+        by_cases hx : μ x = 0
+        · simp [hx]
+        · exact mul_le_mul_right (h x ((PMF.mem_support_iff _ _).mpr hx)) (μ x)
+    _ = c := by rw [ENNReal.tsum_mul_right, PMF.tsum_coe, one_mul]
+
+/-! ### Parallel evaluation, row replacement, and planted challenges -/
+
+/-- Evaluate `f` in parallel on `k n` blocks of width `w n` extracted from `X` via
+`BitString.listRow`, concatenating the resulting bit strings. -/
+def parallelCore (k w : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool) :
+    List Bool :=
+  (List.range (k n)).flatMap (fun j => f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X))
+
+/-- When `f` has fixed output length `outLen |x|` on inputs of length `|x|`, `parallelCore`
+produces outputs of exact length `k n * outLen (w n)`. -/
+theorem length_parallelCore {k w outLen : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hlen : ∀ x, (f x).length = outLen x.length) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool) :
+    (parallelCore k w f n X).length = k n * outLen (w n) := by
+  simp [parallelCore, List.length_flatMap, hlen, BitString.length_listRow]
+
+/-- Extracting the `j`-th output block of width `outLen (w n)` from `parallelCore` recovers
+`f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X)`. -/
+theorem listRow_parallelCore {k w outLen : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hlen : ∀ x, (f x).length = outLen x.length) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool)
+    {j : ℕ} (hj : j < k n) :
+    BitString.listRow (outLen (w n)) j (parallelCore k w f n X) =
+      f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X) := by
+  have h := BitString.listRow_flatMap_append
+    (width := outLen (w n))
+    (fun i => f (BitString.listRow (w n) i X))
+    (List.range (k n))
+    (fun i _ => by simp [hlen])
+    [] j (by simpa using hj)
+  simpa [parallelCore] using h
+
+/-- Any preimage under `parallelCore k w f n` must invert every individual block `j < k n`. -/
+theorem parallelCore_eq_imp_row_eq {k w outLen : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hlen : ∀ x, (f x).length = outLen x.length) {n : ℕ} {X X' : List Bool}
+    (heq : parallelCore k w f n X' = parallelCore k w f n X) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < k n) :
+    f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X') = f (BitString.listRow (w n) j X) := by
+  rw [← listRow_parallelCore hlen n X' hj, ← listRow_parallelCore hlen n X hj, heq]
+
+/-- Truncating the input of `parallelCore k w f n` to `k n * w n` bits leaves the output
+unchanged. -/
+theorem parallelCore_take (k w : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (n : ℕ) (X : List Bool) :
+    parallelCore k w f n (X.take (k n * w n)) = parallelCore k w f n X := by
+  unfold parallelCore
+  refine List.flatMap_congr fun j hj => congrArg f ?_
+  have hj_lt : j < k n := List.mem_range.mp hj
+  apply List.ext_getElem (by simp)
+  intro i hi hi'
+  simp only [BitString.length_listRow] at hi
+  rw [BitString.getElem_listRow hi, BitString.getElem_listRow hi]
+  have hlt : j * w n + i < k n * w n := by
+    have hstep : j * w n + i < (j + 1) * w n := by ring_nf; omega
+    exact lt_of_lt_of_le hstep (Nat.mul_le_mul_right (w n) hj_lt)
+  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_take_of_lt hlt]
+
+/-- Replace row `j` of a `count × width` bit string `Z` with `x`. -/
+def replaceRow (width count j : ℕ) (x Z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (List.range count).flatMap (fun i => if i = j then x else BitString.listRow width i Z)
+
+/-- Reading row `i < count` from `replaceRow width count j x Z` returns `x` when `i = j` and
+`BitString.listRow width i Z` otherwise. -/
+theorem listRow_replaceRow {width count j : ℕ} {x : List Bool} (hx : x.length = width)
+    (Z : List Bool) {i : ℕ} (hi : i < count) :
+    BitString.listRow width i (replaceRow width count j x Z) =
+      if i = j then x else BitString.listRow width i Z := by
+  have h := BitString.listRow_flatMap_append
+    (width := width)
+    (fun r => if r = j then x else BitString.listRow width r Z)
+    (List.range count)
+    (fun r _ => by split_ifs <;> simp [hx])
+    [] i (by simpa using hi)
+  simpa [replaceRow] using h
+
+/-- Construct the `k n`-block output of `parallelCore` with a challenge `y` planted in slot `j`
+and the remaining slots filled by `f (BitString.listRow (w n) i Z)`. -/
+def plantedImage (k w : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (n j : ℕ)
+    (y Z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (List.range (k n)).flatMap (fun i =>
+    if i = j then y else f (BitString.listRow (w n) i Z))
+
+/-- When `y` has length `outLen (w n)`, `plantedImage` has length `k n * outLen (w n)`. -/
+theorem length_plantedImage {k w outLen : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → List Bool}
+    (hlen : ∀ x, (f x).length = outLen x.length) (n j : ℕ) {y : List Bool}
+    (hy : y.length = outLen (w n)) (Z : List Bool) :
+    (plantedImage k w f n j y Z).length = k n * outLen (w n) := by
+  have hmap : List.map (fun i =>
+      (if i = j then y else f (BitString.listRow (w n) i Z)).length) (List.range (k n)) =
+        List.replicate (k n) (outLen (w n)) := by
+    rw [List.eq_replicate_iff]
+    refine ⟨by simp, fun len hlen_mem => ?_⟩
+    obtain ⟨i, _, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hlen_mem
+    split_ifs <;> simp [hy, hlen]
+  rw [plantedImage, List.length_flatMap, hmap, List.sum_replicate, smul_eq_mul]
+
+/-- Evaluating `parallelCore` on `replaceRow (w n) (k n) j x Z` produces `plantedImage` with
+`y = f x` planted in slot `j`. -/
+theorem parallelCore_replaceRow {k w : ℕ → ℕ} (f : List Bool → List Bool)
+    (n j : ℕ) {x : List Bool} (hx : x.length = w n) (Z : List Bool) :
+    parallelCore k w f n (replaceRow (w n) (k n) j x Z) =
+      plantedImage k w f n j (f x) Z := by
+  unfold parallelCore plantedImage
+  refine List.flatMap_congr fun i hi => ?_
+  rw [listRow_replaceRow hx Z (List.mem_range.mp hi)]
+  split_ifs <;> rfl
+
+/-- Replacing row `j < count` of a uniform `count * width`-bit string with an independent uniform
+`width`-bit string preserves the uniform distribution `BitString.uniformList (count * width)`. -/
+theorem uniformList_replaceRow (width count : ℕ) (j : Fin count) :
+    (BitString.uniformList width).bind (fun x =>
+      (BitString.uniformList (count * width)).map (replaceRow width count j.val x)) =
+      BitString.uniformList (count * width) := by
+  classical
+  have hrep (x : BitString width) (Z : List Bool) :
+      replaceRow width count j.val (List.ofFn x) Z =
+        List.ofFn (blocksEquiv.symm
+          (Function.update (block (ofList (count * width) Z)) j x)) := by
+    rw [ofFn_blocksEquiv_symm, replaceRow, List.flatMap_def]
+    congr 1
+    apply List.ext_getElem (by simp)
+    intro i hi hi'
+    simp only [List.getElem_map, List.getElem_range, List.getElem_ofFn]
+    by_cases hij : (⟨i, by simpa using hi⟩ : Fin count) = j
+    · have hval : i = j.val := congrArg Fin.val hij
+      simp [hval]
+    · have hval : i ≠ j.val := fun h => hij (Fin.ext h)
+      simp [hij, hval, listRow_eq_ofFn width ⟨i, by simpa using hi⟩ Z]
+  have hblocks :
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin count → BitString width)).map
+        (fun rows => List.ofFn (blocksEquiv.symm rows)) =
+      BitString.uniformList (count * width) := by
+    have h := congrArg (PMF.map List.ofFn)
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv
+        (blocksEquiv : BitString (count * width) ≃ (Fin count → BitString width)).symm)
+    simpa only [PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, BitString.uniformList] using h
+  have hupd := congrArg
+    (PMF.map (fun rows : Fin count → BitString width => List.ofFn (blocksEquiv.symm rows)))
+    (PMF.uniformOfFintype_update (γ := BitString width) j)
+  conv_rhs => rw [← hblocks, ← hupd]
+  simp only [BitString.uniformList, PMF.bind_map, PMF.map_bind, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def]
+  congr 1
+  funext x
+  have hZ := congrArg
+    (PMF.map (fun rows : Fin count → BitString width =>
+      List.ofFn (blocksEquiv.symm (Function.update rows j x))))
+    (uniformList_blocks count width)
+  simpa only [BitString.uniformList, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, hrep] using hZ
+
+/-! ### Candidate selection, mega-trials, and repeated trials -/
+
+/-- Return the first candidate in `cands` whose image under `f` equals `y`, or `[]` if none
+matches. -/
+def pickPreimage (f : List Bool → List Bool) (y : List Bool)

author: SamuelSchlesinger
body:
reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-09 — findings pre-check at af51ee3c698ee0831ac06046c47c243b68a5725b (not an approval; the approving reviewer is coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023)

Scope: #995's own diff against #992 (`a7d4f4a2`), read against the M2b design on #798 and the AGENTS.md "New statements and definitions" standard. I did not build locally. Line numbers refer to `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/Amplification.lean` at this head.

**Findings**

1. **The Liu–Pass locator and quote are wrong.** In `arXiv:2009.11514v1`, Theorem 2.3 is on printed **p. 8** (PDF p. 9), not p. 7; only Definitions 2.1–2.2 are on p. 7. The exact text is: "Theorem 2.3 ([Yao82]). Assume there exists a weak one-way function. Then there exists a one-way function." The quote in the PR body adds "(strong)", which comes from the preceding prose sentence, and "(and vice versa)", which is not in the paper. Fix the quote in the PR body and change `p. 7` to `p. 8` at L27, L70, L79, L940, L988 and L997. The "p. 7" for Theorem 2.3 in the #798 design comment has the same error.

2. **The equivalence is not Liu–Pass Theorem 2.3.** L73–74 call `exists_oneWay_iff_exists_weakOneWay` an "equivalence form of Theorem 2.3", and its docstring (L996–998) leads with Liu–Pass Thm 2.3. That theorem is one-directional. The iff matches Goldreich Vol. 1 Theorem 2.3.2 ("weak one-way functions exist if and only if strong one-way functions exist"), plus #992's `OneWay.weakOneWay` for the easy direction. Pin the iff to Goldreich 2.3.2 and cite Liu–Pass 2.3 only for the forward direction. Caveat: I could not check Goldreich's text directly. The §2.3 numbering is consistent with secondary course notes that cite Prop. 2.3.3 as the toy example (Prop 2.3.1, then Thm 2.3.2, then Prop 2.3.3), but the exact wording of Thm 2.3.2 is unverified.

3. **Duplicated real-analysis lemmas.** The private `pow_one_sub_mul_one_add_le_one` (L96) is `Real.one_sub_pow_mul_one_add_mul_le_one` (`Complexity/Foundations/Analysis/BernoulliInequality.lean:33`), which needs only `p ≤ 1`. The base step of `pow_one_sub_inv_two_mul_le` (L116–131) is `one_sub_pow_le_half` (`Complexity/Foundations/Data/Finset/Sampling.lean:62`) with `p = 1/(2q)`, `k = 2q`. With both reused, the private block at L96–151 shrinks to a few lines.

4. **The proof strengthens `q` but never uses the extra properties, and the docs advertise them.** `WeakOneWay.exists_oneWay` calls `exists_monotone_poly` (L947–948) but discards monotonicity (`_`) and uses `q N ≥ N + 1` only to get `0 < q N`, which `WeakOneWay g` already provides. Destructure `hg_weak` directly. Then drop "monotone polynomial … q(N) ≥ N + 1" from the module overview (L34–37) and from the PR body.

5. **Redundant hypothesis.** `familyInversionGame_parallelCore_negligible` takes `hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encBits encBits` (L728) alongside `hweak : WeakOneWayAt f …`, and `hweak.polyTime` is exactly `hf`. Drop `hf`. Also consider replacing the `let w … let k …` binders in the statement (L734–735) with explicit terms or named defs, so clients don't have to unfold `let`s in the type.

6. **(Suggestion, not blocking: the design specifies the existential headline.)** `WeakOneWay f → ∃ F, OneWay F` is faithful to Liu–Pass 2.3 and Goldreich 2.3.2. Its conclusion is the library's strong `OneWay`, and it adds no injectivity, length-preservation or regularity hypotheses; fixed output length appears only on the labelled family lemma. But the construction-level result is visible only inside the proof (L949–987): `OneWay (OneWayReindex.reindex m (parallelCore k w f))` for a fixed-output-length `1/q`-weak `f`, with `k = 2q(n+1)(n+1)` and `m = k·(n+1)`. Exposing it as a named public theorem would make the direct product inspectable and reduce `exists_oneWay` to normalization plus that theorem.

7. **(Nit) Public surface and placement.** `pickPreimage`, `slotCand`, `megaTrial`, `runTrials` and their `eval_*`/`*_fail_*` lemmas are plumbing for this single reduction; consider making them private (the intent rule in #926). `replaceRow`, `listRow_replaceRow` and `uniformList_replaceRow` are generic bit-string facts that would fit beside `uniformList_blocks` in `Complexity/Probability/BitString/List.lean`.

**Checked, no finding**
- **Proof shape:** this is Goldreich's argument, a union bound over planted slots plus repetition. I checked the arithmetic. With θ = 1/(2kp) and t = 4qkp, (1−θ)^t ≤ 1/(2q), so P[good] < 1 − 1/(2q) and P[good]^k ≤ 2^−(n+1) with k = 2q(n+1)(n+1). Success is then ≤ 2^−(n+1) + 1/(2p) ≤ 1/p.
- **Reduction:** `B_inv` is a single uniform `IsPPT encBits` inverter for each target degree. It is built from the library's `exists_total_seeded_evaluator`, `IsPPTOn.map_with` and `sampleList`, with no parallel PPT notion. A's coin budget agrees between the family game and the planted calls because the output length is fixed. The weak bound is applied at w(n) = n + 1 through `tendsto_add_atTop_nat`.
- **Reindexing:** handled only through #992's `exists_fixedOutputLength` and `OneWayReindex.oneWay`. Nothing from #992 or `GeneratorReindex` is duplicated.
- **Plain-first:** no public statement mentions tidy; all `computableTidily_*` lemmas are private.
- **Docs:** every name in the module-doc Main lists is a real declaration. The overview's k, t and the schedule m(n) = 2q(n+1)(n+1)² match the code (apart from item 4).
- **Tests:** `decide` evaluates `parallelCore`, `replaceRow` and `plantedImage` on concrete inputs. The theorem-level example can only type-check, since no unconditional weak one-way function instance can exist.
- **CI:** hosted `ci-checks` at af51ee3c (run 40175333897) is **red because of infrastructure, not code**. `lake build`, `lake test`, `lake lint` and the tidy ratchet (1289, matching the baseline) passed. "Changed-file lints" then failed on `git fetch origin a7d4f4a2` with "Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exit 128, so `mk_all --check`, `lint-style` and `checkInitImports` were skipped. The run needs a rerun before any verdict; I have not rerun it.

title: feat(Crypto/OneWay): formalize Yao's weak-to-strong OWF hardness amplification
body:
Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

Refs #733, #798. Restacked onto `main` after #998 squash-merged at 17e656d875374bb21f69f225da0d02e99866fa91; #992 is also consumed from main.

### Summary

This supplier PR (M2b-2) formalizes Yao's weak-to-strong one-way function hardness amplification ([Yao1982]; [Goldreich, Vol. 1, §2.3, Theorem 2.3.2][Goldreich2001]; [Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]) in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/Amplification.lean`:

> **Theorem 2.3 ([Yao82], p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`).** *Assume there exists a weak one-way function. Then there exists a one-way function.*

1. **Construction (`OneWayAmplification.parallelCore`, `OneWayAmplification.plantedImage`):**
   - Given `hf : WeakOneWay f`, apply `WeakOneWay.exists_fixedOutputLength` (#992) to obtain a weak one-way function $g$ with a polynomial-time unary output-length schedule `outLen : ℕ → ℕ` (`∀ x, (g x).length = outLen x.length`) and a positive polynomial $q \in \mathbb{N}[X]$ ($\forall N,\, 0 < q(N)$) such that `WeakOneWayAt g (fun N => 1 / (q.eval N : ℝ))`.
   - At parameter $n \in \mathbb{N}$, set block width $w(n) := n + 1$, block count $k(n) := 2 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot w(n)$, and input schedule $m(n) := k(n) \cdot w(n)$.
   - `parallelCore k w g n X` splits $X$ into $k(n)$ blocks of width $w(n)$ via `BitString.listRow` and concatenates $g(x_0) \mathbin{\Vert} \dots \mathbin{\Vert} g(x_{k(n)-1})$.

2. **Direct reduction and probability bound (`OneWayAmplification.familyInversionGame_parallelCore_negligible`):**
   - For any uniform strict PPT inverter $\mathcal{A}$ (`IsPPT encBits A`) and any target polynomial degree $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $p_d(n) := (n + 1)^{d + 1}$ and $t_d(n) := 4 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot k(n) \cdot p_d(n)$.
   - Using `IsPPT.exists_total_seeded_evaluator`, the internal inverter $B_d(1^N, y)$ runs $t_d(N-1)$ independent mega-trials over `BitString.sampleList`, planting $y$ in each slot $j < k(N-1)$ via `plantedImage` and picking a valid preimage if one is found.
   - Using `BitString.uniformList_all_listRow_true` twice—once across the $k(n)$ input blocks of $X$ and once across the $t_d(n)$ independent seed blocks of $B_d$—together with the exact single-slot planting law `BitString.uniformList_replaceRow` (#998), the weak one-wayness bound on $g$ forces $\mathcal{A}$'s inversion probability at parameter $n$ to be at most $(1/2)^{n+1} + \frac{1}{2 p_d(n)} \le \frac{1}{p_d(n)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

3. **Headline theorems (`WeakOneWay.exists_oneWay`, `exists_oneWay_of_exists_weakOneWay`, `exists_oneWay_iff_exists_weakOneWay`):**
   - Applying `OneWayReindex.oneWay` (#992) to the schedule $m(n)$ ($m(n) \ge n + 1$) extends `parallelCore k w g` to a single strong one-way function on all binary strings.
   - `exists_oneWay_iff_exists_weakOneWay` ([Goldreich, Vol. 1, §2.3, Theorem 2.3.2][Goldreich2001]) combines `exists_oneWay_of_exists_weakOneWay` ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]; [Yao1982]) with `OneWay.weakOneWay` (#992).

### Framework friction

I checked the deletion with my own parser, comparing `origin/main` (`ee4a5892`, which is this PR's base) with this head.

- **Classification on `main`.** It has 1,605 `#print axioms` guard blocks, and every one parsed. 1,549 record exactly `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, 39 record `[propext, Quot.sound]`, 14 record `[propext]` and 3 record no axioms. None lists the standard set in a different order.
- **Kept and deleted blocks.** The head has 56 blocks, byte-identical to the 56 non-standard originals and in the same order. All 1,549 deleted blocks record exactly the standard set. They cover 1,546 distinct names, because three names were guarded twice. No standard-set block remains.
- **Everything outside the guards.** Two things change: the module-doc paragraph (old lines 22–23) and the six deleted `--` section comments. Each of those six sections contained only standard guards. A line-level diff shows the file is a pure deletion apart from that paragraph. GitHub's +152 lines come from how its diff aligns the lines.
- **Unchanged audit code.** The imports, the `run_cmd` audit with its `allowed` list, `namespace` / `end ComplexityTests.Axioms` and the `/-! ### Executable PCP … -/` header are all unchanged.
- **Dependencies and CI.** No script, lint, CI step or abstract check refers to `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean` or requires a named guard. The abstract axiom checks are untouched. Hosted `ci-checks` passed at this exact head (run 40176771453).

**Blocking**

1. `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean:22-24`: the new module doc says *when* to add a named guard but not *where*. It sits right above the guards and begins "The named `#guard_msgs` checks below …", so it reads as "add it here". The old text said exactly that ("Add an entry …"). AGENTS.md (Proof hygiene) says to place the guard in the epic's own test module. Suggested one-line fix: end the paragraph with "…so a named guard is added only for such a result, in the epic's own test module rather than here." If new narrow guards are instead meant to go in this file, change AGENTS.md. Either way, the two should agree.

**Nonblocking**

- `scripts/audit_queries.py references --unused` builds its list from `.ilean` references. For some declarations the deleted guard was the only reference from a test. A rough textual count finds about 20, for example `Cslib.Crypto.isPPT_inversionGame`, and these will now appear as unreferenced. The tool already warns that an unreferenced declaration may still be wanted, so nothing needs to change here. It is worth knowing for the next consolidation audit.
- Under the new rule, the standard-set guards in other `ComplexityTests` modules are also redundant. The PR rightly leaves them out of scope; they could go in a follow-up.

Once item 1 is resolved, the PR is test- and documentation-only and qualifies for the delegated-review exception.

title: test(axioms): drop named guards that repeat the global audit
body:
## Change

`ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean` already audits every declaration stored in the imported `Complexity` modules and rejects any dependency outside `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Most of its named `#guard_msgs … #print axioms X` blocks recorded exactly that set, so they repeated what the audit enforces. This PR removes them and keeps only the guards that record something narrower.

A script parsed each `/-- info: … -/ #guard_msgs … in #print axioms X` block, including `open … in` prefixes and wrapped messages, and classified it by its expected axiom set:

| Expected axioms | Blocks | Action |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` | 1,549 | deleted |
| `propext`, `Quot.sound` | 39 | kept verbatim |
| `propext` | 14 | kept verbatim |
| no axioms | 3 | kept verbatim |

That is 1,605 blocks parsed, every `#print axioms` in the file. The earlier estimate of 1,523 standard guards predates recent merges to `main`, which added more standard guards; the branch was rebased onto `ee4a5892` and the script re-run, which also removed the 8 standard guards added by #992. Six `--` section comments whose first guard was removed went with it. The resulting file is a pure line deletion of the original, apart from the module doc. The audit code, the imports and the 56 remaining guards are unchanged.

The rule for adding named guards changes to match:

- **`Axioms.lean` module doc.** "Add an entry whenever a main result is added to a public module" is replaced: a named guard is added only when a result is meant to depend on fewer axioms than the standard three, for example a choice-free result, because the global audit already covers the standard set.
- **`AGENTS.md` (Proof hygiene).** Same rule. The placement guidance (the epic's own test module) is kept.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`.** "The named headline checks remain readable regression tests" is replaced with the same rule.

No script, lint or test requires a named guard for each main result, abstract or headline. The curated abstracts keep their own axiom checks (`abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/Check.lean` and the per-abstract `#print axioms` guards), and this PR does not touch them. Named guards with the standard set in other `ComplexityTests` modules are also out of scope.

Samuel approved this change on 2026-10-25. It changes only tests and documentation: no public statement or definition is modified.

## Validation and review

- `scripts/check.sh` on head `bfcd35c2`: all six gates pass locally (`build`, `mk_all --check`, `test`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`). `lake test` re-elaborates the trimmed `Axioms.lean`.
- A negative check (one kept guard edited to a wrong axiom list) fails `#guard_msgs` as expected.
- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py` passes.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 351 tests pass (3 skipped).
- Hosted CI for `bfcd35c2`: [Lean Action CI run 40176771453](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40176771453) passed.

## Headline abstracts

- Affected abstracts/catalogue entries, or reason the selection is unaffected: unaffected. No library statement changes, and the abstract axiom checks are untouched.
- Independent abstract review: not applicable.
- PDF artifact/run: not applicable.

title: feat(fo): define native Bit Sum over canonical order and BIT
body:
## Change

Closes #91.

Defines one native first-order `bitSum` formula over canonical order and BIT. For every `Fin n` with `n ≥ 2`, `realize_bitSum` proves that it holds exactly when the second value is the number of set bits of the first. `existsUnique_bitSum` proves that every input has exactly one output in the same universe.

The proof constructs eight bounded words encoding every bit of a balanced addition tree. Native decoding uses PLUS, fixed syntactic literal multiples, and exact binary shifts; it neither assumes a multiplication predicate nor accepts a supplied semantic certificate. Decoding explicitly constrains high bits, and shifts reject lost source bits. A fixed finite disjunction covers small input numerals. The formula covers arbitrary universe sizes, including nonpowers of two. Native TIMES, arbitrary-base tuple BIT and numeric-preserving composition remain open in `ROADMAP.md`.

Sources: Immerman, *Descriptive Complexity*, Lemma 1.18 and Theorem 1.17(1); the historical notes credit Barrington, Immerman and Straubing. This implementation proves a balanced-tree packing variant of the source's packed running-sum construction. It reuses the library's native PLUS theorem and Mathlib/Lean bit arithmetic. Source checkpoint: `eef9229da5388dd750c22ba07eaea612587a10ee`.

## Validation and review

- Clean Lean MCP diagnostics and strict targeted source/client builds.
- All six gates pass: strict build, `mk_all --check`, strict test, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`.
- Boundary clients cover size 2, non-power-of-two sizes, the 255/256 small-input boundary, packed all-one and single-high-bit inputs, incorrect counts, arbitrary relabeling, unavailable fixed numerals, overflowing shifts, large shifts of zero, and decoder high-bit rejection.
- Named axiom guards for `realize_bitSum`, `existsUnique_bitSum` and `realize_shiftLeft`, plus the global audit, pass. No `sorry`, custom axiom, `native_decide` or resource-limit override was added.

All six gates pass on source `eef9229d`, the first integrated revision `98444662`, and final PR head `69f46b24fca3f893789ddc191cfcd5e841876f7f`. The final head cleanly merges main `d642055973ccac06eb4b1213f75ef80c4cf83e85` after #98. The Bit Sum definitions, statements, proofs, tests and reviewed index prose are unchanged in both integrations.

Independent coordinator `bit_sum_design_review` checked the uniform construction, source boundary and packing bounds with no blocker; its two cautions (high-zero decoding and no-lost-bit shifting) are explicitly implemented. Independent coordinator `wpp_proof_cleanup` [approved source/API/correctness at `eef9229d` and index source at `9e15fe71`](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/issues/91#issuecomment-6301436649), with no findings and fresh independent Lean MCP checks, then [approved integrated head `98444662` and its PDF artifact](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/99#issuecomment-6301498262). No mathematical or API findings remain. Root coordinator independently [approved the final integration and artifact at `69f46b24`](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/pull/99#issuecomment-6301619533), then merged after the exact-head CI retry passed. The author did not approve or merge the PR.

## Theorem index

- The new entry states exact BSUM semantics and unique outputs, exact-shift support, source credit and open boundaries. All four declaration links are pinned to `eef9229d`. The PLUS entry's former Bit Sum open-boundary sentence is updated.
- Independent semantic review by `wpp_proof_cleanup` approved source `eef9229d` and prose `9e15fe71` with no findings; both are unchanged in final integrated head `69f46b24`.
- The [final combined PDF run](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/actions/runs/39498046574) passed and produced [artifact 12298747149](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/actions/runs/39498046574/artifacts/12298747149). Its checked-out source is `dac5774197fdb1f1852275b7d19bef35e4d415df`, PR head `69f46b24fca3f893789ddc191cfcd5e841876f7f`, base `d642055973ccac06eb4b1213f75ef80c4cf83e85`, and `source_dirty=false`. Its source tree `41862615bf3fbb77164d536d2cb8e6d0be29c06c` exactly equals the final head tree.
- Final author inspection: 66 pages, 133 automatically counted entries matching the source environment count; pages 1, 10 and 25 render cleanly. Pages 9, 10 and 11 render byte-identically to the independently approved earlier artifact. All four Bit Sum URI targets and the five counting-branch targets from merged #98 match their pinned declaration names and lines. The verified final PDF SHA-256 is `221f5cf4894ccbf82f776effb63a0683f4fc9a424776870d30c63ff924020d12`. The root coordinator's final integration/artifact review is approved at the link above. No generated PDF is committed. AI review does not imply human editorial approval.

Exact-head remote Lean CI [run 39498046643, attempt 2](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/complexitylib2/actions/runs/39498046643) passed, along with the title and PDF checks. The first attempt encountered an SSL/TLS connection error while downloading Lean, before source checks; retrying the failed job resolved it without a code change. Final local six-gate validation also passed.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex worker `ordered-times-20261020` implemented the formulas, proofs, clients and documentation, using Lean MCP for iteration and shell builds for validation. The independent coordinator reviews above are separate from authoring and self-review.
